articles.title: Cómo ha cambiado el valor de la criptomoneda ethereum en las últimas 24 horas
articles.text:
Ethereum es una plataforma digital que adopta la tecnología de cadena de bloques (blockchain) y expande su uso a una gran variedad de aplicaciones, mientras que ether es su criptomoneda nativa. En el mundo de las finanzas digitales es común que la criptomoneda sea llamada como la red, aunque en realidad no son lo mismo.
La plataforma ethereum, creada en el 2015 por el programador Vitalik Buterin, buscaba ser un instrumento para aplicaciones descentralizadas y colaborativas sobre las que se pueden hacer contratos inteligentes (dAPPs)
Al igual que el bitcoin, el valor de ether se disparó en un corto periodo de tiempo. En enero de 2016, ether cotizaba alrededor de un dólar y actualmente tiene un máximo histórico de 4.953,73 dólares.
El precio de la criptomoneda de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2325.34 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital reportó un cambio del -0.36 el último día, así como una variación del 0.0 % en la última hora.
Actualmente, ethereum se encuentra en el lugar #2 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta criptodivisa es de 4891.7 dólares por unidad.
Costo de la criptomoneda Ethereum
Ethereum y su última actualización
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: G.SKILL and Newegg Offer Limited-Time AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D Combo Deals Featuring AMD EXPO ULL DDR5 Memory
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
G.SKILL and Newegg Offer Limited-Time AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D Combo Deals Featuring AMD EXPO ULL DDR5 Memory
G.SKILL, a leading manufacturer of high-performance memory and PC gaming peripherals, is teaming up with Newegg to offer a series of limited-time PC hardware combo deals, featuring the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor, G.SKILL Trident Z5 NeoX RGB DDR5 memory, and select AMD AM5 motherboards. These specially priced bundles offer PC enthusiasts and gamers an opportunity to build or upgrade their systems with high-performance components while enjoying additional combo savings.
The promotion features eight different hardware combinations, pairing the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor with a 32 GB (2x 16 GB) G.SKILL Trident Z5 NeoX RGB DDR5-6000 memory kit and a choice of motherboards from ASUS, MSI, GIGABYTE, and ASRock. Available in black or white memory designs depending on the selected bundle, these combinations offer flexibility for a wide range of PC builds.The bundled G.SKILL Trident Z5 NeoX RGB memory kits with AMD EXPO Technology: Featuring Ultra Low Latency profile features optimized memory sub-timings designed to reduce memory access latency and improve system responsiveness on compatible AMD platforms.In an AIDA64 Cache & Memory Benchmark comparison on the promotional page, G.SKILL DDR5-6000^ CL36 memory achieved 73.3ns of memory latency with AMD EXPO ULL enabled, compared to 78.1ns using a standard AMD EXPO profile. The ULL configuration also recorded lower memory latency than a G.SKILL DDR5-6000 CL26 memory kit running a standard AMD EXPO profile, which achieved 74.9ns. These results highlight the potential benefits of optimized memory sub-timings, demonstrating that lower overall memory latency can be achieved outside of increasing memory speed or tightening primary CAS latency.
^ Requires overclocking/BIOS adjustments. Maximum speed and performance depends on system components, including motherboard and CPU.
The tests were conducted using an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor and GIGABYTE B850 AORUS ELITE WIFI7 ICE motherboard. Actual performance may vary depending on hardware configurations, BIOS settings, and memory profiles.
Limited-Time Combo Savings
The featured combo deals start at $1,029.99 USD, with savings of up to $248.99 USD compared to the listed individual component prices. The limited-time offers are available through October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time, subject to availability and Newegg's promotional terms.
For more information and to explore the available combo deals, visit the G.SKILL AMD EXPO ULL promotional page at Newegg.

articles.title: Jusqu'à 6 000 lumens et 10 000:1 de contraste : XGIMI dévoile ses vidéoprojecteurs les plus ambitieux
articles.text:
Avec ses nouveaux Horizon 30 Pro, Max et Ultra Max, XGIMI franchit un cap dans la vidéoprojection domestique. Ces trois projecteurs laser RGB promettent une luminosité grimpant à 6 000 lumens ISO, un contraste natif jusqu'à 10 000:1 et une véritable restitution 4K à 120 Hz.
XGIMI poursuit sa montée en gamme à l'occasion de sa nouvelle série. Après avoir popularisé les vidéoprojecteurs tout-en-un faciles à installer, le constructeur s'attaque désormais plus en profondeur au marché du home cinéma exigeant. Sa nouvelle série Horizon 30 veut lier forte luminosité, contraste élevé, souplesse d'installation et performances gaming.
Trois modèles, trois niveaux de luminosité et contraste
Succédant à la série Horizon 20, les Horizon 30 Pro, Max et Ultra Max font leur apparition au catalogue du fabricant chinois. Une fois n'est pas coutume chez XGIMI, ils utilisent tous les trois une source lumineuse triple laser RGB, associant directement les trois couleurs primaires.
XGIMI annonce 110 % de couverture de l'espace BT.2020 et une précision colorimétrique avec un Delta E inférieur à 0,8. Des performances ambitieuses, que nous aurons prochainement l'occasion de vérifier.
Si le Horizon 30 Pro offre jusqu'à 4 800 lumens ISO, et un contraste annoncé de 8 000:1, son grand frère le 30 Max, annnonce monter à 5 300 lumens ISO pour un contraste de 9 000:1. Le cador de la gamme, le HORIZON 30 Ultra Max annonce quant à lui une luminosité maximale de 6 000 lumens ISO pour un contraste natif grimpant à 10 000:1.
Enfin, il faut bien accepter quelques compromis. Si l'utilisateur souhaite privilégier la fidélité colorimétrique, en mode cinéma, le Pro descend à 2 300 lumens ISO, le Max à 2 400 et l'Ultra Max à 3 000. En mode lumineux, ces valeurs atteignent respectivement 2 800, 2 970 et 3 500 lumens.
Un double iris pour des noirs profonds
L'autre promesse majeure concerne le contraste. XGIMI revendique jusqu'à 10 000:1 en natif grâce à son système Dual Intelligent Iris. Le fabricant présente notamment jusqu'à cinq ouvertures réglables, de f/2.0 à f/7.0. Cette technologie permet d'adapter la quantité de lumière projetée à l'environnement. L'ouverture maximale fera son travail dans une pièce éclairée, en adoptant une fermeture progressive pour privilégier les tons de noir dans une pièce obscure.
Le fabricant ne précise toutefois pas dans quelles conditions les contrastes natifs ont été mesurés.
De la véritable 4K à 120 Hz
Le constructeur indique que son architecture repose sur deux contrôleurs Texas Instruments DLPC8545. L'intérêt d'une telle architecture est de permettre la restitution effective de la 4K Ultra HD à 120 Hz, plutôt que de simplement accepter le signal entrant à cette fréquence pour le convertir.
Pour les amateurs de cinéma, le 120 Hz présente également un avantage : les films, généralement tournés à 24 images par seconde, peuvent être affichés sans saccades supplémentaires. Chaque image est reproduite cinq fois à intervalles réguliers, ce qui permet de respecter la fluidité d'origine du film, sans avoir besoin d'inventer des images intermédiaires.
Côté audio, le système est assuré par Harman Kardon, comme à l'accoutumée chez XGIMI. La gamme Horizon 30 intègre deux haut-parleurs de 12 watts chacun. Une barre de son peut être la bienvenue pour améliorer l'expérience audio.
Zoom optique et Lens Shift : de vrais arguments pour les cinéphiles
Les Horizon 30 adoptent un objectif X-Master Red Ring Lens, avec une transmission lumineuse annoncée de 99,6 % et un traitement optique à 14 couches.
Surtout, le zoom optique offre un rapport de projection de 1,2:1 à 1,5:1. Une image de 100 pouces peut ainsi être obtenue avec entre 2,66 et 3,32 mètres de recul, sans recourir à une réduction numérique.
Le Lens Shift annoncé atteint environ 50 % horizontalement et environ 130 % verticalement, selon la convention de mesure du constructeur.
XGIMI évoque également six mémoires de position permettant à l'appareil de se rappeler des paramètres de zoom, mise au point et décalage optique. Un atout pour passer d'un programme 16:9 à un film au format CinemaScope 2,35:1 ou 21:9.
Gaming : 240 Hz, FreeSync Premium et 1 ms annoncé
Un vidéoprojecteur, c'est très bien pour regarder des films, mais ça peut également être intéressant pour jouer, et XGIMI n'oublie pas les gamers avec cette nouvelle série Horizon 30.
Nonobstant la 4K UHD à 120 Hz, XGIMI annonce un mode 1080p à 240 Hz pour plus de fluidité, mais également la compatibilité VRR, AMD FreeSync Premium et ALLM.
Le constructeur se targue même d'une latence de seulement 1 ms en 1080p à 240 Hz, mais ne donne pas d'information concernant cette donnée quand l'appareil est en 4K Ultra HD.
Par ailleurs, les trois modèles prennent en charge les technologies Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10+ et HLG, avec un traitement dynamique des contenus HDR.
Quels tarifs pour la série Horizon 30 ?
Les Horizon 30 Pro et Max sont annoncés pour le 1er novembre 2026. Quant à la version Ultra Max, cette dernière arrivera un peu plus tard, le 11 novembre selon le fabricant.
Le Horizon 30 Pro sera commercialisé au prix de 2 499 €, il est disponible en précommande à 1 999 €.
Côté Horizon 30 Max, ce dernier sera commercialisé à 2 799€, il est disponible à la précommande au prix de 2 499 €. Enfin, le Horizon 30 Ultra Max sera vendu au tarif public conseillé de 3 299 €, en précommande, son tarif chute à 2 999 €. Pour ce dernier, deux paires de lunettes 3D sont offertes, ainsi qu'un support au choix, pour installer l'appareil.
Quel avenir pour XGIMI ? Quelles gammes changeront en 2027 ?
Le constructeur nous a teasé une nouvelle catégorie de produits à venir pour le courant de l'année 2027. XGIMI veut "raconter l'histoire autour de la lumière et de la technologie laser", nous indique Julien Labbé, directeur marketing Europe de la marque, sans laisser fuiter plus de détails.
Les lunettes lancées en ce début d'année, les MemoMind, verront une V2 arriver sur le marché en janvier 2027. Par ailleurs, le fabricant entend bien renforcer son positionnement haut de gamme, avec deux nouveaux appareils dans la gamme Titan en 2027. Pour la fin de l'année prochaine, on peut également s'attendre à un renouvellement de la gamme MoGo, avec l'arrivée de la série MoGo 5.
Les prochaines nouveautés du constructeur ne seront pas annoncées avant le CES de Las Vegas, qui se déroulera du 6 au 9 janvier 2027.

articles.title: Compras directas y tarjetas guardadas: WhatsApp prepara un gestor de pagos global para Android e iOS
articles.text:
WhatsApp prepara una sección de Pagos para guardar tarjetas, datos de facturación e información de envío dentro de Android e iOS. La función permitiría completar compras directamente desde la aplicación y administrar los métodos de pago vinculados a las plataformas de Meta, aunque todavía permanece en desarrollo y no está disponible de forma general.
La aplicación ya ofrece pagos en India, Brasil, Singapur y México, pero el nuevo selector de países incluye mercados donde esa herramienta no opera actualmente, como Australia, Austria, Canadá, Alemania, Italia, Países Bajos y Estados Unidos.
WhatsApp prepara la misma herramienta en Android y iPhone
La función apareció primero en el desarrollo de la versión beta para iOS 26.33.10.70. Allí se detectó una nueva sección destinada a reunir tarjetas, direcciones y otros datos necesarios para efectuar compras sin salir de la aplicación.
Ahora, WhatsApp trabaja en una versión equivalente para Android. La novedad fue identificada en la beta 2.26.43.7, distribuida mediante Google Play Store. El apartado se integrará dentro de los ajustes de la aplicación y permitirá gestionar los métodos de pago asociados a la cuenta.
La coincidencia entre los desarrollos de Android e iOS sugiere que WhatsApp busca crear una infraestructura común para ambas plataformas. Sin embargo, la compañía no ha confirmado que los pagos vayan a habilitarse de inmediato en nuevos países ni ha comunicado una fecha para su lanzamiento general.
La presencia de un listado de países más amplio que el de los mercados actuales puede responder a una preparación técnica para futuras compras, aunque todavía no constituye una confirmación de expansión internacional.
Las tarjetas se guardarían desde el Centro de cuentas
Al entrar en la futura pantalla de Pagos, el usuario encontrará un botón para añadir un método de pago. Esa acción abrirá el Centro de cuentas, donde será posible registrar la tarjeta preferida para compras posteriores.
WhatsApp señala que la información de pago se cifra y se almacena de manera separada de los datos del perfil. El objetivo consiste en que las personas puedan utilizar la tarjeta guardada para completar adquisiciones con mayor rapidez dentro de las aplicaciones de Meta.
La función también incluirá una sección para almacenar información de envío. Allí se podrán añadir o modificar:
- Dirección de correo electrónico.
- Número de teléfono.
- Dirección de entrega.
- Datos de facturación.
- Método de pago preferido.
La información permitirá rellenar de forma automática los datos de compra y envío. De esta manera, el usuario no tendría que escribir la misma dirección o número de contacto cada vez que realice una adquisición desde una conversación, un negocio o un servicio integrado.
El gestor permitirá descargar y eliminar datos de pago
La futura sección no solo servirá para añadir tarjetas. También ofrecerá herramientas de control sobre la información almacenada. Los usuarios podrán descargar una copia de sus datos de pago, incluidas las tarjetas registradas y los detalles de envío.
Esta opción puede resultar útil para revisar qué información conserva la aplicación. Además, cuando una persona elimine sus datos de pago, podrá utilizar la descarga para comprobar cuáles de esos elementos ya fueron borrados de los servidores.
La posibilidad de solicitar una copia añade una vía de transparencia sobre los datos vinculados a las compras. En un servicio que reúne mensajes, contactos y potencialmente información financiera, la gestión de los permisos y del contenido almacenado será un aspecto relevante.
La configuración permitirá actualizar los datos de envío cuando sea necesario. Si cambia una dirección, un número de teléfono o una tarjeta, el usuario podrá modificar esos elementos desde el mismo apartado.
El desarrollo de un gestor de pagos en Android e iOS puede facilitar una futura llegada a más territorios, pero WhatsApp no ha anunciado un plan concreto. Por ahora, la función está en una etapa de preparación y se prevé que llegue primero a algunos probadores beta.
La herramienta todavía no puede utilizarse ni aparece para todos los usuarios. Su despliegue dependerá de futuras actualizaciones, pruebas técnicas y, en caso de una expansión internacional, de los requisitos de cada mercado.

articles.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
articles.text:
26,400 credentials that developers left in public code on Gitee, a Chinese code-hosting service, still worked when a researcher tested them. Anyone who copied one from that code could have used it.
Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann found them by scanning 7.25 million public Gitee repositories and reported the results on October 28. Most were keys for cloud and AI services, led by 9,473 Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pairs.
Zimmermann sent the vendors with the most exposed keys a list of their credentials, but he did not contact the developers who leaked them. When he published, he had not confirmed that any of the reported credentials had been revoked. So anyone who has pushed a key to a public Gitee repository cannot assume it has been revoked.
The scan ran for about a month, but Zimmermann did not provide the dates, so it is unclear how long ago the credentials were tested. He also did not say whether anyone else had used them.
He ran two secret scanners, TruffleHog and Kingfisher, over every repository. Both tried each credential against the service that issued it and kept only those that worked, he wrote.
The scanners read each repository's full commit history. A key that a developer later removed from the code could still be found and counted there.
The 26,400 figure counts each credential once, regardless of how many repositories it appeared in. By commit date, 12,242 of the credentials came from 2025, nearly half the total. Some dated to the late 2000s.
What Was Exposed
After the Alibaba Cloud keys, the largest groups were 3,805 YouTube API keys, 3,170 DeepSeek keys, 1,489 keys for Zhipu's BigModel AI platform, and 1,348 OpenAI keys. Smaller numbers were found for GitHub, AWS, Google Cloud and Google's Gemini.
One of the credentials was "an active organization-admin credential for a major enterprise AI platform," Zimmermann wrote. He did not name the platform or say what the credential could reach.
What a working key lets someone do depends on the service. OpenAI says that a compromised key allows another person to use the account's quota without the owner's consent. That can cause "data loss, unexpected charges," a used-up monthly quota, and interrupted API access.
A YouTube API key is a Google Cloud API key that identifies a project, Google says. Without API restrictions, such a key can be used with every API that accepts Google Cloud keys.
What to Do If You Committed Keys
Treat any key that has ever been in a public Gitee repository as exposed, and revoke it at the provider. Deleting a key from the code or rewriting the repository's history does not revoke it, as noted by TruffleHog's maker, Truffle Security.
- Alibaba Cloud: create a new AccessKey pair, switch your apps to it, then disable and delete the old pair. Check for unexpected charges and for resources created or deleted that you did not need, Alibaba Cloud's leak response plan says. ActionTrail shows the key's API calls for the last 90 days, but data operations in services such as OSS and SLS have to be checked in each service's own logs.
- Google and YouTube API keys: rotate the key, which creates a new key with the same restrictions, update your apps to use it, then delete the old key. Add API restrictions so the key works only with the APIs you need.
- OpenAI: rotate the key immediately from the API Keys page, as OpenAI advises, and set spend limits to help limit charges from a leaked key.
Two Scanners, Different Results
MongoDB makes Kingfisher, and Zimmermann's post was developed with its Kingfisher team.
In this scan, TruffleHog found 12,737 credentials that worked, and Kingfisher found 14,664, but only 1,001 were found by both. Each tool alone found about half of the total.
TruffleHog found almost all of the Alibaba Cloud keys. Kingfisher found all 1,489 BigModel keys, because TruffleHog has no detector for Zhipu's keys, Zimmermann wrote.
Teams that rely on a single scanner should verify its detectors against the services they use.
Gitee and Other Code Hosts
China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology chose Gitee in 2020 as the base for a national open-source code-hosting platform.
Gitee's public API is limited, and a 2021 attempt to study leaked credentials on the site gave up because of it.
Gitee's rate, 3.64 working credentials per 1,000 repositories scanned, is higher than the rates from earlier scans of GitLab (3.11) and Bitbucket (2.39). Those scans used only TruffleHog, Zimmermann wrote.
Based on TruffleHog's results alone, Gitee's rate is 1.76, but that count excludes services TruffleHog does not cover, such as Zhipu. So neither figure shows which platform leaks more.

articles.title: ‘Bad actor’ cyberattack on FEC obscures political spending by donors and SuperPACs days before US midterm elections
articles.text:
‘Bad actor’ cyberattack on FEC obscures political spending by donors and SuperPACs days before US midterm elections
Millions of dollars in donations may have gone undeclared
- The FEC was hit by a cyberattack on Monday that took filing systems offline
- 24 and 48 hour donation reports couldn't be filed for almost 41 hours
- The attack has been blamed on a "bad actor", but no other details have been released
Just days before voters head to the polls in what is the most significant voting occasion in Donald Trump’s second term, the Federal Election Commission went offline for almost 41 hours to contain a cyberattack.
During that time, there was a window for big donors and SuperPACs to fund campaigns without being able to submit 24 and 48 hour funding reports, likely leaving millions of dollars undeclared.
Campaign and finance watchdogs have voiced outrage about the lack of transparency into funding at a critical time in the election cycle, especially as there are no caps on how much SuperPACs can spend to help or hinder candidates.
Funding transparency goes dark
An email sent to campaign compliance firms on Monday said that FEC services were taken down after a “bad actor” attempted to gain access to systems. Outside of this, there is little information to go on regarding who would be responsible or what their motives might be.
According to OpenSecrets research director Brendan Glavin, who spoke to Reuters, around $50 million was spent per day in the lead up to the FEC outage, with $250 spent on October 20 alone.
Disclosure delayed is disclosure denied,” Hilary Braseth, executive director of nonpartisan campaign finance watchdog OpenSecrets, said in a statement during the outage. “When hundreds of millions of dollars in outside money flood political airwaves in the final days before an election, transparency is not an optional luxury, it is a fundamental public safeguard.”
As would be expected, numerous conspiracy theories surrounding the FEC outage have been floated online. Many suggested the outage would give donors a window to funnel millions of dollars of undeclared funding into candidates needing a last minute boost.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“We didn't have access to the last-minute spending, which is really ramped up as the election draws nearer,” Molly White, a crypto and Big Tech political spending tracker, told Reuters. “We have no visibility into that when the filing systems are down. It's pretty devastating this close to the election”
“It's hard to say with any real information that that's what happened, but it's certainly I think where people's minds go very quickly,” she concluded.
SuperPACs back pro-AI candidates
AI has been a hot topic ahead of the midterm elections, which take place on November 3. The huge buildout of AI data centers across the US - and the billions spent to fund it - have been met with opposition by the majority of Americans.
To counter the outrage and swing the vote in favor of AI, numerous SuperPACS have spent millions of dollars to support campaigns of pro-AI candidates and millions more to harm those critical of the technology.
President Trump has pushed an administrative policy of AI at any cost, claiming that the US economy and national security depends on continuing AI superiority over rivals such as China. To that end, the estimates on the total AI infrastructural spending range between $2.8 trillion by 2030 to $10.3 trillion by 2032, so there is certainly a lot riding on this election.
With many states enacting or considering moratoriums on AI data centers, anti-AI candidates could scupper the Trump administration's hopes for being an AI powerhouse.

Benedict is a Senior Security Writer at TechRadar Pro, where he has specialized in covering the intersection of geopolitics, cyber-warfare, and business security.
Benedict provides detailed analysis on state-sponsored threat actors, APT groups, and the protection of critical national infrastructure, with his reporting bridging the gap between technical threat intelligence and B2B security strategy.
Benedict holds an MA (Distinction) in Security, Intelligence, and Diplomacy from the University of Buckingham Centre for Security and Intelligence Studies (BUCSIS), with his specialization providing him with a robust academic framework for deconstructing complex international conflicts and intelligence operations, and the ability to translate intricate security data into actionable insights.

articles.title: Biostar Introduces the EdgeComp MS-U320 Fanless Edge AI System
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Biostar Introduces the EdgeComp MS-U320 Fanless Edge AI System
BIOSTAR, a leading manufacturer of edge AI solution, IPC systems, motherboards, graphics cards, and storage devices, today introduced the EdgeComp MS-U320, a compact fanless edge AI system powered by the Intel Core 5 320 processor (Wildcat Lake). Designed for equipment manufacturers and system integrators, the MS-U320 combines on-site data processing, light AI computing, and industrial connectivity for applications in industrial automation, smart manufacturing, industrial IoT, smart retail, and smart infrastructure.
The MS-U320 features an onboard Intel Core 5 320 processor with six cores, clock speeds of up to 4.6 GHz, a 15 W TDP, and integrated Intel graphics. A single DDR5-6400 SO-DIMM slot supports up to 64 GB of memory, while the integrated CPU, GPU and NPU deliver up to 40 TOPS of AI performance. This combination supports local data processing and light AI workloads without requiring a separate accelerator.For industrial connectivity, the system provides four COM ports: two RS232 ports and two ports configurable for RS232, RS422, or RS485 communication. Dual 2.5GbE LAN ports, powered by Intel I226-LM and I226-V controllers, provide connections to industrial devices and networks. Two USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports and four USB 2.0 ports support peripheral connectivity. Onboard audio uses an ALC897 codec with an ALC105 amplifier with separate headphone and microphone jacks.
Display connectivity includes HDMI 2.1, supporting resolutions of up to 3840 × 2160 at 60 Hz, and DisplayPort 1.4, supporting resolutions of up to 4096 × 2160 at 60 Hz.
Three M.2 slots provide storage and wireless expansion options. The M.2 Key-M slot supports 2242/2280 NVMe SSDs through a PCIe 4.0 x2 interface. The M.2 Key-B slot supports 3042/3052 4G/5G modules via PCIe 4.0 x1 and USB 3.2, plus a SIM slot for cellular connectivity. The M.2 Key-E 2230 slot supports Wi-Fi and Bluetooth modules via PCIe 4.0 x1 and USB 2.0.
Housed in a 167 × 135 × 60 mm chassis, the MS-U320 features a fanless design. Its wide-range 9-24 V DC input accommodates various power sources, and it includes a 90 W power adapter. The system supports operating temperatures from -20°C to 50°C and humidity levels from 5% to 90%. It is compatible with Windows 11 64-bit, Windows 11 IoT Enterprise 24H2, and Ubuntu 24.04. Optional DIN rail, wall mount, and VESA mount kits provide additional installation options.
The EdgeComp MS-U320 combines serial connectivity, high-speed networking, wireless expansion, and light edge AI processing in a compact, fanless platform, giving system integrators flexible deployment options for industrial and smart infrastructure projects.

articles.title: Piratage à Strasbourg : les données de 230 000 clients de la CTS compromises
articles.text:
La Compagnie des transports strasbourgeois (CTS) a été victime d’un vol de données touchant environ 230 000 comptes clients. Si les mots de passe et les coordonnées bancaires n’ont pas été compromis, les informations dérobées pourraient faciliter des tentatives d’hameçonnage. Méfiance donc.
Officialisée hier 28 octobre, la cyberattaque concerne près de 40 % des comptes clients de la CTS. Une fuite de données qui a conduit l’opérateur de transports strasbourgeois à prévenir les personnes concernées par courriel. Comme le rapporte Ici.fr, l’incident remonte à la mi-octobre et la faille exploitée a depuis été corrigée.
230 000 comptes clients concernés par le piratage
Dans le détail, les pirates ont pu récupérer plusieurs informations personnelles telles que le nom, le prénom, la date de naissance, l’adresse postale ainsi que l’identifiant Badgéo associé au compte client. En revanche, la CTS assure que les mots de passe et les données bancaires ne font pas partie des informations exfiltrées.
Le directeur général de la CTS, Emmanuel Auneau, précise que l’attaque s’est produite dans la nuit du dimanche 18 au lundi 19 octobre. L’entreprise annonce avoir détecté une activité anormale, caractérisée par une sollicitation particulièrement élevée de sa base de données.
Le responsable tient également à préciser la méthode employée par les pirates : « Nos serveurs ne sont pas altérés, les hackeurs ne se sont pas infiltrés dans notre système informatique, ils ont utilisé une API pour voler des données. La faille est depuis corrigée. ».
Les assaillants ont donc exploité une interface permettant à différents logiciels de communiquer avec le site, sans nécessairement pénétrer dans l’ensemble du système informatique de l’opérateur.
Des risques de phishing pour les clients de la CTS
Si aucune donnée bancaire ni aucun mot de passe n’ont été dérobés, l’incident n’est pas pour autant sans conséquence pour les usagers. Les informations récupérées peuvent en effet servir à concevoir des messages frauduleux particulièrement convaincants (et donc dangereux) en reprenant des éléments personnels pour inspirer confiance à leurs destinataires.
Un faux courriel évoquant un abonnement Badgéo, une régularisation ou encore un remboursement sont autant de scénarios qui pourraient sembler parfaitement légitimes. Tout récemment, c’est Engie qui a tenu à prévenir ses clients après un vol de données personnelles.
Emmanuel Auneau indique : « Je suis vraiment désolé pour nos clients mais ils risquent au pire d’être importunés par des mails indésirables ».
La prudence reste donc de mise, et la CTS rappelle qu’elle ne demande pas à ses clients d’effectuer une transaction financière ou de communiquer leurs coordonnées bancaires par courriel. Comme toujours, en cas de message suspect, on évite soigneusement les liens proposés et on vérifie directement les informations auprès de l’opérateur.
Une plainte va être déposée après la fuite de données
La CTS confirme aussi avoir stoppé l’exfiltration dès la détection de l’incident et renforcé la sécurité de son site Internet. Une déclaration a été effectuée auprès de la Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés (CNIL), tandis qu’une plainte doit être déposée auprès du tribunal de Strasbourg.
L’entreprise ne sait pas encore si les données dérobées ont été revendues ou diffusées, et il faudra donc surveiller les éventuelles conséquences de cette fuite, alors que la protection des informations personnelles représente un enjeu majeur pour les services numériques du quotidien.
Ce n’est pas la première fois que la CTS est confrontée à un incident de sécurité, puisqu’il y a deux ans, certains comptes clients avaient déjà fait l’objet d’accès frauduleux. Cette fois, l’ampleur de l’exfiltration est nettement plus importante, avec environ 230 000 comptes concernés.

articles.title: Colombia tiene ahora un centro de ciberseguridad que detecta ataques en menos de 10 minutos y los resuelve 5 veces más rápido
articles.text:
Indra lanzó en Colombia un Centro de Operaciones de Ciberseguridad (SOC) con inteligencia artificial (IA) para detectar incidentes críticos como ciberataques en menos de 10 minutos y reducir hasta cinco veces los tiempos de investigación y resolución.
El centro incorpora automatización y agentes de IA para clasificar alertas, identificar comportamientos anómalos y priorizar los eventos que requieren intervención, con un alcance que cubre a Colombia y Latinoamérica.
La operación mantiene supervisión humana durante el análisis y la contención de incidentes, según explicó Edwin Walteros, director de ciberseguridad de Indra para Colombia, Ecuador, Centroamérica y el Caribe.
Cómo opera el centro de ciberseguridad
El SOC reúne herramientas de monitoreo que reciben señales desde distintos sistemas de una organización. A partir de esos datos, identifica accesos inusuales, intentos de intrusión, movimientos sospechosos dentro de una red y otros indicios que pueden anticipar un ataque.
La operación busca cubrir el ciclo completo de un incidente: detección, análisis, respuesta, contención y recuperación. El modelo contempla la protección de espacios de tecnologías de la información y de tecnologías operativas, que controlan procesos físicos en sectores como energía, transporte, salud e infraestructura.
Cómo la IA potencia la ciberseguridad
La inteligencia artificial permite filtrar un volumen elevado de alertas y entregar a los analistas una primera evaluación sobre el nivel de riesgo. Los agentes automatizados contrastan eventos, identifican patrones y ayudan a diferenciar una actividad rutinaria de una posible amenaza que requiere una intervención inmediata.
Walteros explicó que los tiempos de revisión se redujeron frente a métodos convencionales. “Generalmente, el tiempo promedio de análisis de una alerta se hacía más o menos entre 25 y 30 minutos. Estamos pasando a hablar de una alerta bien validada entre cuatro y cinco minutos”.
Por qué es clave la rapidez al momento de detectar un incidente de ciberseguridad
La velocidad es uno de los factores que determina la dimensión de un incidente. Un atacante que permanece dentro de una red sin ser detectado puede obtener contraseñas, copiar información, desplazarse entre sistemas, alterar procesos o bloquear archivos y servicios.
“Esta es una competencia de tiempo. Entre más rápido logremos detectar, más rápido garantizamos que no se expanda un ataque dentro de una compañía”, dijo Walteros.
El ejecutivo aclaró que la IA participa en el análisis y la priorización de eventos, aunque los especialistas mantienen la supervisión de las decisiones relacionadas con la respuesta.
Cuáles son los ciberataques más comunes que experimentan usuarios y empresas
El phishing continúa entre las técnicas más utilizadas. “El phishing, que es ese correo malicioso, sigue siendo el top en todos los tipos de ataques”, señaló Walteros. El ataque aprovecha un punto vulnerable que no depende exclusivamente de las defensas tecnológicas: la decisión del usuario que recibe el mensaje.
Según explicó Walteros, los avances en inteligencia artificial mejoraron la redacción, la apariencia y la personalización de mensajes fraudulentos, lo que dificulta reconocerlos a simple vista.
Asimismo, el ransomware mantiene presencia entre las amenazas que enfrentan las organizaciones. En estos casos, los atacantes cifran información o bloquean sistemas y luego exigen un pago.
A ello se suman fraudes que utilizan clonación de voz y videos manipulados para suplantar a directivos, empleados o familiares y obtener transferencias, información reservada o autorizaciones internas.
Qué sectores están más expuestos a ciberataques
El sector financiero continúa entre los objetivos más atractivos por el volumen de recursos e información que administra. A la vez, los ataques contra infraestructuras críticas han ampliado el riesgo a sectores como energía, salud y transporte.
“Hoy en día son todos los sectores”, afirmó Walteros al referirse a los objetivos de los ciberdelincuentes. “Paralizar un hospital es una problemática que pasa más allá del mundo digital. No simplemente la pérdida de una información, sino que puede terminar en afectación de vidas humanas”.

articles.title: Cisco Patches Actively Exploited ASA and FTD VPN Flaw That Can Crash Firewalls
articles.text:
Cisco has released patches to address a high-severity security flaw in Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software that it said has been exploited in the wild.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-76418, is rated 8.6 on the CVSS scoring system. Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
According to Cisco, the issue is rooted in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of ASA and FTD software.
"This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group," it said in a Wednesday advisory. "An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition."
The network equipment major said it became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability in October 2026, but did not share any specifics as to when the attacks began, who is behind them, and the scale of the efforts.
Fixes for the flaw are available in the following versions -
- 
    Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software Release
    
  - 9.16 and earlier - Fixed in 9.16.4.104
  - 9.18 - Fixed in 9.18.4.96
  - 9.20 - Fixed in 9.20.4.50
  - 9.22 - Fixed in 9.22.3.200
  - 9.23 - Fixed in 9.23.1.48
  - 9.24 - Fixed in 9.24.1.27 and 9.24.10.1
- 
    Cisco Secure FTD Software Release
    
  - 7.0 and earlier - Fixed in 7.0.11
  - 7.2 - Fixed in 7.2.13
  - 7.4 - Fixed in 7.4.9
  - 7.6 - Fixed in 7.6.7
  - 7.7 - Fixed in 7.7.14
  - 10.0 - Fixed in 10.0.3
  - 10.1 - Fixed in 10.1.1
Cisco also noted that the vulnerability affects Cisco devices if the following conditions are met -
- They are running a vulnerable release of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software or Cisco Secure FTD Software.
- The SSL remote access VPN login service is reachable.
- Secondary authentication is configured in the tunnel group scope.
"If tunnel-group-list enable is configured, check all tunnel groups, including the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup, for secondary-authentication-server-group," Cisco said.
"If tunnel-group-list enable is absent or has been removed using the no tunnel-group-list enable command, check the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup, for secondary-authentication-server-group because disabling the group list does not remove exposure when that default group uses secondary authentication."
As a temporary mitigation, the company is recommending that customers turn off the tunnel group list if DefaultWEBVPNGroup does not use secondary authentication, or disable secondary authentication on any user-configured tunnel group list or on the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup.
"On Cisco Secure FTD Software, review the deployed remote access VPN policy and the resulting device running configuration in Cisco Secure FMC Software or Cisco Secure FDM," Cisco said. "A successful VPN login is not required to reach the affected processing path."
The disclosure comes as Cisco revealed that a sophisticated advanced persistent threat (APT) actor tracked as UAT-11473 weaponized CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to affected systems.
The activity, which has targeted space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research sectors, is assessed to share infrastructure overlaps with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train covert network.
"UAT-11473 then installed a custom malware framework we track as 'KeyDrift' consisting of multiple components [like PolyFlame and LittleFilch] geared towards collecting sensitive keying information, acting as backdoors and intermediate command-and-control (C2) hosts," Cisco Talos said.
"The framework is designed to provide long-term persistent access and automated exfiltration of sensitive keying material. KeyDrift operates inside SD-WAN control-plane processes and is capable of intercepting decrypted control traffic, extracting control-session metadata and data-plane keying material, and staging or transmitting the collected material using encrypted records."

articles.title: Virgin Galactic présente enfin son vaisseau ultra futuriste, le dernier grand espoir du tourisme spatial
articles.text:
Virgin Galactic vient de baptiser le premier vaisseau de sa nouvelle génération : Apeiron. Alors que le tourisme spatial est à l’arrêt, c’est désormais sur lui que reposent les espoirs du secteur. Encore faut-il être en mesure de répondre aux attentes…
Cela fait plus de deux ans que Virgin Galactic n’a plus emmené de passagers aux portes de l’espace. Son dernier vol, assuré par VSS Unity, remonte à juin 2024, et la compagnie a depuis tout misé sur une nouvelle génération de vaisseaux, baptisée Delta. Mais en août, elle a dû repousser le premier vol commercial de ce nouvel appareil, prévu fin 2026, à février 2027. De quoi laisser planer le doute sur le calendrier.
Apeiron, un vaisseau enfin baptisé et prêt pour les essais
L’entreprise vient enfin de franchir une étape symbolique. Ce mercredi 28 octobre, elle a dévoilé le nom du premier vaisseau de sa gamme flambant neuve : Apeiron, un mot du grec ancien qui signifie « l’illimité ». Un choix issu d’un vote public auquel des milliers de personnes ont participé, depuis 83 pays et six continents. Apeiron l’a emporté face à Horizon, Explorer et Ascend, les quatre finalistes retenus parmi 276 idées proposées par les salariés.
Il « illustre l’ambition des vols spatiaux habités et les perspectives qu’ils ouvrent pour l’humanité », assure Michael Colglazier, P.-D.G de Virgin Galactic. L’appareil pourra accueillir six personnes pour un vol suborbital qui franchira la ligne de Kármán, à 100 kilomètres d’altitude, et leur laissera quelques minutes d’apesanteur avec la Terre en toile de fond. À terme, la société espère faire voler chaque aéronef jusqu’à huit fois par mois.
Ainsi, Apeiron, fixé sous son avion porteur Eve, vient de quitter son usine de Mesa, en Arizona, pour rejoindre l’État voisin du Nouveau-Mexique. Les ingénieurs y finaliseront l’avionique et le logiciel de vol avant une vague d’essais au sol, des vols captifs sous Eve, un largage, puis un premier vol propulsé au-delà de 80 kilomètres d’altitude. Concrètement, le chemin à parcourir est encore long avant de pouvoir accueillir les premiers clients.
Virgin Galactic a le champ libre
Virgin Galactic s’apprête à reprendre du service dans un secteur très prometteur il y a quelques années, et désormais abandonné par quasi tout le monde. Aux États-Unis, aucune mission de tourisme spatial n’a eu lieu depuis dix mois, lorsque Blue Origin a décidé de mettre New Shepard en pause pour se concentrer sur New Glenn et la Lune. SpaceX, de son côté, a effectué sa dernière mission touristique avec Crew Dragon en avril 2025, et concentre aujourd’hui toute son énergie sur Starship et l’IA.
Une opportunité en or pour l’entreprise de Richard Branson, qui vise un premier vol commercial au début du deuxième trimestre 2027. Une échéance à prendre, encore une fois, avec prudence. En parallèle, un second vaisseau Delta est déjà en construction pour épauler Apeiron. Car les candidats ne manquent pas : environ 675 clients attendent toujours leur place, dont plus de cent commencent déjà leur préparation.
Mais il va aussi falloir démontrer que ce modèle est rentable. Les appareils devront ainsi être irréprochables et surtout, capables d’enchaîner les vols.
Sources : Ars Technica, Space.com, Virgin Galactic

articles.title: Audio-Technica Introduces ATH-M50xSTS-WL StreamSet Wireless Headset
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Audio-Technica Introduces ATH-M50xSTS-WL StreamSet Wireless Headset
Audio-Technica today announced the release of its ATH-M50xSTS-WL StreamSet wireless streaming headset, the first wireless model in the StreamSet lineup. Designed for streamers, content creators, and gamers, the headset combines the studio sound of the ATH-M50x professional monitor headphones with microphone technology based on Audio-Technica's 20 Series. 
The ATH-M50xSTS-WL brings low-latency, interference-resistant 2.4 GHz digital wireless connectivity to the StreamSet range, expanding the lineup beyond its XLR and USB models. An included USB transceiver enables plug-and-play use with PCs and compatible gaming consoles, giving users the freedom of a cable-free streaming experience.The headset features a cardioid condenser microphone on a flexible boom arm for clear, detailed vocal reproduction. The boom arm positions the microphone close to the user's mouth to help reject background noise and flips up to quickly mute the microphone. Sidetone circuitry lets users hear their own voice in the headphones for a more natural, conversational experience. 
To further improve voice capture, the headset includes adaptive noise reduction with two selectable levels. The function continuously monitors audio input to prioritize the user's voice-over ambient sounds such as PC fans and air conditioners, and can be switched on or off at the earcup. 
The ATH-M50xSTS-WL uses the same 45 mm large-aperture drivers found in the ATH-M50x, with rare earth magnets and copper-clad aluminium wire voice coils. The drivers deliver exceptional clarity throughout an extended frequency range, with deep, accurate bass response. Two types of interchangeable earpads are included: standard M50x earpads that emphasize audio quality and sound isolation, and breathable mesh earpads for comfort during long streaming or gaming sessions. 
With up to 24 hours of continuous use on a full charge, the ATH-M50xSTS-WL supports all-day streaming. The included USB cable allows users to continue using the headset while charging and also supports optional wired audio operation. 
The ATH-M50xSTS-WL StreamSet will be available beginning October 28, 2026, at a U.S. Retail price of $299.

articles.title: Are you still piloting?
articles.text:
There's no shortage of enthusiasm for artificial intelligence. Organizations across every sector are investing heavily, experimenting, launching proof of concepts, and finding ways to turn the latest developments into real business value.
However, there's a growing disconnect between experimentation and execution. For all the discussions of AI transforming the way we work, many AI projects never progress beyond the pilot stage. It's a familiar story. The proof of concept delivers promising results, the business case adds up, and everything looks like it's heading in the right direction.
Yet somewhere along the way the project hits a bump on the road. This can look like costs beginning to rise, confidence starting to waver, integration with existing legacy systems proving more complicated than expected, and approvals taking longer than anticipated.
VP of Insight AI at Insight.
What started out as an exciting project slowly loses its momentum. As a result, the AI initiative ends up stuck in limbo. The reason is that running a successful AI pilot and successful AI implementation are two very different things. Transitioning from a controlled environment with governed variables to a production environment brings a new set of challenges: security, governance, culture, skills, integration, and readiness.
Unfortunately, this challenge is not uncommon. Research shows that 71% of organizations remain in the pilot or proof-of-concept phase of AI transformation, highlighting just how difficult it is to turn early promise into a business reality.
This limbo is what many organizations are now experiencing: the AI implementation gap. It's the space between proving that AI can work and deploying it at scale in a way that delivers measurable value. For today's technology leaders, bridging that gap has become one of the defining challenges of AI adoption. The pressure to move beyond experimentation is growing, but doing so requires more than just increasing investment or pushing strong proof of concepts into production.
The real challenge is creating the conditions in which AI can move from an isolated trial into a sustainable part of the wider business. That requires establishing the right technical and organizational foundations, preparing people and processes, and finding the right use cases. To deliver real value, organizations need to think less about speed and more about creating something secure, scalable, and consistent.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
It isn’t a technology challenge, it’s a business one
When AI projects stall, it's seldom because of the technology itself. More often, organizations run into strategic, governance, and operational challenges that prevent encouraging pilots from becoming production-ready solutions.
One of the biggest barriers is analysis paralysis. The majority of organizations have no shortage of AI ideas, but they typically lack a clear way of understanding which use cases will deliver the greatest value. This means resources become spread across multiple proof-of-concepts, each showing promise but none receiving the attention needed to reach production. The number of pilots continues to soar while the number of live deployments stagnates.
However, some organizations make the opposite mistake by designing for scale before they've checked the concept works. Major investment is made in infrastructure, architecture, and implementation before a solution has been tested in real-world conditions. If the project then needs to change direction, the amount of investment already committed can make it tricky to adapt. As a result, organizations can end up locked into an approach that no longer delivers the value they envisioned.
Governance is another common stumbling block. For organizations operating across EMEA, navigating regulations such as the EU AI Act, GDPR, and DORA introduces understandable caution. The consequences of non-compliance can be significant, and uncertainty around an evolving regulation often slows decision-making. Many AI initiatives don't stall because the business lacks ambition, but because leaders want greater confidence that they're deploying the technology in the right way: compliantly and responsibly.
Lastly, organizations often underestimate what it will cost to move from a successful pilot to widespread deployment. AI projects that appear affordable during the proof-of-concept phase can become much more expensive once they're scaled, especially if they haven't been properly stress-tested.
That's why due diligence is critical. Yet more than half (56%) of organizations don't carry out a Total Cost of Ownership assessment before deciding where to place significant workloads. Without a clear understanding of the long-term investment required, it's easy for costs to accumulate and confidence in the project to dwindle.
Balancing certainty and speed
Closing the Implementation Gap isn't about moving faster. It's about moving with confidence and know-how.
Time and time again, organizations find themselves at one of two extremes: waiting until every unknown has been resolved before making any moves or rushing ahead with AI projects before they've been properly validated. Neither approach is sustainable. Those seeing the greatest success are the organizations finding a balance between certainty and speed - moving quickly where the evidence supports it, while building in the validation and governance needed to reduce risk.
That starts with validating ideas early. Before major investment is made, organizations need to ask the technical, commercial, and governance questions that could prevent a project from ever reaching production. It's far better to discover early that a use case won't deliver than to invest months of budget and time before uncovering the same conclusion.
Rapid prototyping also plays a crucial role. Instead of debating whether an idea might work in theory, businesses should aim to create something tangible that users can test within days. Seeing a concept in action changes the conversation from speculation to evidence, giving stakeholders the confidence to make informed decisions about where to invest next.
Equally important is maintaining transparency throughout the delivery process. AI projects shouldn't feel like a black box. Defined ownership, clear checkpoints, and agreed assessment criteria help everyone to understand where a project stands, whether it’s a success, and what comes next. Projects rarely stall because the technology isn't capable - they stall because critical decisions weren't made early enough or because expectations weren't aligned from the outset.
Bridging the implementation gap
The implementation gap isn't going to disappear overnight. With 71% of organizations still stuck between pilot and production, the challenge is clearly not a lack of willingness, technical ability or ideas. In most cases, they have all three.
Instead, it's the ability to turn experiments into solutions that actually work in the real world. That means treating the transition as a business issue, not simply a technical one. Organizations need an approach that balances speed with governance, validates value before investment is made, and gives stakeholders the confidence to scale. It also requires leaders to be confident enough to stop projects in their tracks if they're not going to deliver real value.
The organizations taking meaningful steps forward won't be those adding more pilots into the mix. They'll be those that have strong processes and capabilities in place to push the right pilots ahead. Fundamentally, closing the AI implementation gap means creating a path from pilot to production that can be followed again and again.

articles.title: Steve Jobs rechazó los MacBook con pantallas táctiles, 10 años después Apple lanzó uno
articles.text:
Apple presentó un MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil, una función que su cofundador Steve Jobs rechazó de forma categórica hace más de una década. La compañía confirmó así un giro que marca el final de dieciséis años de resistencia a esa tecnología en sus computadoras portátiles.
Durante el evento “Back to the Mac” de octubre de 2010, Jobs explicó por qué Apple descartaba el uso de dedos sobre pantallas verticales. “Hemos hecho muchísimas pruebas de usuario sobre esto, y resulta que no funciona”, afirmó en esa ocasión. Hoy su empresa piensa diferente.
Cuáles fueron las palabras exactas de Steve Jobs
Jobs fue específico sobre el problema que identificaban las pruebas internas de Apple. Según explicó, las superficies táctiles “no quieren estar verticales”, porque generan una demostración vistosa pero insostenible en el uso cotidiano.
“Después de un período corto, empiezas a fatigarte y, tras un uso prolongado, tu brazo quiere caerse”, sostuvo. El cofundador de Apple remató la idea con una frase que se convirtió en referencia obligada del debate: calificó la propuesta como “ergonómicamente terrible”.
Esa postura no quedó en una simple declaración aislada. Apple sostuvo durante años una separación entre el iPad, diseñado en torno al tacto, y el Mac, pensado para teclado y trackpad.
La compañía introdujo en 2016 la Touch Bar en algunos modelos de MacBook Pro, una franja táctil sobre el teclado, pero evitó extender esa interacción a la pantalla principal.
Cómo es el nuevo MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil
El cambio llegó con el lanzamiento de modelos rediseñados de 14 y 16 pulgadas, que incorporan pantalla OLED en tándem junto a procesadores M5 Pro y M5 Max. Las ventas comenzarían el 6 de noviembre, según estimaciones previas al anuncio.
El rediseño también sumó un recorte más pequeño tipo Dynamic Island, similar al del iPhone, en reemplazo de la muesca anterior, y una bisagra reforzada que evita que la pantalla se mueva al recibir toques. La pantalla OLED, según las descripciones previas al lanzamiento, ofrece brillos más intensos, colores más saturados y negros más profundos que las versiones anteriores.
Con la función táctil, los usuarios pueden hacer zoom sobre fotografías, avanzar diapositivas en presentaciones e interactuar de forma directa con aplicaciones creativas. Apple no plantea el tacto como sustituto del teclado o el trackpad, sino como un complemento para situaciones puntuales.
Ternus explicó que la Mac sigue siendo, ante todo, un dispositivo de entrada indirecta, y que el tacto resulta útil solo en determinados contextos de uso. La compañía atribuye la incorporación de esta función a mejoras en la tecnología de pantalla, en el diseño del hardware y en la integración del software.
Ese componente de software también aparece en las primeras versiones de prueba de macOS 27, que incluyen gestos como deslizar para actualizar contenido, soporte táctil en la función Sidecar, controles más grandes pensados para el dedo y menús que se despliegan alrededor del punto de contacto.
Estos elementos funcionarían únicamente cuando el sistema detecta la presencia de un dedo sobre la pantalla, lo cual podría limitar el problema de fatiga que Jobs había anticipado en 2010.
Una contradicción con antecedentes dentro de Apple
La llegada del tacto al Mac no es la primera vez que Apple se aparta de un discurso previo sobre la convergencia entre dispositivos. En una conferencia de resultados de 2012, el actual consejero delegado de la compañía, Tim Cook, cuestionó los equipos que combinaban funciones de computadora y tableta por igual.
“Se puede combinar una tostadora y un refrigerador, pero, ya saben, esas cosas probablemente no van a ser agradables para el usuario”, planteó Cook en ese momento, en referencia a los dispositivos híbridos de la competencia.
Apple ya había incurrido antes en una tensión similar con el propio iPad. Durante años, la tableta funcionó como un sustituto de laptop sin ofrecer trackpad, lo que obligaba a los usuarios a señalar directamente sobre una pantalla vertical mientras usaban un teclado externo, justo el escenario que Jobs había descartado para el Mac.
Esa limitación se corrigió cuando Apple incorporó finalmente un cursor al iPad, lo que permitió combinar teclado y trackpad con el uso ocasional del dedo sobre la pantalla. El esquema que ahora se aplica al MacBook Pro replica esa misma lógica: el tacto se suma como opción adicional, sin reemplazar los métodos de entrada que definieron históricamente a la computadora de escritorio de Apple.

articles.title: IFTTT fait sa révolution : des agents IA, des automatisations illimitées et une nouvelle formule gratuite
articles.text:
IFTTT fait marche arrière sur les restrictions de son offre gratuite. Le célèbre service d'automatisation permet désormais de créer autant de scénarios que souhaité et introduit des agents IA capables de surveiller le Web et d'intervenir dans les applications connectées. Le tout avec un tout nouveau système de crédits.
Depuis 2010, IFTTT (If This Then That) permet d'automatiser des tâches entre différentes applications : enregistrer une information, recevoir une notification ou déclencher une action lorsqu'un événement survient. Le 28 octobre, la plateforme a annoncé sa transformation en IFTTT.ai, avec l'ambition d'aller plus loin que ces scénarios définis à l'avance.
L'intelligence artificielle doit désormais pouvoir interpréter les informations rencontrées et décider de certaines actions. Une évolution qui s'accompagne d'une refonte importante des abonnements.
Des agents IA pour surveiller le Web et choisir les bonnes actions
La principale nouveauté s'appelle AI Agent. Elle permet notamment de surveiller une page web pour détecter une nouvelle annonce, une baisse de prix ou le franchissement d'un seuil défini par l'utilisateur.
L'agent peut aussi intervenir dans les applications connectées. IFTTT donne l'exemple d'une facture reçue dans Gmail : l'IA en identifie l'échéance, vérifie si un rappel figure déjà dans Google Agenda et crée un événement si nécessaire. Elle peut également décider de ne rien faire, par exemple lorsque le rappel existe déjà.
- Simple d’utilisation
- Fonctionne avec des tonnes d’applications
- N’affecte pas la durée de vie de la batterie
Une autre fonction, AI Action assist, permet de générer automatiquement le contenu d'un message ou d'une notification, ou de filtrer certaines informations selon des critères précis.
La création d'automatisations en langage naturel et les connexions avec ChatGPT ou Claude existaient déjà. La nouveauté tient surtout à la capacité des agents à interpréter des événements et à choisir certaines actions. Chaque automatisation reste néanmoins composée d'un déclencheur, d'une action et de règles définies par l'utilisateur, qui peut la désactiver à tout moment. IFTTT précise également que la surveillance de certaines pages web utilisant beaucoup de JavaScript reste limitée.
IFTTT reconnaît son erreur et revoit entièrement son offre gratuite
L'autre changement est de taille. Jusqu'ici, la formule gratuite était limitée à deux automatisations, appelées Applets. Désormais, tous les utilisateurs peuvent en créer autant qu'ils le souhaitent et accéder aux plus de 1 000 intégrations proposées par le service.
Un revirement que Linden Tibbets, fondateur et PDG d'IFTTT, accompagne d'un mea culpa : le modèle freemium introduit en 2020, qui avait progressivement restreint les possibilités des comptes gratuits, était une erreur. Et il en revendique personnellement la responsabilité.
Cette nouvelle liberté s'accompagne toutefois d'un système de crédits. Les automatisations deviennent illimitées en nombre, mais leur utilisation reste plafonnée. Les exécutions d'Applets, les fonctions IA et les appels via MCP, le protocole permettant aux assistants d'interagir avec des services externes, puisent dans une enveloppe mensuelle. Une automatisation comportant plusieurs opérations peut ainsi consommer davantage de crédits qu'une simple notification.
L'offre gratuite comprend 1 000 crédits mensuels, contre 5 000 pour Starter, 20 000 pour Pro et 100 000 pour Pro+. Les abonnements payants débutent à 2,99 dollars par mois. Lorsque le solde est épuisé, les automatisations sont suspendues jusqu'au renouvellement ou à l'ajout de crédits, sans être supprimées.
Les abonnés actuels conservent leur tarif et n'ont pas à changer de formule. IFTTT prévoit également un bonus exceptionnel de crédits pour certains clients Pro et Pro+ dont la consommation habituelle dépasse les nouvelles limites.

articles.title: GitHub Launches npm Firewall to Block Malicious Packages Before Installation
articles.text:
GitHub has announced that it's introducing a new package firewall as a preview to block installation of suspicious npm packages during installation time.
"The firewall inspects both metadata requests and package downloads for signs of malicious activity, acting as an install-time policy gate," GitHub said.
The feature, which currently supports only npm packages, is available in public preview for all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including data-resident GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
According to the Microsoft subsidiary, the firewall is placed between endpoints or internal registries and the upstream package repositories so as to deter malware attacks that compromise systems when packages are installed.
This behavior can expose users to severe security risks, especially when artificial intelligence (AI) agents and CI runners automatically install dependencies to complete a task or build without their explicit permission.
The idea is that endpoints like coding agents and CI/CD hosts use the firewall for their requests instead of directly pointing to the public package registries. The firewall then checks package downloads against policy controls such as minimum package age and malware advisories, and blocks downloads that do not meet those policies.
To use the firewall, administrators are required to configure policy controls, such as the ones listed below -
- Block known malware by checking against the GitHub Advisory Database for active malware advisories
- Block packages based on the severity of vulnerabilities by checking the GitHub Advisory Database for flaws that affect the requested package version. The control defaults to "Critical only" as the severity level that blocks an installation, although users can choose "High or higher," "Medium or higher," or "Any severity."
- Block attestation downgrades by comparing attestations for the requested package version with those of earlier versions and stop the download if the requested version does not have an SLSA attestation.
- Block newly-introduced install scripts by checking whether the package recently added scripts that run using preinstall or postinstall hooks, which can be abused to steal sensitive data.
Block packages based on a cooldown period that prevents versions that are newer than the configured minimum age from being installed. The value can range from 1 to 365 days. The default value is 1 day. Users can disable it by setting it to 0.
Users who need access to a package that gets blocked erroneously by the firewall can submit an exception request, which can then be approved by enterprise administrators and security managers.
The development comes as Rust 1.100, which is scheduled for release on November 12, 2026, readies to add support for a configurable minimum publish age, allowing security scanners and maintainers time to flag and block malicious crate releases before they can be installed or used by users.
The value, defined via the "global-min-publish-age" option in "cargo/config.toml," allows users to specify a minimum publication age in days or weeks. If left unspecified, a seven-day waiting period is applied by default to skip releases published within that window.
Over the past year, similar waiting periods have been implemented across open-source ecosystems, including npm, Python, Microsoft Visual Studio Code, Ruby, Bun, pnpm, and Yarn, as a way to bolster software supply chain security by reducing the chance that a newly published, unreviewed version is immediately pulled into a build.
Cooldown periods help add friction and slow down attacks in which a bad actor publishes a poisoned version of a popular package after seizing control of a maintainer account, thereby preventing rapid spread through manual or automated installations.
"The tradeoff is that legitimate fixes have to wait, too, unless developers make an exception," Socket said. "Malicious code also doesn't magically become harmless with age. A release that escapes detection can simply outlast the cooldown. The value is in buying researchers, maintainers, and registries time to act before the next dependency update carries an attack further."

articles.title: NVIDIA GeForce NOW Gets Phantom Blade Zero and Eight More Games This Week

NVIDIA GeForce NOW Gets Phantom Blade Zero and Eight More Games This Week

articles.title: 'Those gradual rollouts though': Windows 11's right-click menu gets a vital tune-up, and it looks great — the main complaint is people can't get it quick enough
articles.text:
Windows 11's right-click menu gets a vital tune-up — it's now faster, and you can dump options you don't want
The main complaint is people can't get this revamp quickly enough
- Windows 11 has a new preview (optional) update
- This introduces the ability to fully tailor the right-click (context) menu to your liking, as well as speeding up its performance
- That's great, but you're best off steering clear of a preview update and waiting for the full release in under two weeks – but even then, this feature will be on a gradual rollout
Windows 11 now has one of the most-wanted interface capabilities for many people, namely the ability to customize the right-click menu – but it's not quite fully finalized yet (although that's imminent).
The menu that pops up when you right-click on a file (or folder) is also known as the 'context' menu as it presents a bunch of options that vary contextually based on the type of file clicked – but in Windows 11, it's currently a sprawling affair.
Those who hate the lengthy right-click menu will now be able to customize it after installing a new Windows 11 update, although this is an optional release, meaning it's still in preview. This feature will be in next month's patch, the November update, though, so you haven't got long to wait for the full release (less than two weeks, in fact).
The customization settings for the right-click menu include the ability to remove Windows commands you're not fond of – like 'Send to' for example – or add abilities that you'd like to have, and also choose the apps you want to appear in the context menu.
It's a full range of customization and you can also elect to have the top panel of the menu (cut, paste, rename and so forth) directly integrated instead, so these functions appear alongside everything else (in a Windows 10 style – and you can shift the layout around too, moving Properties to the foot of the menu for example).
Microsoft boasts that the new right-click menu is faster, too: "The updated menu opens more quickly, reduces clutter, and gives you more control over the commands and app extensions that appear when you right-click."
As you may have noticed, all this work has been in testing for a while now.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Analysis: rolling frustrations and a lengthy wait
The immediate response on the likes of Reddit seems positive, and there are Windows 11 users who have taken the plunge with this preview update who are observing that the right-click menu is indeed a lot faster.
One Redditor enthuses: "The new context menu is so good! Way faster, customization is cool."
Others acknowledge that this is undoubtedly a good move, but don't understand why it took Microsoft so long to get here: "Not bad imo. Crazy it took them 5 years though."
While the feedback is generally positive, there are complaints from those who have installed the update but haven't received the new context menu. This is because the right-click revamp has been implemented via a gradual rollout, so it's only being drip-fed through to a certain amount of PCs at a time (of those who have installed the optional update). As another Redditor puts it: "Those gradual rollouts though…"
You can force the feature to be deployed to your PC using a Windows configuration utility (ViVeTool), but I wouldn't recommend that approach. Microsoft tests the waters in a limited way for good reasons, especially with features still in preview, so you're running a larger than normal risk of some nasty bug ruining your day.
Anyway, you've waited five years for this performance and options tuning, as those on Reddit are keen to point out – so what's another couple of weeks? I'd hold on for the official November update, keeping clear of this preview, but even then, it'll still be a gradual rollout, and you may need some patience.
Still, the good news is that the context ball is rolling, and it hopefully won't be too long before the majority of Windows 11 users gain access to this important upgrade for a key piece of the UI.
