articles.title: La lucha del hijo de Steve Jobs contra el cáncer tras la muerte de su padre: “personas se sienten motivadas por una razón familiar”
articles.text:
Reed Jobs, hijo de Steve Jobs, decidió enfocar parte de su trabajo como inversor en compañías que buscan evitar muertes por cáncer después de vivir de cerca la enfermedad y el fallecimiento de su padre. Su experiencia familiar, iniciada cuando tenía 12 años, conecta una historia personal con el debate sobre nuevas herramientas de prevención, tratamientos y acceso a la innovación médica.
La reflexión adquiere relevancia porque el cáncer no solo transforma la vida de quienes reciben un diagnóstico. También modifica las decisiones de familiares, investigadores, médicos e inversores. Reed Jobs explicó a Fortune que muchas personas vinculadas a este campo encuentran una razón personal para participar en la búsqueda de soluciones.
Reed Jobs tenía 12 años cuando Steve Jobs enfermó
Steve Jobs, fundador de Apple, recibió un diagnóstico de cáncer de páncreas en 2003. Su hijo Reed tenía 12 años entonces. El empresario murió ocho años después, en 2011, a los 56 años.
Esa experiencia llevó a Reed Jobs a interesarse por el cáncer y a financiar compañías dedicadas a combatir la enfermedad. “Empecé a trabajar en el cáncer cuando mi padre enfermó, y muchas personas se sienten motivadas por una razón familiar”, afirmó en declaraciones a la sección Term Sheet de Fortune.
La muerte de Steve Jobs convirtió una vivencia familiar en una motivación profesional para su hijo. El objetivo que plantea no se limita a acompañar la investigación, sino a contribuir a que el cáncer deje de ser mortal para más pacientes.
La trayectoria del fundador de Apple ya había quedado marcada por el diagnóstico. En 2005, durante su discurso de graduación en la Universidad de Stanford, relató que los médicos le comunicaron inicialmente que podía padecer un tipo de cáncer incurable y que su expectativa de vida podía ser de tres a seis meses.
El diagnóstico cambió la visión de Steve Jobs
Jobs explicó ante los estudiantes que recibió el consejo de volver a casa y poner en orden sus asuntos personales. Para él, aquello significaba intentar comunicar a sus hijos, en pocos meses, lo que esperaba decirles durante la siguiente década.
Más tarde, nuevos estudios determinaron que el tumor era de un tipo poco común que podía tratarse mediante cirugía. Jobs fue intervenido y superó ese episodio, aunque reconoció que fue la vez que estuvo más cerca de la muerte.
“Recordar que voy a morir es la herramienta más importante que encontré para ayudarme a tomar grandes decisiones en la vida”, dijo en Stanford. Esa idea se convirtió en una de las frases más conocidas de su visión sobre el tiempo, el miedo y las decisiones personales.
El fundador de Apple sostuvo que la conciencia de la mortalidad podía reducir el peso del orgullo, el temor al fracaso y la presión social. Esa experiencia no evitó que la enfermedad siguiera presente en su vida, pero redefinió la forma en que habló sobre sus prioridades.
Reed Jobs menciona vacunas y medicamentos GLP-1
Reed Jobs también se mostró interesado en las vacunas experimentales contra el cáncer. Sin embargo, en sus declaraciones destacó el posible impacto de los medicamentos GLP-1, utilizados para tratar la diabetes tipo 2 y la obesidad.
El GLP-1 es una hormona que el intestino libera después de comer. Los agonistas de GLP-1 son medicamentos sintéticos que imitan esa hormona. Jobs los describió como algunos de los fármacos más impactantes creados hasta ahora.
Según explicó, estos tratamientos podrían ayudar en la prevención al reducir la obesidad, una condición asociada con un mayor riesgo de 13 tipos de cáncer, de acuerdo con los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades de Estados Unidos.
Jobs planteó que los GLP-1 pueden tener efectos más amplios que el control del peso, con posibles beneficios para personas con cáncer, enfermedades cardiovasculares y otras afecciones. Su afirmación se sitúa dentro de una discusión mayor sobre el alcance que estos medicamentos pueden tener en la salud pública.
La experiencia de Reed Jobs muestra cómo una pérdida familiar puede impulsar iniciativas vinculadas con la ciencia y la salud. Su caso también recuerda que la lucha contra el cáncer reúne distintas estrategias: prevención, tratamientos, investigación y financiamiento.

articles.title: Espionnés via de simples publicités... L'inquiétant piège tendu aux utilisateurs de Starlink
articles.text:
Une entreprise israélienne est soupçonnée d’avoir exploité la publicité en ligne pour localiser et suivre des utilisateurs de Starlink. Des chercheurs ont repéré une activité inhabituelle jusque dans des pays où le service de SpaceX est interdit ou restreint.
Des publicités en apparence banales auraient servi à pister des utilisateurs de Starlink. Selon une enquête de Reuters publiée le 27 octobre, l’entreprise israélienne Discover-Tech serait derrière ce ciblage. Pour l’identifier, l’agence s’appuie sur les témoignages de six sources proches du dossier et sur les travaux de TrendAI, l’unité cybersécurité de Trend Micro, dont les chercheurs ont repéré des achats d’espaces publicitaires anormalement concentrés sur les connexions Starlink.
Un intérêt appuyé pour les connexions Starlink
En analysant un échantillon d’enchères publicitaires, les chercheurs de TrendAI ont repéré un acheteur particulièrement actif sur les connexions Starlink. Celui-ci arrive en tête d’enchères remportées dans 105 pays, dont la France. Son activité en Syrie, en Libye, au Yémen ou au Soudan du Sud leur paraît difficile à expliquer par la simple volonté de vendre des produits.
Starlink permet notamment de rester connecté lorsque les réseaux terrestres sont coupés ou soumis à des restrictions locales. Cette possibilité est précieuse dans les zones de conflit, mais elle intéresse aussi les autorités qui cherchent à localiser les utilisateurs du service.
Les enchères publicitaires peuvent devenir un outil de surveillance
Lorsqu’un emplacement publicitaire est mis aux enchères dans une application ou un navigateur, les acheteurs potentiels reçoivent des informations pour décider combien ils sont prêts à payer. Adresse IP, identifiants publicitaires, caractéristiques de l’appareil et parfois localisation peuvent ainsi circuler avant même qu’une annonce ne s’affiche sur l’écran de l'utilisateur.
En recoupant ces données, un acteur malveillant peut constituer des profils, suivre des déplacements ou chercher à identifier des personnes. L’annonce diffusée peut aussi exécuter du code sans intervention de l’internaute. Dans une enquête distincte publiée le 15 octobre, Citizen Lab a documenté des infections par le logiciel espion Candiru, diffusé au moyen de publicités achetées par Discover-Tech sur des appareils d’Al Jazeera.
Discover-Tech écartée des grandes plateformes
Le rapport de TrendAI désigne l’acheteur suspect sous le nom de code SHADOW-EARTH-79. D’après cinq sources interrogées par Reuters, les chercheurs avaient envisagé de nommer Discover-Tech, mais leur direction aurait soulevé des réserves juridiques. Sollicitée par l’agence, TrendAI invoque sa prudence en matière d’attribution, sans expliquer directement pourquoi l’entreprise n’a pas été citée.
Google et la plateforme publicitaire Beeswax, propriété de Comcast, ont exclu Discover-Tech de leurs services. Une grande entreprise technologique américaine et une organisation internationale ont également ouvert des enquêtes internes, selon Reuters. Ni SpaceX ni Discover-Tech n’ont répondu aux sollicitations de l’agence.
Les satellites peuvent aider à contourner certaines restrictions locales, mais ils ne font pas disparaître les traces laissées sur les sites et les applications. Le dossier pose donc une question qui dépasse largement Starlink. À force de perfectionner le ciblage publicitaire, les plateformes ont-elles aussi simplifié le travail de ceux qui cherchent des cibles plutôt que des clients ?
Sources : Reuters, TrendAI et Citizen Lab

articles.title: Attacker Tried to Exploit Alpine Linux’s GitLab via CVSS 10.0 Flaw Its Ruby Left Open
articles.text:
An attacker tried to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability on the Alpine Linux project's own GitLab server a week after GitLab released a fix, Alpine Linux said on 28 October.
The flaw, CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0), can let an attacker run code on a GitLab server through a crafted regular expression in a CI configuration. Alpine found no evidence that the attack worked but cannot rule it out, so it rebuilt the server from scratch and reset every account's password.
GitLab's fix is a set of patches to the Ruby that GitLab ships in its own packages and container images. Alpine's GitLab image used standard Ruby, so upgrading the server to GitLab 19.3.6 on 22 October did not fix the flaw.
For anyone running GitLab on their own Ruby, built from source or in their own container image, "upgrading GitLab is not enough," Alpine said. Those servers also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later, and users of Alpine's alpinelinux/gitlab image need to pull 19.3.6 again.
The server gitlab.alpinelinux.org hosts aports, the repository from which Alpine's packages are built. Packages built from 20 to 24 October, and the 21 October releases, came from aports changes verified against records outside GitLab, according to Alpine.
Those releases include the minirootfs files that the official Alpine Docker images are built from. Alpine is extending the checks to 27 October, when it closed the server. The keys that sign its packages and releases have never been on the GitLab server.
How the Attack Unfolded
On 13 October, Alpine upgraded the server to GitLab 19.3.4 instead of 19.3.5, which it calls a mistake. The server was still on that version, without the 12 October fix, when a newly registered account began probing it on 20 October.
The account sent crafted CI configurations to the server on 20 and 21 October. They crashed GitLab worker processes 8 times, and the main attack on 21 October also caused 502 errors and caused CI jobs to fail.
In 4 of those crashes, the attacker got partway through the exploit and failed at the next step, according to Alpine. The attacker also downloaded Alpine's GitLab container image, which Alpine said: "suggests they were tuning the exploit to our exact build."
Alpine blocked the account on 23 October. The attacker came back on 25 and 26 October and tried to get back in, but those attempts failed, Alpine said.
On 26 October, Alpine found that the server was still vulnerable after its 22 October upgrade to 19.3.6. The next day, it closed GitLab to everyone except its developers and build servers and started rebuilding it.
The rebuild finished on 28 October. Alpine also replaced GitLab's secret keys, and the rebuilt server runs Ruby 3.3.13 or later, which has the fix. Alpine is testing it before reopening it to the public.
What Alpine Can and Cannot Rule Out
Alpine found no sign that the attacker's code ran on the server. Timing probes showed no delays;; there were no unexpected files, keys, hooks, or processes; and no private data was sent back to the attacker via any web or API request that Alpine can see.
It cannot be sure, though. "A successful exploit would leave no crash and no trace in the web logs," Alpine said. Some logs from the attack day are gone, including background job logs and the old container's filesystem, and neither Alpine nor its hosting provider logged outbound network connections.
Because the evidence needed to confirm code execution no longer exists, Alpine treated the server as compromised and rebuilt it to remove any foothold a successful exploit could have left.
If the attack succeeded, these could have been exposed:
- Email addresses, names, and IP addresses of all users
- Password hashes
- 2FA secrets, CI/CD variables and runner tokens
- Webhook, integration and push mirror credentials
- Personal access tokens, which are stored as hashes
- Private repositories, and confidential issues and merge requests
Beyond the password reset and the new secret keys, Alpine has not said whether runner tokens, CI/CD variables, access tokens or integration credentials stored on the server have been replaced.
To check its packages, Alpine confirmed that every aports change added from 20 to 22 October arrived through a recorded push by a known developer. It checked this against records it says the attacker could not reach: a developer's copy of the repository and all 45 build servers. Every package built from 20 to 24 October came from aports changes as published on git.alpinelinux.org.
Why the GitLab Upgrade Did Not Fix It
GitLab compiles the regular expressions in CI configurations with Ruby, and the bug behind CVE-2026-97229 is in Onigmo, the regular expression engine built into Ruby.
GitLab's 12 October release fixed it by patching the Ruby inside GitLab's Linux package and container images. Ruby's own fixed versions came out on 22 and 23 October.
A GitLab upgrade does not change a server's own Ruby, so a GitLab install on standard Ruby keeps the flaw until Ruby itself is updated to a fixed version, as Alpine found.
GitLab's fixed Linux packages and its official container images carry the patched Ruby. A self-compiled install, or a container image that installs Ruby separately as Alpine's did, does not get it.
As of 29 October, neither of GitLab's patch release posts for 12 and 21 October tells administrators of self-compiled installs to update Ruby. GitLab's self-compiled installation guide still lists Ruby 3.2 as its minimum version, and Ruby 3.2 reached end of life in April and will get no fix.
Which GitLab Servers Are Exposed
GitLab's advisory says that, "under certain conditions," the flaw could have allowed an unauthenticated user to run code on the server. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched.
Rapid7 built a working exploit in a lab and published proof-of-concept code on 13 October. The exploit ran commands as GitLab's git user on an unpatched official GitLab 19.4.1 image, but the same input did not run on the patched 19.4.2 image.
That exploit needs write access first: the attacker must commit a malicious .gitlab-ci.yml file and a file path with UTF-8 characters to a branch of a public project. That requirement does not apply on servers where new users can register themselves and create projects.
In Rapid7's tested route, "only the final CI lint request is unauthenticated." GitLab's own detection notes also say the attacker must first create that file path through ordinary repository APIs. Rapid7 does not yet know how the attack in the original report to GitLab, which is still private, avoids the write step.
Alpine has not said how its attacker's CI configurations reached GitLab, or whether new accounts could create public projects on its server.
CVE-2026-97229 was not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of the catalog's 28 October update.
What GitLab Administrators Should Do
GitLab's 21 October releases are the newest on each branch listed below, and they also fix CVE-2026-110264, a separate regex flaw.
| Branch | Fixes CVE-2026-97229, per GitLab's advisory | Newest release (21 October) | 
|---|---|---|
| 19.5 | Not listed as affected | 19.5.1 | 
| 19.4 | 19.4.2 | 19.4.3 | 
| 19.3 | 19.3.5 | 19.3.6 | 
| 19.2 | 19.2.8 | 19.2.9 | 
| 19.1, 19.0 and 18.11 | Not listed as affected | 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13 | 
Which release fixes a server depends on how GitLab is installed:
- GitLab's Linux package or official container images: upgrade to the newest release for your branch.
- Self-compiled installs, or images that install their own Ruby: upgrade GitLab and update Ruby to 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9, or later. Ruby 3.2 will not receive the fix, so servers running 3.2 need to upgrade to one of those versions.
GitLab's advisory named 19.3.4 as the fixed version for the 19.3 branch when it was published on 12 October. It now names 19.3.5 and lists 19.3.4 as affected, so servers still on 19.3.4 should move to 19.3.6.
If a server cannot be upgraded right away, Rapid7 suggests restricting anonymous access to public projects, stopping untrusted users from creating or writing to public projects, or blocking the CI lint route. Those steps cover only Rapid7's exploit route and do not fix the vulnerable regular expression compiler, the company said.
GitLab has published six detection rules for exploitation attempts against self-managed servers, written in the Sigma format. Four of them, which GitLab marks as experimental, look for hostile patterns in CI regexp warnings and GraphQL ciLint requests, unusually long file paths with non-ASCII characters, and Ruby crash reports that point to Onigmo.
The guidance with those rules warns that a successful exploit can leave no crash, and it gives these further steps:
- Look for files owned by the git user in /tmp, unexpected child processes of Puma or Sidekiq, outbound connections, and changed crontabs or SSH keys for the git user.
- If there are signs of code execution, treat the server as compromised and rotate the secrets in gitlab-secrets.json, all CI/CD variables, all runner tokens and all access tokens.
- Limit who can create accounts and personal access tokens on the server.
What Alpine Users Should Do
Account holders will need to set a new password with "Forgot your password?" on the sign-in page when gitlab.alpinelinux.org reopens, Alpine said. It has also seen automated login attempts against its GitLab using passwords leaked from other sites, and anyone who used their gitlab.alpinelinux.org password elsewhere should change it there.
Users of the alpinelinux/gitlab image should pull alpinelinux/gitlab:19.3.6 again. The image published on 27 October contains Ruby 3.3.13, while any 19.3.6 image pulled before then, and every older tag, is vulnerable.
Alpine's own Ruby packages already have the fix: Ruby 3.4.12 on Alpine 3.22, 3.23, 3.24 and edge, and Ruby 3.3.13 on Alpine 3.21. Running apk upgrade installs it.
Ruby's maintainers say the bug matters only for programs that compile a regular expression from text an attacker controls, and that Ruby's Regexp.timeout setting does not protect against it.

articles.title: LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
The LattePanda Team today launched LattePanda Sigma 2, an x86 single-board server designed to bring high-performance local AI computing directly into intelligent products and systems. Built around the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H processor with Intel Arc B390 graphics, LattePanda Sigma 2 delivers up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8 in a compact form factor.
As "The Embeddable AI Single Board Server," LattePanda Sigma 2 combines high-performance computing, up to 64 GB of memory, high-speed networking, flexible expansion, and real-time hardware control in a single board. Rather than sitting alongside a product, it is designed to be integrated directly into the product itself, supporting applications from autonomous robots and vision systems to professional instruments and private AI appliances.LattePanda Sigma 2 combines the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 GPU, and integrated NPU to deliver up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8. It features a 16-core CPU with up to 4.8 GHz clock speed, a 12 Xe-core Intel Arc B390 GPU delivering up to 122 TOPS of INT8 AI performance, and an NPU capable of up to 50 TOPS.
With up to 64 GB of LPDDR5X-8533 RAM and 136.5 GB/s memory bandwidth, LattePanda Sigma 2 provides the capacity and throughput required for demanding local AI workloads. Up to 59 GB of VRAM can be allocated for AI workloads, providing enough room for 35B-class quantized MoE models and the KV cache required by long-context AI agents. With INT4 quantization and OpenVINO, the system can run the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model locally at around 30 tokens per second.
Built for Local AI Systems
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed to support both individual AI workloads and multi-agent local AI systems. Developers can expand compute capacity through M.2, OCuLink, or Thunderbolt 4, connecting additional AI accelerators as workloads grow. An integrated RP2350 microcontroller adds GPIO connectivity and real-time hardware control, allowing AI applications to interact with sensors and actuators. Preloaded MicroPython firmware provides a programmable interface for intelligent devices and automation systems.
Server-Class Expansion in an Embeddable Form Factor
LattePanda Sigma 2 provides extensive connectivity for storage, networking, and acceleration. It includes three M.2 M-Key slots, one M.2 E-Key slot, PCIe 4.0 x2 via OCuLink, and two Thunderbolt 4 ports. Dual 10GbE Ethernet supports high-bandwidth networking, while USB 3.2 Gen 2, USB 2.0, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 2.1, and eDP 1.5 provide flexible system integration options. These interfaces allow LattePanda Sigma 2 to operate as a compact local AI server or integrate directly into larger intelligent systems.
Ready for Local AI Development and Deployment
LattePanda Sigma 2 supports Windows 11 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, with compatibility for OpenVINO, llama.cpp, and Ollama. It ships with Ubuntu, GPU and NPU drivers, OpenVINO Model Server (OVMS), OpenClaw, and local AI models pre-installed on the onboard SSD, reducing setup time for local AI deployment.
Designed for Product Integration
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed for product-level integration and long-term deployment, offering a guaranteed 3+ year product lifecycle, custom boot logos and BIOS customization options, and direct engineering support for integration projects. Its combination of local AI compute, high-speed I/O, flexible expansion, and real-time control supports a wide range of applications, including:
- Local AI Appliances—Run private RAG and AI agents while keeping sensitive data on premises.
- All-in-One Homelabs—Combine NAS, virtualization, media services, and local AI in one system.
- Professional Instruments—Capture and process high-speed data streams directly inside compact professional equipment.
- Mobile Autonomous Robots—Unify perception, navigation, planning, and real-time control on one platform.
"Local AI is moving beyond development and into the products and systems people use every day," said Youliang Yu, Product Manager of LattePanda Sigma 2. "With LattePanda Sigma 2, we are combining the computing performance, memory capacity, expansion, and real-time hardware control needed to run AI locally in a compact, embeddable platform. The goal is to give developers a practical way to put local AI directly into the products they build."
Key Specifications
- Processor: Intel Core Ultra X7 358H
- AI Performance: Up to 180 TOPS (CPU + GPU + NPU, INT8)
- NPU: Up to 50 TOPS
- CPU: 16 cores (4P + 8E + 4LPE), up to 4.8 GHz, 18 MB cache
- GPU: Intel Arc B390, 12 Xe-cores, up to 122 TOPS (INT8)
- Memory: Up to 64 GB LPDDR5X-8533 RAM, 136.5 GB/s bandwidth
- Storage & Expansion: 3× M.2 M-Key, 1× M.2 E-Key, OCuLink PCIe 4.0 x2
- Networking: 2× 10GbE RJ45
- Thunderbolt: 2× Thunderbolt 4 Type-C
- USB Type-A: 2× USB 3.2 Gen 2, 2× USB 2.0
- Display: HDMI 2.1, DP 2.1 via USB Type-C, eDP 1.5
- Co-Processor: RP2350
- Operating System: Windows 11, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later
- Dimensions: 146 × 102 mm
For more information about LattePanda Sigma 2, please visit the LattePanda website. During the pre-sale period through mid-November, the LattePanda Sigma 2 is available at a promotional price of $2,599. Following the conclusion of the pre-sale period, the price will return to $2,799.

articles.title: Payer avec Google Wallet sans déverrouiller son téléphone ? Google prépare une option qui pose question
articles.text:
Google Wallet pourrait bientôt permettre de régler ses achats sans avoir à déverrouiller systématiquement son smartphone. Une nouveauté pratique en apparence, mais qui soulève quelques interrogations sur la sécurité des paiements sans contact.
Payer avec son téléphone est devenu un geste presque aussi banal que sortir sa carte bancaire. Il suffit de l’approcher du terminal, à condition toutefois d’avoir préalablement confirmé son identité. Une petite manipulation qui peut parfois agacer, notamment lorsqu’on doit déverrouiller une nouvelle fois son smartphone alors qu'on vient de l’utiliser. Google semble justement réfléchir à un moyen de supprimer cette étape pour les paiements du quotidien. Mais entre gagner quelques secondes à la caisse et protéger ses coordonnées bancaires, il faudra trouver le bon équilibre.
Google Wallet pourrait supprimer une étape avant le paiement
Selon une découverte d’Android Authority, Google travaille sur une nouvelle option permettant potentiellement de désactiver la vérification d’identité avant un paiement sans contact.
Les journalistes ont repéré cette fonction dans la version 26.42.1003171897 de Google Wallet, au sein des paramètres de vérification de l’application. Une nouvelle entrée baptisée « Tap to pay » apparaît aux côtés des réglages consacrés aux transports en commun.
Aujourd'hui, Google Wallet demande de confirmer son identité à l’aide d’un code PIN, d'un mot de passe, d'un schéma ou d’une méthode biométrique suffisamment sécurisée, comme l’empreinte digitale. Cette authentification reste valable quelques minutes, mais doit ensuite être renouvelée pour effectuer un nouveau paiement.
Il existe toutefois une exception : les utilisateurs peuvent déjà payer certains trajets en transports en commun sans déverrouiller leur téléphone, lorsque le réseau concerné prend en charge cette possibilité.
Google pourrait donc reprendre le même principe pour les achats ordinaires. En pratique, il deviendrait possible d’approcher son smartphone d'un terminal de paiement sans devoir systématiquement passer par le lecteur d’empreintes ou saisir son code.
Du moins, c’est ce que laisse envisager cette découverte. Car pour l’instant, la fonctionnalité n’est absolument pas opérationnelle. Android Authority a réussi à faire apparaître manuellement le nouveau réglage, mais une tentative d’ouverture provoque immédiatement le plantage de Google Wallet.
Impossible, dans ces conditions, de savoir précisément comment il fonctionnera.
Quelques secondes gagnées, mais à quel prix pour la sécurité ?
C’est évidemment la principale interrogation soulevée par cette nouveauté. Supprimer la vérification d’identité avant un achat pourrait faciliter les passages en caisse, mais également augmenter les risques en cas de perte ou de vol du smartphone. Une personne ayant accès à l’appareil pourrait théoriquement tenter d’effectuer des paiements sans connaître son code de déverrouillage.
Un scénario qui explique pourquoi Google a progressivement renforcé les mécanismes de vérification de Wallet ces dernières années.
Il serait toutefois prématuré d’affirmer que Google compte autoriser tous les paiements sans aucune protection. L’entreprise pourrait, par exemple, imposer des limites de montant, réserver cette souplesse à certaines transactions ou demander régulièrement une authentification. Aucune de ces mesures n’est confirmée à ce stade.
Autre inconnue : les pays concernés. Les règles relatives à l’authentification des paiements varient selon les marchés, notamment en Europe, et rien ne permet encore d'affirmer que cette éventuelle option sera disponible en France.
Surtout, Google n’a fait aucune annonce officielle. La présence d’une fonctionnalité dans le code d'une application révèle un développement en cours, pas nécessairement une nouveauté destinée à être commercialisée.
En attendant d’en savoir davantage, il faudra donc continuer à confirmer son identité avant de payer ses courses. Ce qui, finalement, n'est peut-être pas une si mauvaise contrainte lorsqu’il s’agit de son argent.

articles.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
articles.text:
Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw, fixed in February, to plant custom malware inside the systems that control an organization's SD-WAN network.
The malware, called KeyDrift, is designed to copy the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and store them for later use, Cisco Talos said on October 28. Talos calls the attacks historical but does not specify when they occurred or whether any keys were sent.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-20127 and has a CVSS score of 10.0. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on these control systems. On a Controller, the attacker can log in as a high-privileged internal account that is not root.
When Cisco disclosed the flaw in February, Talos tracked its exploitation as UAT-8616, a cluster of activity it said went back to at least 2023.
In Cisco's traditional key exchange, each SD-WAN router periodically generates an AES key for its traffic and sends it to the Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart). The Controller passes the keys on to other routers. A process on the Controller called vdaemon runs the encrypted control connections that carry these keys.
On a compromised Controller, a KeyDrift component called LittleFilch hooks into vdaemon and reads control messages after they are decrypted. For a preset list of edge routers, it pulls out their IP addresses and a 32-byte field. Talos assesses that field as the AES-256 key material that the Controller passes between routers.
LittleFilch encrypts what it collects with RSA and writes it to a file. It can then send that data over UDP to an address listed in a settings file, which it deletes after reading. Talos could not recover that settings file.
The group behind KeyDrift, which Talos tracks as UAT-11473, has targeted space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research.
The group's infrastructure "overlaps considerably" with Silent Train, Talos assesses with high confidence. Silent Train is the name Lumen's Black Lotus Labs uses for a network of hacked small-office, home-office, IoT and business devices.
Lumen says Volt Typhoon used the network to hide its activity. CISA, the NSA and the FBI said in 2024 that Volt Typhoon is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber group.
Talos links UAT-11473 to Volt Typhoon only through the infrastructure overlap. It does not say the two are the same group, or how UAT-11473 relates to UAT-8616, the cluster it reported in February.
Separately, Lumen said on October 28 that Volt Typhoon was exploiting CVE-2026-20127 by late 2025 and continued to exploit it after Cisco disclosed the flaw in February. Lumen does not tie that activity to KeyDrift.
KeyDrift primarily starts via modified runit scripts that Cisco SD-WAN devices use to launch their services, according to Talos. In one version, the script for the SSH service starts a loader script, conf_sshd, before the real SSH server. The conf_sshd script writes vdaemon's process IDs to a file, and a tool called rsshd injects KeyDrift's main module, PolyFlame, into each of those processes.
PolyFlame runs in memory inside vdaemon. It can act as a TinyShell-like backdoor that runs commands and reads and writes files, or as a relay that forwards commands between its command server and other machines. It is built to accept commands within SD-WAN control traffic, and the analyzed samples contained no hardcoded server address.
On a compromised Validator, formerly vBond, a fake aaamgr service under /etc/sv/aaamgr/ runs a packed loader, aaamgrd, that decrypts and runs PolyFlame. Cisco's real aaamgr component is a Python package and does not normally run as a compiled service.
There are also signs of timestomping: commands the group ran copied the timestamps and permissions of existing files onto its own files.
Affected Releases and Fixes
CVE-2026-20127 affects the Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart), Manager (formerly vManage), and Validator (formerly vBond), regardless of their configuration. On-premises systems are affected, as are Cisco's hosted SD-WAN cloud deployments, including the Cisco Managed and FedRAMP environments. Cisco added the Validator to its advisory on June 16.
Cisco says it is aware of limited exploitation of the flaw. There is no workaround, and the first fixed releases are:
| Release train | First fixed release | 
|---|---|
| Earlier than 20.9 | Migrate to a fixed release | 
| 20.9 | 20.9.8.2 | 
| 20.11 | 20.12.6.1 | 
| 20.12 | 20.12.5.3 or 20.12.6.1 | 
| 20.13 | 20.15.4.2 | 
| 20.14 | 20.15.4.2 | 
| 20.15 | 20.15.4.2 | 
| 20.16 | 20.18.2.1 | 
| 20.18 | 20.18.2.1 | 
Releases earlier than 20.9 and the 20.11, 20.13, 20.14 and 20.16 trains have reached end of software maintenance.
Until they can upgrade, on-premises customers can limit access to ports 22 and 830 to the IP addresses of known controllers and other known systems. Cisco says this step worked in a test environment, but that customers should check how well it works in their own networks. Such guardrails are already in place for Cisco's hosted SD-WAN cloud deployments.
Blocking the ports does not remove malware already on a device.
Checking for KeyDrift
Talos advises organizations to install Cisco's fixes, follow Cisco's Catalyst SD-WAN hardening guide and watch for signs of post-compromise activity. Anyone who finds such signs should start incident response and can ask Cisco's Technical Assistance Center (TAC) for help.
That advice does not say whether upgrading removes KeyDrift from a device that was already compromised, or whether any keys should be replaced. Cisco's February remediation guide for this flaw warns that there could be "existing exploits which are still in place" from before an upgrade.
KeyDrift uses these files and locations, some given only by name:
- File: the run script under etc/sv/sshd/, modified to start conf_sshd
- Directory: /etc/sv/aaamgr/, a fake service on a compromised Validator
- File: aaamgrd, the packed loader
- File: conf_sshd, the loader script
- File: rsshd, the injector
- File: libdssl.so, PolyFlame
- File: libcommon.so, LittleFilch
- File: /tmp/system-vdaemon, the list of vdaemon process IDs
- File: /var/tmp/vdaemon.bin, LittleFilch's encrypted records
- File: /var/tmp/vdaemon.conf, LittleFilch's send settings, deleted after reading
Talos's report does not include a list of file hashes, IP addresses or domains for KeyDrift.
Talos released Snort rules on October 28 that look for inbound KeyDrift command-and-control connections: 67387 through 67416 for Snort 2, and 7:44 through 7:73 for Snort 3. Rules 65938 and 65958, already available, cover CVE-2026-20127 itself.
The October 28 rule update lists the Snort 2 rules as disabled by default, so users of the paid Snort Subscriber rule set must turn them on. The Snort 3 rules appear with no default state.
To check for exploitation of the flaw itself, Cisco says to look in /var/log/auth.log for Accepted publickey for vmanage-admin entries from unknown IP addresses. Before opening a TAC case, customers should run request admin-tech on each control component. The remediation guide also recommends rescanning those admin-tech files with the Check Bug Applicability feature on the Bug Search Tool page for bug CSCws52722.
For US federal civilian agencies, CISA's February 25 emergency directive sets out what to do if a root account compromise is found. They must report it to CISA, deploy fresh Manager, Controller and Validator instances from patched images, and move their edge routers to the new systems.

articles.title: Morocco's ABA Life secures $40 million investment from Admaius Capital Partners
articles.text: Morocco-based healthtech company ABA Life has signed a $40 million investment agreement with pan-African private equity firm Admaius Capital Partners, subject to customary closing conditions and approval from Morocco's Competition Council. Founded in 2021, ABA Life is the healthcare arm of ABA Technology, founded and chaired by Mohamed Benouda. The company develops and operates healthcare solutions combining artificial intelligence, medical technology, telemedicine, connected healthcare infrastructure and clinical services. ABA Life has developed an integrated, profitable business model, delivering healthcare programmes in partnership with public institutions and foundations to expand access to medical services. The investment will support the company's AI for Sovereign Health programme, including its Mediot AI platform and clinical intelligence solutions, alongside the expansion of its healthcare technologies and services and entry into international markets. Press release: ABA Life, the healthcare arm of ABA Technology, has announced the signing of an investment agreement with Admaius Capital Partners (“Admaius”) for $40 million, subject to customary closing conditions and to clearance by the Competition Council of the Kingdom of Morocco. The transaction marks a major milestone in ABA Life’s growth and in its ambition to build, from Morocco, a healthtech champion with international reach. Founded only five years ago, ABA Life has built an integrated and profitable model combining artificial intelligence, medical technology, telemedicine, connected health infrastructure and healthcare operations. Through large-scale programmes, notably in partnership with public institutions and foundations, the company has shown its ability to turn technological innovation into concrete solutions that widen access to care. “AI for Sovereign Health”: accelerating innovation and scale The investment will support a new phase of growth built around three priorities: accelerating the “AI for Sovereign Health” programme through Mediot AI and the development of clinical intelligence solutions; industrialising and deploying the Group’s healthcare technologies and services at scale; and accelerating expansion into international markets. Building on its technology capabilities and operational experience, ABA Life intends to create a next-generation HealthTech platform combining artificial intelligence, medical innovation and operational excellence, with the ambition of building, from Morocco, one of the Kingdom’s next technology unicorns. “In five years, we have shown that a profitable healthcare technology model, able to deploy at scale, can be built from Morocco. This funding marks the start of a new phase: acceleration and internationalisation. Our ambition is to make ABA Life a global healthtech reference and one of Morocco’s next unicorns. With AI for Sovereign Health, we want to develop a new generation of clinical intelligence in Morocco and take it to international markets,” said Mohamed Benouda, Founder and Chairman of ABA Technology. “From our very first discussions, we were impressed by what ABA Life has built: an integrated healthcare operator combining medical devices, connected infrastructure, care operations and proprietary technology developed in Morocco. We are pleased to support Mohamed Benouda and his teams in this new phase of growth and international expansion,” said Selim Ettriqui, Head of Morocco and West Africa at Admaius Capital Partners. “ABA Life has the qualities we look for in our investments: an ambitious entrepreneurial team, a proven business model, strong technology foundations and significant potential to scale. We are convinced of its ability to become an international healthtech reference and are pleased to support this ambition,” said Marlon Chigwende, Managing Partner at Admaius Capital Partners.

articles.title: Mientras GTA 6 prepara su lanzamiento, trabajadores de Rockstar deciden si obtienen representación sindical
articles.text:
Mientras GTA 6 se acerca a su estreno del 19 de noviembre, trabajadores de Rockstar en Reino Unido votarán si obtienen representación sindical para negociar salarios, horas extras, despidos y políticas sobre IA. La consulta se desarrollará entre el 12 y el 26 de noviembre, un periodo que coincide con la precarga y el lanzamiento de uno de los videojuegos más esperados de la industria.
La decisión importa porque el resultado puede modificar la relación entre parte de la plantilla y la dirección de Rockstar Games. La votación no resolverá el litigio laboral relacionado con los despidos de 31 trabajadores afiliados al Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB), pero podría crear una vía formal de negociación sobre las condiciones laborales después de la salida de GTA 6.
La votación sindical coincidirá con la precarga de GTA 6
Los empleados de Rockstar en Reino Unido podrán votar desde el 12 de noviembre. Esa fecha coincide con el inicio de la descarga anticipada de Grand Theft Auto VI, prevista una semana antes de que el juego llegue a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
El sindicato está vinculado al Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Según la información difundida por la organización y recogida por Aftermath, el reconocimiento permitiría negociar asuntos relacionados con:
- Salarios y bonificaciones.
- Horas extras.
- Despidos.
- Flexibilidad laboral.
- Políticas sobre inteligencia artificial generativa.
Rockstar mantiene cinco estudios en Reino Unido, ubicados en Edimburgo, Dundee, Leeds, Lincoln y Londres. Si la propuesta obtiene respaldo, la organización se convertiría en el mayor sindicato reconocido dentro del sector británico de los videojuegos.
El reconocimiento no se extendería de forma automática a los más de 5.000 trabajadores de Rockstar en todo el mundo. Su alcance quedaría limitado a los equipos contemplados en el proceso de Reino Unido.
Las conversaciones con la dirección comenzaron en julio
El movimiento sindical no surgió durante la etapa final de desarrollo de GTA 6. Desde julio, los representantes de los trabajadores mantienen conversaciones con la dirección de Rockstar para definir los términos del posible reconocimiento.
La consulta de noviembre ocurre, sin embargo, en un momento especialmente relevante para la compañía. GTA 6 llegará a las consolas después de dos retrasos que desplazaron la fecha original de 2025 hasta el cierre de 2026.
La expectativa comercial es elevada. El Financial Times calculó que Rockstar podría ingresar alrededor de USD 1.000 millones solo mediante reservas para consolas y alcanzar USD 3.200 millones durante el primer año. Esa previsión duplicaría los ingresos de su predecesor en 2013.
La coincidencia entre la votación y el estreno sitúa las condiciones de quienes desarrollan el juego junto a las expectativas comerciales que rodean el lanzamiento. Para los trabajadores, la representación sindical busca abrir un espacio estable de discusión sobre decisiones que afectan su empleo.
El litigio por los despidos seguirá su propio curso
La votación no cerrará el proceso laboral relacionado con el despido de 31 trabajadores afiliados al IWGB, ocurrido en octubre del año anterior. Las alegaciones finales de ese procedimiento están previstas para los días 17 y 18 de noviembre, apenas un día antes del lanzamiento de GTA 6.
Shanti Easton-Steel, integrante del comité sindical, explicó que el objetivo es tener mayor transparencia sobre las decisiones de la compañía. Según expresó, sin información suficiente resulta difícil abordar asuntos como la brecha salarial de género, las políticas de pago de horas extras y la seguridad laboral después del estreno.
El reconocimiento sindical no solucionaría por sí mismo los conflictos abiertos, pero permitiría establecer un canal de negociación entre empleados y dirección. Ese mecanismo podría servir para discutir condiciones de trabajo antes y después de la publicación de futuros proyectos.
La nueva entrega llevará a los jugadores al estado ficticio de Leonida, con Vice City como escenario principal. La historia sigue a Lucía Caminos y Jason Duval, quienes quedan atrapados en una conspiración criminal después que un golpe fracasa.
El juego recuperará el sistema de protagonistas múltiples, aunque se limitará a dos personajes. La relación entre Jason y Lucía podrá cambiar según las decisiones del jugador, sin que ello otorgue ventajas directas en la jugabilidad.

articles.title: Cet as de la bureautique avec l'AMD Ryzen 5 et 16 Go de RAM s'offre une jolie promotion de 36%
articles.text:
Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 est un ordinateur confortable pour travailler avec ce grand écran de 15,6 pouces et son format compact pour faciliter son déplacement. En ce moment, vous pouvez le trouver sur Amazon pour moins de 700 euros.
Si vous cherchez un laptop pour vos déplacements professionnels qui mêle performances et prix abordable, rendez-vous sur Amazon où le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 est disponible avec une réduction de presque 250 euros. Pour ce prix, vous aurez entre vos mains une machine performante grâce à l’AMD Ryzen 5 et aux 16 Go de RAM.
Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 passe de 899,99 euros à 659,99 euros sur Amazon
Pourquoi choisir le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 ?
- Un écran confortable : Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 se présente avec une dalle Full HD de 15,6 pouces. Cette grande surface permettra d’avoir plusieurs fenêtres ouvertes côte à côte sans ralentissement grâce aux 16 Go de RAM.
- Taillé pour la bureautique : Ce laptop est équipé de l’AMD Ryzen 5. Pour lire vos mails ou éditer des documents, cela sera idéal. Retoucher des photos sera même possible.
- Pour son prix qui renforce son attractivité : En pleine inflation des composants pour PC, le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 possède un rapport qualité-prix très intéressant au vu de sa configuration
Une configuration parfaite pour la bureautique
Ce Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 est un ordinateur pensé pour les étudiants et les professionnels, des personnes qui sont souvent en déplacement. Il faut donc que cette machine puisse se glisser dans un sac à dos sans trop vous alourdir. Mission accomplie ici puisque l’appareil ne pèse que 1,6 kg pour une épaisseur inférieure à deux centimètres.
L'écran est aussi une réussite avec une dalle Full HD de 15,6 pouces. Un traitement antireflet est présent tout comme un filtre pour limiter la lumière bleue. Vous pourrez donc passer plusieurs heures devant cet ordinateur sans souffrir de maux de tête.
Sous le capot, Lenovo a offert à sa machine un AMD Ryzen 5 et 16 Go de RAM. Un duo efficace pour le multitâche puisqu’il sera possible de profiter de l’entièreté de cette dalle de 15,6 pouces pour avoir plusieurs fenêtres ouvertes côte à côte sans que l’ordinateur ne ralentisse.
Le meilleur rapport qualité-prix du moment ?
Actuellement, le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 coûte moins cher qu’un MacBook Neo. Un peu plus de cent euros séparent désormais les deux appareils. Outre le prix, la machine de Lenovo s’avère plus polyvalente que celle d’Apple. Sur le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3, la retouche photo et le montage vidéo seront possibles même si vous souhaitez travailler sur plusieurs timelines, là où pêche le MacBook Neo.
Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 s’offre aussi un espace de stockage confortable avec 512 Go.
On pourrait donc croire que la copie de ce laptop est parfaite. Cependant, la batterie est un point faible. Outre le chargeur qui n’est pas inclus, le laptop ne devrait tenir que sept heures avant de s’éteindre. Cela peut être insuffisant pour tenir une journée de cours ou de travail.
✅ Les points forts
- Un écran de 15,6 pouces équipé d'un antireflet
- L'AMD Ryzen 5 et 16 Go de RAM
- Un SSD confortable de 512 Go pour la bureautique
❌ Les limites
- Le chargeur n’est pas fourni comme c’est devenu trop souvent le cas
- Une autonomie moins endurante par rapport au reste du marché
Habituellement vendu pour 899,99 euros, le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 chute à 659,99 euros sur Amazon
Si la batterie était au niveau du reste, le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 posséderait le meilleur rapport qualité prix du moment sans trop de débat. Malheureusement, le fait de devoir prendre son chargeur pour partir l’esprit tranquille réduit la portabilité de ce laptop qui était pourtant excellent grâce à ce format compact.
Ce défaut n’est pas rédhibitoire pour autant et la machine trouvera sans doute son public, surtout après cette réduction d’Amazon.

articles.title: Why AI smart glasses need a privacy-first approach
articles.text:
Why AI smart glasses need a privacy-first approach
Why a privacy-first design is essential for responsible AI glasses
Technology innovation should always be driven by one core objective – to improve people’s lives. Unleashing human imagination in new and exciting ways, whether that’s solving complex problems or making everyday life easier.
We’re at a fascinating moment in time, where smartphones have become the de facto platform, but in terms of innovation they have reached a bit of a plateau. New smartphones have largely incremental hardware updates and optimizations without groundbreaking new features.
But then AI came along to shake things up. And that AI, when used well, is making a huge positive impact in people’s lives. AI is best used to complement human abilities – if you look at fields like medical imaging, AI can help to analyze huge data sets and spot patterns for physicians to diagnose fully.
VP of EMEA at HTC VIVE.
Across tech, AI is having a big impact in how we interact with technology. Most notably transforming smartphones and smart devices. And it’s created a new category where you don’t even need to be holding your phone – AI smart glasses.
The AI smart glasses category has been growing rapidly, with research by Omdia finding global shipments of AI glasses had reached 8.7 million units in 2025, up 322% year-on-year.
It’s interesting to look at the ‘why’. On paper, AI glasses don’t have as much processing power or storage or RAM as a smartphone, so how could they be of use? And it's down to the form factor and AI.
Potential for smart glasses
There’s a lot of potential for smart glasses in the B2B sector. Increased productivity, real-time interactivity or enhanced customer experiences, the potential use cases are huge across many verticals.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
One example I love is the potential to change how people engage with cultural subject matter. Imagine a pair of AI glasses as an “audio guide 2.0” that would become a deeply personalized guide, interacting with the knowledge base and curation of the venue – whether it’s a museum, art gallery or historical heritage site.
Visitors can ask specific questions about certain subject matter and get real-time answers as they explore a museum or gallery, making it much more conversational and interactive. Lightweight in form factor, smart glasses can be worn over long periods of time. And in the future, the same tour could generate layers of explanations tailored to different audiences (children, amateurs, experts), without imposing the same experience on everyone. We’re already seeing these concepts being explored by cultural institutions.
This form factor can also blend seamlessly into everyday life, and make tasks easier. How many times have you been somewhere like a concert and witnessed a sea of smartphone screens? The same with navigating around a city. People experiencing life through their device. AI glasses are changing that, allowing you to be more present in the moment without having to live and capture memories through a phone screen.
I actually found myself running late and lost in Rotterdam train station recently. I speak three languages fluently, but if you’ve been to the Netherlands you know it’s hard to guess at some of the words. Safe to say, it was getting stressful. I was wearing AI glasses, and asked it to translate the signs around me – I was on my way quickly.
But with every emerging technology comes new challenges and societal considerations. And there’s a responsibility on manufacturers and innovators to find ways to realize this vision responsibly. For AI smart glasses, there's one crucial piece of the puzzle that will shape their true impact - and that's privacy.
Creating a privacy-first architecture
One element is data privacy. We’re in an era where people’s personal information has been largely commoditized. Where AI smart glasses are concerned, we’re seeing a huge amount of contention about how personal data is gathered by some manufacturers and used to train AI models.
For me, it’s very simple. Our company DNA has always been that privacy should be treated as a core principle, not an afterthought.
But what does privacy-by-design actually look like in practice?
Control of data should ultimately remain with the user. And that’s why it’s crucial to have data stored locally on smart glasses by default – and only transferred off the device when initiated by the user.
And you can safeguard local data even further with military-grade encryption – something that is particularly important for many organizations and will be required when handling internal and customer data. This means that even if someone else tries to take the AI glasses and pair them to another phone, the previous data cannot be accessed.
These concerns over data should also extend to how we interact with LLMs. As AI tools become embedded into our daily lives, the more requests we send to LLMs, the easier it is for them to build a profile of you. And it’s the same for AI smart glasses.
With a privacy-first architecture, third party AI requests are de-identified, so that LLMs cannot build an accurate profile. Policies where user data is not used to train any LLMs should be standard.
There’s also the matter of protecting the privacy of people around you when wearing smart glasses. It’s crucial to have visual indicators, like an LED indicator that lights up during photo or video capture to signal photography or video is being recorded at that moment.
It's obviously not good enough that on some AI glasses, it’s possible to obscure the LED and effectively hide it from view. Any AI glasses worth their salt should use a multi-sensor approach so that photos and video recording should automatically disable if the LED is obstructed or when the glasses are removed.
We collectively have this incredible opportunity - a new technology which combines the versatility of AI with wearables. But AI smart glasses will only be a huge benefit to us all, if privacy is handled correctly.

articles.title: Egypt's Tanmiya Capital closes $130 million fund backed by EIB, IFC and EBRD
articles.text: Egypt-based private equity firm Tanmiya Capital Ventures (TCV) has announced the final close of its second fund at $130 million, exceeding its $120 million target, following a $37.5 million commitment from the European Investment Bank (EIB) through its development arm, EIB Global. The fund is backed by international and local institutional investors, including the Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund (EAEF), European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), International Finance Corporation (IFC) and Egypt's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency (MSMEDA). Founded in 2016, Tanmiya Capital Ventures focuses on growth equity and private equity investments in established mid-market Egyptian businesses. Fund II will target companies operating in healthcare, training, fintech, consumer goods, logistics and transport, providing capital and operational support to facilitate expansion. The fund is expected to build a portfolio of six to eight companies, supporting business growth, corporate governance improvements and job creation. At least 30% of its portfolio companies are expected to meet one or more of the EIB's gender equality financing criteria. Press release: The European Investment Bank (EIB), through its development arm EIB Global, invested $37.5 million in Tanmiya Capital Fund II to expand access to growth capital for established small and medium-sized companies in Egypt. The investment was announced today at a ceremony in Cairo attended by EIB Vice-President Gelsomina Vigliotti and Tanmiya Capital Ventures Managing Partners Ahmed El Guindy, Youssef Ahmed Ayoub and Mohamed Mohsen Mahgoub. The EIB commitment helped Tanmiya Capital Fund II reach a final close of $130 million, exceeding its $120 million target. The fund is supported by a diversified group of international and local investors, including the Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund (EAEF), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the International Finance Corporation (IFC), and Egypt’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency (MSMEDA). Managed by the independent Egyptian investment firm Tanmiya Capital, the fund will invest in a diversified portfolio of established, high-growth companies in Egypt. It will focus on businesses seeking strategic capital to expand, professionalise their operations and strengthen their competitiveness, with investments expected across healthcare, training, financial technology, consumer goods, logistics and transport. The investment addresses the limited availability of long-term equity finance for small and medium-sized companies in Egypt. By combining capital with strategic and managerial support, the fund is expected to help portfolio companies scale up, improve governance and create jobs. At least 30% of portfolio companies are expected to meet one or more of the EIB’s criteria for financing that supports gender equality. “Egypt’s private sector has enormous potential to drive sustainable growth, create quality jobs and deepen economic ties with Europe. Our investment in Tanmiya Capital Fund II will provide ambitious local companies with the growth capital and expertise they need to expand. It also reflects the European Union’s commitment, through Global Gateway and the new Agenda for the Mediterranean, to supporting a more competitive, inclusive and resilient Egyptian economy,” said EIB Vice-President Gelsomina Vigliotti. “The successful closing of Tanmiya Capital Fund II above its target reflects strong investor confidence in our strategy and in the potential of Egypt’s private sector. The EIB’s commitment brings not only capital, but also valuable international expertise and a shared focus on sustainable growth, strong governance and long-term value creation. Together, we will support ambitious Egyptian companies as they scale up, become more competitive and expand their links with regional and European markets,” said Tanmiya Capital Managing Partner Ahmed El Guindy. “Our investment in Tanmiya Capital Ventures Fund II reflects IFC’s commitment to strengthening Egypt’s private sector by expanding access to the long-term growth capital businesses need to grow and create jobs," said Ary Naïm, IFC's Division Director for North Africa and the Horn of Africa. "By partnering with experienced local fund managers, we can help promising Egyptian companies, including family-owned businesses, strengthen their operations, become more competitive, and scale. This is an important part of our broader work to mobilize private investment and support sustainable, inclusive growth in Egypt.” “Our investment in Tanmiya Capital Fund II reinforces MSMEDA’s Fund of Funds program mandate, through which we partner with experienced private equity and venture capital managers and support emerging ones to crowd in private and international capital into promising Egyptian companies. We believe TCVII will channel much-needed growth capital and expertise to businesses with real potential to expand and create jobs, in line with the Egypt’s strategy to empower the private sector and Vision 2030,” said Mostafa Ismail Hassan, CEO of the Egypt’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency (MSMEDA). “We are proud to continue our long-standing partnership with TCV, a team that has consistently demonstrated its ability to invest in and build growing businesses in Egypt. The fund’s oversubscribed close is a strong signal of investor confidence, and our commitment reflects our firm belief in the long-term fundamentals of the Egyptian economy and the central role of its private sector in driving growth and job creation,” said Yasmine Ghobrial, Chief Investment Officer of the Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund (EAEF). The operation follows a Team Europe approach and supports the EU-Africa Global Gateway Investment Package. It is also expected to strengthen commercial links between Egypt and Europe, as portfolio companies may source equipment, technology and services from European suppliers or develop partnerships with European businesses. At its target scale, the fund is expected to build a portfolio of six to eight companies and support thousands of jobs across Egypt. The EIB will also contribute its experience in environmental, social and governance standards and international private equity best practice through its participation in the fund’s advisory committee.

articles.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited VMware ESX Zero-Day to Reduce Audit Trail Visibility
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Wednesday added a security flaw impacting Broadcom VMware ESX to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, after CrowdStrike revealed that it had been weaponized by a China-nexus threat actor known as Warp Panda in attacks targeting the U.S. legal sector.
The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-41709 (CVSS score: 2.7), an a case of insufficient logging that could permit permit a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged.
In an advisory released in July 2026, Broadcom revealed that the issue was addressed in the following versions -
- VMware Cloud Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025
- VMware vSphere Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025
- VMware ESX ESXi80U3j-25429389
- VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.4
- VMware Telco Cloud Platform ESXi80U3j-25429389
The development comes in response to CrowdStrike's 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report, which revealed that Warp Panda had exploited CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day in early 2026 with an aim to reduce audit trail visibility.
Warp Panda "exploits internet-facing edge devices using zero-day vulnerabilities and custom malware to maintain covert, persistent access," it said in the report shared with The Hacker News, adding the adversary "actively circumvents detection by bypassing audit logging, harvesting cloud session tokens, and registering rogue multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices."
The threat actor, also tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221), Clay Typhoon, and VerdantBamboo, has a storied history of weaponizing zero-day vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler and Ivanti Connect Secure devices.
Earlier this month, Google-owned Mandiant also attributed the hacking crew to the zero-day exploitation of a critical improper origin validation flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS score: 9.3) to deliver malware families like SAWFLY and BARECLAW.
Attacks mounted by Warp Panda involve the exploitation of internet-facing edge devices to obtain initial access, after which the threat actor pivots to VMware vCenter environments to deploy custom malware like BRICKSTORM and SharpStorm to maintain persistent access without attracting attention.
Select intrusions have also involved the targeting of cloud services with an aim to extract user session tokens to access Microsoft 365 environments sans raising any credential-based alerts. In at least one case, Warp Panda is said to have registered a new MFA device on a compromised account as a way to set up persistent access even if the password is changed.
"Warp Panda represents a sustained and strategically focused China-nexus cyber espionage threat to U.S. entities across multiple sectors, including the legal sector," CrowdStrike said.
"The legal sector's concentration of client communications, merger and acquisition materials, active litigation strategy, and cross-client access makes it a high-value collection target for a state-directed adversary seeking intelligence with downstream operational utility."
In light of active exploitation of CVE-2026-41709, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the fixes by November 11, 2026.

articles.title: Google y XREAL inician la preventa de las gafas con Android XR, Gemini y funciones con gestos
articles.text:
Las gafas XREAL AURA llegaron a su etapa de preventa como el primer dispositivo de realidad extendida con cable impulsado por Android XR, el sistema operativo que Google desarrolló junto con Qualcomm para la nueva generación de computación espacial.
A diferencia de dispositivos como las Specs de Snap y las gafas de realidad virtual de Meta, estafas son una combinación de realidad aumentada y virtual en un formato de menos de 95 gramos con una propuesta centrada en mantener al usuario conectado con su entorno físico en lugar de aislarlo por completo.
Cómo es el diseño y las pantallas de las XREAL AURA
Las gafas utilizan el sistema óptico transparente X Prism, con un campo de visión de 70 grados que permite superponer imágenes virtuales sobre el entorno real. Incorporan dos pantallas Sony Micro-OLED con resolución de 1.200p (1.920 × 1.200 píxeles por ojo), frecuencia de actualización de hasta 120 Hz y brillo máximo de 1.050 nits, con cobertura completa del espacio de color sRGB.
Las lentes permiten ajustar de forma electrónica la transparencia en cinco niveles mediante atenuación electrocrómica. El equipo cuenta con cinco certificaciones de TÜV Rheinland que respaldan la comodidad visual, el bajo nivel de luz azul y la precisión de color.
Se ofrecen en dos tamaños, pensados para distancias interpupilares de 60 a 66 milímetros y de 66 a 72 milímetros, con apoyos nasales ajustables y compatibilidad con lentes graduadas. El sonido corre a cargo de un sistema calibrado por Bose, con cuatro micrófonos integrados para el control por voz.
El peso reducido se explica por una arquitectura de cómputo dividido: el procesamiento principal y la batería quedan alojados en una unidad externa llamada Computing Puck, que incluye panel táctil y un lector de huellas dactilares para desbloquear el dispositivo.
Esa unidad incorpora el procesador Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite, con un acelerador de inteligencia artificial de 48 TOPS, además del coprocesador propio XREAL X1S, que ofrece una latencia de entre 3 milisegundos entre el movimiento y la visualización de la imagen. El Puck suma entre 12 y 16 gigabytes de RAM, almacenamiento UFS 4.0 de 256 o 512 gigabytes, una batería de 4.455 mAh (34,84 Wh) con refrigeración activa y carga por cable de hasta 57 W.
Funciones con Gemini y el control por gestos
El sistema Android XR permite ejecutar aplicaciones de Google Play, redimensionar ventanas virtuales y fijarlas en el espacio. Dos cámaras realizan el seguimiento espacial con seis grados de libertad y reconocen gestos de las manos, mientras una tercera analiza el entorno, con un indicador LED que señala cuándo está activa.
El asistente de inteligencia artificial Gemini utiliza esas cámaras para reconocer objetos del entorno, responder preguntas y ofrecer información contextual, además de ayudar a operar aplicaciones abiertas resaltando los elementos de la interfaz.
Las gafas se controlan con la voz, con gestos de las manos o a través del panel táctil del Computing Puck, que también admite conexión Bluetooth con teclados, ratones y mandos de juego. Existe además un mando desarrollado junto con GameSir con una tecla dedicada para invocar a Gemini, y un teclado inalámbrico plegable, ambos de venta separada y sin precio anunciado aún.
Entre las funciones más relevantes se encuentra el duplicado por cable, que permite proyectar la pantalla de una laptop o una consola portátil compatible mediante USB-C en una pantalla virtual privada, con las aplicaciones de Android XR abiertas en simultáneo junto a esa imagen. El Computing Puck cuenta con dos puertos USB-C y es compatible con Wi-Fi 6/6E, Bluetooth 5.3 y navegación por satélite.
Cuál es su precio y dónde están disponibles
Los pedidos anticipados de XREAL AURA se abrieron el 28 de octubre en Estados Unidos, Canadá y Corea del Sur, a través del sitio oficial de la marca y de Best Buy. En Japón comenzarán el 2 de noviembre. Los primeros envíos están programados para mediados de noviembre.
En Estados Unidos, la configuración de 12 gigabytes de RAM y 256 gigabytes de almacenamiento tiene un precio regular de USD 1.279. La versión superior, con 16 gigabytes de RAM y 512 gigabytes con un valor de USD 1.499.
El paquete incluye las gafas, el Computing Puck, un cable y un estuche. XREAL prevé ampliar la distribución a otros mercados en 2027, aunque todavía no definió fecha de llegada ni precio para Europa o Latinoamérica.

articles.title: This tiny iFi gadget lets you use your wireless headphones for in-flight movies (to bypass those standard-issue crackly wired buds)
articles.text:
This tiny cheap iFi gadget gives your old iPod Bluetooth support, sends the in-flight movie to your wireless headphones and lets you use your over-ears in the car
Wireless audio, for wired devices
- iFi unveils the UP Travel Max
- It's a Bluetooth adaptor for audio systems that rely on 3.5mm jacks
- Can be used on flights, in cars, and on your ancient iPods
I'm always struck by how odd it is that airlines seem comfortable to let modern tech trends fly straight by.
Only last year, I was given a pair of antique cheap wired earbuds for an in-flight entertainment system, and there's no way of using your own premium Bluetooth headphones instead — that is, unless you own one of a very select set of headphones or earbuds. Models such as the Bowers & Wilkins Pi8, Jabra Elite 10 Gen 2 or LG Tone Free T90S offer a case retransmission function to ping audio to your preferred listening gear wirelessly, from connected analog or digital sources.
But what if you don't want to buy new headphones for better flights? The other option is to buy a Bluetooth adaptor like iFi's new option. It is called the UP Travel Max, and it's up for preorder now for $129 / £129 (roughly AU$260, but iFi's Aussie website doesn't list a price), before going on sale at the end of November.
This device, like the Twelve South AirFly View which arrived only a day prior, is designed to be plugged into a 3.5mm jack. You then pair it to your Bluetooth headphones or earbuds (or speaker, if you're a maverick), letting you connect your wireless option into the wired medium.
The iFi has a 10-hour battery life, supports LDAC and aptX Lossless playback and has a built-in DAC, borrowed from other iFi devices. That's why it's a little pricier than more basic options: you don't just get the function, you want clean audio too.
Audio comes, audio goes
The iFi UP Travel Max is a little different from some other Bluetooth adapter dongles, because it receives or transmits, depending on which mode you put it in.
Plug it into a flight console, and it can transmit from the screen to your headphones. But connect it to your personal vehicle's stereo, and it can receive from your smartphone, to use the big speakers while you're on the go. A button on the device lets you flick between the two.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Using transmit mode, you can also connect wireless headphones to older gadgets, like your classic iPod (which just celebrated its 25th birthday) to avoid using whatever wired headphones you have lying about to enjoy your old-school tunes.
I'm sure there are plenty of other niche use cases that could benefit from the iFi UP Travel Max too; my PC doesn't have a Bluetooth module so I'd be able to use it to pair wireless headphones, for example. The world is your oyster... or you could just use it on flights, to avoid those awful, highly breakable standard-issue buds.

articles.title: Firefox 159 est là et corrige 167 failles de sécurité : à vos mises à jour !
articles.text:
Mozilla vient de mettre à jour Firefox pour corriger une série de vulnérabilités, dont certaines pouvaient permettre à du code malveillant de s'échapper des processus isolés du navigateur. Les correctifs sont disponibles sur ordinateur et Android, sans qu'aucune exploitation active ait été signalée.
Depuis septembre, Mozilla publie une nouvelle version de Firefox tous les quinze jours, et à en juger par la dernière fournée de patchs livrée avec la version 159, on ne s’en plaindra pas. La fondation vient en effet de corriger 167 vulnérabilités, dont 108 présentant un risque élevé. Du moteur JavaScript au rendu graphique en passant par la gestion de la mémoire, les failles touchent de nombreux composants du navigateur, jusque dans les protections censées empêcher une page web compromise d’accéder au reste du système. Vous savez ce qu’il vous reste à faire.
Treize failles qui pouvaient faire céder la sandbox
Le point le plus sensible concerne treize vulnérabilités de type sandbox escape. Pour limiter les dégâts en cas d'attaque, Firefox exécute le contenu des pages web dans des processus isolés aux permissions restreintes. Même si un site piégé parvient à exploiter une faille, cette séparation doit l'empêcher d'accéder librement aux ressources de l'ordinateur.
Les défauts corrigés permettaient justement de contourner ces restrictions, notamment à travers des composants chargés de la navigation ou de la gestion des formulaires. Une sortie de sandbox ne donne pas automatiquement le contrôle du système, mais elle peut considérablement aggraver une première compromission, par exemple lorsqu'un attaquant est déjà parvenu à exécuter du code malveillant. Mozilla ne mentionne toutefois aucune exploitation active de ces failles.
Des erreurs de mémoire à la pelle, mais un décompte à relativiser
Les problèmes de mémoire occupent également une belle place dans le bulletin, avec 97 vulnérabilités de type use-after-free. Ces erreurs surviennent lorsqu'un programme réutilise une zone de mémoire déjà libérée et peuvent, selon les circonstances, provoquer un plantage ou ouvrir la voie à l'exécution de code malveillant.
Mozilla a par ailleurs corrigé des failles d'élévation de privilèges, qui pouvaient accorder à certains processus plus de droits que prévu, ainsi que des contournements de la politique de même origine, censée empêcher un site d'accéder aux données d'un autre. D'autres vulnérabilités risquaient d'exposer des informations sensibles, notamment dans les composants chargés des communications réseau et du traitement audio-vidéo.
À noter que la fondation a récemment revu sa façon de publier ses avis de sécurité et attribue désormais un identifiant CVE distinct à chaque faille de sécurité mémoire découverte en interne, alors qu'elle pouvait auparavant en regrouper plusieurs sous une même référence. Une évolution qui contribue à expliquer le nombre particulièrement élevé de vulnérabilités recensées dans Firefox.
Firefox installe normalement ses mises à jour de façon automatique, mais vous pouvez aussi prendre les devants en ouvrant le menu des réglages > Paramètres > À propos de Firefox. Le navigateur recherche alors la dernière version disponible et propose un redémarrage pour achever l'installation. Sur Android, la mise à jour passe par le Play Store.
Les versions à support prolongé ont également reçu leurs correctifs : Firefox ESR 153.6.0 comble 145 vulnérabilités, contre 80 pour Firefox ESR 115.44.0. Cette dernière continue de recevoir des mises à jour de sécurité sur Windows 7, 8 et 8.1 ainsi que sur macOS 10.12 à 10.14, Mozilla ayant prolongé sa maintenance jusqu'en mars 2027.
- 100 % développé en interne
- Fiable, efficace et stable
- Fonctionnalités d'optimisation de l'interface et de l'expérience utilisateur

articles.title: Attackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Internet-Exposed Palo Alto Networks Management Interfaces
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday warned that threat actors are exploiting the recently patched PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against publicly-accessible management interfaces.
"Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet," the network security company said in an update to its advisory.
The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS scores: 9.2), allow attackers to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on systems running affected versions of PHP. The issues were patched upstream by the PHP Foundation on October 21, 2026, in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
The development comes days after Israeli cybersecurity company Dream said it observed a suspected China-nexus threat actor weaponizing the flaws in conjunction with a local privilege escalation bug in the Linux kernel, tracked as Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300, CVSS score: 7.8), to root 25 servers across the U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea.
Among those were three systems belonging to a U.S. government-affiliated environment.
"The affected devices run specific versions of a large vendor's firewall software," Dream noted. "The attacker then launched attacks against Active Directory. The recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration."
Although Dream did not disclose the name of the affected firewall vendor, the timing of the advisory, combined with the fact that other network security companies have not reported malicious exploitation against their products, suggests that these events may be related.
The Hacker News has contacted both Dream and Palo Alto Networks for comment, and we will update the story if we hear back.
The development has prompted the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to add CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fixes by October 31, 2026.
"This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP web shells and run commands as root," CISA said.
Palo Alto Networks has also noted that no special configuration is required to be affected by this issue, adding the risk is highest on PAN-OS when access to the management interface is allowed from external IP addresses on the internet.
"This issue strictly affects the management web interface, which includes the HTTPS web UI and XML API service," it said. "It affects the dataplane interface only if a management profile is attached to it."
