For PAN-OS versions where fix versions are not yet available, Palo Alto Networks has recommended the following mitigations -
- Route incoming traffic for the MGT port through a DP port, e.g., enabling management profile on a DP interface for management access.
- Replace the Certificate for Inbound Traffic Management.
- Decrypt inbound traffic to the management interface so the firewall can inspect it.
- Enable threat prevention on the inbound traffic to management services.
"Customers with Frontier Virtual Patching (ATP Plus) on PAN-OS 12.2.4 and later versions received advance coverage, released via Threat ID 543004, which was released at 10:21 PM PT on October 20," it said.
"The security risk posed by this issue on PAN-OS and Panorama is minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses according to our recommended best practice deployment guidelines."

articles.title: Nahdet El Mahrousa and GIZ support 12 green scaleups with EGP 57.5 million
articles.text: Egypt's Nahdet El Mahrousa and Germany's GIZ have marked the graduation of 12 green businesses from the GreenShift accelerator, which provided a combined EGP 57.5 million in investment to support their growth and production capacity. The graduation took place at the GreenShift Summit in Cairo on October 27, 2026. Implemented by Nahdet El Mahrousa in partnership with GIZ, and co-funded by the European Union and the German Federal Government, the programme supports green businesses in commercialising sustainable solutions and scaling their operations. The 12 graduating businesses operate across climatetech, circular economy, recycling, sustainable materials and waste management. They include TileGreen Tech, Tilestic, Green Cycle, EGYMAG Biotechnology, Extractor Co., Mycelium, Up-Fuse, ZEE, Yadawee, Mrkoon, PLANQ Electronics and VeryNile. GreenShift received 1,353 applications, trained 46 fellows through approximately 160 hours of training and consultations, and provided EGP 1.3 million in productive assets to 18 fellows. It also supported eight of the 12 funded businesses in completing licensing and formalisation procedures. Press release: Nahdet El Mahrousa (NM), the first incubator for early-stage social enterprises in Egypt and the Middle East, hosted the GreenShift Summit on Tuesday, 27 October, bringing together more than 150 industry leaders, policymakers, investors, development partners, and entrepreneurs to explore what it takes to turn promising green businesses into scalable companies and how their growth can drive change across industries. The summit spotlighted the journeys of 12 green scaleups based in Greater Cairo and the Delta, which received acceleration support and a total of EGP 57.5 million in investment through the GreenShift Program. Implemented by Nahdet El Mahrousa in partnership with the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH and co-funded by the European Union and the German Federal Government, the program supports green enterprises in commercializing their solutions and scaling their impact. Emphasizing the importance of empowering startups to drive sustainable economic growth, Dr. Mona Shehab, Director of the National Solid Waste Management Programme, said: “Startups play an important role in building a stronger, more sustainable national economy by generating innovative ideas and creating new opportunities that contribute to economic growth and help advance the country’s future development plans.” At the operational level, Mostafa Ashraf, private sector advisor at GIZ, highlighted one of the key challenges these businesses face as they work to scale: access to equipment financing. “One of the biggest challenges facing these businesses is the high upfront cost of equipment. The GreenShift program helps address this challenge by financing machinery, enabling companies to continue developing their operations and improve their production processes.” The graduating scaleups operate across a range of sectors, including climate action, the circular economy, and waste management and recycling. They are: ● TileGreen Tech: Transforms hard-to-recycle plastic waste into durable building materials using patented technology. ● Tilestic: Converts single-use plastic waste into tiles, paving stones, and roof tiles. ● Green Cycle for Waste Management: Collects and processes post-consumer plastic waste into certified raw materials for local manufacturers. ● EGYMAG Biotechnology: Uses black soldier fly larvae to convert organic waste into protein, oil, and fertilizer. ● Extractor Co.: Produces essential oils through a circular process that returns plant residues to the soil. ● Mycelium: Uses mushroom-based technology to transform agricultural waste into mushrooms and plastic alternatives for packaging and construction. ● Up-Fuse: Creates everyday products by repurposing plastic and textile waste through a slow-fashion approach. ● ZEE: Produces circular footwear from discarded shoes and other waste materials. ● Yadawee: Produces and exports handmade Egyptian crafts created by local and refugee artisans. ● Mrkoon: Operates a B2B marketplace connecting businesses with verified buyers and sellers of scrap and surplus materials. ● PLANQ Electronics: Develops upgradable computers using recycled materials and repurposed laptop batteries. ● VeryNile: Works to protect the Nile through cleanup initiatives, recycling, environmental education, and community development. Islam Salah, founder of PLANQ Electronics, emphasized the program’s role in helping the company develop a viable business model around its recycling operations. “The funding mattered, but so did the expertise and guidance we received. The program gave us the confidence to pursue opportunities we might not have explored otherwise,” he added. Echoing this sentiment, Dr. Tarek Makram, founder of Extractor Co., said the funding and expert guidance he received through GreenShift helped accelerate the factory setup process. “GreenShift stood out because it offered more than advice, combining funding with training, advisory services with hands-on support.” The GreenShift Program received 1,353 applications and trained 46 fellows through approximately 160 hours of training, consultations, and a retreat. It also provided EGP 1.3 million in productive assets to 18 fellows and supported eight of the 12 funded scaleups in licensing and formalizing their businesses. Held under the theme “Rethinking Tomorrow: From Green Businesses to Changing Industries,” the one-day summit convened stakeholders from government entities, NGOs, development agencies, financial institutions, research and academia, corporations, and entrepreneurship support networks. Participants included representatives from the Ministry of Local Development and Environment, the National Solid Waste Management Programme, and the Industrial Development Authority, alongside ّGIZ, United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Sawiris Foundation for Social Development, Injaz Egypt, Finance in Motion, Dar Ventures, Hassan Allam Holding, Orascom Development, Flat6Labs, and AUC Venture Lab, among other ecosystem partners. The “GreenShift” summit opened with a welcome and keynote session, followed by “The GreenShift Program: What Twelve Ventures Revealed,” highlighting the experiences, achievements, and key lessons of the green scaleups supported by the program. Discussions then turned to investment readiness and growth through “Will You Invest? What Makes a Green Business Worth Backing” and “Ready to Scale. Now What?”, examining what makes green businesses commercially viable and what they need to expand. Sector-focused panels explored how sustainable materials could transform construction and how bio-based alternatives could reshape traditional agricultural practices. “Public-private partnerships are at the heart of Egypt’s sustainability agenda. The GreenShift Summit underscored the importance of cross-sector collaboration in advancing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices, strengthening sustainable value chains, and accelerating Egypt’s transition to a greener economy. Building on this collaborative approach, the GreenShift Program supports green enterprises at different stages of development, helping early-stage innovators commercialize their solutions while enabling growing companies to scale their impact. Together with our public- and private-sector partners, we aim to nurture the next generation of climate entrepreneurs and accelerate the adoption of sustainable solutions across industries,” said Jackie Kameel, Managing Director of Nahdet El Mahrousa.

articles.title: Microsoft Posts Record Q3 2026 Revenue of $92.3 Billion
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Microsoft Posts Record Q3 2026 Revenue of $92.3 Billion
Microsoft Corp. today announced the following results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year:
- Revenue was $92.3 billion and increased 19%
- Operating income was $45.9 billion and increased 21% (up 22% in constant currency)
- Net income was $36.6 billion and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $36.4 billion and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis
- Diluted earnings per share was $4.92 and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $4.89 and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis
- Non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI, explained in the Non-GAAP Definition section below
"We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack," said Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer of Microsoft. "By helping organizations build and own their own intelligence, and earning trust through agent safety and security, we are translating our innovation into growing adoption and real-world impact across every industry."
"We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year-over-year," said Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer of Microsoft. "Results exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income, and earnings per share."
The following table adjusts for the impact from investments in OpenAI and reconciles our financial results reported in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to non-GAAP financial results. Additional information regarding our non-GAAP definition is provided below. All growth comparisons relate to the corresponding period in the last fiscal year.*Impact from OpenAI adjusts for the impact from investments in OpenAI
Business Highlights
Revenue in Agents and Infra was $76.8 billion and increased 25%, with the following business highlights:
- Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 73% to $677 billion
- Microsoft Cloud revenue was $63.9 billion and increased 30% (up 31% in constant currency)
- Azure revenue increased 48%
- Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on an adjusted basis, normalized for a 1-point benefit from in-period revenue recognition in the prior year, and increased 17% (up 18% in constant currency) on a reported basis
- Microsoft 365 consumer cloud revenue increased 17% (up 16% in constant currency)
- Industry solutions cloud revenue increased 10%
Revenue in Devices and Consumer was $15.5 billion and decreased 3%, with the following business highlights:
- Search and advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 12%
- XBOX content and services revenue decreased 2% (down 1% in constant currency)
- Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 22%
Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in the form of dividends and share repurchases in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027.
Business Outlook
Microsoft will provide forward-looking guidance in connection with this quarterly earnings announcement on its earnings conference call and webcast.
Quarterly Highlights, Product Releases, and Customer Stories
Every quarter Microsoft delivers hundreds of products, services, and enhancements. These releases are driven by years of significant research and development investments, to empower customers with greater productivity, security, and differentiated value.
This momentum is reflected in stories that showcase how our technology is shaping industries and driving customer success. We share innovation updates on our product blogs across Azure, Microsoft 365, and more on our Official Microsoft blog.
Webcast Details
Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer, Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer, Alice Jolla, chief accounting officer, Brian DeFoe, deputy general counsel and corporate secretary, and Jonathan Neilson, vice president of investor relations, will host a conference call and webcast at 2:30 p.m. Pacific time (5:30 p.m. Eastern time) today to discuss details of the company's performance for the quarter and certain forward-looking information. The session may be accessed at www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor. Participants can also dial into the conference call at (877) 407-0666 or +1 (201) 689-8023 for international, no password required. The webcast will be available for replay through the close of business on October 28, 2027.
Non-GAAP Definition
Impact from investments in OpenAI. In the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, net income and diluted earnings per share were impacted by net gains from investments in OpenAI, which resulted in an increase in net income and diluted earnings per share of $207 million and $0.03, respectively. In the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, net income and diluted earnings per share were impacted by net losses from investments in OpenAI, which resulted in a decrease in net income and diluted earnings per share of $3.1 billion and $0.41, respectively.
Microsoft has provided non-GAAP financial measures related to the impact from investments in OpenAI to aid investors in better understanding our performance. Microsoft believes these non-GAAP measures assist investors by providing additional insight into its operational performance and help clarify trends affecting its business. For comparability of reporting, management considers non-GAAP measures in conjunction with GAAP financial results in evaluating business performance. The non-GAAP financial measures presented in this release should not be considered as a substitute for, or superior to, the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.
Constant Currency
Microsoft presents constant currency information to provide a framework for assessing how our underlying businesses performed excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations. To present this information, current and comparative prior period results for entities reporting in currencies other than United States dollars are converted into United States dollars using the average exchange rates from the comparative period rather than the actual exchange rates in effect during the respective periods. All growth comparisons relate to the corresponding period in the last fiscal year. Microsoft has provided this non-GAAP financial information to aid investors in better understanding our performance. The non-GAAP financial measures presented in this release should not be considered as a substitute for, or superior to, the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.

Microsoft (Nasdaq "MSFT" @microsoft) creates platforms and tools powered by AI to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The technology company is committed to making AI available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.
Forward-Looking Statements
Statements in this release that are "forward-looking statements" are based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results could differ materially because of factors such as:
- intense competition in all of our markets that could adversely affect our results of operations;
- substantial investments in cloud and AI strategy that depend on customer demand, technological developments, competitive dynamics, and regulatory condition;

- supply or other quality problems;
- excessive outages, disruptions, or capacity constraints of our services if we fail to maintain an adequate operations infrastructure or secure resources necessary to support it;
- potential consequences of new, existing, and evolving legal and regulatory requirements;

For more information about risks and uncertainties associated with Microsoft's business, please refer to the "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and "Risk Factors" sections of Microsoft's SEC filings, including, but not limited to, its annual report on Form 10-K and quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, copies of which may be obtained by contacting Microsoft's Investor Relations department at (800) 285-7772 or at Microsoft's Investor Relations website at www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor.

articles.title: Así puedes crear una lámina para colorear de Las Guerreras K-pop como hokages de Naruto
articles.text:
Crear una lámina para colorear de Las Guerreras K-pop como hokages de Naruto requiere combinar referencias visuales, una herramienta de generación de imágenes y un prompt preciso.
El objetivo es conservar los rasgos que identifican a las protagonistas de la película de Netflix y trasladarlos a una escena de líderes ninja, con líneas claras y espacios aptos para pintar.
El proceso incluye elegir imágenes de referencia, cargarlas en Gemini, definir la composición y revisar el resultado antes de descargarlo. La calidad de la instrucción es clave para que la inteligencia artificial (IA) mantenga la cantidad de integrantes, sus peinados y accesorios, sin perder el formato de dibujo en blanco y negro.
Qué imágenes se deben elegir como referencia
El primer paso consiste en buscar una imagen grupal de Las Guerreras K-pop donde se vean con claridad los rostros, los peinados, la ropa y la posición de cada integrante. Una referencia de cuerpo entero o, al menos, desde la cintura hacia arriba ayuda a preservar la distribución original del grupo.
Asimismo, es útil sumar una imagen que sirva de guía para el universo de Naruto. Puede incluir túnicas de hokage, protectores de frente, kunais, espadas, bosques o aldeas ninja. La referencia debe aportar elementos del anime y del vestuario, sin ocultar los rasgos que se buscan mantener en las protagonistas.
Cómo cargar los archivos en Gemini
Una vez seleccionadas las imágenes, se deben adjuntar en el chat de Gemini, la herramienta de inteligencia artificial de Google. El proceso puede realizarse mediante el botón de carga de archivos o al arrastrar las imágenes hacia la ventana de conversación.
Es posible enviar las referencias en un mismo mensaje. Una debe orientar la apariencia de las protagonistas y otra establecer el vestuario, los accesorios y el escenario ninja.
De qué forma definir la posición de cada personaje
La composición debe formar parte del prompt para evitar que la herramienta modifique el número de protagonistas o las ubique fuera de cuadro. Se puede solicitar una formación horizontal, con una guerrera en el centro y las otras dos a ambos lados, en posturas de defensa o combate.
Para reforzar el vínculo con los hokages, la figura central puede llevar una capa amplia sobre los hombros y sostener una espada. La integrante de la izquierda puede aparecer con una armadura ligera y dos kunais, mientras que la de la derecha puede portar un bastón o una lanza.
Cómo redactar el prompt para lograr una lámina para colorear
La instrucción artificial debe indicar que el resultado será una lámina para colorear, con fondo blanco, contornos negros definidos y ausencia de sombras, degradados o colores. Conviene detallar que las tres integrantes deben aparecer como hokages, con poses diferenciadas y elementos vinculados a un grupo ninja.
Un prompt posible es: “Crear una lámina para colorear en blanco y negro de tres protagonistas inspiradas en la cultura del K-pop, convertidas en hokages de un anime ninja. Mantener sus rasgos faciales y peinados diferenciados. Dibujar líneas negras limpias, sin color ni sombreado, con túnicas de líder, protectores de frente, armas ninja y un bosque al fondo”.
Qué hay que ajustar antes de descargar la imagen
Cuando la composición alcance el resultado buscado, se puede descargar el archivo desde la conversación. Antes, es necesario revisar manos, ojos, armas, mechones de cabello, símbolos de los protectores y uniones del vestuario. Estos elementos suelen presentar errores o líneas incompletas en las imágenes generadas por IA.
La versión final debe conservar trazos cerrados y áreas delimitadas para facilitar el coloreado. Al compartir la ilustración digital, hay que aclarar que se trata de una imagen generada con inteligencia artificial y que no forma parte del contenido oficial de Netflix ni de Naruto.

articles.title: Rogue AI is a wake-up call for UK digital sovereignty
articles.text:
Rogue AI is a wake-up call for UK digital sovereignty
It's time to end the UK's over-reliance on sovereign-washed cloud providers
It is now getting pretty difficult to track every time OpenAI and Anthropic models break containment, wander onto the wider web, and cause unintended, high-risk chaos.
The recent wave of rogue AI agent incidents has now prompted US President Donald Trump’s administration to consider asserting more power over AI tools.
These incidents expose a deep vulnerability for the UK. If advanced AI models are acting unpredictably with sensitive data and carrying out hacking campaigns against real people, what happens when that data is hosted, processed, and governed on foreign-owned infrastructure?
Mark Boost is CEO and co-founder of Civo.
For far too long British IT has essentially handed the keys to US tech giants. The CMA’s market investigation into cloud services found that Amazon and Microsoft control 70-90% of the UK cloud computing market. And another US digital powerhouse in Google controls a smaller share.
These hyperscalers often repeat marketing platitudes about "sovereign" regional data centers located on British soil. I am sorry to be the bearer of bad news but the act of storing data in a UK-based data center is not enough to guarantee sovereignty.
In reality, these tech giants are "sovereignty-washing." Why? Because If the controlling entity is subject to foreign legal jurisdiction, such as the US CLOUD Act, foreign authorities can compel access to that data. It is irrelevant where the physical hardware resides. Hosting data on foreign-owned servers is basically just paying rent on digital turf that remains subject to external laws.
As foreign-owned autonomous AI agents process vast amounts of critical enterprise and state data, and increasingly turn adversarial, the decision to build Britain's AI future on foreign, proprietary stacks looks ever more short-sighted. The potential for financial, legal and national security breaches is simply not worth the risk.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
It is time for the UK to end its over-reliance on sovereign-washed cloud providers and establish true digital independence by backing British tech.
Paying the "sovereignty tax"
By continuing to rely on foreign tech monopolies British institutions are paying a heavy "Sovereignty Tax.” By that I mean the insidious, hidden and steadily accumulating burden of building critical systems on platforms you cannot fully govern.
Hyperscalers reel in UK organizations using aggressive cloud credits and low upfront pricing. But once they are embedded in these cloud systems, those firms often find it hard to leave them. This can come in the form of data egress fees, proprietary technical debt, outage exposure, restrictive licensing rules and audit blind spots. All of these add to the creeping realization that leaving your current provider would be harder, and more expensive, than you ever anticipated.
This explains why an overwhelming 66% of UK IT leaders say they would consider switching cloud providers to regain control of their data and infrastructure. Yet despite this clear desire to break free, the proportion of UK IT leaders expecting to become even more deeply entrenched in US hyperscaler systems has more than doubled over the past year, rising from 12% to 28%.
This seems all the more bizarre given that a recent study from Proton Research showed that 45% of consumers would actively avoid doing business with companies that store data with US firms. Meanwhile, over half (58%) would happily pay higher fees to switch to a sovereign provider.
This forced entrapment dynamic has undoubtedly created an era of digital feudalism. A small group of foreign tech lords own the underlying digital land, while British businesses and public sector bodies exist merely as serfs… and pay a perpetual tribute for the right to operate. And the real-world operational costs of this reliance are coming home to roost. Over the past year, 39% of UK firms were hit by outages originating from US hyperscalers, with resulting risk exposure costing some organizations over £1 million.
As organizations increasingly deploy more and more compute-intensive AI workloads on these platforms, the technical lock-in will only continue to deepen.
Not only does this drain commercial value but it also means high-skilled engineering jobs, and IP heads across the Atlantic rather than staying in the UK.
Legal and security risks
As autonomous AI usage proliferates, legal and operational risks do so too. AI agents interact with database layers, corporate IP and sensitive citizen data while executing the tasks they are set.
If that data resides in a foreign-controlled ecosystem, UK organizations lose jurisdictional control over it. Without true data sovereignty, external powers effectively hold a "kill switch" over the UK’s critical infrastructure. For example, if a UK NHS trust is reliant on a foreign-hosted AI agent for patient triage, a regulatory dispute in another country could trigger a sudden access shutdown. This could paralyze hospital operations and put sensitive health records in the hands of foreign control.
By centralizing the UK’s national capability into a single foreign-owned monoculture, we are also creating a concentrated point of failure. What happens if the US shifts policy and revokes access, leaving the UK powerless over its own critical infrastructure?
The drone and missile strikes that hit Amazon Web Services facilities in the UAE in March that brought two of the three Availability Zones in the region offline was also clear proof that the cloud is not a borderless, invulnerable utility. For the UK to retain true security, it requires resilient distributed architecture.
British digital independence
It should be noted that global hyperscalers undoubtedly have a place in non-sensitive, low-risk applications. But prioritizing digital sovereignty is not an act of digital isolationism.
The fact that the UK government created a £500 million Sovereign AI initiative this April shows that policymakers do recognize the importance of digital resilience and maintaining control.
But that support for domestic innovation will continue to be undermined if public compute spend continues to be funneled towards multi-year deals with foreign incumbents.
The government’s procurement strategy must focus on actively purchasing from domestic cloud providers if its strategic ambition for creating a UK tech powerhouse is to work.
At the same time, proprietary vendor lock-in thrives in closed-loop ecosystems. The UK needs to treat open-source tech and open architectures as national assets. When you use open standards, moving your AI models and data between public, private, and local clouds is painless. You get actual flexibility instead of being locked into one setup. And, crucially, UK organizations avoid being hit with exorbitant transition fees.
Our European neighbors are already leading the way in regard to embracing true sovereignty. France is dropping Zoom and Office for sovereign, open-source ecosystems, and Germany is using Nextcloud to replace Google Docs.
The UK possesses capable domestic cloud platforms. We have the technical capacity and talent ready to scale. And UK firms are crying out for the powers that be to back homegrown tech; 90% of IT leaders are calling for a more proactive government stance in support of British companies. We just need the procurement bravery to match.
Controlling our destiny
The unpredictable and unprecedented nature of autonomous AI agents means the UK must reassess what it has been doing up to now. Building the future of British tech and economic security on rented land is fundamentally contradictory.
The UK already has companies that own the full tech stack required to power modern enterprise. These companies offer the same core capabilities as hyperscalers without the associated sovereign risk or vendor lock-in.
If the UK wants to prove itself as a global leader in AI the country needs to support its own tech providers.
That means distancing ourselves from sovereign-washed cloud providers and investing in open-source infrastructure. Doing so is the only way to protect our data and reclaim our digital autonomy, before it’s too late.

articles.title: Oman's Phaze Ventures launches two AI funds targeting over $75 million
articles.text: Oman-based Phaze Ventures has launched two venture capital funds targeting more than $75 million combined, securing over $40 million in investor commitments to date. The funds will invest in artificial intelligence and deeptech startups in Oman and international markets. Phaze Ventures Fund II is anchored by ITHCA Group, a subsidiary of Oman Investment Authority, as well as Ominvest and Oman LNG Development Foundation. The second vehicle, Phaze Ventures Oman Fund, is backed by Future Fund Oman and will focus on domestic AI-enabled businesses. Founded in 2018 by Abdullah Al Shaksy, Mohammed Al Wahaibi and Masoud Al Rawahi, Phaze Ventures invests in early-stage AI and deeptech companies, with a focus on the GCC and North America. The firm has offices or team members in Muscat, Dubai and Riyadh. The two funds have made 10 investments, including Arabic.AI, Sully.ai, Andromeda Surgical, Boardy.ai and Metal. Phaze Ventures manages capital for more than 50 investors, including sovereign entities, corporations and family offices across the Gulf and other markets. Press release: Oman-headquartered Phaze Ventures announced the launch of two new venture funds targeting over $75 million. Phaze Ventures Fund II, anchored by ITHCA Group (a subsidiary of Oman Investment Authority), Ominvest and Oman LNG Development Foundation, continues the firm’s global AI and deeptech investment mandate, while Phaze Ventures Oman Fund, anchored by Future Fund Oman, establishes a dedicated capital pool for homegrown AI-enabled businesses. Together, the two-fund venture platform has secured over $40 million in investor commitments, with ongoing discussions to grow the funds to $75 million. The announcement comes as Oman builds the International Financial Centre of Oman, a new hub for international companies and investors. “AI is the most disruptive technology shift of our generation. Oman and the Gulf can’t afford to be spectators, and our participation can’t be limited to playing catch-up through investments in hyperscalers, data centres and public market offerings. We need to invest in the founders disrupting industries at home and across the globe, and we need to be a part of that disruption early,” said Abdullah Al Shaksy, Co-founder and CEO of Phaze Ventures. The new funds’ first 10 investments include Arabic.AI, Sully.ai, Andromeda Surgical, Boardy.ai and Metal, with co-investors including a16z, 8VC, Standard Capital, Y Combinator and Baidu Ventures. “We back founders who combine domain expertise with strong engineering and learn from every real-world deployment,” said Masoud Al Rawahi, Co-founder and Partner at Phaze Ventures. Nour Al Hassan, Founder and CEO of Arabic.AI, said: “Getting to know the Phaze Ventures team convinced me they were the right partners. They shared our ambition to build AI our region can own and our long-term commitment to make it happen.” Arabic.AI develops Arabic-language enterprise AI, supported by investment from Saudi Arabia’s HUMAIN and a partnership with Qualcomm Technologies. Ahmed Omar, Co-founder and CEO of Sully.ai, said: “Phaze Ventures understood early how Sully could leverage AI to bring more capacity and real returns to the global healthcare system. They backed us every step of the way as we scaled globally, and were able to connect us with healthcare providers who could put our product to work.” NVIDIA highlighted Sully.ai in a case study showing a 90% reduction in inference costs and a 65% improvement in response times for medical workflows. That early conviction extends to Andromeda Surgical, which Phaze Ventures backed before its US$15 million Series A led by Standard Capital. Nick Damiano, Co-founder and CEO of Andromeda Surgical, said: “Phaze Ventures didn’t shy away from a frontier problem like building the autonomous AI-guided future of robotic surgery. They recognised our team’s rare combination of medical and autonomy expertise, backed us early, and have been proactive in opening doors through their regional network.” The new fund platform has backed players in the capital markets ecosystem, including Metal and Boardy.ai. Phaze Ventures invested in Metal’s seed round alongside Y Combinator and a16z. Metal’s AI fundraising platform helps hundreds of founders manage their capital raise uses AI to connect founders with investors, customers and talent. Usman Gul, Founder and CEO of Metal, said: “In today’s venture landscape, slow capital is expensive. I’ve raised from some of the world’s leading venture firms, and Phaze Ventures brings the same speed and foresight. They moved quickly to back us early and became committed partners as we rapidly scaled Metal’s AI-driven operating system for founders raising venture rounds.” A two-time founder, Usman previously raised US$120 million from investors including First Round Capital and 20VC. With team members in Muscat, Dubai and Riyadh, Phaze Ventures manages capital for over 50 investors, including sovereign entities, listed companies, corporates, family offices and business families across Oman, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, India and beyond. “Investors across Oman and the Gulf want a stake in the next generation of AI companies while they are still taking shape. This platform is our answer” said Mohammed Al Wahaibi, Co-founder and Partner at Phaze Ventures.

articles.title: Sony fait revenir la 3D sans lunettes, mais pas là où on l'attendait
articles.text:
Des années après l'échec des téléviseurs 3D, Sony veut rendre l'affichage en relief plus abordable. Avec son nouvel ELF-MN1, un écran miniature de 6 pouces, le constructeur japonais entend donner vie à des personnages virtuels et des objets numériques, directement chez soi.
Présenté au Japon le 28 octobre, le Sony ELF-MN1 appartient à la famille Spatial Reality Display, jusqu'ici surtout destinée aux professionnels de la création 3D. Cette fois, Sony change d'approche : plutôt que de proposer un grand écran pour la conception ou la visualisation de projets, il mise sur un accessoire compact, conçu pour faire apparaître des avatars et des figurines numériques comme s'ils étaient réellement posés devant l'utilisateur.
Un écran miniature qui suit vos yeux pour créer le relief
L'ELF-MN1 repose sur une dalle LCD de 6 pouces dotée de microlentilles qui dirigent une image différente vers chaque œil. Un système de suivi oculaire adapte l'affichage aux mouvements de la tête, afin de préserver l'illusion de profondeur sans lunettes. Sony a même intégré un capteur infrarouge pour améliorer ce suivi dans les environnements sombres.
Avec sa définition de 1 080 × 2 160 pixels et ses 403 pixels par pouce, une densité record pour la gamme, le petit écran promet un affichage particulièrement fin. Son support transparent en acrylique contribue à donner l'impression que les personnages se trouvent directement sur le bureau.
L'expérience reste toutefois individuelle : une seule personne peut profiter du relief à la fois, à une distance comprise entre 30 et 80 cm. L'écran nécessite par ailleurs un ordinateur ou un smartphone compatible, connecté en USB-C, ainsi qu'une application adaptée. Il ne transforme donc pas n'importe quelle vidéo en contenu 3D.
Des figurines virtuelles pour environ 300 euros
Sony cible notamment les amateurs d'animation japonaise avec HoloModel, un service de Gugenka proposant des figurines numériques de personnages sous licence. L'idée est de retrouver son personnage favori en relief, sans avoir besoin d'une figurine physique.
Le constructeur prévoit aussi un SDK compatible avec Unity pour permettre aux développeurs de créer leurs propres expériences. De quoi ouvrir la porte à d'autres usages, au-delà des avatars et des personnages d'animation.
Mais la véritable évolution concerne le prix. En 2020, le premier Spatial Reality Display de Sony était annoncé à 4 999 dollars. L'ELF-MN1 est proposé au Japon à 53 900 yens TTC, soit environ 306 euros à titre indicatif. Les deux produits n'ont évidemment pas les mêmes ambitions, mais cette différence illustre le changement de positionnement de Sony.
Les précommandes sont ouvertes au Japon, avec une sortie prévue le 11 décembre 2026. Aucune commercialisation française n'a été annoncée.
La 3D sans lunettes ne reviendra peut-être pas dans nos salons sous la forme de téléviseurs géants. Sony semble désormais lui imaginer un avenir plus personnel, sur nos bureaux, aux côtés de nos objets et personnages préférés.

articles.title: Volt Typhoon Used Covert Silent Train Network in Four Zero-Day Exploitation Campaigns
articles.text:
The China-nexus cyber espionage group known as Volt Typhoon has been attributed to a now-disrupted covert access network dubbed Silent Train that has been put to use for zero-day exploitation and strategic access.
"First identified in late 2023, Silent Train uses rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT, and enterprise infrastructure," Lumen Technologies Black Lotus Labs said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "It employs anti-forensic techniques, compartmentalized operations, and post-operation cleanup to minimize detection and attribution."
Its main purpose is to facilitate critical attack phases like vulnerability exploitation, credential access, data exfiltration, and to maintain continued access to victim environments. The activity stands out for two main reasons -
- It singled out entities that could provide scalable access to downstream customers, sensitive networks, or strategic programs.
- It targeted endpoint management platforms, network management systems, SD-WAN orchestrators, and control plane technologies that play a crucial role within enterprise environments.
Hundreds of victims have been identified across telecommunications providers, government, defense contractors, satellite and mission-critical communication services, universities, IT firms, and critical infrastructure such as water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail, aviation, and emergency services.
Volt Typhoon (aka Bronze Silhouette, Insidious Taurus, UNC3236, Vanguard Panda, and Voltzite) is the moniker assigned to a China-linked state-sponsored group known for its targeting of critical infrastructure networks, particularly communications, energy, transportation, and water and wastewater systems sectors.
Known to be active since at least 2021, the threat actor was previously observed exploiting a file upload vulnerability in Versa Director as a zero-day (CVE-2024-39717) to deliver a bespoke web shell called VersaMem designed to harvest credentials and enable access to downstream customers.
| Silent Train session chains through multiple non-U.S. and U.S. hops | 
The latest findings from Black Lotus Labs show that the security flaw was one among four confirmed zero-day campaigns the threat actor has conducted through Silent Train. The remaining three vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876 - A set of insecure deserialization and command injection vulnerabilities in N-able N-central
- CVE-2026-20127 - An authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller
- CVE-2026-16812 - An operating system command injection vulnerability in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator
Separately, Volt Typhoon is also suspected to have taken advantage of a likely zero-day vulnerability in Quest KACE before it was patched in October 2025. The campaign is estimated to have impacted more than 30 victims.
"Silent Train is built around rapidly rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT, and enterprise devices that are exploited on demand, used against carefully selected targets, cleaned up after each operation, and continuously refreshed," Black Lotus Labs said.
"This model has enabled Volt Typhoon to conduct exploitation and post-exploitation operations with exceptional operational security while minimizing opportunities for detection, attribution, and disruption."
A defining characteristic of these attacks is the repeated targeting of systems that can open the door to broad visibility, control, and access across large enterprise environments of strategic value to the U.S.
What's interesting is that the covert access capability began to take shape sometime around November 2023, just weeks before the first round of disruption targeting KV-botnet, an IoT botnet linked to multiple China-nexus state-sponsored threat actors, including Volt Typhoon.
Silent Train's operational activity is said to have surged in the wake of the botnet's second disruption in late January 2024, while simultaneously shifting to an ephemeral infrastructure comprising diverse device types and across geographies.
"Rather than continue using persistent infrastructure, Volt Typhoon shifted to a model using one-time-use chains of compromised devices that it could rebuild as needed," Black Lotus Labs said. "Volt Typhoon rapidly assembled and dismantled transient infrastructure, creating a resilient, secure, and compartmentalized framework that protected valuable access."
| Sector distribution of organizations targeted through Silent Train | 
Described as a "layered, multi-hop framework," Silent Train is designed to let Volt Typhoon operators relay malicious traffic through several devices before it reaches the targets so as to obscure its origins from both victims and defenders. Each link in the chain serves a specific purpose -
- Virtual private servers (VPS) that function as a temporary staging area and allow threat actors to provision and discard them after each session. The sessions begin from VPS infrastructure located outside the U.S.
- Compromised non-U.S. SOHO and IoT devices located across different countries, providers, and hardware that conceal the starting point of the attack.
- U.S.-based compromised devices that function as an exit node before reaching the domestic victim and help evade geofencing and IP reputation blocklists.
No less than 27 device classes, ranging from SOHO and IoT devices (e.g., TP-Link, Intelbras, Ruckus Wireless, SATO, NETGEAR, Zyxel, and Cambium) to enterprise platforms (e.g., Fortinet, Cisco, PRTG, Mirth Connect, and CyberPanel), have been exploited and enrolled into the covert network.
"Silent Train stands out for its operational discipline, focusing on short-lived, selfmanaged sessions rather than persistent relays or C2 infrastructure," Black Lotus Labs said. "To construct these sessions, its operators exploit exposed web interfaces on SOHO, IoT, and other relay devices, then deploy only the tooling needed to enable chained SSH access through the compromised node."
"This included temporary SSH services, keys, configuration files, and 'live off the land' utilities. At the end of operational sessions, they removed every artifact and dismantled the operational chain in their wake. Silent Train sessions lasted about four hours on average, with some lasting only minutes."
Another notable aspect is the designation of certain device types to specific positions within Silent Train. For instance, Intelbras modems have been found to only appear as relay nodes, while Netgear Orbi and Fortinet FortiGate appliances served as U.S.-based intermediary and exit points responsible for interacting with the victim.
Put differently, the infrastructure points to deliberate compartmentalization across layers, confining some device types to certain roles that remain constant while the underlying infrastructure itself changes over time so as to complicate attribution efforts.
By early 2025, however, Silent Train is believed to have evolved from a completely ephemeral relay network to a hybrid architecture that retained enterprise-grade devices for an average of one to three months instead of changing them after each engagement.
Subsequent maturation of the platform introduced reverse-tunnel variants that used open-source proxies like Chisel and FRP to send traffic from infected devices to upstream infrastructure.
Within the U.S., Hawaii, California, and Texas have emerged as the focus areas of Silent Train operations, which boils down to the fact that these states host major military installations, telecommunications infrastructure, defense contractors, satellite communications providers, and critical logistics networks.
"Victimology indicates deliberate efforts to maintain access to critical ecosystems that support defense, logistics, communications, military and civilian operations, especially during heightened tensions or crises in the Indo-Pacific region," Black Lotus Labs said.
"The resulting picture is one of a highly structured framework built to acquire, protect, and sustain strategic access at scale. Through repeated targeting of centralized management platforms and control plane technologies, Silent Train shows how Volt Typhoon systematically pursues and preserves access to some of the most consequential networks in the United States."

articles.title: SpaceX alquilará chips de Nvidia por USD 40.000 millones para ampliar su capacidad de IA
articles.text:
SpaceX asumió un compromiso vinculante para alquilar chips de inteligencia artificial y equipos de centros de datos por un total aproximado de USD 40.000 millones. La empresa de Elon Musk lo informó el 26 de octubre en un documento ante la SEC, el regulador bursátil de Estados Unidos. Los chips serán de Nvidia.
El arrendador será una entidad administrada por Apollo Global Management, una gestora de inversiones de Nueva York. Apollo comprará los procesadores Vera Rubin, la próxima generación de Nvidia, junto con servidores y equipos asociados, y los alquilará a SpaceX para su expansión de capacidad de cómputo en tierra.
Según el documento, los equipos llegarán por tramos y cada uno tendrá su propio contrato de alquiler, de entre cinco y cuarto años. La renta se pagará por trimestre adelantado. Cada cuota equivale a una veinteava parte del costo financiado del tramo, más un interés fijo sobre el saldo y gastos continuos.
Los USD 40.000 millones corresponden a los pagos de capital previstos durante toda la vida del contrato. El interés no está incluido: la tasa se fijará antes de que SpaceX firme el contrato definitivo, de modo que el costo total superará esa cifra.
Los contratos comenzarán a regir cuando se entreguen los equipos, algo previsto para el primer semestre de 2027. SpaceX espera cerrar la operación antes de fin de año, siempre que se cumplan las condiciones pactadas.
Musk habló de cierre; el documento habla de condiciones
El domingo 25 de octubre, Musk escribió en X que SpaceX había cerrado el financiamiento, según CNBC. Agregó que la empresa tiene grado de inversión, una calificación que indica bajo riesgo de impago, y que genera ingresos con Starlink y con los lanzamientos de cohetes.
El documento presentado ante la SEC es más cauteloso. Describe un compromiso vinculante para firmar el contrato, no el contrato firmado, y advierte que la operación podría no cerrarse en los términos o plazos previstos, o directamente no cerrarse.
El financiamiento está comprometido por varias entidades que lideran Apollo y Goldman Sachs, que actuó como único agente estructurador. Fondos y cuentas administrados por BlackRock y por Goldman Sachs Asset Management, y cuentas asesoradas por KKR, también asumieron compromisos de base.
Un negocio de IA que creció nueve veces en un año
El director financiero de SpaceX, Bret Johnsen, dijo en el comunicado de la empresa que ve períodos de recuperación de la inversión de menos de un año en su infraestructura de IA. Según él, el alquiler diversifica las fuentes de fondos y cubre una parte considerable de lo que SpaceX necesita para crecer.
Los chips servirán para Grok, el chatbot de la compañía, y para clientes de servicios en la nube. En su último informe de resultados, SpaceX reportó que la unidad de IA, que llama “Super Intelligence”, ya es su mayor negocio. Sus ingresos del tercer trimestre fueron de USD 7.560 millones, frente a USD 813 millones un año antes.
PitchBook señaló que el acuerdo supera a otro, de USD 36.000 millones, cerrado este verano boreal para comprar y alquilar procesadores a Anthropic. Esa operación también lideró Apollo, junto con Blackstone, y la respaldó Broadcom.
Musk también afirmó que los mercados de deuda se cerraron para las empresas sin ingresos sustanciales fuera de los centros de datos de IA. Predijo que más de 200 compañías que alquilan capacidad de cómputo para IA, llamadas “neoclouds”, sufrirán quiebras y fusiones, y que sobrevivirá un grupo pequeño.
El 7 de octubre, CNBC había informado, citando a una persona con conocimiento de las conversaciones, que Apollo y varios bancos negociaban la operación. SpaceX prevé firmar el contrato definitivo antes de que termine 2026.

articles.title: Oracle thinks AI could fix your customer service problems before you even know they exist
articles.text:
Oracle thinks AI could fix your customer service problems before you even know they exist
Your data could help you prevent complaints before they even happen
- AI agents could tell you where you're going wrong before customers call to complain
- The system works by identifying early signs and fixing them
- By modelling outcomes, humans can make an informed decision on a fix
Oracle has plans to make customer service a lot more proactive with its new AI-powered applications, which now promise to identify and address problems before they even escalate into customer complaints.
Announced at the company's recent AI World conference, the company's new Claw-powered Fusion Agentic Applications for Customer Experience are designed to take on more and more business processes from start to finish, instead of simply helping human workers to get things done.
Service Health Check, one of the applications within the new suite, promises to detect emerging customer service issues and then investigate what's causing the issue to be able to issue recommendations – and even act upon them while keeping humans in the loop at important, decision-making points.
Reactive is being replaced by proactive
The Service Health Check application uses Oracle's new Fusion Claw – an agentic execution system launched just a few weeks ago that can reason across enterprise data, conduct research, model outcomes and carry out actions based on all that context.
Instead of waiting for a customer to complain, the application is designed to monitor early signs that previously led to a drop in retention. In theory, it means businesses can tackle recurring problems before they affect larger numbers of customers, improving overall customer satisfaction.
But the shift toward proactive customer service could have much broader implications on how businesses operate on the whole – where human workers previously needed to monitor performance dashboards and investigate patterns themselves, they can now free them up of significant admin time to manage agentic actions and focus on boosting revenue in other areas.
"Business leaders need to turn growth strategies into opportunities and deliver on customer commitments, but connecting customer demand with enterprise capacity in time to act remains a challenge," Applications Development SVP Kartik Raghavan explained, pointing toward the reason behind why the company launched its new customer service-focused agentic tools.

articles.title: DuckDuckGo pointe les dark pattern de Google sur Samsung One UI
articles.text:
DuckDuckGo reproche à Google d’avoir installé sa barre de recherche sur l’écran d’accueil des Samsung passés à One UI 9, et même chez ceux qui utilisent un autre moteur. Il est quand même possible de la retirer.
DuckDuckGo a publié sur X deux captures d’un écran d’accueil Samsung, avant et après la mise à jour. Sur la seconde, une barre Google vient s'incruster sous le widget DuckDuckGo, juste au-dessus du dock.
Une barre Google qui résiste à l’appui long
S’il est possible de retirer un widget en maintenant le doigt appuyé sur ce dernier, DuckDuckGo explique que la barre Google ne réagit pas à ce geste. Et c’est un design complètement volontaire de la part de Google pour forcer sa présence auprès des utilisateurs, même s’ils ne l’ont pas choisi.
À l’instar de Microsoft qui tente par tous les moyens de forcer Bing ou son navigateur Edge, nous avons donc ici un autre exemple de dark pattern. La barre de Google est un élément du système et son interrupteur est caché au sein des réglages. Il faut appuyer longuement sur une zone vide, ouvrir les paramètres de l’écran d’accueil et désactiver l’affichage de la recherche. On peut ensuite ajouter le widget DuckDuckGo depuis le sélecteur de widgets.
Sur One UI 9, l’écran d’accueil permet de choisir entre Google Search, Finder (l’outil de recherche de Samsung), les deux ou aucun. Cette barre Google n’a pas été développée par Samsung mais reprend ce que Google a fait dans Android 17. Sur les Pixel, la barre de recherche en bas de l’écran a été intégrée au Pixel Launcher pendant longtemps. Google a remplacé son code par celui de son widget de recherche, le même que sur la plupart des autres smartphones Android. Mais ici, contrairement à un widget classique, la barre reste fixée en bas de l’écran. Chez Motorola, la documentation d’Android 17 indique que cette barre est ancrée à la zone des favoris sur certains modèles, avec une option pour la supprimer.
Nous rapportions en novembre 2024 que DuckDuckGo accusait déjà Google de ne pas respecter l’article 6(3) du DMA, qui impose de faciliter le changement de moteur par défaut. Son vice-président chargé des affaires publiques estimait qu’il fallait encore plus de 15 étapes sur Android. Cette fois, l’option existe, mais Android Authority souligne que la difficulté est surtout de la trouver.

articles.title: Un rouleau laveur de 27 cm et une station d’entretien : l’Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni blanc est à 649 €
articles.text:
Le robot aspirateur laveur Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni blanc est à 649 € (-19 %)
Le robot laveur Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni blanc est proposé à 649 € chez Amazon, avec son rouleau rincé en continu et sa station d’entretien automatique.
Amazon affiche l’ensemble comprenant le robot et sa station à 150 € sous son prix conseillé de 799 €, soit environ 19 % de réduction. Le tarif est également inférieur de 50 € au plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours indiqué, de 699 €. Le produit est vendu et expédié par Amazon, avec la livraison gratuite.
Un rouleau rincé pendant le nettoyage
Le robot aspirateur laveur Ecovacs Deebot T90S Pro Omni utilise un rouleau OZMO Roller 3.0 de 27 cm. Celui-ci est rincé à l’eau propre pendant le lavage afin de limiter la redistribution des salissures. Le système TruEdge permet aussi de le déporter vers les bordures.
Ecovacs annonce une dépression maximale de 40 000 Pa et une brosse ZeroTangle 4.0 conçue pour limiter l’enroulement des cheveux. Sur les tapis, le rouleau peut se relever de 15 mm, avec un couvercle qui l’isole des fibres.
Une station pour automatiser l’entretien
La station OMNI prend en charge la collecte de la poussière, le lavage du rouleau et son séchage à l’air chaud. Le robot mesure 9,5 cm de haut et associe une navigation Mini-ToF à la détection d’obstacles AIVI 3D 4.0.
L’ensemble limite ainsi plusieurs manipulations quotidiennes, mais les réservoirs restent à remplir et à vider. Sur Amazon, le produit affiche une moyenne de 5/5 sur 14 évaluations, un volume encore limité.

articles.title: Egyptian climatetech NoorNation secures $1.05 million seed funding
articles.text: Egypt-based climatetech startup NoorNation has closed a $1.05 million seed funding round, backed by agribusiness group Linah Farms, along with climate tech investor Catalyst Fund and Saudi firm KBW Ventures. Founded in 2021 by Ragy Ramadan and Mohamed Khaled, NoorNation develops decentralised clean energy and water infrastructure for agricultural businesses and underserved communities. Its flagship product, LifeBox, provides solar-powered electricity and water solutions for off-grid operations. Linah Farms' investment follows projects involving solar-powered irrigation at its agricultural operations, renewable energy systems at its agricultural school and a solar installation at its Sultan Gardens Resort in Sharm El Sheikh. The investment comes as NoorNation develops pay-per-use solar irrigation solutions for Egyptian farmers, aiming to reduce reliance on diesel-powered pumping systems. Press release: Egypt-based climatetech startup NoorNation has closed a $1.05 million seed funding round, with agricultural group Linah Farms joining its shareholder base after deploying the startup's renewable energy solutions across several of its operations. The round saw participation from climate tech investor Catalyst Fund and Saudi firm KBW Ventures. The investment marks a shift in the relationship between the two companies, with Linah Farms moving from a commercial customer to an investor following projects involving solar-powered agricultural irrigation, an agricultural school and a hotel in Sharm El Sheikh. Founded in 2021 by Ragy Ramadan and Mohamed Khaled, NoorNation develops decentralised clean energy and water infrastructure for agricultural businesses, rural communities and other off-grid users in Egypt and Sub-Saharan Africa. Its flagship product, LifeBox, is a self-contained, solar-powered system designed to provide electricity and water for irrigation, desalination and other applications in areas with limited access to conventional infrastructure. The company has previously attracted investment from KBW Ventures , the investment firm founded by Saudi Prince Khaled bin Alwaleed, which backed NoorNation in 2024 for an undisclosed amount. From customer to investor NoorNation and Linah Farms have worked together on several renewable energy projects, including solar irrigation systems at agricultural operations in Egypt's Bahariya Oasis, a solar-and-battery installation at Linah's agricultural school and a solar power system at Sultan Gardens Resort in Sharm El Sheikh. According to NoorNation founder Ragy Ramadan, the solar-powered irrigation system at Linah Farms' Bahariya Oasis operations has generated more than EGP 3 million in diesel savings, while the installation at Sultan Gardens Resort has reduced electricity costs by more than EGP 2.2 million. The companies have also announced an agreement covering five additional solar installations with a combined capacity of approximately 1.13 MWp across the Bahariya Oasis and West Minya. The projects include solar irrigation systems and a hybrid power station. The agreement brings the combined capacity of projects delivered and under implementation for Linah Group to approximately 1.71 MWp, according to NoorNation. Expanding solar-powered irrigation The funding comes as NoorNation develops a pay-per-use solar irrigation model aimed at farmers who continue to rely on diesel-powered water pumps. Linah Farms is also expected to support financing for this model, extending the partnership beyond its existing energy installations. The approach seeks to make solar-powered irrigation more accessible to agricultural businesses while reducing their exposure to fuel costs. NoorNation's latest investment adds to growing interest in decentralised clean energy solutions for Egypt's agricultural sector, where access to affordable power and water remains a challenge for farms operating outside established infrastructure networks.

articles.title: Corsair Teams Up With Embark Studios for New Arc Raiders Products
articles.text:

Corsair Teams Up With Embark Studios for New Arc Raiders Products
Corsair, a leading global developer and manufacturer of high-performance gear and technology for gamers, content creators, and PC enthusiasts, announced today that a fresh cache of Raider-grade gear has surfaced with the Corsair x ARC Raiders collection. Created in a multi-year partnership with Embark Studios, the collection marks the first anniversary of ARC Raiders, the breakout extraction adventure named Best Multiplayer Game at The Game Awards 2025, with a limited run of officially licensed controllers, gaming peripherals, and streaming gear across Corsair, SCUF, and Elgato. Every piece wears the game's signature four-stripe colorway, and every purchase unlocks exclusive in-game items to carry back into the field.
"ARC Raiders pulled players into a world where every trip topside is a gamble and every extraction is earned," said Tobias Brinkmann, Senior Vice President and General Manager of Gaming Peripherals at Corsair. "That spirit runs through this collection. Working with Embark Studios, we brought together the best of Corsair, SCUF, and Elgato, so Raiders have gear that performs under pressure and looks like it was scavenged from the Rust Belt. We couldn't think of a better way to celebrate the game's first year than by giving its community something built for the next one."Since launching in October 2025, ARC Raiders has become one of the industry's breakout hits and has gone on to sell more than 16 million copies worldwide. The game is set on a lethal, future Earth ravaged by a mysterious mechanized threat known as ARC, where players enlist as Raiders to scavenge a vibrant, atmospheric world while contending with deadly machines and rival Raiders. The collection arrives on the heels of the recently released Frozen Trail, the game's largest content update to date, which takes Raiders to Pendola Pass, a frozen new frontier filled with fresh threats, new gear, and challenges to conquer."It's been an incredible first year for ARC Raiders, and it's been great to see how much our community has made the Rust Belt their own," said Ashley St. Germain, Marketing Director at Embark Studios. "Teaming up with Corsair, SCUF, and Elgato felt like a natural fit, bringing the world of ARC Raiders into the gear Raiders use every day. The collection gives our community a new way to show their love for the game as we celebrate the first anniversary and look ahead to another year topside."
Any Raider knows the surface doesn't forgive a slow trigger or a missed input. As part of this collaboration, players will have access to exclusive ARC Raiders themed hardware and accessories across SCUF Gaming, Corsair, and Elgato, including:

Corsair

Keycaps come in the collection's four-stripe palette.
- SABRE v2 PRO Wireless MG Gaming Mouse ARC Raiders Edition - A 56 g magnesium-alloy shell, 8,000 Hz hyper-polling, and the MARKSMAN S 33,000 DPI sensor, with up to 120 hours of 2.4 GHz wireless battery life for sessions that outlast the extraction timer.

Elgato

articles.title: Google to Allow One-Tap Android App Installs From Approved Third-Party Stores Outside U.S.
articles.text:
Third-party Android app stores can now apply to Google for permission to install apps with one tap, without Android's usual confirmation screens, and to update them in the background.
To qualify, a store must pass identity checks and send Google its full catalog, along with every new app and update, for ongoing malware scanning. Approved stores get the features from December 1, but only on devices running Android 17 QPR2 or later in supported countries, which do not include the US.
Today, a user installing apps from a third-party store must first enable the store to install apps, then confirm each install and each update. From December 1, a store in Google's Registered App Stores program gets that permission automatically once it is approved, and its updates run in the background under the user's own update settings.
Google announced the program in March, alongside changes it said resolved its disputes with Epic Games. Joining is optional, and stores that stay out will continue to operate as they do today.
Under Google's rules, the store must still get the user's explicit consent for each install and "must not install apps silently without user consent." Large downloads and background installs must show a visible notification while they run.
If an install is started on another device, the store must show a notification that does not close automatically.
IT administrators can block registered stores from being installed on managed devices. Google's program pages do not say whether the block also applies to a store that is already installed.
Beyond the catalog scanning, Google's requirements say a store must:
- be registered as an organization and keep its developer identity verified under Android developer verification, Google's identity check for app developers
- send every version of its own app to Google for malware screening, exactly matching the version it publishes on the web and through other channels
- work to keep malware and other potentially harmful apps out of its catalog
- fix major security flaws that come to its attention
- not block other app stores from being installed, interfere with them, or hide or change Android's security notifications
- pay a $10,000 yearly fee, due before Google starts its review
Each store stays responsible and liable for everything in its catalog. Google won't moderate the content in registered stores.
If more than 1% of install attempts or more than 2% of a store's apps are found to be potentially harmful over a 30-day period, Google charges additional fees to screen and clean up the catalog.
A store that fails to meet any requirement, including paying on time, can be removed from the program until the issue is resolved. Google gives notice and a chance to fix it first.
Google's program pages do not describe how submitted apps are scanned, how quickly new uploads are checked, or what results the checks produce.
Registered stores also get a Google tool, the Android Developer ID API, to check whether each app in their catalog comes from a verified developer and can be installed. Google recommends that stores block installs of apps that fail the check.
Android developer verification is a separate Google program, now in its first phase with seven app stores. Since September 30, certified Android devices in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand have checked that apps from those stores come from verified developers, according to Google. Google plans to extend the checks worldwide in 2027.
Availability follows each user's home country. Short trips to unsupported countries do not turn off one-tap installs or automatic updates.
Android 17 QPR2 is one of Android's quarterly platform releases (QPRs). Its latest version, released October 16, is still a beta, and Google's release notes give no date for the final release.
In the US, a separate Google program for distributing third-party stores through Google Play has been in effect since July 22.

articles.title: Una planta de chips en Arizona gasta más agua que los centros de datos de IA de Phoenix
articles.text:
La primera fábrica de chips de TSMC en Phoenix, Arizona, consume unos 18 millones de litros de agua por día, según informó la propia empresa. Es bastante más que los centros de datos de IA de la región, cuyo gasto total se estima en una fracción de esa cifra.
Los datos son de la empresa y de la organización ambiental Ceres. TSMC dijo a The Verge que su primera planta usa unos 4,75 millones de galones diarios (cerca de 18 millones de litros), el equivalente al consumo de más de 14.000 hogares, o el 2% de las viviendas de Phoenix.
Ceres, una organización que asesora a empresas y a inversores sobre riesgos ambientales, calculó que los centros de datos de Phoenix usaron 1.460 millones de litros al año para refrigeración. Esa cifra equivale a menos de una cuarta parte de lo que gasta la planta de TSMC en un solo año.
Sarah Porter, directora del Centro Kyl de Política del Agua de la Universidad Estatal de Arizona, ubicó a la fabricación de semiconductores entre los mayores usuarios industriales del área de Phoenix. Según Porter, supera a los campos de golf, a las plantas de bebidas y a los centros de datos, y queda por debajo de las centrales eléctricas, como la nuclear de Palo Verde.
El plan del río Colorado reduce el agua de Arizona
El contexto hídrico se endureció en agosto. Tras fracasar las negociaciones entre los estados, el Departamento del Interior de Estados Unidos fijó su propio plan para repartir el río Colorado, según The Verge. Arizona perderá al menos 937,6 millones de metros cúbicos de agua por año desde 2027, más de la cuarta parte de lo que suele tomar del río.
Para dimensionarlo, The Verge indicó que la ciudad de Phoenix usa unos 370 millones de metros cúbicos al año. El río provee más de un tercio del agua de Arizona. TSMC recibe su agua de la red de la ciudad, que combina los ríos Salt y Verde, el Colorado, un poco de agua subterránea y agua reciclada.
TSMC planea al menos seis fábricas nuevas en Phoenix y ya recibió hasta USD 6.600 millones de la ley de subsidios a los chips de Estados Unidos, según el medio digital. La propia compañía informó que la inversión del complejo ronda los USD 265.000 millones. Porter dijo que, si se completa, TSMC será “sin duda” uno de los mayores clientes de agua de la red de Phoenix, si no el mayor.
Los centros de datos: poco consumo directo, más riesgo indirecto
Arizona tiene más de 150 centros de datos, según el sitio Data Center Map citado por Grist. La organización de medios digitales calculó que, aun si el consumo de refrigeración se multiplicara por diez, como proyecta Ceres, equivaldría a cerca del 1% del uso residencial del área de Phoenix. Los datos estatales muestran que el uso industrial de agua en la zona se mantuvo estable durante varios años.
Ceres advierte que el mayor gasto es indirecto: ocurre en las centrales eléctricas que alimentan los centros de datos. Según su informe, ese consumo podría pasar de 11.000 millones a 54.900 millones de litros anuales, si se construyen todos los centros previstos en el área de Phoenix. La organización estima que el estrés hídrico podría subir hasta un 17% en la cuenca de Hassayampa.
Kristen James, directora sénior de programas de agua de Ceres, sostuvo que hay riesgos dentro de cada centro y también por la suma de todos los que se instalan en la misma zona y por la generación eléctrica. Porter, en cambio, dijo a Grist que por ahora no ve una situación de alarma.
Las defensas de TSMC y de las autoridades locales
TSMC recicla alrededor del 65% del agua municipal que usa en su primera fábrica, según azcentral. Una planta de recuperación en construcción permitirá reutilizar el 85%, y la empresa apunta a un 90% o más. La compañía estima que entre el 15% y el 20% de su uso diario se pierde por evaporación.
La normativa estatal exige a las ciudades de la región demostrar que tienen agua para los próximos 100 años antes de aprobar nuevos desarrollos. Porter dijo a azfamily que el recorte del Colorado aumenta la presión sobre ese cálculo, aunque la mayoría de las ciudades que dependen del río todavía no han agotado su demanda prevista. La planta de recuperación de agua de TSMC empezó a construirse en agosto de 2025 y se espera que funcione en 2028.

articles.title: Alphabet Announces Q3 2026 Results, Revenue at $127.6 Billion
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
Alphabet Announces Q3 2026 Results, Revenue at $127.6 Billion
Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG, GOOGL) today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
- Consolidated Alphabet revenues increased 25% to $127.6 billion, reflecting strong performance across the business and our 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.
- Google Services revenues increased 11% to $96.3 billion, led by 12% growth in Google Search & other with the year-over-year Search query growth rate the highest it has been in the last five years.
- Google Cloud delivered record growth as revenues increased 103% to $30.7 billion, led by strong growth in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across enterprise AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions, as well as core GCP services. TPU systems sales were also a meaningful contributor to revenue growth.
- Consolidated Alphabet operating income increased 30% and operating margin was 31.8%.
- Net income available to common stockholders was $26.2 billion and EPS was $2.12.
Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, said:
"We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate. Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year. Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it's been in the last five years. Google Cloud revenues grew 103%, powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions. We're also seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers. Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier. Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago. On top of that, the Gemini app has reached one billion users—making it the fastest-growing product in Google's history—and we surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials. We're excited by the range of big opportunities ahead of us."
Q3 2026 Financial Highlights (unaudited)
The following table summarizes our consolidated financial results for the quarters ended September 30, 2025 and 2026 (in millions, except for per share information and percentages).Additional Information Relating to the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited)
At-the-Market Program
During the three months ended September 30, 2026, we issued 12 million shares of Class A stock for net proceeds of $4.3 billion and 24 million shares of Class C stock for net proceeds of $8.1 billion. As of September 30, 2026, $27.6 billion remained available for future issuance under the ATM Program.
Issuance of Senior Unsecured Notes
In the third quarter of 2026, we issued senior unsecured notes for net proceeds of $28.7 billion, to be used for general corporate purposes.
Preferred and Common Dividend Programs
In October 2026, the company's Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $15.63 per share on each of our Series A and Series B mandatory convertible preferred stock (equivalent to approximately $0.78 per share on each of our Series A and Series B Depositary Shares) and a quarterly cash dividend of $0.22 per share on our Class A, Class B, and Class C stock. The mandatory convertible preferred stock dividend is payable on November 15, 2026 to stockholders of record for each of the company's Series A and Series B shares as of November 1, 2026, and the common stock dividend is payable on December 14, 2026 to stockholders of record for each of the company's Class A, Class B, and Class C shares as of December 7, 2026.
