articles.title: DPI Venture Capital closes Nclude Fund at over $112 million
articles.text: DPI Venture Capital has announced the final close of its Nclude Fund at over $112 million, to invest in technology startups across Africa and the Middle East. Established in Egypt in 2022, Nclude came under DPI Venture Capital's investment advisory management in 2025 following a restructuring. The fund focuses on fintech, financial inclusion, AI and technology-enabled businesses, investing between $500,000 and $10 million per company, from Seed to Series C. Egypt remains its core market, with 30% of the fund's investment mandate allocated to opportunities outside the country. Nclude has invested in 15 companies across Africa and the Middle East, including Egyptian startups Nawy, Paymob and Money Fellows, UAE-based FlapKap, Senegal-focused healthtech Kera and Accord Partners, which targets AI applications in accounting and auditing. The final close will support new investments and the regional expansion of portfolio companies, particularly businesses scaling between Egypt, the Gulf and other African markets. DPI Venture Capital is led by Managing Partner Ashley Lewis, alongside General Partner Mohamed Aladdin. Press release: DPI Venture Capital, Development Partners International’s venture capital platform, today announced the final close of the Nclude Fund at over $112 million, supporting its next phase of investment across Africa and the Middle East. Nclude was established in 2022 as a fintech-focused venture capital fund in Egypt. DPI became investment adviser to the fund in 2025 following a restructuring transaction, alongside the launch of DPI Venture Capital, its dedicated venture capital platform. Since then, DPI Venture Capital has selectively broadened the LP base with additional strategically aligned investors. Nclude’s strategy focuses on fintech, fintech-enabled businesses and financial inclusion, and supports companies at the intersection of fintech, AI and emerging technology. The fund invests from seed through Series C, with investments ranging from $500,000 to $10 million, allowing it to back businesses at different stages of their growth. Egypt is a core market for Nclude and a launchpad for businesses with the potential to scale across Africa and the Middle East. The fund also invests across the wider Africa region and the Middle East, with 30% of its mandate available for investment outside Egypt, backing businesses with the potential to expand between markets and build regional scale. To date, Nclude has invested in 15 companies across Africa and the Middle East. The portfolio includes: ● Nawy, the Egyptian proptech company that raised a $52 million Series A as it expands across MENA; ● Paymob, the Egyptian payments business with operations across the UAE and wider Gulf that raised $35 million in a pre-Series C round led by Mubadala and EBRD; ● FlapKap, a UAE-based fintech that raised $34 million in a pre-Series A round to support SME finance and GCC expansion; ● Money Fellows, which raised $13 million to support financial inclusion and expansion across North Africa, including Morocco; ● Kera, a health access AI company operating across Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire; ● Accord Partners, an AI roll-up venture focused on the accounting and auditing space with an immediate focus on Saudi Arabia and the broader MENA region. Ashley Lewis, Managing Partner and Head of DPI Venture Capital, said: “When we became adviser to Nclude, we took stewardship of an existing fund with a strong investment thesis, rooted in improving financial inclusion across Africa and the Middle East. We have grown a portfolio aligned with that central thesis and have built on those foundations by activating more of the fund’s mandate across the region. This has included expansion into themes such as affordable insurance and healthcare access, unlocking credit access for SMEs, and helping individuals save and invest for the future. At the same time, we have selectively broadened the fund’s investor base with additional strategically aligned LPs.” Lewis added: “At over $112 million, we believe Nclude is appropriately sized for today’s market, giving us the firepower to invest with discipline and support ambitious founders as they grow from strong local businesses into regional technology leaders.” Mohamed Aladdin, General Partner at DPI Venture Capital, said: “Across our portfolio, we are seeing ambitious technology businesses increasingly look beyond their home markets as they scale. The growing links between Africa and the Middle East create opportunities for companies to access new customers and markets, whether expanding from Egypt into the Gulf, across North Africa or into Egypt from elsewhere in the region. Companies including Nawy, Paymob, Money Fellows, and FlapKap demonstrate the potential to build regional technology leaders from these markets.” Sofiane Lahmar, Chief Executive Officer of Development Partners International, said: “As one of Africa’s leading investment firms, DPI has a long track record of backing high-growth African businesses through different stages of growth. By institutionalising venture capital as a core part of our platform, we can combine DPI Venture Capital’s specialist expertise with the networks, capabilities and investment experience of the wider firm. This strengthens our ability to support ambitious technology businesses as they scale across Africa and the Middle East and deliver strong returns for our investors while advancing financial inclusion across the region.”

articles.title: Google avoue gagner moins d’argent avec l’IA : l’action Alphabet plonge de 10%
articles.text:
Malgré des revenus en hausse de 25% au troisième trimestre 2026, la maison mère de Google n’a pas convaincu Wall Street. La publicité sur son moteur de recherche rapporte moins qu’espéré, alors que le groupe investit toujours plus dans l’IA.
Alphabet a beau afficher 127,6 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires au troisième trimestre 2026 en hausse de 25% sur un an, Wall Street attendait davantage. Après la publication des résultats mercredi soir, l’action de la maison mère de Google a perdu environ 10% dans les échanges après la clôture.
Un bénéfice plombé par les placements
Le groupe a dégagé 26,2 milliards de dollars de bénéfice net, contre près de 35 milliards un an plus tôt. Ce recul d’un quart tient notamment aux pertes de valeur de ses participations, dont SpaceX. L’activité courante présente un bilan plus favorable, avec un résultat d’exploitation en hausse de 30%, à 40,6 milliards de dollars. La publicité liée au moteur de recherche a rapporté 63,35 milliards de dollars sur le trimestre, soit 12% de plus qu’un an auparavant, sans atteindre les attentes des analystes.
Selon Sundar Pichai, les fonctions d’IA contribuent pourtant à la plus forte croissance annuelle du nombre de requêtes depuis cinq ans. Google tire toutefois moins de revenus d’une requête dans son nouveau mode IA que dans la recherche classique, reconnaît Philipp Schindler, le directeur commercial du groupe. Ce décalage a pesé sur la croissance des recettes du moteur. Le dirigeant cite aussi les effets de change et l’évolution des budgets de certains annonceurs.
Le cloud s’envole, les dépenses aussi
Google Cloud a en revanche dépassé les prévisions, avec 30,7 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires, soit 103% de plus qu’un an auparavant. La demande de services et d’infrastructures d’IA et les ventes de systèmes TPU soutiennent cette envolée.
Pour alimenter cette croissance et ses propres projets d’IA, Alphabet a investi 51,4 milliards de dollars, contre 44,9 milliards au trimestre précédent, principalement dans ses serveurs et ses centres de données. Ces investissements ont ainsi dépassé de 9,1 milliards de dollars l’argent généré par l’activité du groupe sur le trimestre. Le groupe maintient son budget annuel entre 195 et 205 milliards de dollars et prévient déjà que ses dépenses augmenteront sensiblement en 2027.
Ce qu'il faut en retenir
Même si les résultats de Google restent impressionnants, ils déçoivent les investisseurs et les experts en raison du ralentissement de la croissance publicitaire et de l’ampleur des investissements dans l’IA. Le groupe doit donc faire évoluer son produit phare pour tenir tête aux moteurs conversationnels comme ChatGPT et Claude, tout en préservant la mécanique publicitaire qui a fait sa fortune.
Cette transformation se finance à coups de milliards, avec 51,4 milliards de dollars investis sur le trimestre et près de 200 milliards prévus pour l’année. La direction annonce déjà une nouvelle hausse en 2027, ce qui explique que Wall Street s’inquiète pour les comptes d’Alphabet, notamment pour sa trésorerie. Comment rentabiliser ces dépenses XXL dans l'IA ? La question que toute la tech se pose actuellement devant la fuite en avant des géants de l'IA.
Sources : Google et Reuters via Euronext

articles.title: A Google Pixel Watch Ultra could be on the way, but it needs these 3 fixes first
articles.text:
Google Pixel Watch Ultra rumors begin — but a rugged Pixel Watch would need these 3 fixes before challenging Apple, Samsung and Garmin in the adventure space
Can Google make a pebble that belongs outdoors?
A Google Pixel Watch Ultra? Google is reportedly mulling over a sequel to its best Android watch of 2026, and the next iteration might be cut from the same cloth as the Apple Watch Ultra 4, Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Garmin Fenix 9 Pro.
According to Gadgets & Wearables, Google is circulating a survey in its app to 'select users' regarding the future of Pixel Watches. We haven't managed to see the survey — if you do get a screenshot, please email it in to matt.evans@futurenet.com — but G&W states that, among other questions, users were asked 'whether they would pay extra' for a rugged watch and 'what would make the Google Pixel Watch 5 feel more premium'.
That's a clear indication that Google is looking to launch, if not a Google Pixel Watch Ultra, then something along those lines. The use of the word 'rugged' is a dead giveaway: according to G&W, Google is looking at the successes of the Apple Watch Ultra and Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra lines with envy, and is seeking to replicate them.
The only problem is, the Pixel Watch will need some changes before it enters into the Ultra watch arena. Here are three key design elements it needs to adopt, borrow or steal in order to be mentioned in the same breath as the Apple Watch Ultra 4 or Garmin Fenix 9 Pro.
Add a bezel, keep the dome?
The last couple of generations of Pixel watches have sported a domed display, which has become iconic in the world of wearable tech and unique to its Pixel pebble shape. The domed display provides improved glanceability, more surface area overall for its Materia 3 Expressive software design language, and looks the business from all angles.
What happens when we try to rugged-up the Pixel Watch by adding a titanium bezel to the mix? One of the principle functions of a raised bezel is to protect the screen, especially for adventure watches — but when the screen's a dome, the bezel will need to be strangely thick in order to protect the raised section.
Yet, you can't really have a rugged adventure watch, made for a beating, which is all glass — if they're going to get rugged, a bezel must be included.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The folks at Google are much cleverer than I am, and I'm sure they'll come up with a couple of ways to keep the dome and add the bezel. However, I wouldn't be surprised if the domed screen is quietly done away with for the Pixel Watch Ultra.
Improve battery life
One of the Pixel Watch's biggest failings is its lackluster battery life. While each model receives incremental improvements, the drive to also increase the watch's power means it never gets very far. Google will need to address this in order to compete in the Ultra stakes.
The Apple Watch Ultra, when launched in 2022, managed 36 hours of battery life, and since then has crept up to 50 hours with the Apple Watch 4. Samsung managed the get the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 up to 100 hours in low-power mode, although in practice most people will get around three days of use out of it. Meanwhile, Garmin, Coros, Suunto, and others dominate this space, frequently measuring their watch's battery lives in weeks — although their devices tend to be far more specialized and training-orientated than Apple, Samsung, and Google.
Google will have to make strides in this arena if it wants to compete with more expensive watches. It's likely a Google Pixel Watch Ultra would get battery life similar to Samsung's, around 3-4 days of use on paper.
But it will need to be able to hit those numbers in practice too, with long workouts using multi-band GPS and an always-on display enabled. Rugged smartwatch users do not want their tech to die in the middle of an ultramarathon.
Find space for more buttons
The Google Pixel watch is a perfect circular dome, interrupted only by a single digital crown. The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra series was the first in Samsung's rangle to adopt the squircle titanium 'cushion', providing defined sides to the watch, and as such, logical places to put extra buttons. Where the hell do you place them on the watch pictured above?
The reason we need more buttons is that Ultra-style watches have to be able to be operated while wearing gloves during exercise, rather than touchscreen-only. It's why most Garmins have between two and five buttons to aid in interface navigation. A Google Pixel Watch Ultra will need at the very least a programmable Action button-style extra, and preferably more than one.
That redesigned bezel will also have to take button placement into account. If you're thickening up the watch's surrounding casing, you could create something akin to a Garmin Fenix or a Forerunner, which are round watches with thick cases, bezels, and protruding buttons.
But how do you do that while keeping the Pixel Watch's distinctive design language? I guess we might find out one day in the not-too-distant future.

Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: Harry Potter : la première affiche officielle de la série HBO est là, et elle cache un secret
articles.text:
Harry Potter : la première affiche officielle de la série HBO est là, et elle cache un secret
La très attendue série Harry Potter de HBO vient de s'offrir son tout premier poster officiel, et de confirmer sa date de sortie.
La série Harry Potter est sans conteste l'événement télé de la fin d'année. Et à deux mois de son arrivée sur la plateforme de streaming HBO Max, la nouvelle adaptation des livres de J.K. Rowling vient enfin de dévoiler sa toute première affiche officielle, qui met bien sûr son jeune héros à l'honneur.
Un clin d'œil à Voldemort ?
Et oui, car depuis l'officialisation du projet il y a plusieurs années maintenant, les visuels de la série sont particulièrement rares. Les fans (et nous journalistes) ont dû se contenter jusqu'à présent d'une image d'un Poudlard doré et d'un logo légérement remanié, mais c'était tout.
Et alors que la série est attendue pour Noël, HBO a visiblement décidé de réparer ce manque, et de nous offrir donc cette affiche, sur laquelle on peut voir une partie du visage du jeune Harry Potter (incarné par Dominic McLaughlin), avec sa célèbre cicatrice et le reflet de Poudlard dans ses lunettes.
L'image est accompagnée de la célèbre mention "le garçon qui a survécu", surnom de Harry, ainsi que de la confirmation de la date de diffusion : à partir du 25 décembre 2026. Jusqu'à présent, nous devions nous satisfaire d'un simple et vague "Noël".
Un petit détail a enfin attiré notre attention : le reflet vert sur la lunette de Harry. Celui-ci semble en effet être une référence à la couleur de l'Avada Kedavra, le sortilège utilisé par Voldemort pour tenter de tuer le jeune sorcier, et qui se retournera contre lui.
Une manière d'évoquer subtilement "celui dont on ne doit pas prononcer le nom", qu'on ne devrait qu'entrevoir qu'à la toute fin de la première saison, avant qu'il ne fasse sa véritable apparition complète dans la saison 4 de la série, qui adaptera Harry Potter et la Coupe de feu.
La série Harry Potter est écrite et produite par Francesca Gardiner (Succession). Mark Mylod assure également la production exécutive et réalise plusieurs épisodes. Pour la saison 2, Gardiner partage le poste de showrunner avec Jon Brown (Succession).
Composée de huit épisodes, la première saison de la série adaptera naturellement le premier livre, Harry Potter à l'école des sorciers. La deuxième saison, basée sur La Chambre des secrets, est elle d'ores et déjà en pleine production.

articles.title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
articles.text:
A chain of logic flaws, with no memory corruption, can turn a malicious web page into code running on a Windows computer outside Microsoft Edge's sandbox, a security researcher has shown.
Orange Tsai of DEVCORE published the full method on October 28, five months after the chain won $175,000 at the Pwn2Own Berlin contest in May. Microsoft fixed the Edge bugs the day after the contest, so an up-to-date browser is not at risk.
A browser sandbox is the wall that keeps a web page's code inside the browser and off the rest of the computer. Breaking out of it, and then running a program, is what turns a web bug into full control of the machine.
Browser escapes like this almost always rely on memory corruption. This one used none. In his write-up, Tsai describes a chain built solely from logic errors in how Edge and Windows handle ordinary features, and he says the whole exploit is under 100 lines of code.
The result is a universal cross-site scripting (UXSS) primitive: a way to run JavaScript on any website, bypassing the content security policy meant to prevent it.
Because the attack starts from the browser's own process, it can reach sites like google.com that an ordinary web bug cannot touch. Tsai calls this a new attack surface rather than a one-off bug.
This was a competition exploit, not an attack seen in the wild. Tsai demonstrated it on stage at Pwn2Own; there is no evidence it has been used against real users, and the public CVE records list exploitation as none. One step in the chain restarts the browser, which Tsai notes is a convenience for the contest and not needed in a real attack.
The chain begins with an Edge feature for business sign-ins called a conditional access navigation throttle. Tsai found that triggering it lets the browser's own process start a new navigation that is not tied to the page that asked for it, so Edge attaches it to whichever tab is open. That mismatch is the first bug, and it produces the UXSS.
Making it run without a click took four more weaknesses. Edge checked that the request came from a trusted Microsoft site, but Tsai bypassed the check by opening the request from a second window. Edge's popup blocker should have stopped that window, but Edge carried a hardcoded list of allowed addresses, and one of them opened the popup.
The attack also required the victim to be already signed in, which the Edge auto-sign-in feature provides on its own when the user visits a Microsoft site. Lastly, the chain reads the victim's email address from a Microsoft site, assets.msn.com, which returned it to any website due to a misconfigured cross-origin setting.
Running JavaScript everywhere is still not in control of the computer. To escape the sandbox, Tsai used Edge's reading mode, Immersive Reader, which runs under a custom read:// address that Microsoft left off the list of pages barred from running scripts.
From there, the chain called an internal Edge function meant to zip up diagnostic logs and abused it to write a file with an attacker-chosen name and content anywhere on disk.
That file write is turned into code execution in two steps. The chain overwrites a configuration file that controls which websites may launch which protocol handlers, then restarts Edge so the file is read. It then launches a telnet:// link; because Windows does not ship a telnet program by default, it searches the system path for one and runs an attacker-planted copy from a folder the low-privileged user can write to.
Microsoft shipped the fix on May 15, the day after the contest, in Edge Stable version 148.0.3967.70. That release carried three Edge-specific fixes, tracked as CVE-2026-45492, CVE-2026-45494, and CVE-2026-45495. The first is recorded as a security feature bypass, and the second as a spoofing bug, both affecting Edge versions before 148.0.3967.70.
Microsoft's records rate the first two at 5.4 on a 10-point scale, a medium score that reflects a single bug in isolation, not the full chain that strings them into code execution. DEVCORE said the fix came within 24 hours of the disclosure.
Updating Edge closes this chain. Because the fix shipped in May, a browser on automatic updates has long since received it, and no separate action is needed.
Tsai built the chain by hand, over about two months, without any AI help, and frames the work as a point about where human research still matters. "The hard part is finding them, and once you find them all, chaining is the easiest part," he writes of the logic bugs. The research won the 2026 Pwnie Award for Epic Achievement.

articles.title: MS Office 2024 Professional Plus Includes 6 Apps for a One-Time $49.97
articles.text:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
MS Office 2024 Professional Plus Includes 6 Apps for a One-Time $49.97
Microsoft Office 2024 Professional Plus for Windows is on sale for $49.97 (MSRP $249.99) through Nov. 1. The offer reduces the price by $200 and provides a perpetual license for one Windows PC, with no ongoing subscription fees.
The suite includes Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and Access. Together, these apps cover document creation, spreadsheets, presentations, email, notes, and database management. Advanced data analysis and database tools also support work involving business information.The main purchasing distinction is the license type. This Professional Plus offer uses a non-binding, device-linked key, rather than the Microsoft account-linked binding key used by the Home and Business version. Lifetime access applies to the specific device associated with the license. That device-specific arrangement is part of what makes this offer more affordable.
It also differs from the ongoing payment model of Microsoft 365. Instead of paying subscription fees, buyers make a single payment for Office 2024 Professional Plus. For users who want these applications on one computer, this provides a defined upfront software cost.
Office 2024 Professional Plus emphasizes consistent functionality and long-term stability rather than frequent feature updates. It is designed for organizations that prefer a traditional perpetual license, including regulated industries and restricted environments where continuity matters.
The software includes a streamlined interface with dark mode, built-in security and compliance capabilities, and productivity tools designed for dependable performance. It also has minimal system requirements intended to accommodate a wide range of compatible hardware.
Compatibility is limited to Windows 10 and Windows 11 PCs. This license does not support Mac or macOS devices. Buyers receive instant access to the license key and download link.
Get six Microsoft Office 2024 Professional Plus apps for a one-time $49.97 payment through Nov. 1.

articles.title: El jefe de Instagram advirtió que el enojo contra la IA "va a seguir empeorando" en los próximos años
articles.text:
El jefe de Instagram, Adam Mosseri, afirmó que el enojo y la ansiedad que despierta la inteligencia artificial seguirán creciendo durante los próximos dos años. Lo dijo en una entrevista en el podcast Colin and Samir, que The Verge reseñó el 28 de octubre, y reconoció que el rechazo ya no se limita a jóvenes ni a creadores.
Le habían preguntado por la costumbre de estudiantes universitarios de abuchear a directores ejecutivos de tecnología en sus ceremonias de graduación. Mosseri reconoció que a mucha gente no le gusta la IA y describió una tendencia de “más ansiedad, más frustración y más enojo”, sobre todo en las industrias creativas.
“No solo está empeorando, va a seguir empeorando”, dijo. “Vamos a ver más frustración y enojo, parte fundado y parte infundado, durante los próximos un par de años, y eso va a hacer las cosas difíciles para mucha gente, no solo en la industria”.
Mosseri participó del programa para hablar del lanzamiento del formato de pantalla ancha y de videos largos en Instagram, según The Verge.
Los miedos que enumeró el directivo
Mosseri enumeró varias preocupaciones: ser dueño del propio contenido y que los modelos de IA se entrenen con él, la seguridad y el reemplazo de puestos de trabajo, sea de un creador de contenido, un ingeniero o un matemático.
Después dijo que, en una conversación franca con alguien, todo se reduce a “un miedo a quedarse atrás de alguna manera”.
Cómo trata Instagram el contenido hecho con IA
El directivo aseguró que Instagram no ordena de forma distinta a los creadores que usan IA. Reconoció, sin embargo, una duda sobre la calidad de ese ordenamiento: hay mucho contenido de IA valioso y también mucha “basura” generada con IA (lo que en inglés se llama slop). Preguntó si la red ordena ese material tan bien como el que no usa IA y respondió: “Probablemente no”.
También dijo que, a su juicio, el término slop se usa “demasiado liberalmente”. The Verge recuerda que Mosseri ya había tratado el tema en una presentación de Año Nuevo.
Instagram empezó a limitar los perfiles generados con IA en agosto, después de lanzar este año una etiqueta para cuentas de IA, según The Verge. Mosseri sostuvo que la empresa está “empezando a exigir” que esas cuentas se identifiquen como tales, porque considera importante que la gente sepa si lo que mira es real o no.
El problema persiste: The Verge señala que los contenidos engañosos, como los videos falsos de famosos, siguen circulando en la plataforma. A principios de este mes, Mosseri dijo que Instagram está “trabajando activamente” en qué hacer con las falsificaciones hechas con IA.
Sobre una prohibición general, fue tajante en esa misma ocasión: “No creo que sea práctico para nosotros intentar prohibir el contenido de IA en la plataforma”.
Las declaraciones no anuncian una regla nueva: son un pronóstico y una admisión sobre el ordenamiento de contenido. The Verge no recoge detalles de cómo Instagram detectará a las cuentas de IA que no se identifiquen por su cuenta.

articles.title: Et si une seule ligne de commande suffisait pour installer vos logiciels ?
articles.text:
Pour installer un programme sur Windows, vous avez l'habitude de télécharger un exécutable et de lancer l’assistant ? Et si vous voulez installer plusieurs logiciels, vous répétez cette opération autant de fois que nécessaire… Avec Chocolatey, de nombreux logiciels sont installés et gérés depuis une ligne de commande, à partir de paquets qui peuvent aussi prendre en charge les mises à jour et les dépendances.
Chocolatey est beaucoup plus ancien que Winget, le gestionnaire de paquets propre à Windows. Il s’adresse aussi bien aux particuliers qu’aux administrateurs qui gèrent un parc informatique. Il évite de lancer chaque installateur séparément et regroupe tout en une seule commande.
Une commande plutôt qu’un installateur à chaque fois
Avec Chocolatey, l’installation d’un logiciel passe par une commande telle que choco install firefox. L'outil récupère alors le paquet correspondant et lance l’installation. Il est ainsi possible d’enchaîner plusieurs installations sans ouvrir un par un les assistants respectifs. Par exemple, la commande choco install firefox 7zip notepadplusplus -y permet d'installer ces trois logiciels en une fois, sans demander de confirmation.
Un gain de productivité important lorsqu’il faut remettre un PC en état ou équiper plusieurs machines. Les paquets peuvent gérer des dépendances, tandis que Chocolatey permet de suivre les versions installées et de cibler une version précise lorsqu'elle est disponible. Chocolatey permet également de mettre à jour ou de désinstaller les programmes depuis la même interface. Les utilisateurs avancés peuvent aussi créer leurs propres paquets à partir d’installeurs, de fichiers ZIP ou de scripts PowerShell.
- Installation scriptable
- Dépôts internes compatibles
- Client open source
L'outil open source qui simplifie les installations multiples
Chocolatey ne se contente pas de remplacer quelques clics par une ligne de commande. Il automatise l'installation de plusieurs logiciels. Les paquets peuvent être enchaînés pour préparer une machine complète. Les administrateurs disposent ainsi de fonctions idéales pour le déploiement automatisé et la gestion d’un parc. Pour un usage professionnel, il est toutefois préférable de privilégier un dépôt interne plutôt que de dépendre uniquement du catalogue communautaire.
Cette puissance implique toutefois d'être à l'aise avec les lignes de commande et avec le fonctionnement des paquets. L’installation initiale demande généralement des droits administrateur, même si une installation sans ces privilèges reste possible sous certaines conditions. La version gratuite de Chocolatey suffit pour un usage de base, mais certaines fonctions de gestion d’entreprise sont réservées aux offres commerciales.
Chocolatey facilite la reproduction d'une même configuration logicielle en deux coups de cuillère à pot. Pour quelques programmes de temps en temps, l’intérêt est limité. Dès qu’il faut équiper, réinstaller ou maintenir plusieurs machines, le gain de temps est indéniable.

articles.title: Navigating the 'new normal': AI-powered exploits and discovery
articles.text:
Navigating the 'new normal': AI-powered exploits and discovery
AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery and exploitation
Since the launch of Anthropic's Mythos, the debate around the risks that AI-powered tools pose for security teams has steadily ramped up.
Yet, fundamentally, the attack targets aren’t changing: the big shift is one of scale and speed. AI finds more vulnerabilities, giving security teams more to deal with. But at the same time, AI is lowering the technical barrier to exploitation. The result is a situation where the window of time that teams have to respond has drastically reduced.
This has clear implications for how organizations approach exposure management and reinforces the need for solutions that help security and IT teams stay secure amidst this new reality.
CEO and Founder of Intruder.
Vulnerability detection is accelerating
The initial update from Project Glasswing underlined the power behind the Mythos model that has fueled so much speculation and concern.
In approximately one month, Mythos and around 50 partner organizations reportedly identified more than 10,000 high and critical severity vulnerabilities, with 6,202 estimated high/critical vulnerabilities found across more than 1,000 open-source projects.
There’s no doubt Mythos is hugely consequential and its capabilities mark a significant milestone, but the gap between attackers and defenders has already been widening for some time. Security teams have been facing a growing volume of CVEs; in 2025, some 48,185 CVEs were published, a 20.6% increase from the previous year and Advances in AI tools can reasonably be expected to continue fueling this trend for years to come.
This all has huge consequences for security teams. As Cloud Security Alliance analysis has reported, Mythos-type capabilities will mean the number and frequency of complex, novel attacks will rise dramatically alongside the need to patch and respond to AI-discovered vulnerabilities, exploits and autonomous attacks.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
0-day vending machines, no Mythos required
Restricting access to Mythos and other highly capable models is not a practical safeguard. Our research and testing demonstrates the capabilities of general access LLMs in finding and exploiting novel vulnerabilities when being prompted by experienced security practitioners.
One of our security researchers created an automated vulnerability research pipeline, with no human in the loop. On first deployment, this found a remote, multi-stage SQL injection vulnerability sitting on 300,000 WordPress plugins, a process fully automated from discovery to exploitation. The finding, which aligned with an independent discovery by another researcher, was assigned CVE 2026 3985 and publicly disclosed.
And it’s not just the power of AI in finding vulnerabilities that should cause concern. AI-powered attacks can go a step further in automating an entire extortion attempt. An agent can autonomously create and send the exploit, then demand a ransom as we saw when an operator dubbed JadePuffer, exploited a vulnerable Langflow server, harvested credentials, moved laterally and encrypted 1,300 database records in an end-to-end agentic ransomware operation.
Reduce the attack surface as a first line of defense
This is our 'new normal' and LLM models have changed the old assumptions about the speed of vulnerability management. The window that existed between vulnerability discovery, CVEs assigned and defensive action being taken, has fundamentally shifted.
It’s not just about reaction times. Teams also need to take proactive steps to reduce their attack surface as the race to patch can be avoided entirely if assets weren’t unnecessarily exposed in the first place. This is about fighting the battle on two fronts; closing the window between vulnerability detection and remediation and taking pre-emptive action to make the target that attackers aim at smaller in the first place.
These should go hand-in-hand as many teams focus on patching what’s vulnerable, but they also need to question if it should be exposed at all. Attack surface reduction is an area that many organizations may struggle with, but any unnecessarily exposed internet facing asset is now carrying far more risk than ever.
Exposed services, such as leaving a MySQL database or private API documentation exposed to the internet, is an open invitation for attackers and these often don’t even need a CVE to be exploited. This leaves the door open for automated, high-speed attacks.
Always on exposure management
When time to exploit is reduced down to hours, the second key focus area for security teams is reducing the gap between discovery and remediation.
Finding and fixing vulnerabilities requires both context and cadence. Pentesting provides the depth and context but is a ‘point in time’ activity and frequent in-depth investigations can be cost prohibitive for many organizations. Vulnerability scanning provides the cadence but can’t interpret if what it’s found matters for your business environment.
That’s where AI can help and, whilst the traditional pentest isn’t going to disappear right away, we’re at the beginning of an era in which AI offers a new way to support the work that human security analysts and engineers are doing.
Its value lies in instantly alerting teams to new risks, the ability to deploy a pentest on every major release for the fraction of the cost of a manual engagement, agents that can actively investigate and validate findings using the same methods employed by human security experts, and integrating with the tools your teams use to get issues to the right people for fixing, fast.
This way, stretched teams can keep up with the emerging threat landscape. AI is helping teams cross that last mile - validating findings, reducing false positives, and providing necessary context.
These are still relatively early days and the frameworks around the pentest, used by auditors, insurers and compliance bodies, will need to evolve. But the signs are that this new era requires continuous testing as standard practice.
It’s needed because Mythos, and other LLM models, will punish anyone still working to yesterday's timelines. The fundamentals of reducing exposure, validating what's real, and freeing skilled people from the noise haven't changed. What's changed is how little time is left to get them right.

articles.title: PROLED XDR : anatomie du nouvel écran Tandem Oled des MacBook Pro 14 & 16 pouces
articles.text:
PROLED XDR : anatomie du nouvel écran Tandem Oled des MacBook Pro 14 & 16 pouces
Apple fait évoluer l’affichage de ses MacBook Pro avec le PROLED XDR. Cette dalle Tandem Oled cherche à corriger les limites de la technologie Mini-Led utilisée depuis 2021, tout en ajoutant le tactile.
Depuis 2021, les MacBook Pro 14 et 16 pouces sont équipés de la dalle Liquid Retina XDR. Sous l’appellation marketing se cache l’utilisation d’une dalle Mini-Led qui, il y a cinq ans, nous avait impressionnés par des pics HDR inédits dépassant 1500 cd/m² et un noir très profond. Toutefois, cette technologie reposait sur une dalle LCD IPS rétroéclairée par 2554 zones (sur le 16 pouces), chaque zone couvrant environ 30 mm². Malgré les optimisations de l'époque, un léger effet de halo (blooming) demeurait perceptible autour des petits éléments lumineux contrastés, comme les sous-titres sur fond noir.
Avec la nouvelle dalle PROLED XDR annoncée sur les MacBook Pro, Apple délaisse le LCD et le rétroéclairage par zones pour adopter la technologie Tandem Oled. En superposant deux couches émettrices organiques où chaque pixel produit sa propre lumière, la dalle supprime mécaniquement tout phénomène de blooming et améliore grandement le contraste. De plus, le passage à des pixels auto-émissifs réduit le temps de réponse en réglant une bonne fois pour toutes les éventuels problèmes de rémanence caractéristiques de la dalle IPS précédente.
Apple MacBook Pro 14 (PROLED XDR)
Contraste : pourquoi le passage de 1 000 000:1 à 10 000 000:1 ne changera probablement rien
Sur la fiche technique, le taux de contraste passe de 1 000 000:1 sur l'ancien Mini-Led à 10 000 000:1 sur cette dalle Oled, mais ces chiffres marketing n’ont pas grand intérêt. L’Oled reste la meilleure technologie en matière de contraste pour la profondeur des noirs qu’elle offre, mais l’écran Liquid Retina était déjà excellent.
Nous verrons lors de nos tests si les micro-contrastes de l’image sont en effet meilleurs, mais la différence ne devrait pas être aussi flagrante que sur des grandes dalles de téléviseurs.
Une luminosité étendue pour l'extérieur et le SDR
Sur la dalle Liquid Retina XDR de 2021, les 1000 cd/m² constants et les pics lumineux étaient réservés aux contenus HDR, le mode standard (SDR) étant évidemment bien plus limité au quotidien. Apple précise dans sa documentation technique accompagnant la sortie de la dalle PROLED XDR que les 1000 cd/m² en plein écran sont désormais accessibles aussi bien en HDR qu'en SDR (sous 25 °C). Surtout, Apple pousse la luminosité jusqu'à 2000 cd/m² en pic HDR, mais autorise également le SDR à monter temporairement à ce même plafond de 2000 cd/m² en plein soleil.
À l’opposé, la luminosité minimale peut descendre à 1 cd/m². Pour gérer les risques de marquage propres aux composants organiques, le contrôleur d'affichage intégré aux puces M5 Pro et M5 Max applique une compensation en temps réel pixel par pixel en fonction de l'usage et de la température, afin d'éviter le burn-in de l’écran.
Verre nanotexturé
Pour limiter les reflets, Apple annonce une réflectance de 1 % avec la surface en verre standard. Ici, nous sommes obligés de nous fier aux allégations d’Apple puisque c’est la première fois que la marque évoque la réflectance sur les MacBook. Par exemple, le moniteur Studio Display XDR sans l’option verre nanotexturé est annoncé avec une réflectance de 1,65 %. Dans tous les cas, l’option verre nanotexturé reste disponible et, lors de son passage sous notre réflectomètre, nous avions obtenu une moyenne inférieure à 10 %. (lien vers actu labo)
Toutefois, Apple n’est pas le premier constructeur à proposer ce type d'équipement sur le marché des ordinateurs portables. Asus exploite déjà la technologie Tandem Oled au sein de ses gammes et même le GoogleBook 14, associée à un traitement antireflet signé Corning capable d’égaler le niveau de réflectance proposé par le verre nanotexturé d'Apple.
Intégration tactile et fréquences de fonctionnement
Autre évolution notable mentionnée par le constructeur : l'arrivée de capacités tactiles via une conception spécifique. Le capteur Touch est directement intégré à la dalle de l’écran — et non superposé. Cela permet, selon Apple, de réduire la latence au point de donner l’impression de toucher directement l’image. Cette intégration physique au cœur de la structure évite l'ajout d'une couche intermédiaire qui aurait pu dégrader la finesse ou la transmission lumineuse. Elle empêche également la grille tactile de devenir visible sous certains angles de lumière ou sur fond blanc, un compromis que l'on observe parfois sur des tablettes ou des PC portables plus abordables.
La technologie ProMotion, équivalente au VRR, déjà présente sur la dalle Liquid Retina XDR, adapte quant à elle le rafraîchissement entre 10 et 120 Hz, tout en permettant aux monteurs vidéo de verrouiller des fréquences fixes conformes aux normes de diffusion et de cinéma : 47,95 Hz, 48,00 Hz, 50,00 Hz, 59,94 Hz, 60,00 Hz et 120,00 Hz, sans oublier l'alignement automatique sur le 23,976 i/s lors de la lecture plein écran.
Colorimétrie et imagerie médicale avec le protocole DICOM-GSDF
Couvrant simultanément les espaces colorimétriques P3 et Adobe RGB au sein d’un même profil, la dalle bénéficie d’un étalonnage d’usine calibré selon la formule Apple CMF 2026. L’écran intègre également deux modes de référence (DICOM-350 cd/m² et DICOM-600 cd/m²) conformes à la norme DICOM-GSDF (Grayscale Standard Display Function).
Ce protocole ajuste la distribution des niveaux de gris en fonction de la perception humaine et de la lumière ambiante, offrant ainsi aux praticiens une lisibilité optimale lors de la consultation clinique de radiographies ou d’imageries numériques, hors visée diagnostique.
Il reste désormais à vérifier comment ces caractéristiques se traduisent en pratique. Nous avons hâte de poser nos sondes et nos outils de mesure sur un MacBook Pro équipé de cette dalle PROLED XDR afin d'évaluer concrètement les affirmations d'Apple concernant la luminosité réelle, la réflectance du traitement de surface et la fidélité colorimétrique.

articles.title: ¿Cómo funciona el mercado de criptomonedas y cuál es su valor este jueves 29 de octubre?
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 79.940,98 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -1,632% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de -1,871% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.313,52 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 750,22 dólares, con un cambio de 0,82%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 57.025 dólares, tras una variación de -0.17944953.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,08 dólares tras presentar un cambio de -1,4% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: PHP2Shell Attack Roots 25 Servers, Breaches U.S. Government-Affiliated Network
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what appears to be an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted attack orchestrated by a suspected China-nexus threat actor that has leveraged the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to breach exposed systems.
The activity, which was observed on October 25, 2026, involved an attacker combining PHP2Shell with a kernel privilege escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including three systems in a U.S. government-affiliated environment.
"The affected devices run specific versions of a large vendor's firewall software," cybersecurity firm Dream said. "The attacker then launched attacks against Active Directory. The recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration."
The name of the affected vendor was not disclosed, but the Israeli company said it notified the entity. The attack chain essentially brings together two sets of vulnerabilities impacting PHP and the Linux kernel -
- PHP2Shell, a pair of flaws tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS scores: 9.2) that could result in unauthenticated remote code execution
- Fragnesia, a Linux kernel local privilege escalation vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-46300 (CVSS score: 7.8)
"The implementation we recovered is a custom, non-public build, not a copy of any known public exploit for PHP2Shell," Dream researchers explained. "It follows the same underlying concept but appears to have been independently developed and tailored specifically for the targeted firewall platform."
"The vulnerability targets PHP's session.upload_progress mechanism on the firewall's appweb management server. The firewall OS uses PHP 8.0.30 with a high memory limit that enables the memory corruption stages of the attack."
The custom weaponization of the PHP2Shell exploit chain, coupled with CVE-2026-46300, is said to have rooted 25 servers across the U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea.
Artifacts discovered by Dream indicate that the operation started with exploit development in a lab environment before obtaining persistent access to a U.S. government organization's internal Active Directory domain.
"Once rooted, the attacker zeroed in on three specific servers in a U.S. government-affiliated environment," the company noted.
The links to AI-assisted tooling stem from evidence pointing to the installation of Anthropic's Claude Code in the attack infrastructure, along with the presence of API keys for FOFA and an AI-powered offensive security platform called aiscan configured with large language models (LLMs) from DeepSeek and Kimi.
What's more, the code structure, commenting style, and consistency across nearly 40 scripts suggest the use of AI to augment the development process. The entire operation, per Dream, unfolds as follows -
- Attacker uses FOFA to identify approximately 19,000 internet-facing firewalls with exposed management interfaces worldwide.
- A custom version scanner is executed to determine which among those devices are online and what operating system version they are running. About 5,000 devices respond with the version information.
- The attacker filters the servers to those located in the U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, and then limits the scope to systems that match newer release branches running PHP 8.0.30. This step yields 240 targets.
- The target list is fed as input to an automated batch runner that exploits the PHP2Shell-Fragnesia chain, plants a PHP web shell on a publicly accessible directory on the firewall, verifies root access, and logs the target's hostname and IP to a CSV file. This step allows the attacker to gain root access to 24 servers.
- Two of the successfully compromised systems are identified as belonging to a U.S. government-affiliated organization. One of them crashes shortly after it was rooted on October 23, 2026, at 6:14 p.m. UTC and never comes back online. The attacker carries out a dedicated campaign to successfully root a second system on October 24, 2026, at 10:09 a.m. UTC.
- The attacker exploits the second system to build a persistent channel into the internal network via a reverse SSH tunnel connecting the compromised firewall back to the operator's infrastructure. At 11:35 a.m. UTC, a third government server is compromised using the same method, the only difference being that this was an internal firewall management server only reachable through the tunnel. The total number of rooted servers reaches 25.
- The attacker targets Active Directory to decrypt the LDAP service account password, enumerate users, and spray passwords against every user account using organization-themed passwords in an attempt to extract credentials. The operation also attempts to create backdoor Active Directory accounts.
It's unclear if the activity allowed the threat actor to successfully find valid credentials or create backdoor accounts. As a result, the full extent of the compromise remains indeterminate.
"Since [the] U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea are the four primary strategic adversaries and intelligence targets for Chinese state-aligned cyber operations in the Pacific theater, this indicates potential nation-state adversary efforts," Dream said.
"The operation illustrates how an exposed management interface can become a path into an organization's identity infrastructure. The 22 other rooted firewalls remain parked with active web shells. The persistent tunnel into the US government organization is likely still running. And the attacker still has 19,000 fingerprinted targets they can revisit as they develop profiles for additional OS versions."
The disclosure comes as the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities have witnessed only limited exploitation in the wild, with threat actors highlighting the challenges in converting a proof-of-concept (PoC) into a reliable attack vector against real targets despite integrating them into their campaigns.
"In practice it's unexploitable crap. To exploit real targets you need the offsets from libphp.so, which are unique to every build and impossible to brute-force. You can reproduce it on your own test bench, or if you already have access to the target's file system," a member who goes by the handle c0d3x on the XSS forum said, according to Flare.

articles.title: HyperX Omen 35L review: A polished gaming PC for deep pockets
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The HyperX Omen 35L delivers a premium gaming PC experience, pairing a striking black-and-white styling, quiet operation, enthusiast-grade features, and excellent 4K gaming performance. Top-end configurations make the most sense, as entry-level models are expensive for the hardware.
Reasons to buy
- + Impressive gaming performance
- + Sharp black-and-white case
- + Standard liquid cooling
- + Quiet operation
- + Fully modular power supply
Reasons to avoid
- - Steep starting price
- - No USB4/Thunderbolt 4 ports
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
HP’s HyperX Omen 35L is ambitious, and it’s hard not to be impressed by it in our maxed-out test guise with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D and Nvidia RTX 5080. From its monochrome design and extensive RGB lighting to its top-tier components, it checks the boxes enthusiasts are looking for.
But when a PC is $6,211 like our test configuration, it raises the question of whether the Omen 35L’s blend of style, performance, and premium features is enough to justify a purchase, even if that's what high-end PCs cost right now.
Design of the HyperX Omen 35L
The HyperX Omen 35L’s black and white case stands out, looking refreshingly modern, even though parent company HP has used similar designs before. At 8.27 by 16.06 by 16.14 inches, it’s firmly in mid-tower territory. The metal case feels reassuringly solid and makes extensive use of tempered glass. Bright RGB fans shine through the front while many RGB-lit components are visible through the side panel. It’s a classy system.
The contrast continues inside, where the black motherboard, graphics card, and power supply are easily visible against the white case. The white liquid cooling loops are especially attractive, as is the CPU cooler featuring its own LCD panel. The latter shows CPU and GPU temperatures.
HyperX Omen 35L Specifications
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D | 
| Motherboard | HP AMD B850 | 
| Memory | 64GB DDR5-6000 (2x 32GB) | 
| Graphics | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 (16GB GDDR7, 2,617 MHz boost clock) | 
| Storage | 2x 1TB PCIe 5.0 SSDs (non-RAID) | 
| Networking | Realtek 8922AE Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Front Ports | 10 Gbps USB-C, 2x 5 Gbps USB-A, audio combo jack | 
| Rear Ports | 2x 10 Gbps USB-C, 2x 5 Gbps USB-A, 4x USB 2.0, DisplayPort 1.4, Ethernet | 
| Power Supply | 1,000 W fully modular | 
| Cooling | 240 mm LCD liquid cooler | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Pro | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 8.27 x 16.06 x 16.14 inches (210 x 408 x 410 mm) | 
| Price (as configured) | $6,210.98 | 
Ports and Upgradeability on the HyperX Omen 35L
HyperX’s top-mounted front ports include USB-C (10 Gbps), two USB-A (5 Gbps), and an audio combo jack. This location works well if the desktop is on the floor.
At the back, the tower offers a pair of USB-C ports (10 Gbps), two USB-A (5 Gbps), four USB 2.0, DisplayPort 1.4 output, Ethernet, and audio jacks. It’s disappointing to see a desktop this expensive offers neither USB4 nor Thunderbolt 4, though it does include Wi-iFi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 from a Realtek 8922AE networking card. The wireless antennas are built into the chassis, eliminating the need for external protrusions. It’s also notable that HP offers a Clear CMOS button, a surprise on a mainstream tower.
The HyperX Omen 35L offers about as much upgradeability as expected from a mid-tower, without proprietary parts. Its side doors are secured with thumbscrews; the slide rearward and away. The mATX-style motherboard offers four DDR5 DIMM slots, populated in our review unit with two 32GB RGB HyperX modules running at 6,000 MHz.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The system also supports two M.2 2280 drives. The primary slot is covered in a substantial heatsink just above the RTX 5080. Accessing the other slot requires removing the RTX 5080. The card is secured with five screws, two of which hold it to the front support bracket. Deft fingers are required to reinstall the screws at the back of the card.
HP’s wiring work is tidy for a mainstream tower. Sleeved cables would have improved the refinement. On the plus side, HP includes a fully modular power supply, an uncommon feature in big box systems.
Gaming and Graphics on the HyperX Omen 35L
We tested the HyperX Omen 35L in a maxed-out configuration featuring a Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, 64GB of RAM, and a GeForce RTX 5080.
I fired up 007 First Light to test out this system’s prowess. At a 3840 x 2160 resolution with high settings and post effects enabled, I saw up to 120 frames per second (fps) indoors and in the mid-90 fps range in more complex scenes without DLSS. The game never stuttered and remained supremely playable.
The systems we’re using for comparison include a pair of RTX 5090 towers, the Alienware Area-51 (Ryzen 9950X3D, $5,749.99 when tested, $8,899.99 as of this writing) and the Maingear MG-1 (Ryzen 9 9950X3D2, $7,067 when tested, $9,076 as of this writing), plus Corsair’s Vengeance a7500 powered by a Ryzen 7 9800X3D and an RTX 5070 Ti ($2,799.99 when tested, $3,299.99 as of this writing). With its RTX 5080, the HyperX desktop ought to slot in the middle of this group.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The HyperX desktop performed as expected given its RTX 5080. That said, the 1080p numbers show significant variance from system to system. In Shadow of the Tomb Raider (Highest detail preset), the HyperX produced 300 fps to outperform even the Alienware (248 fps), though it couldn’t catch the Maingear (355 fps). In other instances, even the RTX 5070-powered Corsair was able to pull ahead as seen in Far Cry 6 (Ultra settings), where it produced 197 fps against the HyperX’s 141 fps.
But these desktops are designed for 4K play. At that resolution, the HyperX’s RTX 5080 produced admirable numbers. Naturally, it wasn’t in the same league as the RTX 5090 systems; in Red Dead Redemption 2 (Medium settings), the HyperX produced 83 fps against the Alienware’s 122 fps and the Maingear’s 121 fps, and in Borderlands 3 (Badass settings), the HyperX landed at 115 fps against Alienware’s 166 fps and Maingear’s 186 fps. The differences narrowed in Far Cry 6, with the HyperX producing 118 fps to Alienware’s 128 fps. The largest deltas were seen in Cyberpunk 2077 (Ray Tracing Ultra preset), where the HyperX produced 36 fps, well ahead of the Corsair’s 29 fps, but significantly behind the Alienware’s 55 fps. Overall, though, this HyperX desktop is well-suited to 4K play.
We stress-test gaming desktops running 15 loops of the Metro Exodus benchmark at RTX settings, simulating about half an hour of gameplay. During the test, the HyperX desktop averaged 172.21 fps across all runs with a sub-one fps variance, indicating stable performance. During the test, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D averaged 4.79 GHz and 48 degrees Celsius while the RTX 5080 ran at 2.74 GHz and 50 C.
Productivity Performance on the HyperX Omen 35L
Our HyperX test unit features a Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, 64GB of RAM, and two 1TB PCIe 5.0 drives running separately, one hosting the OS andthe other for storage.
Featuring the same Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, the HyperX and Alienware systems performed similarly across our CPU tests. In Geekbench 6, the HyperX system produced 19,923 points against Alienware’s 20,411 points, though it was handily outperformed by the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2-powered Maingear, at 23,741 points. With fewer cores, the Ryzen 7 9800X3D-powered Corsair finished last, at 18,124 points.
The HyperX desktop finished our Handbrake 4K-to-1080p video transcoding test in 1 minute and 47 seconds, tying the Alienware, though the Maingear edged ahead, at 1:32. The Corsair took nearly twice as long, at 3:02.
In our 25GB file transfer test, the HyperX’s average transfer speed of 3,197.42 MBps was excellent, just behind Alienware’s 3,414.29 MBps and ahead of the Corsair’s 2,659.94 MBps and Maingear’s 2,782.43 MBps.
Software and Warranty on the HyperX Omen 35L
HP includes several useful apps. Omen Gaming Hub app provides performance control, with per-fan RPM settings and, in Extreme mode, PPT and EDC settings for the Ryzen 9 CPU. The Advanced Performance Tuning section also provides PBO, CPU Boost, and voltage curve controls plus a benchmark to test your settings. For quick access, the app provides an overlay that shows your power profiles and system monitoring, including component temperatures and fan speeds.
Gaming Hub also provides customization of the LCD display on the liquid cooler. Many faces are available, from system monitoring to static images, GIFs, videos, and a clock. It seems simple, but it’s one of the most fun features of the system, allowing you to easily change up the look.
Lighting is managed through Omen Light Studio, which provides per-device RGB control. Fine control is possible – each of the five fans has 10 LEDs, which are individually selectable. Clicking and dragging selects multiple fans and LEDs at a time, to which you can apply preconfigured light recipes – Galaxy, Ocean, Jungle, Volcano, and Omen – and apply an effect, such as wave, static, ambient, breathing, color cycle, an audio visualizer, and radial. The speed and direction of the effect is also configurable. You can also create layered effects and save everything in profiles that you can export or import. HP covers the HyperX Omen 35L with a standard one-year warranty.
HyperX Omen 35L Configurations
We tested the HyperX Omen 35L with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D processor, 64GB of dual-channel DDR5-6000 RAM, GeForce RTX 5080 graphics, Windows 11 Pro, and two 1TB PCIe 5.0 solid-state drives. The system uses a 1,000W power supply and a 240 mm liquid CPU cooling with a built-in LCD display. This configuration represents the top of the stack, retailing for $6,210.98.
The entry-level is probably where the Omen 35L offers the least value – with standard liquid cooling and a modular power supply, this system is for premium builds. AMD-based starter configurations begin at $2,399.99 with a Ryzen 5 9600X or $2,589.99 with an Intel Core Ultra 5 250KF Plus. Standard components include a GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (8GB), 16GB of memory, and 1TB of PCIe 4.0 storage. Memory tops out at 128GB and two SSDs are supported up to 2TB each.
Bottom Line
Primarily, the HyperX Omen 35L gets one thing right: it feels genuinely premium. Its sharp black-and-white design, quality lighting, quiet operation, and enthusiast-grade components like a modular power supply give it the polish it needs to compete against boutique builders and aftermarket systems. Its performance in our test system with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D and an RTX 5080 match the expectations for this lofty price point.
That said, it’s clear that this desktop is aimed at the more premium side of the market, as prices of the entry-level configurations are difficult to justify given their level of hardware. But if you have deep enough pockets for a well-equipped configuration, the HyperX Omen 35L is a highly compelling gaming desktop well worth considering alongside anything the market has to offer.
Charles Jefferies is a freelance reviewer for Tom’s Hardware US. He covers laptop and desktop PCs, especially gaming models.

articles.title: Here's the secret behind the return of the illuminated Apple logo on the back of the new touchscreen MacBook Pro
articles.text:
Here's the secret behind the return of the illuminated Apple logo on the back of the new touchscreen MacBook Pro
Thanks, tandem OLED
For Apple fans, the touchscreen MacBook Pro PROLED XDR tandem OLED display may be the gift that keeps on giving. Obviously, new integrated digitizing technology made the touchscreen possible, but the ultra-thinness of the display tech can also be credited with enabling the return of a beloved MacBook feature.
The touchscreen MacBook Pro is the first MacBook in almost a decade to feature an illuminated Apple logo on the back. I've seen it in person, and it somehow looks like polished metal when closed, and then a glowing bright white when open.
Apple bringing back the illuminated logo back is directly attributable to the PROLED XDR display. Each pixel in an OLED panel is emissive, which means there's no need for a backlight. Even after Apple made the laptop lid thinner, it still had some room left there — and it turns out there was enough room left to give the Apple logo its own backlight.
As improbable as it seems, there's now a dedicated light for the logo, but not for the rest of the screen. And it still doesn't take up extra space (nor eat up measurable energy).
Do it for the fans
Why did Apple do this? Well, Apple's not telling us, but it's clearly a nod to the fans.
CEO John Ternus tried to tell us the glowing logo was returning in his tiny X tease that showed light shining on the logo, which was on a flat surface. I simply thought it was another way of highlighting the Apple brand, and the big news to come. Granted, I was never that hooked on the old light-up logo.
In fact, my strongest memory around the Apple logo on the back of MacBooks is a conversation I had with Ternus when he was still Apple's hardware lead, during which he explained how Apple milled an ultra-thin and shiny stainless steel Apple logo for the MacBook 12 (the rest of the chassis was brushed aluminum). That was a big deal back then, even if it didn't light up
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
When Ternus revealed that the glowing logo was returning to the new MacBook Pro during the launch presentation ("the logo is back"), the crowd basically lost their collective minds. It's a big deal.
The illuminated logo also serves another purpose, instantly telegraphing that you're using a special MacBook Pro — the first with a touchscreen.
What Apple is not sharing, though — and it merits further investigation — is how it managed to make the glowing logo look like polished metal when the laptop is closed. It's an engineering secret that I suspect Apple execs and engineers will take to their graves, even after the inevitable teardown.

A 38-year industry veteran and award-winning journalist, Lance has covered technology since PCs were the size of suitcases and “on line” meant “waiting.” He’s a former Lifewire Editor-in-Chief, Mashable Editor-in-Chief, and, before that, Editor in Chief of PCMag.com and Senior Vice President of Content for Ziff Davis, Inc. He also wrote a popular, weekly tech column for Medium called The Upgrade.
Lance Ulanoff makes frequent appearances on national, international, and local news programs including Live with Kelly and Mark, the Today Show, Good Morning America, CNBC, CNN, and the BBC.
