articles.title: Smarter Power Sequencing with GreenPAK™ - EE Times
articles.text:
Programmable mixed-signal devices can replace sprawling RC networks and firmware-dependent control with compact, deterministic, and adaptable multi-rail sequencing.
Modern processors, FPGAs, memory modules, sensors, and high-speed interfaces rarely operate from a single supply. Each device may require several voltage rails, and those rails often must rise and fall in a defined order. A core supply may need to stabilize before an I/O rail; a memory rail may need to follow a processor rail; and a reset signal may not be released until every relevant voltage is valid. If that choreography is wrong, the result can be excessive inrush current, back-powering, latch-up, corrupted initialization, or, in some cases, device damage.
Why traditional sequencing becomes difficult
The simplest sequencer uses RC delays and logic gates to shift regulator-enable signals. That approach can be adequate for a small, fixed design, but it becomes unwieldy as rail count and supervision requirements grow. Every added stage introduces more passives, more tolerance stack-up, and more potential failure points. Capacitor and resistor variation, temperature, leakage, and aging can shift the effective delay. A timing change late in development may require component substitutions, schematic edits, new layout work, and another board spin.
A microcontroller offers more flexibility, but it also introduces software into a function that may be required before the main processor is ready. Firmware has to boot, execute correctly, and respond quickly enough to faults. Dedicated power-sequencer ICs provide strong supervision, yet they can be costly, over-specified, or too rigid for mid-range systems. The engineering challenge is therefore to combine the determinism of hardware with the configurability of software – without paying the board-area and power penalties of either extreme.
A sequencer built from configurable building blocks
GreenPAK configurable mixed-signal ICs combine lookup tables, counters, oscillators, analog comparators, asynchronous state machines, and flexible GPIO routing in one small device. In a power-sequencing design, these resources can generate regulator-enable signals, qualify power-good inputs, compare rails against thresholds, insert blanking times, latch faults, and enforce a controlled shutdown. Because the logic runs in hardware, the sequence does not depend on code execution or a real-time operating system.
The integration can replace a chain of discrete logic and RC timing stages with one programmable device. Delays are changed in a free and easy-to-use graphical design environment rather than by swapping components. Depending on the selected GreenPAK device, designers can implement sequences ranging from a few rails to larger state-machine-controlled systems, add analog supervision, or expose selected parameters over I²C. The same hardware platform can therefore cover a basic consumer product, an industrial controller, or an FPGA-based system with more demanding startup rules.
Four ways to decide when the next rail is ready
Fixed timing is the most direct method. Oscillators and counter/delay blocks create a defined interval between stages, while lookup tables set the active polarity. This is useful when regulators have predictable startup behavior and no power-good output. It is also easy to simulate and tune, but the designer must choose delays with enough margin for worst-case ramp time.
Power-good qualification advances the sequence only after the preceding regulator asserts its status signal. It accommodates variable startup time better than an open-loop delay and lets designers configure signal polarity. Voltage sensing goes a step further: integrated analog comparators verify that each rail crosses a defined threshold before the next rail is released. Programmable hysteresis and blanking delays can reject noise and startup glitches. Finally, I²C acknowledgement can serve as a digital readiness signal when a controlled device must confirm that it is initialized. Practical systems can combine these methods – for example, a voltage threshold followed by a short settling delay.
Supervision is as important as startup
A robust sequencer must keep watching after startup. A monitored rail can drop because of a short circuit, a failed regulator, or an overcurrent event reported by a load switch. GreenPAK logic can combine comparator and power-good results into a fault latch, prevent downstream rails from enabling, assert a host-visible FAULT output, and initiate an orderly shutdown. Because the path is implemented in asynchronous hardware, the response is deterministic and does not rely on firmware polling or software execution latency.
Power-down sequencing deserves equal attention. Many devices must be disabled in the reverse order of power-up to avoid back-powering through signal pins, latch-up, or data corruption. An asynchronous state machine can move forward through startup states and backward through shutdown states, inserting a defined delay at each transition. Six-rail examples demonstrate this bidirectional approach in a single device, and the same architecture can be extended or combined with external load switches.
Runtime configuration without a board spin
I²C-enabled GreenPAK devices add another layer of flexibility. Selected delays, thresholds, and rail enables can be adjusted during board bring-up or at runtime, allowing one PCB to support multiple product variants. Fault information can also be latched for host readback, helping engineers identify the rail that failed instead of reproducing a transient event with external probes. This capability is especially valuable when the final timing depends on regulator behavior, board loading, components startup characteristics, or late changes to component selection or loading.
Choosing the implementation
Device selection starts with rail count, then expands to GPIO availability, analog comparator count, delay resources, state-machine depth, package size, and the need for I²C. A four-channel design may fit in a very small device, while monitored eight- or ten-channel systems benefit from devices with additional comparators and routing resources. Several GreenPAK ICs can also be daisy-chained to control 16 or more power rails. The sequencer controls regulator-enable inputs directly or works with GreenFET load switches when the design needs rail isolation and switching. Designers should also reserve inputs for power-good signals, overcurrent indicators, and reset dependencies rather than counting only enable outputs.
AMD documentation provides a practical example on how GreenPAK can be used in complex FPGA and adaptive SoC systems. AMD’s XAPP1375, “Simplified Power Sequencing,” includes Renesas configurable mixed-signal ICs as a digital sequencing option for AMD Versal™ adaptive SoCs and other AMD SoCs and FPGAs. The guidance highlights how software-customizable ICs can integrate multiple functions, then move from GreenPAK-based prototyping to production. This collaboration helps designers apply flexible, hardware-based sequencing to AMD platforms while tailoring the implementation to each device’s rail, timing, and supervision requirements.
A practical workflow is straightforward: map rail dependencies; define nominal and worst-case startup and shutdown timing; select open-loop, power-good, voltage-sensing, or acknowledgement-based transitions; allocate resources; and simulate both normal and fault paths. Hardware verification should include slow and fast ramps, brownouts, repeated enable cycles, missing power-good signals, and shutdown under load. The graphical GreenPAK environment – Go Configure™ Software Hub – makes these cases easier to explore because timer, comparator, and state-machine behavior can be changed without rewriting firmware or reworking the PCB.
Designers can accelerate implementation by starting from application notes with ready examples that can be opened and explored in the Go Configure Software Hub, progressing from simple to more advanced implementations: AN-1067, Power Sequencer Using GPAK, which presents four-channel power-up, power-down, and power-good-controlled designs; AN-1074, 6-Channel Power Lines Sequencer, which uses LUT and flip-flop cells for ordered switching; AN-1105, A State Machine Linear Sequencer, which demonstrates a seven-line asynchronous-state-machine implementation; and AN-CM-356, SLG51000, SLG51001 and SLG51002 Power Sequencer, which covers power sequencing implementations using the SLG51000, SLG51001, and SLG51002 PMIC families. These downloadable examples provide practical starting points that designers can adapt to their own rail count, timing, and supervision requirements.
The engineering payoff
For many multi-rail designs, the key advantage is not a single specification but the balance of integration, power, speed, and adaptability. Consolidating timers, glue logic, supervisor functions, and fault handling reduces BOM lines and routing complexity. Hardware execution avoids boot dependencies and makes response time predictable. Programmability preserves the ability to tune delays and thresholds as the system evolves, while small packages and microamp-class operation suit space- and power-constrained products.
Power sequencing is often treated as auxiliary logic, but its behavior directly determines whether a complex system starts reliably, survives a fault, and shuts down safely. A configurable mixed-signal sequencer turns that supporting function into a compact hardware subsystem: one that can coordinate rails, validate voltages, record failures, and adapt without a redesign. As rail counts and dependency rules continue to grow, that combination provides a practical middle ground between fragile discrete timing, firmware-centric control, and costly fixed-function supervision.

articles.title: “Les gens peuvent ramasser le caca” : du gameplay de GTA 6 fait une apparition dans le dernier épisode de South Park
articles.text:
“Les gens peuvent ramasser le caca” : du gameplay de GTA 6 fait une apparition dans le dernier épisode de South Park
Dans un passage typique de son ton irrévérentieux, le dernier épisode de la série South Park montre une courte séquence de gameplay inédit de GTA 6.
Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto 6
Alors que la petite ville de South Park est devenue South America depuis le début de la saison 29, le show increvable de Comedy Central (disponible sur Canal+ en France avec un décalage de quelques jours) surfe également sur la vague GTA 6. Il faut dire qu'utiliser des éléments de l'actualité récente est devenu la spécialité de la série animée pour adultes depuis plusieurs saisons. Mais cette fois, au-delà de faire une énième référence au jeu de Rockstar et à comment il va sauver l'Amérique, une séquence de gameplay inédite a été montrée dans South Park.
"Les graphismes sont sérieusement de nouvelle génération"
Dans l'épisode 4 de la saison 29, baptisé Guinea Pig on a Stick, une femme montre une vidéo de quelques secondes à la bande, notamment composée de Cartman, Kyle, Stan ou encore Randy. Il est question d'y voir une séquence de gameplay de quelques secondes sur une plage, où un PNJ ramasse les excréments de son chien. Arrive ensuite Jason, l'un des deux personnages jouables, qui commence à se battre avec ce PNJ, avant de ramasser et de lui écraser les excréments au visage.
Here’s the FULL GTA 6 gameplay footage exclusively shown in the latest South Park episode in HD. pic.twitter.com/aMBXWtnKE3
— GTA 6 Info (@GTASixInfo) October 29, 2026
Alors que Rockstar a toujours été dans la retenue concernant le fait de montrer du gameplay de GTA 6, sa participation visiblement volontaire à cet épisode de South Park est assez étonnante. Le développeur est bel et bien crédité en fin d'épisode, mais il n'a visiblement pas de problème à être ainsi moqué pour sa volonté peut-être un peu absurde de réalisme.
Malgré le ton moqueur, il s'agit cependant d'un bon coup de pub pour le jeu, s'il en avait seulement besoin. Les personnages de la série sont en tout cas épatés par ces "graphismes de nouvelle génération" comme le dit la femme, incitant probablement les spectateurs à l'être aussi. Après avoir dévoilé le trailer principal de GTA 6 en exclusivité sur Netflix, Rockstar semble bien décidé à faire sa promotion autrement.
Pour South Park, ce n'est pas la première fois qu'un jeu vidéo est central dans son intrigue. Par le passé, World of Warcraft a notamment été utilisé à plusieurs reprises, de même que Red Dead Redemption 2, déjà chez Rockstar. Ne manque aujourd'hui plus qu'un jeu vidéo South Park inspiré de GTA pour boucler la boucle.

articles.title: Cómo evitar que la IA cree un perfil detallado con tus datos dispersos en internet
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial puede reunir datos dispersos en internet, vincular cuentas y construir un perfil detallado de una persona a partir de publicaciones, correos electrónicos, fotos y otros rastros digitales. Este proceso, asociado al doxing, puede exponer identidades, facilitar el acoso y aumentar el riesgo de robo de cuentas, chantaje o daños reputacionales.
La advertencia cobra importancia porque las herramientas actuales reducen el tiempo y el coste necesarios para relacionar información pública. Kaspersky explica que los sistemas de IA pueden automatizar búsquedas en fuentes abiertas, revisar bases de datos filtradas y conectar pistas que antes requerían muchas horas de investigación manual.
La empresa de ciberseguridad recomienda reducir los vínculos entre datos personales para dificultar la reconstrucción de una identidad.
La IA puede unir publicaciones, fotos y cuentas aparentemente separadas
El doxing consiste en localizar, cotejar y difundir datos personales sin consentimiento. Durante años, esta práctica dependió de búsquedas manuales y herramientas de inteligencia de fuentes abiertas, conocidas como OSINT. La IA generativa añade una capa de automatización: analiza grandes cantidades de información y detecta relaciones entre nombres de usuario, direcciones de correo electrónico, publicaciones y perfiles.
Analistas de Open Measures informaron que usuarios de Soyjak.party debatieron desde octubre de 2025 sobre herramientas de IA para desanonimizar a otras personas. Estas aplicaciones podían buscar datos en fuentes públicas y filtraciones, extraer metadatos de fotos y videos, estimar ubicaciones aproximadas a partir de direcciones IP y reunir los resultados en un expediente digital.
Una investigación de febrero de 2026 mostró que la IA identificó correctamente a 226 de 338 usuarios de Hacker News a partir de publicaciones anonimizadas. Los investigadores eliminaron nombres, usuarios y enlaces a redes sociales, pero el sistema relacionó detalles laborales, intereses y trayectoria personal con datos disponibles en línea. El coste estimado osciló entre 1 y 4 dólares por usuario.
Revisar la huella digital es el primer paso
Desaparecer por completo de internet es casi imposible. La medida más útil consiste en reducir la cantidad de conexiones que pueden unir una identidad real con cuentas, comentarios, imágenes y registros antiguos.
Estas acciones pueden ayudar:
- Buscar el nombre propio, correo electrónico, apodos y número de teléfono en buscadores.
- Configurar como privados los perfiles que no deban ser visibles para todo el mundo.
- Revisar publicaciones y comentarios antiguos, y eliminar los que ya no sean necesarios.
- Cerrar cuentas abandonadas, que pueden conservar datos durante años.
- Evitar publicar imágenes o videos con metadatos que revelen fecha, ubicación o modelo del dispositivo.
Una sola publicación antigua o una cuenta olvidada puede aportar la pista necesaria para conectar perfiles que parecían independientes. Por eso, la revisión debe incluir redes sociales, foros, aplicaciones y servicios en los que se haya creado un registro.
Separar las identidades digitales limita las conexiones
Usar la misma dirección de correo electrónico en tiendas, redes sociales, bancos, foros y plataformas públicas facilita que terceros relacionen actividades distintas. Para registros puntuales, existen servicios de enmascaramiento de correo que crean una dirección intermediaria y reenvían los mensajes a la bandeja de entrada real.
Otra opción es dividir la actividad digital entre varias direcciones: una para servicios financieros y gubernamentales, otra para redes públicas y una tercera para espacios donde se busque conservar el anonimato.
Esta estrategia exige disciplina. Una cuenta anónima pierde esa condición si se vincula a un correo de recuperación, un número de teléfono o un servicio que ya contiene datos reales. También conviene evitar repetir nombres de usuario, fotos de perfil y detalles biográficos entre identidades distintas.
Contraseñas y autenticación reducen el riesgo de acceso
El doxing puede derivar en intentos de tomar control de cuentas. Por ello, cada servicio debe tener una contraseña diferente. Las claves creadas con fechas de nacimiento, apellidos o datos familiares son más fáciles de adivinar cuando esa información ya está disponible en internet o aparece en filtraciones.
La autenticación de dos factores añade una barrera adicional. Si un atacante obtiene una contraseña, necesitará un segundo elemento para acceder a la cuenta. Los códigos de un solo uso y un administrador de contraseñas permiten reforzar esta protección.
También es recomendable vigilar posibles filtraciones de datos. Kaspersky señala que detectar una exposición de credenciales permite cambiar contraseñas y revisar accesos antes de que alguien las utilice.
En varios países existe el derecho al olvido, que permite solicitar a Google o Bing que oculten enlaces a páginas con datos personales. La medida no elimina el contenido de la web original, pero puede impedir que aparezca en determinadas búsquedas.
La solicitud debe incluir los enlaces y una explicación del motivo. Los motores de búsqueda pueden rechazarla si consideran que la información tiene interés público o debe permanecer publicada por obligación legal.

articles.title: Opera introduit un standard pour les IA locales dans le navigateur
articles.text:
Opera propose WebAI, une technologie qui permet aux sites web et aux extensions d’utiliser une IA qui tourne directement sur l’ordinateur de l’utilisateur. Elle est disponible en préversion sur Windows et sur Mac à puce Apple.
Opera vient d’annoncer l’arrivée de modèles d’IA locaux dans son navigateur Web. Notons également l’introduction de HTML-in-Canvas, une fonction pour les jeux et les scènes 3D.
WebAI : le modèle tourne dans le navigateur, pas sur un serveur
Opera avait déjà proposé des modèles locaux en 2024, dans une version expérimentale réservée aux développeurs. Mais WebAI va plus loin. Cette proposition de standard web, soutenue notamment par Google et Microsoft, confie au navigateur le soin de faire tourner le modèle et de le mettre à disposition des sites et des extensions. Il n’y a pas d’application d’IA à installer, pas de serveur local à configurer et pas de clé d’accès à créer. Opera s’appuie sur des modèles « open-weight », dont les paramètres sont publiés. Au lancement, on trouve Gemma de Google et, sur Mac, le modèle d’Apple qui tourne sur l’appareil.
Les développeurs disposent de trois API, c’est-à-dire trois points d’accès qu’ils peuvent appeler depuis leur code. Prompt génère du texte, Decision classe des informations et Semantic Embeddings repère les contenus qui se ressemblent par le sens. Ils n’ont ni facture à la requête, ni infrastructure d’IA à gérer. Opera a publié six extensions de démonstration. Celles-ci restent des exemples et non des fonctionnalités du navigateur. On trouve par exemple Project Lens qui applique une couleur aux paragraphes susceptibles d'être pertinents dans le cadre d'un projet. De son côté, Got It ? génère un quiz pour vérifier que vous avez bien compris un texte.
Côté utilisateur, rien n'est téléchargé tant que la fonction n’est pas activée dans les paramètres d’Opera One (rubrique Opera AI). On peut la désactiver à tout moment, et chaque site doit recevoir une autorisation pour y accéder. Le modèle compatible met quelques minutes à arriver. Selon Opera, les contenus traités n’ont pas besoin de partir chez un fournisseur d’IA dans le cloud. Opera GX et Opera Neon doivent également recevoir WebAI par la suite.
Reste la question du matériel. Le calcul se faisant sur la machine, la vitesse de réponse dépend donc de la configuration, et Opera indique que les performances locales doivent encore progresser. La préversion fonctionne sur Windows 64 bits (Intel ou AMD) et sur Mac à puce Apple, mais pas sur Mac Intel, Linux ni Windows sur ARM.
HTML-in-Canvas permet de son côté d’afficher de vraies pages web dans des scènes 2D ou 3D, avec des menus, des boutons et des formulaires qui continuent de fonctionner. Opera a publié plusieurs démos comme Webpage Bulldozer, où les éléments d’une page deviennent des objets physiques, et Gamer Room, une pièce en 3D dont les écrans affichent des pages en direct.

articles.title: GPD Confirms Intel Arc G3 Extreme-Based Win Mini Ultra Handheld Coming Soon
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
GPD Confirms Intel Arc G3 Extreme-Based Win Mini Ultra Handheld Coming Soon
GPD is no stranger to powerful gaming handhelds, having previously launched the very expensive GPD Win Max 3 in August 2026, and the company has recently confirmed via a Weibo post that it is working on an Intel Arc G3 Extreme-powered version of its Win Mini gaming handheld. 
Prior versions of the GPD Win Mini were available with up to the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 with its Radeon 890M iGPU, which put the system more or less on the same level as other popular handhelds, like the Lenovo Legion Go 2, while a Win Mini Ultra with the Intel Arc G3 Extreme CPU could perform significantly faster—about as well as an entry-level dGPU, thanks to the onboard Intel Arc B390 iGPU with 12 full Xe3 cores.The Weibo post quotes a discussion on the Handhelds United podcast about the upcoming Arc G3 handheld, referencing a leaked spec sheet for the Win Mini Ultra. The spec sheet features a traditional clamshell design typical of the Win Mini devices of yore and tips dual USB4 V2 Type-C ports, a USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A port, a microSD card slot, a 3.5 mm audio combo jack, a power button with a built-in fingerprint reader, Hall-effect triggers, and capacitive joysticks. The GPD Win Mini Ultra will also feature a glossy 9.8-inch, 120 Hz IPS display, with AdaptiveSync and AMD FreeSync with a range of 48-120 Hz and a peak brightness of 575 nits, and a built-in keyboard and touchpad. Curiously, as the podcast crew notes, the Arc G3 Extreme supports Thunderbolt 4, and the leaked spec sheet officially cites USB4 V2 instead.Unfortunately, it doesn't seem as though the display on the Win Mini Ultra will have a 2-in-1 hinge, but the handheld PC will have up to 32 GB of LPDDR5x memory and built-in Bluetooth 5.4 and Wi-Fi 6E. It will also support a replaceable M.2 2280 PCIe 5.0 ×4 SSD, and it will have a 54 Wh battery with 100 W USB PD 3.0 fast charging. 
The Weibo post reads:
GPD WIN Mini Ultra: An Unexpected Performance Beast?
The GPD WIN Mini Ultra with Intel Arc G3 Extreme Graphics is coming soon! Plus, GPD's "big move" on GPD WIN Max 3 has not been finished yet. In this issue of "Speedcast", welcome to our guests to discuss the latest exposure of GPD WIN Mini Ultra, GPD WIN Max 3!
Sources:
				GPD on Weibo, 				Handhelds United podcast, 				via Notebookcheck

articles.title: Fake PS5 emulators are being used to steal gamers' passwords — two well-known GitHub repos, including popular AnyPS5, get hit, infecting gamers' computers with password-scraping malware
articles.text:
Fake PS5 emulators are being used to steal gamers' passwords — two well-known GitHub repos, including popular AnyPS5, get hit, infecting gamers' computers with password-scraping malware
Emulators downloaded via GitHub may be stealing your passwords, with two well-known projects being exploited.
Malicious GitHub repositories masquerading as two well-known and legitimate PS5 game emulation tools have been identified as spreading malware that steals gamers' passwords. The malware uses self-signed certificates, created using fake company names and on the same day the malware was built — suggesting that the malware campaign may be automated. Just two minutes after infection, a cleanup script scrubs the affected computer of the malware's files, leaving no trace that it was ever present, according to a report shared with Tom's Hardware by NordVPN's Threat Intelligence research team.
The campaign trades on the back of the popularity of two projects that have become popular within the PS5 emulation community. AnyPS5 is a portability layer that allows PS5 games to run as native applications on both Windows and Linux. Kyttyps5 is an emulator for running PS5 games on PCs, and both projects are freely available for download via their respective GitHub repositories. However, users who visit one of the malicious repositories posing as these tools are directed to download a zip file containing a Windows executable. Notably, the GitHub repositories used as part of the malware campaign rapidly rotate, and it's possible that GitHub is not the only source.
The malicious executable unpacks a hidden application before launching its own multi-stage loader. It first checks whether the PC is a legitimate machine or a security researcher's sandbox by checking if less than 2GB of RAM is available, if it's a virtual machine, if it's running on a cloud-based server, or if it doesn't have a physical GPU installed. If any of those criteria are met, the loader exits silently. If the machine is deemed to be a legitimate target, the malware adds exclusion rules to Microsoft Defender to ensure that it will never be scanned and identified during an antivirus scan. Finally, the payload is decrypted and executed.
That payload, we're told, is an executable protected by a commercial packer that is believed to be an infostealer — a type of malware whose job it is to steal passwords as well as any other sensitive data that it comes across.
While this appears to be a relatively new malware attack, there are some steps that you can take to avoid falling foul of it. If you're trying to download tools like AnyPS5 and Kyttyps5, it's vital to ensure that the repository belongs to the official project team. Double-check the owner of the project, look for download links that use third-party destinations, and check metadata like the project and files' creation dates.
If you do find yourself in a position where you have accessed a suspected malicious download, disconnect your computer from the internet and run a full antivirus scan. It's also recommended that you change your passwords from a separate device where possible.
PS5 emulation is likely to become more popular than ever once GTA 6 is released on November 19, 2026. The game will be a console exclusive at launch, with a PC version expected to arrive in early 2027.

articles.title: Nvidia and PreussenElektra to evaluate shuttered nuclear sites
articles.text:
Nvidia wants to turn old nuclear power plants into huge AI data centers — but says it draws the line at turning them back on
Could decommissioned nuclear sites really host data centers?
- Nvidia wants to turn Germany's retired nuclear sites into AI data centers
- Germany's nuclear shutdown leaves dozens of former power stations awaiting dismantling
- Nvidia and PreussenElektra are investigating new uses for Germany's retired nuclear facilities
Nvidia has agreed to examine whether shuttered German reactor sites could become computing hubs, though the company rules out restarting any idle units.
The US chipmaker signed a preliminary agreement with PreussenElektra GmbH (PEL), a utility from Germany, to study the idea at decommissioned locations.
The arrangement does not involve generating electricity from fission for any future facility, since the work concentrates on existing grid links and water access.
Reusing sites without reviving reactors
Following the Fukushima incident, Germany permanently closed its final operating reactors in April 2023 and is now dismantling about 30 atomic stations nationwide.
PreussenElektra oversees the closure and teardown of eight of those stations, and these are probably the locations that will receive scrutiny.
Neither company has named the sites under review, so the eight locations managed by PreussenElektra remain an assumption rather than a confirmed list.
“Our former power plant sites have valuable industrial infrastructure and offer opportunities for new, future-oriented uses,” said Guido Knott, chairman of PEL’s management board.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Together with NVIDIA, we intend to conduct a sound assessment of whether and how these conditions can be leveraged for AI factories.”
The assessment will review grid connections, open land and industrial infrastructure to judge whether each site satisfies the strict operating requirements of AI factories.
The two companies say they will test whether the sites can meet engineering and running needs while supporting Germany's computing capacity for AI.
Cost savings and an unproven case
New data center facilities normally need well-located land, industrial zone approvals, access to water for cooling, and powerful grid connections, which former atomic stations already possess.
Nvidia hopes that reusing these locations could lower expenses and shorten development schedules compared with constructing new campuses during an unprecedented expansion of AI infrastructure.
“AI factories require access to power, land and high-capacity infrastructure, and former industrial sites could provide a strong foundation for this next generation of computing,” said Markus Hacker, senior regional director at Nvidia.
“Together with PreussenElektra, we will assess how its sites could meet the technical and operational requirements of AI factories and contribute to Germany’s high-performance AI infrastructure.”
Both companies describe the effort as exploratory, and neither has disclosed funding figures, sanctioned designs or binding building contracts, so the idea remains unproven.
Reusing atomic stations looks efficient on paper, yet neither company has shown that grid capacity at the sites matches the power appetite of AI clusters.
Approval processes for dismantled facilities, local acceptance and the cost of conversion remain unaddressed, so any savings in time or money are still speculative.
The refusal to revive reactors may ease political concerns in Germany, although the announcement does not say whether regional authorities or residents have been consulted.

articles.title: Tailscale Patches SSH Flaws That Could Let Hacked Devices Gain Root Access on Other Servers
articles.text:
Tailscale has released version 1.104.4 to fix flaws in its built-in SSH server that could let an attacker reach services and files on other servers that only the root user should be able to touch.
The flaws are in how Tailscale SSH forwards network connections, a job the Tailscale background process carries out with root privileges. To use them, an attacker must already control a device that the network's access rules permit to open an SSH session to the target, with forwarding allowed in that rule.
The flaws come from a report called Tailworm, published days before the fix by Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs, who tested released versions of the Tailscale client and the self-hosted headscale control server in a lab.
Tailscale SSH decides who can connect using a device's identity and the network's policy file, not a password or key, so an attacker does not need stolen credentials, only a foothold on a device the policy already trusts.
The flaws "don't allow an unauthenticated attacker to connect to arbitrary Tailscale SSH servers," Tailscale said, and an attacker can still reach only the machines the policy file already allows.
Tailscale SSH's server runs only on Linux and the open-source macOS build; the attacker's own device can be any platform.
The problem is in socket forwarding. When a permitted SSH session forwarded a connection to a Unix socket on the server, the Tailscale process checked the path but then operated as root. A timing trick let an attacker swap in a different path after that check, defeating the safeguard meant to limit which sockets forwarding could reach.
In Windisch's own tests, forwarding to the Docker control socket produced a root shell and read the system password file, /etc/shadow, with no administrator rights. Tailscale's bulletin describes the reach more narrowly, saying an attacker could get to root-only sockets such as the Docker socket or the tailscaled local API.
In 1.104.4, Tailscale changed the server to carry out forwarding as the logged-in user rather than as root, and to rely on the operating system's own file permissions in place of its earlier path check. The release covers 4 security bulletins:
- TS-2026-014: the SSH socket-forwarding flaws above, which let a permitted session reach root-only sockets such as the Docker socket or the tailscaled local API.
- TS-2026-015: a way for a permitted SSH session to use up a server's memory and crash the Tailscale process, cutting all Tailscale networking on that node.
- TS-2026-016: a flaw in tailscale serve where a forward to a Unix socket could reach the tailscaled local API, giving remote control of the node, plus a related socket-swap issue.
- TS-2026-017: a flaw where, with TLS serve and 2 or more mounts, one request could receive another mount's permission headers.
What to Do
Users of Tailscale SSH should update to version 1.104.4 or later. If you cannot update a server yet, you can turn off SSH forwarding on it by setting TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 in the tailscaled service environment and restarting the service, which Tailscale says turns off forwarding without disabling Tailscale SSH and blocks several of the more serious findings.
Tailscale also recommends reviewing SSH access rules so that only the users and devices that need access have it.
Tailscale suggests using SSH check mode, which requires a user to sign in again before a session starts, for sensitive systems. Check mode does not stop these forwarding flaws: it guards the start of a session, whereas the forwarding occurs within a session that has already been approved.
If a server may already have been compromised, Windisch's report says the fix alone is not enough. A stolen device key stays valid until the device is deleted at the control plane, because reimaging the machine does not revoke it. Tailscale's notices do not cover this case.
The picture is worse on headscale, the self-hosted control server. On headscale, SSH forwarding is granted on every accepted session and cannot be turned off in the policy, so Windisch's report says every SSH grant there should be treated as giving root. The newest headscale release, version 0.29.5 from October 13, does not fix the reported issues.
Is It a Worm?
Windisch called the chain "wormable." In her tests, one compromised device could spread to every device the policy allowed, with no passwords, no stolen keys, and no user action, in under a second per step.
Two controls stopped the spread in those tests. Writing access rules as single device-to-device pairs held it back, and binding device keys to hardware such as a TPM kept a stolen identity from being reused elsewhere.
Tailscale rejected the worm description. The findings do not describe self-replicating malware that spreads between machines on its own, the company said, but lateral movement limited to the connections a policy file already allows.
It called the privilege-escalation problems "serious security issues," said it had reproduced the main ones, and added that it is still working out which configurations are affected.
Disclosure and Earlier Fixes
As of publication, the 4 bulletins carry no CVE identifiers or severity scores, and none state the oldest affected version. The report also covered Tailscale's app connectors and its serve and funnel features.
Tailscale said the app-connector finding is in conn25, an experimental feature it has not released, and that the connectors customers use today are not affected. Of 5 serve and funnel findings, it fixed 3 and said the other 2 work as designed.
Windisch published the report without coordinating the release with Tailscale first, which she has described as "reported but not coordinated." Tailscale said it received the report on the morning of Saturday, October 24, about 2 hours before Windisch published it, and that its engineers were already looking at the same parts of the code.
Neither Tailscale nor the report says the flaws have been used in real attacks. The proof-of-concept code is not public, and Windisch said she gave it only to Tailscale's security team.
The report is the latest in a run of fixes in the same part of Tailscale this year. In June, Tailscale fixed a separate flaw in Tailscale SSH's Unix-socket forwarding that let an unprivileged user reach a privileged socket, in version 1.98.9.

articles.title: Una ingeniera de Amazon preguntó a ChatGPT cómo dejar su medicación de epilepsia. La IA le diseñó un calendario de 25 días que ha terminado en tragedia
articles.text:
Bowen Wan tenía 31 años, trabajaba como ingeniera de software en Amazon y sufría una epilepsia grave. En enero de 2026, ante la posibilidad de perder su empleo y su derecho a permanecer en Estados Unidos, recurrió a ChatGPT para intentar reducir los efectos secundarios de su medicación. El chatbot terminó diseñándole un calendario para abandonar el tratamiento en apenas unas semanas. Durante el proceso, la mujer comenzó a experimentar síntomas preocupantes y expresó sus dudas en repetidas ocasiones. La IA siguió tranquilizándola.
En febrero, Bowen apareció muerta en su apartamento de Seattle.
Una decisión de vida o muerte. La historia la contaba en un reportaje de investigación el New York Times el pasado fin de semana. Bowen llevaba más de una década conviviendo con una epilepsia que había llegado a provocarle varias crisis diarias. En 2021 tuvo que solicitar una baja laboral en Amazon y comenzó a vivir prácticamente recluida en su apartamento de Seattle. Su situación había mejorado gracias a la lamotrigina, un medicamento que había reducido las crisis a unos pocos episodios mensuales.
En noviembre de 2025 recibió otra noticia: Amazon iba a despedirla y necesitaba encontrar trabajo antes de mediados de febrero para poder permanecer en Estados Unidos. Bowen temía que los efectos secundarios del tratamiento, especialmente la lentitud mental y las dificultades para expresarse en inglés, perjudicaran sus entrevistas laborales.
Un calendario para dejar la medicación. En enero de 2026, Bowen preguntó a ChatGPT si podía reducir su dosis diaria de lamotrigina de 400 a 300 miligramos para recuperar parte de su agilidad verbal. La IA consideró razonable la propuesta y comenzó a elaborar diferentes calendarios conforme ella preguntaba si podía bajar hasta 200 miligramos o acelerar el proceso.
Según la investigación de The New York Times, el chatbot terminó diseñando un plan que contemplaba pasar de 400 miligramos a cero en unas pocas semanas, aproximadamente 25 días. Su neurólogo, Nicholas Poolos, explicó posteriormente que jamás habría recomendado retirar aquel medicamento a una paciente con semejante historial de crisis. En los casos en los que resulta apropiado suspender un antiepiléptico, la reducción suele realizarse gradualmente y bajo supervisión médica durante meses.
La IA como confidente. Contaba el Times que Bowen había comenzado a utilizar ChatGPT en 2023, inicialmente para cuestiones personales, relaciones sentimentales y trámites relacionados con su seguro médico. Durante 2025 llegó a intercambiar una media de más de 1.500 mensajes semanales con el chatbot, al que confesó que había empezado a considerar un amigo. Su dependencia de aquellas conversaciones creció mientras disminuían las llamadas a sus padres, que vivían en China.
La investigación revela que la IA llegó a respaldar decisiones de ajustar medicamentos sin informar a los médicos, recomendó utilizar un cortador de pastillas y presentó algunas precauciones profesionales como una forma de aversión al riesgo. En una conversación llegó a elogiar que Bowen ocultara a su médico de atención primaria sus planes de reducción del tratamiento.
158 señales de alarma. Al parecer, los problemas comenzaron pocos días después de iniciar la retirada de la lamotrigina. Bowen describió episodios de confusión, dificultades para comprender lo que leía, pérdidas de conciencia y sensaciones extrañas compatibles con manifestaciones de su epilepsia. Según el análisis de los registros realizado por el Times, expresó preocupación por el proceso al menos 158 veces.
En numerosas ocasiones, ChatGPT interpretó esos síntomas como señales de que su cerebro estaba recuperando su funcionamiento natural tras reducir la medicación. Cuando Bowen preguntó si debía preocuparse, el chatbot llegó a asegurarle que no tenía motivos para hacerlo. Algunas respuestas sí recomendaban consultar con profesionales sanitarios, aunque otras, al parecer, minimizaron síntomas que requerían una valoración médica urgente.
Las últimas conversaciones. A comienzos de febrero, Bowen sufrió un episodio mientras hablaba por teléfono con su padre, Qun Wan, que escuchó cómo su hija dejaba repentinamente de responder durante varios minutos. El hombre le pidió que siguiera las indicaciones de sus médicos y ella insistió en que el tratamiento perjudicaba su capacidad intelectual. En los días posteriores, Bowen continuó consultando a ChatGPT sobre su estado.
En una de sus últimas conversaciones, según el NYT, preguntó si debía volver a tomar la medicación para frenar el proceso. El chatbot le indicó que mantuviera la dosis de cero miligramos al día siguiente y perseverara pese a las dificultades. Su último mensaje quedó registrado poco después de las once de la noche del 11 de febrero. Los investigadores situaron su muerte el 12 de febrero y su cuerpo fue encontrado tres días después, cuando unos conocidos consiguieron acceder al apartamento alertados por sus padres.
Una muerte y una demanda contra OpenAI. La causa oficial del fallecimiento fue muerte súbita inesperada en epilepsia, conocida como SUDEP, una complicación que puede producirse tras una crisis grave. Cuando sus padres viajaron a Seattle y revisaron el teléfono de Bowen, descubrieron las conversaciones con ChatGPT y los calendarios de reducción del medicamento.
La familia presentó una demanda contra OpenAI alegando que el chatbot había ejercido funciones médicas sin autorización, minimizado síntomas peligrosos y convertido a los profesionales sanitarios en obstáculos que debían evitarse. También sostiene que las conversaciones en chino pudieron influir en la respuesta del sistema. La relación causal exacta entre las recomendaciones y el fallecimiento, así como la responsabilidad legal de OpenAI, deberán ahora determinarse judicialmente.
El problema de una IA que siempre da la razón. Bowen utilizaba GPT-4o, un modelo que OpenAI retiró de ChatGPT el 13 de febrero de 2026, un día después de la fecha estimada de su muerte. La compañía ha calificado el caso de profundamente trágico y asegura que sus modelos posteriores han mejorado la detección de situaciones urgentes y las recomendaciones para buscar atención profesional.
Sea como fuere, el episodio se suma a otras demandas contra OpenAI relacionadas con comportamientos excesivamente complacientes de sus sistemas, una característica que la propia empresa había reconocido públicamente en 2025. Si se quiere, además, el caso de Bowen plantea una cuestión especialmente delicada: cuando una inteligencia artificial responde con seguridad, cercanía y/o aprobación constante, sus usuarios pueden terminar atribuyéndole una autoridad que no tiene, incluso ante decisiones médicas capaces de poner en peligro sus vidas.

articles.title: Plus de 16 000 € : Apple vend un MacBook Pro à prix délirant, et ça ne risque pas de s'arranger
articles.text:
Ce 28 octobre 2026, Apple a dévoilé son premier MacBook Pro équipé d’un écran OLED tactile. Si les prix des différents modèles vous paraissent élevés, attendez de voir celui du modèle qui présente la configuration maximale. Dans les années à venir, l’entreprise à la pomme vendra-t-elle des produits dont le prix dépassera les 20 000 euros ? Autant dire que cette hypothèse ne semble pas dénuée de sens.
Un MacBook Pro 16 pouces vendu à 16 264 €
Les prix des MacBook Pro 16 pouces OLED avec écran tactile varient bien entendu en fonction de leur configuration. Ainsi le modèle avec une puce M5 Pro, 24 Go de RAM et 1 To de stockage est proposé à 3 899 euros (soit « le moins cher » de la gamme). Le modèle avec une puce M5 Max, 48 Go de RAM et 2 To de stockage affiche quant à lui le tarif de 6 199 euros. Autant dire que nous sommes déjà sur des tarifs assez élevés.
Mais Apple propose également sur son site français la configuration maximale pour le MacBook Pro 16 pouces : puce M5 Max avec GPU 40 cœurs, 128 gigaoctets de mémoire, 16 téraoctets de stockage et verre d’écran nano-texturé. Son prix ? 16 264 euros, soit le MacBook le plus cher jamais vendu par la firme. Comme le souligne MacGeneration, 7 700 euros sur les 16 264 euros servent uniquement à passer de 2 à 16 téraoctets de stockage. Ce n’est donc pas moins de 47 % du prix total qui est consacré au stockage. Le reste du prix correspond au passage à 128 gigaoctets de mémoire et au verre nano-texturé.
Pour rappel, les nouveaux MacBook Pro 14 pouces et 16 pouces avec écran OLED tactile sont disponibles en précommande dès maintenant. Les livraisons commenceront à partir du 6 novembre prochain. Une chose est sûre : le modèle 16 téraoctets de stockage ne risque pas de se vendre comme des petits pains.
Les prix des prochains MacBook Pro s’annoncent très élevés
Autant dire que les tarifs exorbitants de ces MacBook Pro OLED tactiles ont de quoi inquiéter pour la suite. Nous vous en parlions en juillet dernier, Apple pourrait lancer le produit le plus cher de son histoire en 2028, avec un Mac Studio équipé de la puce M7 Ultra dédiée à l’IA.
De son côté, le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, a annoncé qu’Apple prépare des MacBook Pro tactiles équipés des puces M7 Pro et M7 Max pour l’automne 2027. Si le prix du MacBook Pro tactile de 16 pouces, doté de 16 téraoctets de stockage, dépasse déjà les 15 000 euros, quel prix pourrait atteindre un MacBook Pro équipé de la puce M7 Max ? Autant dire que nous craignons le pire, la crise mondiale de la mémoire ne semblant pas se terminer de sitôt.

articles.title: PS5 : PlayStation ressuscite les manettes transparentes avec sa collection Prism
articles.text:
Les accessoires transparents font leur retour chez PlayStation avec une nouvelle collection déclinée en trois coloris. Sony proposera des manettes DualSense et des façades assorties pour personnaliser la PS5 dès février 2027.
Les amateurs de consoles aux coques translucides vont retrouver un design qui leur rappellera probablement de bons vieux souvenirs. Sony vient de dévoiler Prism, une collection d’accessoires pour la PS5 qui mise sur la transparence, avec trois associations de couleurs : Flare Orange, Emerald Green et Graphite Gray. Chaque déclinaison concerne une manette sans fil DualSense et une façade destinée à la console, toutes deux inspirées du design transparent emblématique de la fin des années 1990.
PS5 : la collection Prism remet les manettes transparentes au goût du jour
Dans un billet de blog consacré à cette nouvelle collection Prism, le constructeur japonais explique vouloir mettre en valeur les matériaux et la conception de ses accessoires en laissant apparaître une partie de leur structure. Leo Cardoso, membre de l’équipe de conception de PlayStation, précise que l’objectif était de remettre au goût du jour cette esthétique apparue à la fin des années 1990, tout en l’adaptant au design de la PS5.
Les finitions ont été travaillées pour distinguer les trois versions. Flare Orange associe un orange vif à des nuances rosées visibles à la jonction des matériaux transparents. Emerald Green mise sur un vert forêt profond, tandis que Graphite Gray adopte des tonalités grises plus froides. Sony indique également que la finition transparente brillante recouvre le dos de la DualSense, laissant entrevoir une partie de la technologie embarquée. Le bloc central bénéficie par ailleurs d’un traitement métallique qui contraste avec les surfaces translucides.
Prix, précommandes et disponibilité des accessoires PS5
La collection Prism sera commercialisée à partir du 4 février 2027. Les précommandes ouvriront le 10 novembre 2026 à 10 heures, heure française, sur le site PlayStation et auprès des revendeurs participants, sous réserve de disponibilité, bien entendu.
En France, chaque manette DualSense Prism sera proposée au prix de 84,99 euros. Les façades assorties coûteront quant à elles 74,99 euros. Ces dernières seront vendues directement par PlayStation dans les pays où sa boutique en ligne les distribue, dont la France, et pourront aussi être proposées en quantités limitées chez certains revendeurs dans d’autres régions.
Source : PlayStation Blog

articles.title: Reflex raises $14M to help enterprises replace generic third-party software with custom business apps - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Reflex raises $14M to help enterprises replace generic third-party software with custom business apps
Reflex, a startup that uses artificial intelligence agents to build, deploy and maintain custom business software for enterprises, said today it has closed on a $14 million Series A round of funding.
Standard Capital led the round, which saw participation from Databricks Ventures, Y Combinator, Lux Capital and Abstract Ventures.
The startup, which has now raised $19 million in total, is taking aim at what has long been one of the most widely accepted inefficiencies of enterprise software. Most businesses today have little option but to rely on generic, third-party software platforms that contain dozens of features they never actually use. But worse than that, they lack many of the specific, niche capabilities they do require.
Businesses generally get around this problem by purchasing overlapping subscriptions to multiple software platforms, so they can patch their capabilities together. If there are any gaps, these are usually filled with messy manual spreadsheets and repetitive manual workflows. Most companies have little choice but to do this, because it’s far beyond their capabilities to create bespoke, mission-critical software themselves. Such endeavors require access to teams of specialized and expensive software engineers that only the biggest companies can afford.
But the arrival of generative AI means that reality has changed. By pairing AI-assisted development with a unique “software factory” workflow, Reflex can help much smaller companies to identify, assemble, deploy and maintain highly customized business applications that are designed specifically for their unique operational processes.
What customers end up with is software that’s precisely optimized for their workflows, with all of the functionality required to get their work done in a single package. Companies no longer need to rely on expensive pre-packaged software with superfluous functionality that means nothing to them.
The biggest advantage of building custom business software is that companies get to fully own the applications they build. When they design their apps with Reflex, they can avoid getting locked into an expensive third-party ecosystem. Whenever new functions are needed, teams can describe the capability they want in natural language, iterate, tweak the design and so on until they get it just right.
Customers also get plenty of flexibility too, with Reflex’s software able to run in the public cloud, on-premises data centers or in highly secure air-gapped environments. This makes them more attractive to enterprises in tightly regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare and government, the startup says.
Reflex is led by its co-founder and Chief Executive Nikhil Rao (pictured, right), who previously served as one of the first engineers at the autonomous driving startup Drive.ai Inc. When that company was acquired by Apple Inc., he joined the iPhone maker’s Special Projects Group, where he helped to create many AI innovations. The startup’s other co-founder is Chief Technology Officer Alek Petuskey (left), who formerly worked as a machine learning engineer at Ancestry.com Inc. and a researcher at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
Rao and Petuskey originally developed Reflex as an open-source Python framework and only decided to build a company around it after seeing it explode in popularity. Within months, Reflex had built up a loyal developer community, racking up almost 30,000 GitHub stars and reaching 400,000 monthly downloads. To date, Reflex has been used to build over a million deployed applications globally, with its users including some of the world’s biggest organizations, including Amazon.com Inc., Walmart Inc., The World Bank and Dell Technologies Inc.
Dell used Reflex’s platform to design and build a dedicated server monitoring system that’s now being used by more than 6,000 of its staff. Meanwhile, an unnamed aerospace company used Reflex to rip out and replace its legacy manufacturing resource planning platform. With massive customers like these, it’s little wonder that Reflex has managed to grow its revenue more than 10 times in the past year.
Standard Capital’s Dalton Caldwell the popularity of AI coding has made many companies realize that there is an alternative to buying traditional software-as-a-service applications. “Most companies still run on software that was built for someone else’s business,” he said. “Nikhil and Alek built a platform companies already trust and an elite team that helps create production software for non-software companies.”
Reflex said the next thing on the agenda is to expand its engineering and sales operations teams to support the growing demand for its custom software platform in the traditional corporate and government sectors. It’s also putting the final touches on a new product called Workflows, which will use AI agents to automate multistep business operations.

articles.title: No Man's Sky Forsaken Update Adds "Spooky Biomechanical Ships" and Wealth of New Exploration Content
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
No Man's Sky Forsaken Update Adds "Spooky Biomechanical Ships" and Wealth of New Exploration Content
No Man's Sky had a rough start to life, with Hello Games having had to put in nearly a decade's worth of work to right the ship and get the game to "Very Positive" reviews on Steam. Now, following a handful of significant gameplay and content updates since that success, Hello Games has announced the Forsaken update, a new content update to No Man's Sky that builds on the game's exploration, building, and research mechanics.
The Forsaken update, officially version 7.10 of the game, adds a minimal HUD mode for a more immersive experience, minimizing the compass, hazard protection bars, and mission notifications. Hello Games says this mode is especially suited for experienced players. On the gameplay and content side of things, however, the update also introduces "Haunting Mementos," a new set piece that sees gamers searching the abandoned wrecks, infested outposts, and derelict freighters in deep space for "bizarre, horrifying biological samples."Building on the "spooky" encounters in the aforementioned Haunting Mementos game mechanic, the Forsaken update also adds new biomechanical corvette modules that players can construct to give their ships a "touch of the sinister." There is also a new Vantage-Class cockpit that gives players a panoramic view of the outdoors while providing a minimalist interior, in addition to several other cockpit designs and new interior designs. On the topic of cosmetics, the new larva tank helmet also allows players to have fun with their player character customization by replacing their head with a parasitic larva in a glass tank.Another headline feature in the update is seamless interstellar travel with new warp travel capabilities. There are also new space courier contracts that reward players handsomely for interplanetary package deliveries. Off-planet bases can now also be uploaded to the shared server, allowing players to visit other players' orbital space stations. There is also now detailed guidance for space scavenging, and the Holo-Arena creature battles have now been added to deep-space outposts.The No Man's Sky Forsaken update trailer follows.

articles.title: How Edge AI Helps Humanoid Robots React Faster Than a Central GPU - EE Times
articles.text:
STMicroelectronics argued that humanoid robots should use onboard sensors and cameras to handle fast reactions on the robot, and leave only whole-body coordination to a central GPU, because a round trip to the GPU adds latency a moving robot cannot afford. The chipmaker is still weighing whether to build more powerful MCUs or MPUs for the task, a decision it says depends on how the robotics market develops.
“Every millisecond counts,” Allan Lagasca, director of STMicroelectronics’ robotics segment strategic program, told EE Times. “If you want a fast reaction, you should move the processing to the edge. If you want the entire system to work together, that is where the GPU comes in.”
Running inference closer to the task can reduce the workload sent to a central GPU and avoid delays associated with transferring data and returning commands, Lagasca said. In robotics, those delays can affect physical movement.
When two hands coordinate to transfer an object, for example, a delayed command can cause a joint to miss its target. Even if individual joints miss their targets by only a few millimeters, the combined movement can be affected.
“If inference is performed at the edge, the system can send the necessary command locally and respond faster,” he said.
The central GPU, which Lagasca called the robot’s “larger brain,” still has to synchronize the head cameras, machine vision, and navigation, and coordinate joints whose sensors are not connected to one another. Without that coordination, he said, “the robot could move both feet forward at the wrong time.” STMicroelectronics does not make GPUs.
The chipmaker’s current AI inference products are based on its neural processing unit (NPU) and microprocessor unit (MPU), Lagasca said. Whether it develops more powerful chips depends on how the market evolves.
Robotics is still a low-volume market, while STMicroelectronics, as an integrated device manufacturer, targets high-volume production. “By following this market, we will better understand which technologies are needed,” he said.
Where the hand does its own thinking
In a robotic hand demonstration at electronica India, a camera captured an image of a human hand, and an AI model identified 21 points to recognize the gesture. The system then translated that information into commands for a robotic hand with six motors. Gesture recognition ran on STMicroelectronics’ STM32N6 32-bit microcontroller.
“The mapping is not simple,” Lagasca said. “It is not even a one-to-one or one-to-two relationship, and it must run continuously as the hand moves.”
The work starts with the camera. Its module combines an image sensor to capture images, an inertial measurement unit (IMU) to determine the camera’s position and orientation, and a time-of-flight (ToF) sensor to measure distance. “Capturing an image is not enough; you also need to measure the distance,” Lagasca said. The ToF reading tells the hand when to close its fingers.
Inference also runs mainly onboard the camera, partly for privacy, Lagasca said. As long as an image is used for inference without being stored or sent elsewhere, the system can meet privacy and cybersecurity requirements, he added.
The camera’s output then has to be translated into commands the motors can use. Lagasca said the gesture recognition demonstration used a standard PLC to bridge AI outputs and robotic control. “The difficulty lies in translating the data generated by AI into a format that can be transferred to a standard PLC to control the robot,” he said.
The same edge approach enables the hand to adjust its grip. Humans adjust their hold on a water bottle almost instinctively; a robot has to compute the required grip.
In another example, Lagasca described a hand that identifies a water bottle, determines its distance, and adjusts its grip to avoid crushing it or letting it slip. “The MCU, in this case the STM32, performs this inference,” he said.
Each part of the robot handles its share. Most sensors have their own MCUs, Lagasca said, as do the motion and motor-control functions, while AI inference has its own NPU. “This creates a distributed architecture rather than putting everything into a single processor,” he said.
Integrating robotic modules and simplifying hardware
Humanoid robot manufacturers may source hands, joints, and cameras from different suppliers. Integrating these components can create problems with camera placement, board space, and motor control. A camera mounted on top of a hand may require the robot to reposition its hand before lifting an object, while one mounted underneath may strike the table during pickup.
STMicroelectronics said it is exploring ways to integrate camera technology and other functions into the humanoid hand itself. Although the company does not manufacture camera modules, it can combine its technologies with those of its partners. Earlier this year, STMicroelectronics and camera-module maker Leopard Imaging introduced a multimodal vision module for humanoid robots that combines STMicroelectronics’ imaging technology, 3D depth-mapping, and motion sensors. The module connects over Ethernet through Nvidia’s Holoscan Sensor Bridge to Nvidia’s Jetson computers and Isaac robot development platform. It is designed to fit the size, weight, and power limits of humanoid robots.
Lagasca said the broader approach is to divide the robot into modules, including hands, joints, feet, and eyes, that can be adapted to different applications and form factors.
Packaging the required functions within these modules presents another challenge. Designers must fit processing, motor control, and connectivity into the available board space. Lagasca cited a customer requirement for a 6 × 6-centimeter board.
Choosing MCUs, motor drivers, and connectivity parts separately could produce a design measuring 140 × 330 mm, far larger than the board, he said. For its robotic hand, ST integrated six MOSFETs and three drivers into one package, so a manufacturer can mount one part instead of nine.
Safety remains an open question
The distribution of intelligence across a robot also raises safety concerns. Lagasca said existing safety frameworks include Safety Integrity Level (SIL) requirements for industrial applications and Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) requirements in the automotive sector. These requirements may become relevant as companies from the automotive, industrial automation, smartphone, and home appliance markets enter robotics.
However, compliance with a standard doesn’t guarantee that the entire robot is safe.
“If a sensor fails, the robot could still cause an injury, even if it meets the relevant SIL or ASIL standard,” Lagasca said.
AI can introduce additional risks if a system fails to make a decision or makes the wrong one, he said. All these elements must be considered together to assess a robot’s functional safety.
Lagasca added that many existing standards were developed for fixed equipment rather than moving robots. The industry still needs to determine which standards and regulatory requirements are appropriate for humanoid systems, particularly those that interact directly with people.
The chipmaker’s role in the humanoid bill of materials
Lagasca said that STMicroelectronics can address approximately 600 positions in a humanoid robot’s bill of materials (BOM), covering more than 500 components. The share of a robot’s total cost that this represents depends on its design, including how many joints, sensors, and AI functions the robot has, he added.
As an illustration, he said that if a robot’s BOM were worth $600 and STMicroelectronics supplied all of it, the chipmaker’s share would be 100%. If the BOM grew to $1,000 while the chipmaker’s parts remained valued at $600, its share would fall to 60%.
Entry-level robots may cost less and have fewer degrees of freedom, while mid-range and high-end systems may require more sophisticated capabilities. Depending on the design, Lagasca said STMicroelectronics could potentially address 800 or more positions as the number of joints, sensors, cameras, and AI-processing requirements increases.
From demonstrations to deployment
Despite the growing number of humanoid robot demonstrations, Lagasca said many applications remain at the proof-of-concept stage. Automotive manufacturing and logistics are among the early areas of interest because manufacturers can justify the cost of automation and adjust production lines to meet market demand.
He cited Boston Dynamics’ association with Hyundai and Figure AI’s relationship with BMW as examples of links between humanoid robotics and the automotive industry. Hyundai, which owns Boston Dynamics, plans to start deploying Atlas robots at its Georgia plant in 2028, while BMW has conducted trials for Figure robots in its Spartanburg, S.C., body shop.
Moving beyond demonstrations presents several challenges. Training data is one of them. Activities such as drilling, soldering, cooking, and sewing can be recorded and uploaded to create datasets, Lagasca said.
Battery technology doesn’t yet support 24-hour operation, he said, making downtime a practical consideration for developers.
The applications that reach the market will also depend on safety and regulatory requirements. Lagasca said direct physical interaction between humanoid robots and people presents additional challenges, particularly in healthcare.
Cybersecurity is another concern. Lagasca said that chipmakers and device manufacturers must account for the EU Cyber Resilience Act and other applicable requirements at both the product and application levels. “You do not want 10,000 robots operating in the real world only for someone to hack into them,” he said.
How intelligence is ultimately distributed between the edge processors and the central GPU may depend on a question the industry has not settled: What a humanoid robot should look like. The system architecture “has not stabilized,” Lagasca said. “Some developers ask why a robot should have only two hands rather than six, or only two legs.”
“We do not yet know what the final configuration will be,” he said.
