articles.title: Amazon warns engineers against "tokenmaxxing" as it shifts focus from AI usage to actual productivity
articles.text:
Big quote: Amazon is telling its engineering teams to judge AI coding tools by the software they help deliver, not the volume of tokens they consume. The updated engineering guidelines warn against treating AI adoption, token consumption, code changes and code reviews as performance targets. "We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes," Amazon wrote.
Amazon is not abandoning usage data. It is asking managers to examine those figures alongside other indicators.
The company recommends examining teams at both ends of AI adoption. Low usage may suggest engineers are missing opportunities to improve their work. Heavy usage should prompt a different question: whether delivery is improving enough to justify it. Neither figure settles the question on its own.
The guidance targets tokenmaxxing – deliberately inflating AI consumption to appear productive on internal dashboards.
Earlier this year, Amazon employees were using MeshClaw, an internal AI agent that can deploy code and interact with Slack, to increase their token counts. Amazon shut down an internal leaderboard in May after employees gamed the rankings. Amazon says it has not imposed employee token caps.
Amazon's guidance leaves room for engineers to conclude that a particular task does not benefit from the available tools. It describes that conclusion as "a finding, not a failing," treating an explanation of a tool's limitations as evidence of judgment rather than resistance to adoption.
"We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice," the company wrote.
Other companies are confronting similar gaps between AI consumption and useful output. Uber president and COO Andrew Macdonald said in May that higher token usage had not yet translated into useful consumer features. His comments followed the company's disclosure that it had exhausted its 2026 Claude Code budget by April.
At Accenture, leaked audio obtained by 404 Media in June captured executives discussing rising token spending as clients moved from chatbots to agentic workflows. Executives discussed uncertainty about both the cost of individual tasks and whether the spending was worthwhile. The firm was reportedly developing an advisory tool called Token IQ to help clients manage those expenses.

articles.title: Samsung confirms record-breaking operating profit on soaring AI memory chip demand - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Samsung confirms record-breaking operating profit on soaring AI memory chip demand
Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. today confirmed it has set a new world record for quarterly profit in the technology industry.
It delivered a stunning 107.44 trillion won ($80.5 billion) in third-quarter operating profit on the back of soaring demand for the memory chips fueling the artificial intelligence boom.
The company also reported 195.25 trillion won in revenue during the quarter, up 127% from the same period one year ago. In addition, it said its board has approved a 30 trillion won cash dividend for shareholders. Samsung’s operating profit surged more than 780% from the year prior, while its net profit increased by 515%, to 75.15 trillion won.
The impressive results confirmed what Samsung had projected in its preliminary earnings guidance at the beginning of the month, making it the first South Korean company in any industry to cross the 100 trillion won mark in terms of quarterly operating profit.
Samsung is benefiting from unparalleled demand for memory chips, which is being driven by heavy investment from hyperscalers in AI infrastructure. That demand has led to global shortages of memory chips and soaring prices. The lion’s share of Samsung’s revenue and profit stemmed from its Device Solutions unit, which houses its semiconductor business. The company is one of the world’s three biggest suppliers of memory chips, and that helped the unit to generate a massive 147.1 trillion won in revenue and 106.5 trillion won in operating profit.
Samsung’s results come just one day after its Korean rival SK hynix Inc. reported strong earnings of its own and provided an upbeat outlook. The company echoed what its rival said when it forecast the global memory chip shortage to deepen in fiscal 2027. The companies’ strong performances will help to ease market concerns that AI chipmaker’s earnings could lose momentum if the AI boom starts to fizzle out amid funding concerns. Samsung’s stock rose 2% during early trading in South Korea on Thursday morning.
Samsung’s memory chip business could become even more profitable in the coming months. During the quarter, it announced a new partnership with the French AI model maker Mistral AI. As part of that collaboration, Samsung plans to integrate AI within its semiconductor design and manufacturing operations, with the aim of optimizing those processes.
Elsewhere, Samsung’s display business delivered 8 trillion won in revenue and an operating profit of 1.1 trillion won. However, the MX and Networks business unit, which includes sales of Samsung’s smartphones, posted an operating loss of 0.6 trillion won on total sales of 37.7 trillion won.
Samsung’s smartphone sales have been a direct victim of the rising costs of memory chips, which has been reflected in the higher prices of many of its handsets this year. However, the company said it’s hopeful of a boost in the fourth quarter, which is traditionally the peak season for smartphone sales, centered on new flagship devices such as the Galaxy S26 series, the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra and the Z Fold8.
Samsung said it will pay 30 trillion won in dividends to shareholders for the third quarter, amounting to about 4,601 won per share.

articles.title: Formula V Line Launches Crystal Z3 Panoramic PC Case Series
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Formula V Line Launches Crystal Z3 Panoramic PC Case Series
Formula V Line today launches the Crystal Z3 series of panoramic ATX mid-tower PC cases, combining a 90° rotatable rear PCIe bracket with bottom air intake integrated into the case design. The initial shipment consists of Crystal Z3 Plus models in Black and White, each with three PA2 120 mm ARGB PWM fans.
First previewed at COMPUTEX 2026, the Crystal Z3 series supports graphics cards up to 425 mm long, a 360 mm top radiator and up to eight 120 mm fans. Its removable bottom fan bracket and tool-free panels make it easier to assemble, upgrade and clean a display-focused PC.Rotate the Rear PCIe Bracket for GPU Display
The rear PCIe bracket rotates 90°, allowing a graphics card to be installed horizontally or presented vertically through the glass. Vertical installation requires compatible PCIe riser hardware.
Bring Cool Air In from Below
Intake vents along the front and side of the lower panel feed the bottom fan positions while keeping the glass-forward exterior clean. After removing two screws, builders can lift out the bottom fan bracket to clean its nylon dust filter without detaching the installed fans.
Three PA2 Fans Included with Z3 Plus
The initial Crystal Z3 Plus models include three PA2 120 mm fans, with two at the bottom and one at the rear. Each has 4-pin PWM speed control and 3-pin ARGB lighting connectivity. The chassis supports up to eight 120 mm fans in total.
Open the Panels Without Tools
Quick-release latches on the front and both side panels provide access for installation and upgrades. Removable filters at the top, bottom and side air intakes make routine cleaning easier.Fit Large GPUs and Four Storage Drives
The Crystal Z3 series supports ATX, Micro ATX and Mini-ITX motherboards, GPUs up to 425 mm, CPU coolers up to 180 mm and a top radiator up to 360 mm. The chassis can hold two 2.5-inch SSDs and two 3.5-inch HDDs at the same time. Front I/O includes USB 3.0, USB 2.0, 10 Gbps USB Type-C and HD audio.
To leave room for the bottom intake and fan positions, power supplies are limited to 140 mm in length, including cables. Builders should check the length of their PSU and cable assembly before purchase.
Pricing and Availability
The initial Crystal Z3 Plus shipment comprises Black at an MSRP of US$79.99 and White at an MSRP of US$89.99. Both models are available in the United States from October 27, 2026, through Newegg. Formula V Line's regional partners handle availability in other markets.

articles.title: Malaysia seizes $12 million worth of advanced AI chips hidden inside 30 servers — customs says suspected smuggling network used the country as a transit hub
articles.text:
Malaysia seizes $12 million worth of advanced AI chips hidden inside 30 servers — customs says suspected smuggling network used the country as a transit hub
Authorities have seized $25 million worth of chips in cases linked to syndicate
Malaysian customs have seized over $12 million (49.5 million Malaysian ringgit) worth of advanced AI chips in a single bust, as the country clamps down on a suspected semiconductor smuggling syndicate. According to a Reuters report on October 28, officials found 30 servers containing the chips at Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s free trade zone on October 15th. Initial investigations revealed that the shipment originated in an Asian country and was bound for another undisclosed Asian country.
The airport’s customs director, Aspalila Ag Tuah, confirmed that the servers were falsely declared as ordinary electronic goods, saying the suspected scheme used Malaysia as a transit point to avoid restrictions on the goods’ onward movement. The Malaysian company involved in the shipment has been summoned to assist in the investigation.
Authorities suspect that the foiled smuggling attempt was carried out by the same group responsible for a similar attempt last June. On June 5, customs officers discovered 72 server units containing advanced AI chips at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport, valued at approximately $13 million. This shipment had also been falsely declared as computer components and was meant to be reshipped without the required permit. Aspalila said the network has been linked to seizures worth over $25 million so far across at least five cases. She declined to provide further information on the network or the current case, citing ongoing investigations.
Several key facts remain unknown, including the chip type, country of manufacture, final destination, and intended recipient — whether a company or a military organization. The U.S. had placed export controls on the movement of advanced Nvidia and other U.S.-origin AI chips to China, the most likely destination for the seized chips. Smuggling networks began using Malaysia, a U.S. ally not affected by the controls, as a hub, exporting the banned chips to the country before re-exporting them to China.
While the country’s geographic location and mature logistics infrastructure make it important for legitimate international trade, these characteristics also make it ideal for smuggling sensitive technology. To restrict this avenue, Malaysia subsequently imposed export controls on the movement of advanced AI chips of U.S. origin, at Washington’s request. Other Asian U.S. allies, such as Singapore and Taiwan, have implemented similar controls. Demand for powerful Nvidia GPUs remains high in China, fueling a booming market for smuggled hardware.

articles.title: India’s new-age manufacturers to benefit from $3 trillion global AI investment cycle: Avendus Capital
articles.text:
India’s new-age manufacturers to benefit from $3 trillion global AI investment cycle: Avendus Capital
The investment banking firm has identified defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials as the sectors that will drive India’s next phase of industrial growth.
India’s new-age manufacturing sector could benefit significantly from a $3 trillion global AI infrastructure investment cycle, according to a report by Avendus Capital.
The investment banking firm has identified defence and aerospace, space technology, robotics and automation, semiconductors, energy transition, and advanced materials as the sectors poised to drive India’s next phase of industrial growth, offering key opportunities for domestic companies.
The report highlighted 2027–28 as a critical period for commercialisation as companies move from policy support and project approvals towards production.
The opportunity is being driven by rising global investments in AI infrastructure, increasing demand for energy infrastructure, and growing geopolitical security concerns. India’s domestic demand, engineering talent and policy framework could help manufacturers reduce import dependence and build globally competitive capabilities.
“India's new-age manufacturing opportunity is substantial, but its right-to-win manifests in select segments,” said Koushik Bhattacharyya, Managing Director and Head of Industrials Investment Banking at Avendus Capital.
With more than 80% of the $3 trillion AI infrastructure investment yet to be deployed globally, India has an opportunity to capitalise on its domestic demand base, engineering capabilities, and policy support, he said.
Semiconductors and space technology are among the segments showing significant growth potential. India’s semiconductor consumption is projected to more than double from $49.5 billion in 2025 to $106.5 billion by 2030, creating opportunities in chip design, packaging, testing, and specialised materials.
India’s space economy is expected to expand more than threefold, from approximately $13 billion in 2025 to $44 billion by 2033. Domestic defence production is projected to reach around $31.6 billion by 2030, while the robotics market could grow nearly fourfold to $4.6 billion by 2030, supported by wider adoption and import substitution.
The report also expects India’s clean-energy manufacturing ecosystem to move further upstream over the next five years. By the end of the decade, the country could establish an integrated solar manufacturing chain spanning ingots to modules, several gigawatt-hour-scale battery cell plants, and commercial production of indigenous electrolyser stacks and rare-earth-free motor technology.
Advanced materials represent another emerging opportunity, with rising domestic demand and heavy import dependence creating scope for local capacity building. Recycling is expected to scale first, followed by battery materials, while rare-earth magnet manufacturing could advance with policy support.
The coming years will test India’s ability to translate these opportunities into commercially viable manufacturing capabilities, the report said.

articles.title: Google dévoile Gemini 4 Carbon pour enfin détrôner GPT-6 Astra et Claude Opus 5.5, mais presque personne ne peut l’essayer
articles.text:
Google dévoile Gemini 4 Carbon pour enfin détrôner GPT-6 Astra et Claude Opus 5.5, mais presque personne ne peut l’essayer
Deux semaines après Gemini 4 Argon, Google dévoile Gemini 4 Carbon : un nouveau modèle surpassant GPT-6 Astra et Claude Opus 5.5, tout en cassant les prix. Il est cependant disponible pour peu de monde.
La course aux modèles d’intelligence artificielle redémarre de plus belle. Deux semaines à peine après la sortie générale de Gemini 4 Argon, Google officialise déjà Gemini 4 Carbon, son modèle le plus avancé à ce jour. Conçu pour exceller dans le code, les tâches agentiques et la cybersécurité, il devance enfin les fleurons d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic, sortis en septembre dernier. La bonne nouvelle dans l’histoire, c’est que la facture est deux à cinq fois moins élevée pour les développeurs.
Google devient le leader des benchmarks avec Gemini 4 Carbon, mais pour combien de temps ?
Annoncé hier, Gemini 4 Carbon s’impose d’emblée comme “notre modèle le plus puissant, doté de capacités de pointe en cybersécurité et sur les tâches de longue haleine”, souligne Koray Kavukcuoglu, vice-président senior chez Google DeepMind.
Sur l’indice Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, qui évalue les capacités générales d’une IA, il décroche la première place avec 59 points, devançant Claude Opus 5.5 (58 points) et GPT-6 Astra (57 points), là où Argon plafonnait à 50 points. En interne, le modèle a fonctionné “pendant des jours pour persévérer face aux impasses” et corriger des bugs subtils dans d’immenses bases de code. Résultat : il obtient 65,2 % sur Terminal-Bench 4.0 et 9,6 % sur SWE-sweep, tout en faisant bondir son score de 89 points Elo en développement web (4e sur WebDev Arena).
En matière de cybersécurité, Carbon domine SEC-bench Pro (88,2 %), CWE-bench (71,0 %) et ExploitGym (54,8 %). Selon l’équipe de Google Chrome, il s’est même montré “plus de dix fois plus performant qu’un grand modèle concurrent” pour générer des correctifs de haute qualité.
Côté fiabilité, Google indique avoir entraîné son IA pour “répondre aux tâches complexes ou sous haute pression de la bonne manière”. Gemini 4 Carbon divise par deux les affirmations non vérifiées, signale les incohérences au lieu de deviner face à une consigne ambiguë et réduit de près de 80 % les alertes graves de désalignement. En prime, ce modèle ne cherche plus à contourner les règles des tests de code pour gonfler ses scores (0 % de triche réussie sur Terminal-Bench 4.0), et bloque 100 % des attaques par injection de prompt indirecte via le benchmark de Gray Swan.
Au lancement, l’API est facturée 2 $ par million de tokens en entrée et 10 $ en sortie pour les développeurs, contre 4 et 20 $ pour Claude Opus 5.5 (tarif que Carbon rejoindra après sa période promotionnelle) et 10 et 50 $ pour GPT-6 Astra. Engagé dans le processus de tests préalables du gouvernement américain, Google réserve d’abord Gemini 4 Carbon aux experts en cybersécurité du programme Fairwind avant un déploiement élargi.
De quoi combler un retard de quelques semaines face à ses concurrents, qui ne devraient pas tarder à répliquer bientôt avec des modèles encore plus performants pour reprendre la tête.

articles.title: He cambiado mi cartera del móvil por Bizum Pay durante un mes: la app funciona, las tiendas todavía no
articles.text:
Empezó sin hacer ruido y ha terminado por convertirse en el estándar a la hora de enviar dinero a los colegas. Porque ¿quién no tiene Bizum? Es casi tan omnipresente como WhatsApp: Bizum suma 31,5 millones de usuarios. Y poco a poco está colonizando el espacio que le faltaba a la plataforma: los pagos físicos en comercios. Llevo más de un mes pagando con Bizum, y creo que puede sustituir al resto de las carteras móviles.
Bizum Pay, así se llama el invento. Es como pagar normalmente con el móvil, solo que el dinero se mueve entre la cuenta del cliente y la del comercio sin pasar por las redes de las tarjetas. Ni Visa ni Mastercard, por eso los pagos de Bizum suponen un verdadero cambio en Europa. Ahora bien, hace falta un proceso previo. Aquí empieza el lío.
Dos maneras de configurar los pagos de Bizum
Los pagos en comercio físico se hacen acercando el NFC del teléfono al del datáfono. Para que funcionen, debes tener configurados los pagos con Bizum en tu móvil y el comercio debe soportarlos en su terminal de cobro. A partir de aquí el proceso es el habitual: la plataforma hace una transferencia entre cuentas sin que tu banco te cobre comisiones. A la tienda sí podrían cobrarle un porcentaje, todo depende de las condiciones de su banco.
Pagar con Bizum es tan fácil como hacerlo con cualquier tarjeta del móvil. Configurar los pagos es otra historia, porque se puede hacer de dos maneras:
- Pagos físicos con Bizum desde la app del banco. Hay bancos que han habilitado esta manera de pagar sin hacer uso de otras aplicaciones, como BBVA. Abre tu app bancaria, entra en el apartado de Bizum y comprueba si allí está la opción de los pagos con Bizum. Actívala y listo.
- Pagos físicos con la app Bizum Pay. Esta es la aplicación propia de la plataforma, una cartera genérica en la que no solo puedes pagar con Bizum, también con la tarjeta de tu banco. Es la forma más cómoda de usar estos pagos y la que yo te recomiendo.
Tengo descargada la app de Bizum Pay y la configuré con mi cuenta de Bizum. El proceso es sencillo, ya que solo hay que abrir la aplicación y teclear el número de móvil asociado al propio Bizum. Si el banco ya tiene habilitados los pagos, Bizum Pay completa la configuración. A día de hoy, la app funciona con CaixaBank, Sabadell, Unicaja, Caja Rural, Bankinter, Ibercaja, Grupo Cooperativo Cajamar, Abanca, Arquia Banca, Colonya Caixa Pollença e ING.
El truco: la tarjeta secundaria
Los pagos de Bizum aún no están en gran parte de comercios. Por mi experiencia personal, queda mucho para que podamos pagar sin tarjetas, por más que durante las últimas semanas los bancos y tiendas hayan pegado un acelerón. Dado que pagar con Bizum en la aplicación Bizum Pay es una lotería, esta cartera deja añadir algunas tarjetas asociadas a la cuenta bancaria del usuario.
Bizum Pay es una aplicación de cartera como lo son Google Wallet o Apple Wallet. Permite registrar los pagos de Bizum sin contacto, también otras tarjetas. En caso de que la tienda no esté preparada, puedes cambiar a una tarjeta corriente sin salir de la app. Algo que, a día de hoy, vas a hacer a menudo.
El proceso queda de la siguiente manera:
- El cajero escanea los artículos de la compra y pasa la cuenta al datáfono.
- Debes desbloquear el móvil configurado con Bizum Pay (en iPhone, pulsar dos veces el botón lateral) y acercarlo al datáfono. Si no lo añadiste como cartera por defecto en tu móvil (lo que recomiendo), abre manualmente Bizum Pay.
- El datáfono detectará la cuenta de Bizum como medio de pago y cobrará el importe enviando el dinero desde tu cuenta bancaria a la del comercio.
- ¿La tienda aún no acepta los pagos con Bizum? Bizum Pay dirá en pantalla si quieres cambiar a la tarjeta. Tienes que acercar otra vez el móvil al datáfono.
Registrar una tarjeta como pago secundario en Bizum Pay asegura poder usar la aplicación como medio de pago, porque si el datáfono de la tienda no acepta los pagos con Bizum seguro que sí admite los pagos corrientes con tarjeta. El problema es que el cajero ve el pago como cancelado y debe enviar de nuevo la cuenta al datáfono, algo que ralentiza el cobro. Si Bizum se acepta a la primera no hay más inconveniente.
No es una solución 100 % española
Como experiencia, pagar con Bizum es igual que hacerlo con una tarjeta: el usuario no aprecia nada distinto. Lo que va por debajo de la transacción sí supone un cambio. Uno gigantesco: los pagos de Bizum son una solución que no utiliza la plataforma de los dos gigantes estadounidenses, Visa y Mastercard. ¿Supone la soberanía española en los pagos? No del todo.
Contacté con Bizum para contrastar si sus pagos móviles son completamente propios, sin tecnología estadounidense. Es así en su mayor parte, con un detalle del que sigue dependiendo: cómo se identifica el móvil ante el datáfono cuando lo acercas por NFC.
Según me explicó Bizum:
"No utilizamos ninguna tecnología de Visa o Mastercard para realizar el pago, basado en transferencias inmediatas SEPA, desde cuenta con Bizum. Sí se utiliza una pieza EMV de otro proveedor que ya está disponible en terminales de España y Andorra, gracias a un acuerdo de las entidades con la marca".
"Esto permite tokenizar el identificador de la persona usuaria, es decir, el teléfono con el que está registrado en Bizum, para que pueda ser aceptado por los terminales existentes y generar luego una transacción cuenta a cuenta en el ecosistema Bizum, como sucede en los otros casos de uso".
El estándar EMV, acrónimo de Europay, Mastercard y Visa, permite que las tarjetas se autoricen en los datáfonos de forma segura para proceder a la transacción bancaria. Hoy lo gestiona EMVCo, una sociedad que controlan Visa, Mastercard y otras cuatro redes de tarjetas. Es un estándar ampliamente utilizado en todo el mundo y que está disponible en la mayoría de datáfonos españoles. Por eso lo ha elegido Bizum: facilita desplegar los pagos más rápidamente.
El móvil tiene mucho que decir
Aparte del EMV, existe una segunda dependencia de la que se habla menos: el propio teléfono. Android es de Google e iOS es de Apple, y son ellos quienes deciden qué apps pueden usar el NFC para pagar. En el iPhone, Bizum Pay solo es posible porque la Comisión Europea forzó a Apple a abrir el chip a otras carteras.
¿Bizum Pay sustituye al resto de carteras? Puede hacerlo, aunque hoy lo consigue gracias a la tarjeta secundaria, que tapa cada hueco que deja Bizum. El día que las tiendas lo acepten a la primera, pagar con el móvil dejará de pasar por las redes de Visa y Mastercard sin que notemos nada. No es una soberanía al 100 %, pero sí en lo que más importa: el camino que sigue el dinero.
Y el siguiente paso ya tiene fecha. Bizum firmó en febrero con Wero, MB Way, Bancomat y Vipps MobilePay un acuerdo para conectar sus sistemas: los pagos en tiendas de otros países llegarían en 2027. Pagar el café en Lisboa o en París con Bizum, eso sí sería un cambio gigantesco.

articles.title: Lenovo Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 tem R$ 1.500 OFF em até 12x na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Lenovo Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 tem R$ 1.500 OFF em até 12x na Amazon
Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 vem com caneta Tab Pen Plus e tem tela de 13" com taxa de 144 Hz; tablet para jogos da Lenovo sai 32% mais barato no prazo
O Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 Wi-Fi de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 3.149 em até 12x sem juros na Amazon. O tablet topo de linha da Lenovo, com tela de 144 Hz, chip Snapdragon e que inclui no kit a capa Folio e a caneta Tab Pen Plus, recebe desconto de 32% sobre o preço original de R$ 4.649.
O Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 é um tablet premium com alta performance em apps e games, graças ao chip Qualcomm Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 e aos 8 GB de RAM, conforme visto em nossos testes, embora o modelo do review seja o com 12 GB de RAM. Os 256 GB de espaço interno podem ser expandidos com cartões microSD.
Sua tela LCD de 13″ com taxa de 144 Hz e resolução 3,5K (3.504 x 2.190 pixels) oferece amplo espaço para consumir conteúdo e rodar apps de produtividade. O revestimento antirreflexo permite ao tablet ser usado ao ar livre sem problemas.
O kit inclui o tablet, a capa Folio e a caneta Tab Pen Plus, que oferece precisão ao escrever e desenhar. O uso produtivo é reforçado pelo Modo PC, que habilita uma interface de desktop melhor aproveitada com um teclado, não incluso neste kit.
O kit de câmeras do Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 inclui uma traseira de 13 MP com autofoco e Flash, boa para digitalizar documentos e capaz de filmar em 4K, e uma frontal de 8 MP adequada para videoconferências, que filma em 1080p.
Sua bateria de 10.020 mAh resiste a até 14 horas de streaming de vídeo, conforme o review, e suporta carregamento de até 45 W via USB-C. Com o carregador de 20 W incluso no kit, ela recebeu uma carga completa em 2 horas e 26 minutos em nossos testes.
O Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 de 256 GB (R$ 3.149 em até 12x sem juros) roda Android 16 e deve receber mais duas atualizações do sistema operacional. O tablet da Lenovo possui conectividade Wi-Fi 7 e Bluetooth 6.0.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: I've never tested a wireless mouse that performs better than this SteelSeries model, but I still wouldn't recommend it to everyone — here's why
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
SteelSeries’ Sensei Pro Mini packages the brand’s clever ‘infinite’ battery system into a small pointer. It’s exceptional to game with and features an abundance of performance tweaks, the likes of which I haven’t seen before. But while its cableless design might be seen as a positive, I’m sure many will lament the absence of a wired option to fall back on. They may also lament the lack of Bluetooth support and its incredible expense. Ultimately, this means the Sensei Pro Mini isn’t a mouse for casuals, but if you require top-drawer wireless performance in miniature form, the Sensei Pro Mini is nigh-on unbeatable.
Reasons to buy
- + Good size for smaller hands
- + Excellent performance
- + Unmatched tweakability
Reasons to avoid
- - Lacks wired capability entirely
- - No additional Bluetooth connectivity
- - Very expensive
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
SteelSeries Sensei Pro Mini: Review
The Sensei Pro Mini brings pro-grade wireless performance to those who prefer less of a handful, thanks to its state-of-the-art polling technology and ceaseless power.
It has the same symmetrical shape as its larger sibling but on a smaller scale. Its size should prove suitable for those with smaller hands, allowing them to get a secure grip around the entire unit. At just 49g, it’s very light, too — lighter than the standard model by 4g — which makes it easy to maneuver.
The sidewalls have a pronounced cinch that forces you to clamp your thumb and ring finger further inwards than is typical, which some may prefer for added security. Grip tape is included in the box if you require more traction, which is entirely possible given the smoothness of the outer shell. The central hump might prove contentious in terms of fit, though: in my experience, it didn’t sit back far enough in my hand, landing underneath my knuckles rather than in the middle of my palm.
To customize and tweak the Sensei Pro Mini, you can use SteelSeries’ GG peripheral software. Here you can rebind all six buttons, with a fair amount of mapping options available, including keyboard inputs and shortcuts for media controls and system actions. You’ll find some standard performance tweaks as well, including DPI adjustments, although the range is larger than you’ll usually find on other gaming mice (between 1 to 65,000). There are five presets to customize, which you can cycle through using the DPI button underneath the mouse.
There are more advanced tweaks in addition to these, though. You can adjust the click response between 0ms and 20ms, and set the lift-off and landing distances independently, each with a range of 0.7 to 1.7 (presumably this refers to millimeters, though no unit of measurement is given). You can also enable a feature called Scroll Jump Protection, which ignores your first scroll unless a second is performed within a certain time of the first. This threshold is adjustable between 100ms and 1500ms. Motion Sync and Angle Snapping toggles are here as well, with the latter featuring a slider with 10 levels to adjust its straightening effect.
This isn’t all, though: a further section lets you adjust acceleration, with several graph curve presets available to alter cursor speed relative to movement speed, as well as the angle of the mouse’s sensor by 45 degrees either side of center to match the natural angle of your hand movements.
Then there are the polling and sensor adjustments. You can set the ultra-wideband (UWB) polling rate and the sensor report rate independently, each with a range of 125Hz to 8KHz (with added 9KHz overpolling). There are five presets containing various combinations of both rates, which can be cycled through using the button on the UWB base station.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
GG is clearly laid out and proved fast and stable during my time with it. It also contains explanations for many of its settings, which is something I’m always glad to see. One minor gripe I had is that the actual area to make adjustments and customizations opens in a second window, which is somewhat inconvenient.
The first thing that’s noticeable about the Sensei Pro Mini’s performance is just how smoothly it glides. This is no doubt thanks to the large PTFE skates underneath. There’s almost no friction when gliding over a mouse mat, which makes the Sensei Pro Mini feel incredibly gratifying to fling around, yet also allows for super-controlled slow movements.
Next is the Sensei Pro Mini’s buttons. Clicks are light and snappy enough for quick spams, yet still provide enough feedback to allow for controlled inputs. They also have just enough dampening to make them satisfying to use. The side buttons are great to use as well, being easy to reach and offering a clicky, tactile feel. The same is true of the middle click, and I didn’t trigger miscrolls when using it, since the notching, while light, is tight enough to prevent accidental knocks from registering. This also means that quick flicks and controlled single scrolls are both relatively easy to perform.
My one issue with the inputs concerns the DPI button. It’s underneath the Sensei Pro Mini, which makes it harder to access. This is exacerbated by the fact it’s placed on the thumb side (for right handers) rather than the pinkie side, which means you can’t wrap your fingers underneath to press it without turning the mouse over.
I didn’t experience any connectivity issues with the Sensei Pro Mini. Given the sheer size of the UWB station itself I would’ve been disappointed if I had. Also, the cable provided to connect it to your PC is long enough to give you versatile placement options to avoid interference. It’s a shame a mouse this expensive doesn’t have additional Bluetooth support, though; many other wireless gaming mice feature this, allowing you to hot-switch between two devices.
To power the Sensei Pro Mini, SteelSeries has kitted it out with its ‘infinite’ battery system, something it and a few other brands have used in mice and other peripherals before. The idea is that you’ll never need to go wired (the Sensei Pro Mini doesn’t even have a USB port) to charge. Instead, you’re provided a pair of removable batteries that you cycle between your mouse and the charging dock in the UWB station.
This system works well, as it’s quick and easy to remove and insert the batteries — just as well, since the battery life drains rapidly when every performance setting is at maximum, barely lasting a day. At less intensive settings, though, the battery’s longevity is much better, lasting more like several days.
There will be gamers who would like the reassurance of additional wired support, though, should connectivity be compromised for whatever reason (I’m reminded of inference issues derailing a recent Valorant tournament). At this very high price point, such an addition would be especially welcome, as would Bluetooth. As it stands, the Sensei Pro Mini is an elite gaming mouse with all the wireless performance a pro could hope for, and it’s perhaps only this cohort that’ll see the value in it.
SteelSeries Sensei Pro Mini review: Price & availability
- $179.99 / £169.99 (about AU$260)
- Available now in black and white variants
- Top-end of the wireless gaming mouse market
The Sensei Pro Mini costs $179.99 / £169.99 (about AU$260) and is available now in black or white. A full-size variant is also available for the same price. It comes with two swappable batteries, the UWB base station (which doubles as the battery charging dock), and a braided USB-C-to-A cable, as well as spare PTFE skates and optional grip tape.
Even for a pro-grade wireless gaming mouse, the Sensei Pro Mini is expensive. It’s the same price as the Razer Naga V3 Pro, although that mouse has additional Bluetooth and wired support, as well as a lot more buttons. If you want the same limitless battery power, you can pair it with Razer’s charging mouse mat, although this a costly addition to an already expensive mouse.
Another pointer with a similar battery swapping system is the AngryMiao AM Infinity.97. This is even lighter than the Sensei Pro Mini at 47g. However, its garish style won’t be for everyone, and its software pales in comparison to the tweaking depth on offer in GG.
SteelSeries Sensei Pro Mini review: Specs
| Connectivity | Wireless (Ultra-wideband) | 
| Battery life | 120 hours (1K), 32 hours (16 hours per battery) (8K) | 
| Sensor | TrueMove 42K Pro Sensor | 
| Polling rate | 8KHz (with 9KHz overpolling) | 
| Maximum sensitivity (DPI) | 42,000 (65,000 with DPI Overdrive) | 
| Programmable buttons | 6 | 
| Dimensions | 4.65 x 2.46 x 1.43 inches / 118 x 62.5 x 36.2mm | 
| Weight | 49g | 
Should I buy the SteelSeries Sensei Pro Mini?
Scorecard
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
| Design | A great size for those with smaller hands, although the hump might be inconveniently placed for some. The DPI button isn’t easily accessible, either. | 4/5 | 
| Performance | Super smooth gliding and all the buttons respond brilliantly. There are plenty of performance tweaks available in GG, too. | 4.5/5 | 
| Value | It’s very expensive, yet lacks Bluetooth and a wired option. Only gamers most concerned about elite wireless performance will see its worth. | 3/5 | 
Buy it if…
You want elite performance
Glides and inputs are superb, while the tweaking provided by GG is peerless.
You want infinite battery life
Thanks to the swappable battery system, you’ll never need to plug in to charge.
Don't buy it if…
You want a wired security
This mouse might upset Esports pros with its lack of a wired play, for when you can’t rely on a perfect wireless signal.
You’re a casual gamer
Its elite performance features will only be of use to the pros, while its lack of convenience features might deter those after something more versatile.
SteelSeries Sensei Pro Mini review: Also consider
Razer Naga V3 Pro
The Naga V3 Pro has additional Bluetooth support and wired capability, as well as a lot more inputs to customize. It also has ‘infinite’ battery life if used with Razer’s optional charging mouse pad, although this is an expensive add-on. Read our full Razer Naga V3 Pro review.
AngryMiao AM Infinity.97
If you want the same battery swapping system but in something more flashy, the AM Infinity.97 fits the bill. Its software is far less capable, though, and it’s slightly dearer than the Sensei Pro Mini. Read our full AngryMiao AM Infinity.97 review.
How I tested the SteelSeries Sensei Pro Mini
- Tested for a few days
- Used for various tasks, including gaming
- Plentiful PC gaming experience
I tested the Sensei Pro Mini for a few days, using it for not just gaming, but also working and general browsing.
I played Counter-Strike 2, which is a great test for gaming mice, since it demands quick and accurate movements and clicks.
I’ve been PC gaming for over a decade, and used a great deal of pointers in that time. I’ve also reviewed plenty of them before, including the full size Steelseries Sensei Pro.
- Read TechRadar’s reviews guarantee
- First reviewed: October 2026
Lewis Maddison is a Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He previously worked as a Staff Writer for our business section, TechRadar Pro, where he gained experience with productivity-enhancing hardware, ranging from keyboards to standing desks. His area of expertise lies in computer peripherals and audio hardware, having spent over a decade exploring the murky depths of both PC building and music production. He also revels in picking up on the finest details and niggles that ultimately make a big difference to the user experience.

articles.title: Windows 11 permet enfin de personnaliser le menu du clic droit
articles.text:
Microsoft continue de distiller petit à petit les améliorations promises il y a quelques mois pour améliorer Windows 11. La dernière mise à jour facultative distribuée en preview le prouve encore. Estampillée KB5127936 et proposée sur les PC fonctionnant aussi bien sous Windows 11 25H2 que Windows 11 26H2, cette mise à jour fait le plein de nouveautés dans l’Explorateur de fichiers du système d’exploitation.
La firme de Redmond ne s’est pas arrêtée en si bon chemin et y a également intégré d’autres nouveautés notables, comme la prise en charge de nouveaux emojis, de nouveaux réglages dans les paramètres du Bluetooth ou encore l’amélioration de la gestion de l’alimentation. Voici un petit tour d’horizon des principales nouveautés à retenir dans la mise à jour KB5127936.
Le menu contextuel du clic droit enfin personnalisable
Voici sans doute l’une des plus grandes nouveautés apportées par cette mise à jour. Longtemps critiqué pour son manque de cohérence et de flexibilité, le menu contextuel du clic droit s’assouplit enfin. Microsoft vous autorise dorénavant à choisir précisément ce que vous voulez y faire apparaître.
Pour ce faire, il faut se rendre dans les Paramètres > Personnalisation > Menu contextuel.
Le menu permet ainsi de masquer les actions inutiles comme la possibilité d’imprimer, d’envoyer à, de créer un raccourci ou encore de faire pivoter l’image.
Un nouveau réglage permettant de regrouper toutes les extensions d’applications tierces ou natives au sein d’un menu dédié a par ailleurs fait son apparition.
Autre nouveauté qui a son importance, vous pouvez à présent configurer le menu hérité pour qu’il s’affiche directement sans avoir à maintenir la touche Maj enfoncée. Il faut pour cela activer l’option Afficher plus d’options dans le menu de personnalisation du menu contextuel.
À noter que l’accès aux options de personnalisation du menu contextuel du clic droit dans l’Explorateur de fichiers peut également se faire directement depuis celui-ci. Microsoft a en effet eu la brillante idée d’intégrer dans le menu contextuel un accès direct pour Personnaliser le menu (activé par défaut).
De nouvelles améliorations pour l’Explorateur de fichiers
Outre les nouvelles options de personnalisation du menu contextuel du clic droit, l’Explorateur de fichiers accueille aussi un certain nombre d’améliorations. Il sait par exemple afficher par défaut la prévisualisation des fichiers PDF dans le volet prévu à cet effet. Quant aux fichiers HTML téléchargés, Windows affiche un bouton de confirmation avant l’affichage.
Autre nouveauté, comme nous vous l’indiquions il y a quelques semaines, l’Explorateur de fichiers prend désormais en charge le raccourci ~ pour accéder rapidement aux dossiers de profils. Vous pouvez donc saisir directement dans la barre d’adresse de l’Explorateur ~\Téléchargements pour accéder au répertoire des téléchargements, par exemple.
Microsoft a également harmonisé l’application du thème sombre pour que la boîte de dialogue liée aux Options des dossiers soit enfin prise en charge. Enfin, la page d’accueil de l’Explorateur de fichiers conserve désormais son état (réduit ou développé) des différentes sections qu’elle comporte.
De nouvelles options pour la récupération du système
L’environnement de récupération de Windows 11 profite également de cette mise à jour. Comme Microsoft l’avait dévoilé au début de l’été, son module Cloud Rebuild, qui permet de réinstaller Windows 11 sans clé USB, en téléchargeant directement l’image disque ISO et les pilotes depuis les serveurs de Microsoft, est officiellement disponible.
En mode récupération, le système est d’ailleurs capable de réutiliser automatiquement les profils Wi-Fi enregistrés sur le PC pour se connecter tout seul à Internet afin de procéder à la restauration depuis le Cloud. Enfin, après une restauration système, Windows affiche automatiquement une fenêtre récapitulant les applications du Microsoft Store et les paramètres ayant été correctement réinstallés.

articles.title: Panne géante chez Orange : Nokia visé pour une compensation financière
articles.text:
Le problème de réseau d'Orange ayant eu lieu la semaine dernière a fait du bruit. Et le géant des télécommunications veut maintenant que Nokia rende des comptes !
Le mercredi 21 octobre dernier, le réseau d'Orange tombait en panne, mettant de très nombreux de Français en difficulté. Résultat, pour se faire pardonner, l'opérateur des télécommunications a fait un geste commercial, et a doublé pour un mois l'enveloppe de données des clients incommodés. Mais Orange va à son tour se retourner et chercher à obtenir un geste.
Orange veut obtenir des compensations de la part de Nokia
On le sait, d'après le directeur général d'Orange France, Jérôme Héninque, le problème rencontré la semaine dernière par Orange avait pour origine un bug logiciel d'un équipement fourni par Nokia.
Et selon nos confrères de L'Informé, Orange demande maintenant des comptes à l'équipementier. Car l'opérateur a subi un préjudice, notamment lié à son image de marque. Un préjudice estimé tout de même, toujours selon la même source, à plusieurs millions d'euros. Autant dire que le dossier est sérieux.
Orange voudrait obtenir des rabais à l'avenir de la part de Nokia
Mais ici Orange ne souhaite pas obtenir du liquide de la part de son partenaire. Au lieu d'obtenir de l'argent, L'Informé explique qu'Orange pourrait plutôt obtenir un rabais sur les équipements ou les services que Nokia fournit au groupe français. Il restera ensuite à ce dernier la possibilité de se retourner à son tour, cette fois du côté de son assurance, qui pourrait couvrir tout ou une partie de la somme du rabais potentiel fait à Orange.
Si L'Informé nous parle de plusieurs millions d'euros, on ne pourra pas savoir exactement quel arrangement sera trouvé entre les deux parties, l'information devant rester confidentiel - cela à cause des relations contractuelles entre Orange et Nokia.
Source : L'Informé

articles.title: “Podemos tener un ingreso universal por producto”: la promesa de Larry Ellison, director de tecnología de Oracle, sobre la IA
articles.text:
Larry Ellison asegura que la inteligencia artificial terminará por generar un ingreso universal y que, gracias a la automatización de tareas en distintas industrias, “todos” serán más ricos. El presidente ejecutivo y director de tecnología de Oracle expuso esta visión durante un debate en el evento Oracle AI World, realizado en Las Vegas.
En el mismo evento también proyectó avances médicos derivados de la IA, como la posible desaparición de la mayoría de los cánceres en un plazo de entre cinco y 10 años.
Por qué la IA llevaría a un ingreso universal, según Ellison
La idea central del directivo parte de un cambio en la forma de generar valor económico. Según explicó, el uso extendido de robots en diferentes sectores aumentará la productividad humana sin eliminar por completo el trabajo de las personas.
“Decidimos obtener mejores herramientas y vamos a construir mejores sistemas... Las herramientas hacen a las personas mucho mejores, nos hacen mucho más productivos”, sostuvo Ellison.
El directivo mencionó casos como los cirujanos robóticos y los pilotos automáticos en aviones para ilustrar cómo la tecnología puede sustituir ciertas tareas y, al mismo tiempo, reducir costos operativos.
A partir de ese diagnóstico, propuso una transformación en los sistemas tributarios. Dado que los gobiernos gravan “todo lo que producimos”, planteó que es necesario “pasar de gravar el trabajo humano a gravar las declaraciones del impuesto al valor agregado (IVA)”. El ingreso universal por producto, explicó, podría financiarse con el valor agregado que generan los robots.
Un ingreso universal impulsado por IA es una propuesta que sostiene que, a medida que los robots y sistemas automatizados generen valor económico medible a través del IVA, ese excedente podría redistribuirse como un pago básico para toda la población, sin depender exclusivamente del empleo humano como fuente de ingresos.
Ellison reconoció que este escenario no es inmediato. “Eventualmente, los robots harán más y más trabajo que nosotros no queremos hacer, pero están agregando valor”, afirmó, al tiempo que estimó que el proceso tomará más de una década en materializarse.
“Estamos en camino de ser más saludables y más ricos gracias a la IA, y con los sistemas fiscales y los sistemas informáticos adecuados, todo eso es fundamental”, agregó el directivo de Oracle.
Las dudas de la OIT sobre la renta básica financiada por el Estado
La propuesta de un ingreso universal vinculado a la IA no cuenta con respaldo unánime fuera del sector tecnológico. En un informe publicado en mayo, la Organización Internacional del Trabajo (OIT) cuestionó que la renta básica universal financiada por el gobierno sea una respuesta adecuada al impacto de la IA en el mercado laboral.
El organismo de las Naciones Unidas puso en duda dos premisas habituales entre directivos de tecnología: que la IA devastará los mercados laborales de forma catastrófica y que los aumentos de productividad que genere evitarán que las transferencias de ingresos resulten inflacionarias.
“Ambas afirmaciones son empíricamente débiles, y la segunda no es consecuencia de la primera, incluso si la primera fuera cierta”, señaló la OIT en su informe.
El organismo advirtió que, para que una renta básica universal funcione, la IA debería expandir la oferta en los sectores donde las personas gastarán ese ingreso adicional, algo que, según su análisis, la composición actual de las ganancias de productividad no respalda.
“El Estado puede aumentar el número impreso en cada cheque. Que los bienes y servicios que determinan el bienestar real (vivienda, salud, alimentos de calidad, cuidados) estén disponibles en cantidad suficiente a precios estables depende de las condiciones de la oferta, que la IA mejora solo de manera parcial y desigual”, agregó el informe de la OIT.
El impacto de la IA en la cura del cáncer
Más allá del debate sobre el ingreso universal, Ellison destacó el efecto que la IA tendrá en el sector salud, al que calificó como uno de los ámbitos donde el impacto será “extremadamente significativo”.
“El gran regalo de la IA al mundo será... la mayoría de los cánceres desaparecerán en cinco años, y ciertamente en 10 años”, afirmó el directivo, quien remarcó que estas curas no quedarán reservadas para los sectores de mayores ingresos.
Para sustentar esa proyección, Ellison señaló que el aumento en el número de ensayos clínicos y el desarrollo de medicamentos asistido por IA permitirá acelerar la llegada de nuevos tratamientos a los mercados.
“Creemos que el descubrimiento de fármacos va a pasar por una edad de oro. Pero eso es solo la mitad del problema. Consigues los medicamentos. Luego tienes que llevarlos a donde se distribuyan en un volumen tal que los precios bajen”, explicó.
El directivo también se refirió a innovaciones actuales que permiten diagnósticos más tempranos. Mencionó, por ejemplo, una prueba metagenómica habilitada por IA que mejora la detección de la sepsis antes de que la infección se vuelva mortal dentro de un hospital.

articles.title: Americans are losing enthusiasm for their jobs, with AI and remote workers at the center of the decline
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Do you feel a lack of enthusiasm for your job, or struggle with motivation and focus at work? If you do, then you're in the majority. A recent poll of the US workforce found that employee engagement in Q3 fell to its lowest level since 2011. Much of the decline came from remote and hybrid employees across the country, especially those in organizations that have adopted AI.
Gallup began tracking employee engagement in 2000, when 26% of employees in the US said they were engaged. That figure stayed steady between 26% and 30% through 2013, then climbed to a peak of 36% in 2020.
But engagement has fallen since the start of the decade. It stood at 29% last quarter, the lowest level in 15 years. It's also two percentage points lower than the previous quarter.
Gallup writes that each percentage point in engagement represents approximately 1.6 million US employees. The Q3 decline is equivalent to about 3.2 million fewer engaged workers, bringing the total decrease since 2020 to approximately 11 million.
The decline reflected two aspects of employees' work experience: knowing what is expected of them and feeling cared about as a person.
Gallup says businesses should care more about their employees' morale, as disengaged workers can impact a firm's productivity, customer service, quality, safety and profitability.
Interestingly, employees' understanding of what was expected of them declined around twice as much among hybrid and fully remote workers. Jim Harter, chief scientist for Gallup's workplace management and wellbeing practices, suggests this could be due to physical distances contributing to psychological distance between employees and their organizations, especially as companies introduce AI at work.
AI's engagement advantage – the higher employee engagement seen in organizations that integrate AI --narrowed for remote and hybrid employees to just two percentage points in Q3, while remaining around four to five points for on-site workers.
Gallup's bottom line is that AI adoption may be outpacing the communication and managerial support needed to make it effective. It recommends clarifying AI expectations, strengthening manager support – especially for distributed teams – and tracking AI's impact on productivity and engagement.
Today's workplace is turbulent, to say the least. In addition to the AI-driven layoffs, many employees feel so pressured to adopt AI that they're pretending to use it to impress bosses – usually because they aren't confident that they can use it effectively.
Businesses might argue that AI cuts costs and saves them money. But a new Gartner survey found that was true for just 3% of organizations. Despite this, 85% still plan to spend more on the technology.

articles.title: Microsoft's stock rises on solid earnings and revenue beat, with Azure growing 48% - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Microsoft’s stock rises on solid earnings and revenue beat, with Azure growing 48%
Microsoft Corp. delivered better-than-expected earnings and revenue in its fiscal 2027 first quarter, driven by growth of more than 48% in its Azure cloud infrastructure business, sending its stock about 4% higher after-hours.
The company reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $4.89 per share, easily beating Wall Street’s forecast of $4.73 per share, while revenue for the period rose 19% to $92.28 billion, ahead of the $90.69 billion target. All told, the company reported net income of $36.63 billion, up from $27.75 billion in the same period one year earlier.
For the first time in its history, Microsoft disclosed its exact revenue from the Azure business in dollar terms, saying that the unit generated $33.17 billion in the quarter, despite facing delays from some third-party providers. That number came in above expectations, as analysts forecast Azure revenue of just $32.32 billion.
The disclosure was part of a new reporting metric that saw Microsoft’s results broken down into two operating segments: Agents and Infra and Devices and Consumer. For the last 11 years, the company had reported its results under three segments that diced up its Azure, Office and Windows business units.
In the Agents and Infra segment, revenue rose 25% from a year earlier, to $76.8 billion, ahead of the $75.63 billion analyst target. That segment includes Azure along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity tools and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services.
Chief Executive Satya Nadella (pictured) said on a conference call with analysts that the number of people using the Microsoft 365 Copilot artificial intelligence assistant jumped 50% from the previous quarter, but he declined to disclose the number of paid seats it has. However, Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood disclosed that the newly announced Microsoft 365 E7 productivity bundle has already grown to millions of seats.
Revenue in Microsoft’s Devices and Consumer business came to $15.48 billion, down 3% from a year earlier but ahead of the Street’s target of $15.05 billion. That segment includes search and advertising, Xbox devices and Windows operating system licenses that are sold directly to device makers.
The segment was hit by sluggish sales of personal computers, which meant that sales of devices and Windows licenses fell 22% from a year earlier. The reason for that sluggish demand is higher prices, Nadella said, resulting from the rising costs of memory and storage hardware.
Many investors will have been more interested to hear about Microsoft’s ongoing AI infrastructure buildout, which has been sucking up tens of billions of dollars each quarter as the company races to meet demand for AI. During the quarter, Microsoft spent $45.2 billion on capital expenditures and finance leases, up by around 30% from a year before. Analysts had projected this number to be as high as $50.67 billion.
Hood told investors that around 75% of its capex is now tied to short-lived assets such as Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units and Intel Corp.’s central processing units, up from 66% in the prior three quarters. The shift reflects the company’s prioritization of infrastructure that can quickly generate a return on investment, she said.
Hood also reassured investors that the company still has plenty of cash on hand to help fund its capex investments. Though its free cash flow did decline 27% to $18.63 billion during the quarter, that’s still a lot healthier than the $9 billion in negative free cash flow reported by its rival Alphabet Inc. earlier today. Meta Platforms Inc. last week reported that its cash flow also turned negative.
On the other hand, Microsoft will continue to generate positive free cash flow throughout fiscal 2027, Hood insisted, and the company will also still have access to other sources of funding if and when it needs. “We’re fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our rates ratings are, and we haven’t yet tapped that,” Hood said. “And then, of course, there are other options too.”
Forrester Research analyst Tracey Woo said Microsoft’s results show that there’s still strong enterprise demand for AI, but whether the company ultimately benefits depends on where AI value is ultimately going to be captured. She said the company is in a good position because it can connect its AI investments directly to growth in Azure and a broad portfolio of business applications that are already deeply embedded in customer environments. So if the application layer remains the place that creates most value from AI, Microsoft will benefit, she said.
“However, if the value shifts more toward the infrastructure, chips and foundation models, the competitive landscape could evolve as providers with differentiated infrastructure strategies gain influence,” Woo said. “For enterprises, the key takeaway is that AI competition is no longer just about building capacity. It is increasingly about which providers can turn innovation into sustained business outcomes at scale.”
With respect to guidance, Hood said the company is looking for revenue of between $96 billion and $97.1 billion in its fiscal second quarter, which would amount to growth of around 18.8% at the middle of that range. That’s better than expected, since analysts were looking for second-quarter sales of just $95.6 billion.
Hood also predicted Azure’s revenue to grow by between 49% and 50% at constant currency rates, above the Street’s 45.1% forecast. “We still have demand that exceeds supply,” she explained.

articles.title: Apple Unveils MacBook Pro With PROLED XDR Display and Touch for the First Time on Mac
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Apple Unveils MacBook Pro With PROLED XDR Display and Touch for the First Time on Mac
Apple today introduced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, featuring breakthrough tandem OLED technology that delivers game-changing front-of-screen performance. Available in 14- and 16-inch models, MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display offers a visual experience unlike any other, transforming pro workflows with up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for exceptional detail, a 120 Hz variable refresh rate, and a wider color gamut covering both P3 and Adobe RGB for brilliant colors. The new MacBook Pro also introduces intuitive Touch capabilities on the Mac for the first time, opening up a whole new dimension for pros to interact with their content, from manipulating 3D models to playing musical instruments onscreen. 
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. And with up to 24 hours of battery life in thinner and much lighter 3- and 4-pound designs, MacBook Pro is more portable than ever, empowering pros to take their work wherever inspiration strikes. Featuring M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple's most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop, along with up to 128 GB of unified memory and now up to 16 TB of blazing-fast storage, the new MacBook Pro delivers speed and capability for the most demanding workflows. An enhanced six-speaker sound system now provides 50 percent deeper bass and remarkable sound clarity for even more immersive audio. And Thunderbolt 5 and a wide array of connectivity, a 12MP Center Stage camera, studio-quality mics, and the power of macOS 27 with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI complete the MacBook Pro experience. It is available to pre-order starting today, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.
Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer"The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac," "PROLED XDR is the world's best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of. And with the magic of Touch coming to MacBook Pro, combined with the game-changing performance of M5 Pro and M5 Max, we've created a whole new way for pros to interact with their content, taking their workflows to a completely new level. The new MacBook Pro is the result of the deep integration between Apple silicon, hardware, and software, and there's simply nothing else like it."
PROLED XDR: The World's Best Display in a Pro Laptop
The new MacBook Pro debuts the PROLED XDR display, which uses tandem OLED technology and advances it with breakthrough innovations in every layer, advanced algorithms in the display engine, and a state-of-the-art factory calibration process to deliver Extreme Dynamic Range (XDR) and stunning visual fidelity. With exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors, PROLED XDR offers the ultimate front-of-screen performance, enabling a new level of visual acuity and precision for content creators, photographers, colorists, and designers who need a reference-caliber display on the go.
A Tandem OLED Display Unlike Any Other
PROLED XDR is the world's best laptop display, delivering true-to-life color and unparalleled brightness and contrast. The PROLED XDR display offers tandem OLED technology unlike any other, with deep innovations in its layers that keep brightness and grayscale uniform across the entire display, while minimizing internal reflections common in traditional OLED designs. It's all backed by advanced algorithms in the display engine that precisely control each pixel in real time, plus a meticulous manufacturing process and precise calibration of every panel for consistency from display to display.
Breathtaking Brightness and Contrast
PROLED XDR offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, allowing specular highlights to shine with stunning intensity. And through optimizations in the tandem OLED panel and custom compensation techniques, combined with precise control of light across the display, the PROLED XDR display achieves an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, so even the deepest shadows reveal incredible detail, bringing HDR content remarkably close to reality.
An Advanced Display Engine
The display engine precisely controls the color and luminance of every pixel at the sub-millisecond level, compensating for content, pixel use, temperature, and environment all at once to offer exceptional brightness uniformity and grayscale accuracy, even in fast-motion content. It also monitors and adapts each pixel's usage over time to preserve stunning image quality. And ProMotion technology delivers adaptive refresh rates from as low as 10 Hz for better power efficiency and up to 120 Hz for fluid responsiveness for content in motion.
The Ultimate Display for Color-Critical Workflows
PROLED XDR offers pros a super-wide color gamut with P3 and now Adobe RGB—critical for workflows in photography and design—along with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges. This results in more than 80 percent Rec. 2020 coverage for HDR video editing and color grading. Cutting-edge factory calibration ensures luminance, white point, and color gamut are precisely aligned with standard targets. Both color spaces are accessible within a single default preset, streamlining pro workflows and making it seamless to switch between them. With the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, pros have a portable reference display on the go.
Stunning Clarity in Bright Light
With up to 2000 nits peak SDR brightness, combined with a state-of-the-art antireflective coating, the display is easy to read even in bright lighting conditions. For even greater visibility, the nano-texture option—now precisely etched into the cover glass—further reduces reflections and glare to eliminate distractions while maintaining an excellent viewing experience.With breakthrough tandem OLED technology, extreme brightness, and extraordinary contrast, along with a super-wide color gamut, PROLED XDR is truly the world's best laptop display, giving pros an unparalleled visual experience and setting a whole new bar for the industry.
Touch Arrives on Mac
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel—not layered on top of it—reducing latency so users feel like they're touching the content itself.Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Apple apps are optimized for the new MacBook Pro, and many existing apps work with Touch right away, because macOS automatically translates touches into clicks. Updated system gesture APIs also enable developers to create intuitive experiences designed specifically for Touch. And a wide range of third-party apps that pros rely on every day will also take advantage of Touch on the new MacBook Pro, bringing new ways to interact with their favorite tools and workflows. These include everyday productivity and collaboration apps like Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook; powerful creative tools for photo and video editing like Adobe Lightroom and DaVinci Resolve; 3D modeling and animation apps like Blender, Maxon Cinema 4D, Maxon ZBrush, and Shapr3D; along with music apps like Algoriddim djay Pro.
Say Hello to the Dynamic Island on Mac
The Dynamic Island comes to the Mac, serving as the new home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI, where users can quickly search for anything on their MacBook Pro, access real-time updates, or take advantage of Siri AI. Just like on iPhone, the Dynamic Island provides a quick, intuitive way to see and interact with important information. Users can ask a question, pick up a phone call, or control music—all within easy reach. With Live Activities, users can now get timely updates at a glance, and can accept an AirDrop request or pause a song with a tap of their finger.A Thinner and Much Lighter New Design
The new MacBook Pro is thinner and significantly lighter for even better portability. The 14-inch MacBook Pro now weighs half a pound less at 3 pounds, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs just 4 pounds—0.7 pounds lighter than before. Both models feature a slimmer design enabled by OLED's more efficient display stack, with the 16-inch model nearly a millimeter thinner and the 14-inch model half a millimeter thinner.
With slimmer display borders, the 16-inch display grows to 16.3 inches, while the 14-inch display delivers a more portable 14.2-inch design. And a completely redesigned thermal architecture enables the same incredible sustained performance of M5 Pro and M5 Max, even in a lighter design, while redirecting warm air away from the display.M5 Pro and M5 Max: Game-Changing Pro Performance and On-Device AI
The new MacBook Pro features M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple's most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop. Both deliver phenomenal single- and multithreaded CPU performance, along with faster unified memory, giving users blazing speed for the most demanding workflows. M5 Pro offers game-changing performance for scientists, engineers, software developers, and creative pros tackling intensive projects, accelerating everything from compiling code and running AI tasks to sequencing DNA and editing multiple streams of 8K ProRes video. M5 Max is built for users who want to push the limits even further, including 3D VFX artists, AI developers, and film composers. With M5 Max, pros can run LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device and accelerate intense workflows across detailed visual effects, 3D animation projects, film scores, and 8K video post-production.
A powerful Neural Accelerator built into each GPU core lets users speed through AI workloads like running a coding agent with an on-device LLM. And users are able to power through advanced graphics-intensive tasks like rendering a complex scene in Cinema 4D with Redshift. M5 Pro and M5 Max each feature a GPU with enhanced shader cores and a third-generation ray tracing engine, delivering more photorealistic lighting and faster renders for 3D modeling. Dynamic Caching optimizes on-chip memory to significantly increase GPU utilization, driving huge performance boosts for apps like Blender and Unreal Engine, along with AAA games.
The Best Audio System in a Laptop
The industry-leading six-speaker audio system in the new MacBook Pro features an all-new woofer design that provides 50 percent deeper bass and all-new tweeters that shape sound dispersion for remarkable clarity. Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos wraps users in immersive sound for music and movies, and studio-quality mics deliver clean, clear audio for calls, recordings, and voice commands. And for the first time, dedicated audio tuning for closed-lid use delivers exceptional sound quality when MacBook Pro is connected to an external display, so users can enjoy a premium audio experience however they work.
Additional New Features for Pro Workflows
The new MacBook Pro packs features for the most demanding users. The PROLED XDR display offers calibration and industry-standard reference modes in a portable form factor, making MacBook Pro an indispensable tool for filmmaking, design, and even medical imaging. And macOS makes the most of the graphics, memory, and machine learning capabilities of Apple silicon, so apps perform at incredible speed.
- The Apple Pro Display Calibrator gives pros the ability to calibrate their display to specific targets. In addition, pros can take advantage of industry-standard reference modes for cinematic standards, photography, print, design, and more. And with new DICOM medical imaging reference modes, the display can be used today to review medical images with outstanding grayscale accuracy and contrast when used for nondiagnostic reviews, research, and educational purposes.
- Through Apple Color Matching Function 2026, the PROLED XDR display delivers a seamless, consistent visual experience when paired with iPhone 18 Pro or Studio Display XDR.
- With support for genlock, MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display synchronizes a display's refresh rate with a camera's capture to minimize ghosting, tearing, and other visual artifacts when filming, making it highly valuable for virtual productions and on-set work.
- Apple Creator Studio opens up new ways to create on MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, optimizing for Touch alongside the precision of the keyboard and trackpad. With Pixelmator Pro, creators can interact with their designs directly on the canvas, making use of the fully interactive display to draw, paint, and select with even more fluidity. In Logic Pro, musicians can play software instruments with a fully Multi-Touch polyphonic keyboard, along with tappable chord and drum pads onscreen. And in Final Cut Pro, editors can use Touch to precisely mark ranges, drop clips directly into place, pinch to zoom in on a cut, and more.
Advanced Pro Connectivity
The new MacBook Pro includes three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. In addition to the PROLED XDR display, it supports up to three external displays with M5 Pro and up to four with M5 Max. Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 provide fast, reliable wireless connectivity, and Touch ID enables a quick, easy, and secure login experience. With its fast-charge capability, MacBook Pro can charge up to 50 percent in just 30 minutes. In addition, storage is now configurable up to 16 TB.macOS 27 Golden Gate
The new MacBook Pro comes to life with macOS 27. In addition to Touch built for macOS 27, MacBook Pro includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across apps; and an expansive set of improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help pros find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps—all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what's on their display with Visual Intelligence by using a dedicated keyboard shortcut to get help with a specific item. Pros can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user's tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Pros can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. Features users already rely on get even better with improvements to performance and search. Refinements to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and the Environment
The new MacBook Pro was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple's ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminium in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The new MacBook Pro is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple's high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based and designed to be recycled.
Pricing and Availability
- Customers can pre-order the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display starting today, October 28, on apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app in 30 countries and regions, including the U.S. It will begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers, starting Friday, November 6.
