articles.title: AI component hikes force the world's largest PC makers to return manufacturing capacity to China — brands to seek lower production costs and efficiency in established supply chain
articles.text:
AI component hikes force the world's largest PC makers to return manufacturing capacity to China — brands to seek lower production costs and efficiency in established supply chain
Smaller Chinese contractors are raking in orders as traditional suppliers focus on AI servers.
HP, Asus, and Acer have reportedly moved some of their manufacturing capacity back into China as increasing component costs — driven by AI — bite into their margins. According to Nikkei Asia, increasing bill-of-materials costs have made China’s experienced workforce, relatively lower prices, and established supply chain ecosystem a more attractive option. However, they are not going back to traditional suppliers like Foxconn, who have focused their production capacity on AI data centers. Instead, they’re signing contracts with smaller Chinese contract manufacturers, like Luxshare, Huaqin Technology, and Longcheer Technology, that are trying to establish themselves in PC manufacturing.
Many PC brands slowly moved out of China in 2024 and 2025 as the U.S.’s sanctions and tariffs on China have increased prices and forced them to find friendlier nations. While these nations do not have established supply chains and expertise like China, it at least spreads the risk as manufacturers avoid getting caught up in geopolitical tensions.
However, it seems that rising component prices have forced them to move back some of their capacity into China. The biggest culprit is the AI-induced memory and storage chip shortage, which has caused memory prices to climb an unprecedented 500% in 12 months. More than that, other parts like PCBs and fiberglass cloth used in motherboard manufacturing are seeing increasing prices, which Acer chairperson and CEO Jason Chen bemoaned as suppliers hyping shortage fears to protect margins.
While tech companies aren’t abandoning their “China+1” diversification strategy, the mature industry in China is helping offset increased component costs. Aside from that, the Chinese contract manufacturers often have better access to memory chips from domestic manufacturers like CXMT. "These Chinese contract manufacturers have been telling potential clients and computer makers that working with them could be a good option for securing better access to Chinese-made memory chips," a supply chain manager in the computer ecosystem told Nikkei Asia. "They are marketing themselves as a good alternative to even help sort out the supply chain."
Moving back some manufacturing capacity into China is easing some of PC manufacturers’ cost concerns, but it’s also negatively impacting the newly established supply chains in Southeast Asia. "We built two new production lines in Thailand for the PC clients, and now they are moving substantial orders back to China,” one manager at a PC component supplier told the publication. “Those two lines have not yet turned profitable, and I don't know when they will add the orders back."
Unfortunately, building an entire supply chain for PC manufacturing is slow and expensive. The U.S. has been trying to accomplish this for years, and, so far, only Anduril has attempted to build laptops with 90% of its component costs coming from the U.S. and other allied countries. Even then, it expects its devices to be around 20% more expensive than the competition, which it could afford by offering them mostly to critical industries that demand supply chain security, like the government and the military. But if you’re a PC manufacturer vying for customers in the consumer market, you’re likely incentivized to find the lowest possible costs to be able to compete in pricing.

articles.title: One step closer to the Terminator? Experts reveal robot with 'real muscles' strong enough to jump, swim and grasp
articles.text:
One step closer to the Terminator? Experts reveal robot with 'real muscles' strong enough to jump, swim and grasp
“Tissue… grown for cyborgs”
- Laboratory-grown muscle tissue has been developed to improve robot dexterity and motion
- Researchers working at ETH Zurich have demonstrated tissue-based muscle actuators that flex
- The actuators enable small robots to jump and swim, as well as walk and grasp
Flesh-covered robots that can walk, jump, swim and move among us may be closer than we think. Researchers working out of ETH Zurich have been busy developing muscle actuators from centimeter-scale living tissue. These muscle actuators are the latest in a design program, and motion has been improved over 10 times compared with previous iterations.
In designing the biohybrid robots, the researchers have found that it isn’t all about the volume of muscle tissue. How the muscle and the bone (or in this case, an “artificial scaffold”) interact is also important.
Grown from mouse muscle cells, the results are being viewed as a new way of building robots.
Biohybrid muscle
The project is run from the ETH Zurich Soft Robotics Lab and is overseen by Professor Robert Katzschmann, who states that “We’re just beginning to build robots in a more natural way.” The research focuses on biohybrids, which basically refers to integrating biological materials like muscle tissue with artificial, man-made materials like electronics or mechanical scaffold.
Design of the robots has evolved through the research to the current state, where the muscle tissue is secured to the scaffold using grooves that the tissue can attach to. Meanwhile, the robots are currently limited to motion within a nutrient solution intended to feed the muscles and keep them “alive.”
An interesting result from the research is that not all muscle actuators behave in the same way. This “natural variability” that comes from using living tissue contrasts with what is achievable with manufactured components.
Flesh for cyborgs
Development of flesh muscles for robots has taken place over several years, with designs built on computer. Over what has been called an “iterative process” by co-lead author of the published study Aiste Balciunaite, the idea of “a fixed form for our muscle geometry” was eschewed in favor of designing “the whole thing from scratch on the computer.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“With previous systems, you sometimes had to look under a microscope to see the flexing,” Balciunaite adds, highlighting how far the project has come.
The video above demonstrates the range of movement that can be performed by the muscle actuators, with the activity now visible to the naked eye. Measuring over 1cm, the bioactuators can move and grasp, and are shown here swimming. Other biohybrid robots have been programmed to walk, managing to cover 6.2 millimeters a second.
Will these bio-attached structures develop into an army of time traveling, human-destroying cyborgs? Probably not, and as they have applications for exploration and medicine, we shouldn't be too concerned.

articles.title: Blaupause: So haben wir in Alltagssprache einen KI-Agenten erstellt
articles.text:
Blaupause: So haben wir in Alltagssprache einen KI-Agenten erstellt
Im Werbegeschäft mündet jeder Verkauf in eine Auftragsbestätigung. Sie kommt als PDF und listet alle Leistungen, die ein Kunde gebucht hat, etwa ein Podcast-Sponsoring oder zwei Sponsored Posts. Bevor die Umsetzung beginnt, braucht jede dieser Leistungen eine eigene Aufgabe im Projekttool, mit Unteraufgaben und Terminen. Bei uns erledigte das bis Mitte August 2026 die Kampagnenabwicklung von Hand, Auftrag für Auftrag in Asana. Bei großen Buchungen dauerte das bis zu 40 Minuten. Der t3n PRO Use Case zeigt als Blaupause, wie das Team diese Arbeit einem KI-Agenten beigebracht hat.
KI-Agenten erstellen ohne Entwicklerteam
Zum Einstieg fragte die Projektverantwortliche Claude, was er braucht, um die Auftragsanlage in Asana zu automatisieren. Ein interner Skill sorgte dafür, dass Claude ausführlich zurückfragte. Als Material bekam er die knappe Prozessdokumentation und zehn echte Auftragsbestätigungen. Er spielte Aufträge durch, die das Team schon angelegt hatte, und glich sein Ergebnis mit dem echten Eintrag ab. Aus den Abweichungen entstand an einem Nachmittag seine erste Anleitung.
Diese erste Fassung reichte für den Alltag nicht. Also ging die Arbeit im Slack-Thread weiter, das Team benannte Fehler in normalen Sätzen, und Claude trug jede Korrektur in seine Anleitung ein. Beim ersten Test fand er umgekehrt zwei Fehler in einem Eintrag, den das Team von Hand angelegt hatte. Nach 24 Stunden stand die Anleitung bei Version 12. Die Werkzeuge waren alle vorhanden: Claude ist mit den internen Tools des Unternehmens verbunden, und das Asana-Board mit festen Feldern und Vorlagen gab es längst.
Mitte August ging der Agent mit echten Aufträgen live, eine Testkopie des Boards hat das Team nie angelegt. Seither reicht es, Claude im Slack-Thread zur Auftragsbestätigung zu markieren. Was er anlegt, prüft das Team: bei einfachen Aufträgen in unter fünf Minuten, bei großen in höchstens zehn. In den ersten gut zwei Monaten ist kein Fehler bis ins Tagesgeschäft durchgerutscht. Am deutlichsten merkt das Team den Unterschied, wenn jemand im Urlaub ist.
Was du in dieser Blaupause bekommst
In diesem t3n PRO Use Case zeigen wir, wie sich die Kampagnenabwicklung von t3n einen KI-Agenten für die Auftragsanlage gebaut hat:
- Einblick in die Regeln, die Claude aus zehn echten Aufträgen ableitete
- Die Kanalanweisung, mit der Claude im Slack-Kanal arbeitet
- Ein Auszug aus dem Slack-Thread zum ersten echten Auftrag

articles.title: 7 Things emotionally intelligent people do differently
articles.text:
7 Things emotionally intelligent people do differently
Discover seven things emotionally intelligent people do differently to manage emotions, communicate better, and build healthier relationships.
Emotional intelligence is not about staying calm all the time or knowing exactly what to say in every situation. It is about understanding your emotions, recognising how others feel, and choosing how to respond rather than reacting impulsively.
In everyday life, emotional intelligence can influence how we handle disagreements, build relationships, respond to criticism, and navigate difficult situations. People who develop this skill are often better equipped to communicate clearly, understand different perspectives, and manage their emotions constructively.
The good news is that emotional intelligence is not simply something you are born with. Many of its essential skills can be practised and strengthened over time.
7 Things emotionally intelligent people do differently
1. They pause before reacting
When someone criticises them, disagrees with them, or says something hurtful, emotionally intelligent people try not to respond immediately out of anger.
They understand that an emotional reaction can sometimes make a difficult situation worse. Instead of sending an impulsive message or saying something they might regret, they give themselves time to process what happened.
For example, if a colleague points out a mistake, they may initially feel embarrassed or defensive. Rather than immediately arguing, they consider whether the feedback is useful and how they can respond constructively.
Pausing does not mean ignoring your emotions or pretending that nothing bothers you. It means allowing yourself to feel an emotion without letting it make every decision for you.
The lesson: You cannot always control what you feel, but you can practise choosing how you respond.
2. They try to understand before judging
Emotionally intelligent people recognise that their perspective is not the only possible explanation for a situation.
When someone behaves unexpectedly, they try to understand the circumstances before making assumptions about their intentions.
For instance, if a friend takes hours to reply to a message, it is easy to assume that they are losing interest or deliberately ignoring you. However, they might be dealing with work, family responsibilities, or something they have not shared.
Instead of immediately jumping to conclusions, emotionally intelligent people leave room for other explanations and communicate when clarification is needed.
This does not mean excusing repeated disrespect or ignoring unhealthy behaviour. It means distinguishing between what you know and what you are assuming.
The lesson: Understanding another person's perspective can prevent unnecessary misunderstandings and help you respond more fairly.
3. They can admit when they are wrong
Admitting a mistake is not always easy. It can challenge your pride, make you feel uncomfortable, or force you to reconsider something you strongly believed.
However, emotionally intelligent people understand that being wrong does not make them less valuable.
When they hurt someone, misunderstand a situation, or make a poor decision, they try to acknowledge their role instead of shifting all the blame onto others.
A genuine apology involves more than saying, "I'm sorry you felt that way." It means recognising the impact of your actions, taking responsibility where appropriate, and making an effort to behave differently.
They also understand that an apology does not automatically entitle them to forgiveness. Rebuilding trust often requires consistent actions over time.
The lesson: Taking responsibility for your mistakes is a sign of self-awareness, not weakness.
4. They set boundaries without feeling obligated to explain everything
Emotionally intelligent people understand that being considerate does not mean making themselves available to everyone at all times.
They recognise their limits and communicate them clearly. If they are exhausted, overwhelmed, or unable to take on another responsibility, they can say no without turning the decision into a lengthy justification.
For example, they might tell a friend, "I care about you, but I don't have the energy for a conversation tonight. Can we talk tomorrow?"
This approach respects both their own needs and the other person's feelings.
Healthy boundaries also apply to work, family expectations, personal time, and emotional availability. They help people maintain relationships without constantly ignoring their own well-being.
Setting boundaries does not mean becoming selfish or indifferent. It means understanding that care and availability are not the same thing.
The lesson: You can care about other people without taking responsibility for every expectation they have of you.
5. They listen to understand, not just to reply
In many conversations, people spend more time preparing their responses than listening to what the other person is saying.
Emotionally intelligent people try to avoid this habit. They pay attention to the speaker's words, ask questions when something is unclear, and consider the feelings behind the message.
For example, when a friend talks about a difficult day, they do not immediately offer advice or compare the experience with their own. They might first ask, "Do you want me to help you figure it out, or do you just need someone to listen?"
This simple question can make conversations more supportive because it acknowledges that different people need different kinds of help.
Active listening also involves noticing when your assumptions are influencing your interpretation of what someone says.
The lesson: Sometimes, the most helpful response is not advice but the willingness to listen without rushing to fix everything.
6. They do not depend on everyone's approval
Emotionally intelligent people care about their relationships, but they do not treat universal approval as a requirement for feeling secure.
They understand that people have different expectations, values, and opinions. As a result, not everyone will agree with their choices, and that disagreement does not automatically mean they have done something wrong.
For instance, choosing a different career path, declining an invitation, or expressing an unpopular opinion may disappoint someone. Emotionally intelligent people can consider that person's perspective without automatically abandoning their own judgement.
They remain open to constructive criticism while recognising that criticism is not always accurate or fair.
This balance helps them make decisions based on their values rather than constantly changing themselves to avoid disappointing others.
The lesson: You can value other people's opinions without allowing those opinions to define your self-worth.
7. They recognise that other people's emotions are not always their responsibility
Emotionally intelligent people can show empathy without assuming they must fix every uncomfortable feeling another person experiences.
They understand the difference between supporting someone and taking complete responsibility for that person's emotional state.
For example, if they respectfully decline a request and the other person becomes disappointed, they can acknowledge that disappointment without automatically reversing their decision.
Similarly, if a friend is upset, they can offer support while recognising that they cannot control how the friend processes the situation.
This does not mean ignoring the consequences of their own actions. If they have caused harm, taking responsibility matters. The distinction is between being accountable for your behaviour and trying to manage every emotion someone else feels.
Learning this difference can make relationships healthier and reduce the pressure to keep everyone happy.
The lesson: Empathy means caring about how others feel, not believing you must control how they feel.
Final thoughts
Emotional intelligence is often reflected in small, everyday decisions: pausing before responding, listening without interrupting, admitting mistakes, and setting boundaries respectfully.
These behaviours do not mean emotionally intelligent people never feel jealous, angry, insecure, or overwhelmed. They experience difficult emotions like everyone else. The difference is that they can gradually learn to recognise those emotions and respond to them more thoughtfully.
You do not have to master all seven habits at once. Start by noticing one situation in which you tend to react impulsively, seek approval, or struggle to express your needs.
With practice, greater self-awareness and more thoughtful communication can help you build healthier relationships with both yourself and the people around you.

articles.title: 1000 boissons possibles : ce que propose la nouvelle SodaStream
articles.text:
SodaStream Ultimate Multi-Drink : le soda se sert au verre et se règle à la carte
Un verre sur mesure
SodaStream lance en France l'Ultimate Multi-Drink, une machine qui prépare et sert les boissons directement dans un verre ou une carafe. Quantité, bulles et intensité de la saveur peuvent être ajustées, pour un prix de 169,99 €.
Le soda maison prend dorénavant des airs de boisson à la demande. La nouvelle machine SodaStream Ultimate Multi-Drink propose de préparer une boisson puis de la distribuer dans le contenant de son choix, qu'il s'agisse d'un simple verre ou d'une carafe.
La machine permet non seulement de régler le volume servi mais aussi le niveau de gazéification et l'intensité de la saveur. On peut donc obtenir une boisson plus ou moins pétillante et doser le goût selon ses préférences. Selon SodaStream l'appareil serait capable de faire une préparation en moins de trente secondes.
L'appareil est compatible avec les concentrés déjà proposés par la marque, notamment Pepsi et 7UP, ainsi qu'avec la gamme SodaStream Fruits. Le fabricant parle de plus de 1000 possibilités de boissons en tenant compte des combinaisons de réglages et de saveurs disponibles.
L'addition pétille aussi
SodaStream met également en avant un coût moyen des boissons inférieur de 25 % à celui des sodas prêts à boire. Attention toutefois, pour établir le coût réel il faut aussi tenir compte de l'achat de la machine et des consommables. Un flacon de concentré permettrait de préparer jusqu'à 9 l de soda.
L'Ultimate Multi-Drink est proposée en France depuis le 14 octobre 2026, en noir, au prix public conseillé de 169,99 €. Elle est aussi proposée sur le site de SodaStream, en grandes surfaces et chez les revendeurs spécialisés.

articles.title: Subscription Sprawl: Auditing the Software Your Business Pays for but Never Opens - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Understanding Subscription Sprawl in Modern Businesses
In today’s fast-paced digital landscape, businesses increasingly rely on a wide array of software subscriptions to streamline operations, enhance productivity, and stay competitive. However, a growing challenge that many organisations face is subscription sprawl-the phenomenon where companies accumulate numerous software subscriptions that go underutilised or not used at all. This hidden inefficiency can significantly drain budgets and complicate IT management.
Subscription sprawl occurs when businesses continuously subscribe to multiple services without thoroughly assessing their actual usage or necessity. Over time, these unused or rarely accessed subscriptions accumulate, leading to wasted expenditures and operational clutter. According to a report by Flexera, 30% of enterprise software spend is wasted due to unused or underused subscriptions. This figure highlights the scale of the problem, emphasizing the urgent need for organisations to take action.
Recognising and addressing subscription sprawl is crucial for companies seeking to optimise their software investments. Engaging with an IT advisory team at Hardin can provide valuable insights into your current software landscape, helping identify redundant or unnecessary subscriptions and recommending strategic actions to improve cost efficiency. This partnership often brings expertise and tools that internal teams may lack, enabling a thorough and objective audit.
Why Subscription Sprawl Happens and Its Impact
Several factors contribute to subscription sprawl. One common cause is the lack of visibility into software usage across departments. As teams independently adopt tools to meet their specific needs, the organisation may lose track of overlapping or redundant subscriptions. This decentralised purchasing approach, often referred to as “shadow IT,” can lead to multiple subscriptions for similar functions, increasing costs unnecessarily.
Additionally, the ease of subscribing to cloud-based services without central approval can exacerbate the problem. The “freemium” models and low upfront costs of many SaaS products encourage teams to quickly onboard new tools, but without proper oversight, these subscriptions may linger unused after initial trials or projects conclude.
The financial implications of subscription sprawl are substantial. Gartner estimates that by 2024, organisations will waste approximately 40% of their SaaS spending due to inefficient management and lack of utilisation. This not only affects the bottom line but also impacts IT teams’ ability to manage software effectively and ensure security compliance, as unmanaged subscriptions may not receive necessary updates or support.
Furthermore, subscription sprawl complicates contract management and renewal processes. Without a clear understanding of which subscriptions are essential, companies may inadvertently renew unused licenses or miss opportunities to negotiate better terms. The administrative overhead also increases as finance and procurement teams struggle to maintain accurate records, leading to inefficiencies and potential audit risks.
Engaging with experts like HI-TEX in the IT industry can help businesses establish robust processes for managing subscriptions and ensuring that every software investment aligns with organisational goals. Such partnerships can streamline procurement, enhance visibility, and implement governance frameworks that prevent future sprawl.
Conducting a Comprehensive Software Audit
A software audit is the first step towards mitigating subscription sprawl. This process involves systematically reviewing all active subscriptions, assessing their usage, costs, and alignment with business objectives. Here’s how businesses can approach it:
- Inventory All Subscriptions
Create a comprehensive list of all software subscriptions, including those purchased departmentally or by individuals. This inventory should capture contract details, renewal dates, user counts, and costs. Gathering this data can be challenging without centralised records, but it is essential for a full picture.
- Assess Usage Data
Gather usage metrics to identify which subscriptions are actively used and which are dormant. Many SaaS providers offer dashboards or reports indicating user activity levels. Combining this data with employee feedback can help validate actual usage versus theoretical access.
- Evaluate Business Value
Determine the importance of each subscription to business operations. Some tools may be critical despite low usage, such as specialised software for niche functions, while others may be redundant or replaceable. Understanding the strategic value of each subscription ensures that decisions support broader organisational goals.
- Identify Overlaps and Redundancies
Look for subscriptions offering similar functionalities and consider consolidating them to reduce costs and simplify management. For example, multiple teams might subscribe to different project management tools that could be unified under a single platform.
- Engage Stakeholders
Consult with department heads and end-users to understand their needs and preferences, ensuring decisions are well-informed and accepted. This collaborative approach helps in identifying indispensable tools and building consensus for changes.
- Plan for Optimization
Based on audit findings, decide which subscriptions to retain, renegotiate, consolidate, or cancel. This plan should include timelines for contract renewals, potential cost savings, and any necessary transition support.
Statistics indicate that organisations who regularly audit their software subscriptions reduce unnecessary spend by up to 25%. This significant saving can be redirected towards strategic initiatives or innovation projects.
Implementing Best Practices to Control Subscription Sprawl
After completing an audit, businesses should adopt best practices to prevent subscription sprawl from recurring. These practices create sustainable control mechanisms and foster a culture of accountability around software procurement.
– Centralised Subscription Management
Implement a central system or designate a team responsible for approving and tracking all software subscriptions. This visibility reduces duplication and uncontrolled spending. A centralized repository or software asset management (SAM) tool can serve as a single source of truth for all software licenses and contracts.
– Regular Usage Reviews
Schedule periodic reviews of software usage and costs to detect and address underutilised subscriptions promptly. Quarterly or biannual assessments help maintain a lean portfolio and adapt to changing business needs.
– Clear Policies and Governance
Develop organisational policies outlining procedures for software procurement, approval, and renewal. Ensure all employees are aware of these guidelines to reduce rogue subscriptions and encourage responsible software use.
– Leverage Technology Solutions
Use subscription management platforms or IT asset management tools that can automate tracking and provide actionable insights. These technologies can alert managers to upcoming renewals, unused licenses, or overlapping tools, enabling proactive decision-making.
– Negotiate Flexible Contracts
Work with vendors to secure flexible subscription terms, such as adjustable user licenses or cancellation options, accommodating changing business needs. Flexibility reduces the risk of long-term commitments to underused software.
Partnering with dedicated IT support providers can help businesses implement these practices effectively, combining technical expertise with strategic oversight. Such partners often bring industry best practices and tools to streamline subscription governance.
The Strategic Value of Subscription Audits
Beyond cost savings, auditing software subscriptions fosters better strategic alignment between IT and business goals. By understanding the actual usage and impact of software tools, organisations can make informed decisions about technology investments that truly support productivity and innovation.
An optimised software portfolio also enhances security and compliance. Unused or forgotten subscriptions may not receive timely updates or monitoring, increasing vulnerability to cyber threats. Regular audits ensure that all software remains under active management and meets security standards, reducing risks associated with data breaches or non-compliance penalties.
Moreover, subscription sprawl complicates IT operations, and reducing it simplifies management, allowing teams to focus on value-added activities rather than administrative tasks related to managing a fragmented software environment. Streamlined software management improves agility, enabling faster adoption of new technologies aligned with business priorities.
Additionally, subscription audits can reveal opportunities for digital transformation. By identifying redundant tools and consolidating services, organisations can invest in more integrated platforms that enhance collaboration and data insights, driving competitive advantage.
Conclusion
Subscription sprawl presents a significant challenge for businesses striving to manage their technology investments efficiently. By conducting thorough software audits, implementing centralised management, and engaging expert partners like the , organisations can uncover hidden inefficiencies, reduce wasted expenditure, and align their software portfolio with strategic priorities.
With SaaS spending expected to grow exponentially-IDC predicts global SaaS spend will reach $208 billion by 2024-proactive subscription management is not just a cost-saving measure but a critical component of modern IT governance. Embracing these practices empowers businesses to maximise the value of their software investments and maintain agility in an ever-evolving digital landscape.
Ultimately, addressing subscription sprawl transforms software management from a reactive, fragmented process into a strategic asset that supports innovation, security, and sustainable growth.

articles.title: ServiceNow shares drop 18% after mixed earnings results - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
ServiceNow shares drop 18% after mixed earnings results
Shares of ServiceNow Inc. dropped 18% in after-hours trading today after it posted quarterly results that topped its internal guidance, but mostly fell short of analyst expectations.
ServiceNow is best known for its ITSM, or information technology service management, platform. Enterprise IT teams use it to deliver technical support to employees and coordinate infrastructure upgrades. ServiceNow also offers a wide range of other products that ease tasks such as managing customer data and creating artificial intelligence agents.
The company generated $1.04 billion in adjusted operating income during the third quarter, which translated to adjusted earnings of $1 per share. Analysts had expected $1.02 per share. The company’s top line fared better, growing 20.5% on a year-over-year basis, to $4.11 billion. That put ServiceNow $20 million above the consensus estimate.
The company’s sales growth was partly driven by demand from large customers. ServiceNow inked 19 deals with an annual contract value, or ACV, of over $5 million, which represents a 135% increase from a year earlier. Chief Executive Officer Bill McDermott told investors that net new ACV attributed to AI products rose 65% on a year-over-year basis.
One contributor to the company’s AI momentum is its EmployeeWorks tool. It’s an employee portal that displays to-do items, company updates and related information. A chatbot called Otto enables users to search for data across multiple applications at once, as well as automate certain repetitive tasks. ServiceNow says that EmployeeWorks reached $100 million in ACV within three quarters of its launch.
Super Intelligence Control Tower is another core pillar of the software maker’s AI growth strategy. It’s a platform that can automatically map out all the AI models and agents in a company’s technology environment. It protects those assets against risks such as prompt injections. Additionally, the software can track the quality of AI models’ prompt responses and measure the productivity gains they deliver.
McDermott revealed that a core Super Intelligence Control Tower usage metric is growing 500% month-over-month. He added that ServiceNow expects its AI business to achieve “true acceleration” next year.
ServiceNow raised its full-year AI ACV projection to $1.7 billion, a 70% increase from January. However, the company’s fourth-quarter revenue forecast still fell short of expectations. ServiceNow expects sales of $4.25 billion to $4.26 billion, while analysts projected $4.36 billion.
The company announced a series of AI partnerships in conjunction with its earnings report. ServiceNow is teaming up with OpenAI Group PBC to launch a plugin that will enable customers to access its platform through ChatGPT. Separately, the company is forming a partner group designed to prompt the Super Intelligence Control Tower. The consortium, which includes major industry players such as Nvidia Corp., will develop joint offerings and collaborate on go-to-market initiatives.

articles.title: Apple anuncia MacBook Pro com tela OLED sensível a toques; veja preços • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple anuncia MacBook Pro com tela OLED sensível a toques; veja preços
MacBooks Pro de 14 e 16 polegadas agora podem ser equipados com a nova tela ProLED XDR, com painel "touch".
Semana movimentada na Apple. Depois de anunciar o iPad Mini com tela OLED, além do MacBook Pro e do iMac com chip M6, a companhia de Cupertino revelou, nesta quarta-feira (28/10), versões do MacBook Pro de 14 e 16 polegadas que contam com tela OLED sensível a toques, confirmando os rumores. No Brasil, os preços começam em R$ 34.999.
É a primeira vez que um modelo da família Mac recebe uma tela “touch” (isso se desconsiderarmos os notebooks com Touch Bar, é claro). Embora tecnologias do tipo existam há anos, a Apple vinha resistindo à proposta.
A mudança de ideia pode ser uma resposta à demanda de usuários que entendem que esse tipo de recurso é útil para tarefas que envolvam design, edição de fotos ou ilustrações, por exemplo. Nesse sentido, a Apple explica que os toques na tela podem ser usados para ampliar imagens com gesto de pinça, arrastar elementos, alternar conteúdo, entre várias outras ações.
As dobradiças foram reforçadas para evitar que os toques empurrem a tela de modo a atrapalhar o usuário.
Para ser exato, a Apple chama a nova tela de ProLED XDR. Trata-se de um painel OLED Tandem, que usa duas camadas emissoras de luz. O componente pode ainda alcançar 2.000 nits de brilho (pico) e taxa de contraste de 10.000.000:1. A taxa de atualização pode chegar a 120 Hz. Aqui, a tecnologia aparece em modelos com 14 e 16 polegadas de tamanho, como já informado.
Por dentro, o MacBook Pro pode ser equipado com o chip M5 Pro ou o M5 Max. Na linha, o chip M6 está disponível somente para o MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas anunciado ontem, pelo menos por enquanto.
O equipamento pode contar também com até 128 GB de memória RAM unificada, bem como com até 16 TB de armazenamento interno.
A Apple destaca ainda que reformulou o design dos novos MacBooks Pro para torná-los mais leves e, no quesito bateria, afirma que o componente pode alcançar 24 horas de autonomia com uma recarga completa.
Outros atributos de destaque incluem:
No Brasil, os novos MacBooks Pro com tela sensível a toques têm os seguintes preços iniciais, sem considerar descontos ou promoções:
Ambas as versões podem ser complementadas com um vidro “nano-texture”, que reduz os reflexos para melhorar a percepção de qualidade de imagem, mas gera custo adicional. Considere também que há duas opções de cores: prateado e preto espacial.
Apesar de os novos MacBooks Pro já aparecerem no site brasileiro da Apple, a companhia ainda não informou a previsão de lançamento por aqui. Nos Estados Unidos, a pré-venda já começou e o lançamento oficial está previsto para 6 de novembro.
Vale relembrar que, no início da semana, a Apple lançou o iPad Mini com tela OLED e chip A20 Pro. Ontem, a companhia anunciou um MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas e um iMac de 24 polegadas com chip M6.

articles.title: 500 km d’autonomie en 5 minutes : Chery dévoile sa recharge surpuissante pour terrasser BYD
articles.text:
En mars dernier, BYD avait bluffé tout le monde avec le Flash Charging : un 10 à 70 % en 5 minutes et un 10 à 97 % en 9 minutes grâce à une puissance de charge allant jusqu’à 1 500 kW en courant continu DC, c’était tout bonnement révolutionnaire. Depuis, les concurrents ne sont pas restés les bras croisés en déployant peu à peu leurs propres solutions. Ainsi, après la batterie Golden Brick de Geely, c’est au tour de Chery d’apporter une réponse au problème.
Son dispositif nommé « Volt-Dragon » promet une puissance de charge de 1 440 kW en courant continu DC. Si c’est légèrement inférieur à ce que propose BYD, Chery affirme tout de même recouvrir 500 km d’autonomie en seulement 5 minutes. Solide, d’autant plus que la recharge devrait se montrer plus constante que chez BYD, avec un 10 à 97 % de batterie annoncé en 6 minutes et 50 secondes.
CheryMind : quand l’intelligence artificielle pilote la recharge
C’est 2 minutes de moins grâce à l’implémentation de l’intelligence artificielle « CheryMind » dans le processus de recharge. Lors d’une conférence interne sur l’innovation mondiale, le constructeur considère cette innovation comme un « cerveau qui comprend le monde physique ». Celui-ci sera naturellement au cœur des Robotaxis, des systèmes de conduite autonome et de la recharge Volt-Dragon, bien évidemment.
Si la marque n’a pas véritablement précisé le fonctionnement de CheryMind appliquée au Volt-Dragon, elle explique toutefois que son écosystème de recharge Xingrui PowerMind est capable de prédire le comportement thermique pendant la charge en anticipant les variations de température des cellules 30 secondes à l’avance. Le but est d’ajuster continuellement la puissance de recharge maximale en évitant d’abimer les batteries.
Bras robotisés et stations du futur : entre promesses et réalité
Le Volt-Dragon permet donc à Chery de tenir la dragée haute face aux leaders. Seule la batterie Shenxing de troisième génération de CATL fait encore mieux, avec un 10 à 98 % de recharge annoncé en 6 minutes et 27 secondes. On sait alors ce que dira BYD face à ce panier d’annonces : il n’y a encore rien de concret contrairement aux Flash Chargers, déjà existants en Chine et très bientôt en France.
C’est tout à fait vrai. Chery lance des promesses sans encore préciser les véhicules qui seront concernés par la chose. Dans le même genre, la recharge devrait aussi être autonome grâce à des bras robotisés qui viendront automatiquement connecter le câble au véhicule. Chery confirme seulement l’ouverture de 100 stations Volt-Dragon dans 10 villes chinoises d’ici la fin de l’année. Très timide par rapport aux 20 000 Flash Chargers visés par BYD à la même échéance.

articles.title: La Garmin Forerunner 265 fera le bonheur des sportifs surtout grâce à cette réduction de plus de 60€
articles.text:
La Garmin Forerunner 265 est une montre connectée qui s'adresse avant tout aux sportifs comme en témoigne le bouton "Run". Pour séduire tous les sportifs, plusieurs modes d'entraînement sont présents. L'ensemble est proposé pour un peu plus de 250 euros.
La gamme des montres connectées de Garmin est portée par la Forerunner 965. Cependant, cette montre est onéreuse et est vendue autour de 500 euros, ce qui n'est pas adapté à tous les budgets. La marque a trouvé la parade en sortant des produits plus accessibles comme la Garmin Forerunner 265. Plus accessible que la 965, elle passe en plus sous les 300 euros chez AliExpress.
Sur AliExpress, la Garmin Forerunner 265 passe de 349 euros à 283,41 euros
Pourquoi choisir la Garmin Forerunner 265 ?
- Pour sa discrétion : Malgré ce format de 46 mm, la Garmin Forerunner 265 reste discrète au poignet grâce à son coloris entièrement noir. Même les cinq boutons arrivent à se faire discrets.
- L'écran OLED : Par rapport à la Forerunner 255, la Garmin Forerunner 265 opte pour une dalle OLED lumineuse, ce qui est idéal pour les entraînements en plein soleil.
- Parfaite pour le sport : La Garmin Forerunner 265 emporte une multitude de modes d'entraînement, un GPS et un suivi de la fréquence cardiaque précis. Que demander de plus ?
Une montre qui fait le choix de la sobriété
La Garmin Forerunner 265 dans cette version de 46 mm concernée par la promotion d'AliExpress fait le choix de la discrétion. La montre opte pour un coloris entièrement noir. Cependant, si vous voulez ajouter un peu de couleur à cette montre, le bracelet se remplace facilement.
Malgré ce coloris discret, on se rend rapidement compte que Garmin Forerunner 265 est dédiée à la pratique sportive. Preuve en est, elle possède une multitude de boutons, dont une touche "Run" qui dénote avec le reste du design puisqu'elle est rectangulaire et pas arrondie comme les autres.
Si le design est discret, l'écran de cette Garmin Forerunner 265 l'est beaucoup moins. La marque a opté pour une dalle OLED de 1,3 pouce. Un mode Always-On est aussi présent, mais il peut présenter quelques limites lors de vos activités sportives puisqu'un coup de poignet sera nécessaire pour consulter les différentes données.
Seulement pour le sport
Qui dit Garmin dit montre pour le sport et la Forerunner 265 brille sur ce domaine. La montre emporte une multitude de modes d'entraînement. Pour séduire les coureurs notamment, il faut que le GPS soit au rendez-vous. Garmin a ressorti la puce GNSS multibande déjà présente sur la Forerunner 255. Sans surprise, votre parcours est retranscrit avec précision. Autre ajout intéressant pour les sportifs, la possibilité de stocker 8 Go de musique.
Petit bémol à noter : une bibliothèque d'applications limitée. Si tous les indispensables pour le sport sont présents, dès que l'on s'éloigne de la pratique sportive, on a rapidement fait le tour de ce qui est disponible.
Autre point noir : l'autonomie. Étonnamment, la Garmin Forerunner 265 est moins endurante que la 255. En réalité, la différence est minime puisque la 265 peut tenir jusqu'à 13 jours contre 14 jours pour la Forerunner 255.
✅ Les points forts
- Un passage réussi à l'OLED
- La multitude de modes d'entraînement
- La possibilité de stocker 8 Go de musique
❌ Les limites
- Une autonomie en baisse
- Une promotion qui ne s'applique sur le coloris Black Standard de 46 mm
Disponible pour 349 euros, la Garmin Forerunner 265 chute à 283,41 euros sur le site d'AliExpress
La Garmin Forerunner 265 avait une mission simple : être une montre connectée dédiée au sport et plus abordable que les cadors de la marque. Mission accomplie ici puisque l'accessoire de Garmin propose un GPS précis, tout comme le suivi de la fréquence cardiaque.
Cependant, la Garmin Forerunner 265 est peut-être trop orientée pour le sport et si vous cherchez une montre polyvalente pour la vie quotidienne, elle risque de vous laisser sur votre faim.

articles.title: BY Venture Partners closes $60 million Fund III to back AI startups
articles.text:
BY Venture Partners closes $60 million Fund III to back AI startups
- UAE-based venture capital firm BY Venture Partners has closed its third fund at $60 million, bringing its total assets under management (AUM) to more than $200 million. The fund is anchored by the Dubai Future District Fund (DFDF), with participation from MultiLane, Transmed Capital, Idriss Family Office and other institutional and private investors.
- Led by founding partners Ghaith Yafi, Abdallah Yafi, Rami Jisr and Sohrab Jahanbani, BY Venture Partners invests in early-stage technology startups across MENA and international markets. Its previous funds backed companies including NymCard, Toters, Huspy and Invisible.
- Fund III will invest primarily up to $1 million per startup, targeting AI-native companies at the Pre-Seed to Series A stages, particularly those developing AI-powered solutions for enterprise workflows.
- The fund has already made 15 investments out of a planned portfolio of 40 startups, including PQ Shield, Cosyne, Isometric, Huspy and Invisible. BY Venture Partners operates across more than 16 markets, with approximately two-thirds of its capital deployed outside MENA, primarily in North America and Europe.
- Separately, the firm has secured a mandate to manage the Lebanese Angel Investor Network (LAIN), connecting Lebanese founders with diaspora investors. It has committed to reinvesting 50% of its carried interest into supporting Lebanon's startup ecosystem.
Press release:
BY Venture Partners, a global early-stage venture capital firm headquartered in Dubai, today announced the successful $60 million close of its third vehicle, Fund III. The fund is anchored by the Dubai Future District Fund (DFDF), with participation from established regional institutions, corporate venture arms, and prominent family offices, including leading regional player in AI and high-speed data infrastructure Multi Lane, Transmed Capital, and the Idriss Family Office (KSA). Fund III expands BY Venture Partners’s total Assets Under Management (AUM) to over $200 million.
Empowering AI-Native Founders from a Regional Powerhouse
Fund III will invest primarily up to $1m at the Pre-Seed to Series A stages into AI-native companies that reimagine enterprise workflows and scale globally from day one.
Headquartered in the UAE, BY Venture Partners operates from a region embracing AI at a pace. McKinsey’s November 2025 GCC survey found that 84% of organisations used AI in at least one business function, up from 62% in 2023. The firm invests across more than 16 international markets, with two-thirds of its capital deployed outside the MENA region across North America and Europe. Early momentum for Fund III is already underway, with 15 investments deployed to date out of a planned 40-company portfolio, including PQ Shield, Cosyne, Isometric, Huspy and Invisible.
"We are thrilled to officially announce Fund III today," said Ghaith Yafi, Founding Partner at BY Venture Partners. "The focus of this fund is to back AI-native companies with global ambitions. We are particularly excited about the opportunity to attract some of the world’s most innovative AI companies into the Middle East and connect them with the region’s rapidly growing technology ecosystem. We are executing on a thesis designed to generate strong, long-term returns for our partners.”
Institutional backing for regional impact
The anchor commitment from DFDF reinforces BY Venture Partners’s role in elevating the Middle East as a global tech hub and bridging regional capital with international deal flow.
"We committed to Fund III because BY's model works in both directions. It brings global AI-native companies into Dubai and takes founders from this region into international markets, and that exchange is what Dubai's Economic Agenda D33 asks of us. Ghaith, Abdallah, Rami, Sohrab and the team have built and exited companies themselves and have managed capital through a full market cycle. The flow of companies and founders across that bridge is the basis on which we will measure this partnership," said Nader Albastaki, Managing Director, Dubai Future District Fund (DFDF).
“We have been firm believers in BY Venture Partners since inception, and we are delighted to contribute to the firm's Fund III, to help back up-and-coming AI-first startups in the region,” said MultiLane Founder and CEO Fadi Daou. “As an ecosystem builder myself, as well as a former entrepreneur, BY’s vision fully aligns with ours.”
Rebuilding Ecosystems: The Lebanese Angel Investor Network (LAIN)
Rooted in a commitment to ecosystem building, BY Venture Partners won the MITAI-backed mandate to manage and operate the Lebanese Angel Investor Network (LAIN). LAIN connects global diaspora capital with early-stage Lebanese founders, creating a structured pipeline for early-stage capital and connecting the next generation of regional angel investors. Demonstrating its long-term commitment to ecosystem recovery, BY will reinvest 50% of its carried interest directly back into rebuilding the Lebanese startup ecosystem.
Built by Founders, for Founders
BY sets itself apart through its operator-first DNA: all four partners - Ghaith Yafi, Abdallah Yafi, Rami Jisr and Sohrab Jahanbani - are repeat entrepreneurs who built and exited businesses before joining forces as investors. This hands-on, founder-centric approach has earned BY Venture Partners a Founder Net Promoter Score of 87.
BY's track record has been built across more than one market cycle, including a full financial collapse in Lebanon, where Fund I carried significant exposure. That fund is still on course to return a strong multiple to its investors. The fund has had to adapt to fast-changing market conditions and has built a reputation for moving quickly to support founders in their most difficult and challenging days. Fund II continues to perform strongly relative to its vintage. Between them, the two funds have produced four unicorns, two from each, alongside a growing group of companies now valued in the hundreds of millions, and the firm has already returned meaningful capital to its LPs.
With Fund III, BY Venture Partners continues to leverage its global-first, AI-first network to give early-stage founders the operational edge, capital, and global connectivity required to build market-defining technology platforms.

articles.title: Ace Blend bags $9.91M as it looks to scale science-led nutrition
articles.text:
Ace Blend bags $9.91M as it looks to scale science-led nutrition
The nutrition company will use the funding to advance research-led product development and launch patented nutrition formats.
Ace Blend, a science-led nutrition company, has raised $9.91 million in a Series A2 funding round led by 3one4 Capital, a venture capital firm whose portfolio includes Licious, Darwinbox and Kapiva.
Existing investor Fireside Ventures, an early-stage investor in consumer brands, has increased its backing after leading Ace Blend’s $3.3 million pre-Series A round.
The new funds will support research-led product development and the commercial launch of patented nutrition formats, with the first expected in the fourth quarter of FY27.
Founded in 2018 following more than a decade of research, Ace Blend develops supplements targeting heart health, immunity, sleep, recovery and brain health.
Co-founder Saif Mehkri joined in 2022, bringing nearly three decades of experience in the nutrition industry.
The company said its approach starts with clinical evidence, using research to determine a nutrient’s form, dose and delivery rather than building products around popular ingredients. It also controls sourcing, formulation and manufacturing, while clinical validation and automated testing are conducted by accredited laboratories in Europe.
Partnerships with ingredient suppliers DSM and TCI give it exclusive rights in India to certain technologies, according to the company.
Ace Blend claims 300% growth in FY26, with more than 46% of its customers returning to purchase.
Fireside Ventures principal Ankita Balotia cited repeat purchases and word of mouth as evidence of consumer trust. However, repeat buying alone does not independently establish a supplement’s clinical effectiveness.
3one4 Capital managing partner Pranav Pai said the company was “tackling the hardest problems in nutrition”, including developing formulations suited to Indian needs and maintaining consistent quality.
The funding comes amid wider investment activity in Indian nutrition. TruNativ raised $30 million in June, led by healthcare investment firm OrbiMed. In July, daily supplement brand Supply6 secured Rs 48 crore from Unilever Ventures and Zeropearl VC. More recently, The Stack raised Rs 21.5 crore in October to expand research and its product portfolio.
These investments point to growing investor interest in differentiated formulations, product innovation and repeat demand in a crowded market.
Regulation remains important as brands make increasingly specific health claims. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has regulations covering health supplements and nutraceuticals, alongside separate rules governing advertising and claims.
In February, the government said there was no dedicated Ministry of Food Processing Industries scheme for nutraceuticals, although broader food-processing programmes support infrastructure development.

articles.title: Cuánto vale el Nokia 1100 hoy y cuánto costaba cuando salió al mercado
articles.text:
El Nokia 1100, presentado en 2003 con un precio aproximado de 100 dólares, se convirtió con el tiempo en el teléfono móvil más vendido de la historia: comercializó 250 millones de unidades en seis años, según un estudio de Visual Capitalist basado en datos de Yahoo Finance y Omdia. Más de dos décadas después, conseguir una unidad original ya no es sencillo, y quienes lo buscan deben recurrir al mercado de segunda mano, donde los precios varían según el estado del equipo.
En plataformas como eBay, los vendedores ofrecen ejemplares usados por montos que fluctúan entre 25 y 70 dólares, dependiendo de la fecha de consulta y la condición del aparato. A comienzos de 2026, algunas publicaciones ubicaban el piso de precio en 70 dólares. Para septiembre del mismo año, el rango había descendido a entre 25 y 40 dólares. La diferencia refleja la dinámica propia de un mercado de segunda mano, donde la oferta disponible y el estado de conservación de cada unidad inciden de forma directa en el valor final.
Un diseño pensado para resistir
El Nokia 1100 se concibió con un enfoque centrado en la funcionalidad y la resistencia, no en la conectividad. Su carcasa robusta, con bordes antideslizantes, y un teclado protegido por una alfombrilla de silicona le permitieron soportar el uso cotidiano en condiciones que hubieran dañado a otros equipos de la época. La batería extraíble de ion de litio BL-5C, con una capacidad de 850 mAh y un voltaje de 3,7 V, ofrecía hasta 400 horas en modo de espera y unas 4,5 horas de conversación continua.
Con un uso moderado, una sola carga podía durar más de una semana, gracias también a una pantalla monocromática y un sistema operativo básico que reducían el consumo de energía frente a los teléfonos actuales.
Entre sus funciones, el equipo incluía linterna LED integrada, despertador, calculadora, recordatorios y juegos preinstalados, entre ellos Snake, conocido popularmente como “la viborita” o “culebrita”. Estas prestaciones, sumadas a su bajo costo y su autonomía, impulsaron su éxito en mercados de todo el mundo durante la primera década de los 2000.
El Nokia 1100 fue lanzado como un teléfono básico, enfocado en llamadas y mensajes de texto, sin capacidad para conectarse a internet ni ejecutar aplicaciones de mensajería instantánea. No cuenta con sistema operativo compatible, pantalla a color ni conexión a redes móviles de datos.
El ranking que lidera desde hace más de dos décadas
Según una recopilación publicada por Statista, basada en datos de Visual Capitalist, Yahoo Finance y Omdia, el Nokia 1100 encabeza la lista histórica de celulares más vendidos con sus 250 millones de unidades.
Lo sigue el Nokia 1110 (2005), con 248 millones de unidades, y en tercer lugar aparece el iPhone 6 y 6 Plus (2014), con 222 millones de unidades vendidas en todo el mundo. Completan el listado el Nokia 105, con 200 millones de unidades; el iPhone 6s y 6s Plus, con 174 millones; el iPhone 5s, con 165 millones; el Nokia 3220, con 161 millones, y el iPhone 7 y 7 Plus, con 160 millones.
Ningún modelo posterior, ni siquiera aquellos con tecnologías más avanzadas, logró superar las cifras del Nokia 1100, lo que confirma la vigencia de su registro de ventas más de veinte años después de su lanzamiento.
El regreso de su filosofía en 2026
El nombre del Nokia 1100 volvió a la conversación este año por el lanzamiento del Nokia 300 Charge, un celular básico de HMD Global que recupera parte de la propuesta del modelo original: batería de larga duración, diseño resistente y funciones centradas en lo esencial. El nuevo dispositivo incorpora una batería extraíble de 3.700 mAh que, según la compañía, ofrece más de 40 días en modo de espera con una sola carga, además de una pantalla de 2,4 pulgadas con resolución de 320 x 240 píxeles y un procesador Unisoc SC6531E.
El Nokia 300 Charge cuenta con 4 MB de RAM, 4 MB de almacenamiento interno y admite tarjetas microSD de hasta 32 GB. Su conectividad se limita a redes 2G GSM 900/1800, por lo que depende de la disponibilidad de esa tecnología en cada región. El equipo integra también linterna LED, jack de 3,5 mm para radio FM y carga inversa por USB-C de 10 W mediante un botón físico lateral. Por el momento, su comercialización está limitada a Filipinas.
Nokia, como marca de teléfonos móviles, dejó de liderar el mercado con la llegada de los smartphones y los sistemas operativos iOS y Android. articles.title: Valve Won't "Be Gatekeepers" by Banning AI Games, As "AI Slop" Complaints Grow
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Valve Won't "Be Gatekeepers" by Banning AI Games, As "AI Slop" Complaints Grow
Valve has a growing AI problem on its storefront, and it's not only that game developers are using AI, which is a point of contention for many gamers but not necessarily the biggest concern for developers. Instead, game developers are increasingly reporting that their games are being cloned by developers using AI to clone games from short demos or PR materials ahead of the original game's launch. There has also been an outcry over the number of low-effort AI-generated or AI-assisted games bringing down the overall quality of Steam Next Fest. As reported by Inven, during a recent panel at the Steam Indie Connect developer event, Valve's Tom Giardino and Marc Wilkinson addressed some of these concerns by developers.
Tom Giardino via InvenWe don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use...Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective
Giardino's, and seemingly Valve's, stance on AI game cloning is rather lax in the sense that it appears to mostly leave it up to developers to combat those clones by being more competitive. He explains that game clones have always existed, as has chasing trendy concepts and game mechanics during events like Next Fest, even if AI has made these issues more prevalent by making games easier to clone. He advised that developers take a two-pronged approach to dealing with those clones, first building a community and an identity for their game via an online presence, community engagement and building trust. The second step in combating game clones is for developers to continuously improve their games. 
When asked about instances of extortion faced by developers, in which bad actors cloned a game and threatened the developer with releasing it before the original if money wasn't paid to the extortionist, Giardino expressed concern, stating that this was the first time he had heard of such a case, but encouraged developers to report those cases to Valve.
If you report such cases to us, we want to look into them further and help in whatever way we can.
When directly asked about low-quality games flooding Steam Next Fest, which can result in games getting lost in the noise, Marc Wilkinson explained that recommendation system for Next Fest is based on randomized visibility for the first two days, with the following days being based on personalized recommendations. He goes on to explain that the random exposure was put in place in order to ensure fairness and avoid larger developers taking advantage of the recommendation system. That said, he also acknowledged that Valve is working on addressing Steam's game visibility issue, but that it's challenging, because each studio has a different standard for success; where a small indie developer might be over the moon about 10,000 new wishlists during Next Fest, 10× that amount might still fall short for someone like EA or Ubisoft.
We recognize that the trade-off is some low-quality games get exposed. We are fully aware of the situation, and a significant number of people are thinking about how to solve this problem.
Source:
