articles.title: Updates, Patches and Reboots: The Boring Maintenance That Keeps Office Devices Alive - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Why Routine Maintenance Matters More Than Ever
In today’s fast-paced business environment, it’s easy to overlook the seemingly mundane tasks of updates, patches, and reboots for office devices. However, these routine maintenance activities are fundamental to ensuring that your IT infrastructure remains secure, efficient, and reliable. Despite their unglamorous reputation, neglecting these tasks can lead to costly downtime, security vulnerabilities, and poor device performance that ultimately affect productivity and profitability.
The modern office relies heavily on a range of devices-from desktops and laptops to printers and network equipment-that require ongoing maintenance. According to a recent study, 60% of small to medium-sized businesses experienced at least one significant IT disruption due to outdated software or hardware failures in 2023 alone. This statistic underscores the importance of regular updates and maintenance in keeping business operations running smoothly.
Moreover, the average lifespan of office hardware is often extended significantly through proper maintenance. Devices that receive consistent updates and patches can operate efficiently for several years beyond their expected lifecycle, reducing the need for costly replacements. For example, a study found that businesses that maintain their IT assets regularly see a 30% reduction in hardware replacement costs over five years. This emphasizes how routine upkeep is not just about preventing problems but also about maximizing return on investment.
Understanding the Role of Updates and Patches
Updates and patches are critical for fixing security flaws, enhancing system compatibility, and improving device functionality. Software vendors frequently release updates to address vulnerabilities that hackers could exploit. For example, in 2023, more than 70% of cyberattacks targeted known software vulnerabilities that had not been patched promptly. This highlights the urgent need for businesses to keep their systems current.
Beyond security, updates often contain performance improvements and new features that can optimize device operations. Applying patches ensures that your applications and operating systems remain robust against emerging threats and continue to perform efficiently under evolving workloads.
In addition to security and performance, updates can improve compliance with industry regulations. Many businesses operate under strict data protection laws, such as GDPR or HIPAA, which require that IT systems are kept up to date to safeguard sensitive information. Failure to apply necessary updates can result in non-compliance, leading to hefty fines and legal complications. Thus, routine patch management plays a pivotal role in regulatory adherence.
The Importance of Scheduled Reboots
While updates and patches are often automated, scheduled reboots are an equally vital but sometimes overlooked aspect of maintenance. Reboots clear temporary files, reset memory, and apply system changes that can only take effect after restarting the device. Without regular reboots, devices can slow down or become unstable, leading to frustrating user experiences and potential data loss.
Many organizations underestimate how reboot cycles impact overall system health. In fact, research shows that devices rebooted weekly experience 25% fewer crashes and errors compared to those rebooted infrequently. Establishing a routine reboot schedule can therefore preempt many common IT issues.
Furthermore, rebooting can help resolve software conflicts and free up system resources that accumulate during extended periods of continuous operation. This simple step can significantly enhance system responsiveness and reduce the frequency of technical support tickets, easing the burden on IT teams.
Partnering with Experts for Seamless Maintenance
For businesses without dedicated IT teams, managing updates, patches, and reboots can be overwhelming. This is where professional managed service providers come in. Companies like Contego Solutions’ website specialize in delivering comprehensive maintenance services tailored to the unique needs of office environments. Their expertise ensures that updates are applied promptly, patches are tested and deployed effectively, and reboots are scheduled to minimize disruption.
Outsourcing IT maintenance to experts not only guarantees timely implementation but also provides strategic insights into optimizing device performance and security. Providers often offer proactive monitoring tools that identify potential issues before they escalate, allowing for preemptive action rather than reactive fixes.
Similarly, Daystar’s routine technology support offers proactive monitoring and routine technology support that helps organizations maintain device health without dedicating internal resources. Outsourcing these responsibilities to trusted experts allows businesses to focus on their core operations while safeguarding their IT assets.
Partnering with such providers also means access to the latest industry best practices and compliance standards, which can be challenging to keep up with internally, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises.
Best Practices for Effective Maintenance
To maximize the benefits of updates, patches, and reboots, IT managers should adopt several best practices:
- Automate Where Possible: Use automated patch management tools to ensure updates are applied consistently and without delay. Automation reduces human error and helps keep pace with the increasing volume of updates released by software vendors.
- Test Updates Before Deployment: Implement a testing phase to verify compatibility and prevent disruptions in critical systems. This is especially important for complex environments where an update might conflict with existing applications.
- Schedule Maintenance Windows: Plan updates and reboots during off-hours to minimize impact on employee productivity. Communicating these windows clearly to staff helps manage expectations and reduces frustration.
- Maintain Clear Documentation: Keep records of update schedules, patch versions, and reboot logs for compliance and troubleshooting. This documentation serves as an audit trail and aids in diagnosing issues should they arise.
- Educate Employees: Promote awareness about the importance of routine maintenance and encourage users to save work regularly before system restarts. User cooperation can significantly smooth maintenance processes.
Additionally, consider implementing a layered approach to security that complements patch management, such as endpoint protection and network monitoring. This comprehensive strategy further reduces risk and enhances device longevity.
The Business Impact of Proactive IT Maintenance
Consistent maintenance of office devices translates directly into improved business outcomes. Reliable technology infrastructure reduces unplanned downtime, which costs businesses an average of $5,600 per minute according to Gartner. It also enhances data security, safeguarding sensitive customer and company information from breaches that can damage reputation and incur regulatory penalties.
Moreover, well-maintained devices perform faster and more efficiently, enabling employees to work without frustrating delays. This can boost overall productivity and employee satisfaction, fostering a more agile and competitive business environment.
Proactive maintenance also contributes to environmental sustainability by extending the lifespan of hardware and reducing electronic waste. Organizations that prioritize device upkeep contribute less to the growing e-waste problem, aligning with corporate social responsibility goals.
Looking Ahead: Maintenance in a Hybrid Work Era
The rise of hybrid work models has introduced new challenges for IT maintenance. Devices are now distributed across home offices, corporate sites, and mobile locations, requiring remote update and patch management capabilities. Organizations need to adopt flexible maintenance strategies that accommodate diverse environments and ensure all devices, regardless of location, remain secure and operational.
Investing in cloud-based management platforms and collaborating with service providers familiar with hybrid setups can streamline maintenance workflows. This approach allows IT teams to maintain visibility and control over device health while supporting the evolving needs of a distributed workforce.
Furthermore, the hybrid model demands enhanced security protocols due to increased exposure to unsecured networks. Routine updates and patches become even more critical in this context, as vulnerabilities in remote devices can provide gateways for cyberattacks on the broader corporate network.
Conclusion
While updates, patches, and reboots may seem like routine and even boring tasks, they are the foundation that keeps office devices alive and businesses running smoothly. Neglecting these essential maintenance activities can expose organizations to significant risks, including cybersecurity threats, operational disruptions, and increased costs. By prioritizing regular maintenance and leveraging expert support such as and, businesses can ensure their technology infrastructure remains resilient, secure, and efficient-empowering them to thrive in a competitive landscape.

articles.title: One Planet Partners ties up with SMTB of Japan to launch Rs 3,000 cr fund
articles.text:
One Planet Partners ties up with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to launch Rs 3,000 cr fund
One Planet will invest in high growth companies across the sectors of energy, mobility and manufacturing
One Planet Partners, an India-focused private equity firm, has tied up with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank to launch its Rs 3,000-crore maiden fund.
According to a statement, the Japanese financial institution has made an equity investment in One Planet Partners, alongside the anchoring of a dedicated private equity fund managed by One Planet. The fund will focus on high-growth businesses benefitting from India's energy transition, mobility, and manufacturing-led industrial expansion.
Founded in 2024, One Planet is a Mumbai-based asset management firm established by four founding partners Mukund Rajan, Bobby Pauly, Mrinalini Mirchandani, and Sheetal Thakkar.
One Planet Partners will focus on high-growth mid-market businesses, providing scale-up capital of Rs 100 crore to Rs 500 crore to enterprises with attractive unit economics and revenue between Rs 200 crore and Rs 2000 crore.
The firm aims to combine growth capital with active ownership and operational expertise to help businesses scale and strengthen their competitive positioning.
One Planet Partners Founder and Chairperson Mukund Rajan said, "With strong institutional support, our ambition is to build a world-class investment platform focused on high-growth businesses at the intersection of India's economic expansion, energy transition, and industrial transformation."
One Planet Partners has already commenced capital deployment. Bengaluru-based electric mobility company Yulu Bikes Private Limited is the first investment by the platform. The investment was made as part of Yulu's $93 million Series C funding round.
Kazuya Yoneda, General Manager – Equity Investment Department, of Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, said, "India is one of the world’s most compelling long-term investment destinations. Our strategic investment reflects confidence in both the market and One Planet Partners’ proven track record, institutional approach, and differentiated ability to access and create value in India’s private markets.”

O Nintendo Switch Lite está saindo por R$ 1.213,64 no Pix com cupom OFERTAPRATECH no Mercado Livre. O console 100% portátil da Nintendo, com tela LCD de 5,5″ e compatível com quase toda a biblioteca de jogos do modelo original, está com desconto de 36% sobre o original de R$ 1.899.

articles.title: Intel's Lip-Bu Tan Discusses Possible AMD Cooperation, Lays Out CPU and Foundry Plans
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Intel's Lip-Bu Tan Discusses Possible AMD Cooperation, Lays Out CPU and Foundry Plans
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has spoken with AMD CEO Lisa Su about exploring potential areas of cooperation. Tan brought it up during an October 24 fireside chat with Jimmy Cheng, president of the Chinese American Semiconductor Professional Association (CASPA), though he didn't say what those areas are, and neither company has announced anything. AMD was earlier reported to be evaluating Intel's 14A node, so foundry work seems like an obvious guess. However, it could just as well be packaging, software, or something else entirely.
Most of the chat was about Intel's own turnaround. Tan reportedly said Intel has to "reclaim the leadership in CPU" and that it will now tailor chips like Xeon to customer needs, something he admitted the company was too proud to do before. He named ASICs, co-packaged optics, physical AI and advanced packaging as possible growth areas, and wants two or three of them to eventually bring in around 10% of Intel's revenue each. On the foundry side, 18A is in volume production, while 14A has its 0.5 PDK out, with 0.9 next and 1.0 for volume production early next year. Intel had targeted October for handing the 0.9 PDK to outside customers, and Tan's "stay tuned" suggests it hasn't happened just yet.The two x86 rivals already cooperate in several areas. Last week, AMD agreed to fold its ZenDNN optimizations into Intel's oneDNN library for PyTorch, and AMD has also been named among companies reportedly weighing Intel Foundry deals. Intel reports Q3 2026 results on October 29, and Tan may well be asked about AMD on the earnings call that follows.
Sources:
				Chat with Jimmy Cheng, 				via Tom's Hardware			
	
	
	
		
	
		
15 Comments on Intel's Lip-Bu Tan Discusses Possible AMD Cooperation, Lays Out CPU and Foundry Plans
It's not like Intel could just copy AMD's tech, sure, the foundry would have access (if AMD went with Intel), but the CPU group wouldn't be able to see anything at all
and mask can mean anything how they look like
Intel on the other hand I could understand why they'd want to know how AMD uses SMT, or stacked 3D cache.Intel is the only company that holds a majority of patents for X86. The foundry group may have no use for AMD's tech, but they're technically still Intel, with no doubt those secrets could get passed around.
If you want to know everything about a CPU for a company like Intel it's just like a car engine. Buy one and tear it down.
Modern CPU design is well understood and the designs are mostly the result of a set of requirements that prioritize one thing over another. The thing that hurt Intel in the past is that it didn't have TSMCs fabs, so even if it designed a better CPU it couldn't build it.
"“So, computer design is almost all engineering, and reduction of practice of known methods.”"
-Jim Keller
Plus AMD and Intel are leveraging the same designs with tradeoffs in pipeline performance and clock speed. The biggest driver now is prefetch and prediction modeling, cache size and latency.
Tiles for example are not part of the architecture of the Zen core.
i.e. Zen 3 cores exist as both 'chiplet' designs on desktop and servers, and 'monolithic' ones in laptops (Cezanne). The existence of the tile or the packaging doesn't really change the CPUs core architecture. i.e. Cezanne is still Zen 3
That said the packaging and the node is what is giving us faster CPUs. More density, greater power efficiency, faster transistor switching, layered designs = more options for the core design. This is all determined by advancements in TSMCs Fabs or Intel's Fabs, not by AMD (or Intel's CPU design team).
It's actually a very tricky business they are in, trying to predict the future.
Also I wonder if intel could reverse engineer AMD's designs and implement their strengths into their own products.

articles.title: SK hynix-owned Solidigm is plotting a new $45 billion flash memory factory for the US, report claims — wants go-ahead to export equipment for China upgrades in return
articles.text:
SK hynix-owned Solidigm is plotting a new $45 billion flash memory factory for the US, report claims — wants go-ahead to export equipment for China upgrades in return
Solidigm's using the potential US investment as leverage in its attempt to export equipment to upgrade an existing plant in China
Solidigm, an American subsidiary of SK hynix, one of the biggest flash chip makers on the planet, is reportedly in talks with the Commerce Department over plans to invest $45 billion in a new plant to be built in the United States. But, Bloomberg reports, there's a catch — Solidigm wants to be given the go-ahead to export equipment to upgrade its existing plant in Dalian, China. The company has purportedly told officials that the upgrades would allow the Chinese plant to then help finance the cost of its U.S.-based counterpart, according to unnamed sources. It's as-yet unclear how the proposal was received, or whether the Commerce Department is inclined to agree to the deal.
The U.S. government has been keen to drive at-home manufacturing wherever possible, including for chips used in its computers and data centers. National security is regularly cited as a key reason behind the move. It's also the reason for the government's stance on exporting technologies to China, including the equipment that Solidigm says will help upgrade its Dalian plant. Similar export restrictions are in place for high-end AI data center components, with a black market having sprung up to take the place of sanctioned sales. Earlier this month, it was reported that some of Nvidia's powerful Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs are being used in China Telecom data centers, with no explanation of how they got there. A 2025 report claimed that a cool $1 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips had been smuggled into China, a figure that is sure to have increased significantly as 2026 draws to a close.
In this case, Solidigm's planned Chinese factory upgrades could be mutually beneficial, allowing funds to be transferred to the new U.S. plant. But that requires the U.S. government to give it permission to ship the machinery in the first place, something that is far from guaranteed. The Dalian factory produces NAND flash memory, the likes of which are used in everything from relatively simple devices to full-blown data centers. It also comes at a time when global NAND production is a hot-button topic. Samsung and SK hynix are upgrading their Chinese factories to produce more of the chips used in AI data centers in an attempt to meet growing demand. Manufacturers have already slashed production of consumer-focused memory in favor of the more lucrative data center-grade components, causing prices to spike globally. This volatility in the market as a whole was given as one of the reasons SK hynix chose to cancel a planned Solidigm IPO earlier this week.
Beyond dangling a $45 billion plant, Solidigm has also allegedly told the Commerce Department that its total investment in U.S. manufacturing could reach $100 billion eventually, with construction in New York penciled in for 2027. The company is fresh from its latest earnings call, where it announced revenues of $75 billion with $60 billion in operating profit, and $28 billion in net. The company made no mention of its Dalian plant or a planned US investment, but did warn that memory shortages are set to last through 2030.

articles.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17B | TechCrunch
articles.text:
DoorDash announced on Thursday that it has agreed to acquire rival Instacart for $17 billion. The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery.
DoorDash will buy Instacart for a total value of $65 for each Instacart share, the company said. The deal has been approved by the boards of both companies.
“Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Instacart CEO Chris Rogers in a press release.
“When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders.”
DoorDash plans to keep Instacart’s brand, enterprise technology products, and app. The company also notes that the two brands will continue to operate as separate and independent companies until the transaction closes.
DoorDash says the deal could help more grocers build out their own online ordering platforms and advertising businesses using Instacart’s technology, while grocers could also use DoorDash’s fulfillment services to handle more online orders and offer lower-cost delivery.
“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the press release.
“Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts. Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local,” said Xu.
Instacart currently has a market cap of more than $13 billion, and its stock price is up 25% for the year to date. The company likely viewed this as an opportune time to sell at a desirable price, ahead of intensifying competition in the grocery delivery market.
Bloomberg previously reported that Instacart was in talks with Uber, but that the company had walked away from discussions.
The deal is expected to close toward the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028.

articles.title: Canada launches roadmap to improve telecom competition
articles.text:
The Government of Canada has launched the Telecom Competition Roadmap to improve competition and increase the choices for Canadians.
The roadmap outlines actions that the government will implement:
More choice – to increase competition and give consumers more choices, the government will make it easier for competitors to access existing networks and expand their networks.
Better prices- to help Canadians take advantage of more affordable plans, the Canadian government will spotlight competitive offers, make it easier to shop around and switch providers and eliminate unnecessary fees.
High-quality networks – the Canadian Government will make sure consumers benefit from high-quality services across the country, and the government will help companies deploy the latest fibre-optic networks, experiment with new technologies and strengthen access to reliable connectivity in rural and Indigenous communities.
The government will monitor the progress using indicators such as pricing, switching behaviour, network speeds, coverage and consumer complaints. The Government of Canada says that parts of the roadmap have already been underway, offering benefits for consumers.
Why this roadmap is important
When you think telecoms in Canada, everyone thinks of the Big Three: Bell, Telus and Rogers, and even if you think of a sub-brand like Koodo or Lucky Mobile, those are also owned by the Big Three. And while there are other options like Freedom Mobile, owned by Quebec’s Videotron, the lack of competition and options in the country has led to incredibly expensive phone plans, especially compared to other countries.
In November of 2025, the federal budget detailed the country’s plan to increase telecom competition. This includes the ‘dig once’ policy approach to help speed up deployment and allow telecoms to work together and share more of their fibre optic networks.
Source: Government of Canada

articles.title: I chose the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro as the best health and fitness gadget of the year in our awards — here's why
articles.text:
Why the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro's outstanding construction, new stamina metrics and Apple Watch-rivaling accuracy make it my Fitness Device of the Year award winner
The Fenix rises once again
The Garmin Fenix 9 Pro is Garmin's latest — and greatest — watch. The Fenix series always occupies a flagship position in Garmin's lineup: while the company does make more expensive watches, most of those are specialist pieces of gear, such as the Tactix for soldiers, the Descent for professional divers, and the Marq series as an ultra-premium option for fashion-forward Garmin users.
The Garmin Fenix series is its top-tier 'generalist' watch, and considering it only comes out once every few years, anticipation is always high. Fortunately, the Fenix 9 Pro lives up to the hype, and is my Fitness Devices of the Year at the TechRadar Product of the Year Awards 2026.
It's a powerhouse of a watch, from construction and performance, and has coped with every test we have thrown at it, from hikes in Chamonix, to comparison tests against the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and an electrical heart rate monitor, the Frontier X2.
Let's start with construction. The Fenix 9 Pro's entire case is now made of titanium, rather than a titanium bezel and fiber-reinforced polymer (that's plastic, to you and me) elsewhere.
It's thinner, and the lack of visible screws (aside from the back plate) make for a refined, sleek aesthetic. The display is sapphire crystal as standard, too, protecting the super-bright AMOLED touchscreen display, with the usual MIP Power Glass solar charging options as an additional extra.
The construction makes for an amazing watch, and these upgrades make the Fenix 9 Pro really feel just that, Pro — more like a Marq. I'm wearing the 43mm version, and it really doesn't feel like an ultra-chunky Fenix. In fact, it feels far more like wearing an upmarket metal dive watch.
This sealed unit design necessitated a redesign in the buttons, according to Garmin's promotional material, in order to make sure it remained waterproof up to 40m deep, but Garmin cracked it and the watch retains Garmin's distinctive five-button design.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It's even revamped the LED light, with an introduction of a third green option to add to its black and red tones. The green light offers improved visibility compared to the red option, without sacrificing your night-eyes.
Software-wise, the UX is familiar to Garmin watch users, as everything is innately customizable, from the widget stack to workout views to watch faces. New features include Garmin Epic, which allows you to string several workouts together into one mega-event, such as multiple ski runs over one long weekend, for example. You can start it from the watch, and view or share it in the app. Rucking also got a useful redesign, while Maps has been updated to provide an angled POV option.
In our performance test, I was expecting accuracy — after all, the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro retains Garmin's Elevate V5 heart rate sensor array from previous years — but I wasn't expecting it to cleave so close to the heart rate monitor and the Apple Watch Ultra 4 (which Apple claims is the most accurate wearable to date) during my test workouts.
Rerouting course directions has proven to be responsive and speedy, while the battery performs as described, lasting for a week, and the watch is comfortable to wear during sleep, workouts and every day.
There wasn't really any doubt that the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro was going to be a good watch, or even a great one. Like the Apple Watch Ultra 4, it builds on everything Garmin has done before to create a worthy successor to the ever-popular Fenix line. When the Fenix 10 comes out in a few years, this one will come down in price just like the Fenix 8 before it, and we'll see far more adopters take it on and have fun with it.
I suppose I could have chosen something like the cheap Google Fitbit Air, the Garmin Cirqa, or the Apple Watch Ultra 4 to be our Fitness Device of the Year. But when I thought about what was going to dominate my limited wrist real estate if I sign up for a race, there was only ever going to be a handful of options, and the 43mm Garmin Fenix 9 Pro was first on the list.
It's smart enough not to look out of place in the office, it's got everything I need for training, it's got all the complications I need from the Connect IQ score, like Spotify and Komoot, and a week-long battery life (sorry Apple) that cinches it for me over the Ultra 4.

Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

Seagate's 16TB external HDD falls to 0.025 cents per GB at Newegg — this storage deal is $50 cheaper than even its Prime Day sale price
A plug and play portable external storage solution
Spotting any kind of discount on storage as of late has been a bit of a monumental task, as the prices of HDDs and SSDs have only been going one way, and that's up. Seagate's 16TB Expansion Desktop External HDD is reduced to $399.99 at Newegg, a reduction of $150 from its $549.99 list price and $50 cheaper than its Prime Day price. Not only is that a bit of relief during turbulent storage times, but the price on this HDD is actually better than we saw during Prime Day earlier this month.
● Grab this external HDD deal at Newegg
The Seagate Expansion Desktop 16TB HDD is an all-in-one HDD and enclosure that offers a highly versatile plug-and-play solution for storing or backing up your precious data. Seagate ships the drive formatted to ExFAT, so it'll work with virtually any platform out of the box. Of course, you can reformat the drive to any other file system that suits your use case. This external drive has also been a popular choice for those looking to shuck the Hard Disk out of the enclosure and grab a cheaper HDD for use in a NAS or PC.
The Seagate enclosure has its own power supply, which you'll need to connect to a nearby mains socket, while using a USB 3.0 cable to connect the drive to your PC or laptop for easy drag-and-drop file transfers. Should anything happen to your drive causing it to fail, each purchase comes with Seagate's Rescue Data Recovery service included, just in case you need help to recover your data.
The Seagate Expansion Desktop drive is a 16TB HDD that connects via USB 3.0. It's formatted to ExFAT by default, allowing it to work with virtually platform out of the box.
Shucking this drive comes with risks. There's no way to guarantee what version of Seagate HDD is inside; it might be an EXOS, or it might not. But what is guaranteed is that once you open the enclosure and start pulling drives out, your warranty becomes invalid.
If you're looking for 16TB of storage at prices cheaper than the last Prime Day, then today's Newegg deal on this Seagate Expansion Desktop HDD is one of the best storage deals currently on offer.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 29, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 29, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, October 29, 2026.
Artificial intelligence poses numerous challenges for employees but can improve governance in governments, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Vembu’s AI warning: one worker could do the work of ten
Artificial intelligence (AI) could allow one skilled employee to do work that previously required 10, reshaping employment even as it creates new opportunities. That is the warning from Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu. “What it does mean is a rebalancing across the economy and that is painful when we go through it. The only thing we can do is to accept that it is coming and be prepared for it,” he wrote on X.
Maharashtra launches MahaINDUS AI to speed up government work
Maharashtra is giving its government offices an AI upgrade. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis launched MahaINDUS, an AI platform designed for government offices, on October 28, 2026. The government said the initiative aims to improve transparency, accountability and administrative efficiency. By combining AI with integrated databases, departments are expected to find eligible beneficiaries, verify claims and assess welfare schemes more effectively.
Beyond AI infrastructure, India’s tech boom rests on the efficient use of power and water
At TechSparks 2026, founders of SolarSquare and Boson Whitewater unpack why overcoming perception, pricing gaps, and consumer trust matters far more in climatetech than just building the technology.
Funding news
Venttup raises $3M co-led by Rainmatter and Unicorn India Ventures
Industries 5.0 startup Venttup has raised $3 million in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Rainmatter, backed by Zerodha, and Unicorn India Ventures. The company will use the funds to expand its engineering team, establish precision manufacturing capabilities and invest in rapid prototyping and AI-led sourcing.
Venttup is setting up a manufacturing facility in Bengaluru to support precision machining, turning and sheet metal production for energy transition, defence, aerospace and space applications. The company reported fivefold growth to ₹10 crore in FY2025-26 and has added over 15 blue-chip customers in the past year. Its business opportunity pipeline stands at approximately ₹30 crore.
Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre raises Rs 28 crore in Series A
Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre has raised Rs 28 crore in its first institutional funding round, led by Alkemi Growth Capital. The investment will support geographical expansion, increased clinical capacity, specialised care programmes and stronger insurance and corporate partnerships.
Founded in Pune in 2008, Jagruti provides mental healthcare, addiction treatment, rehabilitation and elder care services. The organisation currently operates more than 19 centres across nine cities, with over 1,600 beds and 40 doctors. It has supported more than 82,000 individuals. Jagruti plans to expand to over 40 centres and 4,000 beds across Tier I and Tier II cities over the next three to four years.
Coratia Technologies raises Rs 18 crore for underwater robotics
Underwater robotics startup Coratia Technologies has raised Rs 18 crore in a bridge funding round led by MGF Kavachh. The capital will support execution of its Rs 66 crore Indian Navy contract under the iDEX initiative, research and development, product development and manufacturing expansion.
Founded by Debendra Pradhan and Biswajit Swain, Coratia develops indigenous underwater robotic systems for defence, infrastructure and industrial applications. Its flagship Jalasimha underwater remotely operated vehicle has achieved Technology Readiness Level 9. The company's technologies can also support inspections of dams, bridges, ports, pipelines and offshore assets. Coratia had raised Rs 17 crore from MGF Kavachh, Piper and SIDBI in a pre-Series A round in 2025.
Carbelim secures Rs 10 crore from IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund
Kerala-based deep-tech startup Carbelim has secured Rs 10 crore from the IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund, becoming the first startup from the state to receive investment from the fund. Founded by Karthika Gopi and Rahul Babu, the company develops microalgae-based carbon capture and air-purification systems that absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide and convert it into oxygen. Carbelim has filed 13 patents, including seven in the US and six in India.
The funding is expected to help the company create more than 50 jobs and pursue its target of achieving Rs 100 crore in turnover through international markets. The Rs 1,000 crore fund is backed by IIT Madras, IIT Madras Research Park and Unicorn India Ventures.
Docterz raises Rs 5 crore, with doctors contributing 60% of funding
Healthcare technology company Docterz has raised Rs 5 crore from approximately 35 investors, including doctors who use its platform. Nearly 60% of the funding came from around 20 doctors, alongside investors such as SUGAR Cosmetics co-founder Vineeta Singh and former CaratLane CEO Avnish Anand. Founded by practising paediatrician Atish Laddad, Docterz provides digital medical records, appointment management, billing and patient engagement tools.
Its platform supports more than 5,000 doctors across India, with a strong presence in paediatrics. The company will use the capital to expand its reach, explore acquisitions and develop practical AI-enabled tools for medical practitioners, while maintaining a focus on patient data security and clinical independence.
ISLAND Beauty raises Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC
Skincare brand ISLAND Beauty has raised Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC to support product development, brand awareness and customer acquisition. Co-founded by Shirley Setia, Korean skincare expert Jinsoon Lee, Mayank Jain and Sakshi Jain, the company combines Korean skincare ingredients with formulations developed in India for local weather conditions and consumer needs. Its proprietary Core Barrier Matrix approach focuses on both skin-barrier repair and defence, encouraging simpler and more consistent skincare routines.
The brand's current portfolio includes cleansers, toners, serums, moisturisers and lip-care products. Over the next three years, ISLAND Beauty plans to expand its product range and strengthen its market presence, positioning itself around barrier-focused skincare for Indian consumers.
Viridian Ingni Propulsion raises Rs 1.47 crore in pre-seed round
Chennai-based propulsion technology startup Viridian Ingni Propulsion has raised ₹1.47 crore in a pre-seed round led by Inflection Point Ventures. The company has also secured ₹53.75 lakh in grants from government programmes and other institutions. Founded in February 2024 by Sriram G, the startup develops electric propulsion systems integrating motors, controllers and firmware. The funding will help it move from validated prototypes to pilot production, establish manufacturing infrastructure and complete certification requirements.
Other news
Dialog Axiata, IITM Pravartak partner on technology research
Sri Lankan connectivity provider Dialog Axiata has partnered with IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation to advance applied research and technology development in Sri Lanka. The memorandum of understanding, signed in Colombo, will connect research networks with Sri Lankan universities, government bodies and industry stakeholders.
The collaboration will explore innovation and incubation, applied research, artificial intelligence, skills development and international knowledge sharing. Initial areas under consideration include Sinhala and Tamil conversational AI, technology-enabled dengue prevention and solutions to human-elephant conflict. The partnership will begin with selected pilot projects before considering wider deployment. The initiative aims to strengthen Sri Lanka's research capabilities and translate academic work into practical solutions addressing national and societal challenges.
Zoho upgrades Analytics with agentic AI capabilities
Chennai-based technology company Zoho has upgraded Zoho Analytics with an intelligence layer designed to connect business data, contextual understanding and automated actions. The platform introduces semantic and ontology layers to help AI agents interpret organisational structures, business terminology and key metrics. Its conversational business intelligence assistant, Ask Zia, uses six specialised sub-agents to handle data analysis, modelling, visualisation, preparation, coding and SQL generation. The platform also supports automated workflows, more than 500 existing data connectors and 30 additional connectors.
New governance features allow administrators to monitor agent activity, data access and costs. Zoho Analytics also introduces enhanced visualisations, forecasting tools and data science capabilities, enabling businesses to move from reporting towards AI-assisted operational execution.
Urban households expected to spend Rs 1.97 lakh crore this festive season: Local Circles
Urban Indian households are projected to spend approximately ₹1.97 lakh crore on festive purchases in 2026, according to a LocalCircles study. The estimate is around ₹12,000 crore higher than in 2024, despite moderating from the previous year's GST-related high. About 57% of urban households plan festive purchases, spending an average of nearly ₹20,000 each. Clothing, footwear and accessories lead planned purchases, followed by home appliances, furniture and travel. The study also points to growing demand for quick commerce as consumers postpone purchases until closer to festivals. Platforms including Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, Amazon Now and Flipkart Minutes are expanding their reach and reporting higher festive-season activity.
Fruugo partners with PayGlocal to help Indian sellers reach global markets
Global online marketplace Fruugo is entering India through a partnership with cross-border payments company PayGlocal and technology and operations provider DMSMatrix. The initiative will give PayGlocal's more than 12,000 merchants access to Fruugo's international marketplace, helping Indian businesses sell to consumers across more than 40 countries. Sellers in categories including electronics, clothing and home decor will be able to explore overseas demand and diversify their sales channels. The partnership combines Fruugo's international shopper network with PayGlocal's payments infrastructure and DMSMatrix's onboarding and operational capabilities. The initiative targets micro, small and medium enterprises seeking greater product visibility as domestic e-commerce competition intensifies and international online shopping continues to expand.
upGrad School of Technology partners with MongoDB
upGrad School of Technology has partnered with MongoDB to strengthen industry-integrated engineering education and prepare students for modern software development and AI applications. The collaboration will provide eligible students with access to MongoDB for Academia, technical learning resources and fully sponsored certification vouchers. The two organisations will also explore curriculum enhancements, hackathons, innovation challenges, guest lectures, internships and career opportunities. Faculty members will receive access to technical resources, while designated faculty champions will support adoption of modern database technologies.
The partnership aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements, particularly in cloud-native development, artificial intelligence and database engineering. It will give students practical exposure and recognised credentials to improve career readiness.
Procol's AI procurement platform manages over $30 billion in spending
AI-powered procurement technology company Procol is helping manufacturing enterprises automate purchasing workflows across multiple plants, suppliers and business units. The company works with more than 150 manufacturing businesses across over 10 countries, including Havells, Emami, Blue Star and Aditya Birla Group. Its platform automates processes spanning supplier onboarding, requests for quotations, electronic auctions, approvals and accounts payable, while integrating with enterprise systems such as SAP and Oracle. Procol says its implementations have saved buyers more than 8,100 hours of manual work and enabled procurement cycles to become significantly faster. The company currently manages over $30 billion in spending and reports generating more than $1 billion in savings across its customer base.
Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship Program launched in Karnataka
The Centre of Excellence for Farmer Producer Organizations, supported by Karnataka's Department of Horticulture and the National Entrepreneurship Network, has launched the Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship Program in the state. The initiative aims to strengthen Farmer Producer Organizations through business planning, market access, mentoring and execution support.
Its first Growth Bootcamp brought together 27 FPOs and more than 60 participants, including government officials, business experts and FPO leaders.
Participating organisations assessed their businesses, identified growth opportunities and selected priority initiatives for the next 12 months. They will now enter a structured 10-week programme featuring expert-led group and individual sessions. The programme aims to help FPOs become more sustainable enterprises, improve farmer incomes and create rural economic opportunities.
Devnagri AI expands from translation to multilingual AI infrastructure
Language technology company Devnagri AI has announced an evolution from a translation-focused platform to multilingual AI infrastructure for enterprises. The company aims to integrate language capabilities directly into business workflows rather than treating translation as a standalone function. Its offerings include multilingual content processing and AI-driven communication tools designed for customer-facing services and internal operations.
The platform supports cloud, hybrid and on-premises deployment, enabling organisations to integrate language technology within their existing security and technology environments.
Founded in 2021 by Nakul Kundra and Himanshu Sharma, Devnagri AI focuses on helping businesses engage users in their preferred languages. The company believes contextual multilingual capabilities will be increasingly important as enterprises expand AI adoption across India's linguistically diverse markets.
TutorCloud AI launches integrated platform for K-12 education
TutorCloud AI has launched an integrated artificial intelligence-powered platform connecting students, teachers, parents and school administrators in one ecosystem. Designed for K-12 education, the platform aims to support personalised tutoring while giving educators and families greater visibility into students' learning journeys.
The initiative reflects a focus on using AI to help teachers understand learning progress and identify student needs, rather than simply generating answers. By bringing different stakeholders onto a common platform, TutorCloud AI seeks to improve coordination between classroom instruction, home support and school administration.
The company positions the system as a way to make learning more personalised and connected, while enabling educators to use technology to better understand and support individual students.
Wissen Technology strengthens Singapore leadership with Tinku Gupta
Wissen Technology is strengthening its Singapore operations through a delivery-led strategy focused on engineering expertise, product development and business outcomes. The technology services company has appointed Tinku Gupta as Vice Chairman of Wissen Technology Singapore. Gupta brings more than 30 years of experience spanning technology, financial market infrastructure, business operations and cybersecurity. Wissen aims to help enterprises modernise technology platforms and accelerate innovation.
Founded in 2000, the company says it has delivered projects worth more than $1 billion and serves over 20 Fortune 500 companies.
Vaani AI Research launches self-service platform for voice AI agents
Bengaluru- and Singapore-based Vaani AI Research has launched a self-service developer platform for building, deploying and managing voice AI agents. Users can describe the agent they want, preview its voice, configure actions and deploy it across phone calls, websites, applications and WhatsApp.
The platform is built around Vaani's voice infrastructure, which connects speech models with the systems needed to operate agents in production. Its capabilities include inference optimisation, memory and conversational controls.
The launch follows the company's experience deploying voice AI in enterprise workflows, where poor conversational experiences can frustrate customers and lead to lost opportunities. The platform aims to simplify development and deployment of voice-based AI services for businesses and developers.
Festive invoice financing crosses Rs 20,000 crore, says M1xchange
India's pre-festive financing volumes crossed Rs 20,000 crore in 2026, with micro, small and medium enterprises increasingly using formal invoice discounting to fund seasonal demand, according to trade receivables platform M1xchange. Financing for micro-MSMEs grew more than 100% year-on-year, while average daily festive financing increased over 40%. The company projects overall festive-season financing to grow approximately 30% this year.
Invoice discounting enables suppliers to access working capital against unpaid invoices, helping them purchase inventory and meet delivery commitments before customers make payments.
Sector-wise trends show strong festive-period activity in consumer durables, e-retail, e-commerce and paints. The findings highlight the growing role of formal credit mechanisms in supporting smaller suppliers during peak business periods.
Fluke begins local manufacturing of digital multimeter components in India
Fluke Corporation has launched a local manufacturing initiative in India, marking a step towards expanding its domestic manufacturing capabilities under the government's Make in India programme. The first phase covers manufacturing associated with the Fluke 115 and Fluke 117 digital multimeters, including local production of printed circuit board assemblies. The initiative follows the company's progression from Class II to Class I Local Supplier status.
Fluke said the move would strengthen its engagement with Indian customers and support the country's industrial development. The company aims to build local capabilities while maintaining its global standards for quality, precision and reliability. The initiative is intended to establish a foundation for further expansion of manufacturing operations in India.
Otto launches voice AI CRM for field sales teams
Voice AI company Otto, also known as Ottoverse, has launched a voice-based customer relationship management platform designed for field sales representatives. The system enables sales teams to manage CRM activities through phone calls rather than manually entering information after customer meetings. Representatives can report meeting outcomes, while Otto updates deal records, saves contacts, drafts follow-up emails, creates tasks and prepares summaries for managers.
The platform uses voice AI models trained on field sales conversations and is designed to recognise product names, part numbers and different accents. Its context layer connects calls, meetings, emails, calendars and enterprise resource planning records to provide relevant customer information. Headquartered in New York and Mumbai, Otto is backed by Gutter Capital.
Masai School cuts course fees by 50% in IIT Patna partnership
Masai School has reduced course fees by 50% across its programmes through a partnership with Vishlesan i-Hub at IIT Patna, aiming to make technology upskilling more accessible. The programmes include Analytics with Agentic AI and Applied AI and Machine Learning Essentials, with the latter also available in Tamil and Telugu.
About 70% of Masai's students come from Tier II and III cities. The collaboration will combine industry-led mentoring, access to the IIT ecosystem and placement support. Vishlesan i-Hub has enrolled 14,971 learners across its programmes, with nearly 60% studying in languages other than English. The initiative seeks to address affordability and language barriers affecting access to employment-oriented technology education.
Hoopr launches Smash Plus for music licensing in TV and OTT advertising
Music technology startup Hoopr has launched Hoopr Smash Plus, a platform for licensing music for television commercials, OTT advertising, films, web series and corporate productions. Kisna Jewellers is the first brand to use the service, licensing the track 'Woh Kisna Hai' from the Tips catalogue for a campaign featuring Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput Kapoor. The platform aims to simplify macro-sync licensing, which typically requires separate agreements with record labels, publishers and copyright societies.
Indian corporates drive flexible office demand as BFSI is fastest-growing sector: myHQ
India’s flexible office market is entering a more mature phase, with Indian corporates and banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) companies driving demand, according to a report by myHQ. Indian corporates accounted for 23.4% of flexible workspace demand in 2026, up from 21.9% in 2025, becoming the second-largest company segment after startups. Their average requirement increased from 25 seats in 2023 to 55 seats in 2026.
BFSI’s share of demand rose 2.7 times to 12.2% from 4.5% in 2023, making it the second-largest industry contributor. IT/ITeS remained the largest segment at 43.9%, while startups accounted for 39.2% of demand.
HomeLane turns EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26; targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue in FY27
HomeLane, a technology-enabled home interiors company, reported a return to growth following the integration of its businesses, with revenue increasing 19% and its order book expanding 37% year-on-year in the first half of FY27. The company turned operating EBITDA positive in the fourth quarter of FY26, reporting quarterly revenue of Rs 212 crore and an operating EBITDA margin of 5%.
HomeLane expects to cross Rs 1,000 crore in revenue in FY27 and remain EBITDA positive for the full financial year. The company said its growing order book provides visibility into the second half, as projects typically convert into revenue over six to nine months. For FY26, revenue remained steady at Rs 745 crore as HomeLane prioritised integrating DesignCafe. Direct project costs declined to 52% of revenue from 56.6% in FY25.
Sorry Sugar launches zero-added-sugar Diwali campaign
Zero-added-sugar beverage brand Sorry Sugar has launched its Diwali campaign, ‘Yeh Diwali, Bina Cheeni Wali’, featuring a music-driven film that challenges conventional perceptions of festive indulgence and healthy consumption.
The campaign seeks to position healthier choices as an alternative to traditional sugary treats without compromising on taste or celebration. It will be rolled out across the brand’s digital channels.
The company has also introduced an Assorted Coffee Gift Set featuring zero-added-sugar flavoured coffee premixes, a reusable organiser box and a complimentary frother. Founded in 2026, Sorry Sugar sells its products through its website and leading direct-to-consumer and quick-commerce platforms.

articles.title: Rogers limits auto pay discount to Rogers credit cards, pre-authorized debit
articles.text:
Rogers has changed how customers can get its Automatic Payments discount.
The discount now requires using either a Rogers Bank credit card or a pre-authorized debit card for automatic payments. While this applies to new customers, existing customers will also have to change if they make adjustments to their plan.
A screenshot of an email posted to the r/rogers subreddit, shows the telecom giant asking customers to update their payment method following a plan change.
Notably, a Rogers support page offers some additional information about the auto-pay discount, noting that customers who already receive the discount on an eligible payment method and don’t change their plan should keep the existing discount. However, customers who make changes after July 23, 2026 (for home services) or Sept. 15, 2026 (for mobile) will need to adjust their payment method to continue receiving the discount.
Rogers clarified in an email to MobileSyrup that it’s emailing customers who changed their plan, and the email shared in the Reddit post is one such case. Further, the November deadline in that email is specific to that customer.
You can still use other payment methods like your regular credit cards or direct deposit — but you won’t get the Automatic Payments discount.
This comes right as Rogers posted a notice on its support site that it will start charging a 1.6 per cent credit card processing fee on Jan. 17, 2027. Convenient, as the Rogers Bank credit card is now the only discount-eligible credit card that can be used for payments.
Interestingly, Rogers also announced in August that it would replace the 1.5x cash back rewards redemption for eligible Rogers purchases with the ability to earn five per cent cash back rewards on eligible Rogers purchases (starting Nov. 18, cash back rewards will be valued at a rate of 1 point per $0.01 spent), adding insult to injury.
To summarize all of this, Rogers is now making customers who want the Automatic Payments discount switch over to its own Rogers Bank credit card to get a discount. Worse, the card’s cashback benefits are now significantly reduced thanks to the slashed features and new processing fee.
Or you could use a pre-authorized debit card, but I don’t really trust giving Rogers pre-authorized access to my debit card.
Update Oct. 28, 2026, at 6:41 p.m. ET: Added some additional clarification from Rogers and fixed a few typos.

articles.title: Buying Laptops for a Team: Why Standard Models Beat Letting Everyone Pick Their Own - Tech Guide
articles.text:
In today’s fast-paced business environment, equipping your team with the right technology is crucial for productivity and efficiency. When it comes to purchasing laptops for a team, many organizations face a common dilemma: should each employee choose their own device, or should the company standardize on a single model?
While offering freedom of choice might seem appealing and empowering, standardizing laptop models often proves to be the smarter decision. This article explores the key reasons why standard models outperform a free-for-all approach and how it benefits your business in the long run.
Choosing laptops for a team is more than just picking devices-it’s about creating a cohesive, manageable, and secure IT ecosystem. The decisions made at this stage impact not only the immediate user experience but also support costs, security posture, and operational efficiency. In fact, a study by IDC found that companies that implement hardware standardization experience a 30% reduction in IT support costs within the first year.
Streamlining IT Support and Maintenance
One of the most significant advantages of standardizing laptops is the simplification of IT support and maintenance. When every employee uses the same model, IT teams can create streamlined processes for troubleshooting, repairs, and updates. This consistency reduces downtime and helps technicians resolve issues more quickly.
For example, Computers Made Easy’s tech support model highlights how a uniform hardware setup allows support teams to efficiently manage devices, reducing the complexity of their workflows. This approach not only saves time but also cuts costs associated with managing multiple configurations and compatibility issues.
According to a report by Spiceworks, 80% of IT professionals stated that device standardization improves support efficiency and reduces helpdesk tickets. 
When every laptop is identical, IT staff can maintain a single image for operating systems and software deployment, reducing the number of variables that cause technical issues. This homogeneity enables faster rollouts of updates and patches, lowering the risk of security vulnerabilities caused by inconsistent software versions.
Moreover, having a standard laptop model simplifies training for IT personnel. Support teams don’t need to master multiple device types or configurations, which increases their proficiency and reduces the learning curve for new hires.
Cost Savings Through Bulk Purchasing
Another compelling reason to standardize laptop models is cost savings. Buying the same laptop in bulk often allows companies to negotiate better prices and receive volume discounts from manufacturers or suppliers. This advantage can be substantial, especially for larger teams.
Moreover, having a uniform fleet simplifies warranty management and replacement parts inventory. Instead of stocking multiple types of components, IT departments only need to maintain a limited range of spare parts, which can lower inventory costs and accelerate repairs.
Research from TechRepublic shows that organizations with standardized hardware save up to 20% on procurement and maintenance costs annually.
Bulk purchasing also provides leverage when negotiating service agreements or extended warranties. Vendors are often more willing to offer favorable terms when dealing with a single, consistent order rather than a fragmented set of devices. This can translate into longer warranty periods, faster replacement services, or bundled support plans.
Furthermore, standardization reduces the hidden costs associated with device diversity, such as increased training and administrative overhead. When employees use different laptops with varying capabilities, IT must spend extra time configuring and supporting each model, which adds to labor costs.
Enhancing Security and Compliance
Security is a top priority for businesses today. Managing a diverse range of laptops with different operating systems, software versions, and hardware configurations makes it challenging to maintain consistent security protocols. Standard models simplify the implementation of security policies, making it easier to deploy patches, updates, and antivirus solutions uniformly.
With standardized devices, companies can enforce encryption, endpoint protection, and network access controls more effectively. This consistency also aids in meeting compliance requirements, which often mandate strict control over device configurations and software versions.
Cranston IT’s technical expertise emphasizes the importance of technical expertise in ensuring that security measures are properly integrated into standardized hardware, reducing vulnerabilities and protecting sensitive data.
A survey by Ponemon Institute found that 62% of data breaches are linked to endpoints such as laptops and mobile devices, underscoring the importance of consistent security management. 
Standardization allows IT teams to rapidly deploy security patches across all devices, minimizing the window of exposure to threats. Additionally, uniform hardware configurations mean security tools can be optimized for a single platform, improving their effectiveness.
Compliance with regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI-DSS often requires detailed control and documentation of endpoint security. Standardized laptops make it easier to audit systems and demonstrate adherence to these standards.
Improving Collaboration and User Experience
When everyone uses the same laptop model, collaboration becomes smoother. Team members share a common user experience, making it easier to assist one another with technical issues or software usage. Training sessions are also more effective because the instructor can focus on a single platform rather than multiple variations.
Standardization can enhance productivity by minimizing compatibility problems. For example, certain specialized software may run optimally on specific hardware, and having a uniform setup ensures all employees can use these tools without interruption.
A unified environment also fosters better communication within teams. When sharing files, troubleshooting issues, or collaborating on projects, employees can rely on consistent performance and capabilities. This reduces frustration and supports seamless teamwork.
Moreover, standardized laptops facilitate easier integration with company-wide collaboration tools and cloud services. IT departments can ensure that all devices meet minimum requirements for software like video conferencing, project management, or virtual desktops, leading to a more reliable user experience.
Simplifying Asset Management and Lifecycle Planning
Managing company assets is far easier when laptops are standardized. IT departments can track inventory, assign devices, and schedule upgrades more efficiently. Predictable replacement cycles allow better budget planning and reduce the risk of unexpected expenses.
Additionally, uniform hardware facilitates easier deployment of new software or operating system upgrades, as testing can be done on a single model rather than multiple devices.
Standardization also supports sustainability initiatives by simplifying recycling and disposal processes. When devices are consistent, companies can partner with vendors to implement take-back or refurbishment programs more effectively.
According to Gartner, companies that standardize their hardware experience 25% less downtime related to hardware failures, which translates to higher overall productivity. 
Addressing Employee Preferences
A common argument for letting employees pick their own laptops is that it boosts satisfaction by catering to personal preferences. While this may hold some truth, it often comes at the expense of the benefits outlined above.
Companies can balance employee needs by choosing a few standardized models that cover different use cases-such as lightweight laptops for mobile workers and powerful machines for design teams. Offering limited choices within a standardized framework can satisfy individual preferences without sacrificing the advantages of uniformity.
Another approach is to provide standardized laptops with configurable options like RAM or storage upgrades. This allows some degree of customization while maintaining a controlled environment.
It’s important to communicate the rationale behind standardization to employees, highlighting how it benefits their productivity and security. Involving team leads or representatives in the selection process can also increase buy-in and satisfaction.
Conclusion
Purchasing laptops for a team is a strategic decision that impacts operational efficiency, security, and cost management. While allowing every employee to pick their own device might seem like a way to increase satisfaction, the benefits of standardizing on specific laptop models are clear. From streamlined IT support and significant cost savings to enhanced security and simplified asset management, standard models help businesses stay agile and focused.
By adopting a thoughtful, standardized approach to technology procurement, organizations can ensure their teams are equipped with reliable, secure, and cost-effective tools that enhance productivity and collaboration.
Making the right choice now will pay dividends in the future-both for your IT department and your entire workforce. Standardizing laptops is not just an IT decision; it’s a business strategy that supports growth, innovation, and resilience.

articles.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
articles.text:
United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company’s 2026 launch schedule into oblivion.
The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval.
The launch is critical for ULA after its new flagship rocket suffered nozzle failures on its solid rocket boosters on two of its first four missions, most recently during a flight in February. In both cases, the rocket overcame the nozzle failure and completed its mission, but officials at the US Space Force, ULA’s primary customer, lost confidence in Vulcan.
Space Force officials will closely scrutinize Vulcan’s return-to-flight mission. The Pentagon has entrusted ULA’s Vulcan rocket for roughly half of its major launches through the early 2030s. The Space Force certified the Vulcan rocket for national security launches in 2025, then flew two missions on Vulcan before its grounding after the February booster incident.
Making strides
In a statement, United Launch Alliance said engineers “made great strides” in understanding the booster anomaly that occurred in February. Engineers “have identified several potential contributors, which have been mitigated through design and process improvements to the nozzle,” ULA said.
“To support our customers, this upcoming launch will utilize the improved nozzle design, and additional testing and analysis will continue in parallel with the mission,” ULA said. “By flying the improved design, ULA gains valuable flight data that validates these improvements and is the most beneficial path in support of all our customers.”

articles.title: Tesla abandonne le Cybertruck et annule toutes les précommandes dans deux pays
articles.text:
Le 21 novembre 2019, Tesla dévoilait en grande pompe le Cybertruck. Peu de temps après, le constructeur automobile a ouvert les précommandes pour l’Australie et la Nouvelle-Zélande. Une seule condition pour les habitants de ces deux régions : verser un acompte de 150 dollars australiens. Seulement voilà, ils ne recevront jamais le pickup signé Tesla.
Tesla annule les précommandes du Cybertruck dans deux pays via un simple mail
Ce 23 octobre 2026, les Australiens et Néo-Zélandais qui avaient réservé un Cybertruck ont été avertis par Tesla que leur précommande avait été tout bonnement annulée. Dans un mail, le constructeur automobile explique : « Après mûre réflexion, le projet de produire le Cybertruck pour l’Australie et la Nouvelle-Zélande a été abandonné. Nous ne sommes donc pas en mesure d’honorer votre réservation, qui sera annulée ». L’acompte de 150 dollars australiens leur sera donc remboursé. Par ailleurs, ils pourront bénéficier d’un an de FSD (la conduite assistée de Tesla), à condition d’acheter à la place une Model 3 ou une Model Y neuve. Les Australiens et Néo-Zélandais concernés auront donc attendu près de 7 ans pour finalement apprendre que les précommandes sont annulées.
Pour rappel, le Cybertruck n’a jamais été adapté aux pays qui roulent à gauche. Tesla aurait pu le faire, mais cela aurait impliqué d’adapter une grande partie de la chaîne de production. En réalité, l’annulation des réservations du Cybertruck en Australie et en Nouvelle-Zélande témoigne une nouvelle fois du fiasco industriel que représente ce véhicule.
Une nouvelle déroute pour le Cybertruck
Un an après son lancement, le Cybertruck s’est vendu à seulement 40 000 exemplaires. Les ventes ont ensuite dégringolé d’année en année, atteignant 7 133 unités vendues entre janvier et mai 2026. Les prix à la revente ont eux aussi fortement chuté, témoignant d’un désintérêt pour le véhicule.
Il semble donc que le Cybertruck restera cantonné à quelques pays : les États-Unis, le Canada, la Corée du Sud ou encore les Émirats arabes unis. Le véhicule est par ailleurs utilisé par les services de secours kazakhs pour parcourir les zones montagneuses du pays. Bien entendu, Elon Musk continuera certainement à acheter ses propres véhicules pour les déployer au sein de ses différentes entreprises. Une homologation du véhicule en Europe n’est d’ailleurs pas prévue, et autant dire que cela a peu de chances d’arriver un jour. Précisons au passage que la Roadster Rocket ne devrait pas non plus arriver sur les routes européennes (et dans les airs du Vieux Continent).

articles.title: Tras el accidente de tren en Urda, este es el plan alternativo de Renfe para viajar en el corredor Madrid-Andalucía
articles.text:
Los trenes de alta velocidad entre Madrid y Andalucía están suspendidos desde la desastrosa colisión del miércoles entre un AVE de Renfe y un tren de Iryo cerca de Urda, Toledo. Un accidente que se ha cobrado al menos la vida de 68 personas y 107 heridos, según la última información. Entre las medidas alternativas planteadas por los operadores existen transbordos ferroviarios parciales, cambios de billetes gratuitos y un plan que Renfe promete para este viernes.
Accidente mortal. Adif suspendió el tráfico de alta velocidad en el corredor Madrid-Andalucía tras el accidente, que ocurrió alrededor de las 8:54 del miércoles en el punto kilométrico 118, según El Español. Fuentes de Adif explican que aún no se ha determinado la causa, más allá de la caída del servicio LZB y las preguntas sobre por qué el Centro de Control dio luz verde a que el AVE prosiguiera la marcha si había además un tren Iryo parado en el mismo cantón.
La reapertura tampoco tiene fecha, pues según apuntan desde El Diario de Madrid, depende de los trabajos de emergencia y de las comprobaciones técnicas para certificar que la infraestructura es segura.
El plan de Renfe. Lo que se sabe hasta ahora y lo que se promete para el viernes:
- Ahora. Renfe está operando trenes especiales entre Madrid, Ciudad Real y Puertollano, lo que añade aproximadamente una hora y media al trayecto, según desde Información Cuenca. Los viajeros que vayan o vengan de Puertollano deben hacer transbordo en Ciudad Real, y algunas salidas utilizan un autobús para el último tramo.
- A partir del viernes 30 de octubre. Renfe ha anunciado un "plan alternativo de transporte" para el corredor Madrid-Andalucía. Según cuentan desde Voces de Cuenca, estará operativo mientras el tráfico de alta velocidad permanezca interrumpido. Renfe aún no ha confirmado si combinará tren y carretera, a qué ciudades andaluzas dará servicio ni cuánto más durarán los trayectos, así que queda esperar.
Qué pasa con tu billete. Renfe ofrece cambios y cancelaciones gratuitos para los billetes afectados, todo gestionado desde sus canales oficiales. También ha bloqueado las ventas en esta línea hasta diciembre, según comparten desde El Diario de Madrid. De momento la recomendación es no acudir a una estación con una reserva que hayas hecho previamente y comprobar primero en qué estado se encuentra la línea.
Los demás operadores. Más de lo mismo para el resto de operadores:
- Ouigo. Ha suspendido todos los servicios Madrid-Andalucía al menos hasta el lunes 2 de noviembre incluido y promete reembolsos íntegros, según comparten desde El Diario de Madrid.
- Iryo. También cancelan todos sus servicios entre Madrid-Andalucía y avisan de que no hay previsión, de momento, de que su línea se restablezca. Al igual que los otros operadores, ha habilitado cambios y anulaciones gratuitas para los afectados.
- Iberia. Ha añadido 520 plazas para el miércoles y topado las tarifas desde y hacia Andalucía a 99 euros en clase turista y 149 euros en business hasta el 8 de noviembre.
- Air Europa. Añade un vuelo diario a Málaga y Sevilla, con espacio para dos más a Sevilla.
- Autobuses. varias empresas de transporte han ampliado capacidad en sus rutas Madrid-Andalucía, entre ellas Socibus, Avanza, Samar e Interbus.
El precedente de Adamuz. Tras el accidente de enero, Renfe también aplicó un plan de sustitución, y la línea permaneció cerrada durante aproximadamente un mes, reanudándose el 17 de febrero. Eso no predice el calendario de Urda, pero sugiere que va para largo. Además, la huelga de maquinistas de Cercanías hoy podría complicar aún más el acceso a los transbordos de Atocha.
