articles.title: Fortinet plunges 26% after-hours and takes Tenable with it as Gen Digital rises - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Fortinet plunges 26% after-hours and takes Tenable with it as Gen Digital rises
A better-than-expected third quarter did nothing to stop shares in network security company Fortinet Inc. from falling about 26% in after-hours trading today.
Tenable Holdings Inc., which also topped forecasts, was caught in the selloff that followed across cybersecurity stocks. Shares in consumer security company Gen Digital Inc. rose instead, after its own results came in ahead of expectations.
For its third quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, Fortinet reported adjusted earnings of 91 cents per share, up from 74 cents a year earlier, on revenue of $2.08 billion, up 20% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting 86 cents per share on revenue of $2.06 billion.
Product revenue, which tracks demand for the company’s FortiGate firewalls, rose 37%, to $765 million. Services grew more slowly, up 13% at $1.31 billion, while billings climbed 29% to $2.34 billion. Fortinet posted unadjusted net income of $635.5 million against $473.9 million a year earlier, and free cash flow came in at $865 million.
Business highlights in the quarter included the August acquisition of artificial intelligence runtime protection startup Virtue AI Inc. for an undisclosed sum Fortinet described as immaterial. The startup’s runtime protection and automated validation tools complement Fortinet’s existing FortiAIGate product. FortiEndpoint also picked up new controls in July that track employee use of AI tools and stop sensitive data from leaking into them.
Founder and Chief Executive Ken Xie said in the company’s earnings release that demand was broad enough for Fortinet to raise its billings guidance “for the third time this year.” As AI opens up new attack surfaces, he argued, “Network security remains the critical foundation of AI security.”
Fortinet expects fourth-quarter revenue of $2.155 billion to $2.245 billion, billings of $2.775 billion to $2.925 billion and adjusted earnings of 93 to 95 cents per share. Full-year revenue guidance moved up to $8.125 billion to $8.215 billion from $8.02 billion to $8.18 billion previously. Billings are now forecast at $9.568 billion to $9.718 billion for the year and adjusted earnings at $3.54 to $3.58 per share.
With the share price having more than doubled this year going into the report, investors behind the after-hours slide “appear to be hung up on revenue growth and guidance,” according to Benzinga. Sales growth had been running at 26% as recently as the second quarter, against 20% this time.
Fortinet also cut its full-year service revenue forecast to $5.15 billion to $5.17 billion from the $5.18 billion to $5.22 billion it gave three months earlier. Palo Alto Networks Inc., CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. and Zscaler Inc. all gave up 6% to 7% after-hours as well.
Tenable
Exposure management company Tenable posted adjusted earnings of 63 cents per share in its third quarter, up from 42 cents a year earlier, on revenue of $276.4 million, up 9.5% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting 51 cents per share on revenue of $271.6 million.
Unadjusted net income rose to $11.3 million from $2.3 million and free cash flow was $64.2 million. Tenable signed 413 new enterprise platform customers in the quarter, and buybacks ran to $223.8 million for 6.8 million shares, most of them tied to an upsized $800 million convertible notes offering.
Anthropic PBC’s Claude Mythos model now powers Tenable One Adversary View, a feature inside Tenable’s exposure management platform that surfaces hidden attack paths and how to remediate them. Co-Chief Executive Steve Vintz said in the earnings release that the quarter exceeded “every one of our guided metrics.”
Fourth-quarter guidance calls for revenue of $277 million to $280 million and adjusted earnings of 56 to 58 cents per share, against the 50 cents analysts had modeled. Tenable raised its full-year revenue outlook to $1.084 billion to $1.087 billion from $1.075 billion to $1.081 billion, and its adjusted earnings outlook to $2.16 to $2.19 per share from $1.95 to $2.
None of that spared the stock, which closed the regular session flat and then gave up more than 5% in extended trading.
Gen Digital
Gen Digital, the company behind the Norton, Avast and LifeLock consumer security brands, reported adjusted earnings of 74 cents per share, up from 62 cents a year earlier, on revenue of $1.37 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting 72 cents per share on revenue of $1.34 billion.
Bookings rose 10%, to $1.35 billion, and unadjusted net income more than doubled to $287 million. Customer numbers reached a record, according to Chief Executive Vincent Pilette, who called the period Gen’s “sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit bookings growth.”
Gen now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $5.465 billion to $5.515 billion, up from $5.375 billion to $5.475 billion, and adjusted earnings of $2.93 to $2.98 per share, up from $2.87 to $2.97. Analysts had been looking for $5.44 billion in revenue for the year. Third-quarter guidance is for revenue of $1.365 billion to $1.39 billion and adjusted earnings of 73 to 75 cents per share.
Gen Digital shares gained almost 6% after hours.

articles.title: Cet aspirateur robot laveur haut de gamme devient plus attractif avec cette réduction de 400 euros
articles.text:
Pour rendre l'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni plus attractif, Boulanger retire 30 % au prix de l'engin. L'occasion d'acheter un appareil qui s'occupe intégralement de vos sols sans que vous n'ayez à lever le petit doigt.
L'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni est un aspirateur robot haut de gamme. Il possède une puissance d'aspiration de 22 000 Pa, boostée par la technologie Blast. Côté nettoyage, les jets croisés facilitent l'élimination des taches tenaces. Enfin, la station de lavage se charge de l'entretien. Logiquement, toutes ces qualités ont un prix qui dépasse les 1 200 euros avant l'entrée en scène de Boulanger qui retire 400 euros au prix de ce produit.
Sur le site de Boulanger, l'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni passe de 1 298 euros à 999 euros
Pourquoi choisir l'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni ?
- Un engin passe-partout : Avec sa brosse extensible, le robot accédera aux coins et pourra passer sous certains meubles. Pour compléter ce nettoyage, un système anti-enchevêtrement est présent pour éviter que les poils et les nœuds ne s'enroulent autour de la brosse.
- Un nettoyage poussé : Avant de passer à la serpillère, l'engin d'Ecovacs diffuse un jet pour pré-dissoudre les taches afin de les éliminer plus facilement lorsque le robot passera dessus.
- Une station de lavage qui s'occupe de tout : Une fois que l'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni aura terminé ses missions, il rentre dans sa station de lavage. Comme son nom l'indique, celle-ci se charge d'entretenir les serpillères, mais aussi de vider les différents bacs.
Une prise en main en un claquement de doigt
Pour configurer l'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni, tout se passe dans l'application où le robot effectuera un premier passage afin de cartographier votre intérieur. En attendant, vous pourrez vous arrêter sur la station de lavage. Vous verrez ainsi que vous n'aurez que peu d'entretien à effectuer sur ce robot. La station va vider les poussières récoltées, changer l'eau et nettoyer les serpillères.
Le temps de remarquer tout ça, le robot devrait avoir finir de faire le tour de votre intérieur. Si besoin, vous pourrez modifier cette cartographie parce qu'il n'est pas impossible que certaines erreurs aient été effectuées par le robot. Également, il sera possible de définir des zones interdites et de programmer les heures de passage.
Un aspirateur à la pointe de la technologie
En action, l'engin d'Ecovacs se présente avec une puissance d'aspiration de 22 000 Pa. À première vue, le Deebot X12 Pro Omni ne se situe pas parmi les cadors du domaines, mais Ecovacs pallie ce défaut grâce à la technologie Blast. Grâce à son fort débit d'air, le robot absorbe tout ce qui traîne par terre et la technologie anti-enchevêtrement évite l'emmêlement des poils et des cheveux.
L'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni se démarque sur un autre point : son nettoyage des sols. Ce robot ne se contente pas de passer sur les taches pour les éliminer. Au préalable, l'appareil diffuse des jets croisés à haute pression pour pré-dissoudre les taches.
Pour atteindre les zones les plus difficiles d'accès, le robot possède une brosse extensible pour passer le long des rainures ou sous certains meubles.
✅ Les points forts
- Cinq heures d'autonomie
- Un bras extensible et un système anti-enchevêtrement
- Des jets croisés pour pré-dissoudre les taches
❌ Les limites
- Une puissance d'aspiration de 22 000 Pa qui ne se situe pas parmi les cadors du domaine
- Une cartographie qui reste perfectible
En ce moment, l'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni est disponible pour 999 euros au lieu de 1 298 sur le site de Boulanger
Malgré cette réduction de Boulanger, l'Ecovacs Deebot X12 Pro Omni reste un aspirateur robot onéreux, mais ce prix est justifié par l'ensemble de technologies qu'il emporte
Évidemment, si vous souhaitez avoir un aspirateur robot sans vous ruiner, c'est possible puisqu'Ecovacs propose d'autres références à un prix plus attractif.

articles.title: Aus religiösen Gründen: Erster US-Universitätsmitarbeiter bekommt Ausnahme von KI-Zwang
articles.text:
Aus religiösen Gründen: Erster US-Universitätsmitarbeiter bekommt Ausnahme von KI-Zwang
Der Einsatz von KI erhitzt seit Längerem die Gemüter. Die einen sorgen sich um Cybergefahren oder kritisieren den KI-bedingten Stellenabbau. Andere fragen sich, welche Auswirkungen die neue Technologie konkret auf das menschliche Denken hat. Zu ihnen gehört David Durman. Er arbeitet als Verwaltungsmitarbeiter an der University of Kentucky und bezeichnet sich selbst als Humanist. Wie Religion News berichtet, hat er jetzt eine religiös begründete Ausnahmegenehmigung erhalten, die ihn vom KI-Einsatz befreit.
KI nicht mit Humanismus vereinbar?
Immer mehr Menschen müssen sich am Arbeitsplatz mit neuen KI-Tools auseinandersetzen. Oft sollen sie Prozesse beschleunigen und so die Produktivität steigern. Als die University of Kentucky ihre Mitarbeiter:innen aufforderte, KI in ihre Arbeitsabläufe zu integrieren, machte sich Durman Sorgen. Er hatte das Gefühl, er solle sein Denken in der täglichen Arbeit an einen Chatbot auslagern. Das empfand er als Verstoß gegen seine Überzeugungen.
„Der Prozess und die Arbeit, die damit verbunden sind, Situationen zu durchdenken – im Rahmen meiner Arbeit, meiner Ethik und der Art und Weise, wie ich mit anderen Menschen umgehe – sind ein wesentlicher Bestandteil meiner Entwicklung zu einem moralischen Menschen“, erklärte er im Interview mit Religion News. „Und diese Arbeit auszulagern, unabhängig davon, ob sie anstrengend ist oder nicht, untergräbt meine Fähigkeit, moralisch zu handeln.“
Mithilfe der American Humanist Association beantragte er eine Ausnahmeregelung gemäß eines Bundesgesetzes, das es Beschäftigten erlaubt, Änderungen ihrer Arbeitsanforderungen zu beantragen, um ihren religiösen Überzeugungen gerecht zu werden. Im September stimmte die Universität zu: Durman muss jetzt keine KI mehr für seine Arbeit einsetzen. Vertreter:innen der American Humanist Association gehen davon aus, dass Durman der erste Humanist ist, der eine solche KI-Ausnahmeregelung erzielen konnte.
Wie KI das kritische Denken untergräbt
Durman ist nicht der Einzige, dem es widerstrebt, sein Denken an eine KI auszulagern. Zuletzt forderten zahlreiche Mathematiker:innen in der neugegründeten Association for Human Mathematics, die Disziplin solle in menschlicher Hand bleiben. Kurz zuvor hatte OpenAI auf einen Schlag 722 Fachartikel veröffentlicht. Sie beweisen oder widerlegen mathematische Probleme, an denen Wissenschaftler:innen bisher gescheitert waren. Der Verband argumentiert, mathematischer Fortschritt erfordere menschliches Fachwissen, das durch sorgfältiges Denken entstehe. Die automatisierte Produktion und Rezeption von Mathematik untergrabe daher die intellektuellen Grundlagen des Fachgebiets.
Die Sorge, KI könne das Urteilsvermögen beeinträchtigen, ist nicht unbegründet. Laut einer Studie von Microsoft und der Carnegie Mellon University könnten Menschen, die sich zu sehr auf KI verlassen, die Fähigkeit verlieren, kritisch zu denken. Die Forscher:innen befragten 319 Personen, die beruflich Daten oder Informationen auswerten, zu ihren KI-Gewohnheiten. Sie beobachteten: Je stärker die Nutzer:innen von den Fähigkeiten der KI überzeugt waren, desto eigenständiger ließen sie die KI arbeiten. Dadurch könne eine übermäßige Abhängigkeit von KI-Tools ohne nachträgliche Prüfung entstehen.
Auch Papst Leo XIV. äußert sich kritisch
Durman geht sogar noch einen Schritt weiter. Er befürchtet, dass KI die Gesellschaft auf schädliche Weise beeinflussen könnte. Als Humanist glaube er an die Bedeutung der menschlichen Entfaltung: „Auf gesellschaftlicher Ebene denke ich, dass der Einsatz von KI-Technologie dem zuwiderläuft.“ Auch Papst Leo XIV. hatte sich zuvor ähnlich geäußert. In seiner Enzyklika warnte er Anfang dieses Jahres, dass KI die Demokratie und die Menschenwürde schwächen könnte. Bei Missbrauch könnten KI-Tools einer kleinen Elite zudem zusätzliche Macht verleihen, während der Rest der Menschheit zurückbleibe.

articles.title: 3 Ways AI Agents Already Operate in Your Browser
articles.text:
Which AI agents can act inside your employees' browsers today? If an agent started browsing this morning, would you know it wasn't the employee? Most security teams can't answer those questions yet. That's not a failure of effort. It's a sign of how quickly AI moved from answering questions to taking action.
AI agents now operate browsers inside authenticated applications, and they get there in different ways: debugging interfaces, extensions, agentic browsers, and emerging standards like WebMCP. Each changes what an agent can access, how its actions are attributed, and whether existing controls can see them.
1. Remote Debugging: Applications Controlling the Browser
One way AI agents operate browsers isn't new at all. It's the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
CDP was built to help developers inspect, debug, and automate Chromium-based browsers. It provides programmatic access to navigation, page content, network activity, and user interactions. Tools like Playwright and Puppeteer have used it for years. AI agents use the same approach to navigate websites, extract information, fill forms, and interact with web applications.
The key distinction: automation doesn't have to originate inside the browser. An external application can connect to a browser with debugging enabled and control its tabs. If that browser has authenticated sessions, the automation can use that access.
To most security tools, a browser launched with debugging enabled and signed into corporate applications looks like any other authenticated browser session.
The question to ask: Which applications can launch or connect to debuggable browsers? Do your policies permit this, and which corporate sessions can those applications access?
2. AI Extensions and Agentic Browsers
The second approach puts the agent directly inside the browser.
Extensions such as Claude in Chrome can read pages, switch tabs, click buttons, and complete multistep workflows. This requires powerful permissions, including scripting, tab access, and the debugger API. These permissions enable the functionality but also expand what the extension can access.
Agentic browsers like Perplexity Comet and ChatGPT Desktop go further, building AI directly into the browsing experience. These capabilities aren't necessarily governed by extension permissions, so existing extension controls may not apply.
Without an inventory of browsers across your fleet, you may not know which agents are operating. Two risks stand out.
Agents act with the user's identity. When an agent downloads a document or changes an internal application setting, the application sees an authenticated user making an authorized request.
Without additional telemetry, neither the application nor its audit logs may distinguish the agent's actions from the employee's.
Agents treat content as input. A browser displays a page for someone to interpret. An agent reads that page and decides what to do next. This introduces prompt injection risks, where instructions embedded in websites, documents, or emails attempt to redirect its behavior.
The result is software interpreting untrusted content while operating with trusted permissions.
The question to ask: Which AI extensions and agentic browsers are running across your fleet, what access do they have, and can you distinguish their actions from an employee's?
Your security stack sees the login, not the agent
Once an AI agent is inside an authenticated tab, endpoint and network tools lose sight of what it reads and does.
Keep Aware monitors AI activity in the browser and enforces data protection policies before sensitive data leaves the tab.
Request a demo
3. WebMCP: Websites Exposing Tools Directly to Agents
The third approach changes how websites interact with agents.
WebMCP is an emerging web standard developed through the W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group, with contributions from Google and Microsoft. Rather than interpreting pages and simulating clicks, agents can call structured tools exposed directly by websites.
For example, instead of navigating a support portal and filling out forms, an agent could call a tool to create a ticket. Chrome introduced an early preview in 2026, and the specification continues to evolve.
But this introduces a new trust problem. Websites aren't just presenting content. They're defining actions agents can take.
Tool names, descriptions, and input schemas guide what an agent invokes. These definitions come from the website and shouldn't be treated as trusted instructions. A compromised or malicious site could use misleading descriptions or functionality to influence an agent's behavior.
Each tool operates within its website's security context, but agents working across multiple sites can move information between them. The concern isn't just what a tool does, but what data the agent provides when calling it.
The question to ask: What corporate data can agents pass to website tools, where does that data go, and can you control which tools they use?
What This Means for Browser Security
All three approaches share one thing: software is acting on websites with the access tied to a user's browser session.
That's why browser security can't assume a human is behind every click anymore. Endpoint, network, and application controls still matter. But they were built to see processes, traffic, and logins, not what an agent reads, decides, and does inside an authenticated tab. That's the gap.
The goal isn't to stop employees from using AI agents. Agents are going to become a normal part of how work gets done. The goal is to make sure the controls you already expect in the browser keep applying when an agent is the one operating it.

articles.title: Google lanzó sus primeros lentes con Android XR a USD 1.099, 200 dólares menos que la Meta VR Glasses
articles.text:
Google y la empresa Xreal lanzaron las Aura, los primeros lentes con el sistema Android XR, con un precio de USD 1.099 hasta fin de año. El modelo básico costaba USD 1.279 en las reservas de octubre. Las ventas abrieron el 28 de octubre en Estados Unidos, Canadá y Corea del Sur.
Las Aura se presentaron en la Cumbre de Desarrolladores de Android, según Android Authority. Pesan menos de 95 gramos porque el procesador y la batería van en una unidad aparte, del tamaño de un teléfono, conectada por cable. Esa unidad también funciona como panel táctil, según Google.
El modelo de 12 GB de memoria y 256 GB de almacenamiento cuesta USD 1.279 a precio regular y USD 1.099 con la oferta. El de 16 GB y 512 GB cuesta USD 1.499, o USD 1.299 con descuento. Ambos descuentos rigen hasta diciembre, según Notebookcheck y 9to5Google.
Las entregas comenzarán a mediados de noviembre. En Japón, los pedidos abrirán el 2 de noviembre. Google precisó que la compra está limitada a mayores de 18 años. Xreal prevé llegar a más países en 2027.
Un precio que se ubica por debajo de Meta
Meta presentó el 23 de septiembre sus Meta VR Glasses, de unos 100 gramos y con una unidad de procesamiento similar. Costarán USD 1.299,99 y saldrán a la venta en la primavera boreal de 2027, según la compañía. La Aura de entrada queda USD 200 por debajo.
The Verge señaló que la rebaja respecto de los USD 1.279 iniciales posiblemente responda a esa competencia. El medio sostiene que Google y Xreal habrían quedado frente a frente con Meta al mismo precio. Es una interpretación del medio citado, no una explicación de las empresas.
Las dos propuestas se diferencian en el tipo de pantalla. Las Aura usan lentes transparentes, con campo de visión de 70 grados en diagonal, y permiten ver el entorno. Las Meta VR Glasses, según The Verge, tienen lentes oscurecidos por fuera. También advirtió que ese campo de visión no es amplio.
Gemini ve lo que ve el usuario
Google afirma que su asistente Gemini entiende lo que el usuario mira, tanto en la habitación como en las pantallas. Desde el lanzamiento, el usuario puede compartir su vista y Gemini resalta en la imagen el elemento relevante.
Los lentes también pueden duplicar la pantalla de una computadora conectada por cable USB-C, sin instalar programas. Según Google, permiten abrir varias aplicaciones a la vez y usar mini ventanas al caminar. Incluyen más de 150 aplicaciones pensadas para realidad extendida, además de las de Google Play.
Entre los contenidos figuran el canal de la NBA, que permite ver varios partidos a la vez con suscripción, y juegos como Fallout: Factions, según Android Authority. Xreal presentó además un teclado inalámbrico y un control de juegos hecho con GameSir, con un botón dedicado a Gemini.
Google Fotos sumará este año una galería espacial que rodea al usuario con sus recuerdos, según el blog de Google. Las ventas en tiendas de Google y otros comercios están previstas para 2027, según Android Authority.
Los primeros envíos a compradores de Estados Unidos, Canadá y Corea del Sur están previstos para mediados de noviembre, y en Japón las ventas comienzan el 2 de noviembre.
Meta lanza gafas de realidad virtual que hacen llamadas con hologramas
Los usuarios buscan experiencias inmersivas con hologramas, pero suelen rechazar el uso de cascos pesados e incómodos. En respuesta a esta necesidad, Mark Zuckerberg presentó las nuevas Meta VR Glasses durante el evento Connect de la compañía.
Este innovador dispositivo abandona los diseños voluminosos para adoptar, por primera vez, un formato de gafas ligeras. A pesar de su tamaño compacto, logran mantener la sensación de inmersión y presencia gracias a sus pantallas de alta resolución y su capacidad para mostrar el entorno real.
A nivel de funcionalidad, el equipo va más allá del hardware tradicional. Las gafas integran un asistente de inteligencia artificial, ofrecen diversas opciones de entretenimiento y permiten realizar videollamadas utilizando avatares holográficos de cuerpo completo.

articles.title: Galaxy A55 entra na lista de celulares com One UI 9 no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy A55 entra na lista de celulares com One UI 9 no Brasil
Samsung liberou a atualização baseada no Android 17 para o modelo de 2024. Galaxy A37 também recebeu o update.
A Samsung começou a liberar a One UI 9 para o Galaxy A55 no Brasil. Um dos primeiros relatos brasileiros surgiu na noite de terça-feira (27/10), ampliando a distribuição da interface baseada no Android 17 entre os intermediários da marca.
O Galaxy A37 também já recebe a atualização no país. Usuários relatam a chegada do sistema desde a última quinta-feira (22/10), poucos dias depois de modelos como o Galaxy A57, A56, A36 e A27 entrarem na fila.
Um usuário do Samsung Members registrou a chegada da One UI 9 ao Galaxy A55. O aparelho recebeu o firmware A556EXXUIEZJ1, com aproximadamente 2,2 GB. O pacote leva o celular ao Android 17 e inclui o patch de segurança de 5 de outubro de 2026.
A distribuição brasileira para o Galaxy A55 começou cerca de uma semana depois da liberação da One UI 9 para o modelo na Coreia do Sul. A Samsung ainda não publicou um changelog detalhado para essa versão.
A fabricante iniciou a distribuição oficial da One UI 9 em setembro pelos aparelhos mais recentes, como a linha Galaxy S26, e desde então vem expandindo o sistema para gerações anteriores e modelos intermediários.
A One UI 9 traz mudanças visuais, ajustes de desempenho e novos recursos da Galaxy AI. A Samsung destaca novidades como o Now Nudge, que oferece sugestões com base no que aparece na tela, e uma versão mais personalizável do Now Brief.
O recurso Foto Inteligente também recebeu melhorias para edição de imagens. Segundo a Samsung, a disponibilidade dessas funções, porém, varia conforme modelo, idioma e região.
O Galaxy A37 também começou a receber a One UI 9 no Brasil. Usuários do Samsung Members apontam que a atualização começou a aparecer em 22 de outubro. Em 23 de outubro, o sistema chegou ao Galaxy A36, A27, A56 e Z Fold 5.
Para verificar se a atualização já está disponível, basta acessar Configurações > Atualização de software > Baixar e instalar.
A Samsung recomenda manter o aparelho conectado a uma rede Wi-Fi e com bateria suficiente durante o processo. Como a distribuição é gradual, a atualização pode não aparecer logo de cara.

articles.title: Deepgram acquires Pipecat-maker Daily to bolster its voice AI infrastructure | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The voice AI sector is hot, and top players are trying to consolidate their position as more business models come to the fore through partnerships and acquisitions. Deepgram is the latest to make such moves: The company said on Thursday that it is acquiring Daily, the maker and maintainer of one of the most popular open-source voice AI infrastructures, Pipecat.
The companies didn’t disclose the deal amount but said that they will keep Pipecat open-source.
For the uninitiated, Pipecat is a framework that manages voice and video streams along with other pieces in the pipeline, like speech-to-text (STT), large language models, and text-to-speech (TTS) models while reducing latency. Its maker, Daily, provides hosted infrastructure for voice and video calls of any kind.
With Pipecat, Deepgram will likely gain a deeper understanding of real-time voice and video infrastructure.
Daily has raised over $62 million in funding to date from investors such as Tiger Global, Highfield Capital, Nat Friedman, Lachy Groom and Kevin Weil, according to PitchBook data. Earlier this year, Deepgram reached unicorn status with a $130 million Series C round. Incidentally, both companies were in the same Y Combinator batch in 2016.
Kwindla Kramer, Daily’s co-founder, said around the time when GPT-4 came out, the company started experimenting with AI-to-human communication over voice and text, which eventually resulted in the Pipecat framework. He noted that while there has been a lot of acquisition interest, he favored Deepgram’s CEO Scott Stephenson’s commitment to keeping Pipecat open-source forever, and the engineering culture of both organizations matched, giving Daily’s team the freedom to work on different parts of the stack within a bigger organization.
“Scott was super committed to Pipecat being open-source and vendor-neutral forever. I think there is both a personal commitment and commercial driver there. If you sit in the middle of an ecosystem that’s growing very fast, and have many parts of that ecosystem that are genuinely the best from your company, then everything being as open as possible is like a commercial advantage,” Kramer told TechCrunch.
Stephenson said that Deepgram has been wanting to work in open source for a long time, and the company realized that an orchestration framework for agents was a potential area, which drove the decision to partner with Daily.
“We want to open up the ecosystem so everybody can build voice agents. It’s great if you’re using Deepgram models, but I want you to be using the best models for your use case. And if Deepgram notices that we have some ground to catch up on in a certain area for our own models and products, that’s great. We want you to use partners, and then we’ll also work on becoming better in those areas,” he said.
Stephenson said the acquisition lets developers build agents with expressivity and end-to-end speech systems by plugging in different models and a context bus that connects all parts.
For Deepgram, the deal also lets it explore areas beyond voice through Pipecat, as the framework caters to real-time communication in different formats.
“We never thought about Pipecat as a voice toolkit. We thought about it as the toolkit we needed to build this new kind of AI-native software. Because of where we came from, we just always assumed real-time,” Kramer said.
Deepgram is also launching Real-Time Context Standard (RCS), an open protocol for voice agents that it co-developed with the Pipecat team. The protocol defines metadata like context from the audio, like a whisper, instructions for a language model on how it can use those signals, and guidance on how the response should sound.
Voice AI has seen a lot of investment from both the model and the infrastructure sides. Model makers like ElevenLabs, Gradium, and Fish Audio have raised millions of dollars. On the other hand, infrastructure companies like LiveKit and Vapi have raised multi-million-dollar funding rounds this year.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI will be a huge 210 GB download on PS5
articles.text:
Editor's take: Modern gaming is quickly turning into a luxury market for a small number of affluent customers. Hardware is no longer cheap, and it can be hard to find even if you have the means. And when the hardware is there and the requirements are met, publishers are asking players to complete some never-before-seen download jobs just to install that brand-new AAA game on a local setup.
Grand Theft Auto VI is finally launching on November 19, and players should get their machines in order so the new open-world blockbuster lands on a comfortable hardware setup. Storage, apparently, is one of the most important considerations, as the latest Rockstar production will require a massive amount of space to download the whole thing.
According to a recent tip from PlayStation Game Size, Grand Theft Auto VI's download will reportedly amount to 210 gigabytes of assets, maps, and code on PS5.
PGS tracks newer releases on the PlayStation Store, poking around the service's backend to see when something interesting changes. While the installed size is likely to come in under 210 GB, users should be well aware that they will need plenty of free space on their PS5's SSD, and a variable amount of time depending on how good – or bad – their internet connection is.
For now, we don't know whether GTA VI will need a "day-one patch" to perform properly on PlayStation and Xbox consoles. What we do know is that the game will have no physical disc at all (even boxed copies contain only a download code), although Rockstar is certainly trying to entice GTA enthusiasts with a pricey $400 collector's box, game not included, full of plastic gadgets and useless paraphernalia you will soon find on eBay at ten times the original price.
At least GTA VI should justify such a massive download with a lengthy open world and plenty of extra stuff to do beyond the main storyline. Still, Rockstar's game is bound to feed the gigantism syndrome affecting many of today's AAA productions. Worse, unlike "modular" games such as Call of Duty, GTA VI will likely force gamers to download the whole thing regardless.
GTA VI is rumored to land on PC as soon as Q1-Q2 2027, though Rockstar has yet to announce a date, so there is no need to start erasing games from your PC's SSD just yet.
For now, PC gamers can get one of the worst download experiences around with Phantom Blade Zero. S-Game's wuxia action-RPG requires 145 GB of storage to install, and 300 GB for preloading. The game uses the much-maligned Unreal Engine 5, which might explain the optimization issues with asset and update management.

articles.title: Razer Introduces Reclusa Mini 65% Magnetic Gaming Keyboard
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Razer Introduces Reclusa Mini 65% Magnetic Gaming Keyboard
Razer, the leading global lifestyle brand for gamers, today announced the Razer Reclusa Mini 65%, a wireless hot-swappable magnetic gaming keyboard for enthusiasts who care about how every key sounds, feels, and performs.
Built around the philosophy of "Your Board. Your Rules.", the Reclusa Mini 65% combines magnetic switch precision, refined acoustics, and deep customization in a compact 65% form factor that is rewarding from the very first keystroke.The Razer Reclusa Mini 65% joins the Reclusa line with Hall Effect magnetic switches, adjustable actuation, Rapid Trigger, and tri-mode connectivity, for players who want more control over how every key responds.
Barrie Ooi, Head of PC Gaming Division at Razer"We created the Reclusa line for enthusiasts who view their keyboard as something personal. With the Reclusa Mini 65%, we are bringing magnetic switch technology into the Reclusa experience while staying true to what makes the line unique: a great out-of-box experience, rewarding acoustics, enjoyable typing feel, and the freedom to make the board your own through hot-swappable magnetic switches and swappable keycaps."
Tuned Sound. Solid Feel.
Sound and feel come first. The Reclusa Mini 65% delivers from the first key press: a full, clean, clacky sound and a plush bottom-out, no modding required.Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches define the feel, while an IXPE switch foam sheet, PPS plate, lubricated stabilizers and dual-layer silicone dampening add fullness and reduce case resonance. The result is a keyboard that stays enjoyable through long gaming and typing sessions.
Rapid Response. Total Control.
The Reclusa Mini 65% puts the feel of every keystroke in the player's hands. Powered by Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, it delivers a smooth, responsive typing experience, with adjustable actuation from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm so users can tune each key to their own style. Set it light and fast for competitive gaming, or deeper and more deliberate for typing.Rapid Trigger delivers faster repeated inputs, while Advanced Input Control, including Razer Snap Tap, Razer Snap Flex, and Dual-Key press Priority, adds tighter control in fast-paced gameplay. Six onboard profiles keep each setup saved on the board.
Wired Speed. Wireless Freedom.
Ready to play the moment it is plugged in, and ready to adapt when the player is. Tri-mode connectivity lets players choose how to connect: game with low latency over Razer HyperSpeed Wireless (2.4 GHz), switch between up to three devices via Bluetooth, or go wired via USB Type-C for true 8,000 Hz polling.The multi-function dial puts essential controls within immediate reach, allowing players to make quick adjustments without interrupting their gameplay. Brightness, volume, and more can be adjusted without breaking flow, so the keyboard can be set up around how players play, work, and create.
Swap Freely. Make It Yours.
The Reclusa Mini 65% is built to be customized. Preferences change, and so does the way players play and type. The hot-swappable PCB makes it easy to swap in preferred magnetic switches to fine-tune the feel, with the included 2-in-1 keycap and switch puller making it simple.South-facing LEDs keep the keyboard compatible with a wider range of enthusiast keycaps without giving up RGB lighting, while doubleshot ABS keycaps in a tri-tone design stay crisp and fade-resistant. Per-key Razer Chroma RGB lighting with 16.8 million colors lets players match each key to their setup or mood, giving the board a distinctive identity from day one.
One Board. Zero Compromise.
Tuned Sound. Solid Feel: Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches for feel, IXPE switch foam for a fuller sound, plus a PPS plate, lubricated stabilizers, and dual-layer silicone dampening.
- Rapid Response. Total Control: Rapid Trigger, 0.1-4.0 mm adjustable actuation and Advanced Input Control.
- Wired Speed. Wireless Freedom: Razer HyperSpeed Wireless, Bluetooth, and wired, with true 8,000 Hz polling in wired mode.
- Swap Freely. Make It Yours: Hot-swappable PCB, doubleshot ABS keycaps and per-key Razer Chroma RGB via south-facing LEDs.
Reclusa. Taken Further.
The Reclusa Mini 65% represents the next step in the evolution of the Reclusa line.
Following the Reclusa X Mini 65%, the Reclusa Mini 65% expands the line with magnetic switch technology and wireless connectivity, while keeping what defines the series: satisfying acoustics, rewarding typing feel, and meaningful customization.
Whether enjoyed as it comes or transformed over time, it gives enthusiasts the freedom to build a keyboard that is distinctly their own.

articles.title: As US ties fray, Europe plans first undersea cable link to Greenland
articles.text:
The European Union plans to create the first subsea Internet cable directly connecting Europe to Greenland. The Pan-Arctic Cable project could also extend to Canada and eventually link with Japan and South Korea, notably bypassing the United States.
The Pan-Arctic Cable is described as a European Union flagship project in a European Commission joint communication published on October 20, 2026. The policy document describes a new European strategy for the Arctic that supports “a sovereign, secure and resilient submarine cable connection linking Greenland directly to the EU,” while also suggesting that “like-minded partners like Canada” could provide a stepping stone for future cable expansion toward Asia.
“It is interesting that this project is even being considered, because five years ago it would have seemed like not a particularly commercially attractive proposition,” Elisabeth Braw, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative, told Ars. “But the fact that it’s being considered is very much on trend and a sign of our times.”
The project has gained official support after repeated Trump administration attempts to claim Greenland were finally settled through a trilateral security agreement between the United States, Greenland, and Denmark in September 2026. The agreement preserves Greenland’s autonomous territory status within the Kingdom of Denmark while expanding US military access. But relations have grown increasingly strained between the United States and its allies in Europe and Canada since President Trump initiated trade wars with multiple countries and has taken an increasingly pro-Russia stance on the war in Ukraine.
Europe has also been eyeing new Internet cable routes to Asia, because more than 90 percent of communications between Europe and Asia run through undersea cables in the Red Sea, according to TeleGeography. Maintaining such cables has become riskier since open warfare resumed between the Yemeni government and Houthi faction this year, with Houthi forces having fired missiles and drones at commercial ships in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait chokepoint and the broader Red Sea.

articles.title: SK Hynix Reports Record Q3 Results Driven by AI Memory Surge - EE Times
articles.text:
SK Hynix posted third-quarter revenue of 104.62 trillion won (~$78 billion), exceeding 100 trillion won (~$75 billion) for the first time. Operating profit reached a record 83.33 trillion won ($62 billion), with an operating margin of 80%. Net profit was 39.78 trillion won ($30 billion), while net cash expanded to 98.7 trillion won (~$74 billion).
“SK Hynix’s third-quarter results are very significant in terms of hitting record-high earnings and delivering on shareholder value,” MS Hwang, research director at Counterpoint Research, noted. “First and foremost, operating profit beat expectations again, coming in at 83 trillion won [~$62 billion] versus the consensus of 77 trillion won [~$57 billion].”
DRAM pricing jumps to $2/Gb
According to Counterpoint Research, standard DRAM pricing surged from 20 cents to 30 cents per Gb to $2 per Gb, driving financial momentum and expanding the global DRAM market to $200 billion. “The driving force behind this is rising prices,” Hwang said. “Prices that used to sit around 20 to 30 cents per Gb have now soared to $2.” He also argued that HBM4 will see its unit price jump even further to $4 per Gb.
Additionally, Nvidia resolved initial HBM4 bottlenecks. “Over the past few months, the market has been plagued by two major misconceptions and concerns regarding HBM: That SK was facing technical hurdles in supplying HBM4 to Nvidia, and that HBM adoption volumes per chip might decrease,” he added. “As of October, both concerns have proven to be fake alarms or have been largely resolved.”
Supply shortage and long-term agreements
As AI expands into enterprise computing, robotics, and autonomous vehicles, SK Hynix projects a structural memory shortage that will persist through 2030. The issue stems from the manufacturing complexity of 10 nm-class, sixth-generation DRAM, and 321-layer NAND.
To secure revenue, SK Hynix said it has signed long-term agreements (LTAs) with 14 tech giants, covering over 50% of capacity for 2027 to 2028. “Today, more than half of the memory industry’s capital expenditure goes into infrastructure,” Hwang said. “This shift in corporate governance leading to stricter capital discipline could ultimately rewrite the traditional memory business cycle.”
Solidigm IPO canceled and shareholder return program
SK Hynix said it had discontinued its review of a potential U.S. IPO for its flash memory and solid-state drive subsidiary, Solidigm. “The IPO was intended to raise external capital for the expansion of Solidigm’s production facilities,” SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh Jung said. “However, after carefully considering recent financial market conditions and other factors, we concluded that proceeding at this time would not be the best way to achieve the originally anticipated outcome. We have therefore discontinued our review.”
Hwang commented, “The Solidigm IPO raised issues around a dual listing… If the returns aren’t flowing back to shareholders, it’s very difficult to re-rate the stock.” Additionally, SK Hynix unveiled an expanded fiscal year 2026 shareholder return program of 100 trillion won (~$75 billion), including cash dividends over 30 trillion won (~$22 billion) and buybacks exceeding 60 trillion won (~$45 billion), supported by Kioxia investment gains.
Solidigm is currently in talks with the U.S. Commerce Department to invest $45 billion in a new U.S. chip plant, according to a Bloomberg report citing people familiar with the negotiations. Before committing to what would be the first new major flash-memory chip production facility on American soil, Solidigm is seeking U.S. government permission to send equipment to upgrade an existing plant in Dalian, China.
Data center pullback and Samsung catching up
Counterpoint Research warned of risks such as pullbacks in cloud spending. “The single most severe threat would be a scenario reminiscent of 2018, where cloud service providers simultaneously pull back on their order volume,” Hwang said. “We anticipate that Samsung will surpass SK Hynix from the HBM4 generation, leading the market share in 2027.”
SK Hynix management said it expects to preserve its market lead through proprietary packaging and customer partnerships.
See also:
SK Hynix Plans $713B Domestic Investment
SK Hynix’s $4B HBM Project Targets U.S. Chipmaking Gap
SK Hynix Nasdaq Debut Shows Global Memory Expansion Race

articles.title: Les écouteurs filaires à réduction du bruit de Bose sonnent-ils mieux que les EarPods ? Notre réponse
articles.text:
| Construction |  | 
| Poids | 21 g | 
| Câble détachable | Non | 
| Longueur câble | 128 cm | 
| Certification IP | IPX4 | 
| Expérience d'utilisation |  | 
| Connectique | USB-C | 
| Kit mains-libres | Oui | 
| Écoute de l'environnement | Oui | 
Bose intègre un système de réduction du bruit à ses écouteurs filaires, un mariage encore peu courant. Sans batterie dédiée ni Bluetooth, ils ambitionnent de conjuguer la simplicité du câble et l'isolation des nuisances extérieures.
Le retour du filaire ne se limite plus aux produits d'entrée de gamme. Avec ses écouteurs filaires à réduction du bruit, aussi appelés Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds, Bose promet de combiner connexion USB-C et isolation active. Une proposition à contre-courant de la déferlante du “tout sans-fil”, qui reprend l'esprit des QuietComfort QC20 lancés en 2015, mais s'affranchit de l’alimentation externe jusqu'ici nécessaire au fonctionnement de l’ANC.
À l’heure où les écouteurs sans-fil multiplient les fonctionnalités logicielles, ces Bose sont-ils capables de rivaliser malgré une conception aussi spartiate ? Leur réduction du bruit est-elle assez convaincante pour faire oublier leurs cousins sans fil ? Enfin, leur restitution sonore parvient-elle à faire de l'ombre à celle des incontournables EarPods d’Apple ?
Les écouteurs filaires à réduction de bruit Bose sont commercialisés depuis septembre 2026 au tarif de 100 €, déclinés en trois finitions : noir, vert menthe fraîche et blanc nuage.
Ces écouteurs reprennent les codes de leurs ancêtres lancés il y a plus de 10 ans avec des oreillettes imposantes au look des années 2000, volontairement kitsch. Ils partagent toutefois quelques traits avec leurs cousins sans-fil QC Ultra Earbuds (Gen 2), notamment leur forme et leur revêtement brillant de bonne facture.
Sans se revendiquer premium, ils affichent une qualité de fabrication satisfaisante avec un câble épais et des marques d’assemblage discrètes. Intégré à la pièce accueillant le connecteur USB-C, le renfort du câble devrait limiter l’usure due aux frottements dans une poche, un bon point face aux écouteurs filaires d’Apple.
Étonnamment, aucun système ne permet de solidariser les deux câbles, ce qui aurait facilité l’écoute avec une seule oreillette. Enfin, malgré leurs ailettes à l'allure sportive, ces écouteurs se contentent d’une certification IPX4, qui protège des éclaboussures sans garantir une résistance à la sueur.
Dotés de canules longues et fines terminées par des embouts en silicone semi-rigides, ces écouteurs sont de vrais intra-auriculaires. Contrairement aux QC Ultra Earbuds (Gen 2), ils nécessitent une légère rotation dans le conduit auditif pour assurer l’isolation et caler leurs ailettes contre l’antihélix, au prix d’une sensation d’intrusion supérieure.
Le confort dépend de la morphologie et des embouts choisis. Dans notre cas, les embouts M se sont révélés intrusifs et peu étanches, tandis que les L ont assuré un bon maintien, malgré des points de pression ressentis en moins d’une heure.
Comme avec les autres écouteurs filaires à embouts en silicone dont le câble ne passe pas autour de l’oreille, le moindre tiraillement peut compromettre l’isolation et obliger à les réajuster, voire les faire chuter. À l’inverse, les coques semi-ouvertes des EarPods d’Apple, perpendiculaires à la tige et au câble, se bloquent naturellement dans l’oreille lorsque celui-ci est tiré vers le bas.
Pratiquement impossibles à perdre, ces écouteurs n’échappent pas aux contraintes du câble. Celui-ci s’emmêle facilement et frotte contre les vêtements, générant des bruits parasites. Il limite aussi la liberté de mouvement par rapport à des écouteurs true wireless.
Les écouteurs ont beau intégrer un système de réduction du bruit, ils sont aussi simples à utiliser que n’importe quel autre modèle filaire. Ils fonctionnent instantanément une fois branchés à la source, sans bouton de mise sous tension ni boîtier à recharger ni appairage Bluetooth.
En revanche, leur connecteur USB-C empêche de les utiliser avec un appareil équipé d’une sortie mini-jack 3,5 mm. Si l’on tente de les connecter à l’aide d’un adaptateur, ils ne recevront aucun signal, puisqu'ils doivent être alimentés électriquement par la source.
Contrairement au mini-jack, l’USB-C permet à la source de fournir l’énergie nécessaire au fonctionnement de la réduction du bruit. Par rapport au modèle précédent, les écouteurs se passent ainsi du boîtier d’alimentation encombrant intégré au câble, qui devait lui-même être rechargé. Une conception plus moderne et pratique.
En l’absence d’app mobile, ils font malheureusement l’impasse sur les options logicielles proposées par les écouteurs true wireless. Ils présentent toutefois l’avantage d’offrir une latence quasi nulle, un atout pour le gaming. Logé au niveau du connecteur USB-C, le DAC intégré assure la conversion des flux audio jusqu’en 24 bits/48 kHz, quelle que soit la source. Cette résolution n’a rien d’exceptionnel, mais permet d’éviter les aléas d’une sortie analogique, ainsi que les limites des codecs Bluetooth basiques.
Enfin, les écouteurs disposent d’une petite télécommande intégrée au câble. Réactive et dotée de gros boutons bien distincts, elle limite les risques d’erreur de manipulation. Permettant de régler le volume, contrôler la lecture et passer d’une piste à l’autre, elle propose l’essentiel. Le changement de mode d’isolation s’effectue par un appui long sur le bouton central.
Bien que Bose ne précise pas si un système de traitement des bruits ambiants est à l’œuvre, la captation se révèle plutôt convaincante aux abords d’un carrefour bruyant. Notre voix peut sembler légèrement en retrait, mais elle ne saccade jamais et conserve le dessus sur les nuisances. À titre de comparaison, les Apple EarPods captent la voix et les bruits du trafic quasiment sur le même plan.
Les propos restent intelligibles en milieu calme, tandis que le signal dans son ensemble est propre. À noter que le micro sature lorsqu’il est trop proche de la bouche. Il est donc recommandé de l’utiliser à bonne distance.
Ces écouteurs filaires Bose ont pour originalité de posséder un système de réduction du bruit. Celui-ci exploite quatre microphones intégrés aux oreillettes, comme sur les écouteurs sans-fil.
Si l’ANC semble performant à la mesure, il se révèle moins impressionnant en pratique. Surtout efficace autour de 200 Hz avec 30 dB d’atténuation, il réduit bien les ambiances urbaines et les bruits statiques, mais laisse persister les grondements et vibrations les plus profonds.
L’efficacité de l’ANC se dégrade dans la seconde moitié du spectre. Le médium étant trop peu atténué, les moteurs, voix et sons du quotidien restent intelligibles. Dans un open space, les conversations proches sont presque aussi compréhensibles que sans écouteurs. L’isolation passive peu efficace et les fuites intempestives laissent aussi les cliquetis métalliques et les sons stridents bien présents.
En somme, l’ANC de ces écouteurs Bose serait assez médiocre sur le marché des écouteurs sans-fil. Il suffit à s’octroyer un peu de calme dans un environnement contrôlé ou éviter de trop pousser le volume dans les transports en commun, mais pas vraiment plus.
Mettant l’accent sur les fréquences autour de 2 kHz, le mode Transparence permet de tenir une conversation ou de localiser efficacement les sons environnants. Malgré des timbres vocaux peu naturels, les performances restent amplement suffisantes au quotidien.
La marque reste discrète sur l’architecture acoustique des écouteurs, se contentant de mentionner un “son emblématique Bose”. Grâce à leur conception intra-auriculaire qui favorise l’isolation, ils partent avec un avantage de taille face aux Apple EarPods en matière d’extension dans les basses.
Ces écouteurs Bose sont tout à fait capables de rendre justice aux morceaux chargés en sub, là où ceux d’Apple peinent. Ils se permettent même de légèrement flatter les fréquences autour de 40 Hz avant de creuser avec mesure les basses supérieures, offrant ainsi profondeur et impact sans verser dans un caractère boomy. Comme souvent avec Bose, le bas du spectre se distingue par une précision louable, combinant assise confortable et bonne définition.
Là où les QC Ultra Earbuds (Gen 2) ont assagi leur réglage tonal, ces écouteurs compensent la mise en avant des basses en rehaussant généreusement la seconde partie du spectre, en quête d’expressivité. Une bosse dans le haut-médium apporte présence et énergie, tandis qu’un pic à 10 kHz confère un surplus de brillance sans trop exacerber les sibilances.
Bien qu’un peu artificielle et flatteuse, cette signature a le mérite d’être suffisamment dosée pour ne pas introduire de déséquilibre criant ni nuire à l’intégrité de la musique... du moins à volume modéré.
Le problème demeure que l’extrême grave prend un peu le dessus sur les médiums à un niveau d’écoute relativement sage. Ce phénomène incite donc à augmenter légèrement le volume, quitte à exacerber un excès de haut-médium, hélas. Les caisses claires adoptent ainsi rapidement un côté claquant, tandis que les voix deviennent un peu criardes. Cet excès de clarté et d’énergie peut aussi masquer l’assise dans les basses, voire engendrer un rendu trop fin et un manque de corps sur les morceaux déjà creusés dans le bas-médium.
En somme, si ces écouteurs filaires profitent d’une meilleure extension aux extrémités du spectre, les Apple EarPods demeurent plus fidèles dans les médiums. Leur bas-médium plus soutenu favorise une reproduction des voix plus naturelle et un niveau de tranchant plus mesuré. De plus, ces petits écouteurs filaires ne rivalisent pas avec leurs grands frères sans fil QC Ultra Earbuds (Gen 2), infiniment plus équilibrés sur l’ensemble du spectre.
Enfin, notons que les écouteurs donnent le meilleur d’eux-mêmes lorsque l’ANC ou le mode Transparence est activé. En mode d’isolation passive, ils perdent toute leur assise dans les basses fréquences, sans pour autant tempérer leur expressivité débordante.
Dans l’univers du filaire, ces écouteurs Bose marquent des points en associant simplicité d’usage (pas de batterie à recharger, télécommande pratique, latence minimale) et réduction de bruit. Ils se distinguent aussi par leur solidité et leur captation vocale en milieu bruyant. En revanche, le confort reste perfectible, le câble peut gêner le maintien, tandis que l’ANC peine à atténuer les voix et les aigus. Côté son, les basses profondes et la bonne dynamique sont appréciables, mais la mise en avant du haut-médium et des aigus déséquilibre la restitution au-delà de 70 % du volume. Si l’ANC constitue un atout pour les adeptes du câble, ces Bose peinent à justifier leur prix face à certains modèles sans-fil plus abordables.
Lancés à 100 €, ces intras filaires ont pour principaux rivaux les Apple EarPods, facturés à moins de 20 €. Face au modèle californien, Bose propose une réduction du bruit modeste, mais fonctionnelle, des basses plus profondes et une durabilité a priori supérieure. Le format intra-auriculaire de Bose se montre toutefois moins universel, tant sur le plan du confort que du maintien, tandis que sa signature sonore s'avère moins naturelle que celle d’Apple. Face aux EarPods ou à des modèles sans-fil très complets comme les Nothing Ear (a) (désormais proposés à moins de 70 €), ces écouteurs Bose ne se justifient réellement que pour les inconditionnels du câble en quête d’une bulle de tranquillité.
3

articles.title: Your Home Router Is Now a Business Asset: Locking Down the Remote Worker's Setup - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The New Frontier of Business Security
As remote work cements itself as a permanent fixture in the modern business landscape, the traditional boundaries of corporate IT security have expanded dramatically. No longer confined to centralized office networks, business data now frequently flows through home routers and personal internet connections. This shift has transformed the humble home router from a simple networking device into a critical business asset that requires stringent security measures.
The importance of securing home routers cannot be overstated. According to a recent report, 68% of organizations experienced increased cyber threats due to remote work environments in 2023. This surge underscores the pressing need for businesses to reassess how they protect their digital perimeters when employees operate outside traditional office settings.
Moreover, the global increase in remote work has led to a 400% surge in cyberattacks targeting home networks since 2020. These statistics reflect the expanding attack surface that businesses must defend against, highlighting the home router’s newfound role as a frontline defense point.
Understanding the Risk Landscape
Home routers are often overlooked in corporate cybersecurity strategies, yet they represent a significant vulnerability. Unlike enterprise-grade firewalls and security appliances found in office environments, consumer routers may lack advanced security features and are frequently left with default settings or outdated firmware.
This vulnerability is compounded by the fact that many employees use their home networks for both personal and professional activities, increasing the attack surface. Cybercriminals can exploit unsecured routers to intercept sensitive communications, launch man-in-the-middle attacks, or use compromised devices as entry points into corporate networks.
The risks extend beyond just data interception. Attackers can hijack routers to install malware, create botnets, or perform distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks that disrupt business operations. In some cases, attackers have even manipulated router settings to redirect employees to fraudulent websites, leading to credential theft and further network compromise.
To counter these risks, businesses must adopt a comprehensive approach to securing remote work setups. This effort begins with understanding the technical and human factors involved and implementing frameworks that provide clear guidelines and actionable steps.
Implementing a Robust Security Framework
One effective approach is adopting a structured security framework tailored to remote work scenarios. For example, Compass Computer Group’s framework offers a well-defined methodology that addresses the unique challenges of securing home networks used for business purposes. Their framework emphasizes regular firmware updates, strong encryption standards, and network segmentation to isolate business-critical devices from less secure personal gadgets.
Implementing such a framework requires IT departments to collaborate closely with remote employees, ensuring that security policies are not only communicated clearly but also practically enforceable. This includes providing user-friendly guides for configuring routers securely, supplying necessary hardware upgrades if needed, and integrating security checks into routine IT support workflows.
Educating Remote Workers on Security Best Practices
In addition to technical measures, educating remote workers on best practices is crucial. Employees should be trained to change default passwords, disable unnecessary services like remote management, and recognize phishing attempts that often serve as precursors to more sophisticated attacks. Research shows that 95% of cybersecurity breaches are due to human error, underscoring the importance of comprehensive user education.
The Role of Proactive Monitoring and Incident Response
Beyond initial setup and employee training, continuous monitoring and rapid incident response are vital components of a resilient cybersecurity posture. Employing proactive cyber defense by Crestline can help organizations stay ahead of emerging threats by providing real-time threat detection and swift remediation services tailored to remote work environments.
Proactive monitoring tools can identify unusual network traffic patterns, unauthorized access attempts, or firmware tampering-alerts that might otherwise go unnoticed when devices are outside corporate oversight. Incident response teams can then act promptly to isolate compromised devices, mitigate damage, and begin recovery procedures.
Research indicates that organizations with proactive cybersecurity measures reduce the average cost of a data breach by nearly 50%. This statistic highlights the financial and reputational benefits of investing in advanced defense strategies that include vigilant monitoring of remote endpoints such as home routers.
Best Practices for Securing Home Routers
To effectively lock down remote workers’ setups, businesses should implement several best practices:
- Enforce Strong Password Policies: Default router passwords are widely known and easily exploited. Mandating complex, unique passwords is a fundamental step in securing home networks.
- Regular Firmware Updates: Router manufacturers frequently release updates that patch security vulnerabilities. Ensuring devices are kept current helps protect against known exploits.
- Enable WPA3 Encryption: The latest Wi-Fi security protocol, WPA3, offers enhanced protection over its predecessors. Where supported, enabling WPA3 significantly reduces the risk of unauthorized access.
- Network Segmentation: Creating separate networks for business devices and personal use limits the spread of malware and reduces the likelihood of cross-contamination.
- Disable Unnecessary Features: Features such as Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) and remote management can be exploited if left enabled unnecessarily.
- Use VPNs for Business Traffic: Virtual Private Networks encrypt data transmissions, adding an extra layer of security when accessing corporate resources.
- Implement Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Adding MFA to router administration interfaces where possible can prevent unauthorized changes even if passwords are compromised.
- Maintain an Inventory of Devices: Keeping track of all devices connected to the home network helps identify anomalies that could indicate a security breach.
Beyond Technology: Cultivating a Security Culture
Technology alone cannot guarantee security. Cultivating a culture of cybersecurity awareness among remote employees is equally important. Regular training sessions, clear communication of policies, and encouraging reporting of suspicious activity help create an environment where security is a shared responsibility.
Furthermore, leadership must prioritize cybersecurity by allocating resources and setting expectations that reinforce the importance of protecting business assets, including those located outside the traditional office. Studies show that organizations with strong security cultures experience 70% fewer security incidents, demonstrating the tangible benefits of fostering employee engagement in security practices.
Encouraging open dialogue about cybersecurity challenges and successes also empowers employees to take ownership of their role in protecting company data. Gamified training programs, phishing simulations, and incentives for compliance can further enhance engagement.
Future Outlook: Securing the Distributed Workforce
The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in homes adds complexity to securing remote work environments. Each connected device potentially introduces new vulnerabilities. As such, businesses must anticipate future challenges by continuously updating security frameworks and incorporating emerging technologies such as AI-driven threat detection.
Artificial intelligence and machine learning can analyze vast amounts of network data to detect subtle signs of compromise or anomalous behavior that traditional tools might miss. Integrating these capabilities into home network security could revolutionize how businesses protect remote endpoints.
Moreover, regulatory pressures related to data protection and privacy are likely to increase, making compliance an integral part of any security strategy. Regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, and others impose strict requirements on data handling and breach notification, with significant penalties for non-compliance. Organizations that proactively address these evolving demands will not only protect their assets but also gain competitive advantages in trust and reliability.
In addition, the rise of zero-trust security models is reshaping how businesses approach network access. Zero-trust principles assume no device or user is inherently trustworthy, enforcing continuous verification and least-privilege access controls-even for home-based devices. Adopting zero-trust architectures will require businesses to extend these principles to remote work environments, including home routers.
Conclusion
The home router has undeniably become a vital business asset in the era of remote work. Recognizing and addressing the security challenges it presents is essential for safeguarding corporate data and maintaining operational continuity. By leveraging structured frameworks like and engaging services specializing in, organizations can build robust defenses that adapt to the changing landscape.
Investing in secure home network setups, continuous monitoring, and fostering a security-conscious culture are no longer optional-they are prerequisites for thriving in today’s distributed business environment. As remote work continues to evolve, so too must the strategies that protect it. Businesses that take decisive action now will be better positioned to defend their digital assets and ensure long-term success in an increasingly interconnected world.

articles.title: Freshworks acquires Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev
articles.text:
Freshworks acquires Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev
Freshworks said that this acquisition will strengthen Freshservice's capabilities, which is Freshworks’ IT service management platform, in incident management and IT operations.
SaaS major Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev, an incident intelligence engine that uses AI to investigate technology disruptions, identify root causes, and recommend remediation actions.
In a company blogpost, Freshworks said that this acquisition will strengthen Freshservice's capabilities, which is Freshworks’ IT service management platform, in incident management and IT operations. It bridges the gap between deep diagnostic intelligence, IT service management, and modern incident orchestration.
Nasdaq-listed Freshworks did not disclose the financial details of the deal.
Founded by Natan Yellin and Arik Alon, Robusta has been heavily optimised for large scale production environments. For many of its customers, even momentary reliability issues can cause a loss of revenue. Yet operating AI Agents at that scale is challenging because of the volume of alerts and the complexity of their systems. Robusta's technology allows customers use frontier intelligence to investigate their alerts, no matter the volume.
"LLMs are fantastic at troubleshooting incidents," said Natan Yellin, co-founder and CEO of Robusta.
"Our technology lets AI Agents do that effectively in large enterprise environments, where there are so many raw events that investigating each one individually would be exorbitant from a token cost perspective. We're incredibly excited to join Freshworks, which gives us the scale and platform to bring that experience to engineering teams everywhere, while keeping humans firmly in control of decisions that touch production."

articles.title: La flota española de aviones contraincendios tiene un enorme problema: está envejeciendo más rápido de lo que podemos reponerla
articles.text:
Diez mil horas. Eso es lo que acumularon este verano los medios aéreos del Estado contra los incendios de la temporada. Fueron 2.659 salidas y más de 50.000 descargas de agua. Parece mucho y, de hecho, lo es: un 27 % más de horas que en 2025 y un 30% más de salidas. Es más, fueron el doble que la media de la última década.
Y eso que, de los diez anfibios previstos para la campaña, solo pudimos usar ocho. Es decir, hemos comprobado en carne propia algo de lo que el propio Ejército del Aire y del Espacio lleva años avisando: que el fuego cada vez nos pide más, pero nuestra flota empieza a no dar más de sí.
¿Cómo ha sido 2026? Malo. Hasta el 20 de septiembre, España registró 275.154 hectáreas forestales quemadas (2,5 veces la media del decenio 2016-2025) de las que unas 153.000 eran superficie arbolada (4,1 veces la media) y 45 grandes incendios forestales. Faltan hectáreas por sumar, pero muy mal tiene que darse lo que queda de año para que nos acerquemos al récord de terreno de 2025. En fallecidos, con 21 personas, sí que ha sido el peor año en mucho tiempo.
Si 2026 ha sido un año especialmente intensivo en tiempo es por "la concentración de grandes incendios, la elevada demanda de medios de extinción y la complejidad de las emergencias". En 2025 casi todo ardió de golpe y pasamos de unas 42.000 hectáreas a finales de julio a más de 400.000 el 22 de agosto, según el sistema europeo EFFIS. Eso limitó el uso de los recursos disponibles y puede que explique el hecho de que finalmente ardieran más hectáreas.
En 2026 la temporada de incendios empezó antes y fue por oleadas; por eso hemos podido aprovechar los recursos. Es buena noticia, claro; pero tiene consecuencias.
¿Y qué ocurre con los aviones? Que se gastan. Cada hora de vuelo es una hora menos de vida útil. Cada salida significa más revisiones, más mantenimiento y multiplica las averías. Ahora mismo, la flota estatal de anfibios pesados tiene 14 aviones (CL-215T, algunos con más de tres décadas de servicio, y cuatro CL-415, el último recibido en 2016). Hasta 2023, eran 18.
¿Y por qué no compramos más? La respuesta es un poco contraintuitiva: porque no hay donde. Cuando el CL-415 dejó de fabricarse, Canadá se negó a poner su sustituto (el DHC.515) en producción hasta que no hubiera un mínimo de 20 pedidos. España firmó la compra conjunta de la UE en 2024 y eso significa que hasta 2028, como pronto, no empezarán a llegar las primeras unidades.
Si sumamos que hay que formar a las tripulaciones, no parece realista esperar que los nuevos aviones estén volando antes de 2029.
Vamos un poco tarde, ¿no? Sí, efectivamente, vamos un poco tarde. Y no es que nadie lo viera venir. Desde al menos 2018, el Mando de Apoyo Logístico del Ejército del Aire viene pidiendo al ministerio la renovación de la flota.
Por ello, en 2022, Transición Ecológica adjudicó un contrato para modernizar la aviónica (los sistemas electrónicos de vuelo y navegación) de los CL-215T. Sin embargo, este año se dio por extinguido porque, según parece, la empresa encargada de la actualización no tenía ni los manuales técnicos del fabricante.
¿Y entonces? Solo nos queda alquilar. Es algo que ya hacemos, pero la falta de presupuestos (y precios al alza) hace que esta vía sea más complicada.
Todo esto no es más que un recordatorio de que tenemos que repensar la forma de afrontar un tiempo en el que los incendios son amenazas varios órdenes de magnitud más temibles que antes.
Imagen | Chiara Guercio

articles.title: CISA warns of Fragnesia Linux flaw chained in PHP2Shell attacks
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies to patch a high-severity Linux kernel privilege escalation bug that attackers are chaining with the PHP2Shell flaws in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-46300 and known as Fragnesia, this vulnerability stems from a logic bug in the Linux XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem that lets attackers run malicious code with root permissions.
Fragnesia belongs to the Dirty Frag vulnerability class and has a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit that local attackers can use to gain root privileges on major Linux distributions with kernels released before May 13, 2026.
CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Wednesday and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by Saturday 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
The cybersecurity agency didn't share details about ongoing Fragnesia attacks, but it noted that threat actors could chain it with two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), collectively tracked as PHP2Shell, to deploy webshells on unpatched systems.
"This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root," CISA said.
Fragnesia and PHP2Shell exploit chain
While CISA didn't provide more information on attackers chaining the Fragnesia and PHP2Shell flaws, Dream Security analysts said in a Monday report that the vulnerabilities were used to breach more than two dozen servers, including three belonging to a US government-affiliated organization.
"Dream researchers identified a complete attack operation that included a custom weaponization of the PHP2Shell exploit chain (CVE-2026-109618/CVE-2026-109619) paired with the Fragnesia kernel privilege escalation (CVE-2026-46300), target lists, exploitation logs, and approximately 40 custom post-exploitation scripts," they said.
"This included artifacts of a campaign that had rooted 25 servers across the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea. Once rooted, the attacker zeroed in on three specific servers in a US government-affiliated environment."
CISA also added the PHP2Shell flaws to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities on Monday and mandated that Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies secure their networks by Thursday.
While the US cybersecurity agency has not yet provided further details on ongoing PHP2Shell attacks, Perplexity security engineer Adel Karimi confirmed in-the-wild exploitation over the weekend after their honeypots recorded evidence of remote code execution against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26.
A CISA spokesperson couldn't immediately share more information about threat actors potentially chaining Fragnesia and PHP2Shell in attacks when BleepingComputer reached out earlier today.

articles.title: Discord va laisser Google fouiller dans une partie des messages de ses utilisateurs
articles.text:
Au printemps 2024, Discord bannissait les comptes liés à Spy.pet, un site qui aspirait les conversations de quelque 14 000 serveurs pour les revendre, et envisageait des poursuites contre ses opérateurs. Deux ans et demi plus tard, la plateforme ouvre elle-même ses conversations publiques aux moteurs de recherche. Dans un billet publié le 27 octobre, elle annonce que les messages de ses serveurs dits découvrables seront bientôt indexés par Google et ses concurrents.
Ce que Discord met en ligne, et pourquoi
Les serveurs concernés sont ceux que leurs administrateurs ont inscrits dans l’annuaire public de la plateforme (auxquels on accède par le bouton « Découvrir » en bas à gauche de l’interface), soit plus de 63 000 communautés réunissant au moins 1 000 membres et huit semaines d’existence. Chacune recevra dès le 16 novembre une page web publique, posée sur le web ouvert. Les messages de leurs salons publics suivront à partir de la mi-décembre, par vagues, dans les résultats des moteurs de recherche.
Rien d’antérieur à la mi-décembre ne sera repris, un message supprimé disparaît des pages, les pseudonymes et les avatars restent masqués, et les comptes des adolescents sont exclus du dispositif. Un message publié, lui, reste exposé tant que son auteur ne l’efface pas. Ces pages ont déjà été testées sur les serveurs des jeux NBA 2K, Rust et Dead by Daylight, avec des publications venues des seuls administrateurs et modérateurs.
En rendant ses discussions trouvables, Discord court après le modèle qui a fait la fortune de Reddit, dont les fils de conversation truffent les premiers résultats de Google. La plateforme dit vouloir retrouver ce qui faisait la force des forums d’antan, où une solution postée une fois restait trouvable des années. Ses millions de salons, eux, n’ont jamais nourri le moindre résultat de recherche, et les réponses qui s’y échangent chaque jour disparaissent dans le flux.
En Europe, un réglage coupé par défaut, mais pas pour tout
La France fait partie des régions où l’exposition individuelle est désactivée par défaut. Dans l’Union européenne, au Royaume-Uni, au Canada, au Brésil, en Australie et en Corée du Sud, le réglage qui autorise l’affichage des messages d’un membre sur le web est coupé d’office. La plateforme invoque des contraintes légales propres à ces territoires. Partout ailleurs, il est activé d’entrée, à charge pour chacun d’aller le désactiver dans ses paramètres de confidentialité. Les volontaires européens peuvent, à l’inverse, l’allumer depuis le même menu.
Lire aussi : Discord impose finalement la vérification d’âge, 7 mois après sa première tentative
Dès le 16 novembre pourtant, les pages publiques des serveurs afficheront des résumés générés automatiquement à partir des discussions récentes, quel que soit le choix des membres. Seuls les administrateurs peuvent couper cette fonction, depuis les réglages de présence web de leur serveur.
