articles.title: Meilleure eSIM Europe : Comparatif des forfaits eSIM pour l'Europe en octobre 2026
articles.text:
Vacances de la Toussaint, city-trips d'automne, déplacements pros : en octobre, mieux vaut anticiper sa connexion en Europe plutôt que de compter sur le roaming de son forfait. Saily reste notre meilleur choix pour les petits budgets, Ubigi le meilleur rapport qualité/prix et Holafly la référence pour la data illimitée. Voici notre comparatif des 6 meilleures eSIM pour l'Europe, mis à jour en octobre 2026.
Le roaming est gratuit dans l'Union européenne, mais pas sans limites. La plupart des opérateurs français plafonnent les données utilisables à l'étranger (souvent 15 à 25 Go) et brident parfois les débits. Dès que l'on sort de l'UE (Royaume-Uni, Suisse, Balkans, Turquie), la facture peut s'envoler.
L'eSIM de voyage règle le problème : on achète un forfait data en ligne, on scanne un QR code et la connexion est active dès l'arrivée, sans carte physique ni engagement. Elle s'ajoute à votre SIM principale grâce au dual SIM, et vous gardez votre numéro pour les appels et SMS.
Mais les offres diffèrent beaucoup : 28 à 41 pays couverts, data illimitée ou au Go, 5G ou non, prix d'entrée de 2 $ à plus de 7 $. Nous avons comparé six opérateurs, Saily, Ubigi, Holafly, Airalo, GigSky et GoMoWorld, sur la couverture, les tarifs, la qualité du réseau, l'activation et la fiabilité, pour vous aider à choisir selon la durée du séjour, votre consommation et vos destinations.
- Plus de 200 destinations disponibles
- VPN gratuit intégré
- Des forfaits 7 et 30 jours avec data variable
- Une quantité de data limitée sur certaines offres
- Plus de 200 destinations disponibles
- Des forfaits ponctuels, mensuels et annuels pour plus de flexibilité
- La possibilité de recharger même sans connexion internet
- Une quantité de data limitée sur les offres ponctuelles
- Des offres non compatibles avec l'Apple Watch
- Plus de 250 destinations disponibles
- Des forfaits avec une durée de validité au jour près
- Des données illimitées sur la majorité des offres
- Un prix plus élevé en raison des données illimitées
Classement des meilleures eSIM pour voyager en Europe en juillet 2026
Mise à jour le 1er septembre 2026 par la rédaction.
- 🥇 Saily - La meilleure eSIM Europe pour les petits budgets
- 🥈Ubigi - La meilleure eSIM Europe pour le rapport qualité/prix
- 🥉 Holafly - La référence pour la data illimitée sans stress
- Airalo - La meilleure eSIM Europe pour la flexibilité
- GigSky - La meilleure eSIM Europe pour la couverture géographique maximale
- GoMoWorld - La meilleure eSIM Europe pour les voyageurs connectés avec VPN inclus
Qu'est-ce qu'une eSIM ?
Une eSIM (pour Embedded SIM, soit « carte SIM intégrée ») est une puce SIM directement soudée à la carte mère de votre smartphone, sans support plastique amovible. Elle remplit exactement le même rôle qu'une carte SIM classique, vous authentifier auprès d'un réseau mobile et vous donner accès aux données, mais tout se fait de façon 100% numérique.
Concrètement, plutôt que d'insérer physiquement une carte dans votre téléphone, vous activez un forfait en scannant un simple QR code ou via l'application de l'opérateur, en quelques minutes. L'un de ses grands avantages pour le voyage est la gestion multi-profils : votre eSIM de voyage coexiste avec votre forfait français sur le même appareil grâce au dual SIM, vous conservez donc votre numéro habituel pour les appels et SMS tout en profitant des données de votre eSIM Europe.
Comment avons-nous testé ces eSIM pour l'Europe ? Nos critères de sélection
Pour établir ce comparatif des meilleures eSIM Europe, nous avons évalué chaque opérateur selon six critères objectifs.
- La couverture géographique d'abord : nombre de pays européens couverts, inclusion des destinations moins touristiques (Balkans, Europe de l'Est, îles nordiques) et fiabilité du ou des réseaux partenaires sur place.
- Les tarifs ensuite : prix au gigaoctet, disponibilité de plans illimités, flexibilité des durées (de 1 à 90 jours) et transparence des conditions
- La qualité réseau : accès à la 4G et à la 5G, débits réels constatés et éventuels bridages de vitesse après consommation du quota.
- La facilité d'activation : clarté du processus d'installation par QR code, ergonomie de l'application et disponibilité en français. Les fonctionnalités : partage de connexion (hotspot), VPN inclus, gestion multi-profils.
- Enfin, la fiabilité du service : réputation de l'opérateur, qualité du support client et retours d'utilisateurs réels. Seules les offres actives et disponibles à l'achat en juin 2026 ont été retenues.
Comparatif des 6 meilleures eSIM pour l’Europe en 2026
Holafly, Ubigi, Saily, Airalo, GigSky, GoMoWorld : ces six opérateurs dominent aujourd'hui le marché de l'eSIM Europe et couvrent l'ensemble des profils de voyageurs. Mais entre data illimitée et forfaits volumétriques, couverture de 28 ou 41 pays, prix d'entrée à 2 $ ou à 7 $, les différences sont réelles et le mauvais choix peut vous coûter cher, ou vous laisser sans connexion dans un pays non couvert. Pour vous aider à trouver la meilleure eSIM Europe selon votre usage, votre budget et votre destination, nous avons passé chaque offre au crible : tarifs réels, couverture exacte, qualité réseau et fonctionnalités. Voici notre sélection, classée par ordre de recommandation.
1.🥇 Saily, la meilleure eSIM Europe pour les petits budgets
Saily, lancé par NordVPN, est un opérateur eSIM récent qui a rapidement gagné en popularité grâce à ses tarifs très compétitifs et son interface soignée. Pour l'Europe, les forfaits débutent à 4,99 $ pour 1 Go / 7 jours et montent jusqu'à 95,99 $ pour 50 Go / 90 jours. Les plans disponibles incluent : 3 Go/30 jours à 12,49 $, 5 Go/30 jours à 19,49 $ et 10 Go/30 jours à 35,99 $. Saily ne propose pas de data illimitée sur l'Europe, mais ses prix au gigaoctet sont parmi les plus bas du marché. L'application est disponible en français et propose une gestion simplifiée des plans.

- card_travelForfaits 7, 15, 30, 90, 180 ou 365 jours
- add_shopping_cartRecharge disponible
- devicesCompatible iOS et Android
- pin_dropForfait Monde et packs multi-destinations
✅ Les points forts
- Couverture internationale étendue et offres multi-destinations
- Fonctions de cybersécurité rares sur le marché des eSIM
- Profil eSIM unique et réutilisable
- Forfaits prépayés flexibles et tarifs d’entrée accessibles
❌ Les limites de l'eSIM Saily
- Volumes de données parfois limités selon la destination
- Qualité de connexion dépendante des opérateurs partenaires
Pourquoi choisir Saily ?
Saily est le meilleur choix pour les voyageurs occasionnels ou économes qui consomment moins de 10 Go par mois. Avec 5 Go pour 30 jours à 19,49 $, c'est une offre difficile à battre parmi les grandes enseignes. La comparaison directe avec Airalo est parlante : pour 7 jours aux États-Unis, Saily facture 3,79 $ contre 4,50 $ chez Airalo pour 1 Go. Son ADN NordVPN lui confère également une attention particulière à la sécurité des données et à la confidentialité.
Nos avis sur l'eSIM Saily
Saily est une excellente option pour un voyage court à moyen en Europe avec une consommation de données maîtrisée. Le plan 5 Go / 30 jours à 19,49 $ est le meilleur rapport qualité/prix en data volumétrique de ce comparatif. À éviter si vous comptez streamer ou utiliser des applications très gourmandes en data.
Saily offre 10% de réduction avec le code promo CLUBIC
2. Ubigi, la meilleure eSIM Europe pour le rapport qualité/prix
Ubigi (filiale de Transatel/NTT) propose des eSIM Europe reconnues pour leur fiabilité réseau et leur tarification flexible. Les forfaits Europe partent de 2 $ pour 500 Mo sur 2 jours et montent jusqu'à des plans illimités à 69 $ pour 30 jours ou 26 $ pour 7 jours. La couverture standard couvre 37 pays européens, et le plan "Europe Extended" élargit cette couverture au Royaume-Uni, à la Turquie, à l'Ouzbékistan et aux Balkans. Ubigi propose des plans à la journée, mensuels et annuels, une flexibilité rare dans le secteur. La 5G est disponible dans de nombreuses villes européennes.

- card_travelForfaits ponctuels, mensuels et annuels. De 1 Go à données illimitées
- add_shopping_cartRecharge disponible sans données restantes ou accès WiFi
- devicesCompatible iOS, Android et Windows
- pin_dropForfait Monde et packs multi-destinations
✅ Les points forts
- Tarifs parmi les plus bas du marché, dès 2 $
- Plans illimités disponibles avec accès 5G
- Couverture Extended incluant Turquie, Balkans, Ouzbékistan
- Plans journaliers, mensuels et annuels (grande flexibilité)
- Infrastructure réseau de grande qualité (NTT/Transatel)
❌ Les limites de l'eSIM Ubigi
- Pas d'appels ni de SMS
- Interface moins intuitive que certains concurrents
- L'application mobile est moins soignée qu'Airalo ou Saily
Pourquoi choisir Ubigi ?
Ubigi est le choix idéal si vous recherchez le meilleur compromis prix/performance sur une eSIM Europe. Avec un plan illimité 30 jours à 69 $ contre 74,90 $ chez Holafly, et une couverture tout aussi étendue, Ubigi est objectivement moins cher pour les longs séjours. Son infrastructure réseau (adossée à NTT/Transatel) garantit une qualité de connexion constante et des débits stables, y compris dans les zones moins denses.
Notre verdict sur l'eSIM Ubigi
Ubigi est une valeur sûre et souvent sous-estimée dans les comparatifs eSIM Europe. Son rapport qualité/prix est le meilleur de ce comparatif pour les séjours de 7 jours ou plus. Recommandé sans hésitation pour les voyageurs qui veulent de la performance sans payer le premium de la notoriété.
3. Holafly, la référence pour la data illimitée sans stress
Holafly est l'un des acteurs les plus reconnus du marché des eSIM voyage. Sa proposition de valeur est claire : data illimitée dans 40 pays européens, sans compteur ni bridage de volume, idéal pour les voyageurs qui utilisent intensément Google Maps, les appels vidéo ou le streaming. Les plans Europe débutent à environ 3,79 $/jour et peuvent être souscrits pour 1, 3, 5, 7, 15, 30 ou 90 jours. Pour un séjour de 7 jours, comptez environ 27,49 $ ; pour 30 jours, le tarif est autour de 74,90 $. L'activation se fait par QR code, sans manipulation physique, et le support client est disponible 24h/24.

- devicesCompatible iOS, Android et Windows
- pin_dropForfait Monde, par continent et packs multi-destinations
✅ Les points forts
- Data illimitée sans bridage de volume
- 40 pays européens couverts, dont les destinations les moins touristiques
- Plans flexibles de 1 à 90 jours
- Activation instantanée par QR code
- Support client 24/7 en français
❌ Les limites de l'eSIM Holafly
- Pas d'appels ni de SMS inclus
- Pas le plus économique pour les petits séjours de 1 à 3 jours
- Prix en dollars, fluctuation possible selon le taux de change
Pourquoi choisir Holafly ?
Holafly s'impose comme le meilleur choix pour les voyageurs grands consommateurs de data qui ne veulent pas gérer un quota. La couverture s'étend à 40 pays dont la France, l'Italie, l'Espagne, l'Allemagne, le Royaume-Uni, la Grèce, la Suisse, l'Autriche, la Pologne et la Croatie. La data illimitée est particulièrement avantageuse lors de longs séjours : pour 90 jours, le tarif revient à environ 1,48 $/jour, ce qui en fait une solution très compétitive pour les nomades digitaux ou les expatriés temporaires.
Notre avis sur Holafly
Holafly est le meilleur achat eSIM Europe pour les voyageurs qui partent plus d'une semaine et consomment beaucoup de données mobiles. Son modèle illimité est rassurant, mais son rapport qualité/prix devient vraiment intéressant à partir du plan 15 jours. Pour un week-end, d'autres options sont plus économiques.
4. Airalo, la meilleure eSIM Europe pour la flexibilité
Airalo est la plus grande marketplace d'eSIM au monde, présente dans plus de 200 destinations. Pour l'Europe, le plan phare est l'EUconnect, couvrant 28 pays européens avec des forfaits allant de 1 Go / 7 jours à 4,50 $ jusqu'à 20 Go / 30 jours à 42 $. Airalo propose également des plans illimités (avec bridage à 1 Mbps une fois le quota quotidien atteint) à partir de 16,50 $ pour 5 jours. L'application est disponible en français, très bien notée sur les stores, et le système de codes promo "Airmoney" permet des réductions sur les achats futurs.

Pourquoi choisir Airalo ?
Airalo est idéal pour les voyageurs qui veulent une solution unique pour toute leur année de voyages, Europe et hors-Europe inclus. La plateforme permet d'acheter des eSIM locales, régionales ou mondiales au même endroit, avec une gestion centralisée depuis l'application. Pour un séjour en Europe, le plan EUconnect 10 Go / 7 jours à 26,50 $ est particulièrement adapté aux voyageurs d'affaires.
Notre verdict sur la solution Airalo
Airalo est la meilleure eSIM Europe si vous voyagez aussi hors d'Europe dans l'année, grâce à son écosystème multi-destinations. Pour un usage purement européen, Ubigi ou Saily offrent un meilleur rapport qualité/prix. Le choix de l'ecosystème prime ici sur le prix.
5. GigSky, la meilleure eSIM Europe pour la couverture géographique maximale
GigSky se distingue par la couverture la plus étendue de ce comparatif : 41 pays européens avec un plan unique, incluant des destinations souvent absentes chez les concurrents comme le Kosovo, les Îles Féroé, la Moldavie, le Monténégro ou Gibraltar. Les forfaits Europe démarrent à 6,99 $ pour 1 Go / 7 jours et incluent des plans illimités à partir de 38,99 $ pour 7 jours (bridés à 2,5 Go par jour en haute vitesse). GigSky propose également un plan d'essai gratuit à 100 Mo / 7 jours pour tester le service avant achat. La couverture 5G est disponible dans les pays disposant des infrastructures adaptées.

✅ Les points forts
- Plus grande couverture Europe de ce comparatif : 41 pays
- Inclut des destinations rares (Kosovo, Féroé, Moldavie, Gibraltar)
- Plan d'essai gratuit 100 Mo disponible

❌ Les limites de la solution Gigsky
- Prix parmi les plus élevés : moyenne de 40 $ par plan
- Data illimitée bridée à 2,5 Go/jour en haute vitesse
- Pas d'appels ni de SMS
- Aucun plan illimité au-delà de 14 jours
Pourquoi choisir GigSky ?
GigSky est le meilleur choix pour les voyageurs qui explorent des destinations européennes hors des sentiers battus (Europe de l'Est, Balkans, îles atlantiques) où les autres opérateurs sont absents. C'est aussi une option solide pour les road trips multi-pays grâce à sa couverture de 41 nations avec un forfait unique, plus économique que l'achat de SIM locales à 20-30 $ par pays.
Notre avis sur l'eSIM Gigsky
GigSky est incontournable pour les explorateurs des confins de l'Europe (Balkans, Caucase, îles nordiques) mais reste une option premium pour les destinations classiques. Si vous restez en Europe occidentale, Ubigi ou Holafly offrent un meilleur rapport qualité/prix. Pour les aventuriers, c'est le seul à cocher toutes les cases géographiques.
6. GoMoWorld, la meilleure eSIM Europe pour les voyageurs connectés avec VPN inclus
GoMoWorld est un opérateur eSIM irlandais fondé en 2022 et opéré par eircom Limited, couvrant plus de 200 destinations avec des plans Europe dès 3,99 €. Sa particularité est d'inclure en standard un hotspot partage de connexion et un VPN européen, deux fonctionnalités absentes chez tous les autres opérateurs de ce comparatif. La couverture réseau repose sur un accès à deux opérateurs par pays en moyenne, avec des débits jusqu'à la 5G. L'application, disponible en français, propose une interface moderne et une activation rapide.

❌ Les limites de la solution GoMoWorld

- Routage du trafic via l'Irlande pouvant créer des lenteurs sur certaines destinations lointaines
- Activation manuelle des plans parfois confuse
- Marque moins établie et retours terrain plus limités que Holafly ou Airalo
Pourquoi choisir GoMoWorld ?
GoMoWorld est idéal pour les voyageurs qui veulent partager leur connexion depuis leur smartphone (hotspot) ou qui souhaitent contourner les restrictions géographiques de certains services (streaming, banque en ligne) grâce au VPN inclus. Ses tarifs sont parmi les plus compétitifs du marché, le positionnant en troisième place mondiale sur les prix moyens avec une moyenne de 15,27 $ par plan.
Notre verdict sur l'eSIM GomoWorld
GoMoWorld est une option à considérer pour les voyageurs en Europe occidentale qui veulent le VPN et le hotspot inclus sans surcoût, et cherchent les tarifs les plus bas. En revanche, sa performance hors Europe est en deçà des standards et son manque de maturité de marque appelle à la prudence pour les voyages critiques.

Bon à savoir : toutes ces eSIM sont compatibles avec les smartphones iOS (iPhone XS et ultérieurs) et Android compatibles eSIM. Vérifiez la compatibilité de votre appareil avant l'achat.
Comment choisir son eSIM pour l'Europe ?
Avant d'acheter une eSIM Europe, posez-vous ces 4 questions clés :
La durée de votre séjour
Pour moins de 7 jours, Saily ou Ubigi (plans courts) sont les plus économiques. Pour plus de 15 jours, Holafly ou Ubigi en plan illimité s'imposent.
Votre consommation de data
Si vous utilisez des applications gourmandes (Netflix, appels vidéo, GPS continu), optez impérativement pour la data illimitée (Holafly, Ubigi). Sinon, Saily ou GigSky suffisent.
Vos destinations
Pour l'Europe occidentale classique, tous les opérateurs conviennent. Pour les Balkans, l'Europe de l'Est ou des îles nordiques, GigSky est la seule option qui couvre 41 pays.
Votre usage du hotspot
Seul GoMoWorld inclut le partage de connexion (hotspot) en standard. Vérifiez les conditions des autres opérateurs si vous devez connecter un ordinateur.
Comment installer une eSIM pour l'Europe ?
L'installation d'une eSIM Europe prend moins de 5 minutes depuis n'importe quel smartphone compatible :
- Achetez votre plan en ligne sur le site ou l'application de l'opérateur choisi
- Recevez le QR code par e-mail ou directement dans l'application
- Sur iPhone : Réglages > Données cellulaires > Ajouter un forfait > Scanner le QR code
- Sur Android : Réglages > Réseau > SIM > Ajouter une eSIM > Scanner le QR code
- Activez le forfait au moment de votre départ ou à l'arrivée en Europe
⚠️ Important : Votre smartphone doit être débloqué (non verrouillé opérateur) pour utiliser une eSIM d'un opérateur tiers. Vérifiez ce point auprès de votre opérateur français avant votre achat.
Vous comptez voyager dans d’autres pays ? Consultez nos différents comparatifs des meilleures eSIM pour voyager et trouvez le forfait le plus adapté à vos futures destinations.
eSIM pour l'Europe : les réponses à toutes vos questions
Ai-je besoin d'une eSIM pour l'Europe si j'ai un forfait français ?
Depuis la fin du roaming en Europe (2017), les forfaits français incluent théoriquement l'utilisation des données en Europe. Cependant, la plupart des opérateurs français plafonnent les données disponibles en roaming (souvent 15 à 25 Go selon les forfaits), et les débits sont fréquemment bridés. Une eSIM Europe dédiée garantit des données illimitées à plein débit.
Quelle est la différence entre une eSIM et une carte SIM locale en Europe ?
La principale différence tient à la praticité et à la couverture géographique. Une carte SIM locale s'achète physiquement dans un pays donné et ne fonctionne que dans ce pays, ou dans un périmètre limité. Elle est souvent moins chère pour un séjour long dans un seul pays, mais oblige à changer de carte à chaque frontière. Une eSIM de voyage, elle, s'active en quelques minutes depuis votre smartphone via un QR code, avant même de prendre l'avion, et couvre plusieurs pays européens avec un forfait unique.
La couverture réseau est-elle bonne partout en UE ?
La couverture est globalement très bonne en Europe occidentale, mais elle reste inégale selon les pays et les zones. Dans les grandes métropoles et les pays d'Europe de l'Ouest (France, Allemagne, Espagne, Italie, Pays-Bas…), la 4G couvre la quasi-totalité de la population et la 5G se déploie rapidement dans les zones urbaines. En revanche, dans les régions rurales, les zones montagneuses ou certains pays d'Europe de l'Est et des Balkans, la qualité du signal peut être plus aléatoire, quelle que soit l'eSIM utilisée.
Quelle est la meilleure eSIM pas chère pour l'Europe ?
Pour le plus petit budget, Saily avec son plan 1 Go / 7 jours à 4,99 $ est l'entrée de gamme la plus avantageuse. Ubigi démarre à 2 $ pour 500 Mo et reste la moins chère pour les séjours très courts.
Peut-on utiliser une eSIM Europe pour un forfait international ?
Les plans régionaux Europe sont conçus uniquement pour les pays couverts. Pour un voyage qui combine Europe et destinations hors-Europe (Maroc, Turquie, USA...), optez pour un plan global chez Airalo ou GoMoWorld, ou achetez une eSIM dédiée par zone.
L'eSIM remplace-t-elle ma SIM française ?
Non. L'eSIM de voyage s'ajoute à votre SIM principale via le dual SIM. Votre numéro français reste actif pour les appels et SMS. Seules les données passent par l'eSIM de voyage.
Combien coûte une eSIM pour l'Europe ?
Les tarifs varient de 2 $ à 99 $ selon le volume de données et la durée. Comptez en moyenne entre 15 et 40 € pour un forfait Europe de 7 à 30 jours adapté à un usage touristique standard.
Puis-je passer des appels avec une eSIM en Europe ?
La grande majorité des eSIM de voyage, dont celles de ce comparatif, proposent uniquement des données mobiles, sans appels ni SMS inclus. Pour téléphoner depuis l'Europe, vous pouvez utiliser des applications VoIP comme WhatsApp, FaceTime ou Google Meet via votre connexion data.

articles.title: Une affiche originale de Donkey Kong devient l'œuvre d’art liée à un jeu vidéo la plus chère jamais vendue
articles.text:
Si vous fouillez dans votre poubelle, là, tout de suite, maintenant, vous devriez trouver quelques déchets peu séduisants, qui ne serviront pas à grand-chose. C’est le principe d’une poubelle, cela dit.
Donna Darbous, une ancienne responsable de la publicité chez Nintendo of America, n’a pas les mêmes poubelles que vous et moi. À la fin des années 1980, alors que la filiale américaine de Nintendo réorganisait ses locaux pour gagner de la place, plusieurs documents et illustrations devaient finir à la benne.
Dans la pile d’objets à jeter, Donna Darbous a repéré des enveloppes contenant des dessins originaux et les a récupérées avec l’autorisation de son supérieur, comme elle l’a raconté au New York Times le 8 octobre 2026. Ces documents sont ensuite restés oubliés pendant plusieurs décennies, jusqu’à ce qu’elle les retrouve en rangeant son garage. Parmi eux figurait une illustration originale de Donkey Kong, le jeu d’arcade de Nintendo sorti en 1981.
Elle a été vendue aux enchères ce mercredi 28 octobre, comme le relaye IGN, pour 329 400 dollars (environ 294 000 euros), plus du double de l’estimation, qui allait de 100 000 à 150 000 dollars (environ 89 000 à 134 000 euros).
L’illustration était proposée par la maison Landry Pop Auctions lors de la vente Jumpman : The Beginning of an Icon. D’après la maison d’enchères, ce prix établit un record pour une œuvre d’art originale liée au jeu vidéo vendue aux enchères. Le précédent record appartenait à la peinture originale de Robert Florczak pour une illustration de Prince of Persia, vendue 63 000 dollars (environ 56 000 euros) par Heritage Auctions en janvier 2023.
Une illustration originale liée à l’histoire de Nintendo
Réalisée par l’illustrateur Leslie Cabarga pour le prospectus destiné à vendre la borne Donkey Kong aux exploitants de salles d’arcade nord-américains, cette illustration représente le célèbre primate brandissant un tonneau, tandis que Mario, alors appelé Jumpman, escalade un bâtiment pour sauver Pauline. Landry Pop Auctions la présente comme la première apparition publique de Mario, ce qui explique en bonne partie son prix.
Le dessin a ensuite servi de base aux affiches distribuées aux États-Unis. Comme le rappelle GameSpot ce 28 octobre, il a été repris pendant des décennies sur des produits dérivés de Donkey Kong et a fixé l’apparence de Mario et du gorille dans leurs premières adaptations, notamment dans le dessin animé Saturday Supercade diffusé au début des années 1980.
Cette illustration faisait partie d’une vente de 49 lots issus de la collection de Donna Darbous, tous liés à l’histoire de Nintendo. Parmi les autres pièces figuraient une illustration originale de Mario et Luigi pour Super Mario Bros., vendue 17 080 dollars (environ 15 200 euros), près de trois fois son estimation, et un dessin de Goomba adjugé 10 370 dollars (environ 9 250 euros), plus du double de l’estimation.
L’illustration de Donkey Kong cumulait trois atouts aux yeux des collectionneurs qui peut expliquer son prix de vente astronomique : son ancienneté, son rôle dans la naissance de Mario et son parcours, puisqu’elle a échappé de peu à la benne. On ne sait pas qui a déboursé cette somme, ni si l’œuvre sera exposée au public ou restera dans le salon d’un collectionneur. Toujours est-il que la vente confirme le poids culturel de Mario, 45 ans après ses débuts sur une borne d’arcade.

articles.title: Investigadores de Google y Anthropic detectaron falla de seguridad que afecta a la mayoría de centros de datos del mundo
articles.text:
Alex Matrosov, investigador de Anthropic, y Dan Holmes, de Google, descubrieron una falla en el código de arranque que utilizan la mayoría de proveedores de servidores y centros de datos del planeta, que dejó expuestos a millones de equipos frente a ataques capaces de ejecutar código malicioso antes de que cualquier sistema de defensa pueda activarse. La vulnerabilidad, identificada como CVE-2026-97631, recibió una calificación de severidad de 9,5 sobre 10 y afecta al TianoCore EDK II, el código abierto que las empresas de hardware emplean para construir el firmware UEFI que se ejecuta durante el inicio de los equipos.
El EDK2 es, según un representante del UEFI Forum, “la solución de referencia predominante” para implementar las especificaciones UEFI. Prácticamente todos los proveedores independientes de BIOS, entre ellos AMI, Insyde y Phoenix, utilizan de manera extensa este código base. También lo emplea Project Mu, la versión reforzada de EDK2 desarrollada por Microsoft, que incluye el componente vulnerable.
El fallo permite eludir el arranque seguro de los equipos
El problema reside en un componente del protocolo ICMP y consiste en una corrupción de memoria que un atacante puede aprovechar para ejecutar código antes de que el sistema operativo y el firmware puedan aplicar mecanismos de defensa como el Secure Boot. Esta función establece una cadena de confianza para todo el código que se carga durante el arranque, incluido el que corresponde al Trusted Platform Module (TPM).
Los ataques que exploten esta falla no logran persistencia, es decir, el código malicioso corre una sola vez. Sin embargo, esa única ejecución puede bastar para abrir la puerta a otros programas maliciosos que sí se instalen de forma permanente y se activen en cada arranque posterior del equipo.
Un fallo de 16 años en el controlador de arranque por red
CVE-2026-97631 corresponde a un desbordamiento de búfer presente desde hace 16 años en el controlador PXE-Base Code (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe), responsable de que servidores, equipos de almacenamiento y otros dispositivos puedan iniciarse con código descargado desde una red local. Durante ese proceso, conocido como entorno de pre-ejecución de arranque, el controlador mantiene un escucha de red para detectar mensajes de error ICMP.
El defecto radica en que el controlador no impone un límite de copia de memoria de 504 bytes, por lo que los datos adyacentes pueden sobrescribirse. Un atacante con acceso de bajo nivel a una red local, o un usuario malicioso dentro de esa red, puede enviar un mensaje de error que agregue código más allá de ese límite, lo que corrompe el módulo UEFI que corre en el procesador.
El aviso oficial del proyecto explica que el controlador PXE Base Code mantiene abierta una solicitud de recepción para mensajes de error ICMP y copia cada mensaje recibido en un campo fijo de 504 bytes dentro de su estructura de contexto privada.
Tanto en el manejador de IPv4 como en el de IPv6, el control de límites está mal implementado: si el mensaje supera los 504 bytes, el sistema igual copia los bytes excedentes, y el puntero de destino avanza según la longitud acumulada en lugar de la longitud de cada fragmento, lo cual permite que un mensaje de tamaño excesivo escriba datos controlados por el atacante fuera del campo previsto. Nada en el camino de recepción anterior restringe la longitud del mensaje.
Un ataque que puede ejecutarse con un simple envío unicast
El error malicioso puede entregarse mediante un envío unicast simple desde cualquier distancia de red hacia la dirección IP del dispositivo objetivo, siempre que se transmita durante la secuencia de arranque PXE. Un atacante puede provocar una denegación de servicio con solo hacer que la secuencia de arranque se bloquee. Si además conoce la versión específica del firmware del objetivo, puede introducir lo que el aviso describe como un “evento falsificado” que ejecuta código malicioso directamente sobre el procesador dentro de su entorno de firmware UEFI.
Ese código corre en el anillo 0 (ring 0), el nivel de ejecución más privilegiado de un procesador. Según explicó HD Moore, creador de Metasploit y director de investigación en la firma de seguridad Dragos, esta falla en el analizador ICMP de la pila de red de EDK2 resulta relevante por su efecto sobre la cadena de confianza y el ecosistema en general.
Moore señaló que un atacante interesado en comprometer un terminal o servidor cercano podría usar este error para secuestrar el flujo del programa en un punto donde el proceso de arranque todavía tiene acceso a componentes sensibles, como el TPM del dispositivo, lo que podría emplearse para romper el cifrado de disco en escenarios donde el atacante cuenta con acceso de red de corto plazo, una situación aún más sencilla en un caso de robo físico del equipo.
Los exploits que aprovechan esta vulnerabilidad logran además eludir los procesos de verificación diseñados para demostrar de forma criptográfica a servidores remotos que el hardware es seguro, lo que representa una vía concreta para escalar privilegios limitados.
La divulgación se adelantó al plazo previsto
Matrosov y Holmes habían acordado mantener la falla en reserva hasta una divulgación coordinada prevista para enero. Sin embargo, AMI publicó el mes pasado una solicitud de incorporación de código que detallaba la vulnerabilidad e incluía una corrección. Una vez que esa publicación llegó a conocimiento de los descubridores originales, los miembros del proyecto TianoCore emitieron un aviso público la semana pasada.
Con el código de parche ya disponible públicamente, resultará sencillo para atacantes con conocimientos avanzados comprender cómo se activa la vulnerabilidad y construir exploits funcionales. La urgencia se agrava porque corregir fallas de código UEFI en millones de dispositivos finales, vendidos y utilizados por miles de fabricantes de hardware y proveedores de nube, es un proceso lento y complejo. Esta revelación se produjo seis días después de otra divulgación igualmente apresurada, en ese caso sobre una vulnerabilidad crítica de ejecución de código en el lenguaje de programación PHP.

articles.title: Gemini Notebook agora tem gravador de áudio para palestras e reuniões • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Gemini Notebook agora tem gravador de áudio para palestras e reuniões
Novo recurso do Gemini Notebook (antigo NotebookLM) permite gravar até uma hora de áudio e transcrever o conteúdo resultante.
O Google continua aprimorando o Gemini Notebook (outrora, NotebookLM). A novidade mais recente é um recurso de gravação de áudio implementado especialmente para que o usuário possa registrar o conteúdo de palestras e reuniões. Cada gravação pode ter até uma hora de duração.
Note que este não é um mero gravador de som. O áudio registrado é transcrito automaticamente pelo Gemini Notebook. Na sequência, o conteúdo obtido pode ser resumido, traduzido e até combinado com notas ou fotos registradas pelo usuário durante a palestra ou reunião.
O recurso também é útil para que você possa pedir que o Gemini Notebook explique determinado assunto abordado na palestra ou reunião, ou para localizar uma citação específica.
É claro que a novidade também pode ser usada para outras aplicações. Um exemplo: você pode recorrer ao recurso para descrever uma ideia para o Gemini Notebook e, posteriormente, pedir para a ferramenta organizá-la.
O recurso está disponível nas versões do Gemini Notebook para Android e iOS. Ele pode ser acessado por meio de um botão de microfone que aparece na parte inferior do aplicativo, ao lado do botão de câmera.
Quando a gravação tem início, botões de pausa e conclusão são exibidos. O primeiro é interessante porque retoma a gravação de onde ela parou, sendo útil para intervalos durante o evento, por exemplo. Pode-se ainda deixar a gravação sendo executada em segundo plano. Lembre-se, porém, de que cada áudio pode durar até uma hora.
A novidade é global, mas está sendo liberada gradualmente (para mim ainda não apareceu). Aparentemente, usuários do Gemini Notebook em inglês estão recebendo o gravador de áudio primeiro.
O Gemini Notebook é um serviço de inteligência artificial generativa que ajuda o usuário a organizar, resumir, sintetizar e acessar informações específicas, funcionando como um caderno digital e inteligente de notas.
A ferramenta é especialmente útil para estudantes ou para quem trabalha com grandes volumes de informações. Isso porque, além de texto, o Gemini Notebook pode tratar os dados na forma de áudio (podcast), slides ou vídeos sob medida, por exemplo.

articles.title: Cyber resiliency frameworks for enterprise AI infrastructure - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Experian builds cyber resiliency into its AI infrastructure
Enterprises racing to deploy AI at scale are discovering that models depend on the infrastructure beneath them. As cyber resiliency becomes central to AI deployment, organizations must address foundational issues such as data quality, access controls and recovery.
That work is particularly important in data-intensive industries such as financial services. Experian PLC has built its AI strategy around infrastructure resilience, according to Rodrigo Rodrigues (pictured), group chief technology officer of Experian PLC.
“Speed creates risk when foundations are weak,” he said. “Many teams add AI on top of existing systems that were never designed for it. Data comes from many systems with different rules. Logs are incomplete, backups are slow, access policies are unclear. Everything works, until it doesn’t.”
Rodrigues spoke with theCUBE’s Christophe Bertrand at the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed cyber resiliency frameworks for AI infrastructure, zero-trust identity for non-human agents and how Experian governs AI pipelines at scale. (* Disclosure below.)
Cyber resiliency requires AI recovery and access controls
One of the sharpest lessons Rodrigues shared is that cyber resiliency cannot be assumed from the presence of backups alone. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework, which Experian has embedded directly into its AI pipelines, provides the structural backbone for making that governance real rather than theoretical. Before any model can deploy, data sources are checked automatically, quality rules are enforced and security policies are validated — and if any control fails, the pipeline stops with no manual override.
“Policy enforcement happens at machine speed,” Rodrigues said. “We have AI-specific recovery goals — not just for applications, but for data models and pipelines. We test AI recovery the same way we test disaster recovery: scheduled drills, clear recovery objectives, measured results. There’s no guesswork, no panic — just execution.”
The interconnected risks of bad data, compromised backups and over-permissioned AI agents form a triad of failure modes Rodrigues has tackled head-on. Bad training data does not produce a broken model immediately — it produces a model that learns the wrong patterns and amplifies them at scale.
“AI does not leak data,” he said. “Access leaks data. AI only reflects the permissions we give it. Identity must be designed for AI, not just for humans — that means applying least privilege to AI services just like users, rotating credentials frequently and monitoring access in real time with automated alerts.”
To help developers navigate this complexity without slowing delivery, Experian built an internal AI agent marketplace — an internal registry where product and engineering teams can discover, sandbox and reuse governed agents backed by quality controls. The approach draws explicitly from lessons learned in managing microservices and application programming interfaces, Rodrigues explained, treating agents as versioned assets with defined owners, lifecycle policies and sunset criteria.
“Agentic AI can act on its own — it can scale systems, change routing, update policy,” Rodrigues said. “If this goes wrong, the impact is huge. Autonomy requires control. Simulate before execution. Limit agent permissions until you have a strong foundation and have learned how to operate safely.”

articles.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Reaches Nearly $2,000 Across U.S. Retailers
articles.text:

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Reaches Nearly $2,000 Across U.S. Retailers
NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5080 has seen a significant increase in its listed price over the past few weeks, with this high-end GPU now costing nearly $2,000. Due to price hikes throughout the supply chain and the GPU's 16 GB of GDDR7 memory, which is currently in short supply, the listing price has doubled its original MSRP. NVIDIA initially launched the GeForce RTX 5080 in early 2025 with an MSRP of $999. However, add-in card partners introduced custom solutions such as new PCBs, enhanced cooling, and other features that gradually increased the price. The pricing issue escalated when the memory supply became constrained, making the GDDR7 memory modules used in this GPU much more expensive.
Across U.S.-based retailers like Best Buy, Micro Center, Amazon, Newegg, B&H, and others, the listing price now starts at nearly $2,000. On B&H, older listings show better pricing but are marked as "Temporary out of stock." Only the in-stock listings are priced at $2,000 or more, indicating that new pricing adjustments have been made across all retailers. In just two months, the listings have jumped from $1,200 to $2,000, which is a dramatic increase in pricing.Below are screenshots collected across U.S.-based retailers.

articles.title: Amazon updates Alexa to help you manage shopping lists, subscriptions, and update delivery instructions | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ahead of the holiday season, Amazon has added more than 100 new shopping-related capabilities to Alexa, including subscription and list management, updating delivery instructions, solving payment issues, and answering questions about Prime subscriptions.
The update allows you to use Alexa to create lists, register them, see what’s on them, and add or edit items. You can also manage subscriptions with the AI bot — for example, you could ask it to change deliveries for an item to every three months instead of every month — and edit delivery instructions, such as change an address or add drop-off details.

Amazon has launched various AI-centric shopping features this year, including a shopping assistant, and a way to notify users about new products and offers.
The company said that since the start of the year, the number of people using agentic features has grown 8x, and over the last 12 months, over 400 million consumers have used Alexa for shopping.

articles.title: Why native PC ports of console games are suddenly everywhere
articles.text:
Why native PC conversions of console games are suddenly everywhere — Reverse Engineer Anything gives AI agents a unified toolkit, and byte-for-byte checks keep hallucinations in line
The stage was set, all that was needed was a push... from an army of bots.
Over the past weeks and months, it's increasingly commonplace to encounter native PC ports of previously console-exclusive video games, developed with the help of frontier AI models and a new tool named Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). With dozens of titles ported to PC over the past few months, the big questions are: why is this now possible, and what changed?
The better-known conversions like Super Mario Galaxy and Modern Warfare 2 use AI agents, but their handlers mostly still had to interpret results and direct each step of the process. That's now much easier with Reverse Engineer Anything. Although it shows up in many conversations, REA doesn't do the heavy lifting by itself. It's actually a mix between a toolkit and agent harness, wiring together previously disparate tools under one ceiling.
REA analyzes and manages collected information tools: binary analyzers, decompilers, metadata tools, firmware images, database readers, and so on end up linked via agents. Those tools are made available to your AI agent of choice, along with skill files with additional instructions.
Simplistic as it may sound, it's the glue that once again significantly cuts down the time spent on "chores" that a developer would otherwise have to do while reverse-engineering code, which started with emulating consoles themselves.
Emulation of video game consoles on PC is nothing new, having emerged in the 90s in the 2D era, and gradually transitioning to 3D consoles such as the PlayStation 1, and Nintendo 64. Throughout the early 2020s, emulators and toolkits evolved at a rapid pace, covering more systems than ever — even the PlayStation 3 and its notorious Cell processor. Physical hardware is taken apart and inspected more easily and at deeper levels than ever, as tools like the Raspberry Pi become cheaper and more powerful. These elements set the stage for the ultimate task: to fully decompile and recompile a game and convert it to run on native PC instructions, rather than relying on software emulation. Only one barrier remained: dedicated development time.
To reverse-engineer a game, you need dozens of different tools, analyze the game's executable, run it, inspect which files it reads, which calls it makes to the operating system, what memory it allocates, and so on and so forth. This is exceedingly tedious, and yet can't be done half-heartedly: one errant byte is a bug. It's like undoing a machine with a million cogs and keeping track exactly where each one was, its size, and orientation. Modern games grew, too, and can have millions of lines of code.
But that kind of nitpicky, repetitive work is just what computers excel at — even non-deterministic ones like LLMs. 2026's AI models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude 5.5 families are "smarter" in the sense that they follow complicated instructions more closely and can better keep track of their tasks, granting them a higher degree of autonomy. The high token efficiency of lower-grade variants like Claude Sonnet also makes them somewhat affordable, if not cheap, to use on a humongous project like taking apart an entire game.
Given how AI bots can hallucinate and make up strange replies and code, you may wonder how a project of this scale ever gets accomplished. It's simple: your agent hands you decompiled source code, and it compiles it again to see if it matches the original byte-for-byte. Even if they hallucinate, the bots can try over and over until they get it right, and developers can correct them if needed.
Reverse-engineering needs multiple tools, all with their own technical terms and idiosyncrasies. Whereas before developers had to wrangle them across terminal windows, now you can get your agent to twiddle bits and talk between programs on your behalf, so long as you issue the right orders. They don't have to stop for breaks, either.
With relatively simple prompts, you can poke around and break down a game or application — provided you have one of the pricier agent subscriptions, or can absorb high token bills, as for example the Modern Warfare 2 decomp took three months and up to 700 billion tokens to accomplish. Had its developer used REA, he may have cut down on time and tokens both.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Bei ProSiebenSat.1 wird jetzt ein TV-Relikt der Vergangenheit abgeschaltet
articles.text:
Bei ProSiebenSat.1 wird jetzt ein TV-Relikt der Vergangenheit abgeschaltet
Der Fernsehkonzern ProSiebenSat.1 schaltet seine Videotext-Angebote ab Anfang nächstes Jahr ab. Betroffen sind neben Sat.1 und ProSieben auch Kabel Eins, Sixx, Sat.1 Gold, ProSieben Maxx und Kabel Eins Doku. Die Sender kündigen das in einer Mitteilung „in eigener Sache“ auf der ersten Seite ihrer Videotext-Angebote, die auch Teletext genannt werden, an. Das Medienmagazin DWDL.de hatte die Information entdeckt.
Kaum noch jemand schaut hin
Ein Sendersprecher begründet die Entscheidung gegenüber DWDL.de mit der geringen Nutzung: „Das Interesse der Zuschauerinnen und Zuschauer an unseren Teletext-Angeboten tangiert gegen Null.“ Als Informationsquelle habe die Website von Joyn den Videotext längst abgelöst. Joyn ist der Streamingdienst der Sendergruppe.
Schon Anfang 2025 hatte ProSiebenSat.1 den Teletext stark zusammengestrichen. Seitdem finden sich dort nur noch Programminformationen, keine redaktionellen Infos. Wer auf Seite 111 nach Nachrichten sucht, landet bei einem Verweis auf die News-Seite von Joyn. Damals erklärte die Sendergruppe, Zuschauer hätten im Teletext ohnehin fast nur noch nach dem Fernsehprogramm gesucht.
Untertitel laufen künftig anders
Mit dem Teletext fällt bei ProSiebenSat.1 auch der bisherige Weg zu den Untertiteln weg. Wer sie einblenden will, aktiviert sie künftig direkt in den Einstellungen des Fernsehers oder des Receivers. Damit folge man dem Vorgehen anderer großer Medienhäuser, sagt der Sprecher DWDL.de: „Die Untertitelung fällt nicht weg, sondern lediglich der technische Zugangsweg verändert sich.“
Andere Sender machen hingegen weiter. Das ZDF hat zwar bereits Sportnachrichten und Börsenkurse aus seinem Videotext gestrichen. Und mehrere dritte Programme betreiben kein eigenes Angebot mehr und übernehmen stattdessen den ARD-Text. Doch die Bestückung selbst endet nicht, da man besonders unter älteren Nutzer:innen noch Fans hat. Der ARD-Text wird aus Potsdam bestückt und hat dazu eine eigene Redaktion.
Die Technik stammt aus der Zeit des analogen Fernsehens. Die Sender übertrugen die Textseiten in der Austastlücke des Fernsehsignals – einem ungenutzten Teil des Bildsignals. Abrufen lassen sich die Seiten über die Eingabe von dreistelligen Seitenzahlen auf der Fernbedienung.

articles.title: Peptide peddlers cheer as RFK Jr. unilaterally grants access, overruling FDA
articles.text:
Anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy has unilaterally passed a rule that will allow specialty pharmacies to sell six specific peptide drugs, overruling scientists at the Food and Drug Administration.
The peptides are popular among members of Kennedy’s Make America Health Again movement, and many prominent MAHA figures and Kennedy allies sell them. Kennedy said he uses some of the peptides and called himself a “big fan.” But FDA scientists continue to say there is insufficient evidence to show if they’re effective, and they are potentially dangerous. In 2023, the safety concerns led the FDA to remove the six peptides from a list of drugs that can be made by specialty pharmacies called compounding pharmacies—which make customized formulations of drugs for patients, or, in cases such as this, specialty drugs in bulk.
Kennedy’s new rule sidesteps the need to formally undo that FDA action. The rule is titled “Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances” and was made available Wednesday on the Federal Register, with the final publication date set for October 30. The rule does not change the regulatory status of the peptide; instead, it states the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will no longer take enforcement action against compounding pharmacies for making the peptides, essentially giving them a green light to freely produce and sell them. Kennedy had quietly proposed this rule earlier this month.
Questionable rationale
Along with the notice in the Federal Register, HHS also posted a more detailed explanation of the policy today that includes more of Kennedy’s rationale for easing enforcement of the six select peptides, which are: BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax, and TB-500.

articles.title: DuckDuckGo Privacy Pro data removal service review
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
I recommend DuckDuckGo’s Pro bundle for anyone seeking to maximize their online privacy. The drawbacks are the relatively high price and that features are only compatible with the DuckDuckGo browser.
Reasons to buy
- + Robust feature set
- + Advanced VPN
- + Identity theft protection
Reasons to avoid
- - Short free trial
- - Exclusive to the DuckDuckGo browser
- - Some features are US-only
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Staying safe online is as imperative as ever, especially since AI has inadvertently increased the volume of cyber attacks. Good online safety leans more on preventing attacks from happening in the first place than on countering them, and certain tools help you do that.
DuckDuckGo is most famous for its privacy-focused search engine and browser (we've reviewed it here), but it also provides other tools that help users surf the web without giving out their identities. These tools are offered under a single, cost-competitive Pro bundle. It's a VPN, AI tool, and data removal service all in one.
I’m reviewing the DuckDuckGo Pro bundle to help you decide if it’s worth adopting for your online security. Read on to learn what this bundle offers, its pros, cons, and how it compares to the competition.
DuckDuckGo: Plans and pricing
DuckDuckGo follows a simple pricing system, which I like - you can see all the plans by clicking here. A monthly subscription costs $19.99 and unlocks access to all Pro features. An annual subscription is discounted to $200, equivalent to $17 per month instead of the $19.99 paid on a month-to-month basis. This discount is quite small compared to what I’ve seen on rivals, but is a discount nonetheless.
The pricing varies slightly for users who live outside the U.S. For example, U.K.-based users pay 19.99 pounds monthly and 200 pounds annually. Converted to the U.S. dollar, that sums up to $27 per month and $273 annually (inclusive of value-added tax). Other countries have similar pricing variations, so you may pay more (or less) than the sticker price mentioned.
DuckDuckGo offers a 7-day free trial for its Pro plan. This is shorter than the 14 to 30-day free trials I’ve used on various online security platforms, but still provides an opportunity to test the features before deciding whether to pay.
Subscriptions can be cancelled anytime, but DuckDuckGo’s website doesn’t mention a specific money-back guarantee period. It seems that refunds can be requested, but it’ll take a lot of back and forth, which I consider a drawback.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
DuckDuckGo: Setup
Setting up DuckDuckGo Privacy Pro isn’t as straightforward as most security software bundles I’ve reviewed. You’ll need to first download the DuckDuckGo browser on your PC or smartphone (you can’t use Pro features on Chrome, Firefox, or Edge). The privacy-focused browser is the foundation of DuckDuckGo’s Pro package: it blocks ads, trackers, and cookies that pose privacy risks. The browser is free, but the Pro bundle unlocks enhanced security features, which are the focus of this review.
After paying for a Pro subscription, the first feature to take note of is the VPN. This VPN, built into the DuckDuckGo browser, routes your traffic through remote servers to prevent third-party tracking. Your location, IP address, and browsing history get hidden from third parties, like advertisers or, at worst, malicious actors.
There’s a limitation, though. DuckDuckGo’s VPN servers are concentrated in the U.S. and Europe, with few outside these locations. If you’re surfing the web from, let’s say, the Middle East, connections can get a bit slower because of the server distance. DuckDuckGo’s VPN isn’t like full-fledged VPNs that let you choose from dozens of countries.
On the bright side, DuckDuckGo’s VPN has a default kill switch, which automatically cuts off your internet connection if the VPN malfunctions, ensuring your data doesn’t leak because of a slight network mishap. I checked thoroughly, but didn’t find any button to turn off this kill switch, which is a plus in my perspective. Turning off a kill switch poses privacy risks during network lapses.
The VPN coverage can be used on five devices simultaneously. For example, you can install it on your work PC, home PC, and smartphone via the DuckDuckGo browser. Your traffic gets encrypted on all connected devices.
Another key feature offered under DuckDuckGo Pro is quite unique: identity theft restoration. If you face any incident of identity theft, you can work with an expert to mitigate the effects. For example, the expert helps identify fraudulent transactions that your card may have been used for and then files reimbursement claims with your bank. You'll also get help in fixing any credit report errors from fraudulent transactions.
There’s a catch, though: DuckDuckGo doesn’t offer identity theft restoration services directly. Rather, it has partnered with Iris, a prominent ID protection platform, to provide this service. You’ll be working with Iris’ experts if you use this service.
In this AI era, you’ll hardly find a security platform that doesn’t offer an AI-centric feature. For Pro subscribers, DuckDuckGo offers advanced chatbots (based on ChatGPT and Claude) with active privacy protection. This way, you won’t have to pay separately for the premium versions of Claude and ChatGPT, as DuckDuckGo offers access under the Pro bundle.
Overall, DuckDuckGo’s Pro bundle is feature-rich and effective at maximizing online privacy. However, with plans starting at $19.99 per month, I think it’s quite pricey.
DuckDuckGo: Ease of use
DuckDuckGo is a mixed bag when it comes to ease of use. Its features are exclusive to the DuckDuckGo browser, not the more popular Chrome, Firefox, and Edge browsers.
For most people, paying for the Pro bundle means learning to use a new browser on Windows, macOS, iOS, or Android. I didn’t find it difficult to get adapted to the DuckDuckGo browser, but it took some time because the browser worked differently from the ones I was used to.
DuckDuckGo: Security and privacy
DuckDuckGo offers a very effective online privacy suite, starting with a browser that doesn’t allow cookies, trackers, or anything that keeps a trail of the sites you visit. The built-in VPN encrypts your online traffic and prevents third-party prying eyes.
Identity theft restoration is another valuable service, and so is the bonus of interacting with advanced chatbots. You’ll be a lot safer online when using DuckDuckGo’s Pro bundle.
DuckDuckGo: Support
DuckDuckGo offers decent support resources. You can start with the help page, which lists answers to frequently asked questions (FAQs). I liked the breakdown of questions people often ask about DuckDuckGo’s privacy features and the detailed answers provided.
Users who need direct help can contact DuckDuckGo’s support team via email or by filling out a support form. There’s also an option to interact with DuckDuckGo’s staff via a dedicated forum on Reddit. However, there’s no telephone or live chat support, which I consider a major drawback given the price of a DuckDuckGo Pro subscription.
DuckDuckGo: Competition
Given the many features offered under DuckDuckGo Pro, it’s hard to pinpoint an exact competitor. Instead, I’ll highlight some competitors to key DuckDuckGo Pro features.
For the private browser, Brave is a notable option. After using both, I’ll say Brave offers more privacy controls and is more advanced in general. For instance, Brave supports browser extensions just like you’ll find on Chrome, but the DuckDuckGo Browser doesn’t.
For DuckDuckGo’s VPN, I’ll say any dedicated VPN app like Surfshark and Windscribe would be a better option, with broader server locations to choose from.
However, the point of DuckDuckGo Pro is to kill multiple birds with one stone: you won’t get the best of each feature, but, overall, you’ll get a good deal.
DuckDuckGo: Final verdict
A DuckDuckGo Pro bundle maximizes your online privacy, preventing third parties from tracking your online activities. If you want to surf the web without leaking data that’ll stay on the internet for a long time, I highly recommend it. However, you’d need to be ready to switch to a new browser and pay a significant amount, which I would see as drawbacks.

articles.title: TikTok USDS eyes 4 gigawatts of new power for advanced AI models
articles.text:
TikTok is on the hunt for a huge compute capacity upgrade — so is it replacing Oracle, or just exploring its options?
TikTok explores massive 4GW computing expansion for 2030s AI push
- TikTok could require 4 gigawatts of computing capacity by the early 2030s
- Oracle remains TikTok's primary American cloud provider despite expansion plans
- TikTok's growing AI ambitions could increase demand for computing infrastructure
A potential requirement for 4 gigawatts of computing power has prompted TikTok's American business to investigate additional infrastructure arrangements beyond its current resources.
The company has reportedly contacted potential suppliers about future capacity, although its existing partnership with Oracle remains central to American operations.
TikTok has denied any suggestion of an impending replacement, maintaining that its principal cloud services remain the same.
A massive computing requirement raises supplier questions
“Oracle will continue to be our primary cloud infrastructure provider,” said a TikTok spokesperson.
However, the company did not disclose whether it intends to obtain the additional computing capacity from other providers.
The proposed expansion concerns computing resources that TikTok might need during the early 2030s, rather than capacity already secured through contractual agreements.
According to CNBC, two sources familiar with TikTok's infrastructure discussions confirmed that the company was exploring opportunities to secure additional computing capacity.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
One source estimated that TikTok could require approximately 4 gigawatts by the early 2030s, although potential suppliers and agreements remain undisclosed.
The reported scale comes amid increasing demand for electricity and computing equipment as companies develop more resource-intensive artificial intelligence systems.
TikTok's American business already depends heavily on Oracle, whose cloud operations generally use data center buildings leased from third parties.
That arrangement allows Oracle to provide computing services without necessarily owning the physical facilities containing the servers and supporting electrical equipment.
Machine learning ambitions add another dimension
Beyond operating its social media platform, TikTok is recruiting specialists to develop artificial intelligence applications that could require additional processing infrastructure.
Several vacancies advertised by its American organization concern machine learning, while another describes work involving sophisticated AI models and automated content creation.
The latter position concerns a commercial AI offering designed for business customers, involving model inference and software capable of generating creative material.
These recruitment activities establish ongoing technical development, although the company has not connected individual projects to its reported multigigawatt infrastructure requirement.
TikTok's American operations also face specific computing responsibilities arising from changes to the platform's ownership and handling of domestic user information.
Established in 2026, TikTok USDS Joint Venture followed an executive order from President Donald Trump requiring changes to ByteDance's American ownership arrangements.
ByteDance retained 19.9% of the resulting enterprise, while Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX became managing investors with individual ownership stakes of 15%.
Additional financial backing came from Michael Dell's family investment office, which joined the ownership arrangement following the restructuring of TikTok's American business.
In January, the company announced that its recommendation algorithm would undergo domestic training and evaluation using information collected from users in America.
Oracle was designated to host the algorithm within its American cloud infrastructure, giving the provider an established role in handling TikTok's recommendation technology.
The company has not specified whether its potential 4-gigawatt expansion would support these algorithmic operations, commercial AI development, or other computing requirements.

articles.title: Signs Your Business Has Outgrown the Person Who Is Good With Computers - Tech Guide
articles.text:
In the early stages of a business, it’s common for owners or employees who have a knack for technology to manage all IT-related tasks. This might include troubleshooting hardware issues, setting up software, managing networks, and maintaining cybersecurity.
Often, these individuals are the “go-to” person for anything computer-related, and their efforts keep the business running smoothly without the expense of dedicated IT staff. However, as businesses grow, these tech-savvy employees often find themselves overwhelmed by the increasing demands, leaving critical IT needs unmet. Recognizing when your business has outgrown relying on a person who is merely good with computers is critical to maintaining operational efficiency, security, and long-term success.
Many small businesses start with informal IT support, but the reality is that technology needs evolve rapidly. According to a report by CompTIA, 70% of small businesses experience significant IT challenges as they scale, underscoring the importance of professional IT management. This article explores the key signs that indicate it’s time to move beyond informal IT support and invest in professional services or dedicated IT staff.
Increased Complexity of IT Needs
One of the most obvious signs your business has surpassed the capabilities of an in-house tech enthusiast is the increasing complexity of your IT infrastructure. Initially, a simple network and basic software were sufficient. Now, with more employees, cloud services, and customer data, your IT environment demands specialized knowledge.
For example, integrating complex systems such as customer relationship management (CRM) tools, enterprise resource planning (ERP) solutions, or advanced cybersecurity measures requires expertise that goes beyond basic computer skills. If your current IT person struggles to implement or maintain these systems, it’s time to consider professional IT services.
As your business grows, you may find yourself needing to manage hybrid cloud environments, automate workflows, or ensure seamless integration between various software platforms. These tasks require advanced skills in network architecture, system administration, and cybersecurity. According to a recent survey, 61% of small to medium-sized businesses experience IT challenges that hinder their growth, emphasizing the need for dedicated IT resources.
Failing to address these complexities can lead to inefficient processes, data silos, and security vulnerabilities. This is why many expanding businesses transition from relying on a “computer-savvy” employee to engaging IT professionals who can design and manage scalable, robust systems.
Increasing Security Risks and Compliance Requirements
Cybersecurity threats are becoming more sophisticated, and businesses face increasing regulatory demands regarding data protection. A person who is good with computers may lack the specialized knowledge to implement advanced security protocols or maintain compliance with standards like GDPR or HIPAA.
For example, data breaches have increased by 17% over the past year, affecting companies of all sizes. Failing to adequately protect sensitive customer and company data can result in severe financial penalties and damaged reputation. If your IT support is unable to provide robust security measures or keep up with compliance requirements, it’s time to reassess your approach.
Resources such as CentraLink’s website offer insights into compliance and system requirements that can guide businesses in upgrading their IT practices.
Moreover, cybersecurity today requires continuous monitoring, threat detection, incident response, and employee training. These are complex tasks that go beyond fixing computer problems and require dedicated expertise.
Frequent Downtime and Delayed Problem Resolution
When your business depends on a single individual who is good with computers rather than a trained IT professional, downtime can become a major problem. Frequent system crashes, slow network speeds, or unresolved technical issues can significantly impact productivity and customer satisfaction.
If you notice recurring IT problems that take days to fix or disrupt daily operations, this is a major red flag. Downtime costs businesses an average of $5,600 per minute, underscoring the financial impact of inadequate IT support.
For example, if your sales team cannot access the CRM due to server issues or your employees experience frequent email outages, the resulting delays can lead to missed opportunities and frustrated customers. Moreover, the person handling these problems might be juggling multiple roles, limiting their ability to respond quickly and effectively.
At this stage, outsourcing IT support or partnering with a managed services provider can ensure rapid response and proactive maintenance, minimizing downtime and improving system reliability. These providers often offer 24/7 monitoring and help desk support, ensuring issues are addressed before they escalate.
Lack of Strategic IT Planning
A person who is simply good with computers may be excellent at fixing immediate problems but might lack the strategic vision required for IT planning aligned with business goals. As your company grows, your technology needs should evolve in tandem with your expansion plans.
For instance, planning for scalable cloud solutions, cybersecurity frameworks, and compliance with industry regulations requires expertise in IT strategy. Without this, your business risks falling behind competitors who leverage technology effectively.
Strategic IT planning involves assessing future technology needs, budgeting for IT investments, and aligning technology initiatives with business objectives. If your current IT support doesn’t contribute to long-term planning or innovation, it’s a sign to seek professional guidance.
Many businesses choose to work with Complete Technology Solutions to ensure their IT infrastructure supports their growth ambitions.
Proactive IT planning can lead to better resource allocation, improved security postures, and enhanced operational agility. Without it, companies often face reactive approaches to technology issues, which can hinder growth and increase costs.
Employee Frustration and Inefficiency
When IT issues are frequent and unresolved, employee frustration grows, leading to decreased productivity and morale. If your team spends significant time waiting for technical help or dealing with slow systems, it’s a clear indication that your current IT support setup is insufficient.
Studies show that employees lose an average of 22 minutes per day dealing with IT problems, which adds up to nearly two weeks of lost productivity annually. 
This lost time can translate into missed deadlines, lower quality of work, and higher turnover rates. Employees who feel supported by their IT infrastructure tend to be more engaged and focused on their core responsibilities.
Investing in professional IT services can streamline operations, improve employee satisfaction, and free up internal resources to focus on core business activities. This investment often pays for itself through increased efficiency and reduced downtime.
Preparing for Future Growth
Beyond addressing current issues, outgrowing the person who is good with computers means preparing your business for future technological advancements. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation offer significant opportunities but require specialized knowledge to implement effectively.
A professional IT team can help your business adopt these innovations strategically, ensuring you remain competitive in a rapidly evolving marketplace. Additionally, they can provide training and support to help your staff adapt to new systems and workflows.
Furthermore, as your business expands geographically or into new markets, your IT needs will become more complex, involving multi-site connectivity, remote access solutions, and compliance with diverse regulations. Having a dedicated IT strategy and support system is essential to navigate these challenges successfully.
Conclusion
Relying on a person who is merely good with computers is a common approach for startups and smaller businesses. However, as your company grows, this arrangement can hinder progress, expose you to security risks, and reduce overall efficiency. Signs such as increased IT complexity, frequent downtime, lack of strategic planning, rising security threats, and employee frustration indicate that it’s time to upgrade your IT support.
By recognizing these warning signs early, you can make informed decisions to partner with professional IT providers who offer scalable, secure, and strategic technology solutions tailored to your business goals. Whether it’s seeking advice from resources like or choosing to, taking proactive steps will help ensure your technology infrastructure supports your growth now and into the future.
Making this transition not only safeguards your business operations but also empowers your team to focus on innovation and growth, positioning your company for long-term success in an increasingly digital world.

articles.title: Bengaluru-based Inkle acquires Finally’s bookkeeping arm, expands team to 160
articles.text:
Bengaluru-based Inkle acquires Finally’s bookkeeping arm, expands team to 160
Bengaluru-built, San Francisco-headquartered CPA firm Inkle has acquired Finally's bookkeeping division in an undisclosed all-cash deal, taking its team to about 160 people across five countries and extending it from startups to non-tech small businesses.
San Francisco-headquartered Inkle, an AI-driven accounting and bookkeeping firm for US companies that develops its technology in Bengaluru, has purchased the bookkeeping arm of small-business finance platform Finally. The price has not been revealed. Inkle describes the deal as an all-cash asset purchase and says it is the company’s first acquisition.
Around 100 Finally employees based in the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Miami, Boca Raton and New York will join Inkle’s 60-member team in Bengaluru, comprising engineers, product designers, tax professionals and bookkeepers. With a workforce of about 160 across five countries, Inkle says it can provide round-the-clock support to clients across the Americas and Asia. Finally’s existing bookkeeping customers will continue working with their current teams, while accessing services through Inkle’s software.
The acquisition also changes who Inkle works for. Until now, the firm’s clients have been mainly venture-backed startups. Finally’s customers are largely non-tech small businesses, including contractors, clinics, restaurants, professional services firms and owner-operators, a group Inkle regards as the core of America’s employer base.
“Ranvir and I are delighted to announce Inkle’s first acquisition,” said Anand Krishna, co-founder and CEO of Inkle. “Inkle is an American company that serves American small businesses, and it’s built in Bengaluru. That combination is our edge: U.S. CPAs who own the outcome, and an engineering team in India building the software and AI that let them serve far more businesses, far better, than a traditional firm. We’re building the AI-powered Big Four, and this acquisition helps us take that to the businesses that make up most of the American economy.”
Inkle cites a shortage of accounting professionals in the US as a factor behind the deal, with many CPAs and bookkeepers nearing retirement and fewer new entrants joining the profession. The AICPA’s 2025 Trends Report recorded 55,152 accounting degrees awarded in 2023-24, down 6.6% from the previous year. Inkle expects technology-led platforms to play a role in addressing the talent gap, with Indian engineers and finance professionals contributing to their development.
The company was set up in 2022 by Krishna, who runs it from San Francisco, and Ranvir Singh, who oversees technology from Bengaluru. It combines a US-licensed CPA practice with product, engineering and AI development carried out in India. The Bengaluru team built both Inkle Books, the firm’s general ledger, and its tax and compliance platform. Because developers work next to the accountants who use their tools, Inkle says problems flagged by the delivery side are frequently resolved within a day. It sees moving Finally’s team onto this platform as the most demanding test of that approach so far.
Inkle is also a frequent first stop for Indian founders looking to expand internationally. Each year it helps hundreds of businesses incorporate in the US, many of them Delaware C-Corps formed to raise investment and win American customers. It then looks after their continuing obligations, from federal tax returns and Delaware franchise tax to cross-border filings such as Form 5472 and FBAR. It is also the cross-border compliance partner for Stripe Atlas for Indian founders.
On funding, Inkle says it has become profitable after raising only $1.5 million in pre-seed capital from Picus Capital, Saison Capital and Force Ventures. That is well below what competing firms have raised, and several of those better-funded rivals have since exited the market. Inkle’s software costs nothing to use, and the company charges only for its AI-assisted bookkeeping, tax and compliance services. These can be delivered on Inkle Books, QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho Books or Mercury Books.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5127936 update released with 41 changes and fixes
articles.text:
Microsoft released the KB5127936 preview cumulative update for Windows 11 versions 25H2 and 26H2, with 41 changes, including File Explorer and Cloud rebuild improvements.
KB5127936 is a preview update that adds new features and fixes at the end of each month, letting IT admins and users test them before they roll out to the entire user base during next month's Patch Tuesday.
However, unlike regular Patch Tuesday cumulative updates, monthly preview updates are optional and don't include security patches.
The October 2026 preview update makes the File Explorer context menu faster and easier to customize, letting users choose which app extensions and commands appear and how they're organized.
After you install KB5127936, Cloud rebuild can also reinstall Windows without USB media or a custom image, using an image and drivers downloaded directly from Windows Update, even when Windows won't start.
Microsoft also updated XBOX mode to include a refreshed Gaming Task View with quick access to key system actions like Power Options and Exit to Desktop while gaming via a new navigation bar.
You can install the KB5127936 preview update by downloading it from the Microsoft Update Catalog or by opening Settings, going to Windows Update, and selecting "Check for Updates."
Because this is an optional update, you will need to click the "Download and install" link unless you have "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" enabled (which prompts the OS to install it automatically).
Windows 11 KB5127936 highlights
Once installed, this optional non-security update will upgrade Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2 devices to builds 26200.9818 and 26300.9818, respectively.
The October 2026 preview update adds further changes and improvements, some of the more important ones highlighted below:
- New! This update improves the Privacy & security page in Windows Settings by grouping related Camera, Microphone, and Location privacy controls and elevating usage information from linked pages onto the main page.
- New! This update enables Windows recovery (WinRE) to automatically reuse eligible Wi-Fi profiles already saved in Windows, including supported certificate-based networks. Devices can now get online automatically during recovery scenarios such as quick machine recovery or cloud rebuild, without preconfiguring Wi-Fi credentials in WinRE. This capability is on by default, and IT admins can disable it. Microsoft disclosed this feature last month, and it is now beginning to roll out.
- New! This update introduces a Restore Summary that appears after you restore a backup profile to a new device. The summary clearly shows what was restored, including Windows settings and the list of Microsoft Store apps. This improves transparency during device transitions, helps you validate your restore results, and lets you continue setup on your new device with confidence.
- New! This update improves the adaptive hibernate policy to provide faster Modern Standby instant-on resumes while helping preserve battery life when the charge is low. Noticeable changes include less hibernation when the battery is above 80% and earlier hibernation below 10%.
This month, Microsoft also reminded users that updated Secure Boot certificates are rolling out to replace the original 2011 certificates, which will expire in late June 2027.
Microsoft first announced plans to refresh expiring Secure Boot certificates on eligible Windows 11 systems in January, after warning users and IT admins in November 2025 to update them before they expire.
The company also warned customers they may need to reboot one more time after installing the October 2026 optional update and updates rolling out over the next several months.
"With recent and upcoming Windows updates over the next few months, a limited number of consumer and business devices might experience one additional restart during installation," Microsoft noted in a message center update. "This one‑time restart occurs after a Secure Boot certificate update is applied as part of the Secure Boot update process."
