articles.title: Écran OLED, Dynamic Island et châssis affiné... mais puces M5 Pro / Max : Apple dévoile son premier MacBook Pro tactile
articles.text:
Après des années de fuites éparses, de rumeurs incessantes et de spéculations à tout va, Apple présente enfin son tout premier MacBook Pro à écran tactile. L’appareil s’appuie, comme prévu, sur un châssis affiné et passe à la technologie d’affichage OLED. Voici ce qu’il faut retenir de ce nouveau produit.
On savait que ces 27 et 28 octobre 2026 seraient chargés en matière de nouveaux Mac, ils le sont effectivement. Après avoir dévoilé hier ses iMac M6 et MacBook Pro M6, aux designs inchangés, Apple dégaine aujourd’hui un tout nouveau MacBook Pro qui fera date : il est en effet le premier à intégrer un écran OLED tactile. Une particularité à laquelle le géant de Cupertino s’était jusqu’à présent refusé, et qui propulse donc, pour la première fois, macOS dans l’univers de la commande du bout des doigts.
Un MacBook Pro OLED plus léger, avec Dynamic Island et logo lumineux… Mais sans nouveauté côté puces
La grosse nouveauté de ce nouveau modèle est donc l’écran choisi par Apple : une dalle tandem-OLED (avec deux couches de pixels auto-émissifs) de 14,2 ou 16,3 pouces, avec prise en charge des commandes tactiles et jusqu’à 2000 cd/m2 de luminosité maximale en SDR.
Fidèle à ses habitudes en la matière, Apple donne à cet écran, qui s’annonce d’ores et déjà comme l’un des plus beaux du marché, une dénomination marketing bien particulière : PROLED XDR. Cette dalle organique promet quoi qu’il en soit d’afficher jusqu’à 10 000 000:1 de taux de contraste tout en délivrant une gamme de couleurs toujours plus riche, couvrant cette fois aussi bien le gamut DCI-P3 que le spectre Adobe RGB (ou l’espace de couleurs Rec. 2020, qui sera pour sa part géré à plus de 80 %)… et ce, tout en continuant d’offrir la technologie de rafraîchissement dynamique ProMotion de manière à osciller entre 10 et 120 Hz en fonction des contenus affichés.
Apple annonce aussi exploiter, sur cet écran PROLED XDR, un moteur d’affichage capable de gérer indépendamment chaque pixel, en tenant compte de l’usure, de la température et du contenu. On apprend aussi que des préréglages de référence seront au menu pour le cinéma, la photo et même l’imagerie médicale, tandis que le traitement nano-texturé de l’écran restera proposé en option, mais avec une nouveauté : la nano-texture étant désormais gravée directement dans le verre.
Fonction tactile oblige, Apple explique enfin avoir revu la charnière de son nouveau MacBook Pro pour la rendre moins souple afin d’éviter au maximum les vibrations lorsque l’on interagira de manière tactile avec l’appareil. La firme indique par ailleurs avoir travaillé à une réduction de la latence pour permettre des commandes tactiles extrêmement réactives.
Autre petit détail qui tend à prouver qu’Apple a soigné sa copie, on apprend que la webcam 12 Mpx de l’appareil (désormais logée dans une Dynamic Island et non plus dans une encoche) dispose d’une stabilisation vidéo pour que l’image ne tremble pas quand on touche l’écran durant une visioconférence.
Quant à macOS, il a été calibré pour convertir automatiquement les touchers en clics, avec de nouvelles animations et de nouvelles API proposées aux développeurs pour exploiter toujours mieux ces nouvelles commandes tactiles / gestuelles.
Lancement le 6 novembre prochain, à partir de 3299 euros
Côté design, il y a bien de la nouveauté aussi, mais elle saute un peu moins aux yeux. On retrouve globalement les lignes des précédentes générations de MacBook Pro Apple Silicon, mais avec un châssis légèrement affiné et allégé.
Apple évoque notamment un châssis plus léger : 1,38 kg pour le modèle de 14 pouces et 1,82 kg pour celui de 16 pouces. Pour le formuler autrement, comptez 230 grammes de moins pour nouveau MacBook OLED de 14 pouces et 320 grammes en moins pour son grand frère par rapport à la génération précédente. Quant à leur châssis, il s’amincit de 0,5 mm en 14 pouces et 1 mm en 16 pouces grâce à la finesse induite par la technologie OLED, qui permet aussi de basculer sur des bordures d’écran plus fines. Les deux moutures du MacBook Pro PROLED XDR resteront par contre proposées en noir sidéral et en argent.
Autre nouveauté, le retour d’un logo Apple illuminé sur le capot. La marque a toutefois peu communiqué là-dessus à ce stade, on ignore donc si ce rétroéclairage sera visible uniquement au démarrage (en même temps que le son de lancement de macOS), ou s’il sera persistant, à l’instar de ce que proposaient les MacBook d’il y a une bonne quinzaine d’années.
On notera enfin qu’Apple ne mise pas sur de nouvelles connectiques pour ses MacBook Pro PROLED XDR, qui conservent en l’occurrence trois ports Thunderbolt 5, une sortie HDMI, un port d’alimentation MagSafe 3, un lecteur SDXC et une prise casque.
Comme cela avait été pressenti, le géant californien s’en tient par ailleurs aux puces M5 Pro et M5 Max que l’on connaît depuis le début d’année. Ces nouveaux MacBook Pro ne passent donc pas une génération, ce qui laisse même à penser que les puces M6 Pro et M6 Max sont encore loin d’être prêtes… Et qu’Apple n’a pas souhaité les attendre pour dégainer ses nouveaux MacBook Pro à écran OLED tactile.
On retrouve quoi qu’il en soit une puce M5 Pro pouvant embarquer jusqu’à 18 cœurs CPU, 20 cœurs GPU et 64 Go de mémoire unifiée ; ou un processeur M5 Max combinant cette fois 18 cœurs CPU et jusqu’à 40 cœurs GPU pour un maximum de 128 Go de mémoire unifiée. Apple positionne d’ailleurs clairement cette version 128 Go comme une solution faite pour la gestion locale de très grands modèles de langage. Une manière de faire un joli pied de nez à NVIDIA et ses premières machines RTX Spark… qui ne tiennent pas toutes leurs promesses.
Apple explique enfin avoir doublé les vitesses de ses SSD pour permettre d’accroître encore un peu plus la réactivité du système et doper les transferts de fichiers en grands volumes. Les pros apprécieront. Pour le reste, ces nouveaux Mac sont censés tenir jusqu’à 24 heures sur batterie, se recharger à 50 % en 30 minutes et intégrer de nouveaux haut-parleurs offrant des graves plus profonds. Nous avons hâte de tester tout ça sur Clubic.
Reste le prix de ces nouveaux modèles. Il fait mal, comme on pouvait s’y attendre : 3299 euros en prix de départ pour le modèle de 14 pouces et 3899 euros pour la version de base du modèle de 16 pouces. Comptez d’ailleurs plus de 16 000 euros si vous voulez mettre la main sur le MacBook Pro 16 PROLED XDR le mieux équipé (M5 Max 40 cœurs GPU, 128 Go de RAM et 16 To de SSD). Les deux moutures de l’appareil sont quoi qu’il en soit attendues sur le marché français le 6 novembre prochain.
Source : Communiqué de presse Apple

articles.title: LiberNovo's $1299 office chair solves the big-and-tall ergonomics problem
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
If you can stomach the price tag, the LiberNovo Maxis is an exceptional chair. Specifically engineered for big and tall users, its broad seat, stylish design, and range of features including motorized lumbar support marks it out as a pro choice for professionals who want a comfortable, supportive sitting experience. I found it perfect while working all day. It's more office chair than most people need - the top model even has a cooling fan under the seat and a back massager. but it's that premium price that'll determine if this is the desk chair for you.
Reasons to buy
- + Properly designed for big and tall users
- + Incredibly comfortable all-day
- + Electric lumbar support
- + Built-in fan and decompression massager
- + Highly adjustable and ultra-stylish
- + Comes in three models and a range of bundles
Reasons to avoid
- - Premium pricing
- - Not suitable for small and average-sized users (the LiberNovo Omni series is)
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
- Engineered for users 5'10" to 6'7"
- Reinforced frame with weight load up to 399 lbs
- Motorized lumbar support and bionic FlexFit backrest
- Built-in fan and OmniStretch massager
- Controlled recline with Dynamic Support
I get it. Most people won’t need the LiberNovo Maxis. Most people will see the price, baulk, and close the website. It’s expensive, its headline features run on a rechargeable battery, and it’s more chair than your everyday hybrid or remote worker needs.
But it’s also ergonomic, stunningly designed, cleverly engineered, and built for big and tall users without the usual flabby, foamy designs that I see for half or even a quarter of the price of the Maxis. It’s also one of the best office chairs I’ve tested. If you're over 5'10", you'll want to check this out.
On top of that, the model I’m reviewing here - the Maxis Airflow - includes a cooling fan in the seat, electric lumbar adjustments, and a back massager called the OmniStretch designed for relieving tension.
So, this is not your everyday office chair. It’s an elite seat for professionals who prize all-day comfort, a stylish ergonomic design, supportive top-end features, and don’t mind paying a fair chunk of change for that.
LiberNovo Maxis: Price & availability
The LiberNovo Maxis is available direct from the maker, and I’m also seeing it at online retailers including Amazon and Best Buy.
I’ve danced around that price tag enough. In the US, the LiberNovo Maxis has a list price of $1299; from the UK site, it’s £1099. At the time of review, both are discounted to $1119 / £1002.
And that’s for the base manual model. The Maxis Electric, which includes the electric adjustments to the lower back support sends the price to $1799 / £1579, while the Maxis Airflow reviewed here is priced at $1859 / £1699 (although again, at time of review, they are discounted by around two-hundred bucks).
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
On top of that, you can buy the chair in three different bundles: the standalone chair, the Standard pack which comes with a footrest, and the Premium Bundle which also adds a spare rechargeable battery. Unless you’re using the electric features constantly, I’d recommend either the Basic or Standard bundle.
All in all, the Maxis is firmly in the premium price bracket, alongside top-tier brands in the office furniture world like Herman Miller and Steelcase. I can understand why, in terms of build quality and design.
| Seat depth | 20.47in / 52cm | 
| Backrest shoulder span | 16.93in / 43cm | 
| Backrest waist span | 20.47in / 52cm | 
| Headrest vertical range | 5.51in / 14cm | 
| Headrest horizontal range | 4.72in / 12cm | 
| Weight limit | Up to 399 lbs | 
| User height | 5'10" - 6'7" | 
- Value: 4 / 5
LiberNovo Maxis: Assembly
This beast of a chair came in two massive boxes (three, if you count the footrest).
As ever, I recommend building this in the room you’ll use it in because this one is heavy and unwieldy to move. The gouges and marks on my wall as I struggled to move it upstairs are evidence of that.
All told, it took me around 40 minutes from unboxing to fully built chair. That’s on the longer side, but LiberNovo makes assembly as easy as possible. Forget your little instruction manuals with walls of text. This one comes with a massive sheet of card that pictorially guides you through each and every step.
It’s also the first office chair I’ve ever tested that includes white gloves for handling it. Maybe that’s over the top, but can bet I pulled them on and wore them throughout the assembly process.
- Assembly: 5 / 5
LiberNovo Maxis: Design & build
Build quality and design are superb. The pieces feel weighty, and I experienced no creaking or squeaking as I swivelled, reclined, and generally made a nuisance of myself at my desk.
This is a premium chair across the board, right down to the wide single-piece aluminum base that feels like it will capably and confidently support anyone up to the recommended weight of 399 lbs (181kg).
Being built for big and tall users, the Maxis is designed for those between 5'10” and 6'7”. Now, I’m an inch shy of the minimum recommended height and yes, it is slightly too large for me - particularly in the broad seat, which provides ample width and depth. I had to dial down the adjustability on the headrest and armrests to its minimum settings to stay comfortable and snug. Effectively, my negative experience here is a positive for larger, taller body types.
In terms of design, I had one thought: This is like an office chair designed by HR Geiger with its Xenomorph-like exoskeleton on the tapering backrest. Unlike so many I test, it’s a real executive statement piece.
- Design & build: 5 / 5
LiberNovo Maxis: Performance & features
I always judge office chairs chiefly on two factors: comfort and support. Here, the LiberNovo Maxis is an easy win. I used this chair for eight hours a day while working and it stayed comfortable from first to last hour. After that, I spent a few extra hours in it, feet up on the footrest, while gaming. I still didn’t tire of the chair or feel fatigue or numbness that some cheap chairs can inflict on me.
And then, of course, there’s that back massager. Actually, I’m not sure ‘massager’ is the right word here. LiberNovo calls it the OmniStretch, billing it as a way to lean back and decompress. I’d liken it to having a couple of fists kneading deep into your lower back while the whole backrest quickly but gently vibrates. That may not sound comfortable, but I promise you it is. It runs for a set five minutes at the press of a button. My pregnant wife has been using it daily for relaxation and pain relief.
Now, I generally avoid foam and fabric office chairs. I run hot, and prefer breathable mesh. And while the seat can get warm when sitting down all day, I found the two-speed cooling fan - only available on the Airflow model - was a very good solution that actually helped maintain a cooler body temperature.
Adjustability is excellent on this chair, and I found it easy to fiddle around with the headrest, seat elevation, recline tension, and swivel armrests. However, the standout mechanism is the motorized lumbar support buttons located below the left armrest. So, I’m not constantly reaching under or around the chair to adjust the positioning for continued support.
What’s notable is the Dynamic Support, so when I reclined back, the seat stayed stable while the armrests dropped back with me so I could feel supported in any position. I appreciated the steady recline system in place here, too. As you lean back, it won’t suddenly fall back, but eases itself into position. The tension can be altered using the under-seat knob, while the recline can be set to lock at different angles depending on how far you want to lean back.
Where it lacks adjustments is the seat depth, which is fixed at a larger-than-average 52cm, which makes it more suitable for taller users. I would’ve also liked lockable armrests. Like a lot of office chairs, they’re directional, moving laterally and swinging in and out without much pressure. That’s fine if you’re getting up and moving around a lot, but not if you’re locking in for longer work sessions. But I appreciate this may be a me problem - I had the same complaint with the Boulies EP600 I recently reviewed.
As I say, it’s a lot of chair for the money - the only one I’ve tested that comes with a rechargeable battery. And not every professional, whether in the office or working hybrid/remote, will need a seat at this level. But I can’t fault the comfort or design at all.
- Performance & features: 5 / 5
Should I buy the LiberNovo Maxis?
✅ Buy it if...
You’re built bigger or taller. The Maxis is specifically engineered for larger body types without compromising on style, comfort, or support.
You want all the bells and whistles. This high-quality office chair does it all. If you’re going to splurge out, it might as well be one with a massager and fan.
❌ Don't buy it if...
You don’t need the extra features. You're paying for well-designed ergonomics and features most office chairs will never have.
You’re under 5’10”. I’d recommend the LiberNovo Omni or LiberNovo Omni Pro if you want the same design ethos.
How I tested the LiberNovo Maxis
For two weeks, the LiberNovo Maxis Airflow became my daily driver chair. Eight hours a day, minimum, I've been sitting on it at work. And, once the work laptop was closed, I carried on using it, both while gaming and using the OmniStretch massaging feature multiple times throughout the testing period (when I could get my wife to stop using it!). articles.title: CloudSEK launches incubator for cybersecurity startups
articles.text:
CloudSEK launches incubation programme for cybersecurity startups
Launchpad is a 12-week programme offering mentorship, investor connections, threat intelligence resources, and access to potential customers and channel partners.
Bengaluru-based AI-powered cybersecurity and threat intelligence company CloudSEK has launched CloudSEK Launchpad, a 12-week incubation programme for early-stage cybersecurity startups.
The first cohort will have 10 companies, each eligible for up to $5,000 in AI model credits. Applications are open until November 20, 2026.
According to a statement, the programme is built around product development and commercial adoption rather than mentorship alone. Selected founders will get weekly guidance from CloudSEK’s leadership on research, product, enterprise sales, and fundraising, along with access to its threat intelligence resources and researchers. CloudSEK will also introduce founders to potential customers and channel partners across India, the Gulf Cooperation Council region, and the United States.
The programme ends with a demo day where founders will pitch to investors and prospective customers.
Pre-seed and seed-stage startups can apply; so can idea-stage founders with a strong team and a clearly defined security problem. Areas of interest include security for AI systems and agents, AI-native security operations, threat intelligence, identity and fraud prevention, and software supply-chain security.
Rahul Sasi, Founder and CEO of CloudSEK, said, “When we started CloudSEK, I wished someone had shown us the shortcuts, which customers to call first, which mistakes cost a year and who to trust.
"AI has made it significantly easier to build sophisticated technology, but building a successful cybersecurity company still requires access to real threat intelligence, trusted customers and the right industry network. With Launchpad, we want to share what we have learned and help promising founders get to their first ten paying customers."
Alongside Launchpad, CloudSEK has also introduced KeyVigil, a secure gateway that lets applications and autonomous AI agents access frontier AI models through a single endpoint. It manages master API keys centrally, masks sensitive data before it reaches a model, and flags and blocks prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts. It also logs model interactions and lets organisations set spending limits for teams, applications and agents. KeyVigil is available to enterprise customers, and Launchpad participants will receive access to it through their credits.

articles.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
articles.text:
Cisco released security updates to patch a denial-of-service zero-day in Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Threat Defense (FTD) software that attackers are exploiting to remotely crash vulnerable firewall devices.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76418, this high-severity vulnerability affects devices running ASA and FTD software with configurations containing the 'webvpn' keyword and SSL VPN enabled on at least one interface.
Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition, causing the device to reload unexpectedly.
Cisco advised customers to patch vulnerable firewalls after its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) discovered evidence that the flaw was being exploited in the wild earlier this month. However, the company didn't provide indicators of compromise and hasn't shared additional information about the attacks, including which organizations are being targeted or who is exploiting the flaw.
"This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition," Cisco said.
"In October 2026, the Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability. Cisco strongly recommends that customers upgrade to a fixed software release to remediate this vulnerability."
While Cisco provided no workarounds that address this security issue, admins who can't immediately patch CVE-2026-76418 can mitigate it by disabling secondary authentication on the default DefaultWEBVPNGroup tunnel group or on any user-configured tunnel group list.
Currently, Internet monitoring platform Shadowserver tracks more than 51,000 Cisco ASA SSL VPN devices exposed online, but doesn't provide information on how many have already been secured or are honeypots.
Last year, Cisco patched two other flaws (CVE-2025-20362 and CVE-2025-20333) affecting ASA and FTD firewall devices in September and cautioned customers that attackers had exploited them in zero-day attacks targeting 5500-X Series devices with VPN web services enabled.
The same day, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issued Emergency Directive 25-03, ordering federal agencies to secure their Cisco firewall devices within 24 hours.
Cisco linked the attacks to the ArcaneDoor campaign, which had also been exploiting two other zero-days (CVE-2024-20353 and CVE-2024-20359) to breach government networks since November 2023.
More recently, in August, Cisco addressed another denial-of-service zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-20349) that attackers were actively exploiting in the wild to crash affected ASA and FTD firewall devices with SSL listen sockets enabled.
Earlier this month, it also warned customers to patch an actively exploited zero-day (CVE-2026-76519) in its Secure Email Gateway (SEG) security solution that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands remotely with root privileges.
Since November 2021, CISA has flagged 101 Cisco security flaws as exploited in the wild, seven of which were also abused by ransomware gangs.

articles.title: Oubliez votre carte bancaire : cette nouvelle façon de retirer de l'argent arrive sur tous les distributeurs
articles.text:
Oubliez votre carte bancaire : cette nouvelle façon de retirer de l'argent arrive sur tous les distributeurs
Vous êtes devant le distributeur automatique et votre portefeuille est resté à la maison ? Pas de panique. En 2026, l'absence de carte physique n'est plus un obstacle pour obtenir du liquide. Du retrait par code SMS au déploiement du cashback chez les commerçants, découvrez toutes les alternatives pour récupérer vos billets en un clin d'œil.
Carte perdue, oubliée sur un comptoir ou avalée par un automate capricieux… Les occasions de se retrouver démuni ne manquent pas. Pourtant, l’argent liquide reste indispensable au quotidien, que ce soit pour régler un achat sur un marché ou pour faire face aux petits commerces qui refusent encore le sans-contact. Heureusement, les alternatives à la carte bancaire traditionnelle se sont multipliées. Guichet, application mobile, technologie NFC ou passage chez le boulanger : voici les méthodes qui fonctionnent vraiment aujourd'hui.
Le retrait au guichet : l'alternative humaine et traditionnelle
La méthode la plus classique consiste à se présenter en agence. Munissez-vous d’une pièce d’identité valide (carte nationale d’identité ou passeport) et, si vous l’avez, de votre chéquier. L’agent vous demandera de remplir un chèque à l’ordre de l’agence ou un bordereau de retrait avec vos coordonnées bancaires et le montant souhaité. Aujourd’hui, la plupart des établissements peuvent aussi vous identifier directement par informatique, en vérifiant votre identité et vos coordonnées de compte, ce qui rend le chéquier facultatif.
Attention aux frais de retrait hors agence
L’opération est généralement gratuite dans votre propre agence, mais l’addition peut grimper dès que vous sollicitez une autre agence du même réseau. La Banque Postale facture par exemple 6 € par retrait dans un bureau de poste différent de votre agence de rattachement, avec un plafond de 800 € sur sept jours glissants. Chez Banque Populaire, le retrait est gratuit dans votre agence, mais il peut coûter au moins 11 € si vous vous rendez au guichet d’une autre agence du réseau. La Société Générale se montre plus souple avec la gratuité jusqu’à 3 000 € dans toute agence équipée d’une caisse, mais facture 30 € par opération au-delà de ce montant.
Les limites du service de caisse
Un détail est important à garder en tête : de moins en moins d’agences disposent d’un service de caisse physique. Il est vivement conseillé d’appeler votre conseiller avant de vous déplacer, surtout si le montant souhaité dépasse 1 500 €. La banque peut exiger un délai de prévenance de 24 à 48 heures. Enfin, retirer dans une banque différente de la vôtre avec un chèque non barré est devenu extrêmement rare et reste dissuasif en raison des frais cumulés des deux établissements.
Le smartphone au distributeur : quand votre banque devient virtuelle
Plusieurs banques françaises proposent désormais un service de retrait au distributeur sans carte physique, directement depuis leur application mobile. Le principe reste identique : vous préparez l’opération sur votre téléphone, la banque génère des codes temporaires, et vous les saisissez sur le clavier du distributeur.
SM@RT’retrait de la Banque Populaire
Depuis l’application mobile, vous créez un jeton électronique à 9 chiffres en choisissant le compte à débiter. Ce jeton reste valable 24 heures et le retrait peut être programmé jusqu’à 5 jours à l’avance. Devant le distributeur, il suffit de saisir le jeton puis un code secret à 4 chiffres défini lors de l’activation. L’avantage principal est que ce retrait n’impute pas le plafond de votre carte bancaire habituelle.
E-Retrait au Crédit Mutuel et CIC
Ce système repose sur un double code. L’application génère un numéro virtuel à 10 chiffres valable deux jours, tandis qu’un code de confirmation arrive par SMS. Au distributeur, un bouton spécifique permet de déclencher l’option E-Retrait pour entrer les deux codes. Le service est gratuit mais reste une solution de dépannage, avec des quotas limités à une opération par jour et seulement quatre par an.
Retrait SMS à la Caisse d’Épargne
Le fonctionnement est ici plus simple. Après la demande sur l’application, vous recevez un code à 9 chiffres par SMS. Devant l’automate, une touche latérale active le mode retrait sans carte pour saisir ce code ainsi qu'un code secret à 4 chiffres choisi lors de l'inscription. BNP Paribas et Société Générale proposent des services similaires fonctionnant sur les guichets du réseau mutualisé Cash Services.
Le sans-contact (NFC) : l'avenir du distributeur automatique
Si votre carte bancaire est enregistrée dans Apple Pay, Google Wallet ou Samsung Pay, votre smartphone peut la remplacer directement au distributeur. L’opération est très rapide : il suffit d’approcher le téléphone du lecteur sans contact du DAB, de valider votre identité par empreinte digitale ou reconnaissance faciale, puis de taper le code PIN de votre carte sur le clavier de l'automate. Cette méthode est particulièrement prisée par les clients des néobanques, même si tous les distributeurs français ne sont pas encore équipés de lecteurs NFC.
Le Cashback : transformer votre commerçant en distributeur de billets
Le retrait d’espèces à l’achat, ou cashback, permet de récupérer du liquide en caisse lors d’un paiement par carte. Vous payez un montant supérieur au prix de vos achats et le commerçant vous rend la différence. Bien que le plafond actuel soit fixé à 60 €, le service est en pleine mutation.
La fin des restrictions et l'ouverture à toutes les cartes
Dès 2026, le GIE Cartes Bancaires prévoit d’ouvrir ces points de retrait aux 77 millions de porteurs de cartes CB. Jusqu’ici, seuls les clients de la même banque que le commerçant pouvaient réellement en profiter dans la plupart des réseaux. Les premiers tests de cette ouverture généralisée débutent cette année avec La Banque Postale et le Crédit Agricole.
Évolution législative et nouveaux plafonds
Une proposition de loi adoptée fin 2025 vise à faire passer le plafond de retrait de 60 à 150 € tout en offrant des incitations fiscales aux commerçants. Par ailleurs, la future directive européenne DSP3 prévoit d’autoriser les retraits en magasin même sans achat préalable, avec un plafond pouvant atteindre 150 €, bien que son application complète ne soit pas attendue avant la fin de l’année 2026.
Cash Services : la mutualisation des distributeurs pour vous simplifier la vie
BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Mutuel et CIC ont décidé de fusionner leurs parcs de distributeurs sous une marque commune nommée Cash Services. Ce projet prévoit plus de 6 000 points d’accès d’ici fin 2026, installés dans les agences mais aussi dans les zones de flux comme les gares ou les centres commerciaux.
Un réseau transparent et gratuit pour les usagers
Pour les clients de ces quatre enseignes, les retraits en euros sont désormais gratuits sur tous les automates du réseau, même s'ils appartiennent à une autre banque du groupement. Ces nouveaux automates permettent également de réaliser des dépôts d'espèces, de remettre des chèques sans carte en saisissant simplement son RIB, ou encore d'imprimer des documents bancaires.
Maintenir l'accès aux espèces en zone rurale
Cette mutualisation répond à la baisse globale de l'usage du liquide dans les paiements courants. En rationalisant l'infrastructure, les banques cherchent à maintenir un service de proximité, notamment dans les zones rurales où l'accès aux distributeurs automatiques était devenu problématique ces dernières années.
Urgence à l’étranger : le dernier recours du mandat
En cas de perte de carte à l'étranger, le mandat cash international de La Poste peut dépanner. Un proche en France verse la somme dans un bureau de poste et vous récupérez le montant dans un point de vente local. Il existe une formule ordinaire en quelques jours et une formule express en 24 heures. Bien que les frais soient élevés, c'est une solution de sécurité indispensable quand on se retrouve totalement démuni loin de chez soi.
Un conseil : activez vos services avant d’en avoir besoin
La plupart de ces solutions existent déjà mais restent méconnues des usagers. Le principal obstacle est que leur activation nécessite souvent une authentification forte ou un délai de sécurité. Le bon réflexe est donc d'activer le service de retrait mobile de votre banque dès maintenant, tant que votre carte est encore en votre possession. Repérez également les automates compatibles à proximité de votre domicile pour ne pas être pris au dépourvu le jour où vous en aurez réellement besoin.

articles.title: Android Auto revient sur l’écran de votre smartphone grâce à cette application
articles.text:
Au début d’Android Auto, l’interface fonctionnait sans problème sur les écrans de nos téléphones. Mais Google a décidé de basculer l’application uniquement vers l’écran de la voiture, mettant fin en 2022 à l’affichage sur l’écran des smartphones. Depuis, il n’y avait pas vraiment d’alternative. Un manque qu’a décidé de combler un développeur avec son application PhoneAuto.
Une version encore en bêta
L’application PhoneAuto utilise la fonctionnalité de serveur d’unité centrale pour exécuter Android Auto directement en local sur le téléphone. Cette méthode demande quelques manipulations supplémentaires, comme le fait de devoir appuyer sur un bouton de fermeture dans les notifications pour couper le serveur une fois l’utilisation terminée, même si l’application peut partiellement automatiser cette tâche si vous lui donnez les permissions d’accessibilité nécessaires.
Concernant l’état actuel de l’outil, il s’agit d’une version bêta disponible pour le moment en téléchargement anticipé sur GitHub, avec une date d’expiration fixée au mois de janvier prochain, en attendant une publication officielle sur le Google Play Store.
Une application déjà fonctionnelle
Les premiers retours sont plutôt encourageants, avec encore quelques bugs inhérents à son statut d’application en cours de bêta. Testé sur un Galaxy Z Fold 8, le mode portrait souffre par exemple de quelques ralentissements, mais le mode paysage tourne correctement sur l’écran interne comme sur la dalle externe du téléphone pliant de Samsung, avec un affichage qui s’adapte automatiquement à l’écran.
N’attendez pas un taux de rafraîchissement élevé comme sur les écrans de bord des voitures récentes, mais PhoneAuto a au moins le mérite de proposer une solution viable pour ramener Android Auto sur l’écran de nos smartphones.

articles.title: Mozilla apela a la nostalgia con memes clásicos de internet para recuperar usuarios de Firefox
articles.text:
Mozilla apela a la nostalgia con memes clásicos de internet para recuperar usuarios de Firefox. La compañía lanzó un video publicitario que reúne a varias de las figuras más reconocibles de la cultura viral de los años 2000, con un tono cómico que esconde un mensaje sobre la privacidad digital.
El anuncio, de aproximadamente un minuto de duración, plantea una pregunta que funciona como eje de toda la campaña: “¿Cómo es que internet es menos privado que en 2006, cuando toda la familia compartía un solo ordenador?”.
Qué memes aparecen en el anuncio de Firefox
Entre los protagonistas del video figuran el cantante Tay Zonday, conocido por su canción Chocolate Rain, y Chuck Testa, otro de los rostros recurrentes de la era dorada de los memes.
También aparecen la Novia psicópata, Annoying Orange y el protagonista de Numa Numa, que con una cámara de baja resolución popularizó su particular parodia de Dragostea din tei, del grupo O-Zone.
El listado se completa con figuras que no surgieron en YouTube, como Bad Luck Brian y Apparently Kid, el niño conocido como Noah Ritter que se hizo viral por una entrevista espontánea frente a las cámaras.
Todos ellos representan una etapa en la que el contenido viral se construía con imágenes de baja resolución, texto plano y composiciones caseras que, pese a su simpleza técnica, lograban alcance global.
Por qué Firefox usa la nostalgia como estrategia publicitaria
El mensaje central del video busca contraponer dos momentos de internet. Por un lado, una época en la que la red se percibía como un espacio más personal y espontáneo, incluso cuando los equipos de cómputo eran compartidos por toda una familia.
Por otro lado, un presente en el que los datos de los usuarios circulan de forma constante y las empresas destinan sumas de dinero considerables para acceder a esa información.
Con ese contraste, Mozilla busca posicionar a Firefox como una alternativa para proteger los datos personales, tanto en dispositivos móviles como en computadoras, frente a navegadores como Edge.
Cómo reaccionaron los usuarios al video de los memes
Aunque la campaña incluye una reflexión explícita sobre la privacidad, buena parte de la recepción del público se enfocó en el componente nostálgico del video, dejando en segundo plano el mensaje original de la marca.
Muchos usuarios compararon la pieza con los antiguos YouTube Rewind, aquellos resúmenes anuales que Google producía para reunir lo más relevante y viral de cada año en la plataforma.
También se señaló que algunos de los memes seleccionados tienen un carácter muy específico dentro de la cultura de internet estadounidense y que, en otros países, no alcanzaron la misma repercusión en su momento.
Google Chrome ahora utiliza tus correos de Gmail para autocompletar formularios
Google ha lanzado una versión avanzada de la función de autocompletado para Chrome que extrae información directamente de los correos de Gmail para llenar formularios en línea. Esta herramienta ya se está desplegando en Estados Unidos, tanto en computadoras de escritorio como en las aplicaciones de Gemini en Chrome para iOS y Android.
A diferencia del sistema anterior, que se limitaba a utilizar únicamente los datos almacenados de forma manual en el navegador, la nueva actualización es capaz de escanear los mensajes recibidos para sugerir información específica.
Entre los datos que puede extraer automáticamente se encuentran números de confirmación de vuelos, códigos de seguimiento de envíos, números de pedidos, credenciales de socios, direcciones, teléfonos y tarjetas de crédito.
Esta función es una extensión de Personal Intelligence, un sistema que conecta las diversas aplicaciones de Google con el asistente Gemini para gestionar datos y resolver consultas complejas.
El uso de esta herramienta es completamente opcional, permitiendo a los usuarios activarla o desactivarla desde la configuración de Chrome, y Google garantiza que toda la información sensible se procesa bajo protocolos de cifrado.

Sa dalle PixelSense de 13,8 pouces affiche une définition de 2 304 x 1 536 pixels, soit un format 3:2 plus haut que le 16:9 classique. articles.title: Gartner says only 3% of organizations are getting AI cost savings from productivity, yet 85% plan to spend more
articles.text:
Facepalm: Ever since it started making its way into the workplace, we've been told that AI will skyrocket productivity and cut costs – promises that have also been used to justify layoffs. So, how many organizations are actually exceeding their cost-saving targets through productivity gains? According to Gartner, a massive 3%.
The figure comes from Gartner's HR Symposium in Orlando. In a finding that perfectly sums up the blind faith so many executives have in AI, 77% of board members expect the technology will deliver value in the form of productivity and cost savings. This is despite 97% of organizations being unable to achieve cost savings through productivity alone.
CV Viverito, senior director analyst for Gartner's HR practice, said that organizations will not generate cost savings from AI at this point. "The greater opportunity is to use AI to do things that weren't possible before, such as shifting employee time into new capabilities, outcomes, and sources of growth," Viverito added.
Another entirely unsurprising finding is that almost four in ten companies are now over budget on their AI spending. But when has overspending on something that isn't bringing the promised cost-reduction gains discouraged execs? Despite everything, 85% of companies say they are planning on spending even more next year.
None of this should come as a shock to anyone paying attention to similar surveys. In January, PwC's latest Global CEO survey, completed by 4,454 chief executive officers across 95 countries, revealed that 56% of CEOs had seen no cost or revenue benefits since introducing AI to their businesses.
There was also a 2025 MIT report that said 95% of AI implementations don't increase profits, while a 2024 survey found generative AI could actually be harming productivity at work.
So, what does Gartner recommend companies actually do? For starters, agree on what they're trying to achieve. Its survey of 297 chief HR officers found that 78% reported no agreement among leaders on where AI creates value. Apparently, that discussion can wait until after the money has been spent.
Gartner wants businesses to focus investment where AI can make a difference, help managers redesign work, and use their existing AI expertise. It also recommends doing something useful with the time employees save. Just 21% of the time freed up by AI went toward more innovative work. Meta's CTO would probably have a lot to say about that part.

articles.title: Oji Udezue's $10m Enzi Prize to crack AI's cost for Africa
articles.text:
Oji Udezue has built products that made millions in Silicon Valley, serving as chief product officer at Typeform and Calendly, product lead at Twitter, and head of product at Atlassian. On Moonshot’s Emerging Tech stage, he returned to the question he says keeps drawing him back to Africa: who is a technology actually for?
Frontier AI, he argued, is being priced out of reach for most of the continent, and the Enzi Prize is his attempt to change who can afford to use it. “It’s for the person in your village who’s not educated,” he said. “Otherwise, we would be the most selfish generation that ever existed.”
His argument rests on a number. Running a frontier, “Fable-class” model costs roughly $50 per million tokens today, by Udezue’s benchmark. The prize aims to bring that down to about $5, and ideally to a much lower amount. “We say 100x because maybe we’re hedging our bets,” he told the room.
To pursue that goal, the Enzi Prize Foundation, a Delaware non-profit backed by the Africa Deep Tech Foundation, TechCabal, Future Africa and Talent Nation, is offering a $10 million prize purse as part of a roughly $14 million initiative.
The aim is to make AI cheaper and fluent in African languages and contexts. According to Udezue, a cheap model that scores well on standard tests is of little use if it has never heard of a tropical disease or the things “people in my village know that are not anywhere on the internet”. Entries must first meet a minimum standard — what he called “a master’s in intelligence and a PhD in African context and African languages” — before competing on cost.
Submissions, whether cloud systems or models that run on a phone, are ranked on a public, open-source leaderboard, with rotating, sealed questions to prevent teams from gaming it. Winners retain their intellectual property but must publish an open, royalty-free version for use in Africa and the Global South.
The model is the Ansari X-Prize: offer a reward for a desired breakthrough and let competition draw in investment to achieve it. “If I put up $10 for you to chase,” he said, “people will spend $9 to chase 10.” He noted that a $20,000 pilot had already “brought a lot of talented people out of the woodwork”, producing the demos shown earlier that afternoon. “What would $10 million do?”
The purse is not yet fully funded. Udezue said he had spoken with OpenAI and Google that day, and estimated that winning the prize could take three to six years. His closing appeal was less for money than for belief: “Let’s make inference part of African innovation.”

articles.title: Medio Ambiente autoriza a Amazon a gastar un 48 % más de agua en su centro de datos de El Burgo de Ebro (Zaragoza)
articles.text:
El Instituto Aragonés de Gestión Ambiental (Inaga) ha autorizado a Amazon Web Services a aumentar un 48 % la dotación de agua de su centro de datos de El Burgo de Ebro. Según El Periódico de Aragón, el organismo no aprecia efectos significativos sobre el medio ambiente (aunque sospechamos que muchos agricultores no estarán de acuerdo) y da por hecho que la misma medida se extenderá a los complejos de Villanueva de Gállego y Huesca, para los que la compañía pidió lo mismo. La resolución se publicará en el Boletín Oficial de Aragón en los próximos días.
Cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí. Empecemos con un resumen breve:
- 2022: entran en servicio los primeros centros de AWS en Aragón.
- 2023: el Gobierno aragonés modifica el PIGA para ampliar su capacidad energética.
- Finales de 2024: AWS pide modificar su evaluación ambiental simplificada.
- Enero de 2026: Ecologistas en Acción anuncia un contencioso contra el PIGA.
- Finales de agosto: el Gobierno central presenta un borrador de decreto más exigente.
- 15 de septiembre: nueva restricción de riego en el Gállego.
- 2 de octubre: Heraldo revela que AWS paga el IAE en Madrid.
- 8 de octubre: AWS anuncia que pagará el impuesto en los municipios.
- 26 y 27 de octubre: el Gobierno suaviza el decreto.
Qué ha resuelto ahora. El proyecto no tendrá que pasar por una evaluación de impacto ambiental ordinaria. Eso no significa vía libre sin más: AWS deberá modificar su autorización ambiental integrada y aportar información detallada sobre consumos previstos, caudales de abastecimiento, volúmenes de aguas residuales, sistemas de tratamiento y capacidad de los depósitos. También tendrá que cumplir la normativa contra la legionelosis y de protección contra incendios, aplicar un plan de vigilancia ambiental con seguimiento continuo y restaurar el terreno cuando se desmantele la instalación.
Por qué piden más agua. AWS solicitó el cambio a finales de 2024. El diseño original calculaba 555 horas al año de uso de agua para refrigeración. La memoria, elaborada por la consultora Tauw Iberia, dispara esa cifra a 900 horas. La empresa sostiene que, tras dos años de funcionamiento, los valores aprobados no reflejan con exactitud las últimas condiciones climáticas del emplazamiento. A cambio, ha retrasado el umbral al que el sistema pasa del free cooling a la refrigeración con agua, de 28,3 a 29,4 ºC, lo que, según el documento, reduce el uso.
El número que importa. Los 53.961 m³ no son lo que gastará AWS en la zona. Con la ampliación de la región de datos, el agregado máximo asciende a 917.603 m³ al año, es decir, 0,92 hectómetros cúbicos. Para ponerlo en contexto, el diario recuerda que las papeleras de la Ribera Baja superan los 20 hectómetros cúbicos.
AWS añade que el centro de El Burgo de Ebro toma agua del Canal Imperial de Aragón y que su demanda actual, de 36.662 m³, supone el 0,009 % del total. Esa cifra queda 201 m³ por encima del tope anterior (y el texto no explica por qué). Un estudio ambiental previo hablaba de unos 755.000 m³ para las nuevas instalaciones, y Ecologistas en Acción ya avisaba de que sería difícil comprobar cuánta agua se extrae.
Las medidas de AWS. La compañía ha fusionado dos plantas de tratamiento previstas en una sola, con nanofiltración, que debería recuperar cerca del 70 % del agua, y ampliará el almacenamiento in situ hasta 72 horas. Aparte, el diario enumera dos proyectos relacionados: tres tanques de tormentas en los nuevos centros y la financiación de 25 kilómetros de renovación del Canal Imperial para evitar fugas. Las cifras de ahorro de AWS, más de 10.000 millones de litros al año en 2030, son de la propia empresa.
Las alegaciones. Ecologistas en Acción y Tu Nube Seca Mi Río argumentaron que el cambio climático ya debía estar en la solicitud original. Recordaron además que una investigación de El País estimó que el centro de Huesca consumió casi el doble de lo concedido. Piden controles independientes, porque la regulación no obliga a las empresas a informar de lo que gastan. AWS defiende que necesita margen para años anómalos como 2022, y asegura que sus centros solo usan agua por encima de los 30 grados.
Regantes contra la nube. El 15 de septiembre, la acequia de Camarera, en la cuenca del Gállego, vio recortada su concesión al 35 %. Era la segunda restricción del verano, tras el 60 % de agosto, y afectaba a unas 4.500 hectáreas. El colectivo No es sequía, es saqueo lo vincula con los proyectos de Villanueva de Gállego, Villamayor y La Puebla de Alfindén, y sostiene que los centros conectados a redes urbanas tienen prioridad legal sobre el riego.
El de El Burgo de Ebro no está en esa zona, pero bebe del Canal Imperial, una infraestructura de regadío cuya comunidad de usuarios colabora con AWS en el proyecto de modernización. En Teruel, la comunidad de regantes de Gaén mantiene bloqueadas las negociaciones sobre ceder agua del Ebro.
¿Y la respuesta? Ese mismo 15 de septiembre, Jorge Azcón defendió en un foro organizado por AWS que la industria del dato aporta más agua de la que consume. Los críticos contestan que ahorrar en el campo no elimina el consumo del centro.
Impuestos y calle. Cuando se supo lo del IAE, el alcalde de El Burgo de Ebro, Vicente Royo, habló de algo “lamentable y vergonzoso”. Después hubo manifestaciones y marchas. Ya había precedentes: en Cuarte, los vecinos lograron que Amazon desviara una línea de alta tensión, y en Walqa (Huesca) rechazaron un centro en la primera consulta vecinal de Aragón. AWS prometió pagar el IAE en los municipios y abonar cuatro años de atrasos, sin dar cifras. Según la prensa aragonesa, también saldó 194.000 euros de IBI pendientes en El Burgo de Ebro.
Un decreto más blando. El borrador de agosto aplicaba las normas a partir de 1 MW. Según Reuters, el umbral sube ahora a 10 MW, con el 80 % de suministro renovable y un régimen transitorio de hasta cinco años. El Gobierno de Aragón había presentado cinco alegaciones al texto. Los colectivos del agua señalan que fija parámetros de eficiencia, pero no límites al consumo en sequía.
Lo que está en juego. AWS calcula una inversión global de 33.700 millones de euros hasta 2035. Los centros emplean a pocos trabajadores directos y, a pleno rendimiento, consumirían más electricidad que toda la comunidad. Las preguntas abiertas son tres: quién mide cuánta agua usa cada centro, qué prioridad tendrá el regadío en una restricción y qué dirá la justicia sobre el PIGA.
En la misma cuenca del Ebro, el embalse riojano de Mansilla, que sirve a riego y energía, tiene expuestas ahora calles enteras de su antiguo pueblo sumergido. Esa es la imagen de un otoño seco, el mismo en el que Aragón ha permitido ampliar el agua de un centro de datos. Al menos podremos preguntarle a Alexa qué tiempo hará mañana.
Portada | Propuesta de centro de datos para Meta Platforms Inc. en Kuna, Idaho. Solo con fines ilustrativos.
En Xataka | Aragón se está llenando de centros de datos pero la pregunta es a dónde se está yendo el dinero

articles.title: Jetzt auch Apple: Wieso Laptops mit Touchscreen für mich sinnlos sind
articles.text:
Jetzt auch Apple: Wieso Laptops mit Touchscreen für mich sinnlos sind
Und plötzlich touchen alle am Bildschirm. Denn das ist bei Apples neuem Macbook Pro so gewollt. Es ist nicht nur mit einem OLED-Display ausgestattet, sondern eben auch berührungsempfindlich. Dabei hatte Steve Jobs schon vor 25 Jahren bei einem Mac-Event darüber gesprochen, dass Touchscreens an Laptops ergonomische Albträume sind. „Nach längerer Zeit wird Ihnen der Arm abfallen“, so Jobs damals.
Sicher, solche Ansichten können sich über die Zeit überholen. Schließlich stellte es sich auch als falsch heraus, dass 3,5 Zoll immer die perfekte Größe für Smartphone-Bildschirme bleiben wird. Und so gut wie jeder Windows-Hersteller hat ja ebenfalls Geräte mit Touchscreen im Portfolio. Warum also nicht Apple?
Apple lässt Kreative in der Video-App touchen
Profitieren sollen davon kreative Nutzer:innen. Für die ist so ein Pro-Macbook gedacht. Entsprechend sieht man sie auf Apples eigenen Bildern und Videos jetzt ständig an den Bildschirm greifen, um Fotos zu vergrößern oder in der Video-App Clips hin und her zu schieben. Dinge, die man prima und wahrscheinlich präziser mit der Maus oder dem Multitouch-Trackpad hinbekommt – Apples einstmaligen Argument gegen Touchscreen-Laptops.
Die App-Auswahl bestätigt meinen Eindruck, dass die „neue“ Eingabemethode wahrscheinlich erstmal auch selten bei Nutzer:innen ankommen wird. Neben Apples eigenen Apps werden zum Start ausgewählte Anwendungen neue Touchgesten unterstützen. Dazu zählen neben Notion und Canva etwa Word, Outlook und Excel. Bürosoftware also. In einer Pressemeldung ist von „intuitiven Erlebnissen“ die Rede. Bei der Nutzung auf dem iPad kann ich sagen: Es ist immer noch leichter, mit der Maus eine Textstelle gezielt auszuwählen oder Text zu markieren, als es auf dem Touchbildschirm zu versuchen.
Fairerweise muss man dazu sagen, dass Bildbearbeitungs-Apps wie Lightroom oder Videoschnitt-Anwendungen wie Davinci Resolve ebenfalls als kompatibel genanntwerden. Dass jemand mal schnell ein Foto großzieht oder per Drag-and-Drop ein paar Dateien verschiebt, kann ich mir noch vorstellen. Dass aber jetzt unheimlich viele Musiker:innen ihre Stücke direkt via Touchscreen einspielen oder selbige Grafik-Tablets ersetzen? Vermutlich eher nicht. Schließlich unterstützen die Macbooks den Apple Pencil auch nicht.
Zudem kommt das Henne-Ei-Problem. Alle Apps, die nicht auf die Touchbedienung ausgelegt sind, interpretieren Eingaben schlicht als Klicks. Ob sich das ändert, wird auch davon abhängen, wie viel Zuspruch die neuen Geräte vom Publikum erhalten. Heißt: Sind die Touch-Macbooks eher weniger beliebt, gibt es keinen Grund, Arbeit in Funktionen zu investieren, die dann nicht genutzt werden. Das war auch eines der Probleme bei der Touch Bar.
Wann sich das neue Macbook wirklich lohnt
Uninteressant ist das Gerät dennoch nicht. Da wäre eben jenes OLED-Display, das für kräftige Farben und satte Kontraste sorgen dürfte. Die Displaytechnologie ist dabei dieselbe wie beim iPad Pro. Apple setzt auf ein Tandem-Display, bei dem zwei Schichten übereinander liegen. Das sorgt für ein sehr helles Bild. Zudem sind die neuen Geräte laut Apple leichter. Das 14-Zoll-Gerät wiegt 230, die 16-Zoll-Version sogar 320 Gramm weniger als die Modelle ohne OLED.
Dazu kommen die leistungsstarken Prozessoren, Möglichkeiten zur Kalibrierung und andere nützliche Funktionen für Kreative. Gute Gründe das Gerät zu kaufen. Aber der Touchscreen gehört nicht dazu.

articles.title: QCon AI New York 2026 Program Committee Picks: Agent Identity, Context Costs, and Open-Source Infere
articles.text:
Who authorizes an agent’s actions? How should teams manage growing context costs? What changes when coding agents become part of everyday engineering work? The QCon AI New York 2026 program committee has selected six sessions they are looking forward to at the December 15–16 conference. Their picks examine these questions alongside open-source inference, agent standards, and audio AI.
Conference chair Hien Luu, an AI/ML leader, advisor, speaker, and author, joins committee members Wes Reisz, Technical Principal at Thoughtworks and creator of The InfoQ Podcast, and Faye Zhang, Staff Engineer at Google building autonomous agents for Gemini Enterprise, in sharing their selections.
Wes on Agent Identity and Context Costs
Wes Reisz selected When Software Becomes a User: Identity and Authorization for Agents in Production, a keynote by Nancy Wang, CTO at 1Password.
As agents take on more autonomous work, traditional identity and authorization models start to break down. Nancy will explore delegated authority, credential management, and securing agent interactions, foundational capabilities I believe we must get right to truly adopt agentic delivery.
Nancy’s keynote examines how authority is delegated across subagent chains and how agents can access the credentials they need without exposing secrets in their context.
Wes’s second choice is Make Each Token Count: Compression, Caching, and Retrieval for Production LLM Context, by Tejas Chopra, CEO and co-founder of Headroom Labs.
Token costs and latency are real constraints when building production agents. Tejas will explore compression, caching, and retrieval strategies, particularly token compression, which I believe will become a must-have capability in modern agentic systems.
Tejas will cover learned prompt compression, prefix-cache-aware context alignment, and compress-cache-retrieve pipelines, including failure modes that affect tool calling and agent trajectories.
Hien on Engineering Organizations and Open-Source Inference
Hien Luu selected The Future of the Engineering Org, by Peter Bell, founder and CTO of Gather.dev.
Drawing on conversations with engineering leaders at organizations including Anthropic, OpenAI, Shopify, and Coinbase, Peter will examine how engineering structures and practices are changing around coding agents. Topics include team size and rituals, hiring and assessing engineers, changes in engineering leadership, and the future of junior developers.
Hien’s second pick is Open Source Agentic Inference: Unlocking the Harness with vLLM, by Francisco Javier Arceo, Forward Deployed Engineer at Baseten and maintainer of the vLLM Agentic API project.
Francisco will follow a coding task from the harness through model generation, tool execution, and continuation using Agentic API, vLLM, and llm-d. The session examines where tools run, who owns context, and how serving infrastructure supports these workloads. It also explores how repeated inference and context growth affect cost, including why cost per completed task matters more than token price alone.
Faye on Agent Standards and Audio AI
Faye Zhang described her selections as "two talks at the intersection of frontier research and production engineering". Her first choice is Navigating Agentic Standards: What to Build On Now and What to Watch, by Kevin Kelley, Technical Lead for Standards at Anthropic.
She also highlighted how standards such as MCP, A2A, and OAuth can establish interoperable agent identity, delegated authorization, and trust boundaries without creating new security vulnerabilities. Kevin’s session organizes the standards landscape around questions such as which agent is acting, on whose behalf, and how it reaches tools and other agents. It distinguishes what has shipped from work that remains open.
Her second selection is Audio Processing with Large Language Models, a keynote by Tara Sainath, Distinguished Research Scientist at Google DeepMind and lead of the Gemini audio area.
Faye highlighted the questions raised by LLMs reshaping speech and audio modeling: unified multilingual representations, end-to-end versus cascaded architectures, and the latency–quality trade-offs required for real-time conversational intelligence. Tara’s keynote will discuss research and product developments at Google across speech recognition, generation, translation, and dialogue.
Early-Bird Pricing Changes November 10
QCon AI New York 2026 takes place December 15–16 at the Westin Jersey City Newport, one PATH stop from Lower Manhattan. The two-day conference focuses on production AI for senior software engineers, architects, and engineering leaders.
Early-bird pricing is $1,705 until November 10, after which the two-day pass rises to $1,790. Anyone planning to use their remaining 2026 learning and development budget can explore the QCon AI New York program and the "convince your manager" approval email on the conference website.

articles.title: AI cybersecurity shifts to governing agents with Okta identity - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI cybersecurity shifts to governing agents with Okta identity
AI cybersecurity requires governing what trusted software does as well as keeping attackers out. As AI agents act across enterprise systems on behalf of users, identity must establish who or what is acting, how much authority it carries and where that authority ends.
That change is pushing identity providers past traditional access control and into runtime enforcement for AI agents. Enterprises also need to understand what agents have done when something goes wrong, according to Harish Peri (pictured), senior vice president and general manager of AI security at Okta Inc.
“If something does go wrong, are you able to explain and prove the series of actions that an agent took? Are you able to find all that in your logs in a single unbroken chain?” Peri said. “This is, of course, sort of in the worst-case scenario, but you have to know what happened and you have to be able to show that chain of custody in order to then fix if something does go wrong.”
Peri spoke with theCUBE Research’s Krista Case for the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI cybersecurity and what an identity architecture built for AI agents requires. (* Disclosure below.)
Building AI cybersecurity on agent identity foundations
Okta frames agent maturity as a progression of questions in its blueprint for the secure agentic enterprise: Where are my agents, what can they do, what are they doing and how do I respond? Those answers build toward a harder question — whether an agent should be allowed to take a given action at a specific moment, according to Peri.
“The real risk with agents that we’re seeing is not that [they’re] going to get hacked per se. I think that makes for good headlines, but the reality is more of the risk comes from an agent being misaligned and without any bad intention, taking an action that was never intended by the original user,” Peri said.
Answering that question starts with giving every agent its own identity. An agent that simply impersonates a user is little more than overpriced robotic process automation, while overloading a service account is a quick fix that breaks down as deployments grow, Peri explained.
“Step one is don’t take a shortcut on the foundations. If you do, it might feel like, ‘Hey, I’m innovating.’ But what will happen is, once you get to more than 10 or 15 enterprise agents that have access to your enterprise applications, you will end up having to unwind that,” Peri said.
Authority also has to travel safely as agents work across applications. Peri described a procurement agent that touches SAP, accounts payable and customer relationship management systems for users with very different permissions. The answer is delegation with downscoping, backed by central authorization and centralized logging, he explained.
“In the context of a specific prompt, the agent will never exceed the maximum allowable scope of all the parties in the chain,” Peri said. “That means that even though in theory, this agent can take actions on behalf of a manager, if it’s being invoked by frontline [personnel], it will never exceed their scope.”

articles.title: Robôs de limpeza fazem bonito durante feira em São Paulo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Resumo
- A Redroad, marca de soluções inteligentes de limpeza, apresentou três robôs de limpeza durante a HigiExpo 2026, feira em São Paulo.
- Os robôs RD10 Pro, RD55 e RD70 Pro atendem a diferentes portes de espaços, desde pequenos ambientes até grandes áreas.
- Os preços sugeridos são de US$ 14.900, US$ 32.900 e US$ 41.900, respectivamente.
A marca de soluções inteligentes de limpeza Redroad demonstrou três robôs durante a HigiExpo 2026, feira voltada ao setor de limpeza que ocorreu em São Paulo, na última semana. A companhia garante não apenas produtos com altíssima tecnologia, mas também uma solução completa para os clientes – em sua essência, pessoas jurídicas – que optarem por implementá-los em suas localidades nos próximos meses.
O responsável pela marca, Danny Cui, conta ao Tecnoblog quais são os pilares das novidades reveladas na capital paulista:
- Linha para diferentes portes: os três modelos atendem desde espaços pequenos, como academias e casas de repouso, a grandes áreas, como aeroportos e fábricas. “Como na limpeza comercial existem muitos setores diferentes, precisamos oferecer uma linha ampla de produtos”, disse Cui.
- Operação local: a empresa montou um escritório em São Paulo com central de atendimento em português, um centro de serviço e um estoque de peças de reposição. Os planos incluem, no futuro, uma unidade de montagem em Jacareí, no interior de São Paulo, que vai trabalhar com componentes principais importados.
- IA física: o termo delimita os algoritmos que permitem ao robô perceber o ambiente e se adaptar quando algo muda no caminho. Na prática, a equipe escaneia o local do cliente com um aparelho portátil com o objetivo de criar mapas e rotinas de limpeza antes mesmo de enviar o robô.
- Pós-venda em três camadas: a Redroad explica que os clientes obtêm atendimento via telefone, acesso remoto ou com técnicos de campo que visitam a localidade para fazer os reparos. “Respondemos à dúvida em até duas horas, encontramos a causa e a solução em até 24 horas e consertamos em até 48. Se não conseguirmos consertar, fornecemos máquinas substitutas”, afirmou o executivo.
A Redroad aproveitou a feira em São Paulo para reforçar que quer ser mais do que um fornecedor capaz de entregar dispositivos de limpeza comercial; ela se posiciona como uma parceria que estará junto do cliente desde a detecção das necessidades até o fornecimento dos equipamentos e o posterior pós-venda, inclusive com visitas de manutenção preventiva – ou seja, revisões programadas antes que surjam problemas.
“No fim das contas, o cliente final não precisa do equipamento, ele precisa garantir que o piso esteja limpo todos os dias”, disse Cui ao Tecnoblog. O executivo revelou que os contratos com os clientes costumam durar de 12 meses a cinco anos.
Conheça os produtos
Os três modelos demonstrados pela Redroad funcionam em pisos rígidos de vários tipos – mármore, madeira, granito, cimento, epóxi, cerâmica e piso plástico – e podem ser acompanhados à distância por aplicativo, segundo a fabricante. A ideia é que o cliente escolha o robô pelo tamanho e pelas características do espaço, em vez de adaptar o local ao equipamento.
Os dispositivos compartilham o mesmo software e a mesma estrutura de serviço, o que permite combiná-los num mesmo espaço. Cui dá o exemplo de um supermercado: o robô maior poderia cuidar dos corredores largos com eficiência, enquanto o menor chegaria perto das bordas e garantiria a limpeza embaixo das prateleiras. “Isso sim é uma solução”, resumiu o executivo.
RD10 Pro
O RD10 Pro é o modelo compacto da linha atual, pensado para espaços apertados, como os corredores entre prateleiras de lojas de conveniência. Ele mede 52 cm de comprimento, 42 cm de largura e 49 cm de altura, e pesa 26 kg. A Redroad afirma que o corpo de 42 cm é o mais estreito da categoria. O tamanho reduzido também facilita a entrada em elevadores e a passagem por catracas.
O robô tem dois modos de trabalho: lavagem de piso, com até 3 horas de autonomia, e varrição, com até 8 horas. Ele limpa uma faixa de 350 mm a 0,6 m/s, o que rende de 756 a 1.008 m² por hora, e sobe rampas com até 10% de inclinação. Duas escovas de rolo fazem a lavagem com alta pressão, e o sistema separa os resíduos secos dos molhados. A limpeza chega rente a paredes e pilares, pontos que costumam ficar para trás. Os tanques de água limpa e de água suja têm 10 litros cada, com um reservatório auxiliar de 4 litros.
O RD10 Pro combina visão e laser para se orientar melhor no ambiente. Ele usa câmera de profundidade 3D, sensores ultrassônicos, LiDAR – o sensor que mede distâncias com laser, também presente em carros autônomos e tablets de ponta – e um sensor de movimento (IMU), e desvia de obstáculos em 360°. O ruído fica abaixo de 65 dB, e o robô volta sozinho à base para recarregar a bateria de 20 Ah. A estrutura aberta, de desmontagem rápida, simplifica a manutenção diária. A autolimpeza do sistema de sucção vem de série; a do tanque de água suja é opcional.
A fabricante recomenda o modelo para hospitais, escritórios, shoppings, escolas, hotéis, restaurantes, academias e casas de repouso. O preço sugerido é de US$ 14.900, cerca de R$ 80,5 mil na cotação de hoje (26/10).
RD55
O RD55 é o produto intermediário, para áreas médias e grandes. Mede 82 cm de comprimento, 68 cm de largura e 113 cm de altura, e pesa 170 kg. O principal diferencial é a integração com os sistemas de elevadores e de controle de acesso dos prédios, o que permite ao robô trabalhar em vários setores de edifícios comerciais e escritórios.
O aparelho limpa uma faixa de 550 mm e rende até 1.980 m² por hora. Duas escovas de rolo lavam o piso e também recolhem pequenos resíduos secos. O rodo de sucção tem câmara dupla, recurso que, segundo a Redroad, reduz a água que sobra nas frestas do piso. Os tanques têm 45 litros para água limpa e 45 litros para água suja. O próprio robô faz a própria limpeza de tanque, com remoção de 95% dos detritos, e o ventilador do sistema de sucção tem vida útil estimada de 10 mil horas. O modelo pode trabalhar com uma estação-base que faz a recarga, reabastece a água e limpa o tanque.
A navegação combina laser e visão computacional: o robô monta o mapa do ambiente e se localiza nele ao mesmo tempo, com LiDAR, câmeras e sensores de deslocamento das rodas. Para desviar de obstáculos, cruza informações de vários quadros captados pela frente e por trás. O controle pode ser feito no próprio robô, pela nuvem ou pelo celular.
A bateria suporta 8.000 ciclos de recarga e garante cerca de 3 horas de operação. O ruído fica abaixo de 68 dB, e a garantia é de um ano para o equipamento completo. Os cenários indicados são shoppings, hospitais, supermercados, escritórios e fábricas. O preço sugerido é de US$ 32.900, cerca de R$ 177,8 mil.
RD70 Pro
O RD70 Pro é o maior produto da linha, voltado a aeroportos, grandes armazéns e supermercados. Ele tem bastante apelo para “grandes espaços públicos”, segundo Danny Cui. Para se ter uma ideia de sua robustez, o robô pesa 199 kg sem água. Na versão com escovas circulares, usa discos de 20 polegadas, que, segundo a Redroad, cobrem o dobro da área por passada de produtos concorrentes. A pressão de 27 kg sobre o piso ajuda a remover sujeira incrustada.
O robô limpa uma faixa de 560 mm, anda a até 4 km/h e rende até 2.040 m² por hora. Também sobe rampas com até 6% de inclinação. Os tanques têm 70 litros para água limpa e 50 litros para água suja – somados, são os 120 litros. A bateria de lítio de 100 Ah, que pesa 25 kg, dá cerca de 4 horas de operação e pode ser trocada em um minuto, o que evita esperar a recarga para continuar o trabalho. O robô também volta sozinho para recarregar.
O sistema de navegação NeverLost 360° reúne câmera panorâmica, LiDAR, câmera de profundidade, sensores ultrassônicos, sensor de movimento e para-choques, para que o robô se desloque sozinho e desvie de obstáculos. As limpezas podem ser agendadas conforme a rotina de cada estabelecimento, e o equipamento também pode ser operado manualmente, alternando entre os modos de trabalho.
O RD70 Pro gera relatórios automáticos que servem para inspeção de qualidade, comprovação do serviço feito e rastreabilidade das operações. O ruído fica entre 75 e 80 dB. O modelo segue normas da União Europeia e tem garantia de um ano para o equipamento completo. O preço sugerido é de US$ 41.900, cerca de R$ 226,4 mil.
Robô humanoide vista estande
Além dos três robôs de limpeza, o estande da Redroad na HigiExpo recebeu um robô humanoide, que proporcionou experiências interativas aos visitantes durante os três dias de feira, de 20 a 22 de outubro.
O espaço também teve demonstrações ao vivo dos robôs de limpeza, com limpeza rente às bordas, passagem por corredores estreitos, deslocamento entre andares, integração com sistemas de controle de acesso e retorno automático à base para recarga.
Distribuidores, empresas de serviços de limpeza, equipes de gestão predial e grandes redes varejistas puderam conversar com a equipe da Redroad sobre a escolha de equipamentos, condições para projetos-piloto – as chamadas provas de conceito, em que o cliente testa o robô no próprio ambiente antes de fechar contrato –, aplicações práticas e parcerias comerciais. Segundo a empresa, essas conversas levam em conta as características de cada ambiente e as necessidades específicas de cada projeto.
A companhia aproveitou o momento para anunciar sua chegada ao Instagram, por meio do perfil @redroadbrazil.

articles.title: Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to a new extreme | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple has officially entered the touchscreen MacBook Pro era, and apparently, it wants to drain your wallet while it’s at it.
The new touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, which is already a hefty price tag in this economy. But if you want the absolute top-of-the-line model with every possible upgrade, prepare to cough up around $14,549.
As MacRumors first reported, Apple’s configurator prices the fully loaded 14-inch model at $14,249 and the 16-inch version at $14,549. Both come equipped with Apple’s top-tier M5 Max chip, featuring an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU.
You can blame the ongoing memory shortage and AI’s seemingly endless appetite for hardware for some of the pricing pressure. Moving to a 4TB SSD costs an additional $1,000, while upgrading to 8TB adds $3,000. Want the new 16TB option? That’ll set you back another $7,000.
Another $2,000 gets you 128GB of memory, while nano-texture glass adds $150.
For some perspective, the previous 16-inch MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149. The new model raises that ceiling by a whopping $4,400.
Absurd prices aside, the launch marks a significant shift for Apple, nearly a decade after it first experimented with the Touch Bar. The company eventually abandoned that feature, but now it’s ready to embrace a touchscreen MacBook Pro.
Preorders open October 30, with availability beginning November 6.

articles.title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona
articles.text:
The private space tourism era looked so very promising five years ago. Blue Origin and Virgin Galactic had begun flying customers—real people with zero space experience—on suborbital missions. And at about the same time, private citizens were going to orbit for days at a time aboard SpaceX’s Crew Dragon.
But that was then. Consider the state of play today:
- It has been 10 months since Blue Origin’s New Shepard spacecraft flew its last mission in January. The program was subsequently “paused,” but let’s be real. Blue Origin has moved on. New Shepard’s engineering teams are now supporting the New Glenn rocket and Blue Moon lander programs.
- SpaceX flew its final free-flyer mission on Dragon, Fram2, in April 2025. A handful of non-NASA missions bound for space stations remain on the spacecraft’s manifest, but all are likely to carry at least one government astronaut. Then Dragon will be retired. There is no credible timeline for SpaceX’s Starship to fly humans into space from Earth.
- As for Virgin Galactic, the company flew its final suborbital mission on the VSS Unity spacecraft more than two years ago, in June 2024.
So we are now 10 months, and counting, without a space tourism mission in the United States.
Hello Apeiron, you shiny object
At the time of Unity‘s final flight, Virgin Galactic said it was moving on to the second generation of its suborbital spacecraft. It planned to bring two of these Delta-class ships into service by the year 2026. Of course, it is now 2026, and there are no Delta-class ships in service.
But apparently we are getting closer to that goal. On Wednesday, the first Delta-class ship received a name: Apeiron. According to Virgin Galactic’s news release, the name is drawn from the ancient Greek concept of the boundless, which is an interesting choice for a vehicle that will forever be bound by Earth’s gravity. It was chosen through a public vote.

articles.title: Palit Denies GALAX GPU Factory Closure, Continues Business as Usual
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Palit Denies GALAX GPU Factory Closure, Continues Business as Usual
Palit issued a statement today to address and dismiss current industry rumors that GALAX GPU factories are winding down. The rumor suggested that GALAX and its European-focused KFA2 brand were experiencing supply issues with NVIDIA. However, Palit has clarified that these reports are inaccurate. As one of NVIDIA's largest add-in card partners, Palit sells a significant volume through its brands. The speculation that GALAX factories are shutting down due to supply problems with NVIDIA would imply a risk to NVIDIA's entire business with its AIC partners, which doesn't make much sense. Palit explained that since Palit and GALAX are now operating under one roof, they share some manufacturing facilities, and GALAX products continue to be sold.
Palit has also confirmed that the company is developing next-generation GALAX Hall-of-Fame (HOF) graphics cards, along with regular GALAX and KFA2-branded GPU models. While the current generation of GPUs remains available, the mention of next-generation GPUs in development is particularly intriguing. This indicates that the upcoming NVIDIA GeForce RTX 60-Series "Rubin" gaming GPUs will also be available in GALAX HOF and KFA2 variants, providing extreme overclockers with more HOF generations in the future.
PalitWe are aware of recent reports and speculation regarding GALAX's business operations. We would like to clarify that these claims are inaccurate.
GALAX continues to operate as usual. No manufacturing facilities have been shut down, and GALAX products remain available through our sales channels in both domestic and international markets.
As part of the same group, GALAX and Palit share manufacturing facilities, with production and business operations continuing as normal.
We remain fully committed to delivering high-quality products and supporting our customers, partners, and the global community.
For any further inquiries or clarification, please contact us at info@galaxytech.com.
We sincerely appreciate your continued trust and support.
Source:
