articles.title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications
articles.text:
Cloudflare has recently launched a beta Web Search API through AI Gateway. Available through REST APIs and Cloudflare Workers, it provides unified logging, access controls, and billing, and supports bring-your-own-provider keys.
The API enables AI agents to retrieve live web results from Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. It provides a unified interface, integrates search billing with AI Gateway, logs search requests alongside model inference, and requires providers to follow verified-bot requirements and return source links.
Cloudflare’s Web Search API allows AI applications to retrieve current web content, including recent news, API changes, and technical documentation, and provide the results as context to language models during inference. Michelle Chen, group product manager at Cloudflare, Sam Else, senior director at Cloudflare, and Gabriel Massadas, senior systems engineer at Cloudflare, explain the challenge that the company is trying to address:
When you use an agent and it needs to fetch a live web page, the agent usually just guesses the URL of the page and then makes a tool call to curl it. This is why you’ll sometimes see web fetches come back with a 404 Not Found, which happens if the agent incorrectly guesses the URL of that information. As you can imagine, it’s not super efficient to randomly guess URLs all the time.
Applications and external services can access web search through a REST endpoint by providing an AI Gateway authentication token and specifying a search provider in the request payload, with the endpoint returning the search results. Chen, Else, and Massadas add:
The crawler used by the web search provider must comply with Cloudflare’s publicly stated requirements for "Verified bots" as defined in our developer documentation, and web search responses must include a link to the location of crawled content. These rules are net-positive for a fair Internet, and allow creators to decide what they want to do with their data.
In a popular Hacker News thread, the community discusses search quality, data-retention restrictions, and whether a unified API offers meaningful advantages over existing alternatives. Simon Willison writes:
My number one question about search APIs is always if they allow you to store and resyndicate results you get from them. If I'm running an agent system but I'm not allowed to store the responses - or provide a "share transcript" button - that's a pretty significant limitation. The answer to that question is inevitably buried deep in the terms.
Maximilian Goisser, CTO and co-founder of Erato Labs, notes:
I think Cloudflare is (for companies already using it) approaching the status of trusted main cloud supplier (which usually would be AWS, GCP, Azure) via which the majority of cloud costs are billed (so you don't have to go through a fresh procurement process).
Cloudflare states it will identify providers that support Zero Data Retention and offers search at providers’ list prices without additional markup. The company plans to add native server tools to AI Gateway, starting with web search. Until then, developers can integrate web search into their workflows using Cloudflare Workers.

articles.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ended September 30, the company said in a regulatory filing on Wednesday. That represents nearly 11% of Microsoft’s total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion, highlighting the enormous financial ties that remain between the two companies even as they increasingly compete for the same customers.
(Microsoft’s financial year begins in July, making the quarter ended September 30, 2026 the first quarter of its fiscal 2027.)
For the full 2026 fiscal year, revenue from OpenAI hit $24.1 billion. At its latest quarterly pace, Microsoft would pull in $40 billion annually from OpenAI-related arrangements.
Microsoft also reported $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI at the end of September, up from $6 billion at the end of June. That money represents amounts OpenAI owes for previous transactions, not additional revenue.
It’s not clear how much of Microsoft’s revenue from OpenAI came from revenue-sharing payments or Azure cloud computing services. TechCrunch has reached out for more information. In November 2025, TechCrunch reported, citing leaked documents, that Microsoft had received $865.8 million in net revenue-sharing payments from OpenAI during the first nine months of that year.
OpenAI reportedly shares 20% of its revenue with Microsoft as part of a previous deal in which the software giant invested more than $13 billion in the AI startup. (Neither the AI lab nor Microsoft have publicly confirmed this percentage.) As part of an April 2026 agreement, OpenAI is on the hook to continue sharing revenue with Microsoft through 2030, subject to a cap, even as OpenAI is allowed to work with competing cloud providers.
The companies began loosening the ties of their once-exclusive partnership in October 2025, when Microsoft relinquished its hold on OpenAI to give the startup more freedom to partner with other cloud providers. In exchange, OpenAI committed to buying an additional $250 billion in Azure services as part of an October 2025 agreement.
Microsoft’s ownership stake in OpenAI has also declined slightly from about 25% in June to 24% in September. That continues a gradual decline from roughly 27% following the October 2025 recapitalization. Microsoft did not specify what caused the dilution.

articles.title: ASUS Republic of Gamers Announces Availability of ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace and Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
ASUS Republic of Gamers Announces Availability of ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace and Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace
ASUS Republic of Gamers (ROG) today announced the availability of the Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace and Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace, expanding the Ace esports monitor range with OLED options. Designed with direct input from professional players, these 24.5-inch monitors use a TrueBlack Glossy Tandem WOLED panel with a 0.02 ms (GTG) response time, 1700 nits peak brightness, 99.5% DCI-P3 color gamut and true 10-bit color, setting a new benchmark in the esports monitor category defined by TN panels for decades. Pro-focused features include measurement scales on the stand and base, a Quick OSD menu, Hue Optimizer and three Esports Color Modes to help dial in their setups. The flagship PG259QWS Ace, the official monitor of PGL CS2 Major Singapore 2026, pushes refresh rates to 720 Hz and includes the exclusive Position Sensor and DisplayPort 2.1 (UHBR20) connectivity. Meanwhile, XG259QWPG Ace gives players an identical OLED esports experience at 540 Hz.
Changing the rules of the game
For decades, TN panels have been the default choice for competitive play, trading color, contrast and viewing angles for raw speed. With the Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace and Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace, ROG—the world's No.1 OLED gaming monitor brand—removes that compromise. Self-lit OLED pixels switch almost instantly, delivering motion clarity without sacrificing brightness or relying on backlight strobing technology. Because each pixel produces its own light, there is no backlight blooming, so contrast, color and black levels stay consistent across the entire panel, This reduces flicker for more comfortable viewing experiences versus traditional LCD monitors. The result is a new benchmark for esports professionals: faster, clearer, more consistent visuals that let players see more, react faster and unlock their full potential. In addition, the monitors include Extreme Low Motion Blur (ELMB) technology to take motion clarity to the next level.TrueBlack Glossy Tandem WOLED: Clarity, color and visibility
The 24.5-inch FHD TrueBlack Glossy Tandem WOLED panel used in the Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace and Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace utilize two stacked light-emitting layers to deliver up to 31% higher brightness, 34% larger color volume, and up to 63% longer lifespan than a conventional WOLED panel. articles.title: IT vendor lists massive $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 300 racks of decommissioned GPUs — includes 9,600 Nvidia A100 GPUs and 4,200 AMD EPYC CPUs, plus free shipping
articles.text:
IT vendor lists massive $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 9,600 Nvidia A100 GPUs and 4,200 AMD EPYC CPUs, plus free shipping — 300 racks of decommissioned GPUs on offer
If you ever wanted to own your own supercomputer or data center while earning eBay cashback, Core 4 Solutions has the perfect opportunity. The company is selling a 300-rack AI supercomputer on eBay for $59.7 million, complete with $50 overnight shipping, or free shipping if you're willing to go with FedEx Ground. The cluster packs 9,600 Nvidia A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, enough to jump-start your own sovereign AI nation.
Nvidia and AMD have moved to newer architectures like Blackwell, Vera Rubin, and EPYC Turin. Nonetheless, A100 (codenamed Ampere) accelerators and EPYC Rome processors remain highly relevant for many computing tasks, including AI, machine learning, and scientific research. With the modern Blackwell and Vera Rubin racks from Nvidia, like the GB300 NVL72 and VR200 NVL72, costing up to $6.5 million and $7.8 million per unit, respectively, the A100 has turned into a legitimate budget alternative that can also circumvent the long waitlists and supply chain delays on Nvidia's newer AI hardware.
The cluster's sheer specifications are truly jaw-dropping. Each rack has four compute nodes and three management nodes. Each compute node has two AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, eight Nvidia A100 40GB SXM4 accelerators, and 1TB of DDR4-2933 memory. The management nodes are no less impressive. Each features two EPYC 64-core chips and 192GB of DDR4 memory.
When you sum it all up, the cluster comprises up to 9,600 A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome processors. With 64 Zen 2 execution cores per chip, the entire cluster boasts 268,800 cores. Memory capacity is equally impressive, with up to 1,401.6 TB or 1.4 petabytes for the entire cluster.
At first glance, $59.7 million sounds like a fortune, and it certainly is, but it seems like a reasonable valuation for the cluster. A rough estimate would be about $24 million for the A100S, $3 million for the EPYC Rome chips, and about $1.1 million for the DDR4 memory. That is about $28.1 million in crucial components, before factoring in other hardware like racks, cooling, power supplies, Nvidia Mellanox ConnectX-6 SmartNICs, etc.
Listing a 300-rack supercomputing cluster on eBay sounds absurd, but given today's AI-driven world, it is not as surprising as it may seem. After all, a broker once sold a 405-foot luxury Gigayacht for $168 million on eBay, so there is no reason why Core 4 Solutions cannot move a $59.7 million cluster. As AI farms and data centers expand, some enterprise clients out there will recognize the value and opportunity in the listing.
Shipping that many racks will be a logistics nightmare, and as funny as it sounds, Core 4 Solutions offers free local pickup or FedEx Ground delivery directly to your home. There is even an option to pay for a $25 two-day or $50 overnight delivery. Imagine FedEx casually dropping off 300 server racks at your front porch.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The cluster seems to have already drawn attention, with 11 people reportedly watching the eBay listing and one prospective buyer already letting it sit in their cart. I guess the real question is not whether it will sell, but whether the buyer will choose $50 overnight shipping.

Zhiye Liu is a news editor, memory reviewer, and SSD tester at Tom’s Hardware. Although he loves everything that’s hardware, he has a soft spot for CPUs, GPUs, and RAM.

articles.title: Ojo con los emuladores de PS5 en GitHub: hay versiones falsas que roban tus contraseñas
articles.text:
Si estás buscando emuladores de PS5 para ejecutar en tu ordenador, ten mucho cuidado. Un nuevo reporte afirma que actualmente están en circulación versiones falsas de algunas de las alternativas más conocidas, que están infectadas con un malware que roba tus contraseñas y otros datos sin que te des cuenta.
De acuerdo con lo publicado, varios emuladores falsos de PS5 están distribuyéndose a través de GitHub. Estos utilizan repositorios que imitan los de opciones genuinas y conocidas como AnyPS5 y KyttyPS5, pero cuando los usuarios los instalan en sus PC se dispara un infostealer capaz de exfiltrar grandes cantidades de información y de cubrir sus rastros para evitar que los antivirus lo detecten.
Más allá de la primera fase del engaño, estos emuladores de PS5 infectados con malware sacan provecho de un perfil de usuario bastante especial. Expertos en ciberseguridad consideran que quienes están dispuestos a instalar software de emulación suelen correr más riesgos que los demás al lidiar con programas que no están firmados o que provienen de fuentes desconocidas.
Así es como los emuladores de PS5 que tienen malware son capaces de llegar a un gran número de ordenadores. Después de todo, la posibilidad de ejecutar juegos de la actual generación de PlayStation en un PC sin que exista un soporte oficial para ello, es una opción siempre atractiva para los entusiastas del gaming y la experimentación informática.
Emuladores de PS5 con malware se están distribuyendo en GitHub
Lo más peligroso de los emuladores de PS5 falsos que se han detectado en GitHub es que pueden engañar los sistemas de protección de Windows. De acuerdo con la información disponible, el malware dispara una excepción del sistema operativo tras su descarga. Esto impide que Windows Defender u otros antivirus puedan detectarlo.
Pero eso no es todo, ya que luego descarga un infostealer capaz de extraer contraseñas y todo tipo de datos almacenados en el ordenador. Cuando finaliza el robo de los datos en cuestión, los falsos emuladores de PS5 ejecutan un script que elimina los archivos asociados con su presencia en el PC.
Esto significa que el software malicioso puede cubrir sus huellas el tiempo suficiente para salirse con la suya sin que el usuario se entere. Y para cuando la víctima se entera, ya es demasiado tarde.
El tema es realmente preocupante, considerando que los emuladores de PS5 se han vuelto bastante populares en los últimos tiempos. De hecho, Sony está transitando un momento bastante peculiar en lo que respecta no solo a la emulación de juegos de PlayStation en PC, sino también al hackeo de su consola de actual generación. El furor por la IA generativa ha facilitado el jailbreak de la PlayStation 5, desbloqueando un sinfín de posibilidades para los gamers (para bien o para mal).

articles.title: Madica secures $6m from Flourish Ventures to extend African pre-seed investment pilot - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Madica, a structured pre-seed investment programme for African startups, has secured US$6 million in additional capital from Flourish Ventures to extend its investment pilot by three years.
Launched in 2022, Madica is an Africa-focused pre-seed investment programme empowering underrepresented and underfunded mission-driven founders on the continent. The sector-agnostic platform, affiliated with Flourish Ventures, aims to empower entrepreneurs by providing funding and democratizing access to world-class company-building support.
The programme has so far backed 18 startups in 10 countries across the continent, most recently making three investments last month, and it is now set to invest in between 25 and 30 more ventures over the next three years with the additional US$6 million from Flourish Ventures.
Building on lessons learned and early signs of traction across its portfolio, Madica will also deepen its company-building support for exceptional founders underserved by established venture capital networks. The extended pilot will build further evidence for Madica’s founding conviction that these founders can build world-class businesses capable of generating venture returns when equipped with the right capital and support.
The 18 companies Madica has backed so far, across 12 sectors, have attracted, on average, twice Madica’s investment in additional funding, an early signal of investor confidence as they work towards the commercial outcomes needed to challenge prevailing assumptions about where venture-scale businesses can emerge in Africa.
The extended pilot will allow Madica to track how companies across a broader portfolio translate early traction into sustained business growth, examining the role of its investment and support model in that progress and assessing the potential to generate venture returns through exits.
“Madica was launched as an experiment to test whether pairing capital with hands-on company-building support could help overlooked founders building world-class businesses generate venture outcomes, and in many ways, our work sits at the intersection of the very many questions that underpin the state of early-stage venture investing in Africa. From the outset, we knew that gathering meaningful evidence would require years of investment, support and learning”, said Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Madica.
“Three years have given us valuable lessons and encouraging early signals, but building enduring companies and assessing venture outcomes takes longer. Flourish Ventures’ continued commitment gives us the capital to build on those lessons and test our conviction across a broader portfolio while deepening our company-building support. We want the resulting evidence to give other investors a model they can apply, shaping where funding goes and how founders are backed across Africa, well beyond Madica.”
Efayomi Carr, investment partner at Flourish Ventures and co-founder of Madica, said his company retained its conviction that with the right capital and support, exceptional talent across Africa can build world-class businesses.
“Madica’s first three years have strengthened that belief, and we are excited to continue backing the team as they help more entrepreneurs achieve that mission,” he said.

articles.title: Before Your Small Business Buys an AI Assistant: The Data Groundwork Nobody Mentions - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Understanding the AI Assistant Landscape for Small Businesses
Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistants have moved beyond sci-fi concepts and are now practical tools that small businesses can use to improve efficiency, customer engagement, and decision-making. From automating repetitive tasks like scheduling and inventory management to providing personalized customer interactions via chatbots, AI assistants promise transformative benefits. According to a recent report, 45% of small businesses plan to adopt AI technologies within the next two years, underscoring the growing interest in leveraging AI to stay competitive.
However, before your business invests in an AI assistant, there is a critical aspect often overlooked: the data groundwork required to ensure your AI solution works effectively and securely. Without a solid data foundation, even the most sophisticated AI assistant can fail to deliver value or, worse, generate inaccurate or biased outcomes that harm your business reputation.
Small businesses, in particular, face unique challenges when integrating AI assistants into their operations. Limited resources and expertise can make it difficult to prepare and manage the data that fuels AI systems. Unlike large enterprises with dedicated data science teams, small businesses often struggle with fragmented data stored across multiple platforms such as CRM systems, spreadsheets, and cloud services. This fragmentation can create blind spots in AI training and decision-making processes.
Many businesses trust 24×7 IT Solutions help streamline data management processes, ensuring systems provide reliable and secure data that AI assistants require. Proper data cleansing, integration, and management reduce errors and improve AI performance, directly impacting customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.
The Essential Role of Data Preparation
Data is the lifeblood of AI assistants. These systems rely on large volumes of high-quality, well-structured data to learn and perform tasks accurately. For small businesses, assembling this data isn’t as simple as plugging in an AI tool and watching it work. Raw data may be inconsistent, incomplete, or stored in disparate locations, making it unsuitable for AI consumption.
Studies show that 60% of AI project failures can be attributed to poor data quality or insufficient data preparation, highlighting the critical need for upfront data groundwork.
Building a Robust Data Infrastructure
Before deploying an AI assistant, small businesses need to invest time in establishing a data infrastructure that supports real-time data processing, storage, and security. This infrastructure should be scalable and adaptable to evolving business needs and AI capabilities. For instance, as your business grows, the volume and variety of data will increase, requiring flexible pipelines and storage solutions.
Data engineering plays a pivotal role here. Engaging with experts such as Atmosera for AI data engineering can help small businesses design and implement data pipelines tailored for AI workloads. This ensures that data flows smoothly from source systems to AI models, enabling timely and accurate insights. A well-designed data pipeline minimizes bottlenecks and prevents data loss or corruption, which are common pitfalls in AI projects.
According to a recent survey, 87% of businesses report that poor data quality negatively impacts their AI initiatives, highlighting the urgency of addressing data groundwork before AI adoption.
Data Privacy and Compliance: Non-Negotiable Foundations
Data privacy is a critical consideration when working with AI assistants. Small businesses must ensure their data handling complies with relevant regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), or industry-specific standards like HIPAA for healthcare. Failure to do so can lead to severe financial penalties and damage to customer trust.
Implementing robust data governance frameworks is essential. This includes defining who can access data, how it is stored and processed, and establishing protocols for data anonymization and encryption. For example, encrypting sensitive customer information both at rest and in transit helps mitigate the risk of data breaches.
Managed IT service providers can assist in creating these frameworks, providing peace of mind that your AI assistant operates within legal and ethical boundaries. Moreover, these providers can help implement continuous monitoring and auditing mechanisms to detect and respond to potential compliance issues proactively.
Measuring ROI Through Data Readiness
Investing in an AI assistant without proper data readiness can lead to suboptimal returns. Conversely, businesses that prioritize data groundwork often see faster deployment times, higher AI accuracy, and better decision-making capabilities. According to McKinsey, companies with mature data engineering practices report a 35% increase in AI project success rates compared to those without.
Furthermore, a well-prepared data foundation reduces the time and cost associated with troubleshooting AI errors or retraining models, accelerating the time to value. Small businesses should view data preparation not as a cost but as an investment that multiplies the value of their AI assistant over time.
Practical Steps for Small Businesses to Prepare Data
- Conduct a Data Audit: Identify all data sources, formats, and storage locations. Understanding your existing data landscape is the first step in preparing for AI integration. This includes structured data like sales records and unstructured data such as customer emails or social media comments.
- Cleanse and Normalize Data: Remove duplicates, correct errors, and standardize formats to create a consistent dataset. Data cleansing tools or services can automate much of this process, but human oversight is crucial to catch context-specific anomalies.
- Engage Data Engineering Experts: Partnering with specialists can accelerate building scalable data pipelines tailored to your AI needs. Experts can also advise on best practices for data storage, metadata management, and performance optimization.
- Implement Data Security and Governance: Ensure compliance with privacy regulations by setting up access controls, encryption, and auditing mechanisms. Define clear policies on data retention, sharing, and disposal to minimize legal risks.
- Leverage Managed IT Services: Collaborate with trusted providers such as to maintain the ongoing health and security of your data infrastructure. They can offer 24/7 monitoring, incident response, and continuous improvement strategies to keep your AI systems running smoothly.
Overcoming Common Data Challenges in Small Businesses
Many small businesses encounter specific hurdles when preparing data for AI assistants. Legacy systems may store data in outdated formats or lack APIs for easy integration. Additionally, limited staff expertise can hinder effective data management.
To overcome these challenges, consider incremental data modernization. Start by consolidating critical datasets into a centralized repository such as a cloud data warehouse. Cloud platforms offer scalable storage and built-in security features, reducing upfront infrastructure costs.
Training your team on data literacy and AI fundamentals is equally important. Understanding how AI uses data helps align data preparation efforts with business goals, ensuring that the AI assistant addresses real operational needs.
Future-Proofing Your AI Investment
AI technologies evolve rapidly. What works today may become obsolete as new models and data types emerge. Building a flexible and well-governed data foundation ensures your small business can adapt to these changes without costly overhauls.
Regularly revisiting your data strategy is advisable. Schedule periodic audits to assess data quality, compliance adherence, and infrastructure performance. Engage with managed IT and data engineering partners to stay informed about emerging tools and best practices.
Conclusion: The Hidden Investment in AI Success
Small businesses eager to adopt AI assistants often focus on the technology’s capabilities and overlook the foundational data work required. Proper data preparation, infrastructure, and governance are essential to unlocking the full potential of AI assistants. By investing time and resources in these areas, businesses not only improve the accuracy and reliability of AI but also safeguard their operations against compliance risks.
Partnering with experienced managed IT services and data engineering providers can bridge the expertise gap, making AI adoption smoother and more effective. Remember, the smartest AI assistant is only as good as the data it learns from. Prioritize your data groundwork today to ensure your AI assistant becomes a true asset for your business growth.

articles.title: Sony ISP subsidiary data breach exposes 2.5 million customer records
articles.text:
Sony Network Communications has confirmed a data breach that compromised approximately 2.5 million records containing current and former customers’ personal information.
A Sony Group Corporation subsidiary, the company provides telecommunications and technology services, acting as an internet service provider (ISP) in Japan.
The breach occurred on October 19 and was detected four days later, when the company shut down the compromised servers and blocked external communication.
In an announcement yesterday, the company said that its So-net member database, supporting its internet access service, was accessed by an unauthorized party.
The investigation confirmed that a total of 2,585,481 customer records had been exposed, including the following types of information:
- Full names
- Phone numbers
- Email addresses
- User IDs
- Dates of birth
- Gender
- Internet Connection IDs
No banking, payment card, or other account details were exposed.
An additional 54,401 email addresses from several email services were also exposed along with account passwords. The company advises users to change their passwords.
In the breakdown of exposed records, Sony Network Communications says there are 2,141,986 So-net entries and 443,495 plala (S Course) records. The latter impacts another internet service provider, NTT Docomo, which contracts Sony Network Communications to provide its Docomo Hikari services.
NTT Docomo also notified customers about the breach and warned of phishing emails and fake websites impersonating its d POINT Club and a Universal Studios Japan (USJ) campaign, falsely claiming that recipients had won and prompting them to enter personal information to claim tickets.
Docomo says the incident affects all current Hikari service clients and those who canceled within the preceding six months.
Sony reported the incident to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission and is investigating its cause and scope.
As of October 27, neither company had confirmed misuse of the exposed data in the wild.
Since the start of the year, multiple cyberattacks have targeted high-value companies and providers in Japan.
One of the most recent is the incident at GMO Internet Group and its Onamae Desktop Cloud service, which suffered a widespread malware attack on customer servers.
Telecommunications giant KDDI suffered a breach affecting 12 million customers, and IDC Frontier was targeted by ransomware.
Previously, NTT was hit in early 2025 by hackers who gained access to its systems and stole the data of 18,000 corporate customers.
The recent rate of data breaches is so unprecedented and threatening that the Japanese government held urgent meetings on Monday to plan its response.

Info Edge reports steady growth; Reimagining everyday consumer products
Info Edge delivered a steady Q2, with consolidated revenue rising 12.2% year-on-year to Rs 903.9 crore and net profit surging 87% to Rs 649.8 crore.
Dear Reader,
Jio Platforms made a strong debut on the National Stock Exchange, closing at Rs 1,419, which is a sharp 26.81% premium over its issue price of Rs 1,119.
The listing has catapulted the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 13.06 lakh crore, crowning it India’s second most valuable listed firm. It currently trails only its parent, Reliance Industries, and has moved past heavyweights such as Bharti Airtel and TCS.
The listing day follows a heavily sought-after Rs 30,213-crore IPO, which was fully subscribed within two hours of launch and ultimately closed 22 times oversubscribed.
In other news, PhysicsWallah’s School of Startups (PW SoS) has signed a two-year memorandum of understanding with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) to support early-stage ventures. The programme, which is expected to focus on Tier-II and III cities and rural areas, combines training and mentoring with prototype development, incubation, investor access and seed capital.
Meanwhile, India wants more women in the workforce, but the numbers tell a different story: female labour force participation sits at 34.6% but the country logged nearly 4.4 lakh crimes against women in a single year. Indian women’s safety is a key barrier to their economic ambitions.
In response, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued an advisory across central ministries, Indian Railways, and state administrations. Spanning eight critical fronts, from physical infrastructure and policing to bystander intervention and cyber safety, the message is clear: women’s safety is neither a perk nor merely about physical security. It is an economic imperative and a constitutional right to equal opportunity.

- Info Edge reports steady growth
- Reimagining everyday consumer products

News
Info Edge reports steady growth, CEO Hitesh Oberoi to exit
Info Edge delivered a steady Q2, with consolidated revenue rising 12.2% year-on-year to Rs 903.9 crore and net profit surging 87% to Rs 649.8 crore. Growth was driven by gains in its flagship recruitment vertical, accelerated expansion at 99acres, and steady traction in matchmaking, though its education business continued to face headwinds.
The company is in the middle of a leadership transition. Hitesh Oberoi is due to leave the full-time role of Managing Director and CEO on December 2 this year, after nearly 27 years with the company. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani is slated to assume an expanded executive role from December 3, subject to shareholder approval.
Key takeaways:
- Info Edge operates the brands Naukri (online recruitment), 99acres (property listings), Jeevansathi and Aisle (matchmaking), and Shiksha (education services). It has also invested in other businesses such as Eternal (Zomato), PB Fintech (Policybazaar) and Gnani.ai. So its financial results reflect both operating performance and changes in investment values.
- Consolidated total income, including other income, increased 37.7% YoY to Rs 1,332.3 crore.
- Recruitment remained the largest revenue contributor. The company's earnings presentation puts recruitment revenue at approximately Rs 682 crore, or 75.4% of the total.
Women entrepreneurs
After BabyChakra, Naiyya Saggi is rethinking everyday appliances
Naiyya Saggi co-founded EDT (Everyday Design & Technology) with award-winning industrial designer Vyasateja Rao to simplify everyday living. Moving beyond traditional utility appliances, EDT reimagines household and personal care devices by combining thoughtful industrial design, safer non-toxic materials, and intuitive consumer technology.
Saggi’s core thesis is that everyday home products should not merely perform a baseline mechanical task; they should aid daily routines and reduce cognitive fatigue.
On easy mode:
- EDT prioritises safer, premium materials over cost-cutting shortcuts—exemplified by products like its LUMA PureGlass Air Fryer (using non-toxic borosilicate glass rather than traditional non-stick coatings) and the FLOW Precision Kettle.
- Rather than chasing luxury exclusivity or competing solely on low price, the brand targets an underserved segment: discerning consumers who want well-designed, reliable products that deliver tangible lifestyle improvements.
- Building on Saggi’s background in community-led platforms (such as BabyChakra and Good Glamm Group), EDT gathers direct consumer feedback to co-design and iterate hardware and companion software (like WhatsApp-integrated smart cooking workflows).
News & updates
- Materials research: A multi-institute research team from NIT Rourkela, IIT Guwahati, IIT Bombay, and NISER Bhubaneswar has developed novel materials that emit multiple colours of light under ultraviolet radiation. These materials respond to changes in heat and moisture and can have applications in security systems, sensors, and lighting technologies.
- Public procurement: The government plans to use public procurement to support startups, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh Bhatia said on Tuesday. Addressing the curtain-raiser for the National Startup Awards 6.0, Bhatia also urged the private sector to ramp up efforts to integrate startups into their supply chains.

articles.title: Chrome podrá buscar en Gmail números de vuelo, pedidos y direcciones para llenar formularios
articles.text:
Google anunció el miércoles 28 de octubre una versión avanzada del autocompletado de Chrome que busca en el correo de Gmail del usuario los datos necesarios para llenar formularios en línea, según informó el sitio tecnológico TechCrunch. La función se despliega en Estados Unidos, en computadoras y en las aplicaciones de Gemini en Chrome para iOS y Android.
Hasta ahora, el autocompletado del navegador solo usaba la información guardada en Chrome, como direcciones o tarjetas. La nueva versión puede sugerir datos que están en los mensajes recibidos: un número de confirmación de vuelo, un número de socio, un código de seguimiento de un envío, un número de pedido, una dirección, un teléfono o una tarjeta de crédito.
La función amplía Personal Intelligence, el sistema de Google que conecta sus aplicaciones con el asistente Gemini para recuperar datos y responder preguntas complejas. Cada usuario decide si activa el autocompletado mejorado desde los ajustes de Chrome; Google asegura que los datos sensibles se cifran.
En enero, Google había anticipado en su blog que llevaría Personal Intelligence a Chrome “en los próximos meses”, con la posibilidad de conectar y desconectar las aplicaciones en cualquier momento. Según el sitio especializado Android Authority, ese sistema pasó a la versión gratuita de Gemini en marzo, después de haber sido un beneficio exclusivo para suscriptores de pago.
La función en pruebas
La función ya se había visto en julio dentro de Chrome Canary, la versión experimental del navegador, con el nombre “Find and Fill with Gemini”. Windows Report y Android Authority informaron el 20 de julio que se activaba desde Autocompletar y contraseñas, en el apartado de autocompletado mejorado.
En esa versión de prueba, el usuario podía invocarla escribiendo “@@” en un campo de texto o con un clic derecho y la opción “Buscar y completar desde cualquier lugar”. También podía definir otro atajo y elegir qué aplicaciones conectaba. Además de Gmail, la prueba incluía datos de Google Fotos.
Esos detalles corresponden a la versión Canary. TechCrunch no precisó si el lanzamiento de esta semana mantiene el atajo “@@” ni si incluye Fotos, y no cita un comunicado de Google con esos puntos.
Qué datos recibe Google
Android Authority recogió que Google reconoce que los títulos y las direcciones web de las páginas donde se usa la función “se envían a Google y pueden ser revisados por personas”. Ese punto aparece en la documentación de la versión de prueba.
La información que Gemini inserta en el formulario no es visible para nadie ni se usa para entrenar modelos de inteligencia artificial. Windows Report añadió que Chrome registra si el usuario acepta, edita o descarta cada sugerencia para mejorar la experiencia.
Android Police, que cubrió la prueba en julio, señaló que ese envío de títulos y direcciones era el aspecto más delicado de la función. Para desactivarla, el usuario debe entrar en los ajustes de Chrome, abrir Autocompletar y contraseñas, elegir autocompletado mejorado y apagar el interruptor.
TechCrunch relacionó la novedad con una función de Apple que muestra sobre el teclado los códigos de verificación recibidos por mensaje de texto. A su juicio, aunque parezca menor, puede dar a los usuarios otra razón para seguir en el navegador de Google y en su ecosistema de inteligencia artificial.
Otras novedades en Chrome
Google incorporó en Chrome una advertencia específica para sitios “sospechosos”, distinta de la alerta roja destinada a páginas identificadas como “peligrosas”, con el objetivo de ampliar la detección de riesgos sin bloquear de forma automática sitios sobre los que existe menor certeza.
La función, disponible por ahora para quienes activaron la Protección Reforzada, se complementa con mejoras en Gemini para detectar estafas de soporte técnico, falsos antivirus y supuestas actualizaciones del navegador. Además, el navegador sumó defensas contra las estafas ClickFix, que inducen a copiar comandos maliciosos en el equipo, y envía esos textos —sin datos personales— a Safe Browsing para su evaluación.

articles.title: Puces M5, écran Tandem OLED tactile et Dynamic Island : voici le nouveau MacBook Pro d’Apple
articles.text:
MacBook Pro PROLED XDR : Apple lance son premier PC portable à écran tactile, la facture est salée
C'est la fin de longues semaines de rumeurs et autres bruits de couloirs : Apple officialise la sortie imminente du MacBook pro PROLED XDR, son premier PC portable à écran tactile. Équipé des puces M5 Pro et M5 Max, cette nouvelle mouture compte quelques autres petites nouveautés.
Quelle surprise nous cache ce nouveau MacBook Pro ? Si vous avez raté le titre, ce laptop flagship inclut un écran Tandem Oled tactile, une petite lubie spécifique au public nord-américain que Steve Jobs en personne décriait à son époque. Les temps ont donc changé pour la pomme, qui affiche fièrement les couleurs de sa dalle PROLED XDR, de son nom officiel, avec une luminosité maximale annoncée à 2000 cd/m² en HDR, des contrastes forcément bien meilleurs et une fréquence de rafraîchissement pouvant aller jusqu'à 120 Hz. L'arrivée de ce nouvel écran se fait en tandem (ah !) avec la Dynamic Island, cette petite île de notifications héritée des iPhone depuis plusieurs générations.
Les configurations maximales, aussi, sont revues à la hausse avec la possibilité d'inclure jusqu'à 16 To de stockage sur le SSD, en plus des 128 Go de RAM maximum proposés sur l'Apple Store. Les MacBook Pro PROLED XDR 14 et 16 pouces sont tous les deux configurables avec les puces Apple Silicon M5 Pro et M5 Max, comme les MacBook Pro standards dévoilés dans la journée d'hier. Last but not least, le châssis connaît quelques changements pas piqués des hannetons puisqu'il s'offre une cure d'amaigrissement en passant à 1,38 kg, soit 220 g de moins par rapport à son équivalent non tactile. Ah, et le logo de la pomme s'allume quand le PC est en marche. Wouhou !
Et ça coûte combien, tout ce luxe ? Accrochez-vous : il faudra débourser pas moins de 3299 € pour le MacBook Pro PROLED XDR 14 en M5 Pro avec 24 Go de RAM et 1 To de stockage. Pour passer à la diagonale supérieure du MacBook Pro PROLED XDR 16, c'est 3899 € sans augmentation des tarifs des consommations. Ces nouveaux MacBook seront disponibles le 6 novembre prochain.

articles.title: MacBook Neo 2 : on a une bonne et une mauvaise nouvelle sur le futur PC abordable d'Apple
articles.text:
Apple devrait présenter ce mercredi 28 octobre son premier MacBook Pro avec un écran tactile. Mais ce jour, c’est aussi le MacBook Neo 2 qui fait parler de lui, alors qu’il n’est pas attendu avant plusieurs mois. Au programme : quelques améliorations, mais aussi quelques inquiétudes sur le prix du MacBook le moins cher d’Apple.
En 2027, il devrait y avoir un deuxième MacBook Neo
Comme souvent, c’est le journaliste de Bloomberg Mark Gurman qui nous informe des projets d’Apple. Cette fois-ci, il explique qu’Apple préparerait des versions améliorées des MacBook Air (avec la puce M6) et MacBook Neo. Arrivée prévue « pour le premier semestre de l’année prochaine », écrit-il. Un renouvellement pas surprenant, puisque cette machine a rencontré un énorme succès à sa sortie, au point de connaître des ruptures de stocks.
Aujourd’hui, le MacBook Neo est équipé de 8 Go de RAM. Une quantité de mémoire vive qui commence à ne plus suffire : les fonctions d’IA les plus avancées de macOS 27 demandent 12 Go de RAM minimum (et une puce M3 minimum). Avec sa puce d’iPhone 16 Pro, le MacBook Neo fait pâle figure, alors même que la gamme Air commence à 16 Go. C’est pourquoi Apple chercherait à faire passer le Neo 2 à 12 Go de RAM. Le tout grâce à une puce A19 Pro, qu’on trouve dans les iPhone 17 Pro, Pro Max et iPhone Air.
Pour le moment, on ignore quels seraient les autres changements à venir sur cette deuxième itération du Neo. On sait seulement qu’il pourrait être décliné dans de nouveaux coloris ; actuellement il existe en argent, rose, jaune et bleu.
Attention au prix du MacBook Neo 2
C’est là que l’épineuse question du prix arrive. À sa sortie, le MacBook Neo était vendu à 699 euros (et même 599 euros avec la réduction étudiante !), du jamais vu pour un ordinateur portable de la marque. Mais patatras en juin dernier : le prix augmente de 100 euros, avec en cause, la hausse du prix des composants et principalement de la mémoire vive. Et ce n’était pas le seul produit Apple à voir son prix augmenter ce jour-là.
Apple voudrait donc passer à 12 Go de RAM, ce qui aura un impact évident sur le prix. Si le MacBook Neo 2 sort durant la première moitié de 2027 (peut-être en mars comme le premier), difficile de penser que le prix serait maintenu à 799 euros. Une augmentation qui irait à l’encontre même de la raison d’être du modèle Neo : un ordinateur portable « simple », conçu pour la bureautique légère, endurant, qu’on transporte partout, mais surtout qui est abordable en termes de prix.

articles.title: « Mise en demeure » : attention à ce faux courrier des impôts qui vous piège avec un simple QR code
articles.text:
L’arnaque démarre dans la boîte aux lettres et se referme une fois la victime arrivée sur Internet.
La Police nationale a alerté ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026 sur une campagne de faux courriers envoyés au nom de la Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), qui ciblent les détenteurs de cryptomonnaies.
La lettre, qui reprend tous les codes d’un document administratif, se présente comme une « mise en demeure » liée aux obligations déclaratives sur les actifs numériques.
Elle somme son destinataire de s’inscrire sur un prétendu « Portail des actifs numériques » avant le 29 octobre en scannant un QR code, sous peine de sanctions détaillées avec précision, comme une amende de 750 euros par compte non déclaré ou une majoration de 40 à 80 % des droits éludés.
Un QR code qui mène vers un domaine frauduleux
Le QR code renvoie vers reglement2026.com, un nom de domaine qui n’a en réalité rien à voir avec l’administration fiscale.
Ce domaine est d’ailleurs déjà référencé comme frauduleux sur VirusTotal, un service qui rassemble les analyses de nombreux éditeurs de sécurité pour évaluer la dangerosité d’un fichier ou d’une adresse web.
Le piège est ensuite assez classique. Les victimes se retrouvent face à une interface reprenant les éléments visuels d’un site de l’État. La cible est alors invitée à saisir ses identifiants fiscaux, puis la phrase de récupération de son portefeuille numérique. Cette suite de mots, générée à la création du portefeuille, permet de le restaurer sur n’importe quel appareil, et donne ainsi aux escrocs un accès direct aux cryptomonnaies qu’il contient.
Ne jamais transmettre sa phrase de récupération
Aucune information n’a été communiquée sur le nombre de personnes visées par cette campagne, ni sur le fait qu’il s’agisse d’un envoi de masse ou d’une opération ciblant des personnes détenant effectivement des cryptomonnaies.
Le premier réflexe consiste à ne pas scanner un QR code figurant sur un courrier inattendu, même lorsqu’il semble provenir d’une administration. Le QR code est souvent un subterfuge utilisé pour masquer une adresse web suspecte.
La phrase de récupération, elle, ne doit jamais être communiquée, à qui que ce soit et sous aucun prétexte. Ni l’administration fiscale ni un fournisseur de portefeuille n’a de raison de la demander, et toute sollicitation en ce sens doit être considérée comme une tentative d’escroquerie.
En cas de doute sur un courrier, la Police nationale recommande de se rendre directement sur le site officiel des impôts, en tapant soi-même l’adresse impots.gouv.fr dans son navigateur. Les démarches et messages réellement envoyés par l’administration y figurent dans l’espace personnel de chaque contribuable.

articles.title: La Commission électorale fédérale américaine cible d'une cyberattaque
articles.text:
À mois d'une semaine des élections des midterms aux États-Unis, le site web de la Commission électorale du pays est visé par une cyberattaque.
Aujourd'hui, l'une des manières les plus simples de faire mal à un pays est de l'attaquer informatiquement au moment des élections, soit pour favoriser un personnage, soit, plus généralement, simplement pour créer des disruptions et essayer de créer le doute. En France, même une simple primaire comme la primaire de la gauche a ainsi dernièrement été perturbée par une attaque de bots. Et les élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis ne semblent pas échapper au phénomène.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Le portail web de la Commission électorale ciblé par un piratage
Un mail, auquel Reuters a pu accéder, nous apprend en ce début de semaine que le portail web de la Commission électorale fédérale américaine a été la cible d'une cyberattaque.
Celle-ci a ainsi obligé la Commission a mettre hors ligne son système de dépôt électronique. À l'heure actuelle, elle a indiqué voir identifié le problème, consécutif à la cyberattaque, et être en train de mettre en place un correctif.
Il ne devrait y avoir aucune incidence sur les élections de mi-mandat
Il faut préciser tout de suite que la Commission électorale ne joue aucun rôle dans le décompte des voix - ceci est du ressort des États et des autorités locales. La Commission électorale américaine joue elle un rôle de supervision des dépenses électorales, fait respecter les plafonds des contribution financières et gère l'enregistrement des PAC ou Super PAC (les comités de soutien politique).
Cette cyberattaque empêche ainsi de suivre combien les groupes politiques ont dépensé sur telle ou telle élection spécifique les dernières 24 et 48 heures. Ce qui reste tout de même un point important, quand on sait que dorénavant, ces midterms 2026 sont devenues les élections les plus chères de l'histoire, avec près de 11,21 milliards de dollars dépensés, ce qui dépasse déjà ce que l'on avait pu voir en 2024, avec 11,2 milliards de dollars dépensés (dont 3,2 milliards par les deux candidats à l'élection présidentielle).
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Ein Hauch von Apple-Store: Bei Mediamarkt kannst du jetzt auch beim Verkäufer bezahlen
articles.text:
Der Verkäufer wird zur Kasse: Was sich bei Mediamarkt und Saturn jetzt bei der Bezahlung ändert
Was Kund:innen im stationären Handel immer noch am meisten nervt, ist das Anstehen an der Kasse. Dass die Warterei zum Problem werden kann, zeigt eine aktuelle Studie des Zahlungsdienstleisters Adyen: 16 Prozent der Deutschen haben innerhalb von sechs Monaten mindestens einmal einen Einkauf im Supermarkt abgebrochen, weil ihnen die Wartezeit an der Kasse zu lang war. Selbst im Elektronikfachhandel waren es acht Prozent.
Ein mobiles Gerät als Kartenterminal
Die Elektronikketten Mediamarkt und Saturn setzen hier an und wollen das in Zukunft ändern. Denn wer hier einen neuen Fernseher, eine Waschmaschine oder ein Notebook beim Berater oder der Beraterin kauft, kann dort in Zukunft auch gleich sein Gerät bezahlen.
Möglich wird das über eine Soft-POS-Lösung, also ein mobiles Gerät, das als Kartenterminal funktioniert und den passenden Kassenzettel gleich mit auswirft oder an einen nahegelegenen Drucker sendet. Profitieren könnten davon sowohl die Kund:innen, weil sie nicht mehr anstehen müssen als auch das Verkaufspersonal, das nicht riskiert, dass der Kunde sich auf dem Weg zur Kasse doch noch umentscheidet.
Gleichzeitig kann der Einkauf natürlich schneller werden und die Beratung kann psychologisch angenehm in den Kaufabschluss übergehen. Eher nebenbei werden so natürlich auch die weiter bestehenden Kassen entlastet, weil die Warteschlangen dort kürzer werden. Mediamarkt arbeitet hier ja aus gutem Grund schon in den meisten Filialen mit mehreren Kassen und einer Sammelschlange – auch ein psychologischer Kniff, damit Kund:innen nicht den Eindruck haben, dass es überall schneller geht als in der eigenen Warteschlange.
Bundesweit in 400 Märkten
Die Elektronikkette hatte das Konzept unter dem Namen „Pay-on-Shopfloor“ schon vor einigen Wochen angekündigt. Nach einer Pilotphase in einigen Filialen ist die neue Bezahlmöglichkeit jetzt bundesweit in 400 Märkten verfügbar. Das Onboarding habe jeweils nur zwei Tage gedauert, erklären die Beteiligten. Komplett ersetzen wie im Apple Store will man die Kassenzone allerdings nicht, sondern sie eher ergänzen.
Die Kund:innen können und sollen also weiterhin auch an regulären Kassen und Selbstbedienungskassen bezahlen. Mit der zusätzlichen mobilen Bezahlmöglichkeit könne man das Einkaufserlebnis aber flexibler gestalten, erklärt das Unternehmen.
Technisch basiert das Konzept auf einer SoftPOS-Lösung des Zahlungsdienstleisters CCV. Die Software ermöglicht es, geeignete mobile Geräte zur Annahme von Kartenzahlungen zu nutzen. Der Payment-Anbieter Computop hat die Lösung in die bestehende Zahlungsinfrastruktur von Mediamarkt und Saturn integriert und übernimmt die zentrale Steuerung der Transaktionen. Die gemeinsame Infrastruktur kombiniert dabei unter anderem den Onlinehandel, klassische Kassensysteme und Self-Checkout-Lösungen. Das ermöglicht, es, zusätzliche Bezahlmöglichkeiten einführen, ohne jeweils eine vollständig neue Zahlungsarchitektur aufbauen zu müssen.
Auffällig ist aber, dass die Lösung einmal mehr ein Schritt hin zu bargeldlosem Bezahlen ist – denn naturgemäß funktioniert das Pay-on-Shopfloor-Konzept nur mit Karte oder Wearable, während Kund:innen, die mit Bargeld zahlen wollen, weiterhin anstehen müssen. Je nachdem, wie das System in Deutschland ankommt, wolle man die Lösung auch in den internationalen Filialen von Mediamarkt und Saturn einsetzen, heißt es. Genauere Angaben dazu gibt es allerdings bislang nicht.

articles.title: Grey pitches direct China payments to African businesses at Moonshot
articles.text:
Grey is offering businesses direct payments to Chinese bank accounts to reduce currency conversions and intermediaries involved in paying overseas suppliers, co-founder and chief operating officer Femi Aghedo told Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
Demonstrating the service, Aghedo showed how Grey Business customers could convert dollar or stablecoin balances into renminbi and pay suppliers in China. The feature targets businesses whose international payments can pass through several banks and currencies, adding costs and delaying settlement.
For African importers buying from Chinese manufacturers, the service offers a more direct route to suppliers in one of the continent’s most important trading markets.
The expansion comes as Grey builds its business offering alongside its consumer platform. The company says it serves more than 3 million users across 70 countries and supports payouts to more than 170 destinations.
Grey Business, launched in February, had processed $61.4 million in payment volume by June, according to the company. Stablecoins accounted for the largest share of its cross-border flows.
That mix offers an indication of how customers use digital currencies in their day-to-day financial operations. Grey allows businesses to hold USDC and USDT, transfer them, and convert them into local currencies when needed. The China payment feature extends that offering by allowing customers to convert balances into their suppliers’ required currency.
Aghedo’s demonstration also covered the more routine demands of managing a business account. Companies can hold dollar balances, issue prepaid expense cards to employees and control or freeze their use. They can make bulk payments by uploading a spreadsheet, using the exchange rates available at the time, or connect their own systems to Grey through application programming interfaces that automate payments.
Together, the tools position Grey Business as a service for managing international spending and company payments, as well as moving money across borders.
The commercial case rests on reducing friction in collecting revenue, holding funds, and paying suppliers. For a business earning in one currency and purchasing stock in another, each additional conversion or intermediary can erode its margin.
Aghedo’s presentation put the China service at the centre of that argument: businesses should be able to move from a dollar or stablecoin balance to a supplier’s bank account with fewer steps in between.

articles.title: 12 minutos: ese es el tiempo que necesitaría China para transmitir todo el conocimiento de la humanidad de 2007 utilizando esta fibra óptica de alta tecnología
articles.text:
China acaba de anunciar algo difícil de imaginar hace unos años: una velocidad de transmisión de datos de 3,2 petabits por segundo a través de una sola fibra óptica. Para entender la magnitud del experimento basta con una comparación. En 2007, la humanidad disponía de capacidad tecnológica para almacenar unos 295 exabytes de información, una cantidad equivalente a 315 veces el número estimado de granos de arena de la Tierra. Con la velocidad alcanzada por los investigadores chinos, transmitir ese volumen de datos requeriría minutos.
Una humanidad entera en 12 minutos. Ocurrió el pasado 26 de octubre de 2026, cuando el grupo público China Information and Communication Technologies (CICT), con sede en Wuhan, anunció que sus investigadores habían conseguido transmitir 3,2 petabits de información por segundo a través de una fibra óptica experimental.
La velocidad equivale a 400 terabytes por segundo, suficiente, por ejemplo, para transferir más de 20.000 películas en resolución 4K en un solo segundo, según las estimaciones del equipo. También representa una capacidad equivalente a 3,2 millones de conexiones domésticas de 1 Gb/s funcionando simultáneamente. El resultado supera en un 28% los 2,5 petabits por segundo alcanzados por el mismo grupo de investigadores meses antes.
El conocimiento de la humanidad, reducido a una cifra. En 2011, los investigadores Martin Hilbert y Priscila López publicaron en la revista Science el primer gran inventario de la capacidad tecnológica mundial para almacenar, comunicar y procesar información entre 1986 y 2007. Su conclusión fue que, al final de aquel periodo, la humanidad podía almacenar unos 295 exabytes de información, de los cuales el 94% correspondía ya a soportes digitales.
Esa capacidad equivalía a unos 295.000 millones de gigabytes y superaba 315 veces el número estimado de granos de arena del planeta. A una velocidad sostenida de 3,2 petabits por segundo, transmitir 295 exabytes requeriría aproximadamente 737,5 segundos: exactamente 12 minutos y 17,5 segundos. Y sí, la comparación es teórica y se refiere a la capacidad mundial de almacenamiento de 2007, pero la simple idea sitúa en contexto lo conseguido.
El secreto está en los 24 núcleos. Porque una fibra óptica convencional utiliza un núcleo de vidrio para transportar información mediante señales luminosas. Los ingenieros chinos han desarrollado una estructura con 24 núcleos dentro de una misma fibra, multiplicando los caminos disponibles para transmitir datos sin necesidad de tender 24 cables independientes.
Además, han combinado tres bandas del espectro infrarrojo, conocidas como S, C y L, para transportar múltiples canales de información simultáneamente. El principal desafío consistía en evitar las interferencias entre núcleos y gestionar las diferentes características de cada banda. Cuentan que la prueba alcanzó su velocidad máxima a lo largo de 10,3 kilómetros.
Un récord con una particularidad decisiva. La colaboración entre CICT, el laboratorio Pengcheng y FiberHome Fujikura reivindica un récord mundial de transmisión óptica en tiempo real mediante una arquitectura compatible con equipos comerciales. Para los “humanos” eso significa que las señales se codifican y decodifican mientras circulan, sin depender de un procesamiento posterior realizado en ordenadores de laboratorio.
La distinción importa porque Japón ya había anunciado velocidades superiores en otros experimentos, incluidos los 22,9 petabits por segundo alcanzados en 2023 por el Instituto Nacional de Tecnología de la Información y las Comunicaciones (NICT). Los resultados, en todo caso, corresponden a configuraciones y condiciones diferentes, por lo que los 3,2 petabits chinos no constituyen el récord absoluto de velocidad en fibra óptica.
La IA necesita autopistas cada vez mayores. El elefante en la habitación. El desarrollo responde a una necesidad que está creciendo con rapidez: conectar los enormes centros de datos utilizados para entrenar y ejecutar modelos de inteligencia artificial. Estas instalaciones emplean miles de procesadores que deben intercambiar constantemente cantidades gigantescas de información, y la capacidad de sus conexiones puede convertirse en un cuello de botella.
Según los ingenieros de CICT, los centros de computación de IA de nueva generación podrían necesitar entre cinco y diez veces más fibra óptica que los centros de datos tradicionales. La tecnología también podría utilizarse en las grandes redes de telecomunicaciones y en futuras infraestructuras asociadas a la 6G.
El siguiente desafío está fuera del laboratorio. Los investigadores han demostrado el funcionamiento de su tecnología sobre una distancia de 10,3 kilómetros, suficiente para estudiar conexiones entre instalaciones relativamente próximas. Pero su utilización en redes nacionales o internacionales exigiría resolver problemas adicionales relacionados con amplificadores, conectores, empalmes, fiabilidad y costes de fabricación.
Plus: las fibras multinúcleo siguen siendo más complejas que las convencionales, y todavía falta demostrar que pueden desplegarse de forma competitiva a gran escala. Mientras, el equipo chino ya contempla alcanzar los 10 petabits por segundo como siguiente objetivo. Para que nos hagamos una idea, a esa velocidad, transmitir un volumen equivalente a toda la capacidad de almacenamiento de la humanidad en 2007 requeriría menos de cuatro minutos.

articles.title: BAE Says No Data Extracted in Incident Hitting Bankruptcy Courts
articles.text:
BAE Systems has restored the federal judiciary’s Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) and says no data was taken in the cybersecurity incident that knocked it offline for more than two weeks.
“BAE Systems, Inc., working closely with the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AOUSC), has resumed operations of the Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) system. No other systems were affected. No data was extracted. There was no breach of any PII,” a BAE Systems, Inc. spokesperson told SecurityWeek.
The BNC, which BAE operates under contract with the judiciary, is the channel through which all federal bankruptcy courts in the US send their notices. Notices stopped flowing through the center around October 9.
When the incident first came to light, neither BAE nor the judiciary addressed whether any data had been compromised. BAE’s new statement still leaves out what caused the incident and whether it was a cyberattack.
On October 27, the Administrative Office of the US Courts confirmed that, according to BAE, the problems had been fixed and the BNC was available again.
Bankruptcy court notices show the center came back on October 26 and began clearing the delayed notices, oldest first.
In response to the outage, the Judicial Conference declared a “Bankruptcy Rules emergency” on October 22. The declaration lets bankruptcy judges push back deadlines, pause time periods and issue related orders to deal with the fallout.
No ransomware or other cybercrime group appears to have publicly claimed responsibility for the incident.

articles.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
articles.text:
Airbnb has extended its open source Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real Time (NRT) Model Transform to update sequence based recommendation embeddings within seconds of guest activity. The change reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to less than a minute, with typical updates arriving within 10 to 30 seconds. Airbnb also reported a 1.67% improvement in offline NDCG and an approximately 0.33% increase in uncancelled bookings in online A/B testing.
The work builds on Airbnb’s JourneyFormer based sequence recommender, which uses a Transformer encoder to represent a guest’s booking, review and browsing history. Previously, the encoder ran as a daily batch job, generating embeddings that were stored in a low latency store. During a search, the ranking system retrieved the latest embedding and combined it with the live query, keeping the Transformer outside the latency sensitive serving path. However, activity occurring after the daily batch could remain absent from the embedding until the following run, with processing delays bringing effective staleness close to two days.
Airbnb’s initial architecture showing the daily batch sequence encoder, embedding store and online ranking path. (Source : Airbnb Blog Post)
Airbnb addressed the freshness problem by adding two capabilities to Chronon. Push Mode causes a streaming job to publish a notification when a feature value is committed, allowing downstream processing to react to updated guest activity rather than polling or waiting for a scheduled job. NRT Model Transform allows an already deployed model to run inside that streaming pipeline. Airbnb uses the same Transformer sequence encoder for the near real time path, avoiding a separate inference implementation for the streaming workflow.
The resulting pipeline captures events such as searches and listing views, combines them with the guest’s existing short and long-term sequence data, and triggers model inference when the updated feature state is available. The generated embedding is then written to the same low-latency store used by the batch system. Consequently, the online ranking path remains largely unchanged while the representation it retrieves becomes more current.
Pengyu Hou, Senior Software Engineer, Infrastructure at Airbnb, described the platform change as addressing the gap between event-driven data and model inference:
NRT Model Transform lets Chronon call an already deployed model ... directly from within the streaming flow.
The approach follows a broader feature serving pattern in which predictions can be updated when underlying features change rather than computed on every user request. Feast, another open-source feature platform, documents cached prediction architectures where inference is triggered by feature updates, trading additional writes and pipeline complexity for lower serving latency. Chronon instead integrates streaming computation and model transformation into its feature platform and emphasizes consistency between offline and online computation.
Airbnb’s near real-time Chronon architecture (Source: Airbnb Blog Post)
Airbnb has contributed Push Mode and NRT Model Transform to the public Chronon repository. Chronon supports both batch and streaming computation and provides online feature serving designed to maintain consistency between training and production inference.

articles.title: Watch this autonomous drone chase a person through a forest without GPS, maps, or cloud computing
articles.text:
Why it matters: Plenty of off-the-shelf drones can tail a cyclist down a trail these days, but most of them still lean on GPS to keep track of where they are. That's a problem in a forest, where a thick canopy can make the signal pretty unreliable. A lab at Purdue University has now shown off a drone that chases a person through the woods with no GPS at all.
Purdue computer science professor Aniket Bera posted the 44-second video on LinkedIn last Friday. It shows a quadcopter from his IDEAS Lab weaving between trees to keep a person in frame. And the drone works it all out on its own computer, without a map of the forest to rely on. Bera says skipping the cloud matters because a drone banking hard around a thin branch can't afford to wait on a server somewhere.
The person also keeps disappearing behind trunks, of course. For that, Bera's post lists an occlusion prediction step. It has the drone guess where its target is headed until they come back into view.
Navigating without GPS is also exactly the kind of autonomy the US military has been pouring money into. Last November, Purdue announced that the Army Research Laboratory had signed a five-year, $1.5 million deal with Bera's lab to build drones and ground robots that can find their way through hostile terrain without satellites. That said, the LinkedIn post doesn't say whether that money paid for the forest flights.
In the same post, Bera wrote that his team built every layer of the drone from scratch, from the 3D-printed carbon fiber frame to the software on the chip. As DroneXL noticed, though, the charts overlaid on the video label the drone's motion planner "SUPER" and its altitude estimate "FAST-LIO."
Those names belong to two open-source projects from the University of Hong Kong's MaRS Lab. SUPER is the lab's own LiDAR-guided drone. In a Science Robotics paper early last year, the team had it flying through unfamiliar terrain at more than 20 meters per second, or about 45 mph. A few weeks after that, the lab put the frame's design files online for free, including designs for 3D-printed parts and carbon fiber plates.
The Hong Kong lab doesn't get a mention in Bera's post, even though SUPER's code page asks anyone who builds on it to cite the team's papers. There's no paper covering the forest demo on the IDEAS Lab's publications page yet, either.
For now, anyone who wants to try building a similar drone can grab HKU's SUPER code as a free download. The lab's hardware kit lists every part needed, too, from the Livox Mid-360 LiDAR on top to the Intel NUC mini PC that runs the software.

articles.title: Altera unveils Agilex 2X, betting on AI developers to expand programmable computing - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Altera unveils Agilex 2X, betting on AI developers to expand programmable computing
Altera Corp. today announced Agilex 2X, a portfolio of field-programmable gate arrays and system-on-chip devices aimed at artificial intelligence infrastructure, robotics, communications and intelligent edge systems, pairing new hardware architecture with an agentic software strategy designed to accelerate development.
The first family, Agilex 27, targets applications that demand high throughput and bandwidth. Altera claims a 1.8-times improvement in performance per watt over Agilex 7, alongside a new on-chip data network and support for next-generation connectivity.
Software support is available now in Quartus Prime 26.3, but Agilex 27 engineering samples are expected in the second half of 2027. QuartusIQ, the company’s AI development companion announced last week, is also available now through Quartus Prime Pro Edition 26.3.
The announcement puts a product roadmap behind a theme Chief Executive Raghib Hussain emphasized when I interviewed him for theCUBE’s NYSE Wired AI Factory Series: AI is driving demand for intelligent systems that can change as quickly as their workloads.
“AI is going to force a redesign of every equipment out there,” Hussain told me.
That is the context for this new platform launch. AI is changing the architecture of computing, from the data center to machines operating in the physical world. Altera is betting that programmable hardware will have a larger role in those systems and that AI-assisted engineering can help more customers use it.
The new products come as Altera is eyeing an initial public offering of stock following Intel Corp.’s sale of a 51% stake in Altera to Silver Lake in April 2025, 10 years after Intel acquired Altera. In September, it said its parent company filed confidentially to offer stock to the public, without providing further details.
A portfolio built around different system requirements
Agilex 2X spans four families. Agilex 27 addresses intensive data processing, beamforming and radio-frequency workloads. Agilex 25 targets applications such as high-resolution video, drones and low-latency sensors. Agilex 23 combines embedded computing and real-time processing for robotics, industrial automation and automotive systems. Agilex 22 focuses on input/output-intensive functions, including board control, motor control, security and interface bridging.
Altera says the families share a Quartus software experience, reusable IP and common security and embedded software foundations. That gives customers a framework for extending engineering investments as requirements change, although it does not mean every design moves between devices without modification.
In our conversation, Hussain described a similar spectrum with basic sensor interfaces at one end, sensor aggregation and synchronization in the middle, and more demanding vision processing at the other. The portfolio reflects the view that intelligence reaches the physical world through many different combinations of processing, connectivity, power and cost.
Moving data becomes a source of value
In our conversation, Hussain put data movement at the center of Altera’s AI opportunity. “Compute is one part, but data movement is the biggest problem to be solved,” he said.
Agilex 27 addresses that challenge through two related architectural advances. Third-generation HyperFlex embeds registers throughout the routing fabric, giving the design software more opportunities to retime and pipeline processing without consuming logic resources. New adaptive logic module modes improve how designs fit into the device.
HyperFlow, a distributed on-chip data network, is designed to move multiple terabits of data per second throughout the FPGA without using programmable logic for that transport or creating routing congestion, according to Altera.
My view is that the value lies in what customers can accomplish with the complete data path. Moving information efficiently leaves more capacity for application processing and can help address bottlenecks around accelerators.
That is consistent with the AI factory architecture I have been tracking: The system becomes the unit of value. Processing, memory, networking and software must work together to produce useful intelligence within a power and cost budget.
Altera’s big opportunity is to demonstrate where programmability improves that system. Its performance-per-watt claim is a starting point, but the customer results in sustained throughput, latency and total system cost will be more telling.
Physical AI needs coordinated sensing and action
Altera’s physical AI strategy starts with a fundamental engineering problem. Sensors produce information in different formats, at different rates and with different latencies. A machine or robot needs those inputs synchronized to form a useful view of its environment.
Altera describes FPGAs aggregating, cleaning, organizing and synchronizing sensor data before presenting it to other processors. The implication extends beyond humanoid robots. Industrial equipment, drones, surgical systems and autonomous machines all create opportunities for specialized data handling and control.
This is where I see a meaningful connection between AI factories and the edge. Intelligence developed using large computing systems must ultimately operate within local constraints: available power, physical size, response time and safety requirements.
Programmable hardware offers a way to adapt parts of those systems after deployment. But Hussain acknowleged that some functions will migrate into dedicated chips when volume justifies the investment. The opportunity for Altera depends on continuing to solve the functions that are changing, specialized or difficult to justify in a custom ASIC.
The developer opportunity may be the bigger expansion lever
Hardware flexibility only creates value when customers can build with it. That makes QuartusIQ central to the strategy. The software combines Altera knowledge with the active project’s context and connects AI agents to engineering tools through Model Context Protocol.
Altera reports up to 10-times faster design creation and up to 1.5-times faster total design cycles, based on internal benchmarks comparing Quartus Prime with and without QuartusIQ. Those figures are company measurements, not guarantees across customer projects.
Faster design creation is only part of the process. Engineers must still verify functionality, establish appropriate constraints, close timing and validate behavior in hardware.
My take is that the larger strategic opportunity is expanding who can use programmable computing. Embedded and robotics engineers understand their applications, but they may lack deep FPGA expertise. If agentic tools reduce the specialist work required, more projects could become economically practical.
Altera’s robotics example makes the opportunity tangible. An engineer starts with requirements for sensors, perception and control, then uses QuartusIQ and Nvidia Nemotron to help iterate toward a validated FPGA implementation. The commercial test is whether that process reduces the time, cost and specialist expertise needed to reach production.
Expanding who can build intelligent systems
Altera is building programmable hardware for a world of changing AI systems while using AI to change how that hardware is developed. The larger opportunity is to expand who can build those systems.
If Altera can reduce the expertise and time required to turn an idea into working hardware, it could bring more applications and more developers into programmable computing.
