Jonathan Gitlin
Behind the wheel
However, it drives better. Like many a modern luxury EV, the Escalade IQ is held up by air suspension. Controlled by computers, air suspension is remarkably effective at concealing a car’s mass, although here it has been tuned for a rather floaty ride. In lesser electric SUVs—ones that weigh a mere 3 tons or less—you can often forget that curb weight entirely until it’s time to brake. Here, you just need to drive over something, like a recessed utility hole cover on the road, for the transient shock that makes its way into the cabin to remind you.
From behind the wheel, I find it slightly sobering, perhaps no bad thing when taking responsibility on the road. It’s easier to drive than one might expect, particularly at low speeds where the rear-wheel steering gives the car a shorter effective wheelbase than its actual 136.2 inches (3,460 mm). It might fill a parking space, but it’s not hard work getting it in or out. Forward visibility is good, but I found the passenger mirror less than completely effective and was glad for the blindspot monitoring camera that appeared when I used the turn signals, even if the camera quality was just the right side of potato.
At highway speeds, the rear wheels steer with the front wheels to effectively lengthen the wheelbase and thus increase straight-line stability. Nominal power and torque are 680 hp (505 kW) and 615 lb-ft (834 Nm), which you can increase to 750 hp (560 KW) and 785 lb-ft (1,064 Nm) with the V button on the steering wheel—this engages Velocity Max mode. It’s not ever going to ripple the tarmac like that electric Porsche Cayenne, but you can still hit 60 mph (97 km/h) from a standstill in less than 5 seconds should you need to.
Super Cruise works well.

I wonder if you could fit a Fit inside it?
Jonathan Gitlin
It fills my parking space.

Super Cruise is standard and works well on its premapped roads. The one-pedal driving calibration is, as always on GM EVs, very well-calibrated on its highest setting. It’s very effective for city driving, as you quickly adjust to its rate of deceleration to judge stops perfectly. There’s also a paddle on the steering wheel that will add regenerative braking on demand, should you wish to slow more but don’t feel like using the brake pedal.
The 460-mile range estimate is entirely believable, even with little attention given to driving efficiently. As you’ll note from the photos, on shorter trips the Escalade IQ reported efficiencies that wouldn’t be out of place in something like an Ioniq 5. But at highway speeds, you don’t get to recuperate nearly as much energy, and once it all averages out, the answer is close to 2.1 miles/kWh (29.6 kWh/100 km). Cadillac doesn’t provide a 10–80 percent fast charging time for the Escalade IQ—only that it can add 100 miles in 10 minutes—and by the end of the week, I was still at 65 percent state of charge, so a full DC fast-charge time remains a mystery. (But at least the car had plenty of range when it was collected.)
A tech-filled experience
Even if the Escalade IQ isn’t Cadillac’s flagship EV—that’s the hand-built $300,000 Celestiq sedan—the automaker has still packed in as much technology as it could. In front of the driver is a 55-inch display that encompasses touch-sensitive panels either side of the main instrument display and stretches across the width of the dash. On the left are the trip computer and lights, and to the right of the instrument display is the main infotainment touchscreen, which runs Android Automotive OS.

The dial controller on the center console allows you to interact with the infotainment, so you don’t need to use the touchscreen or try voice commands, something that worked here with moderate success. I would expect a slightly better scroll action considering the $153,490 sticker price for our Escalade IQ Premium Sport, but like the 55-inch display, the hardware is shared across the Cadillac EVrange. Climate controls are on a separate touchscreen, this one ahead of the center console and below the infotainment.
Another touchscreen serves the front-seat passenger, plus a pair for the middle row (the optional $1,995 rear-seat entertainment system). These stream video from a wide range of platforms—the industry mostly adopting Android Automotive OS has meant plenty of app support—and the screen for the front passenger has a filter that prevents the driver from seeing what’s being displayed while the vehicle is in motion. You can use your phone as an input controller, either as a keyboard or to play games, although it’s a little kludgy.
It is roomy in the back, and the middle row moves fore and aft. This can give the third row more than enough legroom for long journeys, although the lack of vertical space to put legs means that sitting back there involves knees next to faces.
I can see the appeal of the Escalade IQ as an alternative to the traditionally powered Escalade. It might not be very efficient for an EV, but 2.1 miles/kWh is still the equivalent of more than 70 mpg (3.3 L/100 km), whereas a standard V8 version only manages 16 mpg (14.7 L/100 km) combined. And you have to stop and fill that one up with gas almost 80 miles (129 km) before the electric one runs out of range.
Jonathan is the Automotive Editor at Ars Technica. He has a BSc and PhD in Pharmacology. In 2014 he decided to indulge his lifelong passion for the car by leaving the National Human Genome Research Institute and launching Ars Technica's automotive coverage. He lives in Washington, DC.

articles.title: Discord Makes Content on Discoverable Servers Searchable on Google and Other Search Engines
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Discord Makes Content on Discoverable Servers Searchable on Google and Other Search Engines
Discord has apparently realized that more and more companies and game studios have moved content, like announcements, guides, and product support, that would ordinarily have been hosted on blogs and forums to official Discord servers, effectively locking that content behind a Discord account and making it extraordinarily difficult to find in some cases. In response, the chat service provider has officially announced the roll-out of Server Web Pages in an effort to make discoverable Discord servers—those publicly available servers often used for support and announcements—more easily discoverable using search engines, like Google and DuckDuckGo.
Prior to Discord's launch, message boards were common, ranging from community-driven forums to official ones run by game studios. These message boards excelled at hosting long-form, structured conversations about helping people, theory crafting, and more. While they still exist today, many have moved into Discord servers. This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this.
Server Web Pages have been around for a while on Discord, and they have traditionally served as a way to find out why a Discord server exists before joining it. The new Server Web Pages update just expands on that functionality by adding a brief automated summary of ongoing conversations to the Server Web Page, along with other content that admins can push to the Server Web Page. These new changes will start rolling out on November 16, 2026, and admins of discoverable servers can opt out by labelling the server as a community server instead.
We expect this to help different types of communities in various ways:
- For fandoms, you can make specific channels an easy-to-find resource that answers the top questions new players ask.
- For content creators, you can more easily promote events and new content drops.
- For indie game developers, you can use public channels, including forums, to share updates and wiki-style information about your games.
Discord will also make actual messages and channels discoverable to search engines via the new Server Pages, and server and channel admins will have the ability to share certain content exclusively. Users will also be able to share or hide their content from public searches.
From mid-December 2026, answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages
Source:

I presume that age-gated channels are wholly exempt from any kind of public listing, so this still remains a wrinkle that won't be worked out. I know many purely informational servers have age restrictions to help combat bot waves and genuine underage accounts from entering channels meant for specialized and professional discussion.

articles.title: Is It Getting Hot In Here? Why Thermal Is No Longer A Signoff Problem
articles.text:
Applying the appropriate level of simulation and abstraction at each stage of the design process is key to effective thermal analysis.
AI, high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor packaging have pushed power density higher, and that means managing heat is becoming one of the most consequential challenges in electronic design.
The issue is no longer simply how to cool a chip after it has been designed. Thermal behavior now affects decisions spanning device performance, package architecture, mechanical stress, reliability, floor planning and ultimately system performance. So engineering teams must shift thermal analysis to earlier in the design process as they consider a much broader multi-physics strategy.
Traditionally, engineers could isolate and analyze many physical effects separately. Electrical performance could be evaluated in one environment, thermal behavior in another and mechanical stress in another and so on. But with increasing integration, a change intended to improve performance in one domain can create unintended consequences elsewhere. Higher power can increase temperature; temperature can change electrical behavior; and thermal expansion can introduce mechanical stress that ultimately affects reliability.
This is particularly worrisome when it comes to chiplets, 3D-ICs and other advanced packaging architectures. Multiple dies, interconnects, substrates, materials and cooling approaches interact within a tightly integrated structure. Designers need to understand not only what happens within an individual die but how the entire assembly behaves as a system.
And addressing this means examining both accuracy and scale. The engineer developing a chip may need detailed information about localized behavior and potential hotspots. A package engineer needs a different level of abstraction, while a system architect may need to evaluate thermal and performance tradeoffs across an even larger environment. Simulating every element at maximum fidelity throughout the entire system would be computationally impractical.
The answer is not simply more simulation. It is applying the appropriate level of simulation and abstraction at each stage of the design process. Techniques such as reduced-order modeling and superposition can help engineering teams scale analysis while preserving the information needed to make architectural decisions. These techniques provide each engineer with the fidelity required for the task while maintaining connections between the physical domains that influence one another.
This also changes when multi-physics analysis needs to occur. Waiting until final verification to discover that a floor plan creates an unacceptable thermal or mechanical condition can lead to expensive redesigns or even a complete (and expensive) design re-spin. If engineers bring multi-physics analysis into architectural exploration and floor planning, they can evaluate performance, package size, thermal behavior and reliability together, when there is still flexibility to make meaningful changes.
AI and agentic engineering workflows offer another opportunity to accelerate this process by using Model Context Protocol (MCP) to help orchestrate increasingly complex tools, models and engineering data. But AI does not eliminate the need for trusted physics-based simulation. AI-generated decisions can be difficult to trace, and models can make mistakes. Engineering teams therefore need workflows that combine automation with reliable simulation and sufficient visibility into how results are produced.
This growing thermal challenge is part of a larger transformation in electronic design. Electrical, thermal, mechanical and other physical effects can no longer be treated as isolated disciplines. They are interconnected elements of the same engineering problem.
Keysight’s goal is to enable engineers to bring these domains together earlier in the development process, applying the right physics, fidelity and automation at the right time. By shifting multi-physics analysis left – from final verification toward architecture and design exploration –engineering teams can identify problems sooner, make better-informed tradeoffs and increase confidence that increasingly complex electronic systems will perform as intended before committing to physical hardware.
So is it getting hot in here? Absolutely. But with the right approach to design exploration and analysis, it doesn’t have to be your problem.

articles.title: The GEO Playbook: How Australian brands can optimise for Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT search - Tech Guide
articles.text:
For more than two decades, the standard playbook for Australian businesses online was straightforward: identify target keywords, optimize metadata, acquire authoritative backlinks, and compete for a spot in Google’s “ten blue links.”
That paradigm has fundamentally fractured.
With the rollout of Google AI Overviews and the rise of conversational answer engines like ChatGPT Search and Perplexity, search engines are shifting from navigational directories to synthesis engines. Instead of presenting users with a list of external destinations to evaluate, large language models (LLMs) parse the web in real time, extract key facts, and deliver direct, conversational answers.
For digital marketers and business leaders across Australia, this shift presents a new challenge: Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO). To remain visible, brands must learn how to earn recommendations and citations directly inside AI-synthesized answers.
What is Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)?
Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) is the practice of structuring, writing, and technically delivering website content so that it can be accurately crawled, ingested, and cited by generative AI engines.
While traditional SEO focuses on maximizing organic rank positions and direct page clicks, GEO focuses on information gain and citation share. It’s structuring and adding information to a webpage that improves the chances that an AI agent selects your brand (or page) as a primary source when answering user queries.
The Princeton GEO benchmark
Optimizing for generative engines is not guesswork. The foundational rules were empirically established in a landmark study led by researchers from Princeton University, Georgia Tech, the Allen Institute for AI, and IIT Delhi, titled, GEO: Generative Engine Optimization.
The researchers evaluated approximately 10,000 queries across multiple domains to measure which on-page adjustments caused generative engines to cite and attribute sources most frequently.
The study revealed two vital insights:
- Specific GEO tactics increased content visibility inside AI responses by up to 40%.
- Traditional keyword stuffing failed completely, actually decreasing visibility inside conversational engines by 10% below the baseline.
The strategies that yielded the highest attribution gains were:
- Statistics Addition: enriching content with verified quantitative data)
- Cite Sources: adding direct citations to credible third-party benchmarks
- Quotation Addition: including authoritative expert commentary.
The 4 pillars of a GEO strategy that works
To capitalize on these dynamics, Australian companies need to modernize their search architecture across four distinct technical areas.
1. Inverted pyramid / Direct answer formatting
Generative crawlers read web pages under strict latency budgets. If a scraper must read through 800 words of introductory preamble to find an answer, the LLM will skip the page in favor of a more direct competitor.
- The Fix: Place a direct, declarative answer of 40 to 60 words immediately beneath your <h2> or <h3> headers. Follow that summary with bulleted specifics, practical criteria, and data points. This provides the AI scraper with a clean, pre-packaged snippet ready for extraction.
2. Entity-based semantic structuring
Traditional crawlers establish trust by understanding index strings of text. In contrast, LLMs assess a brand’s reputation by evaluating entities and the semantic relationships between them. Entities refer to distinct people, places, organizations, and concepts. It assesses a brand’s reputation.
- The Fix: Move beyond basic schema. Implement comprehensive JSON-LD markup that maps your organization to clear entities. Use AboutPage, ItemPage, FAQPage, and sameAs schema linking directly to verified databases, which includes your Australian Business Number register, LinkedIn profile, and industry bodies. This helps language models disambiguate your brand from global namesakes.
3. Machine-readable data tables
LLMs process structured HTML far more efficiently than long paragraphs of text. When benchmarking products, listing pricing, or presenting operational workflows, plain HTML tables consistently outperform narrative prose.
| Feature / Metric | Traditional SEO Focus | Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) | 
| Primary goal | Top 3 organic ranking on Google SERP | Inclusion & citation within LLM synthesis | 
| Optimization focus | Keyword frequency, backlink volume | Reputation and associations, information gain, statistics, entity clarity | 
| Content structure | Long-form, conversational prose | Direct answers, semantic HTML, structured tables | 
| Primary metric | Organic impressions, click sessions | Citation frequency, qualified conversion rate | 
4. Technical crawl access for modern AI agents
Many businesses inadvertently block generative engines from reading their content. When companies update their robots.txt files to safeguard data against AI model training, they often accidentally block the real-time search crawlers that generate live search citations.
- The Fix: Audit your server logs and robots.txt directives. Ensure your site allows real-time retrieval bots, including Google-Extended, GPTBot, and PerplexityBot, access to public-facing informational guides, while keeping sensitive proprietary data protected behind authentication walls.
Winning brand citations in Australia
The implications of AI search are particularly pronounced for Australian mid-market companies and service providers.
When a user in Melbourne or Sydney asks ChatGPT or Gemini, “Which cybersecurity consultancy complies with the Australian Essential Eight framework?”, the engine does not output a directory of 50 links. It synthesizes a short list of two or three validated providers.
To be chosen, a business must demonstrate local consensus. LLMs verify corporate entities through third-party mentions, including regional media outlets, local industry directories, and authenticated customer reviews. If an AI model cannot triangulate your brand across external sources, it will default to citing established competitors.
Implementing comprehensive AI search optimisation is no longer a forward-looking experiment. It is the baseline required to preserve brand discovery in an ecosystem dominated by zero-click interfaces.
The 5-point GEO audit checklist
Before publishing your next digital asset, run it through this operational checklist:
- Clear header-to-answer hierarchy: Does every sub-header answer the search intent within the first two sentences?
- Proprietary data: Does the page contain original statistics, survey findings, or benchmarks that cannot be scraped elsewhere on the web?
- Verified attribution: Are technical assertions backed by outbound references to academic papers, regulatory standards, or recognized industry benchmarks?
- Valid schema implementation: Has the page been validated using Google’s Rich Results Test for appropriate JSON-LD structured data?
- Clean HTML Markup: Are key comparisons housed in standard HTML tables rather than complex JavaScript accordions or embedded images that scrapers cannot parse?
Citations over clicks
The transition toward generative search engines does not mean the end of organic traffic, but it fundamentally redefines its value.
While top-of-funnel, casual informational queries will increasingly be resolved directly within the search interface, users who follow source citations out of an AI summary do so with significantly higher commercial intent. They have already evaluated the synthesis; they are clicking through to verify credentials, request quotes, or initiate transactions.
Australian businesses that adapt their content architecture to the principles of GEO today will secure the institutional citations that define market leadership for years to come.

articles.title: Applications open for Cape Venture Bridge programme for Western Cape startups - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Western Cape tech startups are invited to apply for the first cohort of the Cape Venture Bridge, a new programme run by AfricArise that aims to prepare them for international VC and market expansion.
AfricArise, part of the AfricArena network, is delivering the six-month programme with support from the Western Cape Government’s Department of Economic Development and Tourism (DEDAT).
Twenty startups will be selected for cohort one, to receive training on market entry beyond South Africa, cross-border finance and regulation; and investor pitching, as well as at least 12 hours of one-on-one mentorship and ZAR125,000 (US$7,500) in tech credits through programme partners. All participants will also take part in a public pitch event in Cape Town.
The top five startups will join a fully funded delegation to GITEX Africa in Morocco, which takes place in April next year, with investor and partner meetings arranged ahead of their arrival.
“Cape Town founders are building companies ready to compete well beyond our borders. The Cape Venture Bridge gives them the investment readiness, the mentorship, and for the top five, a seat at GITEX Africa in Morocco, where investors and partners are looking for exactly what the Western Cape has to offer,” said Dan Mabbyalas, director of programmes at AfricArise.
He said the programme was particularly keen to receive applications from women and young founders across the province.
Tim Parle, chief director for the digital economy at DEDAT, said the Western Cape was home to some of the continent’s most innovative technology businesses.
“DEDAT welcomes initiatives of this nature that contribute to entrepreneurship, economic growth and job creation in the province. We are particularly encouraged by efforts to broaden participation by women-owned and youth-owned businesses, as well as entrepreneurs from across the Western Cape,” he said.
The programme is open to technology or innovation-driven startups registered and operating in the Western Cape, across sectors including SaaS, climate-tech, agritech, fintech, e-commerce and e-health. Applicants must be planning to enter international markets within the next 12 months, and must be led by at least two co-founders or full-time team members able to attend programme activities.
Over its first 12 months, the Cape Venture Bridge aims to support 40 startups across two cohorts, deliver more than 80 pre-arranged investor meetings and 50 business-to-business introductions, and help facilitate over ZAR3 million (US$180,000) in capital.
Applications are here until November 15.

articles.title: Pourquoi cette boîte à deux vitesses pourrait changer la donne pour les motos électriques sur autoroute
articles.text:
Sur la plupart des motos électriques, on ne passe pas de vitesses : le moteur entraîne la roue arrière avec un rapport unique, du démarrage jusqu’à la vitesse maximale. E-Motiv Shift Systems, une société britannique spécialisée dans les transmissions, veut changer ça. Elle a confirmé ce lundi 26 octobre qu’elle exposera au salon EICMA de Milan, du 3 au 8 novembre, sa boîte à deux rapports pour motos électriques. E-Motiv promet aux motards de garder des accélérations franches au démarrage tout en consommant moins sur voie rapide, là où les électriques perdent le plus d’autonomie.
Au salon, E-Motiv montrera sa technologie à travers une moto de démonstration, baptisée Demo 1, encore en construction. Le groupe britannique d’ingénierie et de design Envisage l’a conçue, et l’IAAPS, le centre de recherche sur la propulsion de l’université de Bath, se charge de l’assemblage.
Dans un communiqué publié le 25 octobre, E-Motiv vise une fin de chantier en janvier 2027 et ouvre déjà les réservations d’essais pour ce mois-là.
Pourquoi ajouter une vitesse à une moto électrique ?
Presque tous les constructeurs se contentent d’un seul rapport. C’est plus léger et cela demande moins d’entretien. Pourtant, ce rapport unique impose un compromis entre vivacité à l’accélération et régime moteur raisonnable à haute vitesse. Ce réglage pèse sur l’autonomie, et l’écart se voit vite sur autoroute. Par exemple, la Zero DS annonce 249 km d’autonomie en ville, mais seulement 161 km sur voie rapide, soit environ 36 % de moins.
Une boîte ne fera pas disparaître la résistance de l’air, qui explique l’essentiel de cette perte. En revanche, un second rapport plus long permet de faire tourner le moteur moins vite, et donc d’utiliser moins d’énergie. Porsche a fait ce choix dès 2019 sur l’essieu arrière de sa Taycan. Selon le constructeur, le premier rapport donne plus d’accélération départ arrêté, tandis que le second assure efficacité et réserves de puissance à très haute vitesse.
Une technologie venue du MotoGP, mais aucun chiffre pour l’instant
La difficulté tient au passage de vitesse lui-même. Sur une moto thermique, la poussée se coupe à chaque changement de rapport, même si un « shifter » (sélecteur assisté) ramène cette coupure à une fraction de seconde. De son côté, E-Motiv affirme que sa transmission fait passer le couple d’un chemin de transmission à l’autre sans aucune interruption. La technologie dérive du « seamless shift » mis au point par Zeroshift, la société dont est issue E-Motiv, pour les moteurs thermiques il y a environ 25 ans. Aprilia utilise ce système de passage sans coupure sur sa RS-GP de MotoGP depuis 2015.
Sur le papier, l’argument tient. E-Motiv n’a pourtant publié aucun chiffre sur le poids de sa boîte, son coût ou le gain d’autonomie attendu, alors qu’une deuxième vitesse ajoute des pièces sur des machines où chaque kilo compte. La Demo 1 reste d’ailleurs destinée à convaincre des constructeurs, aucune moto de série n’est annoncée.
Pour ce faire, des premiers essais du démonstrateur sont prévus en janvier 2027. D’ici là, l’entreprise recevra constructeurs et curieux sur le stand S79 du hall 9 de l’EICMA, à la Fiera Milano Rho.

articles.title: The EU-Startups Podcast | Interview with Jack Mardack, co-founder of Oyster | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Key points:
- Why impact should be treated as a design problem built into a business model from day one, rather than a values commitment bolted on later
- The difference between impact by intention and impact by design – and how founders and investors can tell the difference
- What it takes to prove impact with evidence, and why investors should fund proof rather than claims
- What replaces the ESG scorecard as the scorecard era comes to an end
- A ten-year vision for the European workforce if talent, capital, and opportunity finally connect across borders
In this conversation, recorded ahead of the MeOut Summit in Budapest, we sit down with Jack Mardack, co-founder of Oyster, the global employment platform that became one of only a handful of companies in the world to reach unicorn status while holding B Corp certification.
Jack shares what he learned scaling Oyster, why he believes the perceived trade-off between financial success and impact is a design failure rather than an economic law, and what the role of Chief Impact Officer actually involves day to day.
We also get into the bigger picture: why the ESG debate has become more ideological than useful, why the notable impact investing market suggests investors have already moved past that argument, and what it would mean for European capital allocation if investors started funding evidence of impact instead of claims of impact.
Finally, we look ahead: whether Europe is measuring itself against the US on the wrong dimensions, what the European workforce could look like in ten years if we get better at connecting talent, capital, and opportunity across borders, and why Jack will be sitting down at the MeOut Summit in Budapest with the founder of Hungary’s first B Corp. His book, “Impact Unleashed: Building Businesses That Scale Positive Change“, unpacks many of these ideas in depth.

Une allure premium qui demande un poignet assez large
Le design de la montre est plutôt original et l’impression générale est vraiment bonne. Sa forme carrée et sa couleur Or Moka, celle de notre exemplaire de test, lui confèrent une vraie allure de montre premium. Le bracelet en cuir composite se montre par ailleurs agréable à porter, tandis que la couronne rotative est particulièrement plaisante à utiliser.
Son gabarit reste toutefois imposant et la destine difficilement aux petits poignets : 46,5 x 41 x 11,3 mm. Elle a perdu 2 mm d’épaisseur par rapport à la Watch D2, mais elle pèse toujours 40 g sans le bracelet. Il faudra aussi tenir compte de l’étanchéité : la montre n’est pas conçue pour la natation.
L’écran AMOLED de 1,92 pouce est l’un des vrais points forts de la Watch D3. La définition de 408 x 480 pixels assure un affichage suffisamment fin et sa luminosité maximale de 3000 cd/m² est deux fois plus élevée que sur la Watch D2. Elle permet de consulter facilement les informations en extérieur, même en pleine journée. Le capteur de luminosité automatique se montre par ailleurs réactif.
Une panoplie santé construite autour du tensiomètre
Dans le détail, la Watch D3 embarque toute une panoplie de mesures, avec le traditionnel suivi de la fréquence cardiaque, globalement fiable, le sommeil, l’analyse des arythmies, la SpO₂, l’ECG ou encore la rigidité artérielle. Son principal atout reste évidemment son véritable tensiomètre au poignet et il s’est montré relativement fiable lors de nos mesures. Huawei annonce en plus une surveillance de la tension sur 24 heures.
HarmonyOS est agréable à utiliser au poignet. Pourtant, l’application Huawei Santé reste perfectible sur smartphone, et beaucoup de cadrans sont payants. Côté autonomie, lors de notre test, elle a tenu 4 jours et 9 heures, tout en activant l’ensemble des fonctions les plus énergivores, soit un peu moins que les six jours promis par la marque. Cela reste un score correct, surtout au regard de certaines montres sous Wear OS.
Toutes nos mesures sont à retrouver dans notre test de la Huawei Watch D3, signé Quentin Lorichon.
Si vous voulez la comparer à d’autres modèles, notre sélection des meilleures montres connectées présente les montres que nous recommandons en ce moment.

articles.title: L’IA devait faire économiser des milliards : seules 3% des entreprises dépassent leurs attentes
articles.text:
Les entreprises investissent massivement dans l’intelligence artificielle, mais les résultats sont encore bien loin des promesses. Selon Gartner, seules 3% dépassent leurs objectifs d’économies grâce aux gains de productivité. Un constat qui n’empêche pas les budgets de continuer à grimper.
L’intelligence artificielle devait révolutionner la productivité des entreprises et, accessoirement, leur faire économiser beaucoup d’argent. Pour le moment, la seconde partie de la promesse peine sérieusement à se concrétiser. Selon des résultats présentés par Gartner le 26 octobre, seules 3% des organisations parviennent à dépasser leurs objectifs d’économies grâce aux gains de productivité générés par l'IA.
Un résultat particulièrement décevant quand on sait que 77% des membres des conseils d’administration s’attendent justement à ce que cette technologie permette de travailler plus efficacement tout en réduisant les dépenses.
Des budgets qui explosent sans les économies promises
Le plus étonnant est que les entreprises ne semblent pas décidées à lever le pied. Selon Gartner, 85% prévoient d’augmenter leurs dépenses dans l’IA en 2027 alors que 38% dépassent déjà leur budget initial.
Les entreprises continuent donc d’investir tandis que les économies réalisées restent en deçà de leurs attentes. Entre les abonnements aux outils, les infrastructures informatiques et l’adaptation des méthodes de travail, déployer de l’IA coûte encore cher.
« À ce stade, les organisations ne réaliseront pas d’économies grâce à l'IA », prévient CV Viverito, analyste chez Gartner, lors du HR Symposium organisé à Orlando. Ce constat ne signifie pas que les salariés ne gagnent pas de temps. Le problème est plutôt de savoir ce que les entreprises font de ces heures libérées.
Gagner du temps ne suffit pas à gagner de l’argent
Automatiser la rédaction d’un compte rendu ou accélérer l’analyse d’un document peut améliorer le quotidien d'un salarié. Mais si son entreprise ne modifie pas son organisation, ces quelques heures économisées ne se traduisent pas nécessairement par une baisse des dépenses.
Gartner a d’ailleurs mesuré ce décalage. Dans une enquête menée auprès de 1 865 salariés, seulement 21% du temps libéré grâce à l’IA a été réinvesti dans des activités plus innovantes.
Pour CV Viverito, les entreprises doivent donc changer d’approche. Plutôt que de chercher systématiquement à réduire les coûts, elles devraient utiliser l’IA pour développer de nouvelles activités, améliorer leurs services ou, encore, explorer des marchés jusqu’ici inaccessibles.
Encore faut-il savoir où investir. Une autre enquête du cabinet, menée auprès de 297 responsables des ressources humaines, révèle que 78% des équipes dirigeantes ne partagent pas de vision commune des domaines où l’IA peut réellement créer de la valeur.
Gartner recommande donc de concentrer les investissements sur quelques usages pertinents, de repenser les processus de travail et de réaffecter le temps gagné à des activités véritablement productives. Bref, mieux vaut mettre l’IA au travail que finir par travailler pour elle.
Source : Gartner via Techradar

articles.title: ‘Keep learning, keep adapting’: Priyank Kharge tells IT professionals to stay ahead of AI
articles.text:
‘Keep learning, keep adapting’: Priyank Kharge tells IT professionals to stay ahead of AI
Priyank Kharge urges IT professionals to adapt to AI, upgrade their skills and prepare for changing industry needs through initiatives like Nipuna Karnataka.
If there’s one rule for surviving the AI tech shift, it’s that your learning curve can never plateau.
As artificial intelligence reshapes industries and job requirements, IT professionals must keep upgrading their skills and adapting to changing business needs, said Karnataka IT Minister Priyank Kharge on Tuesday.
Speaking at the inauguration of RSM US Integrated Services India Private Limited’s new office at Manyata Tech Park in Bengaluru on October 28, Kharge said the pace of AI adoption was creating uncertainty around future roles, making continuous learning essential for professionals.
“AI is one of the most disruptive technologies we have seen, and the speed and scale at which it is being adopted are unprecedented,” he said.
While predicting exactly how jobs and skill requirements will evolve remains difficult, Kharge said professionals must focus on building capabilities that remain relevant to industry and global markets.
“The opportunity lies in our ability to keep learning, adapt quickly and build capabilities that remain relevant to industry and global markets,” he added.
Karnataka’s talent pool keeps global businesses interested
Priyank Kharge also highlighted Karnataka’s talent pool as a key factor in attracting global businesses and Global Capability Centres (GCCs), which handle specialised business and technology operations for multinational companies.
“We have not seen a talent pool as agile as Karnataka’s, one that is ready to unlearn, relearn and be deployed at scale,” he said.
The minister credited the state’s workforce alongside its policies and infrastructure for helping attract investment. He pointed to Bengaluru’s Outer Ring Road (ORR), where approximately 800,000 people work along a 9-km stretch, describing it as one of the world’s most densely concentrated talent pools.
He added that Karnataka would continue strengthening its infrastructure while building on its workforce advantage to attract investment and support increasingly specialised, high-value work.
Nipuna Karnataka puts industry needs at the centre
To help workers prepare for evolving job requirements, Kharge highlighted Nipuna Karnataka, the state’s industry-led skilling initiative.
The programme brings industry partners into the training process, allowing companies to identify the capabilities they need and help shape relevant curricula. The government and industry then work together to prepare candidates for emerging roles.
Under the model, government support for eligible training costs is linked to employability and employment outcomes. The aim is to ensure training responds to actual hiring needs rather than leaving candidates with skills that employers may not require.
Since AI reshapes how businesses operate, the minister stressed the importance of closer industry participation in identifying emerging skill gaps and preparing the workforce accordingly.
Karnataka’s ability to stay competitive will depend on how well its workforce keeps pace with changing technology. As AI changes job roles and the skills employers look for, continuous learning could prove just as important as technical expertise in helping professionals stay relevant.

articles.title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
articles.text:
Microsoft again asked Entra ID administrators to migrate users to phishing-resistant methods to avoid sign-in disruptions before it retires SMS and voice authentication in February 2027.
This retirement process applies only to Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenant authentication scenarios and not to Azure AD B2C or Microsoft Entra External ID customer identity scenarios.
Before Microsoft retires SMS and voice authentication, admins should ensure all users in their organizations use a phishing-resistant method, since they will no longer be able to use them to complete multifactor authentication and log in to their accounts.
Admins can choose from passkeys, QR code authentication, FIDO2 security keys, and other Entra ID-supported sign-in methods.
"Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will retire starting February 1, 2027. Complete your migration before rollout begins to avoid interrupting users' sign-in experience," Microsoft said in a Microsoft 365 Message Center update on Tuesday.
"SMS and voice are vulnerable to phishing and SIM-swap attacks. Microsoft recommends passkeys for stronger, phishing-resistant protection. You can also migrate to another supported authentication method or retain SMS and voice by configuring a customer-managed telecom provider (CYOT) through the Microsoft Security Store."
As Microsoft noted in a previous reminder issued in September, admins with the Authentication Policy Administrator, Global Reader, or Security Reader roles can find users with SMS or voice authentication with the Entra SMS/Voice Policy Scanner PowerShell script.
Organizations that must use phone-based authentication have to configure third-party telecom providers through the Microsoft Security Store.
Passkeys now the default Entra ID auth method
In July, Microsoft announced that passkeys will start rolling out as the default authentication experience for the Entra ID enterprise identity service starting in September.
"As the rollout reaches each organization, users enabled for SMS or voice authentication will automatically be enabled for passkeys, and the next time they perform multifactor authentication, they'll be prompted to register a passkey," Microsoft said.
"Following this transition, on February 1, 2027, Microsoft will retire Microsoft-provided telecom delivery for SMS and voice authentication and will no longer offer SMS and voice as a native Microsoft Entra capability."
Microsoft also retired SMS first-factor sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants in August due to phishing, fraud, and account compromise risks, and stopped enabling it for newly created tenants.
Detailed guidance on deploying and managing phishing-resistant passwordless authentication in Entra ID is available on this dedicated Microsoft documentation page.

articles.title: DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite : une station électrique de 2 kWh qui se recharge au soleil comme en voiture
articles.text:
Six mois après la Power 1000 Mini, DJI est de retour sur le segment de l’énergie avec la Power Auro 2000 Elite. Cette station électrique de 2 kWh (2 016 kWh précisément) est présentée par le géant des drones comme la plus compacte de sa gamme à cette capacité. La station électrique s’inspire en effet de ces aînés pour offrir un volume de 25 litres et un poids d’environ 19 kg, ce qui lui permet d’être 24 % moins volumineuse et 14 % plus légère que la DJI Power 2000. Quant à son encombrement, il se veut proche de celui de la Power 1000 V2, qui ne stocke pourtant que 1 kWh.
Avec ses 456 × 225 × 245 mm, elle se montre aussi un peu plus compacte que l’Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 que nous avons testé (459 × 250 × 257 mm), pour un poids équivalent. DJI précise toutefois qu’elle ne remplace pas la Power 2000, qui reste sa référence pour les usages les plus gourmands.
La Power Auro 2000 Elite délivre jusqu’à 2 000 W en continu sur ses trois prises secteur, avec un signal sinusoïdal pur, et peut alimenter certains appareils d’environ 2 200 W. Elle compte aussi deux ports USB-C de 65 W, deux ports USB-A et, plus original, un câble USB-C rétractable de 140 W. Celui-ci s’enroule automatiquement dans le boîtier, de quoi recharger un ordinateur portable ou un smartphone sans chercher de câble. Dans le but de faciliter l’accès, toutes les prises sont regroupées sur une seule face.
Un chargeur solaire et un chargeur de voiture intégrés
La principale nouveauté avec ce modèle tient à sa conception tout-en-un. DJI a intégré dans le boîtier un régulateur solaire MPPT et un chargeur de voiture, là où la concurrence passe souvent par des accessoires. La station d’Anker demande, par exemple, un chargeur d’alternateur optionnel de 800 W pour se recharger rapidement en voiture.
Le port propriétaire de DJI et bien présent et les deux ports SDC de la Power Auro 2000 Elite acceptent chacun jusqu’à 600 W, pour un total de 1 200 W. Dans ces conditions, DJI évoque une recharge complète en 2,7 heures environ au soleil et 4 heures en voiture. Les câbles nécessaires sont en revanche vendus à part.
Sur secteur, avec un simple câble d’alimentation et le mode de recharge rapide activé dans l’application, la batterie accepte jusqu’à 2 000 W et passerait de 0 à 80 % en une heure, pour une charge complète en 75 minutes. Elle peut aussi combiner le secteur avec le solaire ou la voiture, toujours dans la limite de 2 000 W.
Une batterie qui vise aussi la maison
DJI met également en avant un usage domestique pour les cas de coupure, avec un mode onduleur qui bascule sur la batterie en 0,01 seconde. Cela doit permettre de garder une box internet ou un ordinateur allumés. À faible charge, la station resterait sous les 30 dB, suffisamment discrète pour fonctionner la nuit, et l’application DJI Home permet de suivre en temps réel l’énergie consommée et stockée.
Associée à des panneaux solaires et à un micro-onduleur, vendus séparément, elle peut aussi injecter jusqu’à 800 W dans le circuit électrique de la maison, à la manière d’une batterie solaire domestique, pour consommer le soir l’énergie produite en journée. Cette fonction n’est toutefois proposée que dans certains pays, précise le fabricant. DJI avance qu’avec cinq batteries d’extension, l’ensemble pourrait fournir plus de 1 000 kWh par an, avec un retour sur investissement en 3,5 ans pour l’unité principale seule. Comme toujours, ces estimations sont à prendre avec prudence, puisqu’elles dépendent largement de l’installation solaire, de l’ensoleillement et du prix de l’électricité.
La capacité de la station pourra justement être étendue jusqu’à 12 kWh avec cinq batteries d’extension de 2 kWh, présentées comme les plus compactes de DJI, mais dont la commercialisation n’interviendra que plus tard. Côté sécurité, la Power Auro 2000 Elite repose sur des cellules LFP, réputées plus stables, qui conserveraient plus de 70 % de leur capacité après 6 000 cycles, soit une dizaine d’années d’utilisation quotidienne selon DJI.
Fidèle à son écosystème, le fabricant permet enfin de recharger rapidement ses batteries de drones via les ports SDC, jusqu’à 240 W avec le câble dédié. Une batterie de DJI Air 3 passerait ainsi de 10 à 95 % en 30 minutes. La DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite est disponible dès aujourd’hui au prix de 1 099 euros.

articles.title: Una aceitera de Jaén coloca más de 5.150 placas solares a más de cuatro metros de altura sobre un olivar en producción para que la cosechadora pueda seguir pasando por debajo
articles.text:
Acesur, el grupo aceitero de Sevilla, propietario de las marcas Coosur, La Española y Guillén, ha puesto en marcha las obras de construcción de una planta solar en Vilches (Jaén), que se alzará sobre un olivar en producción. Serán más de 5.150 paneles elevados a más de cuatro metros, que suman 3,65 MWp (la potencia máxima en condiciones de pleno rendimiento) y se sitúan junto a la envasadora de la empresa, “respetando el 100 % de los árboles existentes”, según su comunicado.
Al estar elevados, según Acesur se puede mantener la labor agrícola habitual (incluso la recogida de la cosecha), aunque su instalación requiere una mayor complejidad estructural.
El sistema cuenta con un almacenamiento de 3 MWh diseñado para “optimizar el autoconsumo y mejorar la gestión de la energía generada”, según la empresa, y Greening, una empresa granadina de renovables, es la encargada de llevar a cabo la ejecución, con el apoyo de 2,8 millones de euros del Instituto para la Diversificación y Ahorro de la Energía (IDAE).
La Universidad de Jaén está colaborando en el proyecto a través de Pedro Pérez, catedrático de Tecnología Electrónica y asesor del proyecto, que aparece en el vídeo que Acesur y Greening han publicado con imágenes del prototipo de Navas de San Juan, a modo de referencia para el proyecto.
Se plantea la cuestión de si la sombra parcial supone una pérdida de cultivo de aceituna, o de si puede generar una cierta protección del olivo en periodos de estrés, pero la nota de prensa de Acesur no incluye los datos de producción del proyecto piloto.
“Para ACESUR, innovar tiene sentido cuando se hace desde el origen”, destaca Nicolás Tejada, director de Medio Ambiente de Acesur, que explica que el proyecto permite avanzar en autoconsumo renovable y “proteger el olivar del que nacen nuestros aceites”.
Juan José Pérez, responsable de I+D de Greening, señala que el proyecto demuestra “que la innovación energética puede integrarse en el territorio de forma respetuosa y eficiente”.
Qué dice el estudio de la Universidad de Jaén
Las sombras son un punto de comparación con otra investigación, de la Universidad de Jaén, que en 2023 publicó en Applied Energy un estudio titulado “Potential of agrivoltaics systems into olive groves in the Mediterranean region”, en el que se concluía que, en tal caso, los módulos deberían tener entre un 57 % y un 71 % de transparencia para no frenar el crecimiento del árbol; se trata, al parecer, de una característica específica de los olivares superintensivos, mientras que Acesur indica en su nota de prensa que el olivar de Vilches es tradicional.
Tal y como subraya la misma investigación, el modelo sugiere que un 1 % de la superficie de los olivares mediterráneos con este tipo de instalaciones podría suponer un aumento del 2,5 % de la capacidad fotovoltaica global y reducir unos cuatro millones de toneladas de CO₂ al año; sin embargo, se trata de una estimación basada en el modelo de los autores, que se refiere a otro tipo de olivar.
Cuánto producirá la planta
Tampoco figuran en la nota de prensa los MWh que generará la instalación al año (ni su cubrimiento de la demanda eléctrica, ni su coste, aparte de los 2,8 millones del IDAE, sin que se diga qué parte de la inversión total son). Las previsiones que han circulado hablan de más de 5.000 MWh al año, una cifra que tampoco especifica la nota de prensa.
Un cálculo en la herramienta de evaluación del potencial fotovoltaico (PVGIS), de la Comisión Europea y de acceso gratuito, sugiere unos 5.900 MWh al año para un sistema de 3,65 MWp, con las coordenadas de Vilches, paneles de silicio cristalino, orientación sur, inclinación de 30 grados y un factor de pérdida del 14 %, características de una planta convencional que pueden no ajustarse a las del sistema real.
Si la planta de Vilches se acercara a esa estimación, produciría más electricidad anual que las cuatro instalaciones que ya ha puesto en marcha la empresa; dichas instalaciones se encuentran en cuatro de las fábricas de la empresa, dos de ellas en la provincia de Jaén (Vilches y Jabalquinto) y otras dos en Sevilla (Dos Hermanas y La Roda de Andalucía), con una superficie de 30 000 metros cuadrados capaz de generar 3.654,70 MWh al año y proporcionar un 18 % estimado de autosuficiencia energética.
Cualquiera que haya buscado información sobre si merece la pena instalar placas solares en su tejado tarde o temprano se encuentra con el asunto de las sombras (y de si hay otras cosas que puedan generar electricidad en su lugar). Nosotros ya publicamos un artículo sobre ShadowCalculator, un sitio web gratuito que simula la sombra que proyecta un edificio sobre una zona de interés (y la versión original del artículo es de 2022). La diferencia radica en que, en este caso, no se trata de cuánta electricidad se pierde a causa de la sombra, sino de cuántas aceitunas se pierden; una cifra que no se cita en la nota de prensa.

articles.title: Qué es Media Fabric y por qué lo usarán emisoras de radio y apps streaming como Netflix
articles.text:
Una plataforma streaming como Netflix necesita producir contenidos, adaptar anuncios para públicos distintos y sostener la reproducción cuando una gran cantidad de usuarios ve el mismo evento. Oracle Media Fabric apunta a reunir esas tareas en una sola plataforma para facilitar la gestión.
Oracle anunció que la herramienta está diseñada para ayudar a empresas de medios, proveedores de streaming y marcas a reducir los tiempos y costos de producción de contenido, además de distribuir y transmitir video de alta calidad a gran escala.
La propuesta combina inteligencia artificial con infraestructura de distribución de video para facilitar la creación, edición y entrega de contenidos. Permite desarrollar publicidad dirigida a audiencias específicas, programación personalizada y experiencias de visualización compartida.
Clay Magouyrk, director ejecutivo de Oracle, explicó que la herramienta integra la creación de contenido y el streaming en un mismo flujo de trabajo.
Según indicó, el objetivo es que los creadores aprovechen mejor su material existente y adapten las experiencias de visualización para diferentes audiencias en tiempo real.
Qué compone a Oracle Media Fabric
Oracle Media Fabric reúne Oracle Creative Studio, Oracle AI Media Models y Oracle Video Edge. Además, incluye Oracle Adaptive Media Platform, que conecta la creación con la distribución de contenidos.
Oracle Creative Studio está pensada para que equipos de medios y creadores conviertan ideas en guiones gráficos, escenas, videos cinematográficos, efectos visuales y personajes virtuales.
La herramienta combina modelos de inteligencia artificial de Oracle y de terceros, que pueden elegirse según requisitos de seguridad, procedencia, costos y protección de la propiedad intelectual.
Oracle AI Media Models se enfoca en la generación y edición de videos e imágenes. También permite procesar grandes volúmenes de material audiovisual, realizar búsquedas y clasificar contenidos, además de personalizar modelos dentro de Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.
La plataforma incorpora medidas para proteger la propiedad intelectual de los clientes y reducir el riesgo de que el contenido generado infrinja los derechos de terceros.
Oracle Video Edge está dirigida a emisoras y proveedores de streaming que transmiten eventos en vivo. La plataforma utiliza información de red y reproducción en tiempo real para coordinar la capacidad disponible y dirigir a los espectadores a ubicaciones de distribución adecuadas.
El objetivo es sostener video de alta calidad y baja latencia cuando la audiencia alcanza sus niveles máximos.
La herramienta busca que la reproducción comience rápido y continúe de forma fluida a través de Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, redes de distribución de contenido y redes de proveedores de internet participantes.
Por su parte, Oracle Adaptive Media Platform permite desarrollar publicidad específica para cada audiencia, programación personalizada y experiencias de visualización compartida.
Las marcas pueden generar variantes de un anuncio base dentro de sus directrices y reglas de aprobación, sin tener que crear cada versión desde cero.
Oracle señaló que Media Fabric puede ayudar a emisoras y plataformas de streaming a comprender cómo responde el público a la programación y a la publicidad. La empresa prevé que la plataforma esté disponible en los próximos 12 meses.
Sale jefa de contenidos de Netflix
Netflix anunció la salida de Bela Bajaria, su responsable de contenidos durante los últimos tres años, un día después de comunicar el despido de cerca de 1.000 empleados, el 6% de su plantilla global. Bajaria, que llevaba una década en la compañía, será reemplazada por Peter Rice, exejecutivo de Fox y Disney.
Durante su gestión estuvo vinculada a producciones como El juego del calamar, Merlina, Adolescencia y Bridgerton.
Los recortes alcanzarán distintas áreas y regiones, con mayor impacto en producto, tecnología, asuntos legales y recursos humanos.
Netflix sostiene que seguirá invirtiendo en áreas de alto impacto mientras busca crecer en publicidad, eventos en vivo, deportes, videojuegos, contenidos infantiles, formatos cortos y herramientas basadas en inteligencia artificial.

articles.title: AbleGamers Brasil: 10 edições, 5 anos e mais de 200 controles adaptados
articles.text:
Para quem não nos conhece ainda, a AbleGamers Brasil é uma ONG dedicada à inclusão e à acessibilidade de pessoas com deficiência por meio do videogame. Em 26 de setembro de 2026, realizamos a 10ª edição do nosso evento anual. Ao longo dessa trajetória, foram mais de 200 controles adaptados doados — 82 somente em 2025 — e milhares de pessoas impactadas. Esta é a nossa história.
Como nasceu a AbleGamers?
Para quem ainda não nos conhece, começamos há mais de 20 anos nos Estados Unidos, com um grupo de amigos que se mudaram para cidades diferentes e mantinham contato jogando online toda semana. Mesmo distantes fisicamente, eles seguiam unidos pelo jogo.
Até que a condição de uma delas se agravou. Stephanie Walker, que tinha esclerose múltipla, ficou impedida de jogar. Naquele momento, todos perceberam duas coisas ao mesmo tempo: não havia quase nada de acessibilidade no mundo dos jogos eletrônicos, e essa mídia tinha um poder enorme de conectar pessoas. Dessa necessidade nasceu a AbleGamers, fundada em 2004 por Stephanie e Mark Barlet.
Como surgiu a AbleGamers Brasil?
No Brasil, o início foi mais tímido e até desorganizado. Encantados com o trabalho do projeto e com muita vontade de ajudar, dois amigos, Christian Bernauer e Eduardo Rocha, decidiram fazer uma live para arrecadar fundos. Esse foi o primeiro evento batizado de AbleGamersBR e aconteceu em 2017.
Apesar de simples e sem nenhuma estrutura, o evento deu certo e foi o primeiro passo de uma longa jornada. Ali, eles decidiram torná-lo anual. A live se repetiu ano após ano até levar à fundação da AbleGamers Brasil, em 28 de setembro de 2021 — a primeira ONG do país voltada para pessoas com deficiência em videogames e, até onde sabemos, ainda a única.
O que 10 edições do evento anual deixaram como saldo
Em setembro de 2026, aconteceu o 10º evento anual da AbleGamers Brasil. Ao longo desses anos, foram muitas histórias:
- Mais de 200 controles adaptados doados a jogadores com deficiência
- 82 controles entregues somente em 2025
- Milhares de pessoas impactadas, dentro e fora dos jogos
Por que videogame é mais do que diversão para pessoas com deficiência?
Para muitos, videogame pode parecer só uma diversão sem sentido. Já ouvimos que pessoas com deficiência têm necessidades muito mais prementes do que “jogar joguinhos”. Por esse ponto de vista, quem diz isso tem razão: os jogos eletrônicos podem ser só uma diversão vazia.
Mas eles são muito mais do que isso. São uma janela para o mundo, conectando pessoas com e sem deficiência. Permitem que as pessoas realizem feitos impossíveis na vida real. Para a maioria dos jogadores, isso significa pilotar uma nave espacial, enfrentar dragões ou lançar bolas de fogo de um cajado mágico. Para pessoas com deficiência, pode ser algo simples e mundano como andar de bicicleta, mergulhar no mar ou limpar um carro com uma lavadora de alta pressão.
Os jogos ajudam a quebrar barreiras, romper preconceitos e conectar pessoas. Já ouvimos inúmeras vezes pessoas com deficiência dizerem que, quando saem na rua, todo mundo olha para elas. Nos jogos eletrônicos, elas podem ser iguais a qualquer um.
Como a acessibilidade chega aos eventos presenciais
É justamente essa inclusão que buscamos proporcionar, dentro e fora dos jogos. Por isso, nosso trabalho se estende para além do mundo digital. Desde 2022, participamos de eventos presenciais levando acessibilidade aos visitantes de feiras como BIG Festival, gamescom latam, CCXP e Brasil Game Show.
Entre 9 e 12 de outubro de 2026, levamos acessibilidade para pessoas com deficiência que visitaram a Nintendo, a SEGA e a Devolver Digital na Brasil Game Show. Não só com controles adaptados, para que todos pudessem jogar, mas também com audiodescrição, incluindo pessoas com deficiência visual na experiência que esses eventos proporcionam.
A AbleGamers Brasil na assinatura do decreto do Marco Legal dos Games
Para coroar essa jornada, que está apenas começando, Fabrício “SDW” Ferreira, um dos membros fundadores da AbleGamers Brasil, foi a Brasília no dia 14 de outubro de 2026 para acompanhar a assinatura do decreto que regulamenta o Marco Legal dos Jogos Eletrônicos.
O Decreto nº 13.138/2026, batizado de “Desenvolve Gamers Brasil”, coloca em prática a Lei nº 14.852/2024 e reconhece os jogos eletrônicos como produtos culturais e obras audiovisuais interativas — abrindo acesso a linhas de fomento como a Lei Rouanet, a Lei do Audiovisual e o Fundo Setorial do Audiovisual. Entre as diretrizes previstas está a integração dos games a políticas públicas de educação, saúde e acessibilidade.
Fabrício, que tem Atrofia Muscular Espinhal (AME) tipo 2, pôde compartilhar sua história e contar o quanto os videogames impactaram positivamente sua vida — criando amizades e abrindo oportunidades pessoais e profissionais. Segundo ele, hoje o videogame não só faz parte de sua vida, como a tornou algo muito melhor.
Qual é a missão da AbleGamers Brasil?
Histórias como essa fazem parte do nosso trabalho diário. Nossa missão é promover a inclusão social de pessoas com deficiência por meio do videogame, criando oportunidades para conexões significativas, fomentando uma sociedade mais inclusiva e construindo comunidades e amizades duradouras através de experiências compartilhadas.
Prazer, somos a AbleGamers Brasil. E esperamos que vocês ainda ouçam falar muito sobre nós.
Christian Bernauer
Fundador e diretor-presidente
Perguntas frequentes
O que é a AbleGamers Brasil? É uma ONG brasileira dedicada à inclusão e à acessibilidade de pessoas com deficiência por meio do videogame. Fundada em 2021, é a primeira organização do país voltada exclusivamente a esse tema.
O que é um controle adaptado? É um controle modificado ou construído sob medida para que uma pessoa com deficiência consiga jogar — com botões externos, posicionamento alternativo ou acionamento por outras partes do corpo. A AbleGamers Brasil já doou mais de 200 deles.
Como apoiar a AbleGamers Brasil? As campanhas de arrecadação da ONG financiam a produção e a entrega dos controles adaptados. A organização também atua em formação de desenvolvedores em acessibilidade e na defesa de projetos de lei que reduzem tributos sobre equipamentos adaptados.

articles.title: Unos científicos "culpan" a un virus de colarse en el ADN de los chimpancés e impedirles desarrollar un cerebro humano
articles.text:
Los chimpancés tienen un parentesco increíble con los humanos. Solo tenemos un 1,2% de ADN diferente. Pero entonces, ¿por qué somos aparentemente tan distintos? Es cierto que los chimpancés son animales muy inteligentes, pero no tanto como los humanos. Nuestro cerebro está más desarrollado, por lo que puede que, hace mucho tiempo, sucediese algo que hiciera divergir el desarrollo de nuestros cerebros . Qué pudo ser eso que tanto nos alejó ha sido una incógnita durante mucho tiempo, pero ahora unos científicos de la Universidad de Lund han dado una posible respuesta: quizás se trató de un virus.
El virus que lo cambió todo. Existen algunos virus que no solo invaden las células ajenas y utilizan su maquinaria para reproducirse. También son capaces de insertar su propio ADN en medio del ADN del huésped. Si esto ocurre en las células germinales, la inserción puede pasar de generación en generación. Por eso, los científicos de la Universidad de Lund examinaron el ADN de chimpancé en busca de fragmentos virales que pudiesen resultar sospechosos. Les llamó especialmente la atención la presencia de ADN de un virus llamado Pan troglodytes endogenous retrovirus-1 (PTERV1), ya que se encuentra en estos y otros simios africanos, pero no en los humanos. Era un gran candidato.
Invasión al cerebro. El segundo motivo por el que les llamó la atención este virus fue porque su ADN se encontraba insertado cerca de un gen no codificante llamado LINC00662, que tiene un papel muy importante en el desarrollo del cerebro. Que sea no codificante significa que no tiene las instrucciones para sintetizar proteínas, sino que regula a otros genes de algún modo. En este caso, cuando se activa en el cerebro, regula positivamente los genes que favorecen que las neuronas maduren y desarrollen las extensiones necesarias para poder conectarse.
Estos científicos tenían una sospecha, pero necesitaban confirmarla, así que cultivaron en el laboratorio una especie de minicerebros experimentales, llamado organoides cerebrales humanos, y comprobaron qué ocurría si se inhibe LINC00662. Como se podía intuir, las neuronas y sus conexiones maduraron mucho menos. En cambio, cuando se eliminó la inserción viral del ADN de células madre de chimpancé, LINC00662 comenzó a funcionar con normalidad en el cerebro y las neuronas se desarrollaron mucho más. Eso sí, es importante destacar que estas son pruebas de laboratorio. No sabemos cómo afectaría a los humanos la inserción del ADN viral, ya que el comportamiento resultante depende también del resto del ADN.
Más factores implicados. Los autores del estudio insisten en que posiblemente la ralentización del desarrollo cerebral de los chimpancés con respecto al nuestro sea multifactorial. No obstante, parece que el papel del virus PTERV1 podría ser bastante relevante.
¿Por qué no nosotros? Algo que llama la atención de estos científicos es que, siendo en nuestro pasado tan parecidos a los chimpancés, el virus PTERV1 pudiese infectarles a ellos, pero no a nosotros. Hay varias hipótesis para intentar explicar esto. Una apunta a que quizás alguna de nuestras moléculas inmunitarias, como la proteína antiviral TRIM5α, pudieron actuar como escudo. La otra señala que, quizás, no coincidimos geográficamente con los chimpancés en el momento de este supuesto brote viral.
Ninguna de las hipótesis está clara, como tampoco es seguro que LINC00662 sea tan relevante en la brecha que nos separa de los chimpancés. No obstante, es una buena pista en torno a la que vale la pena seguir investigando.
Imagen|Giles Laurent

articles.title: Hacker stole personnel data about thousands of Homeland Security employees, including CBP and ICE agents | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year.
The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials.
A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access.
More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry.
The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA.
Thousands of additional records relate to staff who work at the department’s headquarters and its other agencies, including U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Federal Protective Service.
“They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” said Department of Peace in a note left with the data, which TechCrunch has seen. The hacker did not respond to TechCrunch’s email requesting comment and with questions about how the breach was carried out.
This is the latest data breach to hit the U.S. government in recent months, following earlier hacks involving the theft of thousands of FBI agents’ personnel records and the personal information of millions of serving and former military service personnel from the Pentagon’s human resources unit. It’s also the second breach involving Homeland Security this year, after the same hacker claimed to have taken thousands of contracts between the department and the private sector, including defense contractors and surveillance vendors.
The latest batch of breached data, which appears authentic, offers a rare — albeit incomplete — view into the scale and operations of Homeland Security, whose deportations, arbitrary detentions, and killings of U.S. citizens under its leadership have become a key issue for voters ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.
The stolen Homeland Security data was provided to journalist and hacker maia arson crimew, who then shared a copy with DDoSecrets, a nonprofit collective that hosts leaked datasets in the public interest.
TechCrunch verified a portion of the data as authentic by matching the names of several known Homeland Security employees against an offline copy of the database. The thousands of employee directory records appear to have been exfiltrated around mid-August, according to the timestamps on each person’s record. The number of leaked records is equivalent to about one-fifth of Homeland Security’s workforce, which totals around 220,000 staff.
It’s unclear whether the vulnerability that allowed the breach has been fixed or if Homeland Security is aware of the data theft.
A spokesperson for Homeland Security told TechCrunch after publication: “DHS is aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively. We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected. We will update the public when more information is available.”
When reached, Okta said it was aware of this report. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” a spokesperson said.
Thousands of ICE agents’ access linked to web surveillance tools, online therapy
While the leaked data includes identifiable information about agents and officers, the dataset also reveals more about the surveillance technologies and cybersecurity tools that Homeland Security employees may be able to access. Critics have called for investigations into tech companies that fund or provide their technology to ICE.
The leaked data contains information about employees’ membership in user groups within the department’s Active Directory, a system that controls access to the department’s internal tools, services, and third-party offerings used for work.
Most of the Homeland Security employees in the dataset were members of the user group that had access to Microsoft 365, the tech giant’s cloud service that hosts the agency’s emails and files, as well as user groups for accessing Adobe Acrobat, Citrix, and other typical desktop software.
The data also shows that around 4,500 users, including ICE agents and deportation officers, are members of a group called “Headspace_users.” Online therapy provider Headspace previously had an $82,500 federal contract with ICE that ended in 2023 to fund “mental health software required for ERO employees,” a reference to ICE’s deportation unit.
A spokesperson for Headspace said the company has not provided any services to DHS or ICE since 2023.
Dozens of other user groups reference Penlink, a web surveillance company that makes technology it claims can track the location data of hundreds of millions of mobile devices. Penlink has had a contract with ICE for years. The user groups vary in size, from a handful of users in local Homeland Security offices around the country to more than 2,000 users across ICE’s HSI unit nationally. One group specifically references Penlink PLX, which the company says is used to capture and analyze “real-time intelligence” from phone calls, texts, web activity, and social media.
A spokesperson for Penlink did not respond to a request for comment.
One user group also includes more than 200 CBP users associated with Mobile Fortify, a facial-recognition app used by both CBP and ICE agents to identify people and verify their information and immigration status.
The user groups also include several employees associated with ChatGPT access, including senior DHS officials, as well as other groups associated with investigations into the China-backed hacking groups known as Salt Typhoon and Volt Typhoon.
Researchers and public information advocates say that the exposed data could provide valuable leads for investigations into alleged abuses by the Trump administration, such as identifying email addresses of agents that can be used in public records requests under the Freedom of Information Act.
“Email addresses and phone numbers are indispensable tools for FOIA researchers, often making the difference between a vague records request that gets stonewalled and one that gets results,” said Ryan Shapiro, the executive director of transparency nonprofit Property of the People.
“Given the Trump administration’s contempt for even basic transparency, the need for such tools is urgent,” said Shapiro.
DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best said that the exposed Homeland Security data will be a “catalyst for investigations, empowering journalists, Congressional inquiries, legal challenges, community action and Freedom of Information Act requests.”
Updated with comment from Homeland Security.

articles.title: Pour avoir contesté ses impôts avec l'IA, elle écope de 500 € d'amende
articles.text:
Pour avoir contesté ses impôts avec l'IA, elle écope de 500 € d'amende
Une contribuable bretonne a saisi le tribunal administratif de Rennes autour d'une histoire d'impôts. Mais plutôt que d'obtenir gain de cause, elle s'en sort avec une amende, notamment à cause de son utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle.
Voilà une histoire qui devrait rappeler aux utilisateurs d'IA que cet outil doit toujours être utilisé avec parcimonie et méfiance dans bien des domaines. Celui du droit est concerné dans le sujet qui nous intéresse aujourd'hui.
Marie-Line X, a saisi le tribunal administratif de Rennes fin 2025. Sa demande concernait, dans les grandes lignes, le montant de ses impôts lié à la TVA. Non seulement le tribunal ne lui a pas donné raison, mais lui a également infligé une amende de 500 €, notamment à cause de son utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle.
L'abus (d'IA) peut déboucher sur une amende
Dans une ordonnance datée du 19 août 2026 rendue publique, le juge note tout d'abord que la requête n'a pas été précédée d'une réclamation au service territorial de la direction générale des finances publiques, comme il doit en être.
Ensuite, il souligne que cette requête a été précédée d'une autre en octobre 2025, dotée "en substance du même objet". De plus, il indique que la seconde requête a été "manifestement écrite à l'aide d'un outil d'intelligence artificielle". Pour ces deux raisons, le juge a estimé la requête abusive, débouchant sur l'amende de 500 €.
Pour le magistrat, cette demande rédigée par IA "n'est pas assortie des précisions les plus élémentaires permettant au juge d'en apprécier la portée et le bien-fondé." En d'autres termes, "aux yeux du professionnel du droit, ces requêtes ont souvent un vilain défaut : elles sont creuses et fourmillent de références fallacieuses", même si pour les justiciables "les requêtes "fabriquées par l'IA" ont toutes les apparences de leur côté : un vocabulaire juridique y est employé et le propos paraît structuré."
Si une requête à une IA concernant un sujet autour de la justice peut donc donner l'impression de pouvoir se passer d'un avocat ou de l'avis d'un professionnel, prudence donc. Le tribunal quant à lui invite à "utiliser avec tact, discernement et mesure" les outils d'intelligence artificielle. Par ailleurs, il indique que, "dans un contexte marqué par une hausse particulièrement forte du nombre de requêtes" due à l'utilisation de l'IA, l'amende de 500 € pouvait atteindre jusqu'à 10 000 € et que le juge avait fait preuve de "sobriété".
