articles.title: Nigeria's Lumora is building a one-login digital ecosystem to replace app overload - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup Lumora is building a multi-app digital ecosystem that brings chat, cloud storage, an AI assistant and study tools together under a single login.
Founded in January 2025 by Samuel Derrick, Lumora is designed to replace the handful of separate apps people typically juggle for everyday digital life.
“Lumora is essentially one platform that replaces the several separate apps people typically juggle for everyday digital life,” Derrick told Disrupt Africa. “Rather than downloading and maintaining five or six different apps, users get one login and one ecosystem.”
The platform currently houses four sub-apps – Sachat, for real-time chat; VaultX, for cloud file storage; RawAI, an AI assistant that generates text, audio and video; and Studium, a set of study tools for students.
“Most digital tools in Nigeria, and Africa broadly, solve one problem each, forcing users to juggle multiple apps that each consume separate data and storage on often-constrained devices,” said Derrick.
Lumora has shipped version 1.2 of its platform and is now building version 1.3. It is live on the web and in closed testing on the Google Play Store, and has grown to 95 registered users who have sent more than 1,000 messages.
“Growth has been entirely organic, through personal networks and direct outreach, since I don’t yet have a marketing budget,” said Derrick.
That growth came after the startup recovered from a setback that saw its active users drop from 25 to zero.
“I learned the hard way that having a working product isn’t enough. My early onboarding flow caused nearly all my first users to drop off,” he said. “That forced me to diagnose the problem and rethink the entire first-time experience.”
The startup is self-funded and has not raised any external capital. It is also pre-revenue, but has a monetisation plan in place.
“The plan is a tiered model, with a free standard tier and a paid ultimate tier, with payments processed through Flutterwave,” said Derrick. “There’s also a longer-term plan for a developer tier, where other builders can create and monetise their own apps within the Lumora ecosystem.”
Getting this far has not been easy.
“The biggest challenge has been building entirely solo – no team, no co-founder, no funding – while also being a full-time student,” Derrick said.
There have also been technical setbacks.
“I ran my own local AI training server and accidentally damaged it with water, which set back one of my in-house AI experiments,” he said.
Lumora currently operates only in Nigeria, but Derrick said the platform could travel.
“There’s no formal expansion plan yet, but the platform is built to scale to other African markets facing similar constraints around data cost and app fragmentation,” he said.

articles.title: Top 6 subscription billing platforms for MSPs and IT distributors in 2026 - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Managed service providers used to sell hours and hardware. Now a growing share of their revenue is recurring cloud subscriptions from Microsoft, Adobe, Acronis and a long tail of other vendors.
The catch is that every vendor and distributor sends its own invoice, in its own format, on its own schedule.
Market analysts don’t agree on the exact size of the managed services market in 2026. Mordor Intelligence puts it at about US$430 billion, while MarketsandMarkets is closer to US$380 billion. Either way, the money is real, and so is the admin. Flexera’s 2025 State of the Cloud Report found 84% of organisations call managing cloud spend a top challenge, and billing teams feel that first. Here are six platforms worth a look, each with one verdict.
1. Infiterra
Infiterra is a strong contender for the best subscription billing platform for MSPs and IT distributors that resell other people’s subscriptions and need one accurate invoice at the end of it. It handles prepaid, postpaid, usage-based and hybrid billing, with proration and multi-currency support, and it can consolidate several subscriptions onto a single customer invoice.
Around that core sits a product catalogue, a white-label cloud marketplace, reseller management with multi-tenant controls, and credit risk management. It connects to ERP, CRM, accounting and PSA systems, supports payment gateways, and exposes open APIs. Pre-built vendor connectors cover names like Microsoft, Adobe, Acronis and Dropbox, which is the part that matters most if Microsoft CSP automation is your pain point.
One customer, the DACH-region MSP Cosmo Consult, reports 95% automation of its billing on Infiterra’s own case page. That’s a testimonial, not independent testing, so treat it as a signal rather than proof.
Best for: distributors and larger MSPs with multi-vendor portfolios.
2. RackNap
RackNap covers subscription management, billing and a cloud marketplace for MSPs, CSPs and cloud distributors. It handles resale of Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, Google Workspace and Acronis, plus usage-based and hybrid models.
It’s feature-rich, and it’s priced like it. RackNap’s own 2026 comparison lists its Standard plan from US$10,000 a month plus setup and transaction fees, a figure the vendor reports itself.
Best for: cloud-heavy providers with the budget to match.
3. Pax8
Pax8 is a distributor marketplace first and a billing tool second. Its integrations with PSAs such as Autotask, ConnectWise, Kaseya, Syncro and SuperOps mean invoices from Pax8 flow straight into your billing, which is genuinely convenient.
The limit is obvious. It reconciles Pax8 purchases, not everything else you buy.
Best for: MSPs sourcing mostly through Pax8.
4. ZaveIT
ZaveIT targets MSPs that want ordering and billing in one place. It offers a centralised product and service catalogue and branded self-service ordering portals, so customers can order without emailing your service desk. That ties in with what managed IT support covers for a small business day to day.
Public detail on pricing and integrations is thin, so confirm connector coverage on a demo before committing.
Best for: small MSPs wanting ordering plus billing.
5. Chargebee
Chargebee is a well-established recurring billing platform, and RackNap’s comparison names it a top pick for SaaS companies. Plans, coupons, trials and dunning are all handled well. It wasn’t designed around distributor reconciliation, so expect custom connectors if you resell lots of third-party licences.
Best for: MSPs selling their own SaaS products.
6. Zuora
Zuora is the heavyweight of subscription billing, and RackNap’s comparison lists it as the pick for large enterprises. Complex pricing models are its strength. Implementation is its weakness: projects are long and costly, and a typical MSP won’t use most of what it offers.
Best for: large organisations with dedicated finance systems teams.
What to look for in a subscription billing platform
Billing for managed services is not the same as billing for a single SaaS product. A good platform has to cope with the messy middle between what you buy and what you resell.
- Vendor and distributor reconciliation. Can it ingest usage and licence data from Microsoft CSP and distributors, then match it to what you charge?
- Proration and mid-term changes. Customers add and drop seats all month. Manual credit notes get old fast.
- Hybrid pricing. Flat fees, per-seat, usage-based and bundles, sometimes on one invoice.
- Multi-currency and tax. Australian buyers need AUD handling and GST done properly, especially when vendors bill in USD. As our look at financial infrastructure for growing tech businesses explains, exchange rates can eat into margins when software is sold across borders.
- PSA, ERP and accounting integrations decide how much re-keying your team does.
- Reseller and multi-tenant controls. Essential for distributors billing through channel partners.
A caveat: no tool nails all six. Be honest about which two or three cost you the most time today, and weigh the list against those.
How to choose
Match the platform to your revenue mix, not the longest feature list.
- Distributor or large reseller with many vendors: a dedicated platform like Infiterra or RackNap.
- Mid-size MSP buying mostly from one distributor: Pax8’s marketplace may be enough.
- Small MSP: ZaveIT keeps things light.
- Own-SaaS vendor: Chargebee, or Zuora at enterprise scale.
Whichever you shortlist, ask about security early. Billing platforms hold customer and vendor data, and the Australian Signals Directorate publishes ACSC guidance on engaging MSPs that’s a sensible checklist for supplier questions.
Conclusion
If cloud resale and multi-vendor invoicing dominate your revenue, a dedicated billing platform will beat PSA billing every time. If you mostly sell your own product, a general SaaS tool is fine. Many businesses are rethinking in-house IT, which only adds to the number of subscriptions MSPs need to bill. Request demos from two or three vendors and test them with your messiest real invoice.

articles.title: Hackers Steal 2.6 Million Records From Sony’s Japanese ISP So-net
articles.text:
Hackers have stolen the personal information of current and former So-net and Plala internet subscribers in Japan, Sony Network Communications announced on October 27. Nearly 2.6 million records were impacted.
The attackers broke into the So-net member database on October 19. The company first spotted the intrusion on October 23, then took the targeted server offline and cut off traffic coming from the attackers.
By the following day, its investigators had confirmed that personal data had been taken and determined the scope of the leak.
The stolen information includes names, dates of birth, gender, phone numbers, email addresses, user IDs, and the IDs customers use to connect to the internet.
Of the roughly 2.6 million exposed records, 2.14 million belong to So-net subscribers and 443,000 to Plala (S Course) subscribers. Roughly 293,000 of them relate to people who left the services in March 2026 or later, as their details are kept for some time to handle final bills and support requests.
The hackers also obtained approximately 54,000 email addresses, along with their passwords, belonging to four additional mail services: Mail Service (G), A-Box, So-net VAIO Mail, and the PostPet email account service. So-net has not identified any password leak for the free basic mailbox that comes with a subscription.
On October 27, the company began resetting the passwords for the impacted email addresses, forcing users to set new ones before they could resume using the services.
“Due to the leak of email addresses and email address passwords, a third party who obtained the information was in a position to view, send, and receive emails using email software and So-net Webmail. We implemented these measures as an emergency step to prevent unauthorized use of customers’ email addresses,” reads a translation of an FAQ issued by So-net.
The breach also impacted 16 records containing bank account details, such as the bank and branch, account type, account number, and account holder’s name. So-net says it does not hold the PINs for these accounts.
Credit card data is not involved, because So-net does not store it. NURO and the company’s other offerings do not appear to be affected.
How the attackers got in has not been disclosed. So-net lists the cause as unauthorized access by a third party and says it is still investigating. The incident has been reported to Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission.
Related: Hackers Steal 1.8 Million Records From Nikkei
Related: 240,000 Hit by Data Breach at Japan’s Digital Agency
Related: Cyberattack Disrupts Operations of Japanese Frozen Food Giant Nichirei

articles.title: Discord öffnet Chats für Google – doch für Nutzer:innen in der EU greift eine Sonderregel
articles.text:
Discord bei Google: Welche Nachrichten bald im Suchindex landen – und warum für die EU andere Regeln gelten
Wie die Kommunikationsplattform Discord im eigenen Firmenblog mitteilt, betrifft die Öffnung für Suchmaschinen wie Google ausschließlich sogenannte „Discoverable Servers“ (öffentlich auffindbare Server). Um diesen Status zu erhalten, muss ein Server mindestens 1.000 Mitglieder zählen, seit wenigstens acht Wochen bestehen, Sicherheits- und Aktivitätskriterien erfüllen und von den Administrator:innen aktiv für die öffentliche Server-Suche freigeschaltet worden sein. Aktuell fallen weltweit mehr als 63.000 Server in diese Kategorie, während sämtliche privaten Freundes-Server, einladungspflichtige Community-Server ohne Entdeckungsstatus sowie Direktnachrichten und Gruppenchats vollständig von der Web-Indexierung ausgenommen bleiben.
Discord öffnet Server-Webseiten für Google: Unterschied zwischen KI-Zusammenfassungen und Einzelnachrichten
Auf den betroffenen Groß-Servern vollzieht sich die Neuerung in zwei getrennten Stufen, die am 16. November 2026 mit öffentlichen Server-Webseiten („Server Web Pages“) und automatisierten Kanal-Zusammenfassungen („Channel Summaries“) starten. Jeder öffentlich auffindbare Server erhält zu diesem Stichtag eine eigene Übersichtsseite im offenen Web, auf der das System laufende Diskussionen aus öffentlichen Textkanälen zusammenfasst, die ab dem 16. November geführt werden. Wie aus Discords Support-Dokumentation für Server-Webpräsenzen hervorgeht, werden diese Zusammenfassungen mithilfe von künstlicher Intelligenz erstellt, können inhaltliche Ungenauigkeiten aufweisen und lassen sich von einzelnen Server-Mitgliedern nicht per persönlicher Einstellung unterbinden.
In einer zweiten Stufe ab Mitte Dezember 2026 sollen zusätzlich einzelne Kanal-Nachrichten („Channel Messages“) im Wortlaut auf den Server-Webseiten und in den Suchergebnissen von Google erscheinen, sodass Besucher:innen dort Antworten auf Fragen lesen können, ohne ein Discord-Konto zu besitzen. Laut der offiziellen Hilfeseite zu auffindbaren Web-Inhalten berücksichtigt das System dabei ausschließlich reine Textnachrichten aus öffentlichen Kanälen, öffentlichen Threads (Unterdiskussionen) und öffentlichen Foren-Kanälen, die ab Mitte Dezember verfasst werden. Ältere Chatverläufe vor diesem Stichtag, private Threads, Kanäle mit Rollenbeschränkung sowie Bilder und Videos – abgesehen von wenigen Partner-Servern aus einer Testphase rund um Spiele wie NBA 2K, Rust und Dead by Daylight, in der lediglich Beiträge von Administrator:innen und Moderator:innen ausgespielt wurden – tauchen nicht im Web auf.
Datenschutz in der EU: Warum deutsche Discord-Nachrichten standardmäßig nicht bei Google landen
Ob eigene Textbeiträge ab Mitte Dezember überhaupt für Google freigegeben werden, hängt maßgeblich vom Standort des jeweiligen Nutzerkontos ab. Aufgrund gesetzlicher Vorgaben ist die Funktion für wörtliche Kanal-Nachrichten in der Europäischen Union – und damit auch für Nutzer:innen in Deutschland und Österreich – sowie in Großbritannien, Kanada, Brasilien, Australien und Südkorea standardmäßig deaktiviert (Opt-in). In allen anderen Regionen ist die Option für Erwachsene hingegen ab Werk eingeschaltet (Opt-out), was neben den USA auch für die Schweiz gilt. Konten von Jugendlichen schließt Discord weltweit komplett von der Veröffentlichung einzelner Nachrichten aus.
Zwar blendet Discord sowohl bei den Zusammenfassungen als auch bei den Einzelnachrichten im Web sämtliche Benutzernamen und Profilbilder aus, doch bedeutet das keinen vollständigen Schutz der Privatsphäre. Enthält der verfasste Nachrichtentext selbst persönliche Angaben oder spezifische Details, lassen sich daraus weiterhin Rückschlüsse auf die schreibende Person ziehen. Zudem betont Gruppen-Produktmanagerin Kelsey Duncombe-Smith zwar, man wolle nach dem Vorbild klassischer Internetforen lediglich das in Chats eingeschlossene Community-Wissen zugänglich machen und verkaufe keine Nachrichten an KI-Unternehmen, allerdings können externe Web-Crawler die öffentlich erreichbaren Server-Webseiten dennoch automatisiert auslesen.
Einstellungen in Discord: Was Nutzer:innen und Server-Administrator:innen beachten müssen
Wer den Status seines Kontos überprüfen oder anpassen möchte, findet in den Benutzereinstellungen unter „Daten & Datenschutz“ den globalen Schalter für die Web-Anzeige eigener Nachrichteninhalte aus öffentlichen Kanälen (im englischen Original „Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages“), der für alle öffentlich auffindbaren Server gleichermaßen greift. Dabei besteht eine technische Einschränkung: Maßgeblich ist immer die Einstellung zum Zeitpunkt des Absendens einer Nachricht, weshalb ein späteres Ausschalten des Schalters bereits veröffentlichte Beiträge nicht rückwirkend aus dem Web entfernt. Solche Nachrichten müssen einzeln in Discord gelöscht werden, woraufhin sie zwar von der Server-Webseite verschwinden, im Zwischenspeicher von Suchmaschinen wie Google aber noch entsprechend deren Aufbewahrungsfristen sichtbar bleiben können.
Für Server-Administrator:innen wiederum sind beide Funktionen in den Servereinstellungen im Bereich „Community“ unter dem neuen Menüpunkt für die Webpräsenz („Web Presence“) standardmäßig für alle öffentlichen Kanäle aktiviert, sofern sie bis zum 16. November 2026 keine Änderungen vornehmen. Dort lassen sich Kanal-Zusammenfassungen und Kanal-Nachrichten getrennt voneinander für einzelne oder sämtliche Kanäle abschalten, während sich die automatische Erstellung der Server-Webseite selbst nur verhindern lässt, indem Betreiber:innen den Status als öffentlich auffindbarer Server aufgeben und zu einem regulären Community-Server zurückkehren.
Wer die neue Vorgehensweise für komplett inakzeptabel hält, sollte sich nach einer Alternative zu Discord umsehen. Drei davon haben wir bei t3n kürzlich vorgestellt.

articles.title: InfraTrust report warns of exploited flaws in critical network infrastructure
articles.text:
Attackers are actively exploiting vulnerabilities across critical network infrastructure, and PHP flaws known as "PHP2Shell" put the web management interfaces of firewalls, VPNs, application delivery controllers, and other appliances at risk.
The findings come from Eclypsium's October InfraTrust Pulse, a monthly report tracking security advisories affecting network devices, servers, firmware, chips, and other infrastructure.
Between September 18 and October 14, InfraTrust tracked 133 new security advisories across 18 vendors, covering 2,813 vulnerabilities.
Of those advisories, 37 were rated critical, five had a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, and 58 could be exploited remotely without authentication.
Sixteen newly published advisories included vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (KEV) as they were actively exploited.
The report also warns that many network appliances, including firewalls, VPN gateways, application delivery controllers, and network-attached storage devices, embed PHP into their management interfaces.
Because vendors compile PHP into appliance firmware, customers commonly cannot install the recent PHP security updates themselves and must instead wait for each vendor to release updated firmware.
InfraTrust therefore recommends that administrators make sure PHP-backed management interfaces are not exposed to the Internet while waiting for PHP2Shell patches.
Critical infrastructure under attack
Some of the most serious vulnerabilities affect systems at the edge of enterprise networks or used to manage other infrastructure.
Threat actors target these devices because they can provide initial access to corporate environments or serve as a springboard for further attacks.
Among the actively exploited flaws highlighted by InfraTrust are:
- Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 were disclosed on September 27 after attacks had already been observed against unpatched appliances. A separate NetScaler flaw, CVE-2026-88779, affecting appliances configured for SAML was also later added to CISA's KEV catalog after exploitation was detected.
- Ivanti Connect Secure: CVE-2026-104935 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands on vulnerable VPN gateways. Ivanti said it had exploited a limited number of customers when it published the advisory. CISA later added it to the KEV.
- Check Point Security Management Server: CVE-2026-93616 allows an unauthenticated attacker to upload and execute scripts on management and logging systems. Check Point Research observed targeted attacks exploiting the flaw on September 12, targeting Spark customers.
- Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager: CVE-2026-76504 allows an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and gain administrator access to the management API. Cisco became aware of active exploitation in September.
- Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator: CVE-2026-93952 is a maximum-severity flaw affecting the system used to configure SD-WAN Edge devices. Arista says it is being actively exploited and later disclosed a second, separate exploited vulnerability (CVE-2026-114625) in the same product on October 22.
- FortiMail: CVE-2026-104286 is a critical path traversal flaw that allows an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files through the web interface. Fortinet confirmed it was exploited in attacks.
- Cisco Secure Email Gateway: CVE-2026-76519 can allow a malicious email attachment to lead to arbitrary file writes and command execution as root on vulnerable systems. Cisco learned of exploitation in October.
- F5 BIG-IP APM: CVE-2026-94127 is a critical heap overflow that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution on systems configured as OAuth authorization servers. F5 says the vulnerability has been exploited.
- PAN-OS management interface: Palo Alto Networks reported exploitation of CVE-2026-0322 in attacks on firewalls, allowing an authenticated administrator with network access to execute code as root.
php2shell exposes another problem
InfraTrust also warns that the recently disclosed PHP2Shell vulnerabilities expose another weakness in network infrastructure, as many appliances embed PHP directly into their management interfaces.
The two PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and the PHP project fixed them on October 21.
While most focus on these vulnerabilities has been on websites and web applications written in PHP, PHP is also used for management interfaces of firewalls, application delivery controllers, VPN appliances, and network-attached storage devices.
For impacted devices, administrators usually cannot update PHP themselves because vendors compile it directly into the appliance firmware. Instead, customers must wait for each vendor to rebuild and release updated firmware or software containing the patched PHP version.
Soon after the disclosure, Palo Alto Networks, F5, NetScaler, Check Point, and QNAP confirmed that some of their products were affected, while they still developed fixes for appliances.
The report also highlights a similar issue in other software components that infrastructure vendors bundle into their products.
CVE-2026-31431, a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw known as Copy Fail, has now appeared in 29 advisories across eight vendors, up from 19 advisories from six vendors last month.
InfraTrust also found older, exploited vulnerabilities in bundled components, including an Android kernel flaw affecting HP LaserJet Enterprise printers and a 2020 jQuery vulnerability in Dell Data Lakehouse software.
InfraTrust recommends that administrators prioritize patching NetScaler and Ivanti Connect Secure because these remote-access gateways can serve as a doorway into corporate networks. Next, it recommends Fortinet's October 22 FortiOS, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer security updates for internet-facing devices.
The report then recommends focusing on Check Point Security Management Server, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, VeloCloud Orchestrator, FortiMail, Cisco Secure Email Gateway, affected BIG-IP APM systems, and PAN-OS management interfaces.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.
The Blue Report 2026 measures defenses technique by technique across 338 million simulations run in customer production environments.

articles.title: Meesho narrows loss by 68% while revenue rises 34% in Q2 of FY27
articles.text:
Meesho narrows loss by 68% while revenue rises 34% in Q2 of FY27
The annual transacting user base of Meesho now stands at 284 million for Meesho and the seller base has grown to 1.13 million.
Ecommerce company Meesho reported a 68% decline in net losses even as revenues rose by 34% on a year-on-year (YoY) basis for the second quarter of FY27.
Meesho reported a net loss of Rs 132.44 crore for the three months ending September, 2026 which is the second quarter of FY27 as compared to Rs 411.36 crore recorded in the similar period a year ago.
Revenue for the second quarter touched Rs 4131.58 crore as compared to Rs 3073.67 crore a year ago.
On the performance of the company, Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey said, “Our Q2 performance reflects the strength of Meesho's operating model, with NMV (net merchandise value) growing 23% year-on-year to Rs 12,911 crore and annual transacting users reaching 284 million. More consumers are shopping on Meesho, and they are shopping more frequently, even as first-time buyers grew 16% quarter-on-quarter.”
According to the company, annual transacting users grew 21% YoY to 284 million while annual purchase frequency increased 7% YoY to 10.4 transactions per user. Meesho said NMV grew 23% YoY.
Meesho said festive-aligned NMV grew 33% YoY over the 90 days preceding Dussehra. The annual transacting sellers increased 60% YoY to 1.13 million. The e-commerce company said over 4 lakh sellers are now part of its Content Commerce ecosystem, enabling entrepreneurs to reach consumers through creator-led product discovery.
For Meesho, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a big differentiator as it transitions towards an agent-led software development with engineering productivity increasing 171% between March and September 2026 and the number of experiments rising 73%.
It noted that approximately 65% of engineering pods now operate with a single engineer directing AI agents.
“Our focus remains on reinvesting these efficiency gains into better consumer and seller experiences, accelerating innovation and building a larger, more efficient marketplace that can generate sustainable free cash flow over the long term,” Aatrey said.
Meesho said as of September 30, 2026, it had a cash balance of Rs 7,048 crore, providing flexibility to pursue long-term growth opportunities while maintaining financial discipline.

articles.title: GTA 6 pèse 210 Go sur PS5, mais vous allez pouvoir le précharger à partir de cette date
articles.text:
Attendu le 19 novembre au prix de 79,99 euros pour l’édition standard, GTA 6 fait parler de lui via le compte PlayStation Game Size, qui a déniché l’information du poids du jeu directement sur le PlayStation Store. Ce sera donc 210 Go, avec une ouverture des serveurs à minuit. Les joueurs impatients pourront lancer le téléchargement en avance dès le 12 novembre grâce au système de préchargement, une option qui n’est pas du luxe compte tenu de la taille du jeu.
Faites de la place sur le SSD de votre PlayStation 5
Le téléchargement de 210 Go représente une part importante de l’espace disponible sur une PS5 Slim dont le SSD de 825 Go ne laisse que 667 Go réellement exploitables. Vous allez donc peut-être devoir anticiper l’installation en faisant de la place dans vos jeux pour vous éviter d’avoir une mauvaise surprise le jour J ou de devoir désinstaller un jeu que vous n’avez pas encore terminé.
 🚨 Grand Theft Auto VI
– 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝 𝐒𝐢𝐳𝐞 : 210 GB
– 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 ($79.99)
Pre-Load : November 12
Release : November 19
𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 : Midnight https://t.co/5vXkgnqfC7
— PlayStation Game Size (@PlaystationSize) October 27, 2026
Depuis le premier aperçu de GTA 6, on pouvait se douter que le jeu ne serait pas léger. La promesse d’un monde ouvert extrêmement dense, bardé de lieux à explorer et d’activités annexes, demande de charger beaucoup d’éléments. La taille exacte de Grand Theft Auto VI sur Xbox Series X et S reste encore à officialiser. Pour cette dernière, qui a un disque dur plus petit que celui des autres consoles, il faudra probablement compter chaque gigaoctet pour ne pas avoir de mauvaises surprises.
Des jeux toujours plus lourds
GTA 6 bat largement les précédents jeux de Rockstar. À titre de comparaison, GTA 5 pesait environ 100 Go sur PS5, Red Dead Redemption 2 pesait de son côté autour de 120 Go pour sa version numérique, et le vénérable GTA 4 n’occupait quant à lui à peine 20 Go.
Notez que le poids de 210 Go n’est probablement pas définitif, la taille du jeu reste susceptible d’évoluer d’ici au lancement. On pense évidemment à un « patch day one » pour peaufiner l’expérience de jeu. Enfin, la vitesse de téléchargement dépendra directement de votre connexion à internet. Pour ceux qui n’ont pas un énorme débit descendant, le préchargement à partir du 12 novembre reste votre meilleur allié, en attendant la sortie officielle le 19 novembre à minuit.

articles.title: “Internet est sur le point de se briser” : le cri d’alarme de ce pionnier du Web après le piratage de 27 000 serveurs de son groupe
articles.text:
“Internet est sur le point de se briser” : le cri d’alarme de ce pionnier du Web après le piratage de 27 000 serveurs de son groupe
Près de 27 000 serveurs exposés, des ordres passés en douce sur les comptes de traders dans plus de 70 maisons de courtage, une rançon de 50 millions de dollars refusée. Le fondateur de GMO Internet Group désigne l'intelligence artificielle comme grande coupable et réclame l'aide de Tokyo. Un détail gênant ternit pourtant son plaidoyer : ses propres hackers éthiques avaient donné l'alerte bien avant l'attaque.
Le 21 octobre 2026, à 4 heures du matin, GMO Internet a commencé à éteindre tous les serveurs de son offre Onamae.com Desktop Cloud. Ces machines virtuelles Windows, louées par des particuliers pour faire tourner des robots de trading sur le Forex, venaient d'être infectées par des programmes malveillants. Les pirates ont aspiré les identifiants de courtage stockés à l'intérieur, puis s'en sont servis pour passer des ordres frauduleux. Quatre jours plus tard, Masatoshi Kumagai, patron de ce mastodonte nippon des noms de domaine, de l'hébergement et de la finance en ligne, a publié un long billet sur son blog.
	
Internet lui-même est en train de se briser. (…) Le cyberespace que nous avons bâti, convaincus qu'il apporterait le sourire aux gens, est en passe d'être détruit de fond en comble par des individus malveillants.
Le patron de GMO dénonce une "attaque par saturation" nourrie à l'IA
Selon lui, les modèles d'IA à poids ouverts, assemblés en outils d'attaque, mettent le piratage de masse à la portée du premier venu. Sa filiale GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae dit avoir détecté ARTEX, un logiciel autonome de test d'intrusion développé en Chine pour la défense, derrière des offensives visant une vingtaine d'entreprises japonaises. Kumagai évoque une "cyberattaque par saturation de l'IA", où le volume des assauts submerge les défenseurs.
【能動的サイバー防御を具申した理由】【ブログ更新】
お客様をはじめ関係者の皆様に多大なるご迷惑をおかけしておりますことを、深くお詫び申し上げます。
なぜ私たちが政府へ「能動的サイバー防御」の適用を具申したのか。 その真意と、いま直面している危機の現実について、ブログに書きました。…
— 熊谷正寿【GMO】 (@m_kumagai) October 25, 2026
Les assaillants ont présenté leur ultimatum : poursuite des manipulations sur les comptes, divulgation du contenu des PC connectés, rançongiciel, et 50 millions de dollars. GMO refuse de payer. Le 24 octobre, le groupe a demandé au gouvernement d'activer la loi de cyberdéfense active, entrée en vigueur le 1er octobre, qui permet à la police et aux Forces d'autodéfense de neutraliser les serveurs ennemis.
Piratage de GMO : une alerte interne restée sans suite
Le billet contient aussi un aveu : des hackers éthiques du groupe avaient signalé des faiblesses sur ce service. Soucieuse de préserver sa disponibilité, l'équipe a avancé trop lentement.
Au Japon, le récit passe mal. ITmedia souligne qu'aucune preuve ne démontre l'usage de l'IA dans cette intrusion. Sur X, beaucoup accusent GMO de faire porter à l'État une faute de gestion. Les pirates affirment même avoir exploité un compte administrateur commun à tous les serveurs, une version que GMO ne confirme pas.
Kumagai promet d'assumer la facture : 5 000 yens (une trentaine d'euros) pour chaque client, prise en charge intégrale des pertes vérifiées et six mois d'hébergement offert.

articles.title: Alex Mestres, divulgador de finanzas, sobre la factura de la luz: “Prioriza el uso del microondas frente al horno. Calentar o cocinar con microondas ahorra entre un 60 % y un 70 % de energía”
articles.text:
Alex Mestres, un divulgador de finanzas personales, explica cómo puede reducirse el gasto en luz en tres consejos. Su vídeo de TikTok describe unos ahorros de hasta un 40 % en la factura de luz, sin explicar cómo llega a ese porcentaje en la descripción del vídeo, publicado el 22 de noviembre de 2024, que arranca con la pregunta “¿Qué haría yo para ahorrarme hasta un 40 % en la factura de luz?”.
En la primera recomendación, el microondas, Mestres habla de priorizar su uso frente al del horno. “Calentar o cocinar con microondas ahorra entre un 60 % y un 70 % de energía en comparación con el horno”, señala la descripción del vídeo.
Los otros dos consejos versan sobre la televisión y los cargadores. Mestres recomienda desactivar el modo de espera de la televisión porque “aunque no lo parezca, este modo consume más de lo que creemos”. “Apaga completamente la TV para ahorrar hasta un 15 % en su consumo”.
En cuanto al tercer consejo, Mestres pide al espectador que desconecte los cargadores de los dispositivos cuando no estén en uso porque “cuando los dejas enchufados, siguen consumiendo energía”.
Lo que dice la guía del IDAE
El ahorro del 60-70 % que menciona Mestres coincide con la Guía Práctica de la Energía (tercera edición de 2010), del Instituto para la Diversificación y Ahorro de la Energía (IDAE), que indica que utilizar el microondas en lugar del horno convencional supone “un ahorro entre el 60 y el 70 % de energía y un ahorro considerable de tiempo”.
El IDAE también enumera métodos de preparación eficientes, en este orden: el microondas, la olla a presión y, por último, el horno. Por ejemplo, un horno eléctrico pequeño de clase D consumiría 1 kWh cada vez que se utilizara. Si se utilizaran los ahorros que propone el IDAE, el microondas consumiría entre 0,3 y 0,4 kWh cada vez que se utilizara.
Por supuesto, no son los mismos platos ni los mismos utensilios. En el modo de espera de la televisión, el 15 % también coincide con lo que el IDAE incluye en su guía: un televisor en modo de espera “puede consumir hasta un 15 % del consumo en condiciones normales de funcionamiento”. Ahora es un régimen diferente el que rige su funcionamiento. Diversas características de la televisión, según si se utilizan determinadas funciones, tienen que reaccionar de forma diferente. Los valores no pueden compararse directamente con los del horno pequeño.
Los límites europeos para la tele y los cargadores
Desde el 1 de marzo de 2021, se aplica un reglamento de diseño ecológico para pantallas de visualización. En este reglamento se indican los límites de potencia absorbida tanto en el modo preparado (espera) como en el modo preparado en red como requisitos; por ejemplo, consumos de 0,50 W o 2,20 W cuando se utiliza el modo de espera o más funciones.
Los modos de espera en la red no pueden superar un consumo de potencia básico de 2 vatios; con las funciones adicionales, esta cifra puede alcanzar hasta un máximo de 7,7 vatios si están activadas todas, entre ellas la de alta disponibilidad de red.
Una televisión que pase todo el año en modo de espera con 0,5 vatios consume unos 4,4 kWh. De ello podría deducirse que lo más importante a tener en cuenta son los ajustes. Así, este reglamento de Diseño Ecológico exige ahora que el modo preparado en red esté desactivado en la configuración de fábrica de los televisores inteligentes. La televisión debe pedir al usuario una confirmación antes de que se active una función que se controle a distancia, y el usuario “deberá poder desactivarla”.
Del mismo modo, en cuanto al consumo de los cargadores, desde el 1 de abril de 2020 se aplica un reglamento europeo de fuentes de alimentación externas: adaptadores de corriente que proporcionan corriente continua a los dispositivos a través de un enchufe.
Su anexo II establece que los adaptadores de corriente continua con una potencia nominal de salida de hasta 49 W deben tener un consumo de energía en el enchufe de no más de 0,10 W cuando no estén alimentando ningún dispositivo (el término técnico es “funcionamiento en vacío”), lo que también equivaldría a menos de 1 kWh al año.
El consejo de Mestres sobre los cargadores es, por tanto, válido, aunque, como mínimo, el consumo eléctrico que ello supone prácticamente se traduce en un ahorro ridículo en la factura de la luz.
Cómo comprobar tu propio consumo
Lo más valioso puede ser comparar las horas de cada hábito con el consumo propio. Datadis, la plataforma común de las distribuidoras, permite explorar el consumo horario, diario, etc., del suministro.
Si se descargan u observan esos datos, se puede ver si las horas en las que se utiliza el horno eléctrico coinciden con los períodos de mayor consumo. En un artículo anterior, en febrero de 2020, explicamos cómo los lectores podían consultar la página web de su distribuidora eléctrica, ya que entonces mostraba su consumo instantáneo (o potencia) en ese momento.

articles.title: El Niño menace les puits de carbone : l'OMM craint une nouvelle flambée de CO2 en 2026
articles.text:
La Nasa a prévenu, nous nous dirigeons vraisemblablement vers un épisode d’El Niño « historique » dans l’océan Pacifique. Le phénomène est officiellement de retour depuis l’été, et selon l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), El Niño va se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027. Cet épisode s’annonce particulièrement intense. Une étude publiée cet été concluait même qu’El Niño est plus puissant qu’à aucun moment depuis 1 000 ans.
Une « nouvelle flambée » des gaz à effet de serre à craindre à cause d’El Niño
Ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, l’OMM a de nouveau attiré l’attention sur l’impact potentiel de ce phénomène, en lien avec un autre triste record planétaire. « Les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre ont atteint de nouveaux records, scellant ainsi une hausse des températures à long terme. L’intensification du phénomène El Niño pourrait entraîner une nouvelle flambée de ces concentrations », résume l’organisme des Nations unies sur X.
El Niño est un phénomène climatique naturel. Il se manifeste par des anomalies de températures de surface dans l’océan Pacifique équatorial. Ces températures plus chaudes que la normale peuvent entraîner une cascade d’effets sur la planète. Avec le réchauffement planétaire, ces effets peuvent être encore plus dommageables.
Dioxyde de carbone : 53 % de plus qu’en 1750, un niveau sans précédent
Le dioxyde de carbone est le principal gaz à effet de serre lié aux activités humaines, suivi du méthane en deuxième, et de l’oxyde nitreux en troisième (qu’on appelle aussi protoxyde d’azote).
L’OMM vient de présenter un nouveau rapport portant sur les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre dans l’atmosphère. Ce texte « montre que les concentrations de surface moyennes mondiales de dioxyde de carbone (CO2), de méthane (CH4) et d’oxyde nitreux (N2O) ont atteint des niveaux sans précédent en 2025 ».
En 2025, la concentration moyenne de CO2 a atteint 426,8 ppm (parties par million), contre 377,5 ppm en 2004, année du premier bulletin. Celle du méthane a atteint 1 948 ppb (parties par milliard), et celle du N2O 339,1 ppb. Par rapport aux niveaux préindustriels de 1750, cela représente une hausse de 53 % pour le CO2, de 167 % pour le CH4 et de 26 % pour le N2O.
Ko Barrett, secrétaire générale adjointe de l’OMM, a commenté ces conclusions dans le communiqué de l’organisation : « Une nouvelle année, un nouveau record. Les gaz à effet de serre retiennent une quantité de chaleur sans précédent dans l’atmosphère, ce qui alimente l’intensification des phénomènes météorologiques extrêmes et les risques qui en découlent pour nos économies et nos sociétés. »
Ce bulletin arrive à deux semaines de la COP31, qui se tiendra à Antalya, en Turquie, du 9 au 20 novembre. L’OMM le publie chaque année pour fournir des données scientifiques aux négociateurs de la conférence des Nations unies sur le climat, qui doit cette fois traduire les engagements pris en actions concrètes.
Les puits de carbone terrestres face à El Niño
Le renforcement d’El Niño attendu pour la fin 2026 et le début 2027 inquiète l’OMM, qui craint qu’il fasse encore grimper la concentration de CO2 dans l’atmosphère. « Nous pouvons nous attendre à une nouvelle hausse des concentrations en 2026, en raison de l’utilisation de combustibles fossiles et du développement d’un épisode El Niño de forte intensité, qui aura un impact sur les puits de carbone terrestres, comme cela a été le cas en 2023/2024 », selon Oksana Tarasova, responsable scientifique chargée de coordonner la recherche et la surveillance mondiale des gaz à effet de serre à l’OMM, citée dans le communiqué.
Comme le résume Reuters, El Niño devrait favoriser un temps plus sec, ce qui compliquera l’absorption des émissions par les puits de carbone. Ces puits, à savoir les écosystèmes terrestres (forêts, sols, végétation) et les océans, absorbent environ la moitié du CO2 émis chaque année selon l’OMM, le reste s’accumulant dans l’atmosphère.
Les alertes de l’OMM au sujet d’El Niño se multiplient ces derniers temps. Quelques jours plus tôt, le 21 octobre, Celeste Saulo, secrétaire générale de l’OMM, aux côtés de Tom Fletcher, secrétaire général adjoint de l’ONU aux affaires humanitaires et coordonnateur des secours d’urgence, a prévenu que l’épisode en cours pourrait atteindre une intensité sans précédent, « au point de sortir littéralement hors du cadre des graphiques de contrôle que nous utilisons depuis 40 ans ». Tous deux ont encouragé à prendre des mesures préventives, pour protéger les personnes les plus vulnérables face aux pires conséquences du phénomène (sécheresse, inondations, faim).
Et en France, quel sera l’impact d’El Niño ?
En France, le phénomène El Niño ne devrait pas avoir un impact direct sur la météo. Le phénomène réchauffe la planète entière, avec des réactions en chaîne fortes dans les territoires des tropiques. Il n’est cependant pas responsable de tous les événements qui pourraient advenir ces prochains mois en France métropolitaine. Mais, indirectement, il augmente le risque de vagues de chaleur et de douceur anormale chez nous.
Le lien entre le changement climatique et l’intensité d’El Niño reste débattu. Ce que l’on sait, c’est qu’El Niño peut amplifier les effets du changement climatique. D’où les appels de plus en plus fréquents de l’OMM à se préparer à cet épisode d’El Niño hors norme.
Toutes vos questions sur El Niño, Numerama va les poser à un expert : voici comment participer !
El Niño est un phénomène aux conséquences complexes, dont nous allons de plus en plus entendre parler ces prochaines semaines, à mesure que l’on approchera de son pic d’intensité. Pour debunker le vrai du faux, Numerama reçoit bientôt Éric Guilyardi, océanographe et climatologue au CNRS. Il est spécialiste d’El Niño, et vous allez pouvoir lui poser toutes vos questions dans une grande FAQ que nous diffuserons sur notre chaîne YouTube.

articles.title: Pendant que l'iPhone Duo se fait attendre, le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 est presque 1 000 € moins cher que son concurrent direct — Frandroid
articles.text:
L’iPhone Duo, disponible depuis le 23 octobre, est déjà en rupture de stock, avec des livraisons repoussées jusqu’en janvier 2027 pour certains sites de revente, y compris chez Apple. Samsung, lui, a son pliable en rayon depuis un moment, le 7 août exactement. Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 se présente comme une sérieuse alternative au pliant d’Apple, où il reproduit même l’effet transparent à l’ouverture, mais pour beaucoup moins cher. Si le format passeport vous séduit, ce Fold 8 donne matière à réflexion, surtout avec 654 euros de réduction.
Les atouts du Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8
- Son format passeport de 201 g, compact plié et large déplié
- Un écran interne AMOLED de 7,6 pouces au format 4:3
- Une puce Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 et l’interface One UI 9
Lancé à 1 999 euros, le Galaxy Z Fold 8 (256 Go) bénéficie de 654 euros de remise sur Amazon, ce qui le ramène à 1 345 euros. C’est quasi 1 000 euros de moins que l’iPhone Duo. L’offre est réservée aux membres Prime, mais les autres peuvent l’obtenir pour seulement 14 euros de plus.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un format passeport qui change franchement la prise en main
Déplié, le Fold 8 mesure 123,9 x 161,4 mm pour 4,5 mm d’épaisseur, et pèse 201 g. On avait peur que ce format lasse une fois l’effet de nouveauté passé, mais les craintes s’envolent à l’usage. L’écran externe de 5,5 pouces est assez large pour taper un message ou consulter une application sans ouvrir le téléphone, ce qui n’était pas toujours le cas sur les anciens Fold, plus étroits.
Une fois ouvert, l’écran AMOLED de 7,6 pouces (2 448 x 1 848 pixels, 403 ppp) adopte un vrai format 4:3, comme une petite tablette. Vous pouvez donc passer du mode horizontal au mode vertical selon ce que vous regardez ou lisez. Les deux dalles montent à 3 000 nits en pic, assez pour rester lisibles en plein soleil. Il manque en revanche le Flex Mode. Impossible donc de poser le téléphone à moitié plié pour une visio ou une vidéo.
Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, photo et batterie face à l’iPhone Duo
À l’intérieur, la puce Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 et son GPU Adreno 840 assurent de bonnes performances. One UI 9 complète l’ensemble avec sept mises à jour majeures d’Android promises et les fonctions d’IA de Samsung. Pour la photo, il faudra faire des concessions. Le Fold 8 embarque deux capteurs de 50 mégapixels, mais ni téléobjectif ni capteur de 200 mégapixels. Les haut-parleurs sont eux aussi assez moyens pour un appareil de ce prix.
L’iPhone Duo a une batterie plus grosse que celle du Z Fold 8, mais moins endurante dans le temps. C’est un argument de plus pour le pliant de Samsung, qui a, pour rappel, l’avantage d’être disponible tout de suite et avec une belle promotion.
Pour en savoir encore plus, rendez-vous sur notre test complet du Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.

articles.title: Para tener las patatas frescas y sin brotes hay que guardarlas en la nevera y no en la despensa, según un grupo de expertos
articles.text:
Dentro de las cocinas españolas hay algunas tradiciones que no cambian, puesto que se han ido pasando entre generaciones. Una de estas es la necesidad de almacenar siempre las patatas en la despensa, en un lugar que sea fresco y alejado de la luz, pero que casi nunca es el frigorífico. Pero ahora hay algunas voces que nos están diciendo que meter este tubérculo en las neveras puede no tener repercusiones negativas.
Un estudio. El hecho de conservar las patatas de manera diferente a lo que lo han hecho nuestras madres viene de una investigación británica que se llevó a cabo entre los años 2020 y 2022. En este se simularon las condiciones de conservación doméstica, guardando dos variedades comunes de patatas en el Reino Unido a 5º y a 18 ºC durante quince días.
Lo que vieron. A lo largo de estos quince días en los que hubo dos escenarios diferentes, se vio que el almacenamiento en frío no produjo un aumento significativo de los azúcares reductores ni de la asparagina en la patata. Además, en algunas muestras el frío retrasó de forma considerable la aparición de los brotes, por lo que concluyeron que guardar las patatas en la nevera puede hacer que duren hasta el triple de tiempo que en un armario.
El hecho de que no aumente la asparagina es fundamental, puesto que es un aminoácido no esencial que tiene la patata y que es el precursor de la acrilamida, un potencial cancerígeno. Y es tan importante que ahora mismo hay esfuerzos por conseguir variantes de patatas que no cuenten con este aminoácido.
Tiene un problema. Aunque parece que los brotes tardan más que aparecer, la realidad es que hay un fenómeno conocido como "endulzamiento por frío" que puede alterar el gusto que tiene la patata. Y es que, aunque parezca algo irreal, hablamos de un proceso biológico real que hace que, por debajo de los 10 ºC, muchas variedades de patata activen una enzima que convierte su almidón en azúcares simples como la glucosa o la fructosa. Y esto hace que se sientan mucho más dulces.
Lo que el estudio británico demostró no es que el endulzamiento por frío no exista, sino que en un plazo corto y con ciertas variedades, ese cambio no es relevante. Y esto es algo que nos importa nuevamente por la acrilamida, ya que cuando freímos a altas temperaturas una patata con muchos azúcares reductores, produce una gran concentración de este aminoácido.
En España somos más cautelosos, puesto que mientras los británicos han priorizado la lucha contra el desperdicio de alimentos con el uso de las neveras, aquí no lo tienen tan claro. La referencia es la Agencia Española de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición, que sigue recomendando que las patatas se guarden en un lugar fresco y oscuro, pero no en la nevera, para no favorecer la liberación de azúcares.
Brotes y luz. En este caso es importante saber que los expertos insisten en proteger a las patatas de la luz, puesto que la exposición lumínica no solo hace que la patata se vuelva verde, sino que desencadena la producción de glicoalcaloides (como la solanina), que son tóxicos y dan un sabor amargo. Es por ello que la luz no provoca brotes, provoca solanina.
De lo que depende la producción de los brotes es el fin del periodo de dormancia del tubérculo, y esto se acelera con las temperaturas cálidas de una cocina o una despensa. Es decir, el frío del frigorífico sí retrasa eficazmente que la patata "despierte" y empiece a echar raíces.

articles.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
If you’ve tried to get an agent into production, the model and tool use are not the blocker. The main bottleneck is everything around them: how many teams can build within a secure environment, which team owns each model and tool, how AgentOps and error handling stay inside a pre-defined boundary, and how platform, Workstream, and finance teams see cost and health across accounts. For a Platform team that wants to support many agentic use cases, that’s a platform product to design and operate. In this post, we refer to the team that manages the platform as the Platform team, and to the teams that build on it as Workstream teams. Workstream teams are the domain or product teams that build and own agents on the platform.
Each Workstream team needs a paved road with approved models and tools, short-lived workload identity, isolated runtime and memory, automated evaluation, rollback, telemetry, and cost attribution. These controls need to remain consistent as Workstream teams customize prompts, tools, data access, and application behavior. When every team assembles them, controls drift, shared services become a bottleneck, and ownership is difficult to audit.
In this post, we walk through the architecture and reference implementation of an enterprise Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover the multi-account operating model, the Platform control plane, a repeatable per-Workstream deployment pattern, separate inference and tool gateways, and an evaluation pipeline that gates each agent before promotion to production. By the end, you should be able to deploy a governed Workstream from the companion blueprint, validate its security and lifecycle contracts, and use it as the foundation for your own agentic AI platform in the organization.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides modular services for building, deploying, and operating agents at scale, including runtime, gateway, identity, memory, policy, registry, and evaluations. The Enterprise Agentic AI Platform Blueprint, built on AgentCore, adds the surrounding enterprise contracts as deployable infrastructure as code: ownership, account boundaries, software delivery, observability, cost governance, and retirement.
Architectural principles
Before diving into the solution details, it helps to understand the organizational needs that drive the platform architecture. The common challenges we have heard from customers who establish an agent platform fall into these five categories:
- Governed model access: Every untrusted inference request must pass through an approved inference gateway. The gateway applies the organization’s guardrails (for example, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails or a third-party provider), restricts which models and inference AWS Regions each Workstream can use, and enforces per-Workstream rate limits, token quotas, and budgets so that no single team can exhaust shared capacity. It also carries workload identity and emits attribution data.
- Governed tool access: Agents must discover and invoke only approved tools through an authenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway, with exact targets, least-privilege execution roles, policy decisions, and an auditable owner.
- Delegated delivery: Workstream teams (for example, product teams) need to ship and roll back independently inside pre-approved boundaries, without waiting for the platform team to deploy each application or granting developers a direct infrastructure write path.
- Fleet operations and cost: Several personas need visibility across accounts without gaining write access to team workloads. Agent operations engineers need logs, metrics, traces, and quotas. Workstream owners need cost per agent against their budgets. FinOps and finance teams need chargeback by team or business unit through AWS Cost Explorer and the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR). Security and governance leads need evidence of which workload called which model and tool.
- Bounded evidence and lifecycle: Every agent release needs proof at each boundary it touches: 
         
  - Model access: An approved model call succeeds, and a call to an unapproved model or Region is denied.
  - Tool access: A subscribed tool call succeeds, and a call to a tool outside the agent’s subscription is denied with the expected error.
  - Identity: A request from another workstream’s account or identity is rejected.
  - Release: The previous agent runtime version can be restored.
  - Retirement: Teardown removes the agent’s runtime, memory, tool gateway, and tool grants in dependency order, and confirms nothing is left behind.
The blueprint addresses these needs through four connected planes: developer experience, platform control, Workstream execution, and assurance and operations. The unit of scale is the Workstream cell, not a manually configured agent or one shared workload account. The blueprint README documents the responsibilities of each plane in detail. And you will read the main planes: Agentic AI Platform control plane and Repeatable Workstream cell in the later paragraphs.
Operating models and platform components
Enterprises usually adopt one of three operating models for agentic AI:
- Centralized: A single artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) team builds and runs every agent. Governance is consistent, but that team quickly becomes a bottleneck as the number of use cases grows.
- Decentralized: Each business unit builds and operates its own agents. Teams can move quickly, but without shared standards, controls tend to drift, effort gets duplicated, and cost visibility suffers.
- Federated: A central Platform team provides shared, governed services while domain teams retain ownership of their agents, tools, and data. This model balances team autonomy with consistent guardrails and is where most enterprises land.
- For assistance choosing, see the AWS Prescriptive Guidance page on Governance Models.
Following patterns we have observed in customer engagements, the blueprint implements the federated model. The Platform team is the hub, typically a Platform product manager, architect, platform engineers, agent operations engineers, and a security and governance lead. Workstream teams are the spokes, made up of agent developers, a domain tech lead, and AI/ML engineers. An executive sponsor and the CISO sit above both.
In this blueprint, the Platform team owns the definition of each component: templates, versions, policies, and admission. Each Workstream account runs its own instance of the per-team components (Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway), so a failure or rollback stays inside one team’s boundary.
Solution overview
This solution delivers a governed, multi-account Agentic AI Platform that platform teams operate, and workstream teams such as internal product and engineering teams consume through versioned, self-service interfaces.
At enterprise scale, the developer experience plane is a catalog of organization-approved, versioned agent templates. The blueprint ships reference templates for Strands, LangGraph, and CrewAI, but you can use your choice of framework when the template preserves the same inference gateway, tool gateway, identity, policy, evaluation, and delivery contracts. Application teams own prompts, agent logic, tools, and evaluation cases. The Platform team owns the common controls and release requirements.
Out of the four planes, two carry most of the architecture:
- Agentic AI Platform control plane: The Platform account publishes versioned templates and interfaces, operates AWS Agent Registry governance records and shared Inference Gateways, admits models and Guardrails, orchestrates reviewed releases, and aggregates fleet signals. Teams consume these capabilities through code, descriptors, and pipelines rather than administrator sessions or deployment tickets.
- Repeatable Workstream cell: Each product or domain receives an isolated boundary with a team-owned source repository, a Workload pipeline, and three Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capabilities: AgentCore Runtime, actor-scoped AgentCore Memory, and an AgentCore Gateway that uses AWS_IAM authorization and exposes only the approved tool targets. The cell also holds local customer managed AWS KMS keys, tags, alarms, budgets, and a CloudWatch Observability Access Manager (OAM) source link. One cell can deploy, fail, roll back, or retire without coordinating with another team’s release.
Key components
The following diagram illustrates the operating model and governed flow of the solution.
The architecture consists of the following account layers:
- Management and governance foundation. AWS Organizations, AWS IAM Identity Center, preventive policy, audit, retention, and cost policy establish the enterprise boundary. These are logical responsibilities that can map to an existing AWS Control Tower landing zone rather than requiring a duplicate account structure.
- Security, audit, and observability layer. AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, AWS Security Hub, Amazon GuardDuty, log archive, and an Amazon CloudWatch OAM sink provide independent control-plane evidence and fleet visibility. Central operators can query shared signals without gaining write access to Workstream resources.
- Platform layer of Agentic AI Platform. Separate Platform environments own golden paths, the governance catalog, Guardrails, shared Inference Gateways, exact tool aliases, pipelines, compatibility, quotas, and common operational interfaces. Platform changes are tested against representative cells before wider rollout.
- Workstream fleet layer. Each product, domain, or regulated boundary receives one or more nonproduction and production cells. Teams own Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway, tools, data, prompts, evaluation cases, application incidents, and service-level objectives (SLOs). The same baseline can be repeated across many cells while preserving account-level isolation.
Solution walkthrough
The following sections trace the key design decisions: account topology, preventive and detective controls, the AgentCore execution path, and the delivery pipeline.
Account topology and organizational units
The blueprint defines logical account roles that separate enterprise governance, shared Platform services, and team-owned execution:
| Role | Landing-zone placement | Purpose | 
| Management foundation | Root / Security and Management | Organizations, Identity Center, preventive policy, audit, retention, and cost policy | 
| Security and log archive | Security | CloudTrail, AWS Config, Security Hub, GuardDuty, and retained audit data | 
| Observability | Security or Operations | CloudWatch OAM sink and fleet logs, metrics, traces, and cost views | 
| Agentic AI Platform | Agent Platform | Golden paths, AWS Agent Registry, Guardrails, Inference Gateways, pipelines, and fleet controls | 
| Workstream cell | Agent Workstreams | Team-owned Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway, tools, data, evaluation, and application SLOs | 
| Additional Workstream cells | Agent Workstreams | Repeat the same baseline per product, domain, environment, or regulated boundary | 
This topology integrates into an existing landing zone, a pre-configured, secure, and scalable multi-account AWS environment, where the Management, Platform, and Workstream labels describe responsibilities rather than a fixed three-account estate. An organization can operate multiple validated Platform environments and many Workstream account pairs. Start with one representative cell and prove onboarding, production promotion, rollback, centralized observability, and zero-residual retirement before repeating the baseline.
Service control policies
Service control policies constrain the maximum permissions available to Platform and Workstream accounts. They complement, rather than replace, IAM, gateway authorization, Guardrails, resource policies, network controls, and pipeline evidence. The blueprint renders and reviews the effective policies for the exact account and Region instead of relying on source-code intent alone.
- Model and Region admission: Organization policy and Gateway execution roles restrict inference to approved models and the supported Region. Adding a model or Region requires service availability, residency, IAM, quality, cost, rollback, observability, and denial validation.
- Guardrail and inference enforcement: Agents do not call model providers directly. Inference crosses the governed gateway, where the stage Guardrail and model allow-list are applied.
- Pipeline-only Workstream mutation: Workstream teams open pull requests and use the Workload pipeline. Direct developer deployment into Workstream accounts is outside the supported operating model, which keeps the reviewed release and evidence path non-bypassable.
- Registry and Gateway governance: Workstream Gateway synthesis fails when a subscribed Registry record is missing, changed, or not approved.
- Scoped deployment roles: Bootstrap policies are generated per account and Region, validated with AWS Identity and Access Management Access (IAM) Analyzer, and checked through effective-policy simulation. Administrator access is reserved for initial setup rather than routine pipeline execution.
- Separation of duties and adversarial proof: Platform controls model, Guardrail, Registry, and shared-service admission. Workstream teams control application behavior. Every denied path is paired with an authorized positive call and a mutation that proves the intended control caused the denial.
An administrator inside a Workstream account can’t create a supported fast path around these controls. New or changed organization policies need a sandbox or representative-cell soak, exact allow and deny tests, and a rollback plan before broad attachment.
CI/CD pipeline with evaluation gates
The blueprint uses reviewed Platform and Workload pipelines to enforce the following promotion sequence:
- Source and review: A pull request establishes the immutable source revision. The pipeline pins the intended branch so an unmerged change can’t silently build the repository default branch.
- Build and synth: The pipeline compiles code, runs tests and linting, creates the agent manifest, scans the digest-bound image, validates policies, resolves approved Registry descriptors, and inspects synthesized AWS CloudFormation and cdk-nag output.
- Stable roles and permission handoff: The Workload pipeline creates stable Workstream roles and pauses. The Platform pipeline grants exact tool aliases to the exact Gateway role, live policies are verified, and only then does the Workload pipeline continue.
- Deploy to nonproduction: The pipeline deploys Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway, observability, alarms, budgets, tags, and application resources into the cell’s nonproduction boundary.
- Evaluate the deployed agent: The gate invokes the real Runtime and measures regression, quality, tool success, refusal behavior, first-token latency, and cost. Every authorized call is paired with an adversarial twin: the gate calls an approved model and confirms success, then calls an unapproved model and confirms the denial. The same pattern applies to tools, cross-account identity, and throttling. If an expected denial is missing, the gate fails the build.
- Human approval: A reviewer examines the deployed evidence, known limitations, and residual risk. A generic green build is not enough when a required probe, resource, or expected denial is missing.
- Promote, observe, and roll back: Production promotion uses the reviewed revision and continuity checks. Runtime sessions are sampled through update, cancellation, rollback, restore, and re-run so the pipeline proves both the forward path and recovery path.
No Workstream deployment step has a manual fast track. The Platform team owns the release contract, but Workstream teams operate their own pipeline instances and deployment cadence. Retirement follows a strict dependency order: Platform alias grants are revoked first, then Workstream Gateway and tool roles, then Runtime, Memory, and application resources. Each step is verified before proceeding, and a final inventory confirms zero residual resources remain.
Security and governance
The blueprint implements defense in depth through reinforcing identity, policy, delivery, data, and evidence controls:
- Identity and trust boundaries: AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Cognito provide short-lived inference credentials. AWS_IAM and SigV4 authenticate tool traffic. Exact Runtime and Gateway roles, issuer and audience checks, account and Region context, and scoped bootstrap trust limit each principal to its intended path.
- Model safety and admission: Inference flows through the governed gateway described in the Solution overview, applying Guardrails and model allow-lists before every call.
- Tool authorization: The Tool Gateway invokes only Registry-approved aliases, as detailed in the Solution overview. Cedar policies provide authorization, with a retained AWS Lambda wrapper for defense in depth.
- Tenant data protection: Workstream accounts isolate application state. AgentCore memory uses actor-scoped namespaces and customer-managed KMS keys. Tools and application data remain team-owned, and retention, deletion, and access policies are explicit rather than inherited from a shared mutable workload account.
- Software supply chain and release: Reviewed source, manifest hashing, reproducible builds, digest-bound image scanning, policy validation, cdk-nag checks, deployed-runtime evaluation, human approval, rollback, and dependency-ordered teardown form one release contract. A missing check fails closed.
- Audit, observability, and cost governance: CloudTrail and retained control-plane data corroborate pipeline evidence. OAM shares logs, metrics, and traces with central operators. Standard allocation tags, budgets, quotas, and AWS Cost and Usage Report reconciliation assign ownership without giving the agent permission to rewrite its own attribution.
The repository is a reference implementation. Developers can adjust it to address their needs. The deployment and available features are based on the eu-west-1 (Ireland) Region. A substituted component, another Region, or a wider organizational rollout requires its own availability, security, load, rollback, observability, and teardown evidence.
Conclusion
In this post, we walked through an enterprise Agentic AI Platform built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The architecture separates a centrally governed Platform control plane from repeatable, team-owned Workstream cells, with distinct inference and tool gateways, and production promotion gated by deployed-runtime evaluation.
The companion repository includes a blueprint that validates these controls end to end, from pipeline gates and adversarial boundary tests through zero-residual teardown. The support claim stops at that tested boundary.
To get started, deploy one representative Workstream cell from the companion repository, prove its full lifecycle, and then automate additional cells from the same versioned baseline.
Related resources:
- Enterprise Agentic AI Platform Blueprint on GitHub
- Enterprise multi-account architecture for running agentic AI in production on AWS (Prescriptive Guidance)
- Building an Enterprise Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Workshop
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation

articles.title: Security infrastructure helps Ascend unlock its data for AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Security infrastructure helps Ascend unlock its data for AI
Manufacturers depend on security infrastructure to protect data and keep operations running when disruptions occur. For companies with complex facilities and decades of operational records, the ability to recover that data is an important part of business continuity.
At Ascend Performance Materials LLC, data protection and cyber recovery are part of preparing for operational disruptions. When a hurricane recently approached one of its major Florida plants, the company checked that local systems were backed up and recoverable at its recovery site, according to Xiong Xiong (pictured), vice president of information technology at Ascend.
“This is the stuff that helps me sleep at night and helps me go back to my executive leadership and the board and say: ‘Look, we have the resilience in place and we’ve double-checked, triple-checked, and we have the right partner helping us,'” he said. “We just put it to test literally last week.”
Xiong spoke with theCUBE Research’s Krista Case for the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Ascend moved from uncertainty about recoverability to operational confidence and what that shift means for AI adoption. (* Disclosure below.)
Proven recovery turns security infrastructure into an AI enabler
AI introduces another dimension to Ascend’s security planning. The company expects its suppliers to incorporate AI defenses into their products, Xiong explained.
“We are looking for solutions out there to have AI built in to prevent AI from causing some of these issues,” he said. “You’re now looking to have the same thing defend against itself. Previously, that was more of a pipe dream; now it’s like a requirement.”
Ascend’s resilience challenges predated its AI push, according to Xiong. Before expanding its relationship with Dell, the company struggled to complete nightly backups, verify them and move them to its recovery site, while operational requirements meant it also needed capabilities on-site.
“We needed … to still have that localization capability. But you can’t have localization capability if you don’t have the ability to back that up thoroughly and recover it,” he said.
Dell racked, configured and validated the hardware before handing it over to Ascend, Xiong noted. His team then tested the deployment, watching backups complete locally, move to the recovery site and come up in isolation.
“We have various technologies. We have technologies that are very modern, that’s very easy to back up and recover. We have some technology that we shouldn’t be running anymore … and we were able to even bring those up,” he said.
The changes have also freed up space and reduced the effort spent reorganizing data to manage consumption at each site, according to Xiong. That shift has allowed Ascend to focus more on making data available where it can be used, supporting the company’s AI strategy.
“With this working now, we’re more focused on what do we do with our data,” he said. “We’re very, very data-rich [and] information-poor, and we’re changing that.”
