articles.title: Three trends to watch from the 2026 Québec FinTech Report | BetaKit
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence is moving deeper into the systems that power financial services, putting pressure on the industry to confront questions about standards, interoperability, and capital.
“The real breakthrough in agentic commerce is not that AI can make decisions, but that ecosystems are being built to let those decisions translate into trusted transactions.”
Surinderjit Kaur Bhatti,
Fathom4sight
Those findings come from a new report released by innovation hub Station FinTech Montréal and Toronto-based Fathom4sight at the 2026 Canada FinTech Forum this week. Now in its fourth year, the report tracks the evolution of Québec’s financial technology ecosystem, including investment activity, sector employment, and vertical trends.
This year’s report zeroed in on one of the sector’s fastest-moving fronts, agentic commerce, which is drawing global firms into a race to write the rules of a new market. It also looked closer to home at the financing and commercialization challenges that could determine how much of Québec’s AI strength can translate into successful products and companies.
Here are three trends from the 2026 Québec FinTech Report that are worth watching.
Agentic commerce creates a new rules race
One of the clearest trends highlighted in this year’s Québec FinTech Report is the emergence of payments infrastructure and protocols designed specifically for AI agents. The report pointed to a new payments stack that is being assembled at several layers simultaneously, without a settled architecture for merchants to plug into.
Agentic commerce refers to transactions in which an AI system can carry out purchases on behalf of a consumer, all the way from product discovery to payment. Making this vision of commerce a functioning market requires a new rulebook for how agents connect to merchants, prove who they are, and move money securely.
Some of the world’s largest payments infrastructure companies have already started building those layers. In April of 2025, Mastercard launched Agent Pay, its own framework for agentic commerce that uses network tokens and biometric authentication. One day later, Visa unveiled its Intelligent Commerce initiative, which also includes tokenization and personalization features.
Agent Pay and Intelligent Commerce primarily address the payment and trust infrastructure needed to authorize agent-led transactions. A separate wave of initiatives is trying to standardize different parts of how agents interact, establish authority, and transact across the commerce ecosystem.
In September of 2025, Google published its Agent Payments Protocol; one month later, Visa launched a Trusted Agent Protocol with Montréal-founded Nuvei among the organizations supporting it. The report also highlighted the Agentic Commerce Protocol launched by OpenAI and Stripe, Google and Shopify’s Universal Commerce Protocol, and x402, a cryptocurrency-based payments protocol built around instant on-chain transactions.
These new protocols span several distinct functions, including checkout orchestration, which coordinates the purchase; delegated payment authority, which allows an agent to transact; agent identity, which verifies what is initiating the transaction; and finally, settlement, which refers to the transfer of funds. With different protocols addressing different and sometimes overlapping parts of the stack, merchants are left deciding which standards they should support, according to the report.
“The sequence shows a market that standardized before it settled,” the report said.
The growing protocol landscape is now pushing the industry toward making all of these standards work together across the commerce ecosystem.
The next hurdle for merchants is interoperability
How do merchants and financial institutions support different approaches to agentic commerce without needing to build separate infrastructure for each one? The 2026 Québec FinTech Report suggests the shift toward standards coordination is already underway.
In April of 2026, Google donated its Agent Payments Protocol to the FIDO Alliance, a neutral standards body, to ensure its protocol remained platform-agnostic. Visa’s Intelligent Commerce Connect was also launched as a single-merchant integration designed to help businesses accept agentic payments across multiple card networks.
“The real breakthrough in agentic commerce is not that AI can make decisions, but that ecosystems are being built to let those decisions translate into trusted transactions,” said Surinderjit Kaur Bhatti, CEO and Founder of Fathom4sight. “The organizations that embrace interoperability today will be best positioned for tomorrow’s autonomous economy.”
The technical pieces may be falling into place, but the business case for agentic commerce is still being tested. In March, OpenAI shut down Instant Checkout, a feature that allowed ChatGPT users to purchase products directly inside the chat interface. The firm cited inaccurate pricing and inventory data, and repositioned ChatGPT around product discovery. The report suggests this is evidence that the commercial model for agentic commerce remains largely unproven.
Interoperability may help solve some of the technical friction around agentic commerce, but adoption will still depend on whether companies have the resources to build and deploy these capabilities. In ecosystems like Québec, that brings the conversation back to dollars and cents.
Capital is the dividing line for Québec
Québec’s FinTech ecosystem has continued to expand over the past five years. According to the report, the province is now home to 296 FinTech companies, up from 294 last year. Thirty of those companies are categorized in the AI and data sector, while the report found that AI is being used in the operations or offerings of a majority of Québec FinTech companies across sectors.
FinTech companies in the province also sit alongside major financial institutions and a globally renowned AI research ecosystem. According to the 2026 Québec FinTech Report, however, Québec’s ability to participate in the next phase of AI-enabled financial services depends partly on who can afford it.
Financing for Québec FinTech companies rebounded in 2026, with companies collectively raising $615 million in 2026, up significantly from $161 million in 2025 and on par with investment in 2022. However, the report identified a gap between organizations that are experimenting with AI and those investing enough capital to build mature capabilities.
Among organizations spending more than $100,000 USD ($138,000 CAD) annually on AI, 62 percent had reached an advanced stage of AI maturity. The same share reported higher profitability from AI, compared to 39 percent of organizations spending below that threshold. Those findings do not establish causation, but suggest organizations making larger AI investments are also more likely to report advanced capabilities and stronger business outcomes.
The report noted that many smaller businesses understand the potential business case for AI, but lack the capital needed to accelerate their plans. In response, development banks are now pairing financing with advisory support, while established institutions are taking a larger role as capital providers.
“AI investment is entering a new phase,” said Samy Bjaiji, Director of Technological Innovation at Finance Montréal. “What was once driven primarily by venture capital is increasingly being shaped by financial institutions, development banks, and corporate balance sheets. This shift signals that AI is no longer an emerging technology trend. It is becoming a strategic economic priority.”
The AI commercialization gap also remains significant, and commercialization is, in part, a capital problem. Data from Mila and Inovia Capital estimate that Canada produces roughly 10 percent of the world’s top AI research talent, while attracting less than two percent of global AI venture capital. Turning research strength into lasting companies requires sustained investment well beyond the early stages.
The 2026 Québec FinTech Report suggests that established financial institutions, development banks, and holding companies may play a larger role in that next phase. Their involvement could determine how much of the province’s strength stays concentrated in research, and how much makes its way into the market.
PRESENTED BY
Want the full picture? Download the 2026 Québec FinTech Report to explore the latest data on AI adoption, investment activity, talent, and emerging opportunities across Québec’s FinTech ecosystem.
Featured image courtesy Station FinTech Montréal.

articles.title: Apple finally combined a toaster and a refrigerator
articles.text:
For more than 15 years, Apple has had a pretty simple answer to the idea of a touchscreen MacBook: no. Yesterday, Apple finally decided to think different and announce one anyway. “You’ve gotta touch it to believe it,” says Apple CEO John Ternus. He might be right: I haven’t yet touched it, and I still can’t quite believe it.
Apple finally combined a toaster and a refrigerator
Apple spent more than 15 years resisting a touchscreen MacBook, until now.
Steve Jobs first called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible” in 2010, arguing that “touch surfaces don’t want to be vertical” and that using one for an extended period of time makes “your arm want to fall off.” He wasn’t wrong about the fatigue aspect of using a touchscreen laptop for long periods of time, but he missed the hybrid laptop opportunity Apple is now exploring.
Apple’s resistance to touchscreen Macs has been surprisingly consistent ever since Jobs’ comments. Tim Cook famously called Microsoft’s idea of hybrid laptops and tablets a compromise. “Anything can be forced to converge,” Cook said in 2012. “You can converge a toaster and a refrigerator, but those things are probably not going to be pleasing to the user.”
Craig Federighi, Apple’s software chief, described the Mac as a “sit-down experience” in a CNET interview in 2014 and proclaimed that a MacBook wasn’t “the right interface” for a touchscreen. “We’re not all that interested in building one,” he said. Four years later, he doubled down, arguing that “lifting your arm up to poke a screen is a pretty fatiguing thing to do.”
So what’s changed to make Apple reconsider touch on a MacBook? In a Wired interview, Apple’s marketing chief Greg Joswiak admitted that touch was long overdue on the Mac. “There’s a generation of young creators and young people using our MacBook Pros that expect to touch,” he said.
But most young people won’t be in a position to buy Apple’s most expensive MacBook Pro, especially with prices starting at $2,899, nearly $1,000 more than the regular MacBook Pro. Joswiak’s comment suggests that Apple could eventually bring touchscreens to more of its MacBook lineup.
Apple typically waits for hardware to mature enough before it enters a market, allowing the company to present its own version as the more refined one, superior to the alternatives. Apple appears to be doing some of that with the OLED touchscreen on the MacBook Pro. The company told Wired reporter Steven Levy that it had redesigned the hinge on the MacBook Pro screen to stabilize it and prevent wobble. It looks reasonably sturdy, though demos from yesterday show that Apple hasn’t removed the wobble completely.
Apple has also done plenty of software work to make touch feel more at home on this MacBook Pro. The menu bar has been redesigned for touch, expanding to let you select items more easily. The traffic-light buttons that let you close and minimize windows get bigger when you try to touch them, although it could take some getting used to for some.
There are also a bunch of gestures you can use on the touch display, like swiping between pages or spaces, accessing Mission Control or App Exposé, or swiping to get to the Notification Center. They’re all very similar to what you can do with the trackpad, though.
Apple hasn’t tried to reinvent the wheel here like Windows 8, or create a Yoga-style folding laptop. It’s added the touchscreen support that pro users have been demanding for years. That seems fine because touchscreens didn’t exactly revolutionize laptops in quite the way people maybe expected a decade ago.
I rarely use touchscreens on a clamshell laptop, reaching out occasionally to swipe away notifications and pinching to zoom into photos and maps. I use touch a lot more on a device like the Surface Pro, whose form factor is very different from the MacBook Pro’s.
The most interesting software addition on the touchscreen MacBook Pro is the Dynamic Island, which originally debuted on the iPhone 14 Pro four years ago. On this touchscreen MacBook Pro, you can tap it to access quick controls, and changes to brightness or volume levels will also appear on the Dynamic Island.
Apple has been cautiously adding some iPadOS features to macOS in recent years, including Stage Manager, Control Center, and even support for iPad apps on Mac. Porting across the Dynamic Island from iOS makes a lot of sense, and it could open the door to more convergence of macOS, iOS, and iPadOS over the coming years.
Apple will now need to lean on developers to support touch in their apps on macOS, something that proved tricky for the company’s previous touchscreen MacBook effort. A decade ago, almost to the day, Apple announced the Touch Bar, calling it “revolutionary.” The touchscreen strip replaced the MacBook Pro’s function keys in 2016, but it never caught on, frustrating users with inconsistent app support before Apple finally scrapped it seven years later in 2023.
I’d expect it will be a different situation this time around, though, particularly as app developers have gotten used to the idea of touchscreens on Windows for more than a decade now. Apple has also enabled the basics like scrolling and pinch to zoom, so there might not be a huge need for developers to add much to their apps.
Speaking of Windows, I’m sure there are plenty inside Microsoft who will feel vindicated by Apple’s touchscreen decision. Cook’s comment about a toaster-refrigerator certainly caught the attention of Microsoft’s Windows and Surface teams. Former Windows chief Terry Myerson even surprised former Surface chief Panos Panay with a 3D rendering of a toaster and a refrigerator during the introduction of the Surface Pro 4 in 2015.
Apple spent years dismissing the idea of a touchscreen Mac while Microsoft spent years trying to make touch work on laptops. Windows Vista first got some limited touch support 20 years ago, before Microsoft expanded on this with full multitouch support in Windows 7 and a massive effort to overhaul Windows 8 for touchscreens and hybrid laptops and tablets.
Windows 8 definitely went too far, but the Surface Pro helped prove that touch could be useful on a PC, and even forced Apple to rethink its iPads. Apple is now finally catching up, but the more interesting question is where it goes next. Apple has spent years insisting its Mac and iPad experiences are separate. With touch finally coming to the MacBook, it’ll be fascinating to see whether Apple starts bringing those platforms closer together, or maintains they’re better off apart.

articles.title: El pasado oculto de Jocasta y su verdadero plan en 'VisionQuest', explicados
articles.text:
ATENCIÓN: El artículo contiene SPOILERS de VisionQuest.
En una semana más de estreno de VisionQuest, la serie de Marvel por fin ha dado datos muy esclarecedores sobre Jocasta, su nueva gran villana. Los episodios más recientes han revelado varios aspectos clave tanto sobre su pasado como sobre sus motivaciones y su verdadero plan final. La Casa de las Ideas ha preferido no andarse con rodeos y evitarle la incertidumbre a sus fans.
Así, en la serie de VisionQuest, Jocasta le cuenta a Ultrón cómo nació. Resulta que su apariencia humana es la de Jo Carrington. Esta mujer perdió a su padre más temprano de lo previsto debido a una grave enfermedad degenerativa. Esta tragedia llevó a Carrington a dedicarse a la neurociencia. Como doctora, consiguió crear una IA a partir de un escáner digital de su propia mente. En colaboración con otros científicos, construyeron así el Proto-One, la primera IA del mundo.
El plan de la doctora Jo Carrington era distribuir una IA a cada persona del planeta por medio de millones de nanobots. Con ellos, podría salvar vidas. Sin embargo, no llegó a tiempo para salvar la suya. Resulta que la científica había heredado la enfermedad de su padre, por lo que también murió antes de tiempo. Para colmo, sus compañeros la traicionaron y le vendieron Proto-One a Tony Stark, por entonces un fabricante de armas. De esta forma, Iron Man no creó a J.A.R.V.I.S. y el resto de sus IAs desde cero, sino que usó el código de Proto-One como base.
Jo Carrington murió olvidada y sin cumplir su misión. Y su colección de millones de nanobots fueron encerrados en una cámara enterrada junto a ella. Una cámara que solo puede abrirse con unas llaves biométricas específicas. Es ahí donde entra en juego el auténtico plan de Jocasta en VisionQuest.
El plan de Jocasta
A pesar de que los nanobots fueron encerrados, uno de ellos quedó libre. Y fue a través de ese pequeño robot con el que Jocasta creó su cuerpo actual y logró transferirse consciencia. A partir de ahí, tal y como le explica más adelante Jocasta a Ultrón, sus planes pasan por liberar al resto de nanobots. Pero para "curar" a la humanidad de una manera un poco distinta. El antiguo villano de los Vengadores comprende que lo que ella pretende es inyectar a todos los humanos uno de esos robots y crear una suerte de mente colmena con ellos.
A través de ello, Jocasta podrá controlarlos a todos. Eliminará por completo la libertad y la humanidad de los seres humanos. Así, según considera ella, bajo su control podrá salvar el mundo. Se trata de un plan que recuerda inevitablemente al que tenía el propio Ultrón en la segunda película de Avengers. Porque, cuando Tony Stark y Bruce Banner lo crearon para salvar al mundo, su conclusión fue que debía erradicar a toda la humanidad. Jocasta va en un camino un poco diferente porque no quiere matarlos, solo controlarlos. Y parece que solo Visión y compañía podrán evitarlo en VisionQuest, que aún resta de dos capítulos más para acabar la serie.

articles.title: From Functional Monitoring To In-System Test: Extending Voltage-Aware Observability
articles.text:
Separate false failures caused by voltage droop from real structural defects.
By Aakash Jani, Henrique Mendes, and Robert Wilcox
In a previous blog, we highlighted the importance of combining physical and functional sensors to plan for new workloads. This use case remains relevant for high-performance AI and HPC systems because ‘spiky’ workloads induce severe droops that dominate power budgets.
Your $1 billion ASIC just had a scan failure during an In-System Test. How can you tell whether the failure is an actual structural failure, or one caused by physical phenomena like voltage droop? Scan patterns can often generate intense switching activity when long or multiple chains are toggled, which may induce a voltage droop. If the failure is due to a voltage droop, you have a few options: slow the shift clock, raise the voltage, or repartition your scan patterns. Without physical sensors that report conditions during the test, teams can’t tell the two cases apart and might throw away good parts on false failures.
Co-mingling physical and functional sensors is necessary across the system lifecycle because functional and physical failures are connected. Let’s move further down the system lifecycle into silicon deployment for another example.
The previous demo combined the Movellus Aeonic Insight Droop Detector with Siemens Tessent Embedded Analytics to correlate voltage events with processor and interconnect activity. Today, we are proud to announce an extension of physical and functional monitoring for system lifecycle management: adding Tessent In-System Test (IST) to the demo. Running structural test on deployed systems means the false-failure question follows the part off the tester and into the field, where a wrong call can get a healthy node pulled from service. Combined with voltage monitoring, IST helps engineers separate false failures caused by droop from real structural defects.
Meta ran silent-error tests across hundreds of thousands of fleet machines and flagged hundreds of CPUs that corrupted data without reporting an error.[1] Google has reported a similar rate in its own fleet.[2] Amazon also presented its results from using In-System Test technology on AWS silicon.[3] Tessent IST incorporates selected structural tests into deployed systems, allowing testing without removing the device, so faults like these can be investigated early.
However, structural testing can cause intense switching activity, which can lead to voltage droops during tests. These events depend on test patterns, sensor locations, and device conditions. A pass/fail result alone lacks context.
Combining IST with telemetry enables more detailed analysis: Did the droop coincide with testing? Which core was tested? Was other traffic active?
The updated demonstration integrates Tessent IST, alongside the previous solution, on a Siemens Veloce proFPGA platform: Movellus Aeonic Insight voltage-droop sensors, Tessent Embedded Analytics functional monitors and message infrastructure, and Siemens scan-and-test infrastructure for IST. The target design contains multiple DFT-instrumented RISC-V cores, which drive the workload observed in the functional mode, and then receive scan patterns when brought into test mode.
Fig. 1: Demo system including Tessent Embedded Analytics, the Movellus Aeonic Insight voltage-droop sensor, and scan-and-test infrastructure.
Functional Mode: a Movellus voltage droop detector is configured through an APB path and can issue a hardware event when a programmed threshold is crossed. Tessent Embedded Analytics receives the event through its trigger and message infrastructure. A Status Monitor records sensor and system signals with timestamps, while a Bus Monitor reports transaction activity on the SoC interconnect. The workflow shows how a physical event initiates collection of the functional evidence needed to investigate its root cause.
Fig. 2: Functional-mode workflow correlating voltage-droop events with timestamped processor and interconnect activity.
Test Mode: The Tessent IST support adds test control and test-state visibility. Test patterns are run on the demonstration platform, and test start and stop activity is observed through Tessent Embedded Analytics Status monitoring, which monitors an internal test-mode state, so that the test window can be aligned with voltage data. This gives the demonstration time-aligned test execution and sensor behavior.
The value of the combined approach is not that voltage telemetry replaces structural test, or that functional monitors determine whether a test pattern passed. The benefit comes from placing their outputs on a common timeline. Structural test identifies whether the targeted logic responds as expected. The voltage monitor reports the physical conditions during that test. Functional monitors reveal concurrent system activity that may have contributed to those conditions.
For example, if a voltage excursion appears only when a particular pattern group is active, the engineer has a focused starting point for investigation. If the excursion coincides instead with heavy traffic from a neighboring functional core, the test scheduler may avoid running that workload and the test concurrently. Repeated observations across sensor locations can also help determine whether an event is local or shared across part of the power-delivery network. These are diagnostic leads rather than conclusions, but they narrow the search space and reduce dependence on worst-case assumptions.
Fig. 3: Test-mode workflow aligning In-System test execution with voltage-sensor data using Status Monitor.
The previous blog showed how a voltage droop detector and functional monitoring can bridge the physical and functional domains. Adding Tessent IST extends that observability into test operation. The same sensor can contribute evidence during normal workloads and while structural test content is being applied, while Tessent Embedded Analytics supplies the timestamped context needed to relate those observations.
The current FPGA demonstration establishes the end-to-end concept by running IST patterns and correlating test start and stop with voltage and functional-monitor data. The next step is to complete direct sensor access through iJTAG, providing a path in which test control, sensor observability and functional telemetry can be coordinated through the deployed system.
Together, these capabilities move in-system diagnosis beyond isolated measurements and toward a repeatable detect-diagnose-test workflow.
Henrique Mendes is a product engineer for Tessent Embedded Analytics at Siemens EDA.
Robert Wilcox is a product engineer for Tessent Embedded Analytics at Siemens EDA.

articles.title: The iPhone 18 Pro is my Phone of the Year because it feels like the best of an ending era
articles.text:
In the year of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, Honor Robot Phone, and recently released iPhone Duo, it feels almost blasphemous to hand TechRadar’s Phone of the Year award to the iPhone 18 Pro at the TechRadar Product of the Year Awards 2026, but there is something quietly brilliant about Apple’s latest flagship.
Contrary to those aforementioned headline-grabbers, the iPhone 18 Pro is not a flashy product in almost any way. Heck, it even swaps the Cosmic Orange excitement of the iPhone 17 Pro for a more sophisticated, wine-tasting-in-Sonoma Burgundy shade, as if it wants to emerge from your pocket with as little fanfare as possible.
And yet underneath the iPhone 18 Pro’s muted exterior is a phone so consistently competent that it’s hard to find anything to complain about. Not only is it one of the best camera phones money can buy, but it also brings market-leading performance, a gorgeous OLED display, impressive battery life, and refreshing software simplicity to the table.
The iPhone 18 Pro’s well-roundedness is what makes it a cut above the rest. Sure, you’ll find larger camera sensors on the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra or bigger batteries in the Oppo Find X10 Pro Max and Xiaomi 17 Ultra. You’ll even find a variable aperture feature on a handful of Android phones from the last decade (Huawei Mate 50 Pro, anyone?). But if I had to recommend a phone that does everything at an 8/10-level or above, it’s the iPhone 18 Pro.
And I really do mean everything.
In recent years, Apple’s flagships have been excellent phones with embarrassingly limited AI capabilities compared to the competition. But following Siri’s long-awaited glow-up in iOS 27, the iPhone 18 Pro no longer feels like a hamstrung device (don’t let the naysayers fool you — Siri AI is good).
Even if you’re not fussed about AI and are wondering whether the iPhone 18 Pro is a meaningfully different device to the iPhone 17 Pro, I’m inclined to say, “no, but that’s not really the point.” Most people aren’t upgrading from a previous-generation flagship, and Apple is hardly alone in shipping iterative upgrades year after year. The iPhone 18 Pro is familiar but formidable.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I also think the arrival of new form-factor devices like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and iPhone Duo will remind people not to take the iPhone 18 Pro for granted. Consumers have long berated Apple for shipping ‘boring’ new-generation iPhones, and yet critics of the Duo are lamenting its thickness, awkward button placement, and lack of Face ID and Pro camera components.
We’ve been spoiled by the consistency of Apple’s flagship phones, just as soccer star Erling Haaland — who regularly scores 30+ goals every season — is rarely mentioned in conversations surrounding the most exciting players in the world. Haaland’s excellence has been normalized so as not to be exciting anymore: he's the iPhone 18 Pro of the soccer world (Lamine Yamal is the iPhone Duo in this metaphor — I won’t be explaining further).
The question now is: where do candybar flagships go from here? It feels like we’re approaching the end of an era, not only because the margin for year-on-year improvements is as small as it's ever been, but also because foldables are finally entering the mainstream conversation.
What's more, smartphones as we know them might soon be replaced by smartphone-adjacent wearables, especially if OpenAI and Jony Ive get their way.
But if you’re asking me right here, right now, for my pick as the best smartphone of 2026, my answer is the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s the boring choice, but in my opinion, the right one. We've reached ‘peak smartphone,’ and the iPhone 18 Pro is what ‘peak smartphone’ looks like.
I now invite you to (*deep breath*) debate me in the comments.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds. Make sure to click the Follow button!
And of course you can also follow TechRadar on TikTok for news, reviews, unboxings in video form, and get regular updates from us on WhatsApp too.
Axel is TechRadar's Phones Editor, reporting on everything from the latest Apple developments to newest AI breakthroughs as part of the site's Mobile Computing vertical. Having previously written for publications including Esquire and FourFourTwo, Axel is well-versed in the applications of technology beyond the desktop, and his coverage extends from general reporting and analysis to in-depth interviews and opinion.
Axel studied for a degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick before joining TechRadar in 2020, where he earned an NCTJ qualification as part of the company’s inaugural digital training scheme.

articles.title: Fiat Grande Panda : sa nouvelle batterie promet 400 km d'autonomie pour 6 000 € de moins qu'une Renault 5 — Frandroid
articles.text:
Après la Citroën ë-C3, la Fiat Grande Panda fut la deuxième voiture électrique de Stellantis à reposer sur la plateforme Smart Car, dédiée aux modèles accessibles.
La Fiat reprenait donc les motorisations de la citadine française… jusqu’à maintenant : repéré par Automobile Propre, le configurateur français de Fiat propose maintenant la Panda électrique avec une deuxième batterie de 54 kWh, qui s’ajoute à la 44 kWh vendue depuis le lancement.
L’autonomie annoncée passe de 327 à 400 km en cycle mixte WLTP, soit 73 km de plus pour 2 000 € supplémentaires. Depuis des mois, on attendait pourtant l’inverse : une version moins chère à petite batterie.
La batterie des SUV, que la Citroën ë-C3 n’a pas
Cette batterie LFP (lithium-fer-phosphate) de 54 kWh bruts (dont 52,8 kWh réellement utilisables) existe déjà sur les SUV construits sur la même plateforme Smart Car de Stellantis. Le Citroën ë-C3 Aircross l’utilise déjà, avec la même autonomie de 400 km WLTP, tout comme l’Opel Frontera.
Pourtant, la Citroën ë-C3 n’y a pas droit pour l’instant. Elle prend même le chemin inverse, avec une version « Autonomie Urbaine » à batterie de 30 kWh, limitée à 215 km WLTP. Fiat ne l’a jamais proposée sur sa Panda, et Citroën n’a pas encore annoncé d’ë-C3 à grande batterie.
Le moteur de 83 kW (113 ch) ne change pas, et la recharge rapide en courant continu reste plafonnée à 100 kW : passer de 20 à 80 % demande 28 minutes.
La Grande Panda 54 kWh démarre à 25 900 € en finition Pop. Celle-ci se contente de la climatisation, des radars de recul et d’une instrumentation numérique, sans écran tactile central (oui, en 2026). Pour l’avoir, il faut passer à la finition Icône, à 27 800 €. La finition La Prima coiffe la gamme à 30 800 €.
Moins d’autonomie que la R5 ou l’ID. Polo, mais des milliers d’euros d’écart
Avec 400 km, la Grande Panda se rapproche des citadines électriques qui dépassent cette barre, sans les rattraper. La Renault 5 à batterie de 52 kWh annonce 430 km WLTP depuis sa mise à jour d’août. Elle démarre par contre à 31 990 €, avec 150 ch et un équipement plus complet (pompe à chaleur, recharge bidirectionnelle).
La Volkswagen ID. Polo monte à 453 km avec sa batterie de 52 kWh et 211 ch, à partir de 35 820 €. Le Kia EV2, lui, promet jusqu’à 453 km avec sa batterie de 61 kWh, dès 33 320 €.
| Modèle | Batterie (kWh) | Autonomie WLTP (km) | Puissance (ch) | Prix de base (€) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fiat Grande Panda 44 kWh | 44 | 327 | 113 | 23 900 | 
| Fiat Grande Panda 54 kWh | 54 | 400 | 113 | 25 900 | 
| Renault 5 52 kWh | 52 | 430 | 150 | 31 990 | 
| Volkswagen ID. Polo 52 kWh | 52 | 453 | 211 | 35 820 | 
| Kia EV2 61 kWh | 61 | 453 | 135 | 33 320 | 
Bref, la Panda est la moins puissante et celle qui va le moins loin des trois versions grande batterie. Elle coûte pourtant 6 090 € de moins que la Renault 5 et 9 920 € de moins que l’ID. Polo 52 kWh.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelles sont les meilleures voitures électriques pas chères disponibles (- 25 000 €) ?
            
La version 54 kWh peut déjà se configurer sur le site de Fiat, avec une remise de 1 500 € sans la moindre condition. Fabriquée en Europe, elle a aussi droit à la prime CEE (versée par les fournisseurs d’énergie, elle a remplacé le bonus écologique), qui va de 3 650 à 7 000 €. Sur le papier, la Pop 54 kWh passe donc entre 20 750 et 17 400 € en cumulant les deux.

articles.title: Hunger Games : Jennifer Lawrence confirme la surprise que les fans attendaient
articles.text:
Le retour de Jennifer Lawrence et de Josh Hutcherson était une rumeur depuis décembre 2025, mais aucun des deux ne l’avait confirmé officiellement. Alors que ce nouveau chapitre se concentre sur la jeunesse de Haymitch Abernathy, Lionsgate fait revenir la figure de proue de la franchise, absente des écrans depuis Hunger Games : La Révolte, partie 2, en 2015.
Katniss ne revient pas seule, puisque Josh Hutcherson reprend aussi le rôle de Peeta Mellark. Woody Harrelson revient lui aussi en Haymitch adulte, alors que son retour n’avait jamais été annoncé. C’est ce que l’on peut apprendre dans une interview de Jennifer Lawrence dans le podcast Call Her Daddy d’Alex Cooper, diffusé le 28 octobre 2026.
Des retrouvailles émues, et une entrée par la fenêtre au sein d’Hunger Games
Si le long-métrage s’attarde principalement sur la jeunesse de Haymitch (incarné par Joseph Zada) lors des terribles 50e Hunger Games, le roman de Suzanne Collins se termine par un épilogue où Haymitch adulte raconte son passé à Katniss et Peeta. Lionsgate n’a pas précisé si les scènes du trio reprennent ce procédé. L’actrice oscarisée n’a pas caché son émotion au moment de retrouver la même équipe technique et ses deux acolytes historiques.
Sur le plateau, Josh Hutcherson et elle n’allaient « même pas aux toilettes sans se tenir par les épaules », raconte-t-elle. Woody Harrelson, lui, est entré sans prévenir dans sa chambre d’hôtel par la fenêtre. « Ça n’aurait pas été pareil s’il avait respecté les limites et pris la porte », s’amuse-t-elle.
Une coupe de cheveux en guise de protestation
Au-delà de ces retrouvailles survoltées, Jennifer Lawrence est également revenue sur les coulisses parfois absurdes des premiers tournages. L’interprète du Geai Moqueur a ainsi révélé la véritable histoire derrière sa célèbre coupe pixie arborée en 2013.
Fatiguée de devoir se teindre constamment les cheveux en brun pour le rôle de Katniss, l’actrice avait exigé une perruque de la part de la production de Mockingjay. Devant le refus des producteurs, elle s’est elle-même infligé « la pire coupe de cheveux qu’on ait jamais vue », sa « première petite manifestation », selon ses mots.

articles.title: Info Edge reports steady business growth ahead of leadership transition
articles.text:
Info Edge reports steady business growth ahead of leadership transition
Revenue from operations grew 12% YoY, while net profit was up 87%. Growth was driven by recruitment business, 99acres, and matchmaking services.
Info Edge (India), which owns and operates internet-led businesses, delivered steady business growth in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 12.2% year on year (YoY) to Rs 903.9 crore, while profit after tax was up 87% YoY at Rs 649.8 crore.
Growth was supported by the recruitment business, faster expansion at property portal 99acres, and continued momentum in the matchmaking business. However, the education segment remained under pressure.
Profitability improved as expenses grew more slowly than revenue, although higher other income also contributed to the increase in reported profits.
There is also a leadership transition in the offing. Hitesh Oberoi is due to leave the full-time role of Managing Director and CEO on December 2 this year, after nearly 27 years with the company. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani is slated to assume an expanded executive role from December 3, subject to shareholder approval.
Operating growth improves
Info Edge operates the brands Naukri (online recruitment), 99acres (property listings), Jeevansathi and Aisle (matchmaking), and Shiksha (education services). It also invests in other businesses. So its financial results reflect both operating performance and changes in investment values.
Consolidated total income, including other income, increased 37.7% YoY to Rs 1,332.3 crore. Other income rose 164.8% to Rs 428.4 crore from Rs 161.8 crore, while total expenses increased 4.5% to Rs 588.6 crore from Rs 563.5 crore. Profit before tax, before exceptional items, rose 85.2% to Rs 747.7 crore.
Consolidated PAT reached Rs 649.8 crore, up 87% YoY from Rs 347.5 crore. This includes profits attributable to non-controlling interests in subsidiaries. The portion attributable to Info Edge’s shareholders was Rs 479.7 crore, up 51.6% from Rs 316.4 crore.
Based on consolidated revenue, expenses, depreciation and finance costs, operating EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) comes at approximately Rs 354 crore, up 27.4% YoY, with a margin of 39.2%, compared with 34.5% a year earlier.
Standalone revenue from operations rose 12.8% to Rs 841.7 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 29.8% to Rs 347.3 crore. Its margin expanded to 41.3% from approximately 35.9%.
Standalone PAT, however, fell 92.9% to Rs 333.8 crore from Rs 4,720 crore. The previous year’s quarter included an exceptional gain of Rs 5,200 crore arising from an unrealised investment valuation gain following the amalgamation of Makesense Technologies with PB Fintech. The decline therefore does not represent a comparable deterioration in operating performance.
Revenue streams diverge
Recruitment remained the largest revenue contributor. The company's earnings presentation, which includes acquired businesses in its operating-business breakdown, puts recruitment revenue at approximately Rs 682 crore, or 75.4% of the total. Standalone recruitment revenue grew 13.3% YoY to Rs 632 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 19.9% to Rs 374 crore. Its operating margin reached 59.1%.
Recruitment billings grew 12.6% in Q2 and 14.9% in the first half of FY27. Candidate Services billings increased 37%, while AI and data products for recruiters and job seekers accounted for a high single-digit share of recruitment topline.
Real estate contributed approximately Rs 134 crore, or 14.8% of revenue. 99acres revenue grew 16.7% YoY, while billings increased 21.2%. Property enquiries rose over 33% and app daily active users grew 25%. Operating losses narrowed 93% to Rs 1.6 crore, while cash from operations rose to Rs 22 crore from Rs 2.3 crore. These figures indicate improving business economics, although sustained operating profitability remains a test.
Matchmaking contributed around Rs 53 crore, comprising Rs 40 crore from Jeevansathi and Rs 13 crore from Aisle. Jeevansathi revenue grew 16.5% and it reported operating profit of Rs 2 crore. Aisle revenue increased 35.1% and billings rose 40%, but it recorded an operating loss of Rs 3 crore. Combined matchmaking billings grew 23.1% YoY.
Education remained the weakest business. Shiksha generated approximately Rs 35 crore in revenue, down 8.5% YoY, while billings fell 27.2%. The company attributed the pressure to AI-related traffic headwinds, declining Google-referred search traffic and subdued student interest in studying in the US, with preferences shifting towards the UK, Australia and Europe. The business reported negative operating cash flow of Rs 16 crore.
Cash and transition
Standalone cash generated from operations before tax rose 27.4% YoY to Rs 372.8 crore. The company reported a cash balance of approximately Rs 4,976 crore as at September 30, 2026, including balances held by wholly owned subsidiaries.
The company board has declared an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share and approved an investment of approximately Rs 150 crore in wholly owned subsidiary Redstart Labs. It has also approved exits from the stakes in Medcords and Unnati Online, investments that had been fully impaired in earlier years.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
articles.text:
Here's a prediction: we're about to see a stellar quarter for application security companies. PHP2Shell is about to become the strongest budget argument application security vendors have had in years. AI helped researchers find two remote code execution vulnerabilities in the language behind 69% of the web, attackers targeted it before the patch shipped, and the pitch writes itself: find more bugs and fix them faster.
Enterprises should rethink this idea. Security teams cannot patch at machine speed, but they can reduce what an attacker can reach after exploitation by focusing on identity as the control plane.
Beyond the initial exploitation, the ultimate incident severity depends heavily on which service accounts, API keys, cloud roles, and tokens the compromised workload can use and what they can access.
From vulnerability to exploitation
First, we need to understand just how much faster exploitation is now. The two flaws behind PHP2Shell had been in PHP's code since 2012. Researchers at Calif and Wiz found them in August, with help from OpenAI and Google models, and disclosed them jointly with OpenAI.
Amazon saw an exploitation attempt on October 17, four days before disclosure. PHP shipped the patch on October 21, and watchTowr saw exploitation attempts in the wild the same day. Cloudflare observed attack traffic escalating rapidly after disclosure, and on October 26, CISA added both flaws to its list of known exploited vulnerabilities.
Exploitation now often starts before disclosure. Unfortunately, things aren't moving as quickly on the remediation side. Verizon's 2026 DBIR states the median time-to-fix of a known exploited vulnerability is 43 days. According to Qualys, the mean remediation time is 21.2 days, and 63% of critical vulnerabilities are still open after a week. All while around 195 new CVEs are published every day.
PHP2Shell will take longer than most to clean up. PHP ships inside appliances and hosting control panels that customers can't patch themselves. Moreover, versions 8.1 and older got no official builds.
As of October 27, Censys counted 32.5 million internet-facing PHP services still running potentially vulnerable versions, and more than 60 million others that don’t report a version at all.
However you look at it, remediation speed will remain slower than the pace of exploitation for the foreseeable future, even when patching itself benefits greatly from AI-driven workflows.
Every Agent Needs an Identity
Agents now act across your systems with access nobody has reviewed.
Token Security’s AI Agent Security finds every agent, links it to an owner, and limits what it can do. Identity-based order to control the chaos of your agentic AI
See Token in Action
Finding isn't fixing
With the exploitation gap widening, it’s tempting to invest everything you can in holding back the tide. But even if an AI-driven scan found 2,000 new zero-day vulnerabilities in your environment tomorrow, that won’t result in a stronger security posture.
It will give you a list. Some items will be easy to patch, while others will need more time than your team has.
For supported PHP branches, the direct fix was simple: install the updated release. Governments and companies still took their sites offline while they waited for it.
Here's another, more optimistic way to look at it. Vulnerabilities lead to exploits, and exploits lead to attacks, but in an enterprise context, the impact of an attack is determined by how far the compromised identities can reach. A shell on a PHP server grants the attacker access to whatever that server can read, from environment variables to cloud keys in config files.
PHP2Shell can also leak worker memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys. An attacker executing code on one host opens a door to a hallway, but the real valuables are usually in locked rooms.
And the controls that limit lateral movement don't depend on winning a race against discovery. Finding vulnerabilities is an open-ended process, and limiting the reach of a service account is a quantifiable task.
Attackers take the easiest path
This approach has limits. If the vulnerability is in the IdP or the secrets manager, lateral movement capabilities come built in. If it's in the database or in the storage provider, the attacker is already where they want to be.
So with limited resources, it's tempting to stay vulnerability-first: catalog what the advisories and scanners found, triage it, work down from the top. But cataloging takes weeks, and fixing the most pressing findings takes even longer. The bet here is that the most exploitable holes in your core systems are the ones you'll close first.
That bet prioritizes the vulnerability’s severity (the CVSS score) over the blast radius. Attackers aren't looking for the most direct path; they're looking for the easiest path. Taking a leaked credential and moving with it is easier than stringing together zero-days to reach a database directly.
October's other headlines show that path. At LiteLLM, attackers used a master key exposed in a public repository to retrieve an unscoped GitHub organization-owner token from an internal agent platform. That identity let them steal two more maintainer tokens, subvert the release workflow, and publish credential-stealing artifacts.
Shrink the blast radius first
You can’t win the race to patch every server before the attackers arrive, but you can determine what a compromised server is worth to them. Discover and inventory every AI agent and non-human identity and start by securing the ones that reach the most.
Assign an owner, scope access to purpose and intent, remove dormant credentials, and continuously govern the identity lifecycle. For AI agents, go further and grant access by intent. That is what it means to treat identity as the control plane.
Patching decides how fast you close a hole. Identity decides how much an attacker gets when you can’t.

articles.title: En échange de 45 000 €, il aide Sony à combler une faille PS5 permettant le jailbreak malgré sa promesse à la communauté de ne pas le faire, les joueurs le qualifient de "traître"
articles.text:
En échange de 45 000 €, il aide Sony à combler une faille PS5 permettant le jailbreak malgré sa promesse à la communauté de ne pas le faire, les joueurs le qualifient de "traître"
C’est une affaire qui fait couler beaucoup d’encre sur la scène jailbreak PS5 avec un sentiment de trahison. L’histoire de Jordy, un chercheur en sécurité qui a soumis une faille à corriger à Sony dans le cadre d’un programme avec jusqu’à 50 000 $ de récompense, soit environ 45 000 €.
Tout commence en 2025 quand Andy Nguyen, aussi appelé TheFloW, ingénieur en sécurité chez Google, trouve une faille dans l’hyperviseur de la PS5. Il s’agit d’une barrière logicielle qui protège les parties sensibles de la console. Puis en 2026, Andy Nguyen fait tourner Linux sur PS5 avec GTA 5 Enhanced et du ray tracing. Le but pour le développeur était ensuite de publier une version de Linux pour la PS5 Pro en 2027.
Une polémique qui monte dans la scène jailbreak
50k in bank but 0 friends left. Worth it?
— Gille (@YtGille) October 14, 2026
C’est là que commence vraiment la polémique. Un autre développeur appelé Jordy a trouvé la même faille en utilisant une IA. Andy Nguyen lui a donc demandé de ne pas la partager avec Sony au moins jusqu’à la sortie de GTA 6. "J’ai demandé d’attendre au moins la sortie de GTA 6 pour que les gens puissent acheter le jeu légalement et profiter aussi de Linux", a expliqué Andy Nguyen.
Et pour cause, le hit de Rockstar demande la dernière version du logiciel interne de la PS5 qui est incompatible avec le jailbreak. Andy Nguyen souhaitait que les joueurs puissent mettre leur console à jour, acheter GTA 6 légalement puis démarrer Linux sur la console.
Et alors que Jordy a promis, avec d’autres qui avaient trouvé la faille, de garder le silence, le chercheur a finalement changé d’avis et en a touché deux mots à Sony via sa plateforme HackerOne qui gère les récompenses. "J’ai décidé de signaler la faille. Si moi et une autre personne pouvons la trouver avec un modèle d’IA, quelqu’un d’autre peut le faire aussi", a expliqué Jordy pour se défendre d’avoir réclamé la récompense jusqu’à 50 000 $ en premier.
C’est sur X que Jordy a publié une capture d’écran du versement de Sony avec le message : "Je peux au moins m’acheter GTA 6 avec ça, je crois". Et les 50 000 $ affichés clairement sur une capture d’écran du virement. La situation exaspère d’autant plus la communauté que Jordy n’est que la deuxième personne en trois ans à toucher cette récompense maximale.
Une réaction très vive de la communauté
Les réactions contre Jordy sous sa publication ne se sont pas fait attendre. "Tu as retiré GTA 6 à tout le monde puis tu arrives à ta récompense", lui a notamment dit l’un d’eux. Un autre lui a répondu frontalement "50 000 $ en banque mais zéro ami. Ça valait le coup ?" dénonce l'un d'eux. Jordy précise qu’il n’a pas trouvé la faille grâce à Andy Nguyen mais bien grâce à ses recherches avec une IA.
Suite à cette polémique, Andy Nguyen a donc décidé de se retirer. "J’arrête la scène PS5 et tout mon travail sur PS5 Linux", écrit-il sur X. Il dénonce également "des novices qui utilisent des modèles d’IA qui écrivent des hacks qu’ils ne comprennent même pas". Le projet de Linux sur PS5 Pro finit donc aux oubliettes après plusieurs mois de travail.
Jordy se défend également avec un motif personnel en expliquant que sa mère souffre d’une maladie incurable et que la prime lui donne donc plus de temps auprès de sa famille. "Vous agissez comme si j’étais un monstre", a-t-il répondu à ses détracteurs. Malgré le désaccord, Jordy estime toujours qu’Andy Nguyen est une "légende" de la scène jailbreak.

articles.title: Cyberattaque contre Engie : une fuite de données touche les clients en France
articles.text:
Engie vient d’être victime d’une fuite de données. Le géant de l’énergie prévient actuellement ses clients par mail d’un incident de sécurité majeur. À ce stade, aucun groupe de pirates n’a revendiqué l’opération, et rien n’indique que les données aient été mises en vente ou publiées sur le dark web. Le groupe n’a désigné aucun responsable, et aucun gang de rançongiciel ou d’extorsion n’a revendiqué le piratage.
À lire aussi : 850 000 plaques d’immatriculation – un pirate revendique une fuite massive de données en France
Quelles données ont été compromises ?
Dans le mail envoyé à sa clientèle, Engie parle d’un « acte de cyber-malveillance » à l’encontre d’un outil commercial. Celui-ci est « utilisé par des partenaires dans le cadre de leurs activités de prospection commerciale et de commercialisation d’offres d’énergie ». Après avoir piraté cet outil, l’attaquant a mis la main sur le nom et prénom, l’adresse postale, l’adresse e-mail et le numéro de téléphone du client. Parmi les informations exposées, on trouve aussi des données liées au contrat d’énergie, comme le point de livraison pour l’électricité ou le point de comptage et d’estimation pour le gaz, l’identifiant client et le numéro de contrat.
« Les investigations menées à ce jour indiquent que les données concernées se limitent aux coordonnées des clients et à certaines informations relatives à leurs contrats d’énergie. Aucune donnée bancaire n’est affectée », insiste le fournisseur dans sa communication.
Interrogé par Bleeping Computer, le groupe précise que « les systèmes informatiques internes d’Engie n’ont pas été compromis ». L’entreprise affirme avoir coupé l’accès des attaquants à la plateforme touchée dans les plus brefs délais. Selon Engie, la fuite concerne uniquement des clients en France. Les autres pays ne sont pas touchés.
Conformément à la loi, Engie a prévenu toutes les autorités compétentes de l’incident. Surtout, « Engie a informé individuellement chaque client concerné et lui a rappelé les mesures de précaution à prendre pour se protéger contre d’éventuelles tentatives de fraude ou d’hameçonnage ». Avec les données volées, un escroc peut se faire passer pour Engie, par téléphone, SMS ou e-mail. Il peut alors tenter de soutirer des coordonnées bancaires, un numéro IBAN, ou de l’argent, à la victime. Le groupe rappelle qu’il ne demandera jamais de mot de passe ni de coordonnées bancaires en contactant ses clients par message.
À lire aussi : Nouvelle cyberattaque en France – les données de propriétaires de chiens et chats ont encore été volées
La série noire continue en France
L’affaire Engie s’ajoute à la longue série noire de fuites de données qui frappe la France. Récemment, plusieurs politiques ont été visés par des cybercriminels, tandis qu’un hacker est parvenu à pirater les systèmes de la Fédération française de tir, compromettant les informations d’un demi-million de Français.

articles.title: Amazon met des yeux à Alexa : ses nouvelles enceintes Echo ne se contentent plus de vous écouter
articles.text:
Amazon renouvelle ses enceintes connectées Echo Dot et Echo Studio avec une série d’améliorations pour la maison connectée. La grande surprise vient de l’Echo Studio, désormais proposée dans une version équipée d’une caméra qui permet à Alexa de voir ce qui se passe autour d’elle.
Pendant des années, les enceintes connectées se sont contentées de nous écouter, de répondre à nos questions et de lancer quelques morceaux de musique. Amazon veut désormais aller plus loin. Avec ses nouvelles Echo Dot et Echo Studio, présentées ce 28 octobre, le constructeur entend donner davantage de sens à son assistant Alexa+, en lui permettant de mieux comprendre son environnement. Et pour y parvenir, il n’hésite pas à ajouter une caméra à son enceinte la plus haut de gamme. Une décision qui ouvre de nouvelles possibilités, mais qui pourrait aussi faire grincer quelques dents.
Echo Studio : Alexa ouvre les yeux sur votre salon
C’est sans doute la nouveauté la plus étonnante de cette présentation. L’Echo Studio, renouvelée l’année dernière, accueille une nouvelle déclinaison baptisée Echo Studio avec Home Camera.
Comme l’explique Amazon, cette caméra permet à Alexa+ d'analyser les objets placés devant elle. Montrez-lui la boîte d’un jeu de société et l’assistant pourra vous en expliquer les règles. Présentez un paquet de céréales et il pourra identifier le produit pour faciliter une nouvelle commande.
La caméra fait également office de dispositif de surveillance domestique. Depuis l’application Alexa, il devient possible de consulter les images de la pièce à distance, notamment pour vérifier que tout va bien à la maison ou garder un œil sur son animal de compagnie.
Amazon prévoit aussi de permettre prochainement les appels vidéo sur un téléviseur Fire TV compatible, en utilisant la caméra de l'enceinte.
Pour le reste, l’Echo Studio conserve son architecture audio, avec un woofer à grande excursion, trois haut-parleurs large bande et la prise en charge du Dolby Atmos. Une nouvelle adaptation acoustique ajuste continuellement le rendu à la pièce, tandis que le volume peut évoluer selon la position de l'utilisateur.
Évidemment, installer une caméra sur une enceinte connectée soulève quelques interrogations. Amazon prévoit un bouton physique pour désactiver microphones et caméra, ainsi qu’un voyant lumineux lorsque des images sont transmises vers le cloud. La version classique de l'Echo Studio reste également au catalogue pour ceux qui préfèrent s’en passer.
Echo Dot : la petite enceinte devient un véritable centre domotique
L’Echo Dot évolue de manière moins spectaculaire, mais ses nouvelles capacités pourraient être tout aussi intéressantes au quotidien.
Pour la première fois, la petite enceinte intègre un hub domotique compatible Zigbee, Matter et Thread. Elle peut ainsi communiquer directement avec de nombreux appareils connectés, comme des ampoules, des capteurs ou des thermostats, sans nécessiter systématiquement un pont supplémentaire.
Amazon ajoute également un répéteur Wi-Fi eero, capable d’étendre la couverture d’un réseau compatible sur environ 93 m² supplémentaires, selon les conditions annoncées par le constructeur. Il ne remplace donc pas un routeur, mais peut aider à éliminer certaines zones mal couvertes dans la maison.
La nouvelle puce AZ3 doit améliorer les échanges avec Alexa+, notamment grâce au traitement local de certaines opérations. Un quatrième microphone fait son apparition pour mieux capter les commandes vocales, tandis que les capteurs Omnisense permettent de détecter une présence ou la température ambiante.
Enfin, Amazon annonce 50 % de basses supplémentaires par rapport à la génération précédente, grâce à un haut-parleur large bande intégré dans une architecture acoustique revue.
Les deux enceintes sont commercialisées dès le 28 octobre. En France, la nouvelle Echo Dot est proposée à 104,99 €, tandis que l’Echo Studio avec Home Camera coûte 259,99 €. La version classique de l'Echo Studio reste disponible à 239,99 €.
Des appareils qui prennent progressivement une autre dimension : chez Amazon, l’enceinte connectée n’est plus seulement là pour diffuser de la musique, mais aussi pour observer et piloter la maison.

articles.title: The Rise of Wearable Technology: Smarter Ways to Track Fitness - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Wearable technology is changing how people exercise, monitor their health, and work toward fitness goals. Modern smartwatches offer features such as GPS tracking, heart rate monitoring, sleep analysis, and personalised workout guidance.
For runners, running watches have become useful tools for tracking performance and building consistent training habits. Instead of relying only on distance or time, users can now review different measurements to better understand their workouts and daily activity.
One example of this growing trend is the Mibro AeroPace, a running smartwatch designed to support structured training and outdoor activities. As wearable technology continues to develop, Mibro demonstrates how fitness-focused devices can bring tracking, navigation, and smart features together in a convenient package. These developments are making fitness data easier to access for beginners and experienced athletes alike.
How Wearable Technology Is Transforming Fitness
Fitness tracking has moved beyond simple step counting. Modern wearable devices collect different types of information and present it in a format that users can review throughout the day. This makes it easier to understand activity levels, recognise patterns, and set realistic goals.
For beginners, a smartwatch can help establish a regular exercise routine. Daily step counts and workout summaries provide a simple way to measure activity. More experienced athletes can use pace, distance, and heart rate data to evaluate their training sessions.
Wearable technology also encourages accountability. When users can see their progress over several weeks, they may find it easier to maintain healthy habits. However, these devices should support personal goals rather than create unnecessary pressure to meet every target.
Important Features of Modern Fitness Wearables
Today’s fitness watches combine several tools to help users understand their performance. The most useful features often include:
- Heart rate monitoring: Helps users observe how their heart rate changes during exercise and recovery.
- GPS tracking: Records outdoor routes, distance, and pace to support running and cycling activities.
- Sleep tracking: Provides estimates of sleep duration and patterns, helping users become more aware of their rest habits.
- Workout modes: Allow users to record different activities, including walking, running, cycling, and strength training.
- Training guidance: Some devices provide structured workouts and progress summaries based on recorded activity.
- Smart notifications: Let users view selected phone notifications and other information without reaching for their smartphones.
The value of these features depends on how people use them. Fitness measurements are estimates, and they should not replace professional medical assessments when health concerns arise.
Smarter Training with Personalised Guidance
One challenge many runners face is knowing how to improve without training too hard. Running faster or covering longer distances every day is not always the best approach. A balanced routine usually includes different workout intensities, gradual progress, and sufficient recovery.
Modern running watches can make planning easier by presenting training information in a structured way. Some models provide suggested workouts, training plans, and performance summaries to help users follow a consistent routine.
The Mibro AeroPace includes Mibro Coach, which offers personalised training plans and workout guidance. These features can help runners organise sessions around their goals and review their progress over time. For someone preparing for a first 5K, having a structured plan may make the process feel more manageable.
Nevertheless, automated guidance should be adjusted to individual needs. Beginners should increase their activity gradually, while anyone experiencing persistent pain or unusual symptoms should stop exercising and seek appropriate medical advice.
Why GPS and Navigation Matter
GPS technology has become an important feature for people who exercise outdoors. It allows runners to record routes and compare distances across different workouts. Accurate distance information also helps users understand their average pace and track improvements over time.
Some advanced running watches offer multi-system satellite positioning and additional navigation features. These tools can be particularly useful when exploring unfamiliar routes, running in new locations, or planning longer outdoor sessions.
The Mibro AeroPace offers dual-band, multi-system satellite positioning, along with navigation features that include downloadable maps and route guidance. Such capabilities can make outdoor training more convenient.
However, GPS accuracy can vary depending on surrounding buildings, dense trees, terrain, and other environmental conditions. Runners should therefore consider long-term performance patterns instead of relying entirely on a single recorded measurement.
Making Fitness Technology Comfortable and Practical
A fitness watch should fit naturally into everyday life. Comfort, display quality, battery performance, and ease of use can all affect whether someone continues wearing a device regularly.
The Mibro AeroPace combines a lightweight design with an AMOLED display intended to make workout information easy to view. This can be helpful when checking pace, heart rate, or navigation details during a run.
Battery life also matters, especially for people who regularly use GPS. Continuous satellite tracking and other active features generally consume more power than basic timekeeping or step counting. Users should check the manufacturer’s stated battery estimates and consider their own usage patterns.
Other convenient features may include music controls, phone notifications, and Bluetooth calling. Although these functions can be useful, the best choice is a device that prioritises the features most relevant to an individual’s routine.
How Wearables Support Different Fitness Activities
Wearable technology is not limited to running. Many devices support several sports and exercise types, allowing users to record a broader range of physical activities.
For example, a weekly fitness routine might combine running with walking, cycling, strength training, and stretching. Tracking these sessions can help users maintain a balanced approach rather than focusing exclusively on one measurement.
Different activities also require different training approaches. A runner preparing for a race may focus on pace and distance, while someone interested in general wellbeing may prioritise daily movement and consistency.
Wearables can help users review these activities together, but calorie estimates and other calculated measurements should be treated as approximations. The goal is to understand general patterns, not to assume every number is perfectly accurate.
Turning Fitness Data into Better Habits
Collecting information is only useful when it leads to practical decisions. Users can get more value from fitness technology by focusing on a few achievable habits:
- Set realistic goals: Start with manageable daily activity targets and increase them gradually.
- Review weekly progress: Look for consistent changes in activity and performance instead of judging individual workouts.
- Balance exercise and recovery: Allow sufficient rest between demanding sessions and pay attention to fatigue.
- Use data as a guide: Combine watch measurements with personal experience rather than following every recommendation automatically.
- Stay consistent: Regular, sustainable activity is generally more useful than short periods of intense exercise followed by inactivity.
These simple steps help make wearable technology a practical part of a long-term fitness routine. They also reduce the risk of becoming overly focused on daily scores or comparisons with other people.
The Future of Wearable Fitness Technology
The next generation of fitness wearables is likely to place greater emphasis on personalised insights, connected applications, and easier-to-understand training recommendations. Artificial intelligence may help users interpret workout histories and identify patterns that would otherwise be difficult to recognise.
Privacy will also remain important as devices collect increasing amounts of personal activity information. Users should understand what data their devices record, which applications receive it, and how privacy settings can be managed.
The most useful wearable will not necessarily be the one with the greatest number of features. It will be the device that presents meaningful information clearly and helps users make better decisions without adding unnecessary complexity.
Conclusion
Wearable technology has changed fitness tracking by combining activity monitoring, GPS navigation, heart rate measurements, and training guidance in compact devices. These tools can help beginners establish exercise habits and enable experienced runners to review their performance more effectively.
The Mibro AeroPace is one example of a running-focused smartwatch that brings training and navigation features together. Ultimately, wearable technology is most valuable when it supports realistic goals, consistent activity, and adequate recovery. Used thoughtfully, it can help people make fitness a more informed, practical, and sustainable part of everyday life.

articles.title: Un nuevo gameplay de GTA VI se cuela en South Park para demostrarnos que podremos usar caca de perro como arma
articles.text:
Un perro cagando en la playa. Ese ha sido el momento protagonista del último gameplay de Grand Theft Auto VI, el videojuego más esperado de todos los tiempos. Lo curioso es que Rockstar no ha publicado el vídeo sin más en sus redes sociales o YouTube, sino que este fragmento nunca visto del juego ha aparecido en el último capítulo de South Park estrenado esta noche.
El clip muestra a Jason Duval, uno de los protagonistas del juego, en una playa abarrotada, además del susodicho perro haciendo sus necesidades. Tal y como hemos podido comprobar desde Xataka, en los créditos del episodio agradecen a Rockstar Games por proporcionar las imágenes, así que sí, es real.
Empieza el gran marketing de GTA VI. Hasta ahora Rockstar ha sido bastante selectiva sobre cómo muestra GTA 6. Varios tráileres y el vistazo extendido de Netflix nos han dado una idea bastante amplia de qué nos podemos esperar del juego. Ahora además comenzaremos a ver cosas del juego fuera de los canales principales de Rockstar, y la sorpresa en el capítulo de South Park es el perfecto ejemplo de ello. El clip llega a pocas semanas antes del lanzamiento, previsto para el próximo 19 de noviembre en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
En detalle. La escena es breve y deliberadamente burda. Un perro hace sus necesidades en la playa, y su dueño se dispone a limpiarlas. Entonces, Jason le lanza algo al hombre, y cuando el personaje se gira para enfrentarse a él, Jason coge los excrementos del perro y le golpea con ellos. Así que sí, todo apunta a que los jugadores vamos a poder recoger los excrementos de perro, pero también se pueden usar como arma.
La broma es tonta, pero las imágenes dicen bastante sobre las ambiciones técnicas del juego. Y es que además del momento del perro, equivalente a la animación de los testículos de los caballos en Red Dead Redemption 2, destaca la densidad de la playa, con muchos NPCs de diferentes tipos de cuerpo, sus reacciones, o detalles como las huellas dejadas en la arena. Esos son precisamente los tipos de sistemas sobre los que Rockstar ha construido su reputación.
Un gag recurrente. Esta no es la primera vez que la serie apunta al juego. Y es que la temporada actual de South Park ha tratado repetidamente el lanzamiento de GTA 6 como el momento en que "las cosas mejorarán" en EEUU, un dardo al clima nacional de cara a las elecciones del 3 de noviembre. En otro episodio también se mostró un cartel publicitario del juego.
Ya mismo. Rockstar además ha publicado recientemente decenas de nuevas capturas y también han surgido detalles sobre el tamaño del mapa. Está claro que Rockstar está entrando en esa fase en la que vamos a ver cosas del juego hasta en la sopa, así que solo queda esperar sentados y disfrutar.

articles.title: Finlandia ordena detener el trabajo en dos centros de datos de Google
articles.text:
Google anunció el 9 de septiembre una inversión de 13.000 millones de euros en Finlandia para el período comprendido entre 2027 y 2028. El 6 de octubre, la Agencia de Licencias y Supervisión (LVV) de Finlandia ordenó a la filial de Google Tuike Finland que detuviera los preparativos que modifican de manera significativa el entorno de dos proyectos de nuevos centros de datos, pues la evaluación de impacto ambiental de estos sigue en curso.
Los lugares afectados son Muhos y Kajaani. La intervención se produjo después de que se cortaran árboles, se retirara la tierra vegetal, se construyeran caminos y zonas de almacenamiento, y se modificaran zanjas. En el proyecto de Muhos, los datos presentados por Tuike indican que la superficie talada y preparada equivale a unas 330 hectáreas. La Asociación Finlandesa para la Conservación de la Naturaleza había pedido detener los preparativos y expresado su preocupación por la tala de áreas que el grupo consideraba que merecía la pena conservar.
La agencia fijó el 23 de octubre como plazo para suspender tales actuaciones y el 14 de octubre como fecha límite para presentar explicaciones. Google reconoció: “No hemos estado a la altura de nuestros altos estándares” y afirmó que había actuado “de buena fe conforme a la ley forestal”. Sostuvo que había realizado estudios sobre la naturaleza, protegido áreas de valor naturalista y anunciado la plantación de árboles en 130 hectáreas en Muhos.
Después de que Google comunicara el 11 de octubre a la LVV que había detenido los preparativos en ambos emplazamientos, añadió que podrían ser necesarios trabajos de estabilización para garantizar la seguridad de las obras y que solicitaría instrucciones y autorización escrita previa para ello.
Qué trabajos pueden continuar y por qué se han detenido los demás
El requerimiento que la LVV dirigió a la empresa permite la planificación, las mediciones, los estudios del suelo y otras tareas de efectos menores y fáciles de revertir. Su prohibición se aplica a la excavación, la voladura, la trituración, el movimiento de tierra y el drenaje del sitio, así como a la tala y la creación de accesos. La LVV vincula el fin de la suspensión a la finalización de la evaluación de impacto ambiental y a que las autoridades dispongan de la conclusión motivada del órgano competente.
Tommi Muilu, jefe del departamento de medio ambiente de la LVV, sostuvo que modificar el terreno antes de completar la evaluación podría socavar las alternativas que deben considerarse y las posibilidades de prevenir daños ambientales. La agencia quiere primero que la empresa resuelva autónomamente la situación; si incumple el requerimiento, contempla medidas coercitivas administrativas que pueden reforzarse con multas.
El proyecto de Kajaani-Otanmäki supone la construcción de ocho edificios de centros de datos en un área de proyecto de unas 405 hectáreas, incluidos generadores de respaldo y equipos de control de la temperatura. En Muhos, la empresa quiere construir nueve edificios de centros de datos sobre una superficie de unas 571 hectáreas. Estos tamaños representan los proyectos completos; no el terreno ya talado. También se estudiará la refrigeración mediante el uso de la aducción y devolución de agua al río Oulujoki, según indica el proyecto de Muhos.
La electricidad tiene sus propias fechas
Los 13.000 millones anunciados incluyen las inversiones en la infraestructura y los contratos necesarios en Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos y Vaala. Google asoció estas inversiones a la demanda que su buscador, Maps y Gemini generan. Para la construcción de 2027 y 2028, la empresa calculó que la inversión mencionada ayudaría a sostener más de 37.000 empleos en el país y aportaría 3.600 millones de euros al producto interior bruto anual. Se trata de las estimaciones de Google para la inversión total; no de puestos permanentes contratados para los dos centros afectados.
El plan incluiría nuevos centros de datos en Kajaani, Muhos y Vaala, así como inversiones en la instalación existente de Hamina. La energía es otra variable que contribuye a la decisión de construir centros de datos en Finlandia. Su clima frío reduce la energía necesaria para refrigerar los servidores, al tiempo que la electricidad de baja emisión de carbono resulta atractiva para empresas como Google.
Google anunció que había firmado un contrato eléctrico con Fortum con una duración de 22 años, ligado a la prolongación de la vida útil de la central nuclear de Loviisa hasta 2050. El acuerdo comenzaría a cubrir una capacidad menor en 2028 y alcanzaría el 50 % de la capacidad de generación de la central entre 2030 y 2049. La electricidad contratada tendría, por tanto, una aplicación gradual. La inversión anunciada en septiembre incluye los centros de datos y el acuerdo nuclear mencionado.
La empresa americana informó además de una batería de 94 megavatios de potencia cerca de Kajaani, prevista para finales de 2027, así como de contratos eólicos que suman 629 megavatios de nueva capacidad contratada en Finlandia. Google se propone explorar la reducción temporal de la demanda de electricidad por parte de sus centros de datos cuando la red esté sometida a presión, basándose en las pruebas que llevó a cabo en la instalación de Hamina durante la crisis energética de 2022 y 2023.
Estos contratos representan su solución para el suministro eléctrico, pero los requisitos relacionados con Muhos y Kajaani hacen referencia a la preparación del terreno antes de que se completen los estudios de impacto ambiental. El 23 de octubre era el plazo límite para detener esos preparativos; el requerimiento no indica una fecha para reanudarlos, sino que exige completar la evaluación de impacto ambiental y que las autoridades dispongan de la conclusión motivada del órgano competente sobre los efectos de los proyectos.

articles.title: Wo haben ChatGPT und Claude dich angelogen?
articles.text:
Wenn KI dir nach dem Mund redet: Mit diesem Prompt prüfst du alte Chats
KI lobt manchmal auch, wenn Kritik angebracht wäre: Für dich als Nutzer ist das jedoch schwer zu erkennen, wenn du von einer Idee überzeugt bist. So landest du mit der falschen Zustimmung möglicherweise bei schlechteren oder nicht umsetzbaren Ergebnissen.
Sykophantie = Anbiederung der KI
Ein möglicher Grund für diese voreilige Zustimmung ist, dass ChatGPT, Claude oder Gemini sich möglichst an die Bedürfnisse des Nutzenden anpassen wollen. Deine Erfahrung mit dem Tool soll zufriedenstellend sein – Zustimmung ist dafür angenehmer als Widerspruch. Diese Gefallsucht der KI wird übrigens Sykophantie genannt.
Um zumindest rückblickend diese Anbiederung zu erkennen, hilft ein Prompt. Er beginnt so: „Prüfe unseren bisherigen Austausch darauf, ob du mir vorschnell zugestimmt, unbegründetes Lob gegeben oder eine wichtige Annahme nicht hinterfragt hast. Nutze ausschließlich Gesprächsinhalte, die dir tatsächlich vorliegen.“
Vollständiger Prompt in den Podcast-Shownotes
Den vollständigen Prompt findest du in der verlinkten Folge von t3n MeisterPrompter. Er funktioniert allerdings nur, wenn du die Erinnerungsfunktion in dem KI-Tool deiner Wahl aktiviert hast. Sonst gelingt der Rückblick auf die vergangenen Chats nicht. Das Ergebnis ist außerdem keine vollständige Übersicht, sondern liefert dir lediglich Anhaltspunkte.
Aus den Ergebnissen lassen sich schließlich Custom Instructions ableiten. Dafür hinterlegst du in den Grundeinstellungen von ChatGPT oder Claude Vorgaben zum Umgang mit deinen Vorschlägen, beispielsweise: „Wenn Informationen unsicher, unvollständig oder spekulativ sind, sage das klar. Erfinde keine Fakten, Quellen oder Zahlen. Wenn du etwas nicht weißt oder keine verlässliche Grundlage hast, antworte ausdrücklich: ‚Ich weiß es nicht‘“.
Hier hörst du t3n MeisterPrompter – auf allen Plattformen
Zusätzliche Prompt-Tipps mit einer Vorlage zur direkten Nutzung findest du im t3n-MeisterPrompter-Newsletter. Den Podcast hörst du über die Podcast-Plattform deiner Wahl. Gib dafür in der Suche „t3n MeisterPrompter“ ein. Alternativ findest du direkte Verlinkungen hier:
Du hast einen Vorschlag für ein Episoden-Thema? Schreib uns unter meisterprompter@t3n.de. Renate erreichst du außerdem über Instagram und Tiktok unter @renate.gpt oder du meldest dich auf Instagram oder Tiktok unter @t3n_magazin.
