articles.title: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
articles.text:
In partnership withAVEVA
Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync.
Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities.
Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems.
AI is at the center of this change. Rob McGreevy, chief product officer at AVEVA, likens newer, AI-infused digital twins to organisms that grow and evolve. These “living” versions are adaptive, evergreen models of a plant’s assets and processes. Because they keep pace with live conditions and connect systems that once ran in isolation, they provide a previously missing layer of visibility and orchestration that better reflects the organic rhythms of the facility itself.
Now, agentic AI is also enabling industrial systems to move beyond diagnostics or suggestions and act of their own accord. As the technology progresses toward greater autonomy, it’s starting to develop the reflexes for a kind of industrial homeostasis, in which small, constant adjustments keep a plant or factory healthy and humming.
All that said, human judgment and operator oversight still play an instrumental role by defining what healthy looks like to begin with—and flagging when AI systems are falling out of alignment. Living digital twins provide the means for human engineers to monitor what AI is doing and ensure execution is on track.
The technologies that keep digital twins in sync
Living digital twins link engineering and design information with real-time operational data through a digital thread, or a connected record of an asset that follows it through its lifecycle. A couple of notable technological shifts have helped string this thread together: Sensors (which have gotten more affordable in recent years) now stream telemetry from IoT devices and industrial control equipment, and software platforms bring that information into user-friendly interfaces. Predictive and physics-based models can also provide AI-enriched insights into how a machine or process might behave.
The lenses through which operators view digital twins have evolved in turn. “You can look at the digital twin through the lens of sustainability: What are my emissions?” says McGreevy. “Or, through the lens of maintenance: Is this asset performing in a healthy way? Or, through a performance metric: Is it producing the number of widgets I need?”
Setting boundaries for semi-autonomous systems
The next phase is letting AI act on select insights those lenses illuminate. For their part, manufacturers are eager for this chapter: In a 2026 Manufacturing Leadership Council survey of manufacturers (opens in new tab), 66% said they are using or plan to use agentic AI in their operations, and 40% expect some degree of factory autonomy by 2030. At the same time, they’re wary of the potential risks: In Deloitte’s 2025 smart manufacturing survey (opens in new tab), 65% of executives ranked operational risk, including the potential for business disruption, among their top concerns.
Manufacturers are accelerating toward agentic AI and greater factory autonomy
Source: MIT Technology Review Insights with data from Manufacturing Leadership Council (opens in new tab), 2026
“There is a lot more refinement to be done, a lot more proof points, testing, and validation needed,” McGreevy says about the ongoing process of making AI autonomous. In the near term, McGreevy expects agentic AI to follow the path seen in other industrial technologies like SCADA systems. “The ‘S’ in SCADA means supervisory, and supervisory means there’s a human in the middle,” he says. He sees AI working mostly in that advisory mode for the foreseeable future, with full autonomy limited to narrow, highly repetitive tasks.
As for the role human operators play, the day-to-day is evolving. Workers who once specialized in a single process line or maintenance task can now take on multiple disciplines. They can spend less time and effort approving routine actions one by one, and more on defining acceptable operating limits. Because AI can reinforce patterns in the data it receives, catching missteps early is a core part of the job. Human knowledge and experience in interpreting what AI is seeing and doing is instrumental.
Governance on a company- and industry-wide scale, too, needs to adapt to the times. Organizations must establish clear guardrails for which decisions AI can make on its own and how its actions are monitored and audited. Still, many have yet to set up comprehensive safeguards: In a recent study from AVEVA and IMD (opens in new tab), 43% of organizations said AI has changed decision-making and accountability across ecosystem partners only slightly or not at all, while just 23% reported a significant or fundamental change. (Only 27% reported sharing data substantially or extensively with partners.)
In the meantime, regulators are starting to define some of the rules. The EU AI Act classifies certain AI safety components used in critical infrastructure as high-risk and imposes requirements for human oversight. Companies are setting up their own structures as well; AVEVA, for one, has a responsible AI governance board and a published set of principles for how AI is developed and deployed.
Agentic AI and living digital twins: Real-world case studies
Inside the semi-autonomous systems already running, that oversight looks different from one deployment to another. In some cases, an operator approves every action; in others, AI acts on its own while people oversee and define the boundaries it can operate within. McGreevy cites several examples of what machine autonomy and human-plus-machine collaboration looks like among AVEVA customers:
- At Saudi Aramco’s Yanbu refinery, optimization algorithms adjust production in a closed loop, with operators overseeing as needed. At its Ras Tanura refinery, the algorithms recommend changes, and operators decide whether to implement them.
- Nestlé uses AI optimization at Nesquik plants to tune the industrial dryers used to produce powdered beverage ingredients. In a landmark test, this tuning reduced energy use by 16%, while improving quality and yield.
- At Thailand’s SCG Chemicals, an AI-supported digital twin spanning engineering, operations, and maintenance monitors asset health and flags potential failures. The company reports 99% plant reliability and a ninefold return on investment within six months.
- The National Laboratory of the Rockies in the U.S. has built a generative AI model for grid control rooms to provide oversight at scale. The model supports operators with renewable energy forecasting and estimates of grid conditions.
Looking to the future
The same synchronization that was once missing from individual plants’ technology systems has also been lacking on a larger scale. “Manufacturing and critical infrastructure have operated as siloed systems for the last 50 years,” says McGreevy. But certain emerging technologies, he suggests, are creating opportunities for more holistic coordination.
On an enterprise level, this might involve the integration of physical AI: systems that pair robotics and sensing technologies with AI-powered decision-making. Drones that fly over pipelines and power lines, for instance, can feed visual inspection data to algorithms that spot gas leaks and other hazards. Not only does this create a more accurate and interconnected flow of information, but it spares humans from needing to physically enter potentially dangerous environments. “The robotics-meets-software convergence will mean fewer incidents, fewer outages, and a more sustainable way of operating,” McGreevy predicts.
A bigger-picture version extends beyond any one plant or process to entire industrial networks, something McGreevy dubs the “integrated value chain.” “Living digital twins make digital manifestations of the entire value chain possible,” he says. “This allows companies to react quickly to supply chain changes, demand changes, tariffs, and material availability.”
Amid today’s realities of turbulent geopolitics and shifting regulatory demands, such resilience will be “an absolute necessity,” adds McGreevy. “Without it, it will be very hard to run an effective business.”

articles.title: Scaling Autonomous Root Cause Analysis For Regression Triage
articles.text:
Solving difficult bugs while intelligently deciding what to investigate, what to rerun, and where to spend compute.
As semiconductor designs grow larger and more complex, debugging is becoming increasingly difficult to scale.
At DVCon earlier this year, Nvidia’s Stuart Oberman described first-silicon success as approaching a “statistical impossibility.” Semiconductor Engineering cites that debugging accounts for 44% of verification effort; a number reported in 2018, before the scale and complexity of today’s designs.
As designs get larger and design spaces are expanding, engineers are working across systems containing millions of gates. If design complexity continues to scale, debugging needs a fundamentally different approach. In this article, we will explain an AI-native approach to root cause analysis (RCA) and regression triage.
There are two important ways that debugging effort scales.
The first is bug difficulty.
Some bugs require deep tracing across design hierarchies, long pipelines, large waveforms, and multiple interacting components before the actual root cause becomes clear.
ChipAgents RCA was designed specifically for this axis. Rather than treating debugging as a simple question-answering problem, the system approaches RCA as a search problem. It explores high-probability traces, executes across different hypotheses, ranks the resulting explanations, and provides confidence scores to the engineer.
Consider one bug encountered in a real customer environment.
The design contained a bidirectional serialization interface between a manager and subordinate. During a transaction, a reset was triggered by the subordinate while the manager continued transmitting a frame beyond the reset grace period.
Part of the transmitted data happened to contain the same value used to represent the protocol’s start code. The subordinate interpreted that payload as the beginning of a new frame, eventually causing a downstream failure.
Several conditions had to coincide: a reset needed to occur during the transaction, the data needed to resemble the start code, and the transmission needed to outlive the reset grace period.
This is the type of bug where autonomous RCA becomes particularly valuable because identifying the root cause requires reasoning through a long chain of events.
But difficulty is only one dimension.
The second is bug quantity.
A regression may contain hundreds of simulations across many test cases and seeds. Multiple simulations can fail simultaneously, and those failures may represent different bugs—or many apparently different failures may actually originate from the same root cause.
The most challenging case lies at the intersection of these two axes: hard bugs at scale.
Now the problem is no longer simply finding one root cause. The system must determine how many distinct problems actually exist, decide which failures are related, identify which simulations contain the information needed to debug them, and orchestrate RCA across those problems efficiently.
Regression debugging creates a fundamentally different scaling challenge.
There can be an arbitrary number of bugs with varying levels of difficulty. Fixing one problem may expose another. Hundreds of simulations may be running across different test cases and seeds.
And every simulation generates data.
Individual debug cases can already involve enormous logs and waveforms. At regression scale, that data multiplies across every failing simulation.
The naive approach would be to apply an agent to every failure, rerun simulations whenever more information is needed, generate waveforms for every failing test, attempt fixes, and then rerun the entire regression.
But this quickly becomes inefficient.
For autonomous regression triage to work at commercial scale, the system needs to minimize the amount of expensive work it performs.
That means being selective about which failures actually need independent investigation and which simulations actually need to be rerun.
It also means that the underlying RCA system needs to be highly reliable. If an autonomous system proposes an incorrect fix, reruns a simulation, fails again, tries another hypothesis, and repeats the process across dozens of failures, the compute cost can grow quickly.
Accuracy and efficiency therefore become tightly coupled.
The first step is understanding how many distinct bugs actually exist.
Traditional regression systems already use binning techniques, often relying on deterministic scripts and pattern matching to group failures with similar signatures. These methods remain useful.
But there is an opportunity to go further.
Two simulations may produce different log signatures while still sharing the same underlying root cause. An intelligent system should therefore be able to collapse failures beyond what deterministic pattern matching alone can identify.
ChipAgents RCA Triage uses a secondary pass after conventional binning to identify failures that are most likely related by a common root cause.
Instead of treating every failing simulation as an independent debugging task, the system attempts to reduce the regression into a smaller set of meaningful failure groups.
That creates a much more manageable problem for the RCA system.
The same principle applies to waveform generation.
One straightforward approach would be to rerun every failing simulation and dump a waveform for each one.
But that is expensive and often unnecessary.
Instead, the system can identify a minimum set of witness simulations capable of explaining the failures represented by each bin.
Those witness simulations are then rerun with waveform dumping enabled.
The goal is not to collect every possible piece of debugging information. It is to collect the smallest amount of information necessary to explain the regression failures.
This is an important distinction because regression triage is a long-horizon task. A regression might take minutes or hours to execute. Every unnecessary simulation adds cost and delays the final result.
Binning and selective waveform reruns already represent forms of automation.
But automation does not have to stop there.
Once the regression has been reduced into meaningful failure groups and the necessary witness simulations have been identified, those debug packages can be handed directly into autonomous RCA.
The RCA system investigates the root cause for each bin, generates potential fixes, and performs verification.
If verification succeeds, the system gains another signal that the proposed fix is correct. Combined with RCA confidence scoring and the result of the witness simulation, the system can determine whether the fix is likely ready for a final regression run.
The final step is to rerun the regression and verify that the failures have actually been resolved.
This creates an end-to-end workflow:
Regression → intelligent binning → witness selection → waveform rerun → autonomous RCA → fix → verification → final regression.
Instead of an engineer waking up after an overnight regression, discovering a collection of failures, and beginning the triage process manually, the regression can become the beginning of an autonomous debugging workflow.
By the time the engineer returns, the system could have resolved some or all of those failures. If some remain unresolved, the engineer can receive a report showing what was fixed and what still requires investigation.
The paradigm shifts from starting regression triage to reviewing the results of regression triage.
There is another challenge that becomes increasingly important as these systems scale: cost.
Multi-agent systems naturally consume more resources than a single agent because they execute the agent primitive multiple times. That tradeoff exists for a reason: parallel exploration can improve performance and accuracy.
But simply spending more compute is not a sustainable path to better engineering results.
The objective should be to gain the accuracy advantages of multi-agent reasoning while improving token and cost efficiency.
In our internal benchmarks, ChipAgents’ multi-agent systems achieve state-of-the-art performance while operating at costs comparable to traditional single-agent systems.
That is an important direction for autonomous semiconductor engineering.
As agents take on longer-horizon workflows, the question will increasingly move beyond whether an agent can perform a task.
The question becomes whether the system can perform that task reliably, efficiently, and economically across the scale of real semiconductor development.
Regression triage is a useful example of that transition.
Solving one difficult bug autonomously is valuable.
Solving difficult bugs across an entire regression while intelligently deciding what to investigate, what to rerun, and where to spend compute is the next step toward autonomous debugging at commercial scale.

articles.title: Les AirPods 5, avec leur réduction de bruit bluffante, sont à prix cassé juste avant le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
La relève des AirPods 4 avec ANC est assurée. Apple a réussi un tour de force avec ses AirPods 5 : proposer un format ouvert particulièrement confortable tout en y intégrant une réduction de bruit active d’une efficacité bluffante. Alors que le Black Friday approche à grands pas, Amazon dégaine une première promotion très intéressante sur ces nouveaux écouteurs. Les AirPods 5 voient ainsi leur prix chuter sous les 130 euros.
Ce qu’on apprécie sur les Apple AirPods 5
- Une réduction de bruit active efficace malgré le format ouvert
- Un son riche et dynamique, avec un audio spatial convaincant
- Une certification IP57 et 20 heures d’autonomie avec le boîtier
Lancés à 149 euros, les AirPods 5 avec boîtier USB-C sont affichés à 129,95 euros sur Amazon. C’est le prix le plus bas constaté sur le site. La version avec boîtier sans fil est aussi en promotion à 149 euros au lieu de 169 euros.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant les Apple AirPods 5. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Une réduction de bruit qui défie le format ouvert
Isoler l’auditeur avec des écouteurs qui laissent le conduit auditif ouvert, c’est un sacré défi. Apple l’avait relevé avec les AirPods 4 ANC. Avec les AirPods 5, la marque va plus loin : durant notre test, Apple réussit à créer une véritable bulle de calme avec un écouteur ouvert, au point de dépasser de nombreux modèles intra-auriculaires.
Il faudra tout de même tenir compte d’une limite. Dans les environnements très bruyants, la réduction de bruit peut se montrer légèrement instable lors de mouvements brusques. Les AirPods Pro 3 restent toutefois plus efficaces lorsque le bruit devient extrême.
La qualité d’appel reste très bonne, même au milieu du bruit. Leur maintien est excellent, le confort quasiment inégalé et l’IP57 apporte une protection bienvenue. Les commandes par pincement sont souples et efficaces.
Un son riche, mais une autonomie un peu courte
Côté audio, les AirPods 5 ne bouleversent pas la signature sonore des AirPods 4, ils la peaufinent. Grave plus dense, médium mieux maîtrisé, restitution plus fluide et dynamique : l’écoute est aussi agréable que précise. L’audio spatial est particulièrement convaincant : il est naturel à partir de contenus stéréo et souvent épatant avec les pistes en Dolby Atmos d’Apple Music.
En revanche, l’autonomie reste le talon d’Achille des AirPods 5. Quatre heures d’ANC suffisent pour de nombreux trajets, mais imposent des recharges régulières lors d’une journée complète. Sachez enfin que cette version fait l’impasse sur le réglage du volume par balayage sur la tige, la recharge sans fil et le haut-parleur du boîtier. Ces trois fonctions sont réservées au modèle avec boîtier sans fil vendu 20 euros plus cher.
Pour le détail de nos impressions d’écoute, vous pouvez lire notre test des AirPods 5, où ils sont comparés aux AirPods 4 ANC et aux AirPods Pro 3.
Si vous souhaitez les comparer à la concurrence, notre sélection des meilleurs écouteurs sans fil regroupe les modèles que nous avons testés.

articles.title: Avec Echo Time, Amazon mise sur un réveil connecté qui veut (enfin !) vous faire aimer le moment de vous lever
articles.text:
Avec son petit écran rond, ses cadrans personnalisables et ses fonctions dédiées au sommeil, l’Echo Time veut transformer le réveil matinal en un moment (un peu) moins pénible.
Se lever du bon pied, c’est une chose. Réussir à sortir du lit sans négocier cinq fois avec son réveil, c’est encore mieux. Avec son nouvel Echo Time, Amazon entend apporter une petite dose d’intelligence à ce rituel quotidien, grâce à Alexa+ et à plusieurs fonctions pensées pour accompagner l’endormissement comme le réveil.
Un petit réveil tout choupinou qui soigne son apparence
Avec son format compact, sa silhouette arrondie et son écran tactile circulaire de 3,2" (8,1 cm), le réveil Echo Time a de quoi trouver sa place sur une table de chevet. Amazon annonce des centaines de cadrans personnalisables, des plus classiques aux plus fantaisistes, avec des thèmes inspirés de la nature, du sport ou encore de célèbres personnages de fiction.
Evidemment, le réveil vise aussi à afficher diverses informations utiles, programmer des alarmes et s’appuyer sur l’IA Alexa+ pour organiser les routines du matin et du soir.
« Dites à Alexa que vous devez être prêt à 8 heures et que vous ne devez surtout pas oublier votre déjeuner avant de partir : elle réglera votre réveil au bon moment et programmera un rappel. Le soir, demandez-lui de diffuser une musique relaxante : elle sélectionnera la playlist adaptée sur votre service musical préféré, ou ajustera la température de la pièce pour favoriser votre sommeil » explique Amazon.
Un réveil qui veut respecter sommeil et vie privée
Avec Echo Time, Amazon promet aussi un « réveil intelligent ». Grâce à la technologie Omnisense, l’appareil utilise notamment des ultrasons et des capteurs de température pour détecter certains signes de présence et suivre des paramètres liés au sommeil, et cela, sans montre ni bracelet connecté.
L’objectif est de réveiller son propriétaire pendant une phase de sommeil plus léger, dans une fenêtre de 10 à 60 minutes avant l’heure programmée. L’écran peut également s’éclaircir progressivement à l’approche du réveil, à la manière d’un lever de soleil, tandis que l’alarme gagne doucement en intensité.
Amazon insiste aussi sur un point : l’Echo Time ne possède aucune caméra, afin de préserver la vie privée dans la chambre. Les microphones peuvent être désactivés à l’aide d’un bouton dédié, et la détection du sommeil reste facultative. Des précautions pour le moins bienvenues pour un appareil qui s’invite dans l’un des espaces les plus intimes de la maison.
Un réveil malin, mais à près de 200 dollars
Reste une question essentielle, combien coûte ce petit compagnon du matin ? L’Echo Time est annoncé à 200 dollars… auxquels il faut ajouter 40 dollars pour son support réglable vendu séparément. Un tarif qui risque de faire grimacer plus d’un curieux.
À l'heure actuelle, le nouveau réveil signé Amazon est vendu uniquement aux États-Unis, et décliné en Graphite, Glacier White, et Coral Pink.

articles.title: Info Edge’s Hitesh Oberoi to step down as MD and CEO; founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani to take over
articles.text:
Info Edge’s Hitesh Oberoi to step down as MD and CEO; founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani to take over
After nearly 27 years with Info Edge, Hitesh Oberoi will step down from his full-time executive role in December 2026. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani will take over as MD and Group CEO, subject to shareholder approval, as investors watch how the leadership transition shapes the company's next phase.
Hitesh Oberoi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Info Edge, will step down from his full-time executive role on December 2, 2026, after nearly 27 years with the company, including more than 16 years as MD. The parent of Naukri.com announced the leadership change alongside its second-quarter FY27 results.
Sanjeev Bikhchandani, the founder of Info Edge, will take over as Executive Vice Chairman, Managing Director and Group CEO from December 3, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. The move will see Bikhchandani return to an active management role after serving as Executive Vice Chairman. According to the company's regulatory filing, his term will run until April 26, 2031.
Oberoi, however, will continue to be associated with the company. Subject to shareholder approval, he will remain on its board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director. Info Edge said he had chosen to step back from his full-time executive role to devote more time to education, entrepreneurship, institution building, investing and philanthropy, while spending more time with his family.
In a statement, Oberoi said that after nearly 27 years, he felt it was the right time to begin transitioning out of his full-time operating role. He added that he would miss the colleagues and teams who had made those years special. Bikhchandani said the two had built Info Edge together over more than 27 years.
Oberoi's tenure spans much of Info Edge's growth. According to a report citing the company's filing, its market capitalisation increased from Rs 2,500 crore to Rs 80,000 crore during his tenure. Oberoi formally took over as CEO and MD in 2010, when Bikhchandani moved into the role of Executive Vice Chairman. The company said it has a strong institutional foundation, supported by senior leaders who have been with Info Edge for more than 20 years.
Investors will be watching how the leadership change affects Info Edge’s core recruitment business and broader strategy. The move comes after CFO Chintan Thakkar stepped down in November 2025, with co-promoter Ambarish Raghuvanshi taking over as interim CFO.

articles.title: Aïe, le prix du premier MacBook Pro tactile risque de faire (très) mal
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 28 octobre à partir de 18 heures se tient l’événement d’Apple intitulé « Pro and Tell ». Une annonce qui intervient après une semaine déjà chargée pour Apple : lundi, la marque a présenté son iPad mini Oled ; et ce mardi, elle a présenté son premier MacBook Pro équipé de la puce M6 ainsi que son iMac M6. Selon les rumeurs, la marque devrait présenter ce jour pour la première fois un MacBook équipé d’un écran tactile : il s’agirait d’un MacBook Pro OLED avec la puce M5 Pro. Mais les prix de ce nouvel ordinateur pourraient en refroidir plus d’un.
2 899 dollars pour le MacBook Pro tactile : ça pique
C’est le journaliste Mark Gurman de Bloomberg qui rapporte les propos d’une source proche d’Apple. La marque envisagerait de vendre ce MacBook Pro tactile avec une puce M5 Pro à 2 899 dollars. Quant à la version 16 pouces, son prix pourrait être de 3 399 dollars, si l’on part du principe que la version actuelle est vendue à 2 999 dollars. Interrogée par le journaliste, Apple s’est refusée à tout commentaire.
Avec cet écran tactile, ce modèle serait vendu 400 dollars plus cher que la version actuelle (avec la même puce), débarquée en mars. Rappelons que cet ordinateur a vu son prix augmenter de 400 euros en juin pour les deux versions principales : 14 et 16 pouces. Ces deux versions devraient continuer à être commercialisées selon Mark Gurman. C’est d’ailleurs le cas même avec l’arrivée hier des modèles M6. Au vu de ces tarifs, ce nouveau MacBook Pro tactile serait l’ordinateur portable le plus cher jamais commercialisé par Apple. Il devancerait même les autres constructeurs d’ordinateurs portables tactiles, comme ceux de Dell (qui ont aussi des dalles Oled).
Au regard de la différence des tarifs américains et français habituellement pratiquée par Apple, on peut supposer que les prix français seront également très chers. Pour une fourchette large, on peut estimer que le MacBook Pro tactile en version 14 pouces pourrait être vendu entre 3 200 et 3 400 euros. Quant au modèle 16 pouces, ça s’envole encore plus haut : entre 3 800 et 4 000 euros.
Qu’est-ce qui changerait sur ce nouveau MacBook Pro ?
Comme nous l’avons dit, la puce ne changerait pas : pas de puce M6 malheureusement sur ce modèle tactile. Ce serait toujours la puce M5 Pro à l’intérieur, comme sur la gamme actuelle, et le design ne devrait pas changer. Ou presque : les bordures d’écran seraient plus fines, le design global un peu plus compact et le poids serait réduit. Apple aurait par ailleurs conçu un nouveau système de charnière pour éviter de faire bouger l’écran lorsqu’on le touche (pratique sur un écran tactile). Enfin, le système de refroidissement aurait été retravaillé.
Pour la première fois sur un MacBook, cet ordinateur serait équipé d’un écran OLED XDR tactile : on pourrait utiliser macOS 27 au doigt pour faire défiler des pages, déplacer des fenêtres, etc. Sur cet écran, on trouverait d’ailleurs la Dynamic Island qu’on connaît bien sur les iPhone. Autour du poinçon de la webcam, il y aurait des animations qui se déclencheraient : elles ont déjà été aperçues dans le code du système d’exploitation.

articles.title: Cuál es la fecha en la que Meta iniciará a usar el contenido web de empresas para entrenar su IA
articles.text:
Meta pospuso del 30 de octubre al 20 de noviembre de 2026 la entrada en vigor de unos términos comerciales que le permiten tomar contenido de los sitios web vinculados a las cuentas de empresas de Facebook e Instagram. Editores y reguladores europeos pidieron frenarlos.
La empresa liderada por Mark Zuckerberg tomó esta decisión tras las críticas de varios medios de comunicación.
Así lo confirmó al medio Rapporteur un portavoz de la Autoridad de Competencia y Mercados (CMA), el organismo británico encargado de regular la competencia. La Comisión Europea también celebró la postergación.
El texto original autorizaba a Meta a usar “cualquier contenido” de los dominios y páginas web asociados a una cuenta para “proveer, desarrollar, mejorar, investigar, entrenar y mantener la integridad” de sus productos.
Después de las críticas, Meta eliminó la palabra “entrenar” y limitó el uso a “productos publicitarios y comerciales”. Un portavoz de la empresa dijo a Ars Technica que la cláusula no cambia la forma en que Meta usa sus rastreadores web y que los dueños de contenido pueden indicar sus preferencias con el archivo robots.txt.
Meta dijo que aprovechará la prórroga para explicar a sus socios qué cambia y qué no. Los términos entrarán en vigor el 20 de noviembre, salvo que cambie algo antes de esa fecha.
Siguen las críticas a pesar del ajuste hecho por Meta
Según Nieman Lab, especialistas legales consultados sostienen que los términos revisados todavía permiten un rastreo masivo de sitios web. Ese medio también señaló que la nueva redacción no menciona de forma expresa que Meta respetará el archivo robots.txt.
El Consejo Europeo de Editores afirmó que “poco ha cambiado en lo sustancial” y pidió a la Comisión Europea medidas provisionales antes del 20 de noviembre. Dos asociaciones alemanas de editores, que representan a más de 9.000 marcas de medios, calificaron el plan de “robo flagrante”.
La CMA advirtió que podría usar sus poderes de aplicación si encuentra pruebas de una infracción. Su directora ejecutiva, Sarah Cardell, dijo ante el Parlamento británico que sus opciones son limitadas porque Meta no fue designada con “poder de mercado afianzado”, una categoría que sí se aplicó a Google y a Apple.
Por su parte, el gobierno británico informó el 27 de octubre de 2026 en la Cámara de los Lores que la Comisión Europea recibió el 22 de octubre una denuncia formal de competencia contra los términos revisados. La Comisión dijo que la evaluará, y no hay decisión ni sanción anunciada.
Cómo objetar el uso de datos en la UE y el Reino Unido
Los usuarios individuales de la UE y el Reino Unido pueden oponerse al uso de sus datos mediante el derecho de oposición previsto en el Reglamento General de Protección de Datos y su versión británica. Esta opción está disponible en el Centro de Privacidad de Instagram y permite rechazar el uso de la información para la IA de Meta o por parte de terceros.
Dos usuarias de Instagram publicaron guías de cómo lo hicieron: llenaron un formulario donde explicaron sus motivos y recibieron un correo de Meta que aprobaba la objeción, según 404 Media.
Anthropic, Google, Meta y Microsoft consultan a sacerdotes para enseñar ética a sus IA
Empresas tecnológicas como Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft y Amazon consultan a sacerdotes, teólogos, filósofos y referentes de diversas religiones para orientar la conducta ética de sus sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
El propósito es evitar que los chatbots adopten una sola visión moral y recoger perspectivas religiosas, seculares y políticas. Sin embargo, expertos alertan que convertir las tradiciones de fe en principios comparables puede favorecer a las religiones abrahámicas y deformar otras cosmovisiones.
Anthropic sostiene que busca respuestas más profundas y cuidadosas, mientras críticos advierten que mezclar creencias distintas en un modelo podría diluir aquello que las vuelve particulares entre sí.

articles.title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
articles.text:
Attackers have begun probing the Internet for systems unpatched against a recently disclosed critical Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) vulnerability.
Discovered in a core component of EBS's Application Object Library and tracked as CVE-2026-101767, this flaw lets unauthenticated threat actors with HTTP network access take over vulnerable systems in low-complexity attacks.
Oracle released security updates to address the issue in its October 2026 Critical Security Patch Update on October 20 and urged customers to patch their systems immediately.
"In some instances, it has been reported that attackers have been successful because targeted customers had failed to apply available Oracle patches," it said. "Oracle therefore strongly recommends that customers remain on actively-supported versions and apply security patches without delay."
While Oracle has not yet tagged CVE-2026-101767 as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that it already spotted threat actors scanning the Internet for vulnerable systems.
"Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in EBS's Thin Client Framework servlet that chains to remote code execution, this morning, Oct 27," Defused warned.
Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 670 Internet-exposed Oracle EBS instances, most of them with IP addresses from the United States. However, Shadowserver doesn't indicate how many are honeypots or have already been secured against the CVE-2026-101767 flaw.
Attackers often target Oracle vulnerabilities because they let them breach enterprise systems on the networks of many Fortune 100 corporations, government organizations, and healthcare networks around the world.
For instance, since early August 2025, the Clop extortion gang has exploited another Oracle EBS flaw (CVE-2025-61882) in zero-day attacks targeting high-profile victims like Logitech, GlobalLogic, and the Washington Post, as well as US universities (including Harvard University, the University of Pennsylvania, Dartmouth College, and the University of Phoenix)
More recently, in June, Oracle released emergency mitigations for a critical PeopleSoft Suite zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) that the ShinyHunters extortion gang exploited between May 27 and June 9.
By abusing this flaw, the threat actors gained unauthenticated remote code execution on victims' systems and stole data from many organizations worldwide, including Nottingham University, Nissan, and the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC).
Since November 2021, CISA has added 46 Oracle security bugs to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities, 13 of which have also been abused in ransomware attacks.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Photoroom vs Designkit: Which Background Remover Fits Small Businesses? - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Why do you usually need a background remover? Do you need it to just “clean up images” and resize them for different platforms, or do you need it to create beautiful, branded visuals with AI backgrounds and templates as well? Photoroom and Designkit can both clean up product photos, though they offer different ways to get there.
Let’s compare their features and workflows to see which is a better fit for your small business.
Photoroom vs Designkit at a Glance
| Feature | Photoroom | Designkit | 
| Main focus | Product photography and marketing visuals | Background removal and image preparation | 
| Cutout workflow | Background removal within a broader editor | Dedicated online background remover | 
| Background options | Replacement backgrounds, AI backgrounds, and shadows | Transparent, white, black, or custom-color backgrounds | 
| Templates | Extensive template library | Focuses on cutouts, resizing, and basic preparation | 
| Batch processing | Batch editing with shared changes across images | Background removal for up to 15 images per batch in its dedicated tool | 
| Resizing | Resize and position images within the editor | Preset sizes for marketplaces and social platforms | 
| Free-plan considerations | Feature, export, and commercial-use restrictions apply | Background remover is advertised as free, with no signup required | 
| Best suited to | Businesses creating finished product visuals | Businesses needing straightforward cutouts and resizing | 
*Features and limits can change, so check each tool’s current plan details before committing.
1. Background Removal and Cutout Quality
If the cutout looks rough, the whole product photo looks unfinished.
Both Photoroom and Designkit use AI to cut out the subject. For this comparison, we used the same image in both tools — the ceramic mug and the “EAU DE LUMIERE” perfume bottle.
The real difference is in the details. For the test, we checked three tricky spots: inside the mug handle, the embossed leaf pattern, and the edges of the clear perfume bottle and its gold cap. That’s where you usually get leftover background or jagged edges.
In both results, the overall shape is clean — no halos, no cut-off handle. The perfume liquid still looks natural. For a standard catalog image like this, both give you a clean file ready for the white background.
2. Templates and Product Styling
This is where the two tools feel different, even though both have a full suite.
Photoroom builds everything around product styling. Right after background removal, you’re inside a full editor with templates, AI backgrounds, shadows, and brand tools. It’s made for turning a cutout into a finished ad in one place.
Designkit also has a full suite — template library, AI backgrounds, AI photography, listing images, image to video — but its background removal itself stays simple. You remove the background, pick a color or transparent, crop and resize, and download.
Designkit doesn’t push you into the full editor unless you want to. That keeps the core task fast and distraction-free, while the rest of the tools are there when you need them.
3. Batch Processing / Workflow Speed
Batch processing only matters when you have more photos than patience. Updating 10 listings? You won’t feel it. Prepping 60 new products? You need something that doesn’t make you upload one by one.
Designkit’s dedicated remover lets you drop up to 15 images at once — not through a little plus button, but together. You process them in one go and hit Download All. For a 60-image collection, that’s four batches instead of 60 separate uploads.
Photoroom also does batch editing and is great for keeping the same look across a catalog — same background, same styling. Just check your plan first, since batch features and limits depend on subscription. For straight, high-volume cutouts, Designkit is faster. For batch + styling, Photoroom makes more sense.
4. Resizing and Marketplace Requirements
Getting a clean cutout is only 50% of it. Amazon wants white, Shopify wants square, Etsy wants something else — a perfect cutout at the wrong size still gets flagged.
Designkit makes the second half easy: cut it out, toggle between transparent and solid colors, and pick the preset size for your platform. You get your white main image and your transparent banner version from the same cutout.
Photoroom is better when the banner itself needs to look designed, not just resized, because you get more control over positioning. Either way, double-check the platform rules — Amazon’s main image is stricter than the rest. If you just need standard sizes, Designkit is enough.
5. Ease of Use / Learning Curve
When you’re running a small store, the last thing you want is to spend an hour figuring out a photo editor just to remove a background. You have products to list and orders to get out, so the editing part needs to be quick.
Designkit keeps things pretty simple. Upload your photo, check how the cutout looks, choose a background or image size, and download it. You can try it without an account, too. If all you need is a transparent PNG, there’s no reason to dig through a bunch of design templates first. In terms of ease of use, it’s pretty much a straight-up remove.bg alternative.
Photoroom offers a lot more creative control with its templates, AI backgrounds, and shadow tools. It’s ideal for ongoing promotional design, but for businesses that just need fast, accurate background removal, it can be more than necessary.
Already living in Photoroom for your promos? Keep everything there. Just need clean, ready-to-list images? Designkit gets you there with fewer clicks.
6. Pricing, Free Plans, and Export Limits
Don’t just look at the “monthly price”. Look at export limits, resolution, how many images you can batch, and commercial rights.
Photoroom’s free plan works for a few images. But it restricts exports and batch processing. For daily product work, you’ll need a paid plan. Make sure the plan you pick actually covers batch and styling.
Designkit’s background remover is free to use -up to 100 free images per day. It also supports 15 images per batch, bulk download, preview without signing in, full-res with a free account. Confirm the terms before you scale.
Final Verdict
Photoroom and Designkit solve similar problems, but in different ways. Photoroom is built to style product images and create marketing content. Designkit Background Remover stays focused on getting a clean cutout and basic prep done fast.
If you already have a design tool and JUST need “clean product images”, Designkit is a practical place to start. If you want to create finished product scenes and promos in one workspace, you’ll get more value from Photoroom.
Simple way to decide: Start with your workload. If you need 20 images a month, almost anything works. If you need 200, limits and batch speed start to matter a lot. Pick the one that handles your busy days without “extra clicks”.

articles.title: Detienen a una mujer en Cangas por una estafa bancaria de más de 47.000 euros
articles.text:
La Guardia Civil ha detenido a una mujer de 29 años en Cangas do Morrazo (Pontevedra) por su presunta participación en múltiples sucesos de hurto y una estafa continuada, con un perjuicio económico superior a los 47.280 euros, según las investigaciones. La mujer habría sustraído carteras y teléfonos móviles al descuido, utilizando los datos y las tarjetas de las víctimas para acceder a sus aplicaciones de banca electrónica.
La sospechosa habría realizado transferencias y compras, enviado dinero mediante Bizum, retirado efectivo de diferentes cajeros automáticos con HalCash y solicitado préstamos personales no autorizados. Los investigadores no especifican cuánto dinero perdió cada una de las víctimas ni la cantidad que corresponde a cada tipo de operación.
La investigación surgió a raíz de tres denuncias presentadas en enero de 2026. Los hurtos eran similares y se produjeron los martes y viernes, días de mercado en Cangas. Las investigaciones revelaron que la misma persona retiraba efectivo en todos los cajeros automáticos.
La detención y el paso por el juzgado
Fue el 17 de octubre cuando la sospechosa intentó robar un bolso en una cafetería y huyó junto a otros dos hombres en un vehículo, que fue interceptado por una patrulla de la Guardia Civil. Al identificarlos, los agentes se dieron cuenta de que la mujer ya estaba siendo investigada por actividades delictivas similares.
Tras su detención, la mujer fue puesta a disposición del Tribunal de Instancia de Cangas junto con las diligencias, y quedó en libertad mientras continúa investigada por los hechos. No hay información sobre cómo accedió a las contraseñas ni qué comprobaciones de autenticación se saltó.
Las funciones antirrobo de Android y iPhone
Los propietarios de teléfonos Android pueden proteger sus dispositivos frente al robo y al acceso no autorizado a sus datos utilizando funciones de protección antirrobo. Estas opciones se pueden encontrar en Ajustes, Google, Todos los servicios y Protección antirrobo, y constan de varias funciones de seguridad.
El bloqueo por detección de robo utiliza los sensores de movimiento y las conexiones del dispositivo y puede bloquear la pantalla si alguien arrebata el móvil y huye. Sin embargo, la disponibilidad de estas funciones puede variar en función del modelo del teléfono; un ajuste atenuado indica que no es compatible con esa función.
La guía de protección antirrobo de Android describe el funcionamiento de las herramientas. El bloqueo remoto exige, entre otros requisitos, que el número de teléfono esté verificado, la tarjeta SIM esté activa y que la función “Localizador” esté activa en el móvil, tal y como se indica en las instrucciones de Google. Si el dispositivo no tiene conexión a internet cuando se solicita el bloqueo remoto, el teléfono se bloqueará automáticamente una vez que se restablezca dicha conexión.
Los iPhones ofrecen funciones de protección antirrobo similares; sin embargo, algunas acciones exigen Face ID o Touch ID, sin que el código pueda usarse como alternativa. Dichas funciones requieren autenticación biométrica para acceder a contraseñas guardadas cuando se cumplen las condiciones de esta protección. Además, si se intenta cambiar las opciones de seguridad, como la contraseña de la Cuenta de Apple, tendrá que esperar una hora y utilizar Face ID/Touch ID una segunda vez para confirmar su identidad.
La protección antirrobo adicional del iPhone se aplica por defecto fuera de lugares conocidos, como casa o el trabajo. La opción “Siempre” permite exigir estas medidas también en esas ubicaciones. Las funciones de protección antirrobo deben activarse antes de que se produzca un robo.
Si ya se han realizado pagos fraudulentos, el Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) aconseja contactar con el banco para intentar anularlos y, en su caso, bloquear la tarjeta y denunciar el problema. El bloqueo del teléfono y la reclamación de las operaciones son actuaciones distintas.

articles.title: Grey wants 20 million users. Its next bet is salary accounts
articles.text:
Grey, the Y Combinator-backed cross-border payments company, has launched Paycheck, a salary account for professionals earning in United States dollars, British pounds, and euros, as it sets its sights on growing beyond its current base of three million users.
The company, which has processed nearly $5 billion in payments since its inception and recorded a 170% year-on-year increase in total payment volume, announced the new product at Moonshot by TechCabal 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria, on Wednesday.
“After a month of work, employees should have more to look forward to than the additional responsibility of sorting through transactions and keeping track of their earnings,” Idorenyin Obong, Grey’s co-founder and chief executive officer, said during a keynote address at Moonshot.
“A salary is central to how people meet their needs, plan ahead, and build financial security. We believe the financial services they use should reflect that importance.”
Founded in 2020 by Obong and Femi Aghedo, Grey has expanded from a currency exchange platform to a cross-border payments company serving individuals and businesses.
Its latest product, Paycheck, extends that expansion into salary management for professionals earning in foreign currencies.
Paycheck allows users to receive and manage their salaries in foreign currencies, automatically organise salary transactions, and access benefits including higher interest rates on savings, increased transaction limits, and priority customer support.
Existing customers receiving salaries through Grey can activate Paycheck without changing their account details. New users can share their Grey account information with employers or payroll providers, with the service activated after their next qualifying salary payment.
The launch marks another step in Grey’s efforts to move beyond facilitating cross-border transactions into offering financial services built around recurring income.
Grey Business, its multi-currency payment platform for startups and small businesses, has processed nearly $100 million since launching in February 2026. The platform allows businesses to receive international payments, manage foreign currency accounts, and send money across borders.
In June, TechCabal reported that the platform had processed $61.4 million in its first four months, driven partly by demand for stablecoin-based transactions.
The company said African markets, including Kenya, continue to record strong growth, with 30% month-on-month growth.
Grey has also introduced Chinese yuan payouts, enabling individuals and businesses to pay suppliers and other recipients in China. The company operates across 70 countries and supports payouts to over 170 destinations worldwide.
During his Moonshot keynote, Obong said the company was looking to expand beyond its current customer base, with ambitions to reach 10 million, and eventually 20 million users.
Grey’s strategy is that customers who come to the platform to collect money from abroad will have more reasons to stay if they can also manage their paychecks there.
With Paycheck, the company wants to turn an occasional transaction into a regular financial habit.

articles.title: El misterio de las ITS en España: las infecciones de transmisión sexual dan un frenazo brusco tras años desbocadas
articles.text:
Las enfermedades de transmisión sexual son un problema de salud pública de primer nivel, y durante casi una década las gráficas de evolución nos mostraban cómo no paraban de aumentar año tras año con un importante incremento tras el fin de las restricciones de la pandemia. Sin embargo, los últimos datos que tenemos encima de la mesa muestran un escenario mucho más positivo con un frenazo a este incremento.
El informe elaborado por el Centro Nacional de Epidemiología del Instituto de Salud Carlos III muestra una ralentización evidente en el incremento de estas infecciones. Pero, por desgracia, esto no es una victoria, sino que todavía queda ver cómo evoluciona con el paso del tiempo para saber si efectivamente estamos ante una curva mucho más plana.
Las cifras apuntan a que con los datos cerrados de 2025 se han notificado 37.467 casos de gonorrea, que es un dato prácticamente idéntico al de 2024, cuando se informaron 37.457 casos. Y para poner en perspectiva este frenazo, podemos ver que entre 2020 y 2023 la tasa de gonorrea crecía a un ritmo del 36 % anual. Ahora se ha estabilizado en un porcentaje de cambio del 3,5 % con un perfil mayoritariamente de hombres con una edad media de 32 años.
Por otro lado, la clamidia se sigue manteniendo como la ITS más prevalente en nuestro medio con 44.511 casos notificados y un crecimiento interanual que ha caído al 2,9 % frente al 11 % de subida que se experimentó al año anterior.
Hay algunos problemas. Aunque sobre el papel todo pinta bastante bien, debemos saber que hay un retraso en la consolidación de los datos. Esto quiere decir que las cifras epidemiológicas son prácticamente entes vivos que van variando bastante, como ocurrió en el informe anterior, que cifraba los casos de gonorrea en 37.527, pero ahora se ha corregido con 37.457 casos.
El segundo matiz importante es la geografía, ya que, por ejemplo, la caída del linfogranuloma venéreo no es un fenómeno nacional, sino que es bastante local al estar asociado a un desplome que se ha registrado en Cataluña, donde se han pasado de 811 casos a solo 484. Esto no es lo mismo que ocurrió en Madrid, donde los casos han incrementado en casi 200.
De manera internacional. La situación en España es un extraño punto intermedio cuando miramos el panorama exterior, puesto que en Europa se están batiendo récords históricos. En concreto, los últimos daños recogen 106.000 casos de gonorrea, que suponen un incremento del 303 % con respecto al año pasado.
Por otro lado, Estados Unidos vive la situación inversa al ver cómo los casos de clamidia, gonorrea y sífilis bajaron un 9 %. Y aquí ya hablamos de algo más consolidado, puesto que es el tercer año consecutivo en el que se ha dado un descenso así.
¿Por qué? El comportamiento de las ITS en los últimos cinco años ha sido objeto de intenso debate en revistas médicas, y lo que ha quedado claro es que la caída de casos que se vio en 2020 fue un mero espejismo causado por el confinamiento y la falta de cribados. Pero lo más importante es que, ante este panorama, España se va rearmando con la investigación de nuevas herramientas como, por ejemplo, DoxyPEP, que es una profilaxis postexposición para evitar la contracción de ITS bacterianas.
El VIH también está viendo ralentizada su incidencia gracias a la implantación de los tratamientos antirretrovirales universales y el despliegue de la PrEP, que han sido determinantes para frenar la transmisión comunitaria. El problema que tenemos es que se está diagnosticando tarde y esto implica tanto que la persona desconozca su verdadero estado de salud como que aumente la morbilidad o el desarrollo de infecciones oportunistas.

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Neil K. R. Sehgal, Jena Shaw Tronieri, Benjamin Rader, Lyle Ungar, Sharath Chandra Guntuku. Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide. JAMA Network Open, 2026; 9 (10): e2638929 DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38929

articles.title: Adieu Visa et Mastercard : 130 millions d'Européens passent au paiement 100 % souverain
articles.text:
Adieu Visa et Mastercard : 130 millions d'Européens passent au paiement 100 % souverain
L'Europe règle ses comptes
Face au monopole des géants américains, cinq leaders européens du paiement regroupent 130 millions d'utilisateurs sous une même bannière. Objectif : bâtir une infrastructure 100 % souveraine capable de rapatrier des milliards de transactions sur le Vieux Continent.
C'est un séisme pour le secteur bancaire européen. L'initiative française Wero s'associe officiellement aux poids lourds du marché : Bizum (Espagne), Bancomat (Italie), MB WAY (Portugal) et Vipps MobilePay (pays nordiques). En interconnectant leurs réseaux régionaux, ces acteurs ne se contentent plus de faire de la résistance : ils bâtissent une alternative transfrontalière massive pour garder le contrôle total sur les données financières du continent.
Interopérabilité : la clé de voûte de la souveraineté technologique
	
L'Europe dispose de l'infrastructure, de l'échelle et de la vision nécessaires pour offrir une alternative européenne souveraine, robuste et fiable dans le domaine des paiements.
Le projet s'appuie sur la création d'un hub central d'interopérabilité, géré par une entité commune que les partenaires établiront au premier semestre 2026. Cette plateforme technique permettra aux différents systèmes de dialoguer entre eux, sans que les utilisateurs n'aient à changer leurs habitudes. Un Français utilisant Wero pourra ainsi transférer de l'argent à un ami espagnol sur Bizum, avec la même simplicité qu'un paiement domestique.
Feuille de route : 13 pays connectés d'ici 2027
Le déploiement se fera progressivement. Les virements entre particuliers seront disponibles dès 2026 sur l'ensemble des treize pays couverts – d'Andorre à la Suède. Les paiements en ligne et en magasin suivront en 2027. À terme, cette coalition couvrira 72 % de la population de l'Union européenne et de la Norvège.
	
La souveraineté européenne des paiements n'est pas une vision, mais une réalité en devenir.
L'alliance EuroPA, qui connecte déjà l'Espagne, le Portugal, l'Italie et Andorre depuis mars 2025, sert de prototype. Six millions d'euros y ont transité en un an, sans campagne promotionnelle particulière. Un signal encourageant pour cette ambition d'autonomie européenne dans un secteur longtemps dominé par des géants extra-continentaux — une préoccupation que Christine Lagarde avait déjà martelée en avril 2025.
Suivez toute l'actualité des Numériques sur Google Actualités et sur la chaîne WhatsApp des Numériques
