articles.title: Radeon 9070 XT vs. Radeon 7900 XTX: 50+ Game Benchmark
articles.text:
In today's market, the Radeon RX 9070 XT is the best-value high-end GPU you can buy, which is brutal considering that pricing starts at around $900 (against a $600 MSRP). Still, that's about how much you'll pay for an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB in some markets, and the Radeon GPU is on average 70% faster at 4K gaming.
With that kind of performance gap, it's hard to make a case for GeForce right now, at least if you're shopping for something with more than 8GB of VRAM.
So, is it an open-and-shut case for the 9070 XT? Well, not so fast. Many readers have been asking us to revisit the Radeon RX 7900 XTX. Some have cited it as a potentially viable purchase in their region, while others simply want to see how AMD's RDNA 3 flagship has aged, and not just across 10 games, but more like 50+ titles. And that's exactly what we're going to do.
There's a lot of data to go over, after all we did test 51 games in total. However, much of it tells a similar story because the 9070 XT and 7900 XTX often deliver very similar gaming performance. So we'll focus on the games where we found notable results before diving into the overall performance summaries.
Test System
As usual, we're using our Ryzen 7 9800X3D GPU test system, equipped with 32GB of DDR5-6000 memory. The latest available display drivers at the time of testing were also used.
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1AA7] | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 32GB CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | Radeon RX 9070 XT, Radeon RX 7900 XTX | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 26H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.9.2 (9070 XT) AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.10.1 (7900 XTX) | 
Gaming Benchmarks
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
Believe it or not, the margins we're seeing here in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced are on the larger side of what we observed across the 51 games. In this example, the older 7900 XTX was 6-7% faster using the Very High quality preset, but when we enabled Extended Ray Tracing, that margin dropped to just 3-5%, depending on the resolution.
Black Myth: Wukong
Performance in Black Myth: Wukong is also much the same, though we are seeing up to a 6% performance advantage for the 7900 XTX using the High preset at 4K. That margin is reduced to just 3% when using the Cinematic preset.
Arc Raiders
Arc Raiders is more representative of the typical performance margins we saw. Here, the 9070 XT was 2-3% faster at 1440p, while the 7900 XTX nudged ahead at 4K by just 1%.
Borderlands 4
Borderlands 4 is a mixed bag. For example, the 7900 XTX was up to 7% faster at 1440p using the High preset, and 5% faster at 4K. However, switching over to the Badass preset allowed the 9070 XT to pull out a 4% win at 1440p, though the results were tied at 4K.
Crimson Desert
The older 7900 XTX enjoyed Crimson Desert, delivering 11% greater performance at 1440p when using Medium settings. Beyond that, though, we're looking at margins of around 6% or less.
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
The Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 results are very typical. For the most part, we're seeing nearly identical performance between these two GPUs. The only exception was at 1440p using Medium settings, where the 7900 XTX pulled out a 5% win. That's close enough to call a tie, but in this data set, it stands out as a relatively large margin.
Doom: The Dark Ages
The 9070 XT does quite well in Doom: The Dark Ages. At 1440p, we see no real difference between these two GPUs, but at 4K using the Ultra Nightmare settings, the newer Radeon GPU was 10% faster. However, despite the RDNA 4 architecture offering better ray tracing support, that advantage doesn't matter much with path tracing enabled, as both GPUs get smashed.
F1 25
F1 25 saw the 7900 XTX delivering up to 5% greater performance when using the High preset, as seen at 4K. However, enabling ray tracing favors the 9070 XT, though only slightly, with the newer Radeon GPU pulling ahead by 4-6%.
Hell is Us
Performance in Hell is Us is pretty typical of what we saw across most of the 51 games tested, with just a few frames separating these GPUs. In this example, the 9070 XT was generally ahead, but again, we're talking about low single-digit margins here.
Indiana Jones and the Great Circle
Indiana Jones and the Great Circle is another example where performance was largely the same. The 7900 XTX was up to 5% faster at 1440p using the Supreme preset, but that margin quickly shrank to just 2% at 4K. Then, when enabling full ray tracing, the 9070 XT takes the lead, though only just, offering around 5% better performance.
Lego Batman
Lego Batman provided us with more of the same. For the most part, there's little to nothing separating these two GPUs. At most, we saw a 4% margin at 4K using Medium settings, which favored the 9070 XT.
Monster Hunter Wilds
The same is true of Monster Hunter Wilds. Here, we're looking at identical or near-identical performance for the most part. The only somewhat noteworthy results can be seen at 4K using the High ray tracing settings, where the 7900 XTX was actually faster. So the 9070 XT isn't always superior when using RT effects.
Pragmata
Another typical example can be seen in Pragmata. Here, the 7900 XTX and 9070 XT deliver virtually identical performance, with or without ray tracing enabled.
Marvel Rivals
The same is also true of Marvel Rivals. The two GPUs trade blows using Medium settings, with performance swings no larger than 4%. But once we max out the quality settings, performance is virtually identical.
007 First Light
007 First Light gives us a mixed bag of results. Using Medium settings at 1440p, the 7900 XTX was 4% faster, not a big margin, but at 4K the results are flipped, and now it's the 9070 XT that's faster, leading by a slim 6% margin. Back at 1440p, but this time with Ultra settings, the 7900 XTX gets out to a 9% lead, only for that margin to shrink to 2% at 4K.
Cities: Skylines
Cities: Skylines provides us with some unusual results. In this example, the older 7900 XTX is quite a bit faster, delivering 12-13% greater performance using the Medium preset and then 12% at 1440p using High settings, though just 6% at 4K. Still, overall, the 7900 XTX was the faster GPU in this title.
Counter-Strike 2
The 7900 XTX was also dominant in Counter-Strike 2, delivering 18% greater performance at 1440p with Medium settings and 25% at 4K. These gains were maintained using Very High settings, with the older Radeon delivering 22% greater performance at 1440p and then a massive 32% increase at 4K.
Delta Force
In this example, we see that Delta Force favors the newer 9070 XT. Here, the RDNA 4 GPU delivered 14% more performance at 1440p using Ultra settings, though just 5% more at 4K. We also saw similar scaling using the Ultimate preset.
Forza Horizon 6
Forza Horizon 6 provided the kind of data I expected to see more of, that is, competitive rasterized performance with the newer 9070 XT taking the cake once ray tracing is enabled. Using the Extreme preset, the 9070 XT was 3% faster, but when we switched over to ray tracing, that margin grew substantially to 23%.
Fortnite
Testing with Fortnite, we find the limits of our Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor at 1440p using Performance mode, reaching just over 700 fps, which seems like enough to me, for now. Anyway, at 4K, the 7900 XTX delivered 18% stronger performance, and even with ray tracing enabled, the older RDNA 3 GPU still came out on top, offering 14% better performance.
Grand Theft Auto V
Testing with Grand Theft Auto V shows very similar rasterized performance between these two GPUs, but once we enabled ray tracing using the Maximum RT preset, the 9070 XT takes over, crushing the 7900 XTX by 35% at 1440p and 33% at 4K.
Spider-Man 2
The 9070 XT also dominated our Spider-Man 2 testing, well, at least at 1440p, where it was 9% faster using the Very High preset and then 22% faster with the maximum ray tracing settings enabled. At 4K, the margins were much smaller, in the 5-6% range.
Performance Summary
Across the 51 games tested, how do the 9070 XT and 7900 XTX compare?
Well, they're nearly identical in terms of performance. This data doesn't tell us too much, other than the fact that overall, these GPUs deliver very similar performance. So let's take a closer look at the per-game results.
Average Performance by Game
Please note that this data is based on average frame rates, calculated using the geo mean, and combines the two quality configurations tested, as well as both resolutions.
As you can see, the vast majority of games saw less than a 10% difference in performance between these two GPUs. In fact, just five games exceeded 10%. The worst examples for the 9070 XT were Counter-Strike 2 and Red Dead Redemption 2, while its best results came in GTA V, Forza Horizon 6, and Naraka: Bladepoint.
What We Learned
The Radeon RX 9070 XT has continued to age well, and we've seen plenty of evidence of this recently. We've seen it matching and even beating the RTX 5070 Ti in newer titles such as Gears of War: E-Day, The Witcher 3 Remastered, and Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, to name a few, though that will depend on the settings used.
Not only did most early reviews of the 9070 XT find it trailing the 5070 Ti by a reasonable margin, but also the 7900 XTX. Now the 9070 XT and 7900 XTX appear to be pretty much neck and neck.
Looking across all 51 games tested, the performance margins generally fall into three categories: 1) near-parity in standard rasterization, 2) ray tracing and path tracing gives the advantage to the newer RDNA 4 architecture, and 3) specific titles where the older 7900 XTX flagship flexes its memory bandwidth and compute muscle.
Where the GPUs Differ
At native 4K, the Radeon 7900 XTX's additional bandwidth can help, particularly in memory-intensive games. However, that doesn't translate into a 50% increase in FPS simply because it has 50% more memory bandwidth.
The 7900 XTX also has 50% more VRAM: 24GB versus 16GB for the 9070 XT. But right now that only matters when playing heavily modded games with UHD texture packs, running games at extreme settings, working with large 3D scenes, or using local AI models that exceed 16GB.
With ray tracing enabled, particularly in newer games, the 9070 XT generally comes out on top, sometimes by a substantial margin. Both GPUs now support FSR 4.1 upscaling, as AMD extended support to the RX 7000 series back in June. This means the 7900 XTX is no longer restricted to the lower-quality FSR 3.1 upscaler.
The key difference to note here is that the 9070 XT uses FP8 acceleration to run FSR 4.1 more efficiently. It also supports the newer ML frame generation and ray regeneration features in FSR Redstone. The 7900 XTX, on the other hand, runs FSR 4.1 through INT8 processing, which comes with higher overhead. It still supports older FSR frame generation, but not all the RDNA 4-exclusive Redstone features.
As an example, AMD reports roughly 1.3 ms of FSR 4.1 upscaling processing time at 4K on the 9070 XT, compared with 3.1 ms on the 7900 XTX. In short, this means the 9070 XT can deliver better performance when both GPUs use the same upscaling settings, even in games where the 7900 XTX is faster natively.
Both GPUs support AV1 encoding for streaming, though the 9070 XT also gets PCIe 5.0 support, which can be viewed as a modest future-facing benefit. That said, the 7900 XTX's PCIe 4.0 x16 interface really isn't a limitation, especially given that you're far less likely to exceed its VRAM capacity.
Pricing can vary from month to month, sometimes substantially, but as of writing the 9070 XT costs $900 in the US, or $1,250 in Australia, while secondhand 7900 XTX models are selling on eBay for between $800 and $1,100, or around $1,500 in Australia. At those prices, the 9070 XT makes far more sense for most buyers. Obviously, if you already own the 7900 XTX, upgrading to the 9070 XT would be a sidegrade at best, so don't do that.
Bottom line, the 7900 XTX has continued to age well and remains highly competitive with current generation high-end GPUs. Like the 9070 XT, it has only gotten better since release through updated features such as FSR 4.1, even if AMD did take its sweet time rolling out support.

articles.title: Cloudflare Opens Quicksilver to Customers as Workers KV Instant, Inside a 1 MB Envelope
articles.text:
Cloudflare recently made Quicksilver available to customers for the first time, as a new mode for Workers KV called KV Instant. Reads resolve in 1.62 ms at the 99th percentile, compared with 287 ms for classic KV. What determines whether a team can use it isn't the latency, but the envelope around it.
Quicksilver is Cloudflare’s own configuration store, introduced in 2020. Nearly every request to Cloudflare looks up at least one key in it, Rob Sutter writes, and it has never been a customer-facing product. Brendan Irvine-Broque, who works on Cloudflare’s developer platform, announced the change on X:
we have this crazy key-value store at Cloudflare called Quicksilver
instantly updates keys across our whole network. microsecond reads from every location. stupid fast
our customers have asked us for years to make it available
we finally did – in a way we think is quite simple - as a new mode for Workers KV
The published figures, measured to over 300 edge locations:
| Mode | p99 reads (all) | median write replication | p99 write replication | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Instant | 1.62 ms | 107 ms | 256 ms | 
| Classic | 287 ms | under 1 s | 4.38 s | 
Cloudflare notes it has no sub-second fidelity for replication lag in classic mode, so the classic median and p95 figures are upper bounds rather than measurements. p95 reads in Instant mode are reported in microseconds.
The API is the Workers KV one, with three differences. Mode is set at namespace creation with a "mode": "instant" attribute, and cannot be changed afterward. Metadata is unsupported, so getWithMetadata always returns null. And list returns every matching key with no pagination.
Then the limits. A namespace holds at most 10,000 key-value pairs and one megabyte in total, with keys up to 300 bytes. Writes are capped at one per namespace per second, which Cloudflare contrasts with classic KV’s one write per key per second, on the grounds that a single system of record "makes it easier for you to reason about update order in your application." That difference is the one most likely to catch a team migrating: a pattern classic KV permits across many keys concurrently becomes a single serialised queue.
Pricing points the same direction, and Cloudflare says so plainly: "storage and Class A operations are significantly more expensive than Workers KV."
|  | Reads (Class B) | Writes, deletes, lists (Class A) | Storage | 
|---|---|---|---|
| KV Instant | $0.20 per million | $0.10 per operation | $100 per MB, per month | 
| Classic KV | $0.50 per million | $5.00 per million | $0.50 per GB, per month | 
Reads cost 60% less. A write costs ten cents, against five dollars per million in classic mode. Storage runs $100 per megabyte per month, and since a namespace tops out at one megabyte, that is also the ceiling. Multi-key reads bill per key, so requesting three keys in one get costs the same three Class B operations as three separate calls.
Irvine-Broque set out the reasoning in the same thread:
just like how we use Quicksilver ourselves, it’s for small data that is read often and updated infrequently
pricing reflects this - reads actually cost 60% less than even Workers KV
Writes cost what they cost, he added, because writing a key replicates it to hundreds of locations. This is a store priced so that you read from it constantly and write to it rarely.
Benjie Malinao, also on X, read the fit the same way:
This is the config store agents actually need. Sub-2ms p99 reads and global writes landing in about a quarter second at p99, on the same KV API. Feature flags and agent settings without waiting on a TTL. I’d move hot-path config over first.
Feature flags, routing tables and agent settings fit that shape. Session state, user records and anything with a write path do not.
The comparison practitioners reached for was Vercel. Developer Shawn Mclean asked Irvine-Broque directly:
I’m looking into using Vercel Global Config for a middleware read. They claim 15ms. If I move my workloads to CF, are you saying I can read from middleware for a platform tenant domain mapping in 2ms?
The answer did not quite confirm it:
even p50 of Workers KV (non-instant) from 2 years ago was ~5ms. KV Instant is even faster than that (see numbers in the post)
Cloudflare’s own worked example is a launch flag read on every request and flipped at a keynote, which is precisely the workload: one key, one write, read everywhere immediately.
Classic Workers KV, which launched during Birthday Week in 2018, remains the recommendation for large or frequently updated data. The two modes now sit under one API with opposite economics.
KV Instant is in private beta with a sign-up form, and Cloudflare says it plans to open it up more widely. No general availability date is given.

articles.title: Women-led companies dominate top ranks of 2026 Deloitte Fast 50 | BetaKit
articles.text:
For the first time, half of Canada’s 10 fastest-growing companies are led by women, according to the 2026 Deloitte Technology Fast 50.
The annual list recognizes Canada’s fastest-growing technology companies across three categories based on their revenue growth percentage over the past three or four years, depending on the category.
The top of the flagship list featured more women-led companies than usual this year, including Toronto-based rewards platform Chexy, which placed second with a four-year revenue growth rate of 23,183 percent. Other women-led companies at the top of the list include legaltech company BorderPass, led by co-CEO Sally Daub, in third place; cleantech software WeavAir, led by CEO Natalia Mykhaylova, in fourth; AI automation platform SimplyAsk.ai, led by CEO Shuli Gortler, in fifth; and online therapy provider Total Life, led by CEO Neelam Brar, in sixth place.
Women-led companies featured more prominently than usual on this year’s list, taking spots two through six.
In a statement, Chexy CEO Liza Akhvledziani-Carew said the company has proved its rent-to-rewards model, and that the growth rate indicates it’s “onto something much bigger.” Earlier this year, the company raised a $14-million Series A round led by Khosla Ventures, one of Silicon Valley’s most reputable venture firms, to help its users earn credit card rewards on more everyday expenses.
The list’s top spot went to Toronto-based Finni Health, which sported a four-year revenue growth rate of 46,754 percent. The Y Combinator alum, founded by Canadian Bucky Khan, provides a platform for autism care providers in the United States to start, run, and grow their practices.
The average revenue growth rate of this year’s Fast 50 was 3,079 percent, a jump from last year’s average growth of 2,623 percent. Other companies on the 2026 Fast 50 include, in descending order, Toronto-based legaltech Spellbook, Québec City-based pipeline inspector Flyscan, Montréal-based digital lender Nesto, and Vancouver-based private stock marketplace Clarity (formerly known as Hiive).
In addition to the Fast 50, Deloitte also recognized 15 Canadian companies on its Enterprise—Industry Leaders ranking and another 17 on its Companies to Watch list, which showcases companies with the potential to be future Fast 50 program winners.
Richmond, BC-based last-mile delivery company UniUni topped this year’s industry leaders list, sporting a 2,143-percent four-year revenue increase. While its reported revenue increase vastly exceeded others below it on the list, UniUni has faced trouble recently. The company’s attempt to go public through a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) fell through after the SPAC terminated the deal, citing UniUni’s deteriorating business and financial performance.
RELATED: Neo Financial completes first-ever hat trick of Deloitte Technology Fast 50 rankings
Other companies on the Enterprise—Industry Leaders list include Toronto-based FinTech firm Koho, which placed second with a 580-percent four-year revenue increase, Calgary-based PurposeMed (which is set to be acquired by Grindr) in seventh, and Ottawa-based surveillance tech firm Solink in tenth.
Ottawa-based Turbopuffer, which provides a fast data search engine, decisively took the top spot on the Companies to Watch list with a 65,443-percent growth rate, confirming founder Simon Hørup Eskildsen’s fears that he runs Canada’s fastest-growing company. In a distant second was another Ottawa-based company, defence tech firm Tactiql, with a 4,395-percent growth rate.
Companies on the flagship Fast 50 list are automatically eligible for the broader North American Technology Fast 500, which will be released on November 18. Deloitte says 80 Canadian companies made that list this year, down from 114 last year.
Feature image courtesy Chexy.

articles.title: Monte Carlo Data launches Bayes, an AI agent for autonomously monitoring and fixing autonomous agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Monte Carlo Data launches Bayes, an AI agent for autonomously monitoring and fixing autonomous agents
Enthusiasm for artificial intelligence agents is at an all-time high and many enterprises have gotten so carried away that they’re deploying them faster than they keep up.
Their human AI engineers only have the capacity to watch over a handful of AI agents at any one time, so they’re in desperate need of help. What better solution could there be than more AI agents?
That’s what the big data observability company Monte Carlo Data Inc. seems to think anyway. Today it announced a new offering called Bayes, described as an “AI teammate” to differentiate it from the autonomous agents it’s designed to watch. Bayes is really an agent itself, but rather than do work itself, it’s tasked with observing the ones that do get work done.
It watches for signs of unreliability and if it spots something, it troubleshoots the problem, whether that’s with the agent itself or the data being fed into it, implements a fix autonomously and then verifies that the agent is now functioning as it’s supposed to.
Bayes is the culmination of Monte Carlo’s evolution from big data observability to AI. The company borrowed the observability concept from the world of software applications, pioneering tools to help humans keep tabs on their structured data environments. It later expanded to cover unstructured data too, before pivoting last year to embrace generative AI, launching tools for monitoring both inputs and outputs.
The company says there’s an urgent need for Bayes. The average human engineer struggles to monitor more than two or three AI agents and their associated data pipelines at a time, but many organizations have deployed many more than this. With each new agentic deployment, there’s a need to evaluate its work constantly and ensure that its outputs don’t start going astray later on. Clearly, it’s time to automate that task too.
Monte Carlo’s pitch has resonated with customers such as Axios Media Inc., the technology news website that uses AI agents for research, drafting, localization, managing news feeds and other tasks. Shreye Saxena, senior data scientist at Axios, explained that the nature of media work means it cannot compromise on its agent’s accuracy. “If the injected data is incorrect or the trajectory is wrong and it produces a response without checking the database, then we’re not going to get the outcomes we need from our agents,” he said.
Bayes works by scanning a company’s technology environment to discover the agents they’ve deployed and the data environments that power them. It can be given as much or as little responsibility as the customer feels comfortable with, performing tasks like monitoring agent’s outputs, triaging issues and executing fixes in the background.
When it spots a problem, it will trace that failure all the way back to the developmental decisions made pre-deployment, studying both the model that powers it and the data pipelines it relies on. To do that, it integrates with third-party coding assistants and software deployment pipelines.
Gartner Inc. analyst Sanjeev Mohan said Monte Carlo is effectively going after the Holy Grail of AI, giving enterprises a way to build self-improving AI agents. “The idea isn’t new, but pulling it off has been elusive,” he said. “You have to see what agents actually do at runtime and trace it back through the system all the way to the data.”
Monte Carlo says Bayes has already had a profound impact on early adopters. A South American financial services institution reported that Bayes detected 200% more incidents than its internal monitoring systems, while also reducing the number of false positives by 80%. The cloud data warehouse giant Snowflake Inc. is using Bayes to help its own customers build and run more reliable Cortex-based agents.
The goal, according to Monte Carlo co-founder and Chief Executive Barr Moses, is to make customers feel as if they can trust their AI agents. “There aren’t enough engineers to keep those agents trustworthy, but Bayes changes the math,” he said. “It understands your agents and your data together, fixes what breaks and gets better at your environment every day, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time shipping.”

articles.title: As AI agents reshape the web, Google opens Gemini and Search to more apps | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google is making it easier for businesses to connect their apps to its AI experiences across Search and Gemini with the debut of its Connected Apps Platform.
Introduced in Gemini and Google Search earlier this year, connected apps let users securely link and interact with popular third-party services, then use them to take specific actions. For instance, you could connect to Canva to design a flyer, or to YouTube Music to build a playlist.
We’ve seen varying takes on the idea by other consumer-facing AI services like ChatGPT and Meta’s Muse. The premise is that such integrations could ultimately shift consumer behavior away from launching and using individual apps to instead using their favorite services through their preferred AI provider.
However, to successfully capture and retain consumers’ attention, there have to actually be a wide range of connected apps to explore.
Google’s idea is to open its doors to any business or developer that wants to reach users through Search or Gemini by allowing them to submit their own connected apps and monitor their performance.
The platform preview is currently available in beta to developers in the U.S., and will allow developers to build and submit apps that can be used across Google’s products.
To get started, developers would integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app, Google explains.
Essentially, this process lets devs connect their app to Google’s services so it can be used with the search giant’s AI features. Developers can also choose whether they want their app to be available via Search, the Gemini app, or both.
After the app is live, developers can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and maintain control over their brand identity, such as their verified logos and authenticated accounts.
Similar to how SEO allowed companies and websites to show search engine rankings, this could well be one of the initial steps for businesses that want their services to be more visible to users on the agentic web.
Google already has over 50 Connected Apps available in Gemini, including from partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, Peloton, and others, in addition to its own expansive set of services, from Workplace and Photos to YouTube Music and Google Home.
These apps will now come to Google Search over the next few weeks. Search today has fewer integrations, featuring apps like Instacart, Canva, YouTube Music, Yahoo Fantasy Football, and others.
Google said meditation app Calm is another new partner on this effort, and that its app will soon launch on both Gemini and Search.
The new Connected Apps platform is in public preview for U.S. developers who sign up for the waitlist. Google did not share when it would become more broadly available.

articles.title: Anvisa aprova 5 novas canetas de GLP-1 para diabetes e obesidade
articles.text:
A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) aprovou o registro de cinco novas canetas de GLP-1 para o tratamento de diabetes e obesidade. A autorização foi publicada nesta quinta-feira (29/10), na Resolução nº 4.244/2026, no Diário Oficial da União (DOU).
Com os novos registros, a agência chega a 20 canetas dessa classe aprovadas em 2026. Os medicamentos contêm liraglutida ou semaglutida e são fabricados por empresas indianas.
Quais são as novas canetas aprovadas?
Três medicamentos são indicados para diabetes e dois para obesidade. Confira os produtos, suas indicações e as empresas responsáveis pelos registros e pela fabricação.
- Aribet (liraglutida): indicado para diabetes; registro da Farma Vision Importação e Exportação de Medicamentos Ltda. e fabricação da indiana Biocon.
- Lyrza (liraglutida): indicado para obesidade, associado a exercícios físicos e mudanças na alimentação; registro da Farma Vision e fabricação da Biocon.
- Wylovol (liraglutida): indicado para obesidade, também associado a exercícios físicos e mudanças na alimentação; registro da Farma Vision e fabricação da Biocon.
- Embeltah (semaglutida): indicado para diabetes; registro da Dr. Reddys Farmacêutica do Brasil Ltda. e fabricação da indiana OneSource Specialty.
- Sevema (semaglutida): indicado para diabetes; registro da Aché Laboratórios Farmacêuticos S.A. e fabricação da OneSource Specialty.
Por que a Anvisa priorizou os registros?
A aprovação faz parte de uma estratégia iniciada em agosto de 2025, após solicitação do Ministério da Saúde. A priorização busca atender aos interesses do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), no âmbito do Complexo Econômico-Industrial da Saúde (Ceis), e à necessidade de abastecimento do mercado nacional.
A iniciativa resultou na publicação do Edital de Chamamento nº 12/2025, que estabeleceu prioridade para a análise de medicamentos à base de liraglutida e semaglutida.
O que muda com as aprovações?
As duas substâncias pertencem à classe dos agonistas do receptor de GLP-1. Esses medicamentos imitam a ação de um hormônio produzido pelo intestino, que participa da regulação da glicose no sangue e dos mecanismos de fome e saciedade.
O registro sanitário, porém, não significa que os produtos já estejam disponíveis nas farmácias. As datas de lançamento e os preços de comercialização das cinco canetas não foram informados. No Brasil, os preços máximos dos medicamentos são regulados pela Câmara de Regulação do Mercado de Medicamentos (CMED).
Desde 2025, a venda de medicamentos agonistas do receptor de GLP-1 exige receita médica, que deve ficar retida na farmácia.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: German startups are betting big on Japan. Should the rest of Europe follow? | EU-Startups
articles.text:
German startups are increasingly looking towards Japan as a destination for international expansion, industrial partnerships and technological cooperation.
From DefenceTech and nuclear fusion to quantum computing and space infrastructure, recent developments suggest that Tokyo is becoming an important partner for some of Europe’s most ambitious technology companies.
This momentum became particularly visible today, during German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s visit to Japan. Munich-based Proxima Fusion announced two Japanese partnerships, while drone manufacturer Quantum Systems unveiled agreements with Mitsubishi Chemical and Panasonic, alongside plans to establish a permanent presence in Tokyo.
The announcements form part of a wider diplomatic push. According to Japanese news agency Jiji Press, Germany and Japan were expected to sign 33 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) spanning AI, nuclear fusion and other advanced technologies.
However, the more interesting story for Europe’s startup ecosystem extends beyond a single diplomatic visit.
More than handshakes
For Quantum Systems, the visit marks a step towards becoming an established player in Japan’s DefenceTech market.
Founded in 2015 in Gilching by Florian Seibel, Michael Kriegel, Tobias Kloss and Armin Busse, Quantum Systems develops unmanned aerial systems and software for defence, security and civilian applications.
The company announced the establishment of Quantum Systems Japan K.K., including a Tokyo office, alongside MoUs with Mitsubishi Chemical and Panasonic. The agreements aim to combine Japanese manufacturing capabilities with German drone technology, strengthening local supply chains and bringing Quantum Systems closer to Japanese customers.
Sven Kruck, co-CEO of Quantum Systems, said: “Japan has understood where defence is heading: unmanned systems, rapid innovation and the industrial capacity to deliver at scale. Ukraine has shown why this matters. When personnel are scarce and threats evolve fast, technological advantage is decisive. Japan’s manufacturing strength and our operational experience are a powerful combination. We are proud to put down roots in Japan and honoured to help strengthen its defence industrial base.”
Meanwhile, Munich-based Proxima Fusion, founded in 2023 as a spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, announced two separate agreements involving fusion energy.
As EU-Startups reported earlier today, its agreement with Kyoto Fusioneering focuses on plasma-heating systems and fuel-cycle technologies. A separate agreement with Fujikura explores industrial-scale manufacturing of superconducting tape in Lower Saxony, building on a previously announced €140 million manufacturing initiative.
The cooperation also extends into space. Established German aerospace group OHB signed an MoU with Japanese space-tech company Astroscale, founded in 2013, to explore opportunities in orbital servicing, surveillance and space security. Astroscale, on the same day, also announced a €17 million (£15 million) MOD Contract from the UK Government.
Tokyo was already calling
The latest announcements are part of a broader trend we’v seen here at EU-Startups.
Munich-based defence AI startup Helsing, founded in 2021, has already been pursuing opportunities in Japan. In August 2026, Reuters reported that Japanese conglomerate Rakuten was helping Helsing pursue a potential contract to supply unmanned systems to Japan’s military. Its HX-2 strike drone was undergoing testing by Japan’s Ground Self-Defence Forces.
Industrial cooperation has also attracted Japanese capital into Germany. In March 2025, Panasonic announced a €30 million equity investment in Munich-based tado°, founded in 2011, expanding an existing partnership combining Panasonic’s heat pumps with tado°’s smart heating controls and energy management software.
Quantum computing provides another example. Braunschweig-based QUDORA Technologies, founded in 2021, established a Japanese subsidiary and partnered with Fixstars in May 2026 to make its quantum computing tools accessible through a cloud platform.
By October, QUDORA Japan had been selected for a government-backed research project alongside Kyocera and Japan’s National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology.
Even outside DeepTech, German companies have recognised the opportunity. Cologne-based translation technology company DeepL, founded in 2017, established a Japanese subsidiary in 2023 to strengthen its local commercial operations.
These developments suggest that Japanese partnerships are becoming an increasingly deliberate part of German startups’ international strategies.
Why Japan, why now?
Japan’s strengths in electronics, robotics, precision engineering, advanced materials and industrial manufacturing offer European startups capabilities that can be difficult and expensive to develop independently.
For companies building fusion reactors, quantum computers or advanced robotics, access to established manufacturers and specialised suppliers may be just as valuable as attracting new customers.
Japan has also been working to strengthen its startup ecosystem. Its five-year startup development plan, introduced in 2022, set an ambitious objective of increasing annual startup investment to approximately €56 billion (¥10 trillion) by the 2027 financial year.
Meanwhile, cooperation between Brussels and Tokyo is expanding. In May 2026, the EU and Japan agreed to deepen collaboration in AI, quantum technology, semiconductors, digital infrastructure and cross-border data flows.
The Tokyo test
Despite the momentum, Japan is not necessarily an easy market to enter.
Language barriers, different business practices, complex procurement processes and the importance of long-term corporate relationships can make expansion challenging, particularly for startups with limited resources.
The experiences of Quantum Systems, Helsing and QUDORA highlight one possible solution: finding established Japanese partners rather than attempting to navigate the market independently.
German startups appear to have recognised the opportunity Japan offers foreign tech and talent. The question now is whether the rest of Europe will follow.

articles.title: HHS Filing Puts iRhythm Data Breach Toll at 8.2 Million
articles.text:
More than 8 million people were impacted by a June 2026 data breach at medical equipment provider iRhythm.
The company, which specializes in wearable cardiac monitoring technology and is best known for its Zio wearable ECG monitor, disclosed the incident in mid-June.
iRhythm said right from the start that sensitive information might have been stolen from certain third-party-hosted business applications and that the hackers attempted to extort a ransom, threatening to leak the compromised data.
Earlier this month, the company started sending notification letters to the potentially affected individuals and filed notices with regulators in several states, as well as with the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
The incident has now been listed on the HHS data breach portal as affecting 8,179,772 individuals, a number iRhythm previously reported to the Oregon Attorney General’s office.
Per iRhythm’s previous notices, the hackers compromised patients’ names, addresses, dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers, and iRhythm account and device data (including account/serial/insurance numbers and dates of service).
“iRhythm has no evidence that any personal information has been or will be used to commit identity theft,” the company said earlier this month.
It also encouraged potentially affected individuals to protect themselves against medical identity theft and identity fraud, but its notice does not mention free identity theft or credit monitoring services.
“We have not identified any impact to our products, our clinical or medical device systems, our connections to customers, our manufacturing and distribution operations, patient safety, or our ability to meet patient needs,” the company said.

articles.title: Samsung 8LPU+ Gets Floated as the Node for a Future Switch 2 Lite
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Samsung 8LPU+ Gets Floated as the Node for a Future Switch 2 Lite
Samsung Foundry will present 8LPU+, the second generation of its 8LPU platform, at IEDM 2026 on December 14, and Nintendo Patents Watch has already pegged it as a possible fit for a Switch 2 Lite. It's speculation for now. Nintendo hasn't announced a Switch 2 Lite, and Samsung's material doesn't mention Nintendo or NVIDIA. The link exists because the Switch 2's NVIDIA T239 SoC is built on Samsung's 8 nm node, so a refined version of that process is an obvious candidate for a cheaper handheld-only model.
Samsung's IEDM abstract lists 12% higher performance, 15% lower power, and an 8% area shrink over 8LPU, along with roughly 10% smaller I/O area and lower standby leakage. It's a DUV-only node, and Samsung pitches it at automotive, robotics and edge AI chips. Korea's Electronic Times reports the platform should arrive before year's end, and quoted an industry official who named existing 8 nm customers as likely candidates. Of course, these are process-level figures, so they don't directly translate into a future Switch 2 Lite that runs 12% faster or lasts 15% longer per charge. We also don't know how closely NVIDIA's custom 8N variant maps onto 8LPU+.Of course, cost is the other major concern. Nintendo raised the Switch 2 to $499.99 on September 1, largely blaming memory prices, and Samsung reportedly bumped 8 nm wafer prices by nearly 10% for new orders in July. A smaller die on already-depreciated DUV lines could claw some of that back, though it probably won't offset rising DRAM costs by itself. Until Nintendo says otherwise, a Switch 2 Lite remains a rumor.
Sources:
				IEDM 2026, 				Nintendo Patents Watch, 				Electronic Times, 				via Videocardz

articles.title: Chrome's AI-powered Autofill can now dig through your Gmail to fill out forms | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s Chrome browser is getting an update that will improve its autofill capabilities using AI. On Wednesday, the company said that Chrome will get an advanced version of autofill that will help users fill out online forms with suggestions pulled from their Gmail.
That means Chrome could suggest things you might need to know, like a flight confirmation number, membership ID, tracking information, order number, address, phone number, or credit card number by referencing your email.
The update is an expansion of Google’s Personal Intelligence, which already allows users to connect their Google Apps to its AI assistant, Gemini, to retrieve certain details and then use them to answer complex questions.
Though seemingly minor, the update could make Chrome easier to use, which could give users another reason to continue to use Google’s browser and stay in its AI ecosystem. It’s reminiscent of one of Apple’s most appreciated features: the ability to automatically detect verification codes sent via text and display them above the keyboard, allowing users to enter them with a single tap.
As with other Personalized Intelligence features, users can decide whether or not to enable enhanced autofill from their Chrome settings. Sensitive data is encrypted, Google notes.
The feature is rolling out to U.S. users on the desktop, and in the iOS and Android apps for Gemini in Chrome.

articles.title: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
articles.text:
Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don’t like AI, and it’s not just young people and creatives. Appearing on the Colin and Samir podcast to talk about the launch of widescreen and long-form video for Instagram, Mosseri said he thinks there’s a trend of “more anxiety and more frustration and more anger about AI,” particularly in creative industries:
Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
The Instagram boss said that worries about AI come down to ‘a fear of being left behind in some way.’
It’s not only getting worse, it’s going to continue to get worse. I think we’re going to see more frustration and anger, some of it founded, some of it unfounded, over the next couple of years, and that’s going to make it hard for a lot of people, not just in the industry.
Mosseri claimed Instagram doesn’t rank AI creators differently, but raised the question of ranking quality, saying, “There’s a lot of great AI content out there, there’s also a lot of AI slop. Do we rank AI content as well as we rank non-AI content? Probably not.” Talking about AI slop again after previously bringing it up in a New Year’s slideshow dump, he said he thinks the term AI “slop” is used “too liberally.”
Instagram began cracking down on AI-generated profiles in August, after launching a label for AI accounts earlier this year, but misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes remains an issue. Earlier this month, Mosseri said Instagram is “actively working out what to do” about AI fakes, but he noted, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.”
Mosseri said Instagram is “now starting to require AI accounts to label themselves, because we think it’s important that people know if what they’re looking at is real or not real.” He also acknowledged there are fears around AI, including from creators:
I think people are concerned about a lot of things. I think they’re concerned about owning their content and models getting trained on their content. I think they’re concerned— there’s people who are concerned about safety. They’re concerned about job displacement, having AI displace whatever it is they do, if you’re a content creator or an engineer or a mathematician. I think there’s concerns about— I mean, fundamentally what I think it comes down to when you really have, like, a heart-to-heart with someone is a fear of being left behind in some way.

articles.title: Why Physics Needs To Move At The Pace Of Design
articles.text:
Physics-based analysis becomes more consequential as chips, packages, boards, and systems are designed together.
Every hardware design contains decisions made before the team fully understands their physical consequences. An architecture is chosen. Components are placed. Materials are selected. Engineers bring experience and judgment to those choices, but the detailed physics often arrives later, when changing course is harder and more expensive.
That order of work limits what engineers can build. When every answer requires substantial preparation, compute and specialist time, teams have to decide which questions are worth asking. Promising ideas can be set aside because there is no practical way to investigate them within the schedule.
We built Vinci to change that. We recently announced a $250 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation. The investment gives us the resources to accelerate a goal that reaches well beyond any single analysis: shortening the distance between what engineers can imagine and what they can build.
The cost of slow analysis extends into decisions made long before a simulation begins. Teams simplify designs so they can evaluate them. They add margin where uncertainty remains. They carry assumptions forward because testing every alternative would take too long.
Consider a change in component placement. It may improve one aspect of a design while changing how heat moves through the board. Differences in temperature and material expansion can also affect warpage. The engineer needs to understand those interactions while the placement is still a choice. If that understanding arrives after other decisions depend on it, even a small change can require substantial rework.
This becomes more consequential as engineers design chips, packages, boards and systems together. A decision about power affects cooling requirements. A packaging choice changes the physical constraints elsewhere. The number of interactions grows, while the time available to investigate them remains limited.
AI adds urgency to this problem. As engineering workflows become increasingly automated and agentic, they will be able to propose and act on more design choices. Each of those choices still has physical consequences. Generating possibilities is useful only if engineers can determine which ones will work.
Continuous Physics Reasoning makes trustworthy physical understanding available throughout design. Engineers can investigate a change, understand its consequences and use that understanding to decide what to do next, while the design is still moving.
Making this practical requires changes to the entire computational process. Vinci automates design understanding and preparation, combining agentic orchestration with our Foundation Model for Physics and GPU-native physics kernels. The platform delivers deterministic, solver-accurate results at manufacturing resolution and works across new designs without customer-specific training or fine-tuning.
Those properties matter together. Engineers need enough physical detail to evaluate the design they intend to manufacture. They need repeatable answers they can trust. And they need to investigate a new design without first building a model trained specifically for it.
We chose semiconductors as our first proving ground because their physical demands leave little room for compromise. Vinci is already running on production engineering programs, with commercial capabilities across thermal, thermo-mechanical and convective fluid behavior. Manufacturing-scale analyses that once required hours or days can be completed in minutes.
For an engineering team, that changes how much it can learn before committing. More alternatives become practical to evaluate. A question that would once have been deferred can inform the next design decision. Engineers can pursue ideas that would otherwise have been too costly or time-consuming to investigate.
Continuous Physics Reasoning gives us the foundation for a broader ambition. Once physical understanding can keep pace with design, we can work toward helping engineers determine what should change to improve a product, and eventually toward creating designs from human intent.
That is a demanding engineering problem. A useful recommendation has to account for how changing one part of a system affects the rest. It must work within constraints imposed by materials, manufacturing and the other disciplines involved in building a product. Extending physical understanding into that kind of engineering intelligence is central to our long-term work.
This financing will accelerate progress across both physics and engineering. We will expand physical coverage beyond the capabilities available today, develop more capable agentic engineering workflows and deepen integrations with the systems our customers use. We will also invest in the people and computing infrastructure needed to bring Vinci into more production programs.
The need extends well beyond semiconductors. Engineers developing vehicles, aircraft and satellites face different physical problems, but they share the need to understand the consequences of decisions while those decisions can still change. Our ambition is to make that understanding part of the infrastructure on which hardware engineering runs.
I am grateful to our customers, investors and team for helping us pursue this work. Our customers are putting Vinci to use on real engineering programs, where the value of an answer depends on whether it can inform the work in front of them.
That is the standard we intend to keep building toward. Engineers should be able to pursue an idea because they can investigate it, understand its constraints and improve it. Giving them that ability throughout design can expand the range of products they are able to create. That is what this next chapter of Vinci is for.

articles.title: Firefox pourra bientôt remplir automatiquement vos formulaires et surveiller vos pages Web
articles.text:
Les fonctionnalités d’IA de Firefox vont s’enrichir de deux nouveautés. Déjà capable de rechercher sur le Web grâce à l’IA, de regrouper automatiquement vos onglets ou encore de rechercher dans votre historique de navigation à l’aide d’instructions en langage naturel, l’assistant de navigation IA Smart Window du navigateur va profiter de deux nouvelles fonctionnalités.
Le remplissage des formulaires assisté par l’IA
La première nouveauté concerne le remplissage des formulaires en ligne. Très bientôt, Smart Window pourra se charger de remplir ceux-ci en prenant en compte le contexte.
Contrairement au système de remplissage automatique déjà en place qui ne gère que les données personnelles enregistrées dans le navigateur (comme votre nom, prénom et adresse), cette fonction s’appuie sur le contexte des autres onglets ouverts pour vous suggérer des réponses.
Concrètement, lorsque vous cliquerez sur un formulaire comportant au moins quatre champs de saisie, une option « remplir à partir de la source » (Fill from source) s’affiche. Vous pourrez choisir les onglets sur lesquels s’appuyer et ainsi vérifier les propositions de remplissage avant de les valider. Mozilla précise que « Smart Window ne soumettra jamais le formulaire à votre place ».
Pour proposer cette fonction qui analyse les champs et extrait les données des onglets, Mozilla s’appuie sur le modèle de Google, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite. Cela « signifie que les informations provenant de ces pages sont partagées avec le modèle d’IA en vue de leur traitement. », tient toutefois à préciser Mozilla.
Un outil pour surveiller les changements sur les pages Web
L’autre grande nouveauté à venir dans Firefox concerne la surveillance du Web. Comme l’a fait récemment Apple avec Safari sur iOS 27 et macOS 27, vous pourrez prochainement configurer Firefox pour surveiller les modifications apportées sur certaines pages Web. Cela vous permettra, par exemple, d’être alerté d’une baisse de prix sur un article, de la disponibilité d’un produit après une rupture de stock, de la publication d’une nouvelle offre d’emploi, etc.
Pour l’utiliser, il suffira de saisir la commande /watch dans le chat Smart Window et de décrire en langage naturel ce que vous souhaitez surveiller. La fonction, qui s’appuie sur le modèle d’IA Qwen, a toutefois quelques limites. Vous ne pourrez en effet pas surveiller plus de 5 pages web par tâche, avec un maximum de 15 tâches actives en parallèle.
Le module, qui ne fonctionne que lorsque Firefox est ouvert, vous permettra en outre de choisir la fréquence de vérification quotidienne ou hebdomadaire.
Mozilla précise par ailleurs que les tâches seront mises en pause automatiquement passé 60 jours sans changement détecté et qu’elles s’arrêteront automatiquement après 90 jours.
Quid de la disponibilité de ces deux nouveautés ? Mozilla précise que ces nouvelles fonctionnalités ne sont pour l’instant accessibles qu’au sein de la version bêta de Firefox desktop, et qu’elles restent pour l’heure limitées aux seuls utilisateurs anglophones résidant aux États-Unis et au Canada. Si aucune date de disponibilité pour la France n’est à ce jour connue, Mozilla envisage d’étendre leur disponibilité à d’autres marchés dans les mois à venir.

articles.title: How to get corporate gifting right across multiple cities
articles.text:
How to get corporate gifting right across multiple cities
From managing recipient lists and budgets to coordinating packaging and deliveries, here's how businesses can make large-scale festive gifting more organized and efficient.
Sending Diwali gifts to a handful of employees or clients is relatively simple. Sending hundreds of gifts to recipients spread across different cities is another matter. Addresses need to be verified, budgets finalized, packaging standardized and deliveries timed to arrive before the festival. A missed shipment, incorrect address or last-minute change can quickly complicate the exercise.
For businesses managing large-scale Diwali gifting, the key is to plan early, coordinate the details and ensure that every recipient has a consistent experience, regardless of location.
Start with a detailed recipient list
The first step is to organize all recipient information in one place. This should include names, delivery addresses, contact numbers, and any other information required to complete the delivery. For employee gifting, it may also be useful to group recipients according to city or office location. Client and partner lists can be organized separately so that different gifting requirements are easier to manage. Checking the information before placing the order is important. Incorrect or incomplete addresses can create delivery problems, particularly when gifts are being sent to several cities.
Personalize where it matters
Large-scale gifting does not have to feel completely impersonal. Businesses can add small details that make gifts feel more thoughtful. A personalized greeting card, recipient name or company message can add a sense of occasion without making the process significantly more complicated. For key clients or long-term partners, businesses may choose a more customized gift, based on the relationship. The goal is to find the right level of personalization for each recipient group while keeping the overall process manageable.
Use bulk ordering to simplify the process
When a business is managing a large number of recipients, placing individual orders can quickly become time-consuming. Bulk ordering can make the process more organized, particularly when the same or similar gifts are being sent to multiple locations. A single gifting plan can cover product selection, quantities, packaging, and delivery requirements. This also makes it easier for the internal team to monitor the overall budget and track the progress of the campaign. Businesses planning corporate Diwali gifts can also establish recipient categories in advance, making it easier to decide which gift goes to which group.
Keep packaging consistent
Packaging plays an important role in professional Diwali gifting. When gifts are being sent to different cities, consistent packaging can create a unified brand experience. The same box style, colour scheme, greeting card or branding element can be used across the entire order. This helps ensure that recipients receive gifts that feel like part of the same Diwali campaign, even if they are in different locations. Packaging should also be practical enough to protect the contents during transportation. Fragile products or items sensitive to heat may need additional consideration.
Set a clear budget
Diwali gifting costs can increase quickly when the recipient list is large. Setting a budget before selecting products helps businesses narrow down suitable options. The budget can be divided by recipient category. For example, employee gifts may have one price range, while client or business-partner gifts may have another. It is also useful to account for packaging, delivery, and personalization costs rather than looking only at the product price.
Track every shipment
Once the Diwali gifts are ordered, tracking becomes one of the most important parts of the process. A simple tracking sheet can include the recipient, city, order status, and delivery status. This allows the business team to quickly identify delayed or unsuccessful deliveries and take action where required. For larger gifting programmes, having one person or team responsible for monitoring the campaign can make communication much easier. It also prevents different departments from working with separate or outdated recipient lists.
Decide what the gift should include
The next step is deciding what will go into the Diwali gift. Businesses have several options, from traditional sweets and dry fruits to chocolates, snacks, candles and curated hampers. The choice can depend on the recipient group. Employee gifts may follow one format, while important client or partner gifts may have a different product mix. A consistent selection across cities can make large-scale gifting easier to coordinate. At the same time, businesses can create different categories of gifts based on the relationship with each recipient. This balance can help maintain consistency without making every gift identical.
Plan for different delivery locations
Sending gifts across multiple cities requires attention to delivery coverage and timelines. Businesses should confirm whether the selected gifting provider can deliver to all the required locations and understand how long each delivery may take. This becomes especially important during Diwali because demand for gifting and delivery services can increase significantly around the festival. Businesses can group orders by city and create a delivery schedule before placing them. This makes it easier to track which gifts have been dispatched, which are in transit, and which have already reached the recipients.
Start planning before the festive rush
One of the easiest ways to make multi-city Diwali gifting smoother is to start early. Early planning gives businesses more time to finalize recipient details, compare gifting options, approve designs, and schedule deliveries. It also leaves room to handle unexpected issues, such as an incorrect address or a product becoming unavailable. Waiting until the last few days can limit the available options and put additional pressure on both the business team and the delivery network.
Making multi-city Diwali gifting easier
Diwali gifting across several cities requires more planning than a small personal gifting exercise, but the process becomes manageable when it is treated as a structured campaign. A clear recipient database, suitable gifts, consistent packaging, planned delivery schedules, and proper tracking can help businesses coordinate gifting across locations. The aim is not simply to send gifts to as many people as possible. It is to create a consistent and thoughtful festive experience, even when recipients are spread across different cities.

articles.title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
articles.text:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update, warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
"Google Brotli contains an unchecked return value vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream," it said.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise."
While CISA's BOD 26-04 applies only to federal agencies, the cybersecurity agency urged all network defenders to prioritize patching this security flaw to block incoming attacks.
Security teams that can't apply the updates immediately should block incoming Brotli-compressed requests at the proxy or firewall level, or disable the Brotli decoding feature until they can update.
After patching, administrators must also restart affected processes and rebuild and redeploy affected container images.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Xgimi Horizon 30 Series : des vidéoprojecteurs toujours plus lumineux, plus de contraste et support de la 4K à 120 Hz — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les Xgimi Horizon 30 Pro, Max et Ultra Max reprennent le triple laser RVB de la génération précédente, ajoutent la 4K à 120 Hz et un double iris, pour 4 800 à 6 000 lumens ISO.
Une série qui succède à l’Horizon 20
Un an après la série Horizon 20, dont la version Horizon 20 Max avait remporté l’Award du meilleur vidéoprojecteur de l’année 2025, le fabricant chinois met à jour sa gamme lifestyle. La série correspond à la version internationale du RS30, commercialisé en Chine fin avril 2026. Les deux évolutions majeures sont l’affichage 4K à 120 images par seconde et le double iris mécanique. Ce dernier provient des modèles haut de gamme de la marque, comme le Titan Noir, un modèle que l’on installe en fond de salle.
    Pour aller plus loin
Meilleur vidéoprojecteur 2026 : comparatif et guide d’achat
            
Les trois références partagent le même châssis et les mêmes fonctions. Elles reprennent le système de balancelle des générations précédentes, que l’on voit ici et là sur ce type de vidéoprojecteurs.
Seuls la luminosité, le contraste natif et le tarif varient. Le fabricant vise les amateurs de grande image qui ne disposent pas d’une pièce dédiée. Ainsi, ces appareils s’installent dans un salon lumineux et se déplacent d’une pièce à l’autre.
Concernant le double iris, il s’agit de la même technologie embarquée dans les Aura 3 Pro et Aura 3 Max avec la possibilité de laisser la fonction sur un mode automatique ou de choisir manuellement le niveau (2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0 et 7.0).
Luminosité, contraste et formats d’image
Selon Xgimi, le Horizon 30 Pro délivre 4 800 lumens ISO pour un contraste natif de 8 000:1. Le Max atteint 5 300 lumens et 9 000:1. L’Ultra Max culmine à 6 000 lumens et 10 000:1. Avec le traitement DBLE, le contraste dynamique annoncé monte à 80 000:1, 90 000:1 puis 100 000:1, toujours d’après le fabricant.
Tous reposent sur une puce DLP de 0,47 pouce. La définition 4K y est obtenue par décalage de pixels. Les formats Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR10, HLG et IMAX Enhanced sont gérés, de même que le Filmmaker Mode, les contenus 3D et la calibration ISF. L’image projetée mesure de 65 à 300 pouces de diagonale, soit environ 1 à 7,6 mètres.
Face à la concurrence, la 4K à 120 Hz reste encore peu courante sur ce segment. Plusieurs fabricants l’ont toutefois annoncée récemment : dans la catégorie lifestyle, JMGO avec ses Iris Ultra et Iris Ultra Max et, en ultra courte focale, les Xgimi Aura 3 Pro et Aura 3 Max, Awol Vision LuxVision et Hisense PX4-Pro.
Jeu, installation et partie audio
Pour les joueurs, Xgimi annonce une latence de 1,9 ms en 4K à 120 Hz et de 1 ms en Full HD à 240 Hz. Le VRR, l’ALLM et l’AMD FreeSync Premium sont pris en charge. Par ailleurs, la fréquence élevée profite au cinéma : le 24 images par seconde s’affiche en cadence 5:5, sans interpolation de mouvement.
L’installation s’appuie sur un pied intégré inclinable (non motorisé, contrairement aux derniers modèles JMGO) et pivotant, un zoom optique et un décalage d’objectif vertical (±130 %) et horizontal (±50 %). Le Lens Memory mémorise jusqu’à cinq configurations, ce qui est pratique quand on déplace l’appareil. La mise au point, la correction trapézoïdale et l’évitement d’obstacles sont automatiques. Le zoom optique couvre un rapport de projection de 1,2 à 1,5:1 sur les trois modèles.
Google TV assure l’accès aux applications de streaming. Deux entrées HDMI acceptent la 4K à 120 Hz, dont une avec eARC. Le Wi-Fi 6 et le Bluetooth 5.2 sont aussi de mise. Enfin, deux haut-parleurs Harman Kardon de 12 watts gèrent le Dolby Audio et le DTS Virtual:X.
Disponibilité et prix
Les tarifs recommandés s’élèvent à 2 499 euros pour l’Horizon 30 Pro, 2 799 euros pour le Max et 3 299 euros pour l’Ultra Max. Le prix d’entrée de la gamme monte nettement, puisque la série Horizon 20 commençait à 1 699 euros et que l’Horizon 20 Max était affiché à 2 999 euros.

articles.title: Amazon lance trois enceintes Echo : l'une d'elles s'offre une caméra pour doper l'IA contextuelle
articles.text:
Amazon lance trois enceintes Echo : l'une d'elles s'offre une caméra pour doper l'IA contextuelle
Amazon renouvelle sa gamme Echo avec quatre nouveautés qui misent sur l’intelligence artificielle, le son et la maison connectée. Entre enceinte compacte enrichie en fonctions domotiques, réveil intelligent qui surveille le sommeil et enceinte premium dotée d’une caméra, Alexa+ s’invite dans tous les recoins de la maison.
Amazon vient de dévoiler une nouvelle gamme d’appareils Echo, avec trois enceintes au programme : un Echo Dot repensé, un réveil connecté baptisé Echo Time et un Echo Studio équipé d’une caméra. Ces appareils viennent compléter les Echo Dot Max et Echo Studio 2025 lancés l’année dernière, afin de répondre à une plus grande variété de besoins.
Cette nouvelle gamme mise sur des améliorations sonores, une compatibilité étendue avec les équipements de la maison connectée et bien sûr la prise en charge de l’assistant Alexa+, dopé à l'intelligence artificielle.
Echo Dot : une enceinte qui fait aussi office de hub domotique
Amazon Echo Dot (nouvelle génération)
L’Echo Dot de nouvelle génération succède à l’Echo Dot (Gen 5). La marque avait bien caché son jeu, puisqu'elle avait dévoilé l’an dernier l’Echo Dot Max, une version tout aussi compacte s'équipant d'une architecture sonore 2 voies et d'une nouvelle interface de commandes. On pouvait alors penser qu’elle remplacerait le modèle classique.
Cette enceinte connectée conserve donc le format circulaire épuré de sa devancière lancée en 2022, tout en misant sur une plus grande polyvalence. Elle intègre désormais un hub domotique compatible avec Zigbee, Matter et Thread, permettant de piloter de nombreux équipements sans passerelle supplémentaire. Cet Echo Dot embarque également un répéteur Wi-Fi eero, annoncé comme capable d’étendre la couverture du réseau existant jusqu’à 90 m².
Sur le plan acoustique, l’enceinte intègre un haut-parleur large bande revisité, qui promet 50 % de basses supplémentaires par rapport à l’Echo Dot (Gen 5). Amazon ajoute par ailleurs sa puce AZ3 et un quatrième microphone, destinés à améliorer la réactivité d’Alexa+ et la détection de la voix, notamment dans les environnements bruyants. En somme, ce nouvel Echo Dot se rapproche de l’Echo Dot Max sur le plan des fonctions logicielles, tout en apportant de nouvelles possibilités, mais conserve une architecture sonore plus simple.
Comme à son habitude, Amazon décline également son enceinte compacte en version Kids. L’Echo Dot Kids reprend les caractéristiques du nouvel Echo Dot dans un habillage destiné aux plus jeunes, avec des contenus adaptés à leur âge. Associé à l’abonnement Amazon Kids+, il permet notamment d’accéder à des livres audio, des jeux et des contenus éducatifs, tout en proposant des contrôles parentaux pour encadrer les usages.
Echo Time : un réveil connecté qui surveille le sommeil
Amazon Echo Time
Avec Echo Time, Amazon investit la table de chevet. Ce réveil connecté adopte un écran circulaire personnalisable et une conception sans caméra. Plusieurs centaines de cadrans sont proposés, des affichages analogiques aux designs plus modernes, en passant par des thèmes sportifs.
Contrairement à l’Echo Spot, qui se concentre sur les fonctions classiques d’un réveil connecté avec Alexa, l’Echo Time met l’accent sur le sommeil. Grâce à la technologie Omnisense, il peut détecter les phases de sommeil plus léger et déclencher l’alarme entre 10 et 60 min avant l’heure programmée, sans nécessiter de bracelet connecté. À l’approche du réveil, l’écran s’éclaire progressivement pour reproduire un lever de soleil, tandis que la tonalité augmente doucement en intensité.
Pendant la nuit, l’affichage s’atténue pour ne laisser apparaître que l’heure. Amazon indique également que l’appareil a obtenu la certification SleepMark de la National Sleep Foundation, qui distingue les produits répondant à des critères scientifiques en matière de sommeil. Une version Echo Time Kids est également prévue, avec un an d’abonnement à Kids+ inclus.
Echo Studio avec Home Camera : une enceinte premium avec caméra dédiée à l'IA
Amazon Echo Studio avec caméra pour la maison
L’Echo Studio avec Home Camera reprend les caractéristiques de l’Echo Studio 2025, tout en intégrant une caméra de 13 mégapixels. Alexa+ peut ainsi analyser visuellement son environnement pour répondre à des demandes contextualisées, par exemple reconnaître une boîte de céréales ou expliquer les règles d’un jeu de société. La fonction Live View permet également de consulter à distance les images de la pièce.
Côté acoustique, comme l’Echo Studio lancé l’an dernier, ce modèle embarque trois haut-parleurs large bande de 57 mm disposés sur les côtés et sur la face supérieure, associés à un woofer à "haute excursion". Grâce à son canal orienté vers le plafond, l’enceinte prend également en charge nativement les contenus Dolby Atmos. Au même titre que l’Echo Studio classique, l’Echo Studio avec Home Camera compte ainsi parmi les enceintes les plus imposantes du catalogue d’Amazon, aussi bien pensée pour les interactions avec Alexa+ que l’écoute musicale.
L’ajout d’une caméra soulève néanmoins des questions de confidentialité. Amazon prévoit un bouton dédié permettant de désactiver la caméra et les microphones, ainsi qu’un voyant LED signalant la transmission d’images vers le cloud.
Alexa+ au cœur de la nouvelle gamme
Le lancement de ces nouveaux appareils s’inscrit dans la stratégie d’Amazon autour d’Alexa+, déjà disponible en France. Par rapport à l’ancien assistant vocal, cette version s’appuie sur l’intelligence artificielle pour favoriser des interactions plus naturelles et fournir des réponses mieux adaptées au contexte. Elle tire notamment parti d’une puce plus avancée et de microphones supplémentaires.
Les prix de lancement sont fixés à 104,99 € pour l’Echo Dot, 214,99 € pour l’Echo Time et 259,99 € pour l’Echo Studio avec caméra.
