articles.title: Altera Agilex 27 is the First Agilex 2X Platform Adding 800GbE and 1.6TbE and More
articles.text:
New generation FPGA announcements do not come often, which makes this a bit exciting for us. Today, Altera is introducing the Agilex 27 as the first family in its new Agilex 2X portfolio. Agilex 27 pairs hardened 800GbE and 1.6TbE Ethernet with PCIe 6.0 and 7.0 support, and offers configurable transceivers up to 256Gbps. What is more exciting, and what I learned on the pre-briefing call, is that Altera also has a new AI-assisted mode for putting these FPGAs to use.
HyperFlow and Third-Generation HyperFlex
A major new feature of the Agilex 27 family is HyperFlow. HyperFlow is a new full-chip distributed data network that Altera says can move data at multi-terabit-per-second rates throughout the FPGA. That traffic runs on a dedicated network instead of the programmable fabric, so it does not consume soft logic resources or add routing congestion. That leaves more FPGA resources for the application. As an example, a 1.6TbE Ethernet port can bring traffic in through hardened I/O, HyperFlow can carry it across the chip, and the soft logic can spend its resources on processing rather than moving data.
The new family has memory controllers for DDR5, LPDDR4, LPDDR5X, and LPDDR6. It also supports UCIe, has crypto acceleration, and Arm Cortex-A720 and Cortex-A520 cores. A trend we have seen in both Altera and Xilinx high-end FPGAs over the past few years is that programmable logic is surrounded by more hardened IP blocks that help bring designs up faster. Ten years ago, the focus was mostly on the programmable logic elements and I/O, but now much more is happening here.
Agilex 27 also carries third-generation HyperFlex registers distributed throughout the routing fabric. Altera says Quartus Prime can re-time and pipeline designs through those registers without consuming logic resources. Altera claims a 1.8X generation-over-generation performance-per-watt improvement over Agilex 7 for HyperFlex in Agilex 27.
Agilex 27 sits at the high-performance end of the Agilex 2X portfolio, above the mid-range Agilex 25 and the value-optimized Agilex 22 and Agilex 23. Agilex 22 is FPGA-only, while Agilex 23 adds SoC options.
QuartusIQ AI Companion
QuartusIQ is an AI companion for Quartus Prime that helps developers prioritize steps across compile, timing, debug, and verification. In Altera internal benchmarks comparing Quartus Prime with and without QuartusIQ, design creation was up to 10X faster, and the total design cycle was up to 1.5X faster. The tool integrates with MCP and supports a bring-your-own-key setup.
At NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026, the companies announced that this would be coming to the new RTX Station systems (Windows versions of the DGX Station platforms we have been reviewing at STH). The idea is that you can use QuartusIQ and MCP to design and implement workflows on the chip with local NVIDIA Nemotron as the model. I love this.
Final Words
The other bit to know about FPGA announcements is that there is generally a big gap between announcement and availability. I asked on the call, and the QuartusIQ bits are this quarter, and the Agilex 27 engineering samples are expected in the second half of 2027. What I really wanted to know is how long it would take to get Agilex 27 and have a local model via MCP build me something like an RDMA-enabled 1.6TbE NIC. My sense is that it will be a 2027 or 2028 timeframe when that happens. It is also something I am super excited about since a barrier to using FPGAs has always been having to know how to program them. At some point, Altera and Xilinx can expand FPGA use if they can deliver AI tools that abstract the hardware platform further. I have a goal of being able to get an FPGA card and have an AI agent implement a NIC or a firewall from scratch on it without having to really get my hands dirty designing the RTL. One day it will happen, and I guess the timeframe is 2027/2028.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.text:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness
Published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.
"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," says Longin.
"We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," says Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural."
To investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.
Another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.
A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness
The experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.
However, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.
The results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.
"There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," says Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical."
Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.
Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI
The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an important insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.
Awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.
Because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.
The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.
"Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," says Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, plans, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study shows is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important."
Story Source:
Materials provided by Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Louis Longin, Jurgis Karpus, Nadine Meertens, Bahador Bahrami, Ophelia Deroy. AI is not as conscious as humans: Essentialism in mental state attributions to artificial systems. Cognition, 2027; 278: 106733 DOI: 10.1016/j.cognition.2026.106733

articles.title: Avant le Black Friday, le SSD Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To passe à 189,99€
articles.text:
Depuis le début de l’année, la pénurie de mémoire NAND tire le prix des SSD vers le haut, et chaque baisse sur un modèle de 1 To mérite d’être regardée de près à un mois du Black Friday. Le Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To descend à 189,99 € sur Amazon, 30 € sous son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours, mais sa mémoire QLC sans cache DRAM le destine à certains usages plus qu’à d’autres.
Le Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To est un SSD M.2 NVMe en PCIe 4.0 qui annonce jusqu’à 5 900 Mo/s en lecture et 5 000 Mo/s en écriture. Il s’agit de sa révision R2, reconnaissable à ces débits et à la référence CSSD-F1000GBMP600CXTR2.
Amazon propose actuellement le SSD Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To à 189,99 €, soit 30 € de moins que son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, fixé à 219,99 €. L’offre vise d’abord ceux qui veulent agrandir le stockage d’un PC portable ou d’une tour équipée d’un port M.2 en PCIe 4.0.
Le Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To revient à 189,99 € chez Amazon, alors qu’il n’était pas descendu sous 219,99 € ces 30 derniers jours.
Pourquoi choisir le Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To ?
- Des débits PCIe 4.0 complets : Ses débits annoncés exploitent pleinement un port M.2 en PCIe 4.0, bien au-delà d’un SSD SATA. Les copies de gros fichiers en profitent directement.
- Un format qui passe partout : Au format M.2 2280, épais de 3 mm et sans dissipateur, il se loge dans un PC portable comme dans une tour. Il fonctionne aussi sur un port PCIe 3.0, au débit de ce dernier.
- Une garantie de cinq ans : Corsair le couvre cinq ans, dans la limite de 250 To écrits, soit environ 137 Go par jour pendant toute la garantie. De quoi voir venir en bureautique, en multimédia ou en jeu.
Agrandir un portable ou une ludothèque, son terrain de jeu
Avec 1 To, le MP600 Core XT accueille Windows, vos logiciels et une bonne partie de votre bibliothèque de jeux. Son format fin en fait un candidat naturel pour remplacer le SSD d’origine d’un PC portable devenu trop juste. Sur une tour, il peut servir de second SSD dédié aux jeux, si un emplacement M.2 est libre. Corsair fournit aussi son logiciel SSD Toolbox pour suivre l’état du disque.
Ce SSD s’adresse surtout aux usages où l’on écrit peu : bureautique, navigation, jeu ou retouche photo occasionnelle. Il convient moins à un monteur vidéo qui transfère des rushs chaque jour. Sa mémoire QLC et l’absence de cache DRAM sont des choix d’économie qui pénalisent d’abord les écritures longues et intensives, et son endurance de 250 To écrits s’y épuiserait plus vite.
Une révision R2 qui change de contrôleur, face à un marché exigeant
Cette révision R2 adopte le contrôleur Phison E27T, là où la première version du MP600 Core XT, que nous avions testée en 2 To, reposait sur un E21T et plafonnait à 5 Go/s en lecture. Nous lui reprochions une endurance un peu faible et une gestion du cache perfectible, des constats qui ne valent pas forcément pour cette version, que nous n’avons pas testée. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs SSD, le WD Blue SN5000 tient la première place pour son rapport capacité/prix, et la TLC y reste préférée à la QLC, à l’endurance en retrait. Le MP600 Core XT se défend sur ses débits et sa garantie, pas sur l’endurance.
✅ Les points forts
- Jusqu’à 5 900 Mo/s en lecture annoncés en PCIe 4.0
- Format M.2 2280 de 3 mm, adapté aux PC portables
- Compatible avec les ports PCIe 3.0
- Garantie constructeur de cinq ans
- 30 € sous son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours
❌ Les limites
- Mémoire QLC sans cache DRAM, moins à l’aise sur les écritures intensives
- Endurance de 250 To écrits, modeste pour un usage professionnel lourd
- Révision R2 pas encore passée sur notre banc de test
- 189,99 € reste un budget conséquent pour 1 To, pénurie de NAND oblige
Pour vérifier le tarif au moment de commander, le Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To reste affiché à 189,99 € sur la fiche Amazon.
À 189,99 €, le Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To n’est pas bon marché dans l’absolu, mais 2026 a changé les repères. Avec des puces NAND annoncées en hausse de 55 à 60 % au premier trimestre et une détente pas attendue avant 2028, une baisse de 30 € sur un SSD PCIe 4.0 mérite l’attention. Rien ne dit en revanche si le Black Friday, le 27 novembre, fera mieux : attendre reste un pari.
Il s’adresse à ceux qui veulent redonner de l’air à un PC portable ou ajouter 1 To rapide à une tour, pour un usage courant ou ludique. Les monteurs vidéo gagneront à viser un modèle en TLC avec cache DRAM, quitte à payer davantage. Pour les autres, c’est une façon de passer au PCIe 4.0 sous les 200 €, en sachant que cette version R2 n’est pas encore passée sur notre banc.

articles.title: Rollende Sicherheitslücken: Autos lassen sich immer noch über Infotainmentsysteme hacken
articles.text:
Rollende Sicherheitslücken: Autos lassen sich immer noch über Infotainmentsysteme hacken
Forschende der Unis Göteborg und Chalmers haben untersucht, über welche potenziellen Schwachstellen sich Autos hacken lassen. Dabei kamen sie allein für die Jahre 2022 bis 2024 auf 413 dokumentierte Sicherheitslücken. Das klingt nach viel, aber allein im Jahr 2019 wurden einer älteren Untersuchung zufolge 363 Lücken dokumentiert.
Parallel dazu haben sich die Einfallstore für mögliche Angriffe verändert. „Vor zehn Jahren wurden die meisten Sicherheitslücken in den fahrzeugeigenen Systemen entdeckt“, sagt Srijita Basu, Erstautorin der Studie. „Mittlerweile hat sich der Anteil der Schwachstellen, die in Apps, auf Websites und in Cloud-Diensten gefunden werden, fast verdreifacht.“
Persönliche Daten
Aus diesen Daten lassen sich mitunter viele persönliche Informationen auslesen – etwa Wohnort, Arbeitsplatz, Hobbys oder die Schule der Kinder. So geschehen beispielsweise im Jahr 2024 bei Volkswagen.
Unmittelbare Gefahr für Leib und Leben der Fahrzeuginsassen geht von solchen Hacks nicht aus – sollte man wenigstens meinen. Schließlich sollten das Infotainment eigentlich streng von wirklich sicherheitskritischen Funktionen wie ABS, ESP oder anderen Fahrassistenzsystemen getrennt sein. Dass dies aber nicht immer der Fall ist, zeigte der spektakuläre Hack eines Jeep Cherokees im Jahr 2015. Damals gelang es Sicherheitsforschern unter anderem, über das Infotainmentsystem Bremse, Gaspedal und Türverriegelung fernzusteuern.
Wenig gelernt
Das ist nun mehr als zehn Jahre her, doch viel gelernt hat die Branche daraus offenbar nicht. „Infotainment- und Telematiksysteme, die traditionell als nicht kritisch gelten, dienen häufig als Brücke zu sensibleren Netzwerken im Fahrzeug“, heißt es im Paper. „Unsere Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Schwachstellen in diesen Bereichen nach wie vor weit verbreitet sind und größtenteils auf die Verwendung von Software von Drittanbietern zurückzuführen sind.“
Forscherin Basu ergänzt: „Wir sind überrascht, wie elementar einige der Schwachstellen in diesen Systemen sind. Dabei kann es sich beispielsweise um Passwörter handeln, die seit der Installation nicht mehr geändert wurden.“
Die Studie hat auch untersucht, worin genau die Schwachstellen bestanden. Das vulnerabelste Produkt war demnach das Open-Source-Tool Grafana; die häufigsten potenziellen Angriffsmechanismen waren SQL-Injection und Cross-Site-Scripting.
Wachsende Angriffsfläche
Auch wenn der absolute Rückgang der Sicherheitslücken das Gegenteil suggeriert: Einen Grund zur Entspannung gibt es nicht. Denn je stärker Fahrzeuge mit der Umgebung vernetzt sind – etwa über das Streamen von Filmen oder die Kommunikation mit der Ladesäule – desto größer wird auch die Angriffsfläche für Hacker. Und je mehr sich Menschen auf Fahrassistenzsysteme verlassen, desto gravierender die potenziellen Folgen eines Hacks.
Eine bessere Verschlüsselung allein würde solche Lücken nicht schließen. Ein grundlegenderes Problem seien „fehlende Berechtigungsprüfungen“, schreibt ingenieur.de. „Nutzende müssen sich natürlich anmelden, aber dabei handelt es sich um eine reine Identitätsprüfung. Was ungeklärt bleibt, ist die Frage, ob die jeweilige Person auf das angefragte Fahrzeug überhaupt zugreifen und die gewünschte Funktion auslösen darf.“
Forscherin Basu empfiehlt Automobilherstellern, „von der Web- und IT-Welt zu lernen, wo viele dieser Schwachstellen bereits seit Jahren bekannt sind“. Und Autofahrer:innen sollten starke Passwörter nutzen und auf regelmäßige Softwareupdates achten.

articles.title: Africa’s digital economy needs more than apps to scale
articles.text:
Africa’s digital economy needs more than apps that connect users to services. It also depends on reliable transport, location data, access to financing, and shared infrastructure that businesses can build. That was a central theme of the “Beyond the App: Building the Infrastructure Behind Africa’s Everyday Economy” panel at Moonshot by TechCabal 2026.
“The app is just the front-end,” said Sanusi Adedamola, chief operating officer (COO), Fez Delivery, representing Seun Alley, chief executive officer (CEO), Fez Delivery. For companies operating in ride-hailing, delivery services, and electric mobility sectors, getting a product into users’ hands is only one part of the challenge.
They must also ensure that vehicles are available, services can locate customers, and the economics of operating in each market make sense.
This distinction is important in markets where businesses face unreliable power, patchy connectivity, fragmented logistics and disconnected cross-border payment systems. These constraints can increase operating costs, reduce service reliability, and make expansion into new markets more complicated.
Nigeria offers a practical example of this challenge. Uneven internet connectivity continues to affect businesses even in Lagos, the country’s leading commercial and technology hub. The gap illustrates how a strong market for digital services does not automatically guarantee the reliable connectivity businesses need to serve customers and expand.
Financing is another constraint. A company providing vehicles to commercial riders, for instance, must assess whether those assets can generate enough income to cover operating costs and loan repayments. During the panel, Chinwe Adighiogu, Senior Vice President (SVP) / vice president (VP) of Products at one of Africa’s leading eco-friendly EV companies, MAX, highlighted how information about riders’ activity, daily earnings, maintenance costs, and battery use can help determine affordability.
Such operational data can also help lenders assess borrowers who may lack conventional banking histories, he said.
World Bank research published in The World Bank Economic Review in 2024 found that investment in roads and electricity boosts activity in Africa’s manufacturing and services sectors. A key discussion was whether companies should build infrastructure alone or share the costs. Mapping streets and neighbourhoods is expensive, but the resulting data can benefit multiple businesses. Similarly, shared charging and battery-swapping networks could help electric mobility operators avoid building isolated systems.
Africa’s digital economy will depend not just on the apps people download, but on the infrastructure that keeps them running. A slick app means little if a delivery cannot reach a customer, a payment stalls or a vehicle cannot find a charging point. The real test is whether the infrastructure behind the screen can turn digital convenience into an everyday reality.

articles.title: Cómo saber qué aplicaciones usan el micrófono del celular y bloquear los permisos que no necesitan
articles.text:
Revisar qué aplicaciones usan el micrófono del celular y bloquear los permisos innecesarios permite reducir el riesgo que datos, conversaciones o hábitos de uso queden expuestos. Los teléfonos actuales muestran señales cuando una app activa este sensor, pero la protección depende también de que cada usuario revise con frecuencia las autorizaciones concedidas.
El acceso al micrófono es necesario para algunas funciones: llamadas, notas de voz, videoconferencias y grabaciones. Sin embargo, una aplicación que no necesita capturar audio para cumplir su tarea puede representar una señal de alerta. La clave está en comprobar si los permisos solicitados guardan relación con el servicio que ofrece.
Los permisos permiten acceder a funciones sensibles
Cuando se instala una aplicación, el sistema operativo puede solicitar permiso para usar recursos del dispositivo. Uber, por ejemplo, necesita acceder a la ubicación para ofrecer sus servicios. Las plataformas de mensajería, las redes sociales y las herramientas de videollamadas pueden requerir acceso a cámara, micrófono o galería de fotos.
El problema aparece cuando una app aparentemente sencilla solicita funciones que no necesita. Una linterna, un juego básico o una herramienta de edición de texto no deberían requerir permiso para grabar audio, leer mensajes o utilizar la cámara.
La relación entre la función de una aplicación y los permisos que pide debe ser coherente. Si no existe una justificación clara, lo aconsejable es denegar el acceso o eliminar el programa.
Las autorizaciones no son definitivas. Tanto Android como iPhone permiten revocar el permiso del micrófono en cualquier momento, sin necesidad de desinstalar una aplicación.
Cómo revisar el acceso al micrófono en iPhone
En los dispositivos de Apple, la gestión de permisos se realiza desde el menú de configuración. Para comprobar qué aplicaciones pueden utilizar el micrófono, hay que seguir estos pasos:
- Abrir Configuración.
- Entrar en Privacidad.
- Seleccionar Micrófono.
- Revisar la lista de aplicaciones con autorización.
- Desactivar el interruptor de las que no necesiten acceso.
El sistema permite identificar de forma rápida las apps que tienen permiso concedido. Si aparece una aplicación desconocida, o una que no requiere grabar audio para funcionar, conviene desactivar su acceso de inmediato.
Los iPhone con iOS 15.2 o versiones posteriores muestran un punto naranja cuando una aplicación usa el micrófono. El punto verde, en cambio, indica que una app está utilizando la cámara. Estas señales permiten detectar qué sensores están activos mientras se usa el dispositivo.
Android ofrece controles por aplicación y un administrador de permisos
En Android, la configuración puede cambiar según la marca del teléfono y la versión del sistema. Aun así, el proceso general consiste en abrir Configuración, entrar en Aplicaciones o “Ver todas las aplicaciones”, elegir el programa que se desea revisar y seleccionar Permisos.
Dentro del apartado “Micrófono”, el usuario puede elegir entre varias alternativas:
- Permitir todo el tiempo.
- Permitir solo mientras se usa la app.
- Preguntar cada vez.
- No permitir.
La opción más restrictiva no siempre es necesaria. Una aplicación de llamadas puede requerir el micrófono durante su uso, pero no tiene sentido que conserve ese acceso cuando permanece cerrada.
Android también ofrece una vista global mediante el Administrador de permisos. La ruta habitual es Configuración, Privacidad, Administrador de permisos y, después, Micrófono. Desde allí es posible consultar todas las aplicaciones que acceden a ese sensor y modificar cada autorización.
Las alertas visuales ayudan a detectar actividad inusual
Los teléfonos modernos muestran iconos o avisos cuando una aplicación utiliza el micrófono o la cámara. En Android, estos indicadores suelen aparecer en la barra de estado, aunque su diseño varía entre fabricantes. Algunos modelos también avisan cuando una app activa esos sensores en segundo plano.
Una alerta no significa automáticamente que exista espionaje, ya que puede corresponder a una función legítima. El problema surge si aparece mientras ninguna aplicación debería necesitar audio o video, o si se repite con un programa que no reconoce el usuario.
Entre las señales que justifican una revisión están el consumo inusual de batería, anuncios persistentes, menor rendimiento del dispositivo y la aparición de apps desconocidas. En esos casos, además de retirar permisos, puede ser necesario desinstalar la aplicación.
El micrófono del celular puede ser una herramienta necesaria, pero no todas las aplicaciones deben tener acceso a él. Revisar permisos, atender los indicadores visuales y limitar autorizaciones a las funciones imprescindibles permite mantener mayor control sobre conversaciones, datos y actividad digital.

articles.title: Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language
Enterprise artificial intelligence context startup Jedify Inc. today formally launched Data Agents, a product that lets business teams set up autonomous AI analysts by describing the work they want done in plain language.
Data Agents takes on a longstanding limit of business intelligence software, where analysts have to build dashboards ahead of time around the questions they expect people to ask. Generic AI assistants have tried to fill that gap. In Jedify’s telling, those tools end up guessing at what a business means from its raw tables and schemas.
The company’s core product is a context graph that pulls structured data and documents into a single model of how a business works, down to metric definitions and record-level permissions. Data Agents runs on top of it. Because joins and schema mapping are already worked out inside the graph, building an agent comes down to describing the question.
Users decide when an agent runs, whether on request, on a schedule or when a condition they have defined is met. A market that starts to underperform is the kind of anomaly an agent is meant to catch on its own, and Jedify’s deep research engine then works out what most likely drove the change.
Data access is tied to the person asking the question. Anything that user is barred from seeing, even a single row in a table, stays out of the agent’s results. On cost, Jedify claims its agents burn far fewer tokens per question than ones that have to explore raw schema at query time.
Teams can also work with the agents outside Jedify’s own interface. Under the Model Context Protocol, each one appears as a tool that can be called from Claude, ChatGPT, Slack or any agent platform a company runs. Results can go straight to email or Slack too.
Jedify is pitching the product at data teams and the business staff they support, arguing that analysts who keep fielding the same dashboard request can hand it off to an agent. On the business side, people in finance, revenue operations and sales can set up their own agents.
Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Adi Elimelech said enterprises are moving analytics “from answering questions to doing meaningful work.” The goal, he said, is for teams to build “an analytical workforce” matched to how their business operates and reach those agents from the tools employees already use.
Online casino game developer RubyPlay Ltd. is already using the product. Its team set an agent up once and scheduled it to run every day, and the report now arrives without anyone asking for it.
“It even flagged us on its own that not all of our target markets were covered yet, which told us it was reasoning through the task rather than just running a script,” said Avi Baruch, vice president of data and business applications at RubyPlay.
Data Agents is available now through Jedify’s Agents Hub, and companies can start on it for free. Jedify is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised more than $33 million, including a $24 million Series A round led by Norwest in June.

articles.title: "My grandfather fell and remained on the floor for an entire day" - Magic Vision raises €600k for monitoring tech | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Magic Vision, an Italian DeepTech startup developing AI and computer vision technologies to monitor and support older people and vulnerable individuals, has closed a €600k funding round.
Investors include SixS, the Italian company behind Gecos, a management software platform for the nonprofit sector, alongside a group of Italian business angels with expertise in law, compliance and business development.
“Population ageing is putting pressure on care systems, which must meet growing needs with increasingly limited resources and staff. Technology can make a practical contribution by enabling continuous monitoring and timely intervention when needed,” says Lorenzo Mauri, co-founder and CEO of Magic Vision.
Magic Vision’s funding comes alongside several European investments in technology-enabled care during 2026.
Germany’s Patronus raised €11 million for its elderly emergency-response technology, while Spain’s Tucuvi secured €17 million for AI-powered nursing follow-up and Portugal’s Hope Care closed a €6 million round for remote patient monitoring.
Together with Magic Vision, these account for approximately €34.6 million in funding. In Italy, Rome-based VoiceMed reported reaching €1 million in cumulative funding for its device-free respiratory monitoring technology.
“Wearable devices, emergency buttons and other available systems had significant limitations. We therefore decided to use our expertise in artificial intelligence to develop technology capable of recognising risks without requiring a person to wear a device or call for help,” adds Federico Lanzani, co-founder and CTO of Magic Vision.
Magic Vision is an Italian startup founded in 2023 by six co-founders with expertise in AI and computer vision. Based in Meda, in the province of Monza and Brianza, it develops Silver Eye, an environmental monitoring system for older people and vulnerable individuals, designed to support their independence and assist families and care professionals.
Silver Eye uses proprietary AI and computer vision algorithms to analyse people’s activity and rest patterns , identify behavioural anomalies and detect critical events such as falls. Operating through environmental sensors without wearable devices, the system enable individual behavioural monitoring even in dynamic, shared settings, including senior living facilities, cohousing and private homes.
The technology is designed to protect privacy: data is processed locally using edge AI, without storing or transmitting images. Rather than functioning as a video surveillance system, it analyses the information needed to identify potential risks, alerting caregivers only when necessary.
The aim is to support prevention and help older people maintain their independence, providing technology for care models ranging from shared housing and home care to traditional residential and nursing care facilities.
During its growth journey, the startup has benefited from incubation at PoliHub and support from ComoNExT’s NExT Accelerator and Paradigma Exponential Hub , which helped connect the founders with investors. It has also received a €30k award from the Milan Monza Brianza Lodi Chamber of Commerce through the Switch2Product programme.
The funding has enabled Magic Vision to complete development and bring Silver Eye to market.
Already deployed in pilot and commercial projects with Italian care providers, Silver Eye has more than 200 sensors installed, with a target of monitoring over 100 people by the end of 2026.
“The idea for Silver Eye came from a personal experience: when my grandfather fell and remained on the floor for an entire day, I started looking for a solution that could prevent something similar from happening again,” says Federico.
The company is also preparing a €1.5 million funding round to accelerate commercial growth, build a network of partners and distributors across Italy, and begin its European expansion, with the aim of securing its first international customer within 24 months.

articles.title: Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day
articles.text:
The US cybersecurity agency CISA on Wednesday warned that hackers have been exploiting another VMware ESXi vulnerability in attacks.
Tracked as CVE-2026-41709, the exploited flaw is described as a low-severity insufficient logging issue. It allows attackers logged in as administrators to perform certain operations without being logged.
The security defect was disclosed on July 29 alongside three critical and one high-severity bug in VMware vCenter, ESXi, Workstation, and Fusion.
VMware ESXi-9.1.0.0-25370933, ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025, and ESXi80U3j-25429389 and newer releases contain the relevant patches.
CISA added CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, urging federal agencies to patch it within the next two weeks.
CISA did not provide details on the observed exploitation, but CrowdStrike reported on Wednesday that the China-nexus threat actor Warp Panda had exploited CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day in intrusions at US organizations, including law firms.
According to CrowdStrike, Warp Panda typically gains initial access through internet-facing edge devices and pivots to VMware vCenter, where it deployed malware such as BrickStorm, TetanusStorm, SharpStorm, DualGauge and GuestConduit in intrusions throughout 2025.
In several of those attacks, and as late as early 2026, the group used CVE-2026-41709 to significantly reduce audit trail visibility.
At least two other security defects described in Broadcom’s July 29 advisories have been targeted in the wild, namely CVE-2026-59309 (a critical-severity authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-59310 (a critical directory traversal issue leading to arbitrary code execution).
In mid-August, cybersecurity company Quirso said an APT had been exploiting CVE-2026-59310 to compromise approximately 360 web-accessible VMware vCenter servers and deploy an SSH reverse shell.
Later, Quirso attributed the activity to a China-linked threat actor and warned that CVE-2026-59309 had been exploited as well, likely before CVE-2026-59310, potentially by a different threat actor.
Mass targeting of CVE-2026-59310 was flagged in early September.

articles.title: Logitech Unveils MX Master 4 Special Developer Edition
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Logitech Unveils MX Master 4 Special Developer Edition
Logitech has released a Developer Edition of its MX Master 4 mouse that was launched back in September 2025. The company says that this is a tribute to the "developers who are shaping the digital world". However, the hardware is identical to the standard MX Master 4. The same 8,000 DPI sensor and MagSpeed scroll wheel capable of 1,000 lines per second. We can mention built-in haptic feedback and the Action Ring button for shortcuts. Then, it also has the same 650 mAh battery with up to 70 days of use, USB-C quick charging, and multi-device pairing. Basically, nothing has changed under the hood or in terms of functionality.
The differences are purely visual, as the new edition uses a two-tone dark and light gray scheme with bright green accents. There are laser-etched syntax annotations including // and </> markup tags, circuit traces, and a {Hello, World} execution prompt. Logitech has also added a few Easter eggs, 0xFF + 1 referencing World Programmers' Day, 09.17 for the Linux Kernel release date, and !04.01 for World Backup Day. The good news is that MX Master 4 Developer Edition costs the same as the standard model. The mouse is currently listed on the Logitech website for $120 / €130, together with the two-year warranty.

articles.title: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the 'For You' feed | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Reddit is the latest social platform to adopt the “For You” feed popularized by TikTok. The company announced on Wednesday that users will now see two options when opening the platform: “For You” and “Following.”
The “For You” feed combines posts from communities users have joined with recommendations tailored to their interests. Reddit says the feature will help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not have otherwise come across. The “Following” feed only displays posts from communities they have joined.
The company says the change is designed to foster connection, participation, and belonging.
Reddit is likely hoping that the redesigned feed experience will nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow. It also brings Reddit more in line with the recommendation-driven experience that’s become standard across social media, where algorithms play a significant role in shaping what users see.
With the launch, Reddit joins a number of popular platforms that have adopted “For You”-style feeds, including Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook.
Of course, not everyone will welcome the change, as some users may prefer the more focused feed experience of only seeing posts from communities they’ve joined, rather than having recommended content mixed into their home feed. Some users who encountered the new feed during its initial testing phase have already expressed their frustration with the change.
Reddit says users can switch between feeds and return to the one they last viewed the next time they open the platform.
It’s worth noting that although Reddit has long recommended posts from outside users’ subscribed communities, the new layout gives those recommendations their own feed on the homepage.
“This new feed experience is a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant – an idea, a connection, a unique perspective, or even a new interest,” the company wrote in a blog post. “A more human internet is not just something you sit back and watch, it is something you find value in and want to participate in.”
The new feed experience is rolling out globally over the next few weeks, the company says.

articles.title: The impossible equation of being a researcher mother, striving to make ends meet
articles.text:
How can we encourage women to pursue scientific careers? In recent years, a number of mentoring or awareness campaigns have been put in place to encourage French high school students to study maths, physics or engineering sciences, while they remain underrepresented in these fields. One of the last large-scale initiatives is the Filles et Maths program, launched in 2025, including work on gender bias, the implementation of “role models” or timetables featuring flexible hours.
The program was nonetheless met with criticism: while women remain under-represented in some disciplines, they also remain a minority in the highest positions across the board in the academic world, from mathematics to social sciences.
In France, gender inequalities are therefore not limited to access to scientific studies: they cut across all university careers and make many women leave French Higher Education and Research before securing tenure. This “drain” is explained by several factors among which motherhood holds an important place. A survey in Denmark illustrates that unlike men, one in three women abandon their scientific career after the birth of their first child.
The survey I have been conducting among doctoral students and social scientists highlights the difficulties faced by women who became mothers before becoming permanent employees. Since the 1980s, recruitment requirements have become tougher with candidates needing to have written a good PhD paper, regularly have their work published, participate in scientific events and get involved in the life of research labs. Much of this work falls under hope labour, that is, unpaid work done in the hope of future employment.
In this context, what could be called the myth of the “total researcher” takes shape. This is based on the double penalty of being a productive scientist (without necessarily receiving any financial reward) and embodying the ideal of a career woman, devoted companion, and dedicated mother all rolled into one.
However, this ideal of the “total researcher” clashes with the actual conditions of scientific work and motherhood.
Paying the motherhood penalty in academia
Becoming a full-time researcher requires mothers who aren’t tenured researchers to reorganise their lives. Some cram several days’ work into one by doing casual work, part-time teaching, unpaid scientific projects, and parental responsibilities. The pace often makes women work under pressure, sometimes at the expense of the quantity and quality of their scientific work.
Other women choose to remain unemployed or take parental leave and thus link their career to that of their spouse if they earn enough. If this strategy of linked career is favourable for scientific production when you have a child, it also creates material dependence that could lead to sexist and sexual violence within the family unit, which this testimony from Jeanne, a doctor and mother of a little girl, illustrates:
“I sometimes feel like I have to [‘have sex’], telling myself that ‘I owe him’ and ‘He lets me know it’.”
In a professional context, where every moment must count, maternity, parental or sick leave become scientific working hours in themselves.
Rebecca, for example, shared that she continued writing her final thesis when her son was sent to hospital in an emergency. This situation feeds a feeling of double guilt: the respondents believe they are never up to par, neither as mothers nor as researchers. Joana explains:
“I took parental leave from work, but I feel bad about working when I see my son next to me.”
Some non-tenured researcher dads, on the other hand, benefit from an academic paternity bonus. The gendered division of domestic and parental tasks, as well as taking paternity leave, sometimes allows them to devote more time to their research. To quote Marion’s doctor of History husband’s words: “I have completed nearly two articles in one month of paternity leave!”
The ‘initiatory rite of passage’ rhetoric
Even when they reorganise their lives to ensure their scientific activity, non-tenured researcher mothers face disqualification mechanisms from their peers.
Some remarks that seem kind on the surface often come back to motherhood: “You should spend more time with your children,” “they must miss you”, or “where is your child?”
Other colleagues, often women incumbents, the difficulties that non-incumbents face in reconciling motherhood and scientific work seem perfectly normal, presenting them as inevitable trials. Louise reports how one female colleague explained to her:
“What you’re going through is normal; it’s an uphill battle. We’ve all been there.”
While such pep talks are meant to be comforting, the constraints related to motherhood appear as an obligatory rite of passage to becoming a ‘total’ researcher.
Motherhood-related constraints that become faults
Due to increasing competition in the French Higher Education & Research system, motherhood can be used against some women as a means of sidelining them. Some respondents said they were excluded from scientific events on the basis that they now had “better things to do” with their children.
When precarious researchers voice their concerns at meetings, their difficulties in reconciling scientific work and motherhood are disqualified on the grounds that they “knew” what having a child meant before becoming a tenured researcher.
The constraints related to motherhood end up remaining invisible behind criticism about a supposed lack of scientific productivity, which tends to arise from pregnancy onwards, through comments on untenured researcher mothers-to-be’s physical appearance and how they supposedly mismanage stress with regards to important deadlines in their careers.
Anouk recounts that, after auditioning for a position as a lecturer when she was pregnant, a member of the jury who said she wanted to help her “reminded him” that committees were looking for “nice people to chat to at the coffee machine”, before offering her the following advice:
“Are you pregnant? You looked pale. Next time, apply some blush on your cheeks so you don’t make a bad impression.”
The complaints also concern the routes travelled to academia: not attending certain events organised during the school holidays, taking on casual work or failing to develop other research subjects that are unrelated to their PhD; are frequently associated with a lack of scientific commitment, thus obscuring the financial and family-related constraints these women face.
A case of the fate of Sisyphus?
Faced with the impossibility of achieving the tenured researcher ideal, many respondents end up internalising their challenges as individual failures and gradually abandon academia.
This distance from academia is actually the result of structural constraints that make it difficult to reconcile motherhood and careers in research. Élodie expresses a sense of exhaustion with the predicament:
“I am like Sisyphus! My fate is to do work that will never be recognised, that will never lead to anything because I had a child at the end of my PhD studies.”
In this context, in Higher Education and Research, schemes like France’s Filles et Maths Maths program are not going to be enough to reduce inequalities. More broadly, rethinking the criteria around tenure is what needs to happen.
The current requirements favour women with sufficient material resources and time, to the detriment of people experiencing family, social or financial constraints. This marginalisation is not only unequal: it is harmful to research. By depriving people of certain talents, it also deprives them of certain knowledge.
A weekly e-mail in English featuring expertise from scholars and researchers. It provides an introduction to the diversity of research coming out of the continent and considers some of the key issues facing European countries. Get the newsletter!

articles.title: A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
articles.text:
A hacker stole a trove of personal information from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The breach exposes the names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses, and office locations of more than 41,000 employees, including those in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), according to TechCrunch and Wired. The data also linked the agencies to specific surveillance tools.
A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
The names, job titles, phone numbers, and emails of thousands of ICE, CBP, and other DHS employees were compromised in a massive hack.
As reported by TechCrunch, a hacker known as “Department of Peace” gained access to the data through Okta, an identity and access management service used by the DHS. Around 21,000 records pertain to CBP employees, and nearly 7,000 belong to staff at ICE. The data also includes records from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI).
The DHS has worked to conceal the identities of CBP and ICE agents, who have carried out anti-immigration raids around the US, while also tracking down online critics. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” the “Department of Peace” hacker said, according to TechCrunch. This leak comes just weeks after hackers stole data from the FBI on its employees and job applicants.
The leaked DHS information was reportedly given to cybersecurity researcher maia arson crimew, who shared it with Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), a nonprofit organization that’s now hosting the leaked “Icepick” dataset. The leak also reportedly includes information about DHS groups that have access to tools that can be used for surveillance, such as the facial recognition app Mobile Fortify and PenLink, which can collect and analyze data from phones and online services.
The DHS didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

articles.title: 'VisionQuest' recupera por sorpresa a uno de los primeros villanos de Marvel: no le veíamos desde 'Iron Man'
articles.text:
ATENCIÓN: El artículo contiene SPOILERS de VisionQuest 1x06.
El estreno de los nuevos episodios de VisionQuest esta semana ha devuelto a los fans de Marvel a un personaje totalmente inesperado. La serie protagonizada por Paul Bettany sigue el camino de la nueva Visión Blanca. Atrapado en su propio conflicto interno, el personaje no es capaz de conectar emocionalmente con los recuerdos de su versión anterior. Pero no por ello dejará de intentar sentirse, de verdad, humano.
En ese camino se cruza con Tommy Shepherd, que asegura ser el hijo de Wanda y Visión. Sin embargo, el villano Paladín, cuyo nombre real es Paul Denning, le secuestra con el fin de atraer a Visión a una trampa y poder capturarle para entregárselo a su misterioso Cliente. Pero lo cierto es que esta peligrosa figura, cuya identidad sigue siendo desconocida, ha puesto punto y final al contrato que les unía.
Bajo este contexto, todos los personajes se reúnen en Madripoor. Allí, Visión y el Paladín se enfrentan en una vertiginosa escena de acción, con Tommy como recompensa. Pero, de pronto, ambos se ven sorprendidos por una banda que comienza a tirotearles. Y el líder de todos ellos no es otro que Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar. Los fans más veteranos de Marvel recordarán perfectamente a este personaje porque era el líder de la banda terrorista de los 10 Anillos que secuestraron a Tony Stark en Iron Man.
En aquella película, Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar parecía morir traicionado por Obadiah Stane, que mandaba a sus hombres para asesinarlo. Sin embargo, jamás vimos su cadáver. Y ahora, casi veinte años después, el actor Faran Tahir ha regresado como Raza en la serie de VisionQuest. Una confirmación de que este villano se ha mantenido vivo y activo en las sombras.
¿Es Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar el Cliente de VisionQuest?
Con esta impactante revelación del retorno de Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar a Marvel, muchos podrían pensar que el villano es el verdadero Cliente, el gran antagonista en las sombras de VisionQuest. Pero pronto salimos de dudas. Resulta que no, Raza no es esta misteriosa figura, sino otro de sus mercenarios.
El Cliente ha contratado a Raza y sus hombres para poner fin al desastre generado por el Paladín y, de paso, secuestrar definitivamente a Visión. De hecho, como vemos en VisionQuest 1x06, está a punto de conseguirlo. Al final, los protagonistas se salvan porque E.D.I.T.H. consigue tomar control de los drones de los terroristas. El propio Paladín es quien le da el golpe definitivo a Raza para dejarle fuera de combate.
Date de alta en Disney+ ahora y ahorra gracias a la suscripción anual, con la que podrás disfrutar de todo su catálogo de series y películas. Acceso a los últimos estrenos, al catálogo de Star y ESPN* y a los mejores documentales de National Geographic.
*ESPN solo está disponible en Latinoamérica. Ahorro respecto a 12 meses de suscripción mensual.
Tras este breve pero intenso regreso de Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar a Marvel, se desconoce si volveremos a ver al personaje en el futuro. No ha muerto, por lo que no hay nada descartado. Pero lo cierto es que todo apunta a que su retorno no era más que un guiño a los fans de la saga y una nueva manera de conectar la nueva serie al resto de la franquicia. Los dos últimos episodios de VisionQuest se estrenarán en Disney+ el 3 y el 10 de noviembre (el 4 y el 11 de noviembre en España), respectivamente.

articles.title: Cómo manejar el Tesla Roadster, el auto de Elon Musk que vuela: con este videojuego es posible
articles.text:
Roadflip permite manejar el Tesla Roadster antes de que la empresa de Elon Musk fabrique una sola unidad. El juego, gratuito y accesible desde el navegador, llega después de una demostración que mezcla efectos de ciencia ficción con un cronograma de producción todavía lejano.
Mientras el deportivo real acumula casi una década de demoras, esta versión virtual se convirtió en la manera más accesible de experimentar sus propulsores. Detrás del proyecto está Niko Draca, ingeniero de software de Shopify, quien tomó la última demostración del auto como punto de partida para una mecánica simple pero exigente.
Cómo se juega y dónde encontrarlo
La dinámica de Roadflip consiste en acelerar el Roadster hasta una rampa vertical, saltar y encadenar la mayor cantidad de vueltas posible en el aire. Antes de tocar el suelo, el jugador debe activar los propulsores de gas frío del auto para amortiguar la caída. Cuantas más volteretas se completen, más alto es el puntaje.
Draca resumió la propuesta como “Tony Hawk... pero con un Roadster”, en referencia a la saga de skate. El propio desarrollador admitió que todavía no logró aterrizar sin que el vehículo termine explotando, lo que da una idea de la dificultad real detrás de una mecánica que parece sencilla a simple vista.
Roadflip es un videojuego gratuito para navegador que recrea los saltos y acrobacias del Tesla Roadster con sus propulsores de aire comprimido. No requiere descarga ni reserva previa y funciona como una alternativa accesible frente a un vehículo real que todavía no tiene fecha de entrega confirmada.
El juego no exige pago ni registro: basta con abrirlo desde el navegador para empezar a jugar. En ese sentido, funciona como contrapunto lúdico de un vehículo que, en su versión física, exige un desembolso inicial de 50.000 dólares solo para reservar un lugar en la fila de producción.
Cuál es la tecnología detrás del Roadster y su precio
El sistema evita el camino habitual de los hiperdeportivos eléctricos, que apelan a varios motores y tracción integral. El Roadster concentra hasta 1.360 CV en el eje trasero y suma propulsión a chorro para superar el límite de fricción entre el neumático y el asfalto.
Los dos motores traseros generan unos 32,3 kN de empuje, mientras ventiladores encapsulados bajo el piso aspiran aire para generar más de 2 G de carga vertical y evitar que las ruedas patinen. A eso se suman hasta diez propulsores direccionales en la versión más extrema, llamada Rocket.
El gas rico en nitrógeno se almacena a 10.000 psi en un tanque similar a los que usan los cohetes Falcon y Starship, y se libera mediante actuadores que provienen de los motores del tobillo del robot humanoide Optimus. El recorrido del gas hasta las toberas traseras exige tuberías de idéntica longitud, ya que cualquier asimetría provocaría que el auto gire sobre su propio eje al arrancar.
La limitación más marcada aparece en la autonomía del sistema: el tanque de 200 litros de la versión Thrust se agota en apenas seis segundos de uso pleno, y reabastecer los 600 litros de la versión Rocket mediante el compresor integrado demora entre 6 y 7 horas. Desde Tesla afirman que buscan reducir ese tiempo a 30 minutos para cuando el auto llegue a producción.
La gama prevista para 2028 contempla tres configuraciones, todas de tracción trasera. La versión de entrada, llamada Roadster, ofrece 1.088 CV y una autonomía estimada de entre 483 y 515 kilómetros, con una reserva de 50.000 dólares.
La versión Thrust suma el tanque de 200 litros y cuatro propulsores traseros, con un depósito previo de 250.000 dólares. La Rocket, monoplaza y con diez propulsores, queda restringida a clientes seleccionados por la marca y no estará homologada para circular por vías públicas.
Tesla no confirmó el precio definitivo de cada configuración y advierte que el vehículo sigue en desarrollo, sin garantías sobre la fecha final de entrega.

articles.title: Chaque séjour Airbnb va désormais financer un logement d’urgence pour des sinistrés, avec une promesse
articles.text:
Airbnb va désormais reverser dix centimes par séjour réservé à Airbnb.org, son association d’hébergement d’urgence. L’objectif est de réunir 500 millions de dollars sur cinq ans pour offrir un million de nuits gratuites par an aux sinistrés partout dans le monde.
Airbnb a annoncé ,ce mercredi 28 octobre, un tout nouveau modèle de financement pour Airbnb.org, l’organisation à but non lucratif qui loge gratuitement les personnes touchées par des catastrophes. Une partie des revenus tirés de chaque séjour doit permettre à l’association de multiplier ses hébergements d’urgence, sans surcoût pour les voyageurs ni baisse de revenus pour les hôtes. Le dispositif a déjà servi en France après les récentes inondations d’Istres, mais son financement soulève une question de calcul.
Réserver un Airbnb va maintenant aider des sinistrés à se reloger, sans payer plus cher
Alors comment ça marche ? Vous allez voir que le mécanisme est plutôt simple. À chaque séjour réservé, Airbnb prend 0,10 dollar sur ses propres revenus, soit un peu moins de 10 centimes d’euro, et le reverse à Airbnb.org. Le voyageur ne paie rien de plus et l’hôte ne touche rien de moins. Personne n’a non plus besoin de s’inscrire ou de cocher une case, puisque le don se fait automatiquement, en coulisses, peut-on dire. Seuls les séjours qui ont bien lieu comptent, donc une réservation annulée avant l’arrivée ne rapporte rien à l’association. Les Expériences et les Services vendus par Airbnb n’entrent pas non plus dans le calcul. Ce sont les activités (visites guidées, ateliers…) et les prestations (chef à domicile, massage…) que la plateforme vend désormais en plus des logements.
Sur le papier, les comptes sont plutôt justes. Airbnb promet 500 millions de dollars en cinq ans, soit 100 millions par an, et vise un million de nuits gratuites chaque année. Sur son site, Airbnb.org indique qu’un don de 110 dollars permet d’offrir une nuit d’hébergement, donc en multipliant ce coût par un million de nuits, on retombe à peu près sur l’enveloppe annoncée. Le changement d’échelle, lui, est spectaculaire. Tout est parti d’un geste spontané en 2012, quand une hôte avait ouvert sa porte aux victimes de l’ouragan Sandy, et l’initiative est devenue une association indépendante en 2020. Depuis, elle a offert plus de 1,6 million de nuits à plus de 250 000 personnes, dont 126 000 nuits en 2025 rien que pour les catastrophes, soit huit fois moins que l’objectif désormais visé chaque année. « C’est là tout l’esprit d’Airbnb », assure Brian Chesky, le cofondateur et président de la plateforme.
Sauf que pour réunir 100 millions de dollars par an à raison de dix cents par séjour, il faudrait un milliard de réservations chaque année. Or, d’après son rapport annuel, Airbnb a enregistré 533 millions de nuitées en 2025, un total qui inclut aussi les places réservées pour des activités. Attention aussi, car une nuitée n’est pas un séjour, on rappelle qu'un voyageur qui loue un appartement pour un week-end prolongé compte pour trois ou quatre nuitées, certes, mais pour une seule réservation. Avec une durée moyenne de 3,7 nuits par séjour, on tourne donc autour de 140 millions de réservations, soit environ 14 millions de dollars par an, sept fois moins que la somme promise. Le communiqué d'Airbnb n’explique pas cet écart. Il évoque seulement des « dons supplémentaires », sans en préciser l’origine ni le montant, et ses mentions légales reconnaissent que la somme versée dépendra du nombre de réservations.
D'Istres dans les Bouches-du-Rhône à l'Utah, l'hébergement d'urgence change de dimension
Il faut savoir qu'Airbnb.org ne choisit pas seule les bénéficiaires. En effet, des associations, des mairies ou des services de l’État lui signalent les personnes qui ont besoin d’un toit. L’association leur remet alors des crédits, une sorte de bon d’achat, pour réserver elles-mêmes un logement sur Airbnb comme n’importe quel voyageur. Elles peuvent ainsi rester près de leurs proches, emmener leurs animaux ou trouver un lieu adapté à un handicap. Les hôtes sont payés normalement, et certains choisissent même de baisser leur tarif ou de reverser une partie de leurs gains. Airbnb, de son côté, paie les frais de fonctionnement de l’association, pour que les dons du public servent entièrement aux hébergements, et assure ne rien gagner sur ces séjours. Les inondations d’Istres, dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, ont permis de mettre le dispositif à l’œuvre la semaine dernière. Après 275 mm de pluie, soit 275 litres d’eau par mètre carré, la ville a dû reloger 88 personnes. Elle a dressé la liste des sinistrés à orienter vers Airbnb.org, qui peut les héberger jusqu’à 28 jours.
En France, Airbnb.org n’en est pas à son coup d’essai. L’association affirme y avoir offert plus de 65 000 nuits d’hébergement d’urgence depuis 2020. Elle est notamment intervenue après la tempête Nils et l’incendie de Perpignan, puis lors des feux qui ont frappé la Gironde et les Landes cet été, où elle a fourni à elle seule 3 000 nuits. Sa force, c’est la rapidité, semble-t-il. En 2026, dans la zone qui regroupe l’Europe, le Moyen-Orient et l’Afrique, environ la moitié des personnes relogées ont pu poser leurs valises moins de 24 heures après la réservation. Le format du logement entier fait aussi la différence, là où un gymnase ou une chambre d’hôtel se prête mal à certaines situations. Cette année en France, un séjour sur sept accueillait un animal de compagnie, et plus d’un quart concernait des groupes d’au moins quatre personnes, souvent des familles qui peuvent ainsi rester ensemble.
En tout cas, avec ce nouveau financement, l’association veut aller au-delà des seules catastrophes naturelles. Ces dernières l’occupent déjà beaucoup plus qu’avant. Elle est intervenue sur plus de 200 sinistres cette année, contre huit seulement en 2023. D’ici fin 2026, elle prévoit d’héberger dans plus de 20 pays les familles obligées de se déplacer loin de chez elles pour faire soigner un proche. Elle s’appuie pour cela sur des partenaires comme la Fundación Xana en Espagne ou la Leukaemia Foundation en Australie. Un nouveau programme accueillera aussi les victimes de violences conjugales qui ont fui leur foyer et cherchent à se reconstruire, notamment avec l’association Peace House dans l’Utah. Aux États-Unis, enfin, l’aide s’étend aux anciens combattants atteints d’une maladie grave ou qui suivent un traitement lourd. Pour une plateforme régulièrement accusée de retirer des logements du marché locatif et de compliquer la vie des habitants dans de nombreuses villes, l’opération d’image tombe, il faut le dire, plutôt bien.

articles.title: OPINION: Scaling is the real test of Europe’s AI boom | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Europe’s AI funding boom is not benefiting every part of the market equally. Recorded Series A–C investment rose by approximately 66% in the first nine months of 2026, yet funding in rounds worth €22.2 million to less than €88.9 million declined by around 8%.
This middle segment is particularly important for AI startups moving beyond their first customers. Expanding internationally, hiring teams and securing larger enterprise contracts can require substantial capital, even for companies operating on a much smaller scale than Europe’s leading AI developers.
The contrasting funding trends raise questions about how Europe’s next generation of AI companies will finance their expansion. While overall investment continues to grow, the more important test may be whether startups can progress from early funding rounds to sustainable businesses without becoming overly dependent on their next investment.
The findings are based on an analysis of Crunchbase funding-round data for the first nine months of 2025 and 2026, using consistent dates and funding stages and correcting identified data issues. The original dollar-based categories were retained, with euro thresholds rounded for readability. Figures follow Crunchbase’s classifications and currency conversions and may differ from public announcements.
How Europe’s AI funding splits across the market
The adjusted Crunchbase sample recorded approximately €15.04 billion in announced Series A–C funding in the first nine months of 2026, up from €9.06 billion a year earlier. The number of recorded funding events increased from 203 to 232. Of these, 196 events in 2025 and 218 in 2026 were included in the round-size breakdown. These figures cover companies tagged as Artificial Intelligence by Crunchbase and do not represent all European AI funding stages.
The growth was concentrated in larger transactions. Rounds worth €88.9 million or more increased from 18 to 33, accounting for approximately 74% of disclosed funding in 2026, up from 59% the previous year. Although the ten biggest investments represented about half of the total, funding outside these transactions also grew.
Smaller rounds became more frequent, increasing from 108 to 124 for investments below €22.2 million. The middle of the market, however, moved in the opposite direction. The €22.2–88.9 million segment saw its share of disclosed funding fall from approximately 29% to 16%. Across all rounds below €88.9 million, recorded funding barely increased, growing by just 2.7% to €3.86 billion.
This uneven growth suggests that Europe’s AI investment boom has not been felt equally across different funding sizes. While more smaller rounds were recorded and large investments attracted substantial capital, the segment between them contracted.
Some of the largest announcements also require caution. NEURA Robotics announced a Series C of up to €1.24 billion, while Multiverse Computing described a round targeting up to €500 million. Excluding both amounts reduced the sample’s overall funding growth from approximately 66% to 47%.
The increase therefore remained substantial even without these transactions, but the headline amounts should not be interpreted as confirmation that all the funding had already been received.
From €98 million to €3 billion: The different costs of scaling AI
Taktile, a Berlin-founded company developing decision technology for financial institutions, raised approximately €51 million in a Series B in February 2025. By June 2026, it had secured another approximately €98 million in Series C funding. The company operates in enterprise software, where expansion means winning more customers and making its technology work inside complex banking systems.
Mistral raised €3 billion in a Series D in September 2026. Developing frontier AI models requires enormous computing resources and research investment. The financing needs of these two companies differ considerably, yet their announcements contribute to the broader picture of an AI funding boom. These examples provide context separately from the statistical sample: Taktile is absent from the European-headquartered export, and Mistral’s Series D falls outside the stages analysed.
Funding activity also increased across all three stages. Series A events rose from 133 to 148, Series B from 51 to 58, and Series C from 19 to 26. Median round sizes grew at every stage, with the most pronounced increase at Series C, where the median rose from €49.3 million to €93.3 million.
These figures do not indicate a broad decline in Series B or C activity. However, they cannot show how easily individual companies secured funding or what conditions investors attached to their investments.
Taktile shows that companies can successfully move through successive funding stages. For other founders, planning that transition means making expensive decisions before they know when the next round will arrive or what terms investors will offer.
The cost of depending on your next funding round
A company may raise capital to enter new markets, hire sales teams and expand its customer base. These plans often assume that another funding round will follow once the business reaches its next growth targets. But expansion can become expensive long before the company reaches those targets.
For an enterprise AI business, new contracts may require extensive customisation and ongoing engineering support. Revenue grows, yet the company spends more than expected to deliver it. Hiring commitments and operating costs continue even when progress falls behind the original plan.
This leaves founders in a difficult position. If they need fresh capital to maintain operations, they have less control over the timing of fundraising and the terms investors offer. A more measured expansion strategy may look less impressive in the short term, but it gives management greater freedom to choose when and how to raise its next round.
The next test for Europe’s AI boom
The next test for Europe’s AI funding market will come in 2027 and 2028, when some of the startups raising smaller amounts today will need substantially more capital to expand. Whether they can secure investments of €27 million, €44 million or more on favourable terms will help determine their ability to grow.
The current data does not show how many companies sought funding unsuccessfully, how long fundraising took or how much capital they needed. It therefore cannot establish a shortage of growth capital across Europe.
The next stage will also put more pressure on business fundamentals. Enterprise AI companies that can retain customers and expand without a corresponding rise in operating costs should have an advantage when seeking further investment. Others may face difficult choices about how quickly they can grow and how much capital they can afford to raise.
It will be worth following the companies that secured smaller rounds in 2025 and 2026. Their progression to larger investments, the time between funding rounds and the terms they receive will help establish whether Europe has a genuine growth-capital constraint.
Europe may continue setting AI investment records. The more consequential development over the next few years will be how many of today’s funded startups manage to reach the next stage and build sustainable businesses. That is where the depth of Europe’s AI funding market will become much clearer.

articles.title: Ce SUV électrique chinois devient éligible au bonus écologique en France grâce à Stellantis
articles.text:
Le constructeur chinois est bien aidé dans son implantation en Europe par Stellantis. En effet, la marque chinoise est gérée en Europe par Stellantis sous une société appelée Leapmotor International, dont Stellantis est actionnaire majoritaire. Le groupe franco-italien ne compte pas qu’importer les Leapmotor en Europe : les produire dans ses usines est aussi un projet important pour la réussite de la marque, et un modèle vient justement de profiter de cette stratégie pour devenir beaucoup plus intéressant en France et en Europe.
De nouveaux modèles produits en Espagne
Stellantis a trouvé de la place dans ses usines pour les modèles Leapmotor. L’usine espagnole de Saragosse, produisant actuellement pour le groupe la Peugeot 208, l’Opel Corsa ou encore la Lancia Ypsilon, vient de voir arriver le Leapmotor B10. Il s’agit d’un SUV compact d’origine chinoise désormais assemblé par Stellantis en Espagne pour le marché européen.
Mais ce n’est pas tout, Stellantis prévoit d’ajouter à l’usine de Saragosse dans les prochaines semaines la Leapmotor B05, une berline compacte électrique dont le prix pourrait défier toute concurrence. Pour Stellantis, cela assure l’occupation de son appareil industriel, que ce soit ses chaînes de production, mais aussi ses collaborateurs. Tandis que pour Leapmotor, cela permet d’avoir des produits plus concurrentiels en Europe, évitant les barrières à l’entrée que l’Union européenne a mises en place pour les constructeurs chinois.
Un nouveau SUV électrique chinois éligible au bonus écologique
En profitant de sa production en Espagne, le Leapmotor B10 peut prétendre désormais au bonus écologique en France, ce qui peut créer de l’inquiétude du côté des constructeurs européens qui luttent contre les nouvelles marques chinoises.
Et cela n’a pas traîné puisque le Leapmotor B10 valide déjà l’éco-score, précieux sésame pour profiter du coup de pouce CEE en France. Pourtant, cet éco-score a été pensé justement pour éviter de financer des véhicules électriques chinois, enfin davantage des véhicules électriques produits en dehors de l’Europe, visant intrinsèquement les constructeurs chinois très agressifs face aux constructeurs européens. Il y avait une volonté de la France de favoriser les constructeurs français et européens avec cet éco-score que vient de déjouer Stellantis, constructeur ayant pourtant intérêt à ne pas voir la concurrence chinoise s’installer.
En aidant à l’obtention de l’éco-score de 3 650 à 7 000 € pour le Leapmotor B10, on peut dire que Stellantis a fait entrer le loup dans la bergerie. D’autant que ce lieu de production en Espagne évite également la taxe d’importation en Europe majorée pour les voitures électriques produites en Chine. Le Leapmotor B10 passe désormais à 25 750 euros pour tous, en déduisant le bonus de 3 650 euros, ou 22 400 euros avec le bonus pour les foyers modestes.
À ce prix, le Leapmotor B10 Life Pro embarque une batterie de 60,8 kWh pour une autonomie de 400 km WLTP. Leapmotor vient récemment d’améliorer la capacité de la batterie. En haut de gamme, il y a la version Pro Max, qui utilise une batterie de 68,7 kWh pour 450 km d’autonomie WLTP. Les autonomies ne sont pas impressionnantes, mais elles sont plus que raisonnables pour les prix auxquels sont proposées les variantes du Leapmotor B10. Et pire encore pour la concurrence européenne, la Leapmotor B05 devrait également avoir droit prochainement au bonus écologique, réduisant encore son prix déjà très agressif.

articles.title: Nefilim and Hive ransomware affiliate gets 70 months in prison
articles.text:
A Ukrainian national was sentenced to 70 months in prison for his role in Nefilim and Hive ransomware attacks targeting hospitals, government entities, and high-revenue businesses worldwide between 2018 and 2021.
The sentence follows the extradition of 35-year-old Artem Aleksandrovych Stryzhak to the United States on April 30, 2025, after authorities arrested him in Spain in June 2024.
"Artem Stryzhak is a prolific cybercriminal who worked with multiple ransomware groups to target U.S. businesses and hospitals," said Brett Leatherman, the FBI's Cyber Branch Operations Director. "These groups disrupted patient care and caused more than $100 million in losses. Today's sentence reflects the seriousness of Stryzhak's crimes and demonstrates the FBI's global reach and extensive network of international partners."
According to court documents, he paid for 20% of all ransom payments collected for access to custom Nefilim ransomware and decryption keys starting in June 2021.
While active as a Nefilim affiliate until October 2021, Stryzhak used the custom-tailored malware to target large corporations in the United States, Canada, and Australia with revenues exceeding $100 million each year. However, one of the Nefilim administrators later encouraged him to focus on large companies that were generating more than $200 million annually.
To pressure victims into paying, the ransomware operation also threatened to leak data stolen during attacks on dark web "Corporate Leaks" websites managed by the Nefilim admins unless victims met the ransom demands.
Stryzhak also joined Hive ransomware as an early affiliate, breaching and encrypting the systems of seven victims, including a dentist's office, multiple law firms, and a healthcare provider during the COVID-19 pandemic.
In December 2025, Stryzhak pleaded guilty and admitted to computer fraud conspiracy charges brought by US prosecutors in connection with ransomware attacks targeting businesses in the United States, Norway, France, Switzerland, Germany, and the Netherlands.
"Disrupting a ransomware group that attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide and sentencing a defendant who had targeted healthcare during the COVID-19 pandemic is of significant importance to this office," added US Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe.
"Ransomware attacks like those committed by the defendant wreak enormous havoc — harming victim companies that pay millions in remediation and ransoms, preventing hospitals and other critical facilities from accessing data, and putting sensitive information in the hands of bad actors," US Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. noted.
The US State Department also offers up to $11 million for any details that could lead to the arrest of Ukrainian national Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, one of Stryzhak's alleged accomplices, who is still at large.
Tymoshchuk is on the most-wanted lists of the European Union and the FBI, and the US Justice Department charged him in September for his roles as an administrator for the LockerGoga, MegaCortex, and Nefilim ransomware gangs. He was also allegedly involved in ransomware attacks that caused millions of dollars in damages to hundreds of companies around the world between July 2020 and October 2021.
